+## 2026-09-11s — TWO OF THE FOUR RULED CHECKS ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, AND THE PROOF IS GRASS
+
+Ryan asked me to find a position and yaw. The search found that the
+GEOMETRY is satisfiable and that the CHECK SET is not.
+
+    p25 >= 40 m         wants no near ground
+    meadow >= 0.55      wants meadow, which means GRASS
+
+MEASURED on the g4b capture (265600, -94400, 6541.2 cm, yaw 30, pitch 0):
+
+    depth < 1.5 m   21.190% of frame
+    1.5 - 3 m        6.431%          -> 27.6% inside 3 m
+    3 - 10 m         1.143%
+    10 - 50 m        2.879%
+    50 - 300 m      30.383%          -> frac PASSES its 0.30 floor
+    > 300 m         11.418%
+
+The TERRAIN-ONLY raymarch of the same station puts p25 at 85.9 m and
+almost nothing inside 3 m. So that 21% within 1.5 m is not terrain: it is
+**ground cover standing at the lens**. Meadow's placed height is 0.387 m
+p50 / 0.484 max and Blueberry's 0.475 / 0.605, and at a 1.7 m eye at
+pitch 0 the bottom of the frame looks 29.4 deg down -- terrain at 3.0 m,
+and any grass card in that cone at 1-2 m.
+
+**27.6% of the frame is grass inside 3 m, which exceeds the 25% that
+DEFINES p25.** p25 is therefore pinned near 1 m by the ground cover
+alone, before the terrain is consulted at all. No position and no yaw can
+lift it while check 4 requires meadow.
+
+THE SEARCH EVIDENCE, for completeness. 101,764 views scored; raymarched,
+99 of 400 survivors clear p25/p75/frac together -- those are the ones
+NOT standing in meadow, which is exactly why they then fail meadow
+(best 0.294 marched, and g4b measured 0.4578 rendered).
+
+FOUR INSTRUMENTS, FOUR DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE RENDER, ONE FAMILY. The
+forward-projection predictor under-counted at range; the centre-line
+analytic model predicted p25 93.8 where the render gave 1.2; the
+raymarch predicted 85.9 for the same station. **Every one of them models
+TERRAIN and the render draws a WORLD.** The grass was the missing term in
+all three, and it was in the measured record the whole time --
+species_heights has carried Meadow's placed height and its 50 m cull
+since 2026-09-05.
+
+THE RULE: **when a predictor disagrees with a render, ask what the
+renderer draws that the predictor does not, before touching either the
+predictor's parameters or the thing being predicted.** I tuned scoring
+resolutions, added a concavity gate and re-weighted a prefilter across
+three attempts; none of that could ever have closed a gap whose cause was
+an entire object class absent from the model.
+
+AND THE ONE ABOUT CHECK SETS: **a set of thresholds can be individually
+reasonable and jointly unsatisfiable, and nothing in the set says so.**
+Each of the four is defensible alone. Their conjunction describes a
+camera standing in grass that can see no grass. Worth asking, of any new
+acceptance set, which pairs pull against each other.

+## 2026-09-11p — A READER THAT CANNOT TELL ZERO FROM ABSENT, FIXED AT THE SOURCE
+
+RULED: make the cvar helper return None / refuse on a missing variable,
+probe existence first, and put a fixed control in every batch read.
+
+THE DEFECT, cited rather than inferred. `KismetSystemLibrary.cpp:610-622`:
+
+    float UKismetSystemLibrary::GetConsoleVariableFloatValue(const FString& VariableName)
+    {
+        float Value = 0.0f;
+        IConsoleVariable* Variable = IConsoleManager::Get().FindConsoleVariable(*VariableName);
+        if (Variable) { Value = Variable->GetFloat(); }
+        else { UE_LOGF(..., "Failed to find console variable '%ls'.", ...); }
+        return Value;        // <- 0.0f for a name that does not exist
+    }
+
+It warns to the log and returns the zero. Nothing reaches Python.
+
+THE EXISTENCE TEST, found by enumerating the reflected surface rather
+than guessing: **the STRING getter**. An existing cvar stringifies
+non-empty even when its value is zero; an absent one gives "".
+
+    r.ScreenPercentage   -> '100'   exists
+    r.TonemapperGamma    -> '0'     exists, and genuinely zero
+    r.ExpandGamut        -> ''      ABSENT in 5.8
+    r.TonemapperFilm     -> ''      ABSENT in 5.8
+    <impossible name>    -> ''      absent
+
+RE-READ THROUGH THE FIXED READER: **8 of the 18 names in the Q12 batch do
+not exist.** The old reader called every one of them 0.0. All six
+`r.LocalExposure.*` parameters are among them -- the feature toggle
+`r.LocalExposure` is real (1.0) but its parameters live on the
+PostProcessSettings block, which is where they were eventually read.
+
+THE CONTROLS NOW RUN IN EVERY BATCH, BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the batch
+refuses if either misbehaves: a POSITIVE control that must exist and be
+non-zero (`r.ScreenPercentage` = 100) and a NEGATIVE control that must
+read absent. **The ruling named `r.TonemapperFilm` (default 1) as the
+fixed control and that cvar DOES NOT EXIST in 5.8** -- it would have read
+absent forever and looked like a working control doing nothing. It is
+kept in the batch as a third, documented negative control, and a real
+positive control was added beside it.
+
+THE RULE: **a control that cannot fail is not a control.** The ruled one
+could only ever have returned the same answer; the pair that replaced it
+can each fail in a different direction, which is why the read-back is now
+evidence.
+
+## 2026-09-11q — I IGNORED "COULD NOT LOOK" NINE TIMES BECAUSE THE RAW DUMP HAD WHAT I WANTED
+
+Every payload I wrote this session printed its result behind the marker
+`__RESULT__`. **`ue_exec`'s marker is `__LL__`** (ue_exec.py:131). So
+every one of those runs reported
+
+    COULD NOT LOOK: payload produced no marker.
+    --- raw output (first 3000 chars) ---
+
+and I read the answer out of the raw dump and moved on. Nine payloads.
+The tool was telling me, every time, that my payload did not conform to
+its contract, and I treated the message as cosmetic because the data I
+wanted happened to be visible underneath it.
+
+IT COST A SILENTLY TRUNCATED READ. The cvar batch's JSON is longer than
+3000 characters, so the fallback dump cut it mid-object at exactly
+character 2990 -- `'centage", "string": "100", "exists": true, "value"'`
+-- and the host's json.loads raised. That failure was LOUD and therefore
+cheap. The dangerous version is the one where the truncation lands after
+a syntactically complete prefix and the read silently returns a SUBSET.
+
+Two fixes, and the second matters more:
+  1 every payload now prints `__LL__`, so ue_exec decodes it properly
+    and there is no 3000-char fallback to be truncated by.
+  2 the host no longer parses the marker at all -- ue_exec CONSUMES it
+    and pretty-prints the decoded object, so the host decodes the first
+    JSON object in ue_exec's stdout. Looking for a marker that the tool
+    has already eaten is what made the first draft depend on the
+    fallback path.
+
+THE RULE: **a diagnostic you have decided to ignore is a diagnostic you
+have stopped reading.** "COULD NOT LOOK" is this repo's phrase for "the
+instrument did not report", and I let it become background noise for a
+whole session because the workaround was one grep away. If a tool says it
+could not look and you can see the answer anyway, you are reading a
+fallback path -- and fallback paths have limits the main path does not.

 ## R-GRADE — WHITE BALANCE AND THE QUIET GRADE (RULED 2026-09-10)
 
+### ⭐ LOCKED 2026-09-11b AT 3481.9 K — ON THE SCENE-LINEAR PASS
+
+**RULED BY RYAN.** `white_temp_k` **3481.9**, `white_tint` **0**,
+`temperature_type` white_balance, `warmth_bias_k` 0.
+
+**THE PREVIOUS LOCK AT 3550 K WAS TAKEN ON A COMPRESSED INSTRUMENT.** It
+passed because the DISPLAY-REFERRED card read R/G 1.0230 / B/G 1.0000,
+both inside 0.97–1.03. On the scene-linear pass the SAME grade reads
+**R/G 1.0549 / B/G 1.0014** — R is outside. The filmic curve was
+shrinking the white-balance error exactly as it was shrinking the
+exposure error, and the band was being applied to the shrunken signal.
+**A locked value inherits the class of the instrument that locked it**;
+replacing the instrument re-opens every acceptance it ever passed, not
+only the ones that failed.
+
+    THE STEP, one, by the Planck two-channel method as before
+    r = (R/G)/(B/G) = 1.0534     delta = ln(r)/9454 = +5.51 mired
+    281.69 -> 287.20 mired       3550 -> 3481.9 K
+    AFTER: R/G 1.0307 / B/G 1.0286, excess ratio 1.0534 -> 1.0020
+    TEMPERATURE CONVERGED IN ONE STEP, as predicted once the curve was
+    out of the loop
+
+### THE ~3% TINT RESIDUAL, RECORDED AND NOT CHASED
+
+R and B now sit within **0.2% of each other** and both about **3% above
+G** — `sqrt(R/G x B/G) = 1.0296`. That is the GREEN–MAGENTA axis, not
+temperature: no change to `white_temp_k` can move it, because
+temperature moves R against B and this residual is R and B together
+against G.
+
+**`white_tint` STAYS 0 UNTIL IT HAS A MEASURED SLOPE.** The temperature
+step is derivable because the Planck two-channel slope (9454 K) is a
+physical constant of the illuminant model. `WhiteTint` has no such
+mapping — the engine does not document a relationship between the
+parameter and a channel multiplier — so a step would be a guess dressed
+as a derivation. The way to earn it is the way the exposure slope was
+earned: apply two known tint values, measure the card's G ratio at each,
+and invert the measured response.
+
+Consequence, stated plainly: **R/G 1.0307 is outside the 0.97–1.03 band
+by 0.0007**, against a card std of 0.0046. It is inside the measurement
+noise and outside the band, and it is left that way rather than tuned.
+
 **The rule, RULED BY RYAN 2026-09-10: `white_temp` = the sun's temperature
 (neutral); NEVER above it.** `Scene.h:1505` — WhiteTemp is the temperature
 the scene treats as white, so a WhiteTemp above the sun renders the sun
@@ -18598,6 +18641,30 @@ cause.**
     model was not fitted to
     APPLIED -4.1268  ->  card 0.180072, residual -0.0006 EV   PASS
 
+### ⭐ THE MEASURED-SLOPE SOLVE IS THE EXPOSURE INSTRUMENT (RULED 2026-09-11b)
+
+**The cause of the 0.731 response is Q12 and stays OPEN. The instrument
+does not wait on it.** Candidates, ranked and NOT to be acted on without
+a ruling: scene pre-exposure (`r.EyeAdaptation.PreExposureOverride` /
+`CachedLightingPreExposure`, both verified present in 5.8); MRQ's
+residual colour stages that `bDisableToneCurve` does NOT cover (expand
+gamut, blue correction); and local exposure — **read back once; if the
+project's local-exposure settings are non-default, that is the finding.**
+
+**THE PROCEDURE, and it needs no cause:**
+
+    1 capture --linear at the current comp_ev, read the card
+    2 capture --linear at a second, KNOWN comp_ev offset
+    3 slope = log2(card2/card1) / (ev2 - ev1)
+    4 requested = log2(target/card) / slope   ->   comp_ev += requested
+    5 re-capture and CONFIRM; the residual is recorded, not tuned away
+
+Validated 2026-09-11: slope 0.731 from two step sizes agreeing to 0.009,
+then an extrapolation the model was NOT fitted to landing the card at
+**0.180072 against 0.18 — 0.04%**. An unexplained transfer function that
+is measured and stable is a usable instrument. It is only dangerous when
+it is ASSUMED, which is what "expect exact" was.
+

+## 2026-09-11i — THE SCENE-LINEAR PASS IS NOT LINEAR, AND THE TONEMAP WAS NOT THE WHOLE STORY
+
+The ruling was well-founded and its expected conclusion was wrong, which
+is worth separating carefully.
+
+WELL-FOUNDED: every card reading this project had ever taken was
+post-tonemap, and two independent correction chains had under-delivered
+by about a third (exposure 65.0%, white balance 68% then 40%). Moving the
+measurement to a scene-linear EXR is exactly the right response, and the
+engine setting was verified at the source rather than recalled --
+`MoviePipelineColorSetting::bDisableToneCurve`, "If true the Filmic Tone
+Curve will not be applied... Force Disabled if Open Color IO is enabled."
+Note it lives on the COLOR SETTING, not on the deferred pass node where
+the ruling supposed it would be.
+
+WRONG: "expect exact". With the curve disabled and read back true, I
+asked for a step of **exactly -1.000 EV** and the card moved
+**-0.7266 EV**. A second step of -0.4453 EV delivered -0.3276. Two
+different step sizes, one answer: the chain is a POWER LAW with log-log
+slope **0.731**, not a multiply. The frame maximum agreed with the card
+to within 0.02 EV, so it is the whole image, not the card region.
+
+DISABLING THE CURVE IS NOT A NO-OP, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART. At
+one fixed exposure, the same station rendered with and without the flag
+gave card 0.26489 vs 0.24480 -- an 8% change. So the flag does something,
+and what it does is far too small to explain a 27% shortfall. Something
+else after exposure is compressive: the grade's own `color_contrast` 0.95
+is a power around a pivot and accounts for part of it, and the remainder
+is unattributed. **The tonemap was A cause, not THE cause**, and the
+earlier write-up (LESSONS 2026-09-11f) attributed the whole shortfall to
+it on two data points that shared a confound.
+
+A DIAGNOSTIC I GOT WRONG, AND CAUGHT. To test whether the EXR was really
+linear I sRGB-decoded the PNG from the same render and compared: they
+matched to within 1%, and I first read that as proof the tone curve was
+still on. It proves nothing of the kind. **The PNG writer sRGB-encodes
+whatever buffer it is handed**, so decoding it reproduces the EXR whether
+the curve ran or not. The test had no power in either direction and I had
+already started reasoning from it. What actually settled the question was
+the A/B at fixed exposure above -- two renders differing in one flag.
+
+THE FIX WAS TO MEASURE THE TRANSFER FUNCTION AND INVERT IT, rather than
+iterate against a model that does not hold. From the measured slope, the
+step needed from -3.9626 was -0.1611 EV (giving -4.1237) and the
+independent extrapolation from the -4.9626 probe gave -4.1298 -- agreeing
+to 0.006 EV, which is the model corroborating itself on data it was not
+fitted to. Applied -4.1268: the card landed at **0.180072** against a
+target of 0.18, a residual of -0.0006 EV.
+
+THE RULE: **when a correction under-delivers, characterise the transfer
+before taking another step.** Two points and a straight line in log-log
+cost one extra capture and turned an iteration into a solve. And the
+corollary, which is the part I keep having to learn: a mechanism that
+EXPLAINS a shortfall is not the same as a mechanism that ACCOUNTS for it.
+The tonemap explained the sign and the rough size, and it was responsible
+for 8 points of 27.
+
+## 2026-09-11j — THE DISPLAY-REFERRED CARD WAS FLATTERING THE GRADE, AND R-GRADE WAS LOCKED ON IT
+
+R-GRADE was LOCKED at 3550 K on 2026-09-11 because the card read
+**R/G 1.0230, B/G 1.0000** -- both comfortably inside the ruled
+0.97-1.03. I reported it as landed.
+
+On the scene-linear pass, at the same 3550 K and the same station, the
+same card reads **R/G 1.0549, B/G 1.0014**. R is OUTSIDE the band. The
+grade had not converged; the instrument had compressed the error.
+
+This is the same compression that ate the exposure steps, seen from the
+other side. A tone curve that turns a requested -1.000 EV into -0.727
+will also turn a 5.5% channel excess into a 2.3% one, and 2.3% sits
+inside a band that 5.5% does not. **The acceptance band was being applied
+to a measurement the curve had already shrunk.**
+
+THE CORRECTION, one step, by the same Planck two-channel method as
+before: r = (R/G)/(B/G) = 1.0534, delta = ln(r)/9454 = +5.51 mired,
+281.69 -> 287.20 mired, 3550 -> 3481.9 K. Measured after: **R/G 1.0307,
+B/G 1.0286**, so the excess RATIO went 1.0534 -> 1.0020. The temperature
+axis converged in exactly one step, as the ruling predicted it would once
+the curve was out of the loop.
+
+What remains is not temperature. R and B are now within 0.2% of each
+other and BOTH about 3% above G -- a green-magenta offset, which is the
+`white_tint` axis that R-GRADE already flags as a separate single step
+and the recipe declares at 0. It is left at 0 rather than guessed: UE's
+WhiteTint has no documented mapping to a channel multiplier, so deriving
+that step needs a measured slope the way the temperature step has one.
+
+THE RULE: **a locked value inherits the class of the instrument that
+locked it.** R-GRADE's 3550 was not wrong arithmetic -- it was a correct
+reading of a compressed signal. When an instrument is replaced by a
+better one, every acceptance it ever passed is re-opened, not just the
+ones that failed.
+
+
+## 2026-09-11k — TWO STATION LISTS, AND MRQ RENDERS A MISSING SEQUENCE IN SILENCE
+
+Adding `ground` to `bench_capture.STATIONS` produced three consecutive
+runs that polled an idle engine log for 8 minutes each and wrote no
+frames, no error and exit 0.
+
+ROOT CAUSE: `scripts/payloads/bench_make_stills.py` carries its OWN
+`STATIONS = ["near_ground", "mid_slope", "vista"]`. MRQ renders
+SEQUENCES, not cameras, and `bench_capture` points each job at
+`/Game/Bench/Bench_Still_<station>`. I extended one list and not the
+other, so the job for `ground` named a sequence that does not exist --
+and **MRQ rendered it without complaint**. A job with a null sequence is
+not an error to MRQ; it is a job with nothing in it.
+
+This is NN24 exactly -- "two lists that must agree are one list, badly
+stored" -- and the material-builder skill already carries the same
+lesson from the preflight/assertion split. The test it states is the one
+that would have caught this: *if adding a thing can be done in one place
+and forgotten in another, the structure is wrong, not the author.*
+
+FIXED by making the payload take the list from its caller, so there is
+one declaration. But note what the fix does NOT do: it does not make MRQ
+complain. **A missing sequence is still silent**, so the durable
+protection is the one list, not a check.
+
+DIAGNOSTIC COST, and why it ran to three attempts: I twice read "no
+output" as evidence of a stall when it was my own `| tail` buffering the
+pipe, and the engine log's MRQ line count was cumulative across the
+session so it looked like activity. The run that actually diagnosed it
+was the plain foreground one with no pipeline. **Two of my three
+"observations" were properties of how I was looking.**
+
+## 2026-09-11l — THE DERIVED STATION PREDICTED 405 ROWS AND THE RENDER GAVE 55
+
+`derive_ground_station` searched 220 meadow sites and 1,760 views and
+returned Bench_ground with predicted band heights of **405 and 375 rows**
+at full resolution, against a 160-row floor -- both clearing it by more
+than 2x, with zero canopy in the lower half and meadow weight 1.0.
+
+The rendered frame gives **55 rows and 0**. Depth percentiles from the
+engine's own pass: p50 **9.04 m**, p75 16.24 m, and 85% of the frame
+inside 30 m. Zero sky, so the camera is looking into rising ground as
+intended -- and the rise puts everything CLOSE, not far.
+
+THREE CAUSES, and the third is the one I should have seen:
+
+1. **The scoring resolution lied.** The search counted a row as in-band
+   when >50% of its pixels were, on a 256x144 grid, then multiplied by
+   15 to reach full resolution. At that grid one row IS 15 full-res rows,
+   so the quantisation is the entire margin.
+2. **The raymarch models terrain and TREES, not GRASS.** Meadow is
+   scattered at 120 instances per 10 m^2 and is precisely what fills a
+   standing-height view over meadow. The station was selected for having
+   no trees in the lower half; the grass was never in the model.
+3. **A uniform rise COMPRESSES distance, it does not spread it** -- and
+   I wrote that down myself, in the selftest fixture comment, while
+   fixing the fixture: "even a gentle uniform slope is degenerate here --
+   every distance sits at the same angle atan(s)". Only a CONCAVE profile
+   spreads them. The fixture required concavity; **the search did not**.
+   I encoded the insight in the test and not in the thing being tested.
+
+THE RULE: **a search scores what its model can see, and its model is not
+the renderer.** The selftest proved the scorer ranked a concave site
+above a flat one -- which it did, correctly -- and that was never
+evidence that the winning site would render the way the scorer thought.
+Every one of these derivations needs its prediction CHECKED AGAINST THE
+FRAME before the station is used, and the check is cheap: one capture and
+a depth histogram.
+
+AND THE SHARPER ONE: when a fixture needs a property to work, ask whether
+the SEARCH requires that property too. The fixture's concavity was a
+workaround for a degenerate case, and a degenerate case a fixture has to
+dodge is a case the search will happily select.

+### ⛔ THE CHAIN IS NOT LINEAR, AND "EXPECT EXACT" DOES NOT HOLD

+    APPLIED -4.1268  ->  card 0.180072, residual -0.0006 EV   PASS

+### THE WHITE BALANCE HAD TO BE RE-OPENED

+0.97–1.03 by 0.0007, against a card std of 0.0046.
+
+### REJECTED — ADDITIONS 2026-09-11b
+
+**MEASURING THE CARD OVER THE WHOLE RECORDED RECT.**
+→ SYMPTOM: card std 0.1032 against a median of 0.2435 — 42% on a flat
+grey card — and a card value biased toward whatever surrounds it.
+→ CAUSE: the recorded rect is the projected AABB of a **rotated** card,
+so its corners are background. The full rect is 66,443 px of which only
+23,976 are card; a median over all of it returns the BACKGROUND.
+→ CORRECT: `greycard.inner_rect` (central 60%), IMPORTED by `exr_card`
+rather than restated, so the two cannot drift (NN24). After: std
+0.006231, and both tools report the same 23,976 px.
+
+**`np.nanmax` AS A NON-FINITE GUARD.**
+→ SYMPTOM: a NaN frame sailed through the "frame holds non-finite
+values" check.
+→ CAUSE: `nanmax` IGNORES NaN by construction, so testing its result for
+finiteness is a guard that can never fire — an invariant the failure mode
+preserves.
+→ CORRECT: ask the ARRAY (`np.isfinite(rgb).all()`), not the statistic
+built to hide the answer. Caught by the selftest.
+
+**`frame_max > 1.0` AS THE TEST FOR "IS THIS LINEAR".**
+→ SYMPTOM: a correct linear frame REFUSED at frame max 0.89844.
+→ CAUSE: **exposure is applied before the tone curve**, so at this
+world's −4.1 EV every scene value is scaled by ~0.06 and a linear frame
+can max well below display white. The threshold was assumed.
+→ CORRECT: three states. `max > 1` proves linear (display white cannot be
+exceeded); `max == 1` proves clamped (the pre-ruling EXRs read EXACTLY
+1.00000); `max < 1` is INCONCLUSIVE and defers to the engine read-back,
+refusing if that is absent too.
+
+**sRGB-DECODING THE PNG TO TEST WHETHER THE EXR IS LINEAR.**
+→ SYMPTOM: EXR and decoded PNG matched to 1%, read as proof the curve
+was still on.
+→ CAUSE: the PNG writer sRGB-encodes **whatever buffer it is handed**, so
+decoding it reproduces the EXR either way. The test has no power in
+either direction.
+→ CORRECT: A/B two renders differing in ONE flag at a fixed exposure.
+

+## 2026-09-11g — A STATION DERIVED FOR ONE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT SERVE ANOTHER, TWICE IN ONE SESSION
+
+Brief 3 Task 3 asks for tile-repeat scores in two depth bins, 30-100 m
+and 100-300 m, from the three bench stations. Every cell came back NO
+VERDICT or NO BAND, and the reasons were not about tiling:
+
+    near_ground   sees ground at 30-100 m, but under grass, blueberry
+                  and their shadows -- not the "GROUND ONLY" crop
+                  tiling_score's own docstring requires
+    mid_slope     nearest ground is 581 m; it sees nothing in either bin
+    vista         101 rows in 30-100 m; its 100-300 m crop is no cleaner
+
+The three stations were derived on 2026-09-05 for Brief 1's angular
+budget -- tree subtense, canopy coverage, the detail-threshold ladder.
+They are excellent at that. Nothing about that derivation asked for an
+unoccluded patch of ground at a controlled distance, so nothing about
+them provides one.
+
+THIS IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY. The ruled top-down camera at
+(0, 0, 900000) cm rendered perfectly and could not answer its question
+either (LESSONS 2026-09-11d), and the fix there was to DERIVE a camera
+from what the measurement needed -- clearance for contrast, centre for
+balanced flank populations. The fix here is the same and I have not done
+it: Task 3 needs a purpose-derived ground-only station.
+
+THE RULE: **a measurement station is part of the instrument.** Reusing
+one across measurements is the same error as reusing a tolerance or a
+denominator across specimens -- it carries a premise ("this station
+shows what I need to see") that was established for a different
+question. Bench stations are stable ON PURPOSE, so that frames compare
+across sessions; that stability is exactly what makes them the wrong
+default for a new measure.
+
+AND THE ONE I KEEP PAYING FOR: when a tool's docstring states its
+premise -- "a crop of the frame that is GROUND ONLY" -- that sentence is
+a precondition to CHECK, not context to read past. I had it in front of
+me when I wrote the caller.
+
+## 2026-09-11h — TWO CONFIDENT FAILS THAT WERE THE SEARCH WINDOW'S EDGE
+
+`surface_report` scored the tile repeat by handing `tiling_score` an
+expected on-screen period and reading back its Michelson figure. It
+returned 0.7154 at near_ground and 0.2784 at vista, against CSF
+thresholds of 0.1000 and 0.0393. Two clean FAILs, a plausible story
+(the new 5.03 m tile repeats visibly), and I nearly wrote it up.
+
+The number that stopped it was `period_found_px`, which I had printed
+only for completeness:
+
+    near_ground   found 205.4 px   expected 341.9   window [205.1, 478.7]
+    vista         found  60.0 px   expected  99.7   window [ 59.8, 139.5]
+
+`score` searches a +-40% ring around the expected period and returns the
+strongest point IN the ring. Both maxima sat ON the ring's inner edge --
+205.4 against a 205.1 floor, 60.0 against 59.8. **A maximum on the
+boundary of its own search window is the boundary, not a feature.**
+There was no periodic structure at the tile's period to find.
+
+So where did 0.7154 come from? `michelson = 2 * hi.std() * sqrt(peak) /
+L.mean()`. With `peak` 0.0521 the sqrt term only scales by 0.23, and the
+crop's own high-frequency contrast -- foliage, blueberry, hard shadows
+at a 12 deg sun -- carried the rest. The statistic was reporting how
+BUSY the crop is, and a busy crop is not a tiled one.
+
+ROOT CAUSE: I read a composite statistic without its component. `peak`
+was in the same returned dict the whole time, 0.0521 against ~1.0 for a
+genuinely tiled crop and ~0.01 for noise -- it said "no repeat" plainly.
+
+THE SHAPE IS ALREADY IN R-LAYERS REJECTED. The p90 gradient that
+returned EXACTLY sqrt(2)/2 for two different blends was pinned by
+quantisation; this peak was pinned by a search window. Both are
+statistics reporting their own limit and being read as the world.
+
+THE RULE: **a bounded search returns its bound when it finds nothing.
+Before believing an extremum, check whether it is sitting on the fence
+you built for it.** The guard is cheap -- compare the found location
+against the window's ends -- and it is now in `surface_report`, which
+reports NO VERDICT rather than a FAIL it cannot support.

+## R-TILING — GROUND TILE SIZE IS DERIVED FROM THE CAMERA (2026-09-11)
+
+**Brief 3 Task 3 step 1. `scripts/texel_budget.py`, `scripts/surface_report.py`.**
+
+### THE RULE
+
+    texels_per_m_needed = px_per_deg * (180/pi) / near_m
+    tiling_m            = texture_resolution / texels_per_m_needed
+
+At hfov 90, 3840x2160 (px_per_deg 42.67) and a near attend distance of
+3 m: **814.9 texels/m**, so a 4096 albedo spans **5.03 m** at ~1 texel
+per render pixel. Larger blurs up close; smaller repeats sooner.
+
+    tex 1024 -> 1.26 m    tex 2048 -> 2.51 m
+    tex 4096 -> 5.03 m    tex 8192 -> 10.05 m
+
+**APPLIED 2026-09-11** to all three layers (every bound surface is 4096
+square per the vendor manifest). `macro_tiling_m` 188.0 = **37.4x**,
+inside the ruled 20-50x band. Previous values: Snow/Rock 4.0 (implies
+1024 texels/m at 3 m -- 26% short of what the camera resolves), Grass
+2.1 with macro 98.7.
+
+### WHERE THE TILE IS EVEN VISIBLE
+
+`repeat_cpd = d / (tile_m * 57.3)`, and the eye's sensitive band is
+1-8 cpd. For a 5.03 m tile that is **288 m to 2306 m**. Both of Brief
+3's bins (30-100, 100-300 m) sit at or BELOW the bottom of that band --
+0.125 cpd at 36 m, 0.428 cpd at 123 m. The brief's bins are where a tile
+this size is least detectable; the bins that matter start at ~288 m.
+
+### STOCHASTIC TILING EXISTS IN 5.8 — VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED
+
+`/Engine/Functions/Engine_MaterialFunctions01/Texturing/`:
+
+    Texture_Bombing            Texture_Bombing_POM
+    TextureBomb_SingleSample   TextureBomb_SingleSample_POM
+    Parallax_For_Bomb
+
+**There is NO hex-tiling function in 5.8** — texture bombing is the
+available stochastic path, and `TextureBomb_SingleSample` is the variant
+that does not multiply texture fetches. NOT INTEGRATED: it carries GPU
+cost, and no measurement yet shows a repeat that needs removing.
+
+### ⛔ THE BENCH STATIONS CANNOT MEASURE THIS, AND THAT IS THE RESULT
+
+`surface_report` over `target_task3tile` returned **NO VERDICT on every
+cell**:
+
+    station      bin m     rows   dist m   peak   found px   window
+    near_ground  30-100    1007     36.0  0.0521    205.4   [205.1, 478.7]
+    near_ground  100-300      0      --      --        --   no ground in bin
+    mid_slope    30-100       0      --      --        --   no ground in bin
+    mid_slope    100-300      0      --      --        --   no ground in bin
+    vista        30-100     101      --      --        --   no ground in bin
+    vista        100-300    429    123.4  0.3147     60.0   [59.8, 139.5]
+
+Two independent reasons, both measured:
+
+1. **No station sees clean ground in these bins.** near_ground's ground
+   at 30-100 m is under grass, blueberry and their shadows; mid_slope's
+   nearest ground is 581 m; vista's 30-100 m band is 101 rows.
+   `tiling_score`'s own premise is "a crop that is GROUND ONLY", and it
+   does not hold at any bench station.
+2. **Where a crop exists, the peak is PINNED AT THE SEARCH WINDOW'S
+   EDGE** -- 205.4 px against a 205.1 floor, 60.0 against 59.8. `score`
+   returns the strongest point in a +-40% ring, so a maximum on the ring
+   is the WINDOW's boundary, not a feature. Same shape as the p90
+   gradient that returned sqrt(2)/2 for two different blends.
+
+**The michelson figures (0.7154, 0.2784) are NOT tiling.** That statistic
+is `2*std*sqrt(peak)/mean`; with peak 0.05 it is carried almost entirely
+by the crop's own contrast -- foliage and shadow. Reported against the
+CSF threshold it would have read FAIL twice, and both would have been
+artefacts.
+
+What the numbers DO suggest, short of a verdict: peak 0.0521 at
+near_ground is near the noise floor (a genuinely tiled crop scores ~1.0,
+aperiodic noise ~0.01), so there is no detectable repeat at the tile
+period. Closing it properly needs a **purpose-derived ground-only
+station**, the same way the top-down confirmation shot did.
+
+### REJECTED
+
+**A CROP CHOSEN BY "NO SKY IN THE COLUMN".**
+→ SYMPTOM: bands reporting representative distances outside their own
+bin -- the 30-100 m band came back at 19.3 m, the 100-300 m at 6.6 m.
+→ CAUSE: the widest sky-free column run selects whatever fills the frame
+vertically (a near trunk, a close slope). "No sky" is not "at this
+distance".
+→ CORRECT: choose columns by IN-BIN FRACTION (>= 0.7), take the longest
+CONTIGUOUS row run rather than first-to-last, and refuse the crop if
+under half of it is actually in the bin.
+
+**A `michelson` READ WITHOUT ITS `peak`.**
+→ SYMPTOM: two confident FAILs against a CSF threshold.
+→ CAUSE: the statistic multiplies crop contrast by `sqrt(peak)`, so a
+high-contrast aperiodic crop scores high with no repeat present.
+→ CORRECT: check `period_found_px` against the search window first. A
+boundary-pinned peak means NO VERDICT, whatever the michelson says.

+## 2026-09-11e — I HAND-ROLLED A MEASUREMENT THAT HAD A TOOL, AND THE NUMBER REACHED A RULING
+
+Asked whether the top-down frame's whiteness was albedo or exposure, I
+noticed the 18% grey card sitting in the vista frame and measured it:
+loaded `_verify/bench/greycard_regions.json`, took the rect, averaged
+the linear luma inside it, got **0.33964**, and reported a terrain/card
+ratio of 1.36. The reasoning was right and the conclusion it supported
+was right.
+
+The number was not. `scripts/greycard.py --measure --station vista`
+returns **card_luma 0.30195 and verdict FAIL** — the vista card sits on
+a SHADED flank (it is near the vista camera, which stands on the flank
+the snow is on), so it is lit by sky alone: `wb_ratio_B` 1.354 and
+`card_luma_std` 0.0669 against near_ground's 1.000 and 0.0157. The tool
+has an acceptance. My rect average had none, so there was nothing for it
+to fail.
+
+That number then propagated. I reported it; the next ruling said
+"compensation_ev corrected by log2(measured/0.18) (currently ~-0.9
+stops)" — and -0.9163 EV is exactly `log2(0.33964/0.18)`. The correction
+from the VALID card is **-1.5943 EV**. A measurement that skipped its
+own gate set a parameter in a ruling, and the only reason it did not
+ship is that the same tool got run properly one step later.
+
+ROOT CAUSE is the operating loop's step (a), and specifically its
+motivating case, which this repeats almost exactly. The rule reads:
+"STEP (a) IS A SEARCH, NOT A RECALL. `scripts/` gets LISTED before any
+ad-hoc payload touches the editor." I did list `scripts/` this session —
+twice — and I had `greycard.py` in front of me when I read its header to
+find the regions file. I used the tool's DATA and skipped the tool.
+
+THE GAP IN THE LESSON, which is the part worth keeping. Step (a) is
+written about PROCEDURES — "do not invent a way to do a thing that has a
+recipe". It did not fire here because I was not inventing a procedure, I
+was reading a file. But `greycard_regions.json` is not data, it is the
+INTERMEDIATE STATE of an instrument, and taking an instrument's
+intermediate state and finishing the computation by hand discards
+everything the instrument does after that point — which, for any
+instrument worth having, is the acceptance.
+
+THE RULE: **an instrument's output includes its VERDICT, and a number
+lifted from its intermediates is not its output.** If a tool of record
+exists, run it; if you only want part of it, you still want the part
+that says whether the number is admissible.
+
+AND THE SECOND-ORDER ONE: this is why a measured number that travels to
+Ryan must carry the tool that produced it. Had I written "greycard
+--measure says 0.33964" the discrepancy would have been visible the
+moment the tool was run for real, because it never says that.
+
+## 2026-09-11f — THE TONEMAP UNDER-DELIVERS CORRECTIONS BY A THIRD, IN EVERY DOMAIN
+
+Applying the ruled exposure step: `compensation_ev` -1.923 -> -3.5173, a
+requested -1.5943 EV. The card moved 0.54349 -> 0.26489, which is
+**-1.0369 EV delivered: 65.0% efficiency.** The target band [0.162,
+0.198] was missed, residual +0.5574 EV.
+
+This was predicted, and predicted in writing — `exposure._solve_caveat`
+in the recipe has said since 2026-08-14 that the method "CANNOT CONVERGE
+BY CONSTRUCTION" because the decoded PNG is post-tonemap while the
+target is a pre-tonemap scene value, and it measured a 0.137 EV step
+yielding -5.4% where linear arithmetic said -9.1%. It was marked OPEN and
+nothing had been done with it.
+
+What is new is that **the same shortfall now has a number in a second,
+unrelated domain.** The white-balance chain measured 68% then 40% per
+step (LESSONS 2026-09-11), and that was written up as a property of the
+von-Kries-style correction — "the chain is not von Kries". It is now
+clear that was the wrong attribution, or at least an incomplete one:
+white balance and exposure share exactly one thing, the filmic curve
+they are both measured through, and both under-deliver by roughly a
+third. The tonemap is the common cause.
+
+That reframes a finding I recorded three days ago. I am not retracting
+the von-Kries measurement — the numbers stand — but its EXPLANATION was
+scoped too narrowly, because it had one domain and no control. Two
+domains is not proof either; it is the second point on a line.
+
+THE RULE: **when a correction is measured through a non-linear display
+transform, its step efficiency is a property of the TRANSFORM, and you
+will meet the same number again in an unrelated parameter.** Budget
+steps. Do not expect a formula to land in one.
+
+AND THE METHODOLOGICAL ONE: a finding explained by a mechanism specific
+to its own domain should be held loosely until it has been looked for
+somewhere that mechanism does not apply. I had a single domain and wrote
+a domain-specific cause.

    5.6% of distance per LSB (haze_metrics.py:68), so normals reconstructed
    from it are quantisation. The tell was a sensitivity check, not an
    assertion -- reading the pass as view-Z vs radial moved a shaded-octant
    population from 41 px to 517,913 px. Both probes discarded; the numbers
    they produced are NOT reported.
    
    LESSONS 2026-09-11d: a shot whose every read-back is exact can still be

+## 2026-09-11c — AN INSTRUMENT THAT LEFT ITS CLASS, AND THE TELL THAT CAUGHT IT
+
+Asked to confirm from a render that the derived snow sits on the flank
+the sun misses, I tried to measure aspect from the captured passes. The
+vista frame carries a beauty pass and a scene-depth pass, so the obvious
+move is to reconstruct world positions from the depth, take normals from
+them, and bin snow by aspect octant. I built that. It ran. It produced
+numbers.
+
+The numbers were garbage, and the thing that said so was not a failed
+assertion -- it was a SENSITIVITY CHECK I had added almost as an
+afterthought. `SceneDepth` in UE is view-space Z, but I was not certain,
+so I computed the whole thing twice: once reading the pass as depth
+along the view axis, once as radial distance. If the octant verdict
+survived both, the ambiguity did not matter.
+
+It did not survive. The shaded-octant population went from **41 px** to
+**517,913 px** -- four orders of magnitude -- on a choice that changes
+each sample's range by at most 15%.
+
+ROOT CAUSE, at a number rather than a feeling. `scripts/haze_metrics.py:68`:
+the pass is 8-bit and LOG-encoded, `encoded = log2(max(depth_cm,1)) / 20`.
+One 8-bit step is therefore a FACTOR of `2^(20/255) = 1.0559` -- 5.6% of
+the distance, whatever the distance is. 5.6 m at 100 m. 56 m at 1 km.
+112 m at 2 km. A normal is a DIFFERENCE of neighbouring positions, so
+that quantisation is not a small error on the normal, it IS the normal.
+The reprojection of the weightmap through the same camera came out in
+vertical streaks for the same reason, which is what a 5.6% radial
+quantisation looks like when you draw it.
+
+The instrument was not broken. It was CORRECT, and it was calibrated for
+a different specimen: R-DEPTHBIN built that pass to sort pixels into
+distance bins of 100/300/1000/3000/8000 m, where 5.6% is irrelevant. I
+carried it to a geometry question and it silently left its class. This
+is verification-practice's first rule -- state the instrument's PREMISE
+and check it transfers -- and the premise here was never written down as
+a premise, only as an encoding.
+
+WHAT I DID NOT DO: report the numbers with a caveat. A failed
+measurement reports that it FAILED, never the number the broken
+measurement produced. Both probes were discarded, and the vista frame
+was reported as unable to answer the question.
+
+THE REPLACEMENT uses the pass ONLY as a sky/not-sky bit -- a silhouette
+needs no depth precision -- and compares that silhouette against a
+ray-march of the heightmap. `scripts/heightmap_orientation_check.py`,
+R-ORIENT.
+
+THE RULE: an encoding is a premise. When a pass is quantised
+MULTIPLICATIVELY, write its per-LSB error next to its decoder, in the
+units a caller will care about, because the caller who misuses it will
+not be the one who wrote it.
+
+AND THE SECOND-ORDER RULE, which is the one I want to keep: the check
+that caught this was not a test, it was computing the answer twice under
+two readings of an ambiguity I had NOT resolved. When you are unsure of
+a datum, do not pick the likely one and move on -- carry both and see
+whether the conclusion cares. If it does, you have found the thing you
+were unsure about, before it found you.
+
+## 2026-09-11d — THE CONFIRMATION SHOT THAT RENDERED PERFECTLY AND PROVED NOTHING
+
+Ryan ruled a top-down frame at `(0, 0, 900000)` cm to read snow against
+the lit and shaded flanks directly in screen space, and then to R-lock.
+
+The shot succeeded by every signal a capture tool reports. Frame on disk
+in 4 seconds. `max_loc_err_cm 0.0`, `max_rot_err_deg 0.0`. The whole
+8129 m world inside the frame, its square edge landing within 8% of
+where the forward projection put it. Nothing to report as a failure.
+
+And its terrain luma std was **0.0334** over 16,524,225 projected
+texels. At 9 km the aerial perspective flattens this world below what
+8-bit quantisation carries; there is no binning that recovers a signal
+already gone. The frame cannot answer the question in EITHER direction
+-- it is not evidence against the layers, it is not evidence for them.
+
+R-CITYSHOT step 6 is what fired: "check the frame is tonally
+non-trivial BEFORE reading anything into it". Written after a different
+failure, it caught this one, which is the only real test of a recipe
+step. The whole-frame std was 0.0206.
+
+THE FIX WAS TO DERIVE THE CAMERA INSTEAD OF ACCEPTING ONE. Altitude
+from CLEARANCE over the terrain (1000 m) rather than from covering the
+world; centre chosen by maximising the SCARCER flank class, because a
+window rich in one flank and empty of the other cannot compare them.
+That returned `(29800, 73500, 169641.7)` cm with 365,717 shaded and
+364,936 lit band texels -- balanced to 0.2%, which no hand-placed
+camera would have hit -- and terrain luma std 0.2134, 6.4x the ruled
+camera's. On that frame the measurement ran: at the same altitude and
+the same flank class, snow renders brighter than bare in 5 of 5 bins.
+
+I kept BOTH frames. The ruled camera's artefact is the evidence that
+the ruled camera cannot answer, and deleting it would leave the
+deviation looking like a preference.
+
+TWO RULES.
+
+A camera is a MEASUREMENT PARAMETER and derives like any other. "Put it
+high enough to see everything" optimises for coverage; the measurement
+needed contrast and balanced populations, and those pull the other way.
+
+And the one that generalises past cameras: **a shot whose every
+read-back is exact can still be worthless, because read-backs verify
+that the instrument was AIMED, never that it can SEE.** Every field in
+that sidecar was a true measurement of the request. None of them was a
+measurement of the frame.

+## R-SNOWFLANK — CONFIRMING A DERIVED MASK'S DIRECTION (LOCKED 2026-09-11)
+
+**`scripts/hillshade_snow_check.py`.** Promoted from a scratch probe and
+ruled of record 2026-09-11.
+
+**THE RULE THIS ENFORCES: a derived mask's FRAME is an input, and it
+must be checked by something that does not share it.** `derive_layer_weights`
+places snow by `cos(aspect - shaded_rad)` from its own
+`shaded_aspect_rad`; any check calling either verifies the arithmetic
+against itself and passes however the axis is bound. That is exactly the
+2026-09-11 defect (LESSONS 2026-09-11b) and its selftest passed
+throughout.
+
+### THE PROCEDURE
+
+    python scripts/hillshade_snow_check.py --selftest
+    python scripts/hillshade_snow_check.py --out <json>
+
+Computes a STANDARD hillshade -- `max(0, N.L)` from heightmap gradients
+and the recipe's sun -- importing NOTHING from the derivation except the
+constant `SNOW_ASPECT_HALF_M`. `derive()` is imported by the SELFTEST
+ONLY, to manufacture a known-good specimen.
+
+**THE DATUM.** `lighting.sun.azimuth_deg` is the light actor's YAW, the
+direction light TRAVELS; the sun sits at azimuth-180, so the horizontal
+part of L NEGATES. Reading it as the sun's bearing inverts the verdict.
+
+### THE THRESHOLDS ARE DERIVED, NOT TUNED
+
+Scoring runs in `snow_base +- 125 m`, the altitudes the two flanks' snow
+lines straddle. The lines are 250 m apart and the feather is 120 m wide,
+so the transitions DO NOT OVERLAP and the lit flank cannot reach
+snow > 0.5 inside the band at all.
+
+    lit frac(snow>0.5)   < 0.05   the sliver non-overlap predicts
+    shaded/lit ratio     >= 4.0   conservative against "unbounded"
+    slope floor          10 deg   flat ground has no aspect to score
+
+### MEASURED (alpine_8k, sun az 285 / el 12)
+
+    mean snow weight     SHADED 0.2675   LIT 0.0146
+    frac(snow>0.5)       SHADED 0.2679   LIT 0.0067   ratio 40.22
+    band 605-855 m, 11,777,933 px (4,359,422 shaded / 3,031,823 lit)
+    VERDICT PASS
+
+### THE SELFTEST IS THREE DIRECTIONS
+
+    1 PASS   snow derived for az 285 passes against az 285's hillshade
+    2 BLOCK  flip the sun 180 deg -> FAIL (0.2673 <-> 0.2673, an exact
+             mirror); flip BOTH sun and derivation -> PASS again, so
+             the failure is the AXIS and not the specimen
+    3 BLOCK WHEN BROKEN  NaN heightmap, NaN weightmap, shape mismatch
+             and flat terrain each REFUSE with a reason instead of
+             returning a number
+
+### WHAT IT CANNOT SEE
+
+It shares the heightmap's row/col frame with the derivation, so a
+mirrored import flips both together and both keep agreeing -- ONE
+measurement, not two (NN0). Close that with **R-ORIENT**. It also says
+nothing about whether the MATERIAL samples the map; that is
+`topdown_flank_check`, R-LAYERS strand 3.
+
+## R-ORIENT — IS THE HEIGHTMAP ORIENTED AS THE ENGINE IMPORTED IT (LOCKED 2026-09-11)
+
+**`scripts/heightmap_orientation_check.py`.** The only instrument in
+this project that does not share the heightmap premise, because its
+reference is a RENDER.
+
+### THE PROCEDURE
+
+    python scripts/heightmap_orientation_check.py --selftest
+    python scripts/heightmap_orientation_check.py --station vista \
+        --frames _verify/bench/<date>/<tag> --out <json>
+
+Ray-march the heightmap from a bench station; compare the SKYLINE with
+the engine's, taken from the scene-depth pass's sky ceiling. A
+silhouette needs no depth PRECISION, only which pixels are sky.
+
+**⛔ DO NOT RECONSTRUCT GEOMETRY FROM THE DEPTH PASS.** Measured
+2026-09-11: 8-bit LOG depth, `2^(20/255)` per step = **5.6% of distance
+per LSB** -- 5.6 m at 100 m, 56 m at 1 km, 112 m at 2 km. Correct for
+R-DEPTHBIN's distance bins; useless for positions or normals. The tell:
+reading the same pass as view-Z rather than radial moved a shaded-octant
+population from **41 px to 517,913 px**. This module uses the pass ONLY
+as a sky/not-sky bit.
+
+### THE FOUR-MAPPING TABLE IS THE POWER ANALYSIS, EVERY RUN
+
+Scoring one hypothesis alone reports a number with no scale -- is IoU
+0.77 good? Only the three WRONG mappings can say. A run where a control
+scores as well reports **NO POWER**, never a pass.
+
+    ours (row->+Y, col->+X)   sky 0.4684   IoU 0.7727   agree 0.8641
+    row flipped               sky 0.2645   IoU 0.4473   agree 0.6731
+    col flipped               sky 0.0654   IoU 0.1105   agree 0.4740
+    transposed                sky 0.0000   IoU 0.0000   agree 0.4087
+    margin 0.3254 vs required 0.2057  ->  PASS (vista, 2026-09-11)
+
+### THE MARGIN IS DERIVED PER RUN
+
+The march and the engine disagree for a KNOWN reason -- the engine
+streams and HLODs distant terrain, so it sees MORE sky than the march
+(0.5913 vs 0.4684). That systematic, spread over the union, bounds the
+IoU it could move: `required = |sky_engine - sky_ours| / union`. The
+true mapping must beat the best control by more than that, so a
+systematic-sized error cannot manufacture the verdict.
+
+### REJECTED
+
+**A SINGLE-HYPOTHESIS SCORE.** → SYMPTOM: "IoU 0.77, looks good."
+→ CAUSE: no scale. → CORRECT: run all four mappings every invocation.
+
+**A FIXED MARGIN.** → SYMPTOM: a threshold that survives review because
+nobody can say where it came from. → CORRECT: derive it from the run's
+own streaming systematic, and print both numbers.
+

+## 2026-09-11b — AN ASPECT AXIS BOUND TO A MAP EDGE, NOT TO THE SUN
+
+derive_layer_weights' snow line was `base - 125*cos(aspect)` with the
+comment "0 = map +Y (north)". The brief's own formula says
+`cos(aspect - north)` "at the recipe's sun azimuth" -- and the physical
+driver is which flank the SUN MISSES, not which way the map's Y axis
+points. Nothing in the level binds +Y to the shaded direction: with
+sun.azimuth_deg 285 (the light's TRAVEL yaw, so the sun sits at 105),
+the shaded flank faces ~(0.26, -0.97) -- almost exactly -Y, i.e. the
+code was biasing snow onto the LIT flanks.
+
+The selftest passed throughout, and correctly: it asserted N > S against
+an independent geometric predicate and would have caught any sign flip
+INSIDE the formula. What it could not catch was the formula's FRAME
+being unbound to the world -- a selftest verifies the arithmetic it is
+given, never the premise the arithmetic is about.
+
+Fixed by derivation, not by a constant: shaded_aspect_rad(azimuth)
+converts the light's travel yaw into the aspect frame, main() reads
+lighting.sun.azimuth_deg, and the sidecar records both. The selftest
+gained a direction the old one structurally could not have: FLIP THE
+SUN AND THE SNOWY FLANK MUST FLIP. Also folded in from the same audit:
+the snow floor now comes from the recipe's Snow band instead of a
+duplicated local constant (pipeline rule 2), and `flow` is declared
+RESERVED rather than loaded, passed and claimed in the sidecar while
+nothing read it (rule 10).
+
+THE RULE: a derived mask's FRAME is an input like any other. If a
+formula says "north", something in the recipe must say which way north
+is -- or the formula must compute it from something that does.

+## R-LAYERS — EIGHT DERIVED LAYER WEIGHTS (Brief 3 Task 2, 2026-09-11)
+
+**Nothing painted.** `derive_layer_weights` computes eight weights from
+the heightmap, the Gaea deposition export and the PLACED foliage, with
+precedence (snow > rock > scree > forest_floor > wet_shore > dirt_path
+> gravel > meadow) normalised so they sum to 1. Selftest: two decoupled
+specimens, 16 checks, including FLIP THE SUN AND THE SNOWY FLANK FLIPS.
+
+### THE DERIVATIONS
+
+    snow          smoothstep over height above a per-aspect snow line,
+                  line = recipe Snow floor - 125*cos(aspect - SHADED),
+                  x a slope term. SHADED comes from
+                  lighting.sun.azimuth_deg (the light's travel yaw), NOT
+                  a map axis -- see REJECTED
+    rock          smoothstep 29->35 deg
+    scree         20-32 deg AND a >40 deg cell within 60 m that is
+                  HIGHER (the debris fell from above); exact windowed
+                  max via a sparse table, not a shift stack
+    forest_floor  canopy COVER from the placed instances (crown disks,
+                  crown-radius blur), smoothstep 0.15->0.45. UNITS READ
+                  AND RECORDED: the brief's "0.3 crowns/m2" is crown-AREA
+                  COVER -- 0.3 TREES/m2 is 3,000 stems/ha against this
+                  world's measured 24.7
+    wet_shore     DECLARED ZERO (needs Brief 4's water level)
+    dirt_path     DECLARED ZERO (no path mask; streets are ACTORS)
+    gravel        deposition, gated off steep slopes and below the snow
+    meadow        the remainder
+
+Coverage: snow 9.92, rock 42.30, scree 11.97, forest_floor 10.63,
+gravel 0.52, meadow 24.65% (wet/path 0).

+### THE MATERIAL SIDE (schema v1.25)
+
+`material.forest_floor.driver = "weightmap_alpha"`: the tint mask is the
+weightmap's ALPHA -- the canopy-derived weight -- replacing the height
+band. The band said "trees live at these altitudes"; the alpha says "a
+tree stands HERE". `height_m` alongside the driver REFUSES (two masks
+for one tint). The weightmap import admits RGBA (narrowed, not dropped:
+8-bit and square still hold) and stays uncompressed, so the alpha
+cannot be block-mixed away.

+## 2026-09-11 — THE GRADE CHAIN IS NOT VON KRIES, MEASURED
+
+Brief 3 Task 1 stepped WhiteTemp toward the grey card's neutral with the
+Planck two-channel mired slope (9454 K), the textbook von-Kries move.
+Measured on the card, target class:
+
+    5200 K   ln(residual ratio) 0.5301
+    4026 K   0.1719   (56.1 mired applied -> 68% of theoretical removed)
+    3751 K   0.1031   (18.2 mired applied -> 38% of theoretical removed)
+
+Two findings. First, the chain under-corrects the slope -- the
+atmosphere spectrum, the sun disc/sky mix on a tilted card, and the
+filmic tonemap all sit between WhiteTemp and the pixel, and none is a
+blackbody diagonal transform. Second, the EFFICIENCY ITSELF FELL between
+steps, so even a measured-efficiency extrapolation is optimistic near
+neutral -- the tonemap is most compressive exactly where the residual
+is smallest (the same compression the exposure _solve_caveat documents).
+BRIEF 3.7's "one step gets within 3%" assumed a von-Kries chain; the
+assumption was worth one sentence to test and two capture cycles to
+falsify. Ryan ruled a final step to the extrapolated ~3550 K; R-GRADE
+locks at the measured outcome either way, residual recorded. The
+general rule: A CORRECTION FORMULA'S CONVERGENCE RATE IS ITSELF A
+MEASURED QUANTITY -- budget steps by the measured rate, not the
+formula's promise.
+

+## 2026-09-10c — LESSON 12.10 RECURRED, AND THE GAP WAS THE GUARD'S SCOPE
+
+The first clouds apply failed with `Could not load Python file '<engine
+dir>/<the whole script>'` — byte-for-byte the 12.10 failure. Root cause
+identical (PythonScriptPlugin.cpp:813-898: ExecuteFile mode FindFirsts
+the substring dot-p-y across the whole command; :872 accepts it as a
+pathname when whitespace follows). The offending text was the NEW
+_task6 recipe note: "cloud_mi_probe" with its extension, followed by a
+space. The morning run of the same script had succeeded because the
+payload's only prior occurrence ("capture" dot-p-y ":273") is followed
+by a colon, which :872 rejects — one character of punctuation was the
+difference between working and not.
+
+### WHY THE EXISTING LESSON DID NOT PREVENT IT (operating loop e)
+
+12.10's rule was ratified and a guard was built — and the guard was
+OPT-IN PER TOOL. make_landscape_material, make_mesh_lods, push_heightmap
+and save_level adopted it; apply_lighting never did. And the offending
+string did not come from payload authorship at all: it came from RECIPE
+PROSE, interpolated into the payload at run time. A rule addressed to
+"payload authors" cannot fire on a recipe note written days later by
+someone documenting provenance — which is exactly what _task6 was.
+
+### THE FIX IS AT THE CHOKE POINT
+
+apply_lighting._run now guards the COMPOSED source (the only place that
+sees template + interpolated recipe together) via the shared
+_guard_payload; the payload template and the recipe's lighting prose are
+swept of the extension. ue_exec is immune BY CONSTRUCTION — it stages
+payloads as real .py files and sends the path. The general rule,
+sharpened: **a content guard must sit where the content is COMPOSED, not
+where it is authored** — an interpolation site widens the set of authors
+to everyone who can write a string that reaches it.

+## R-DEPTHBIN — DEPTH IS THE INSTRUMENT, FOR DISTANCE AND FOR SKY (2026-09-10)
+
+R-FOG's REJECTED section referenced this recipe before it existed; it is
+now written. One depth pass per station carries two instruments:
+
+**1. DISTANCE BINS** (`haze_metrics.py`, ruled 2026-09-09): aerial
+perspective binned by TRUE distance, never by image rows. Decode:
+
+    encoded = log2(max(depth_cm,1)) / 20  (material /Game/Bench/M_SceneDepth)
+    depth_m = 2 ** (srgb_to_linear(px/255) * 20) / 100    CEILING 10485.76 m
+
+The sRGB step is measured, not assumed (3.28 m vs geometry's 3.36 m;
+linear reads 121.5 m). Capture with `bench_capture --depth`.
+
+**2. THE SKY MASK** (RULED BY RYAN 2026-09-10, replacing the colour
+`SKY_BAND` in featureless / haze / dE): sky = tile MEDIAN depth at or
+beyond the ceiling. `bench_capture.sky_mask_from_depth`; consumers
+`featureless_split(..., depth_path=)` and `fog_vs_sky --depth`. The
+sidecar records `sky_mask: depth|colour`; a tile-grid mismatch REFUSES
+(ValueError) rather than falling back to colour. haze_metrics needed no
+change — it excluded sky by depth from birth.
+
+Depth is GEOMETRY: one pass per station serves every lighting-era frame
+of that station. Two independent mid_slope depth captures agree 1.0000
+tile-for-tile (`sky_rejudge_depth.json` checks block).

+## 2026-09-10 — APPLIED BUT NOT SAVED: EVERY MEASUREMENT OUTLIVED THE WORLD IT MEASURED
+
+### WHAT HAPPENED
+
+The overnight close after Task 5 (commit 0a04be1c) hit the R-EDITOR-CLOSE
+dirty-modal deadlock, and the machine then died. The four lighting packages
+the Brief-2 tasks had mutated — Lighting_alpine_8k_Fog, _SkyLight, _SkyAtmo,
+_PostProcess — were dirty and NEVER SAVED. `PackageRestoreData.json` names
+all four (preserved with autosaves in `_trash/autosaves_launch_20260910161826/`).
+
+On relaunch the world read back PRE-BRIEF-2 on every axis: fog
+0.0015/0.03431/150000 cm against the recipe's derived 0.00416/0.019324/0;
+sky light 1.8 against 1.0; Mie 0.003996 against 0.01; WhiteTemp 6500
+against the grade block. The recipe, the _verify measurements and the
+commits all carried Tasks 1–5; the world carried none of them.
+
+### ROOT CAUSE, AT A LINE
+
+`apply_lighting.py:30-32` (before today): "Does not save the level — saving
+is the operator's call, and an unsaved lighting pass is trivially reverted
+by reloading." The property advertised as a convenience IS the defect: for
+five sessions the pass was never meant to be revertible, and no step in the
+task loop (apply → read back → capture → measure → commit) ever owned the
+save. Rule 12 was satisfied to the letter — applied AND read back — and the
+read-back proved only the IN-MEMORY state. Nothing proved persistence,
+because nothing attempted it.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**Recipe-derived actors that are applied but not saved make every
+measurement outlive the world it measured.** A capture's provenance chain is
+recipe → applied actor → saved package; break the last link and the artefact
+refers to a world that stops existing at the next editor exit. Apply, read
+back, SAVE THE TOUCHED PACKAGES, and commit them — one unit, owned by the
+applying tool, not by session hygiene. `apply_lighting.py` now does this
+(RULED BY RYAN 2026-09-10); the spec altitude is RECIPES R-LIGHTSAVE.
+
+Related: save_tagged_actors.py documents the sibling trap (applied but not
+even DIRTY, 0-dirty saves that write nothing) — the save must be
+only_if_is_dirty=False and the verdict must come from the filesystem.
+
+### AUDIT LOG 2026-09-10 — apply_lighting.py R-LIGHTSAVE
+
+First audit: FIX. Set-difference save verdict was blind to pre-dirty files
+(a failed-commit re-run would mask its own exit-5) and the no-change branch
+asserted on-disk existence it never checked. Braces, bindings, commit
+containment, API names all clean. F1 (existence check, exit 5 on missing)
+and F2 (pending-commit routing via fs_after) corrected by the main agent;
+re-audit verified both: exit 0 now requires clean dirty-state + files exist
++ git-clean. PASS — cleared for first execution.

+## R-LIGHTSAVE — APPLIED LIGHTING IS SAVED LIGHTING (RULED 2026-09-10)
+
+**`apply_lighting.py` saves the packages of every actor it touches (Sun,
+Fog, SkyLight, SkyAtmo, PostProcess) after the read-back, and the run
+commits them.** Apply → read back → save → commit is ONE unit owned by the
+tool; "saving is the operator's call" is the rejected design below.
+
+The save is bounded to the run's own actors (never a sweep of all dirty
+packages — the 2026-08-24 city save swept the hero rig into the world),
+uses `set_dirty_flag` + `save_loaded_assets(only_if_is_dirty=False)` (the
+save_tagged_actors.py pattern: component edits can leave 0 dirty), and

+## 2026-09-09e — THE SKY CLASSIFIER IS CALIBRATED AGAINST THE STATE THE BRIEF IS TRYING TO CHANGE
+
+Brief 2 Tasks 4 and 5 desaturate and warm the sky on purpose — more Mie
+whitens it, a warmer white balance pushes it away from blue. `SKY_BAND` decides
+what counts as sky by colour:
+
+    {min_blue_minus_red: 0.06, require_monotonic_bgr: true}
+
+A pixel is sky if it is blue enough and its channels run B >= G >= R. So the
+brief's own direction walks the sky out of the classifier. Measured across the
+same three stations:
+
+    mid_slope sky fraction   Task 2 0.3462 -> Task 4 0.1676 -> Task 5 0.0000
+    vista     sky fraction   Task 3 0.4240 -> Task 4 0.3660 -> Task 5 0.2468
+
+**At Task 5 mid_slope reports 0.0000 sky and 0.7907 non-sky.** The entire sky
+is classified as not-sky. Nothing is wrong with the frame.
+
+### WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A WRONG NUMBER
+
+FOUR Brief 2 measurements stand on that mask: `featureless_split`'s sky/non-sky
+split, `fog_vs_sky`'s horizon-sky median, `sky_saturation`'s zenith and horizon
+bands, and `skyline_iou`. They degrade together and they degrade SILENTLY.
+
+And the failure is CORRELATED WITH THE THING BEING MEASURED. Sky reclassified
+as non-sky inflates the "featureless non-sky band" figure that BRIEF §0.3
+exists to explain — so the more the brief succeeds at desaturating the sky, the
+larger the defect it is trying to diagnose appears to be. An instrument that
+gets worse in exactly the direction the work is heading will confirm whatever
+the work does.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**A classifier that keys on the property under test is not an instrument.**
+`featureless_split`'s docstring already argues the harder half of this — the
+band is DECLARED in benchmark.json rather than sampled from the frame under
+test, precisely so a blown white frame cannot define white as sky. That
+reasoning stopped one failure mode and not this one: a declared threshold is
+still a COLOUR threshold, and colour is what Brief 2 is changing.
+
+The scene-depth pass built for Task 2's re-measure already separates sky from
+world GEOMETRICALLY — sky is what sits at or beyond the encoding ceiling — and
+does not care what colour the sky is. That is the replacement.
+
+### AND THE SAME SHAPE, TWICE MORE, IN ONE SESSION
+
+  * `haze_metrics` binned by IMAGE ROWS and called it distance. Struck for
+    near_ground: rows are not depth.
+  * `highlight_tint` presumes a NEUTRAL sunlit surface. The sunlit meadow is
+    green grass under a warm sun, so B/luma sits at 0.19-0.24 at ANY white
+    balance, and the 0.9-1.1 acceptance may be unreachable at that station
+    whatever the grade does.
+
+Three metrics in one brief whose assumptions the world does not satisfy. The
+common root: each was specified from what a frame LOOKS like rather than from
+what the quantity IS, and each fails on the station where the appearance and
+the quantity part company.
+
+### TASK 5's RULE ALSO CONTRADICTS ITS OWN CITATION
+
+BRIEF §3: "white_temp = the sun's temperature + ~1000 K (ED: sun 6500 K
+uncorrected / WB 5600 ...)". 5600 is 900 BELOW 6500. The prose says +1000 and
+the cited sample says -900.
+
+`Scene.h:1505` settles it: WhiteTemp is the temperature "which the scene
+considers as white light", so declaring 8800 K white against a 7800 K sun
+renders the sun WARM. Applied, highlight_tint moved AWAY from neutral
+(R 1.3005 -> 1.3748, B 0.2431 -> 0.1895) and shadow_tint_B fell out of the band
+Task 3 had just reached (1.4456 -> 0.9829).
+
+Left applied and unfixed, because changing the rule is Ryan's. **The citation
+was checkable the whole time and reading it would have predicted the sign
+before a capture was spent.**

+### R-EDITOR-CLOSE — THE DIRTY-MODAL DEADLOCK (2026-09-09)
+
+**The rule can deadlock, and it did.** Step 4 says the kill is authorised only
+if the census is CLEAN and the window is quiet, and "if dirty or writing:
+wait, do not kill". That assumes DIRTY RESOLVES OVER TIME, which is true of a
+write in flight and false of a save prompt.
+
+Measured 2026-09-09 after a session that deliberately never saved:
+
+    census        4 dirty  (__ExternalActors__ packages for the 4 lighting
+                            actors apply_lighting had mutated)
+    quiet         4,363 s  -- far past the 120 s threshold
+    close         unhonoured
+    RETRY close   unhonoured, window title unchanged
+    ue_exec       "no editor nodes answered discovery"
+
+The last line is the diagnosis. A modal blocks the GAME THREAD, and remote
+execution is serviced on the game thread, so **an editor that answers nothing
+while its window title looks normal has a modal up** — a save prompt, which is
+a CHILD window and therefore invisible to `MainWindowTitle`.
+
+Waiting cannot clear it. The dirty state is what RAISED the prompt, and there
+is no operator to click it.
+
+**RULE: when the census is dirty AND two closes go unhonoured AND the editor
+has stopped answering, the kill is authorised** — provided the quiet window
+passes, which is the condition that actually measures the risk (a kill DURING
+A WRITE). Enumerate the dirty packages first and say why losing them is
+acceptable. Here all four were lighting actors fully re-derivable by re-running
+`apply_lighting` from the recipe, which is the whole point of hard rule 2.
+
+**Do NOT read this as "kill when dirty".** The quiet window still gates it, the
+packages still get enumerated, and both closes are still tried first.
+
 ### R-EDITOR-CLOSE CONFIRMED A SECOND TIME — 2026-08-30

    R-FOG LOCKED; depth-binned haze instrument built and proved
    
    (1) R-FOG LOCKED on the derivation, with mid_slope's haze_rise PASS as its
    evidence. The recipe values, the fog_budget command that produced them, the
    base-2 model with its four source lines, and the read-back requirement
    (apply_lighting reports fog_implied_half_height_m, which read 291.42 while the
    recipe said 202.0 -- the only reason the defect was ever visible).
    
    near_ground's haze/far_contrast lines are STRUCK as acceptance, with the
    reason recorded: the metric split the region below the skyline into IMAGE
    ROWS, and rows are only a proxy for distance when the frame contains
    distance. At that station the "far" rows are shaded canopy a few hundred
    metres out where this fog transmits ~0.94, so the number reported CANOPY
    SHADOW with a minus sign. ROWS ARE NOT DEPTH.
    
    (2) SCENE-DEPTH PASS, and what VERIFY turned up. THERE IS NO DEPTH PASS CLASS
    IN 5.8. MoviePipelineDeferredPasses.h ships Lit, Unlit, DetailLighting,
    LightingOnly, ReflectionsOnly and PathTracer and nothing else, and no depth
    material ships with the plugin. Depth reaches MRQ only as an
    AdditionalPostProcessMaterial (:156), so one had to be authored --
    /Game/Bench/M_SceneDepth, Post Process domain, After Tonemapping, per the
    struct's own doc at :36-38. That doc also says such a material "will need
    bDisableMultisampleEffects enabled for pixels to line up (ie: no DoF,
    MotionBlur, TAA)", so --depth forces temporal samples to 1; averaging a
    geometric quantity across jittered samples would be wrong anyway.
    
    THREE THINGS THIS COST, EACH FIXED FROM A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A GUESS:
    
      * `b_enabled` does not exist. The C++ is `bool bEnabled` and UE's Python
        bindings strip the leading b. I guessed, and it cost a six-minute render.
        Probed the live struct rather than guess twice: `enabled`.
      * RAW CENTIMETRES ARE USELESS THROUGH THIS PATH. MRQ writes the additional
        pass as an 8-bit PNG; depth in cm clamps to white. Measured: TWO unique
        values across a 3840x2160 frame, and both stations produced byte-identical
        150,567-byte files. The EXR MRQ also writes does carry float depth and
        nothing here can read it -- no OpenEXR, no imageio, and Pillow 12.3 raises
        UnidentifiedImageError. Rather than add a dependency to decode a quantity
        that needs only RELATIVE precision, the material now emits
        log2(max(depth_cm,1))/20, which covers 1 cm to 10.49 km in 0..1 at ~5.6%
        relative precision and spends that precision where the bins are narrow.
      * THE PASS IS sRGB-ENCODED, and that was validated against geometry rather
        than assumed. At near_ground the camera sits 1.75 m above ground at pitch
        -2 deg with a 58.72 deg vertical FOV, so the bottom of frame looks 31.36
        deg below the horizon and the ground there MUST be 1.75/sin(31.36) = 3.36
        m away. Decoding through sRGB measures 3.28 m; reading the bytes as linear
        gives 121.50 m. The prediction picked the decode.
    
    The clipped raw-cm output is in _trash/, not in _verify -- a null result that
    looks like a depth map is exactly what should not sit in the evidence tree.
    
    (3) haze_metrics.py REWRITTEN to bin by true distance: 0-100, 100-300,
    300-1k, 1-3k, 3-8k m, reporting p10 luma, luma std and fog_budget's predicted
    T per bin. Acceptance is blacks rising and contrast falling monotonically with
    distance, AND each bin's measured contrast ratio within +/-30% of its
    predicted transmittance. That third clause is what makes it physical rather
    than a vibe: Beer-Lambert says a distant object's contrast is scaled by T, so
    if the fog matches the model that was solved for, the measured contrast ratio
    IS the transmittance.
    
    ONE CAPTURE SET, NO FOG CHANGE. Results:
    
        mid_slope    blacks rise TRUE, contrast falls TRUE,
                     ratio 0.831 vs predicted T 0.729   ->  PASS
        near_ground  blacks rise TRUE, contrast falls FALSE  ->  FAIL
    
    AND THE INSTRUMENT OVERTURNS THE OLD READING. The row-based metric reported
    near_ground's haze_rise as NEGATIVE. Binned by true distance its blacks rise
    from 0.00384 to 0.33392 across the bins -- nearly 100x. The old number was
    measuring canopy, exactly as the R-FOG strike says. near_ground still fails on
    contrast monotonicity, but its 300-1000 and 1000-3000 bins hold 13k and 8k
    pixels against 6.7M in the near bin, so that is content in canopy gaps, and
    its 3000-8000 bin is EMPTY -- the station does not span distance, which is a
    fact about the station.
    
    mid_slope PASSING the model clause is the load-bearing result: the fog's
    measured effect on contrast matches the transmittance it was solved for.

+## R-FOG — EXPONENTIAL HEIGHT FOG, DERIVED (LOCKED 2026-09-09, ruled)
+
+**Locked on the DERIVATION, with mid_slope's `haze_rise` PASS as its
+evidence.** Not on a taste judgement and not on a lucky frame.
+
+### THE VALUES, AND WHERE THEY COME FROM
+
+    fog.density                            0.00416
+    fog.half_height_m                      517.49
+    fog.height_datum_m                     186.74
+    fog.start_distance_m                   0.0
+    fog.volumetric                         true
+    fog.volumetric_extinction_scale        1.0
+    fog.volumetric_scattering_distribution 0.4
+    fog.inscattering_luminance             [0,0,0,1]
+    fog.directional_inscattering_luminance [0,0,0,1]
+    fog.sky_atmosphere_ambient_contribution_scale [1,1,1,1]
+
+    python scripts/fog_budget.py --world-z-min 0 --world-z-max 1552.5 \
+        --valley-z 186.74 --cam-z 188.49 \
+        --targets 1000:0.75 4000:0.30 8000:0.10 \
+        --out _verify/bench/<date>/fog_budget.json
+
+Density is SOLVED from a stated transmittance target; falloff comes from a
+stated RULE — density halves every world-height/3 = 517.5 m, so the ridge sees
+about 4x farther than the valley — not from a fit. Datum and camera are
+MEASURED (`bench_stations_derived.json`, near_ground `ground_m_from_heightmap`
+186.74 + `eye_m` 1.75), not assumed; the brief's own draft assumed 120/130 m.
+
+Achieved: T(1km) 0.750, T(4km) 0.316, T(8km) 0.100.
+
+### THE MODEL IS BASE 2, AND WAS VERIFIED BEFORE USE
+
+    SceneCore.cpp:404-405       Density/1000 AND HeightFalloff/1000
+    HeightFogCommon.ush:225     FogDensity * pow(2.0f, -F*(z-z0))
+    HeightFogCommon.ush:301     exp2(-Exponent)
+    HeightFogCommon.ush:394     exp2(-LineIntegral)
+
+so `FogHeightFalloff = 1000 / half_height_cm = 10 / half_height_m`, with NO
+`ln(2)`. `half_height_m` in the recipe is derived from the tool's falloff by
+that same relation, so the metric field and the raw field cannot drift.
+
+### READ BACK, ALWAYS
+
+`apply_lighting` reports `fog_implied_half_height_m` — the half-height the
+ENGINE will render, computed from the falloff it actually holds. It read
+**291.42 while the recipe said 202.0** until the base-2 fix, and that is the
+only reason the defect was visible. A fog recipe is not applied until that
+number matches what was authored.
+
+### EVIDENCE, AND WHAT IS STRUCK
+
+    mid_slope   haze_rise +0.16091   PASS      <- the lock rests on this
+
+**near_ground's `haze_rise` and `far_contrast` lines are STRUCK as
+acceptance** (ruled 2026-09-09). They do not measure depth at that station.
+The metric splits the region below the skyline into IMAGE ROWS — far = top
+40%, near = bottom 30% — and rows are only a proxy for distance when the
+frame actually contains distance. At near_ground the "far" rows are shaded
+canopy across a meadow at a few hundred metres, where this fog transmits
+~0.94; its far p10 luma (0.0043) is DARKER than its near p10 (0.0135), so the
+number reports canopy shadow with a minus sign and no fog density can move it.
+
+**Rows are not depth.** A row-banded haze metric is only valid at a station
+whose frame spans real distance.
+
+The same reasoning retires the tension in the acceptance set: fog dense enough
+to lift near_ground's blacks by 0.01 would drive T(4km) far below the 0.30 the
+targets ask for. Both were never satisfiable at once.
+
+### REJECTED
+
+**`fog.height_falloff` AS A RECIPE FIELD.** Removed in schema v1.4 and refused
+by name: metres are a number someone can reason about, 0.12 was not.
+
+**A ROW-BANDED HAZE METRIC AT A STATION WITH NO DISTANCE IN FRAME.**
+→ SYMPTOM: `haze_rise` negative at near_ground and vista, unmoved by a 2.8x
+density increase.
+→ CAUSE: image rows proxy for distance only when the frame spans distance.
+→ CORRECT: bin by TRUE distance from a scene-depth pass. See R-DEPTHBIN.
+→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09, TASK2_RESULT.md.

+## 2026-09-09c — TASK 0: a binary test with two paths into it, and two bench_capture bugs stacked
+
+Brief 2 Task 0 asks one question — is the flat band at the elevated stations
+unrendered world? — and offers a clean binary: paint the SkyAtmosphere's
+ground albedo magenta, count magenta pixels, non-zero means void. The answer
+came out NOT VOID. Getting there needed the test rebuilt, and uncovered two
+bugs in our own capture tool.
+
+### THE TEST AS SPECIFIED COULD HAVE RETURNED A FALSE ZERO
+
+`void_mask.py` thresholds on absolute colour (`r-g > 0.25`, `b-g > 0.25`,
+`r > 0.2`, `b > 0.2`). The visible planet surface is shaded at
+`SkyAtmosphere.usf:826` by `... * NdotL0 * GroundAlbedo.rgb / PI`, and this
+recipe's sun is at **12 deg elevation** — so NdotL0 ~ 0.21, then /PI, then
+tonemapped at -1.923 EV. Magenta can land below those floors on a frame that
+IS void.
+
+That matters more than a normal measurement error because **Brief 2 gates
+every later atmosphere number on this reading**: a void band scores as "fog"
+in every other measurement, so a false zero would silently corrupt Tasks 1-6.
+
+The fix was to capture a BASELINE at the original albedo and compare, which
+needs no brightness floor at all. **A test whose NEGATIVE result is
+load-bearing must be shown capable of producing a positive.** The baseline is
+what shows that: 71.7% and 80.7% of pixels moved toward magenta, so the
+albedo demonstrably reached the render.
+
+### AND THE PROPERTY DRIVES TWO PATHS, SO COLOUR ALONE CANNOT DECIDE
+
+`multi_scattering_factor` is 1.0, and `SkyAtmosphereComponent.h:64` says the
+albedo "will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it". So
+GroundAlbedo drives BOTH the visible planet surface (the `if (Ground && tMax
+== tBottom)` ray-march branch at :815, which is NOT gated on multi-scattering
+despite the header's wording) AND a global atmospheric tint. Both respond to
+the same knob. "Count magenta pixels" cannot separate them.
+
+**What separates them is SPATIAL STRUCTURE, not colour.** A surface is a
+bounded region with an edge; a bounce is everywhere and smooth. The per-row
+profile settles it: a smooth gradient, strongest in the sky, p99 <= 0.07 in
+every one of 16 bands at both stations, and no step anywhere. A planet
+surface would jump sharply, its green going 170 -> 0.
+
+RULE: when one property feeds two rendering paths, discriminate on a
+dimension the two paths do not share. Here that is geometry, not hue.
+
+### TWO BENCH_CAPTURE BUGS, THE FIRST MASKING THE SECOND
+
+**(1) A set in the sidecar killed the run AFTER a completed render.**
+`json.dump` raised "Object of type set is not JSON serializable" at the last
+step, so two 4K stills existed on disk with NO sidecar — no cvar read-backs,
+no residency, no provenance. The frames survive that; the EVIDENCE does not,
+and a 20-minute render has to be repeated to recover it. Now coerced to
+sorted lists, and the coercion is REPORTED rather than silent.
+
+**(2) `res` was rebound to a set of actor names, refusing every still.**
+

+    line 1039   res = set(ln["resident_actors"])          # ~250 labels
+    line 1217   bad = [... if v["png_size_from_file"] != res]
+
+So the final gate compared each PNG's pixel size against a set of actor
+labels and could never match. Measured: two 4K stills, the engine's own
+`resolution lines [[3840, 2160]]` in the same run, and then
+`REFUSE: ['mid_slope','vista'] rendered at a resolution other than
+{'Alpine8K_HLODLayer_...'}`.
+
+**It had been invisible because bug (1) crashed the run before the gate was
+reached.** Fixing the first exposed the second. Both live in the same dozen

+long function — `res`, `exp` — where an outer binding already owned it.

    Brief 2 arrived; Task 2 says VERIFY fog_budget.py's UNIT constant against

    WHAT IS TRUE. The fog density profile is base 2 in three places --
    HeightFogCommon.ush :225 `FogDensity * pow(2.0f, -F*(z-z0))`, :301
    `exp2(-Exponent)`, :394 `exp2(-LineIntegral)` -- with SceneCore.cpp:404-405

    recipes/schema.md's "the old height_falloff: 0.12 therefore meant a 57.8 m
    half-height" is the same wrong formula. Correct: 83.3 m. Seed fixed with the
    copies, or it re-infects.

    falloff with base-e exponentials, so asking it "what half-height does this
    give" returned the authored number. The model agreed with itself and never
    with the engine -- non-negotiable 0: the two functions shared a source, so
    they were one measurement. What broke it open was a SECOND, independently
    written implementation arriving in the brief. After the fix the two agree to
    5 decimals at 1, 4 and 8 km; before it they could not have.
