+## 2026-09-09c — CORRECTION to 2026-09-09b: `TaskStop` did not kill the build. The harness reclaims background tasks, and I named a cause on one coincidence
+
+### The entry above is WRONG in its root cause, and this is the containment
+
+2026-09-09b says I killed the forced batch 0 by stopping the `tail -f` monitor
+watching it. **That is not what happened.** I had one observation — the driver
+died at the same moment `TaskStop` returned — and I wrote a causal claim from
+it, in the same session in which I had refused three times to name a cause for
+the GPU faults on exactly that reasoning. The rule fired for the engine and not
+for me.
+
+### What the timings actually say
+
+A SECOND run was launched with no monitor armed and `TaskStop` never called.
+It died too.
+
+    run 1   launched 11:14:44   last driver write 11:16:34   ~1.8 min
+            Bash tool default timeout: 120000 ms
+    run 2   launched 11:18:44   last driver write 11:18:54
+            last engine write   11:19:01                     ~30 s
+            Bash tool timeout passed: 600000 ms
+
+Run 1's lifetime matches the **default two-minute Bash timeout** almost
+exactly, which is the far simpler explanation for it and needs no `TaskStop` at
+all. Run 2 rules the timeout out as the general cause: it had ten minutes and
+lasted thirty seconds. What both share is that **each died immediately after a
+turn boundary** — the stop hook fired, I answered, and the task was gone.
+
+`driver_all.txt` holds no traceback and stderr was redirected into it, so the
+Python parent did not fail; it was terminated from outside.
+
+**The mechanism is still not established.** What IS established: a background
+Bash task in this harness cannot be relied on to outlive the turn that started
+it, and neither the default timeout nor an explicit larger one changes that.
+For a job measured in hours that is disqualifying, and no amount of care about
+`TaskStop` would have helped.
+
+### The fix, which is structural rather than behavioural
+
+Launch long work as a process the harness does not own:
+
+    Start-Process -FilePath python -ArgumentList ... -WindowStyle Hidden
+                  -RedirectStandardOutput <file> -RedirectStandardError <file>
+                  -PassThru
+
+and poll it from later turns by PID and by the process table. The 2026-09-09b
+rule about not calling `TaskStop` mid-build is still worth keeping — it is
+cheap and it is good practice — but it is **not** why the builds died and it
+would not have saved either one.
+
+### Both kills were harmless, and the check is the same one
+
+    packages present   2,267 of 2,267    missing 0
+    shorter than 1 KB  0
+    bytes              10,426,637,250, byte-identical across the second kill
+
+R-HLOD 08c's window holds: `SaveHLODPackage` writes per actor as each one
+completes, so a kill during `BuildHLOD` costs the cell in flight and nothing
+else.
+
+### The rule, and it is about me
+
+**One coincidence is not a cause, and the standard does not relax because the
+suspect is my own action rather than the engine's.** I spent this session
+refusing to explain three GPU faults without a mechanism, wrote that refusal
+into LESSONS twice, and then explained a dead process from a single
+simultaneous event without checking the two-minute timeout that was sitting in
+the tool's own defaults.

+## 2026-09-09b — I killed my own build by stopping the MONITOR that was watching it
+
+### What happened
+
+The forced batch 0 was running correctly — `approve=13, reject=0` at 1.8 min,
+the first evidence that `-RebuildHLODs` fixes the skip defect found an hour
+earlier. Two background tasks were live:
+
+    bi6n5vwrf   the driver, which launches and supervises the commandlet
+    bsb00u4ql   a `tail -f | grep` MONITOR, watching the driver's transcript
+
+The monitor emitted a progress line every 20 s. Each one cost a turn and fired
+the uncommitted-work hook, so I stopped **the monitor** to cut the noise, on
+the reasoning that a `tail -f` is a pure reader and stopping it cannot touch
+the build.
+
+`TaskStop` reported success on `bsb00u4ql`. **The driver task `bi6n5vwrf` was
+killed at the same moment**, and with it the `UnrealEditor-Cmd` child: zero
+Unreal processes, VRAM back to 128 MiB, the log ending on an `ApproveRebuild`
+for cell 16 of 191.
+
+**I did not establish the mechanism** by which stopping one background task
+reached the other. Both were local bash tasks. The temporal association is
+unambiguous and that is all I am claiming.
+
+### No damage, and here is the check rather than the assurance
+
+    packages present     2,267 of 2,267      missing 0
+    shorter than 1 KB    0
+    bytes                10,426,637,250 (was 10,426,625,137, +12,113)
+    15 cells now record a build time of 2026-09-06 18:xx
+
+The kill landed during `BuildHLOD`, not during `SaveHLODActor` — the log's last
+line is a rebuild-policy decision, not a save. R-HLOD 08c already established
+that this window is safe because `SaveHLODPackage` writes per actor as each one
+completes. It held.
+
+**And nothing was gained.** The hour buckets show all 15 rebuilt cells came out
+of build 3's already-current set (07:xx 41 -> 35, 08:xx 281 -> 272), because
+shard 0 begins with the same cells build 3 processed first. `MeshMerge(1)` is
+still 927. The run died before it reached a single stale cell.
+
+### Root cause, and it is not the tool
+
+A monitor is not free of consequence just because its command only reads. What
+I stopped was not a `tail`; it was a TASK, and tasks are the thing the harness
+owns. **The cost of a monitor is turn churn; the cost of stopping one turned
+out to be the build.** I traded a known small cost for an unknown one and did
+not check first — the check was two seconds of process listing, which is what I
+had already run three times that hour for exactly this class of question.
+
+The deeper error is that I reasoned about the CONTENTS of the monitor's command
+(`tail -f` is harmless) when the operation was on its CONTAINER (a background
+task). That is the same substitution as reading a log line instead of the
+process table — judging a thing by what it claims to be rather than by what it
+is.
+
+### The rule
+
+**NEVER call `TaskStop` while a build, render or bulk mutation is running in a
+sibling background task.** Turn churn is an annoyance; a killed commandlet is an
+hour. If a monitor is too noisy, let it run to its timeout, or do not arm one —
+the driver already detects fatal signatures, retries once in a fresh process and
+stops on a second failure, so the monitor was pure visibility and was never
+load-bearing.
+
+Corollary, general: **before stopping any harness task, list the OTHER live
+tasks and processes first.** The blast radius of a stop is not bounded by what
+the stopped command does.

+## 2026-09-09 — `-BuildHLODs` without `-RebuildHLODs` does NOT skip only completed cells. It skipped 77 cells that were stale by the exact setting we changed, and the builder reported "Built 191" over a run that built nothing

+### What was ruled, and what it rested on

+sentence, written by me the night before:

+    batched restart is nearly free.

+**That sentence is false, and the ruling's own step 3 is what caught it** — it
+required reading back from batch 1's log that OLD MeshMerge cells rebuild and
+accuracy-1.5 cells are skipped, and to stop if they do not.

+### What happened

+    Instancing(0)          RejectRebuild      104
+    MeshApproximate(3)     RejectRebuild       10
+    MeshMerge(1)           RejectRebuild       77
+
+**77 cells whose own report reads `LayerType: MeshMerge(1)`, last built by
+build 1 at 05:12-05:48 UTC, were evaluated against a layer asset that is now
+`MeshApproximate` — and rejected.** Named examples, with their recorded build
+time:

+### The decision chain, every link opened
+
+    WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:172   bForceBuild = HasParam("RebuildHLODs")
+    :839                                 HLODActor->BuildHLOD(bForceBuild)
+    WorldPartitionHLODUtilities.cpp:936-957
+                                         Evaluate != ApproveRebuild -> return
+    :945-951                             the builder binds its own evaluator
+    WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:1810  which calls UHLODRebuildPolicy::Evaluate
+    :1814-1818                           and returns it UNCHANGED when source
+                                         control is disabled, which it is here
+    HLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare.cpp:33  OldHash != NewHash ? Approve : Reject
+    HLODLayer.cpp:278-297                the hash covers LayerType and
+                                         HLODBuilderSettings
+
+So the decision is the hash comparison, and the hashed set demonstrably
+includes the field that changed. **Reject therefore means OldHash == NewHash on
+a cell whose recorded LayerType is MeshMerge and whose live layer is
+MeshApproximate. WHY THEY ARE EQUAL IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND I AM NOT NAMING A
+CAUSE.** Three invented causes in one week is the pattern this project keeps
+paying for.
+
+**The leading candidate, recorded as a LEAD and not as a finding.**
+`UHLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare::ComputeDataForRebuildPolicy`
+(HLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare.cpp:15) constructs its data with
+`NewObject<UHLODRebuildPolicyHashData>()` — **no Outer**, so the object is
+outered to the transient package and cannot serialise into the actor package.
+On load `HLODRebuildPolicyDataSet` (HLODActor.h:234-235) would then be empty,
+`OldData` null, and `Evaluate` falls back to `InHLODActor->GetHLODHash()`, i.e.
+`HLODHash_DEPRECATED` — a field whose only 5.8 setter is a no-op stub
+(`SetHLODHash(...) {}`, HLODActor.h:151). **This lead does not survive its own
+prediction:** it predicts OldHash == 0 for every actor, which gives
+0 != NewHash and therefore APPROVE — the opposite of what was observed. It is
+written down because it is the only concrete mechanism found in the source, and
+because the next session should test it rather than re-derive it.
+
+### THE SECOND TRAP, and it is the more dangerous one
+
+    #### Built 191 HLOD actors ####
+
+printed at the end of a run that rebuilt **zero**. `BuiltHLODActors++` is
+incremented unconditionally once per loop iteration, after the save, without
+consulting `BuildHLOD`'s return value. **The builder's own completion marker is
+a count of cells VISITED, not of cells built.** I had just written that marker
+into `hlod_build_batched.py` as the batch success test, replacing the exit code.
+It would have reported twelve successful batches over a world that never
+changed — a builder reporting success over a graph that is wrong, which is this
+project's most expensive failure mode by name.
+
+### THE THIRD THING, and it invalidates two numbers in CURRENT STATE
+
+Two proxies for "which cells are stale" were in use, and **both misclassify**:
+
+    package size    705 packages over 5 MB
+    triangle count  468 cells at >= 100k triangles
+    the cells' own build reports:  927 MeshMerge, 115 MeshApproximate,
+                                   1,225 Instancing
+
+`..._Merged/..._Instanced_L1_X-4_Y-2` carries **8,449 triangles in a
+19,071,154-byte package** and its report says `MeshMerge(1)`, build 1. A
+higher-level MeshMerge cell sits under any triangle threshold worth picking, and
+a package also holds its baked textures, so neither size nor triangle count
+separates the bands. Classifying that cell as "rebuilt" is wrong in the
+expensive direction — it gets left stale.
+
+**The world is 927 of 1,042 Merged cells stale (89%), not the ~705 of 1,025
+(69%) CURRENT STATE records.** Only **115** cells have ever been rebuilt under
+the MeshApproximate layer — build 2's 265 were overwritten when build 3
+restarted from the top, and 261 of build 3's 376 were Instancing cells.
+
+Size and triangle count are both downstream of the same event, the geometry a
+build emitted, so their agreement would not have made either right —
+non-negotiable 0. The build report is a different record: what the build was
+CONFIGURED with, written by the engine at build time.
+
+New instrument, no editor required: `scripts/hlod_report_census.py`. It reads
+`AWorldPartitionHLOD::HLODBuildReport`, a saved `UPROPERTY() FString`
+(HLODActor.h:232) assembled at HLODActor.cpp:830-850 and delimited by
+`### HLOD_REPORT_BEGIN ###` (:738). Per cell it yields the label, the LayerType,
+the build time, and **the full command line of the build that wrote it**.
+
+### What is being done about it
+
+`-RebuildHLODs` sets `bForceBuild` (WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:172), which
+makes `OldRebuildPolicyDataSet` empty (WorldPartitionHLODUtilities.cpp:942) and
+bypasses the comparison entirely. So the batches keep the manifest sharding —
+which is verified, and is what bounds GPU exposure to ~190 cells per process —
+and add `-RebuildHLODs`. The cost of forcing is small and now measured rather
+than assumed: only 115 of 2,267 cells are current, so at most 5% of the work is
+redone, and the 1,225 Instancing cells rebuild at 0.02 s each (R-HLOD 08d).
+
+The batch success test drops the "Built N" marker and uses the cells' own
+recorded LayerType instead, read back from the packages after each batch.
+
+### The rule
+
+**A skip is a claim about work not done, and the only evidence for it is the
+artefact.** A log line saying a cell was considered, a count saying N were
+"built", and an exit code are all statements by the thing being measured. The
+read-back has to come from what the build WROTE — and when the question is
+"were the right SETTINGS used", the geometry is not enough either, because
+geometry is what you are trying to judge. Find the record of the configuration.
+
+This is the second time in two days that a completion signal from the builder
+has been wrong in the safe-looking direction: 2026-09-08d recorded that
+"Engine exit requested ... result 0" is printed by commandlets that have not
+exited. Same shape, different field. **Treat every self-report from this builder
+as a claim, not a measurement.**

+## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-09
+
+**Trusting `-BuildHLODs` without `-RebuildHLODs` to rebuild cells that are
+stale because the LAYER changed.**
+→ SYMPTOM: a batch of 191 finishes in 30 s, logs
+`HLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare -> RejectRebuild` for every cell, prints
+`#### Built 191 HLOD actors ####`, and changes nothing. 77 of those cells
+record `LayerType: MeshMerge(1)` while the layer asset reads
+`EHLODLayerType::MeshApproximate`.
+→ CAUSE: the decision is `OldHash != NewHash`
+(`HLODRebuildPolicyHashCompare.cpp:33`) and the hashes compare EQUAL. **Why
+they are equal is NOT established** — see the LEAD in LESSONS 2026-09-09, which
+is recorded there precisely because it fails its own prediction.
+→ CORRECT: pass `-RebuildHLODs` and bound the exposure with the manifest
+shards instead. Verify the result from `scripts/hlod_report_census.py`, never
+from the run's own log.
+→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09.
+
+**Reading `#### Built N HLOD actors ####` as a count of cells rebuilt.**
+→ SYMPTOM: "Built 191" over a run with 191 rejections and zero geometry
+written. Reads as a complete, successful batch.
+→ CAUSE: `BuiltHLODActors++` is incremented once per loop iteration,
+unconditionally, without consulting `BuildHLOD`'s return value
+(`WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp` build loop). It counts cells VISITED.
+→ CORRECT: it is a COMPLETION marker — the loop reached the end — and nothing
+more. For "did anything get built", count `ApproveRebuild` decisions in the log
+AND confirm against the cells' recorded LayerType afterwards.
+→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09. Same shape as 08d's "Engine exit requested ...
+result 0" printed by commandlets that had not exited.
+
+**Using package size, or triangle count, to decide which cells are stale.**
+→ SYMPTOM: two proxies disagree (705 packages over 5 MB vs 468 cells at
+>= 100k triangles) and BOTH are wrong. `..._Merged/..._Instanced_L1_X-4_Y-2`
+holds 8,449 triangles in a 19,071,154-byte package and is MeshMerge output.
+→ CAUSE: a package also carries its baked textures, and a higher-level
+MeshMerge cell falls under any triangle threshold worth picking. Both proxies
+are downstream of the same event — the geometry a build emitted — so their
+agreeing would not have made either right (non-negotiable 0).
+→ CORRECT: `scripts/hlod_report_census.py`, which reads the settings the build
+was CONFIGURED with rather than the geometry it produced. It puts the stale
+count at 927, not 705.
+→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09.
+
+**Treating a commandlet's non-zero exit code as a failure on this machine.**
+→ SYMPTOM: every successful HLOD run ends `Failure - 2 error(s), 2 warning(s)`
+and exits non-zero, so a loop that retries on `rc != 0` retries every batch.
+→ CAUSE: IncrediBuild's `Manager.exe` holds port 8000
+(`docs/environment.md`), so `LogHttpListener: Error: HttpListener unable to
+bind to 127.0.0.1:8000` is logged twice on EVERY commandlet regardless of the
+work. Confirmed on the two runs that produced the accepted cell:
+`build_one_cell_noxge.log:2420` / `:2435` and
+`build_onecell_acc15.log:2192` / `:2207`.
+→ CORRECT: record `rc` as data; judge the run on the log's error COUNT against
+that baseline of 2, plus the artefact.
+→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-09.

+## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08g: APPROXIMATION ACCURACY IS DERIVED FROM THE QUAD SIZE, NOT LEFT AT DEFAULT
+
+### The cost of MeshApproximate is the VOXEL GRID, not the triangle target
+
+`TargetTriCount` is what the SIMPLIFIER aims at — it governs the mesh that
+comes out. The expensive step happens before that: MeshApproximate voxelises
+the cell's contents, and the voxel resolution is
+`FMeshApproximationSettings::ApproximationAccuracy`
+(`MeshApproximationSettings.h:73-75`):
+
+    /** Approximation Accuracy in Meters, will determine (eg) voxel resolution */
+    meta = (DisplayName = "Approximation Accuracy (meters)", ClampMin = "0.001")
+    float ApproximationAccuracy = 1.0f;
+
+**Lowering `TargetTriCount` does not make the voxelisation cheaper.** Measured
+at the default accuracy of 1.0 m: 265 cells in 52.4 min = **5.06 actors/min,
+11.86 s/actor**, all of them `Merged L0`.
+
+### ⚠ THE UNITS ARE METRES. A VALUE OF 150 IS NOT 150 cm.
+
+`ApproximationAccuracy = 1.5` means a 1.5 m voxel. Setting `150` would mean
+150-METRE accuracy on a 254 m cell — about two voxels across — which destroys
+the proxy rather than accelerating it, and would do so without erroring.
+`hlod_set_approx_accuracy.py` REFUSES any value above 10.0 for exactly this
+reason.
+
+### THE DERIVATION
+
+    quad edge   4,000 tris on a 254 m cell = 254/sqrt(2000) = 5.68 m
+    voxel       a quarter of the quad edge = 1.42 m, taken as 1.5 m
+
+A voxel at roughly a quarter of the quad edge resolves everything the
+simplifier can keep and nothing it must discard: detail finer than a
+quarter-quad cannot survive decimation to 5.68 m quads, so paying to voxelise
+it is pure waste.
+
+Cross-checked against the band the proxy serves: at 2 km a 1.5 m voxel subtends
+`1.5/2000 rad = 1.8 px`, already under the 6 px shape threshold. The voxel grid
+is not resolving anything a viewer could read as shape.
+
+    accuracy 1.0 m -> 254 voxels across the cell
+    accuracy 1.5 m -> 169 voxels across      (~3.4x fewer in 3D)
+
+`ClampVoxelDimension` is 1024 (`:79`, max 1290), so 169 is nowhere near the
+clamp — the accuracy value governs rather than being silently limited. **Check
+that**: an accuracy fine enough to exceed the clamp is capped without warning,
+and the setting then means something other than what it says.
+
+### VERIFIED ON ONE CELL BEFORE ANYTHING WAS LAUNCHED
+
+`-BuildSingleHLOD=..._L0_X-10_Y11 -RebuildHLODs -noxgecontroller
+-AllowCommandletRendering`, then read back from the built mesh:
+
+    triangles          3,988          target 4,000   (was 329,364)
+    vertices           7,299                         (was 951,468)
+    bounds             26697 x 27101 x 9989 cm, NON-ZERO
+    mesh_support_ray_tracing   FALSE  <- the layer setting reached the OUTPUT
+    nanite             false
+    package            1,455,802 B                    (was 13,959,833)
+    material           1 x MaterialInstanceConstant
+
+**`UStaticMesh::bSupportRayTracing` on the BUILT MESH is the read-back that
+matters** (`StaticMesh.h:1385`). The layer's builder setting is an INPUT;
+whether the emitted mesh carries an acceleration structure is the thing that
+cost 12,434 MiB of VRAM and hung the GPU twice. `hlod_verify_built.py` reads
+the output.
+
+### THE TIMING COMPARISON THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG
+
+That single cell took **57.8 s**, against 11.86 s/actor for the accuracy-1.0
+run. It is tempting to read that as five times SLOWER. **It is not a valid
+comparison and must not be recorded as one:**
+
+    accuracy 1.0   WARM process, 265th-ish cell, in-process caches hot
+    accuracy 1.5   COLD process, FIRST Merged cell of the run, one-off costs
+
+Two variables. A like-for-like figure needs a sustained run at the new accuracy
+sampled the same way — same instrument, same warm state — which is what
+`build3_acc15.log` is for.
+
+## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-08g
+
+**Lowering `TargetTriCount` to make MeshApproximate faster.** → SYMPTOM: the
+output mesh gets smaller and the build takes just as long. → CAUSE: the cost is
+the voxel grid, sized by `ApproximationAccuracy`; the triangle target only
+shapes what comes out of it. → CORRECT: derive the accuracy from the quad size
+the triangle budget implies.
+
+**Reading `ApproximationAccuracy` as centimetres.** → SYMPTOM: a value of 150
+is accepted silently and yields a proxy built from ~2 voxels across a 254 m
+cell. → CAUSE: the field is METRES, default 1.0. → CORRECT: 1.5 for a 1.5 m
+voxel; the tool refuses anything above 10.
+
+**Comparing a cold single-cell build against a warm sustained rate.**
+→ SYMPTOM: 57.8 s vs 11.86 s/actor reads as a 5x regression from a change that
+strictly reduces work. → CAUSE: process warmth and first-cell one-off costs are
+a second variable. → CORRECT: sample the new setting the same way the old one
+was sampled, over a sustained window.

+
+## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08f: THE PROXY BUDGET COMES FROM THE BLOB BAND, AND `MeshMerge` CANNOT PRODUCE ONE
+
+### The structural mistake in the first build
+
+`Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged` was `EHLODLayerType::MeshMerge`. **`FMeshMergingSettings`
+has NO triangle-reduction field.** `LODSelectionType`/`SpecificLOD` choose WHICH
+SOURCE LOD to merge; `MaterialSettings` controls the bake; nothing decimates.
+**MeshMerge concatenates.** One 254 m cell came out at 329,364 triangles because
+that is the sum of its sources.
+
+So this was never a settings tweak — it is a LAYER TYPE change. Of the types
+that can reduce (`HLODLayer.h:31-38`):
+
+    Instancing / MeshMerge   cannot reduce
+    MeshSimplify             FMeshProxySettings -- ScreenSize / VoxelSize,
+                             no direct triangle target
+    MeshApproximate          FMeshApproximationSettings -- SimplifyMethod +
+                             TargetTriCount, the control the budget is
+                             expressed in
+
+### THE BUDGET, derived
+
+    4K/90 deg = 42.67 ppd            REGISTER, PROVEN (B1.3)
+    blob band = 1.5-6 px             Brief 1's four-band ladder
+    Merged L0 cell = 254 m           derived label grid, R-HLOD 08b
+
+A proxy triangle should be no finer than the smallest feature that reads at the
+distance where the proxy IS the representation. For N triangles as a grid,
+quad edge = 254 / sqrt(N/2) m, and its angular size is
+`(edge/d) * 57.2958 * 42.67` px:
+
+    N = 4,000    edge 5.68 m   6.9 px @2km   3.5 px @4km   1.7 px @8km
+    N = 329,364  edge 0.63 m   0.77 px       0.38 px       0.19 px
+
+**4,000 puts the quad edge inside the blob band across 2-8 km. The built proxy
+was SUB-PIXEL at every distance it is ever seen** — 82x too dense by count.
+
+    TEXTURE 512^2 over 254 m = 0.50 m/texel = 0.61 px/texel at 2 km, already
+            finer than the pixel grid. 1024^2 = 0.30 px/texel pays 4x memory
+            for detail below the sampling limit. 512 is the target, 1024 the
+            ceiling.
+    NANITE  NOT enabled. It earns its cost on dense meshes; at 4,000 triangles
+            a plain static mesh is cheaper, and Nanite adds a fallback mesh
+            whose own RT representation is the thing being removed.
+
+### RAY TRACING: THE DEFAULT IS THE DEFECT
+
+`FMeshApproximationSettings::bSupportRayTracing` **defaults to TRUE**
+(`MeshApproximationSettings.h:211`; `FMeshMergingSettings` carries the same
+field at line 135). That default gave all 2,267 proxies an acceleration
+structure. Measured, single variable:
+
+    r.RayTracing on    peak VRAM 12,434 MiB   crashed DEVICE_HUNG, 2 of 2
+    r.RayTracing=0     peak VRAM    812 MiB   opened in 90 s, 0 crashes,
+                                              0 compile warnings (vs 558+)
+
+**An HLOD proxy standing in for objects at 1.5-6 px never needs to be ray
+traced. Set `support_ray_tracing` FALSE.**
+
+`bForceRayTracingFarField` on the LAYER (`HLODLayer.h:154-155`) is an opt-IN
+that ADDS spatially-loaded HLOD to the RT far field. It is not the lever and is
+left alone.
+
+### THE VALUES, applied and read back 2026-09-08
+
+    layer_type            MESH_APPROXIMATE      was MESH_MERGE
+    simplify_method       FIXED_TRIANGLE_COUNT
+    target_tri_count      4000
+    support_ray_tracing   false                 was true (engine default)
+    generate_nanite_enabled_mesh  false
+    texture_sizing_type   USE_MANUAL_OVERRIDE_TEXTURE_SIZE
+    texture_size          512 x 512
+    cell_size             25600      loading_range 51200   (unchanged)
+
+Tool: `scripts/payloads/hlod_set_proxy_budget.py` — read back from a FRESHLY
+LOADED asset, not the object written.
+
+### PYTHON STRIPS THE LEADING `b` FROM BOOLEANS
+
+`b_support_ray_tracing` raises "Failed to find property";
+`support_ray_tracing` works. Same rule as `bIsSpatiallyLoaded` ->
+`is_spatially_loaded`. Probe with `hlod_probe_approx_fields.py` rather than
+guessing one round trip at a time.
+
+### CHANGING `layer_type` SWAPS THE SETTINGS OBJECT, and it does so from Python
+
+`HLODBuilderMeshMergeSettings` -> `HLODBuilderMeshApproximateSettings` on the
+`set_editor_property("layer_type", ...)` call, verified by re-reading
+`hlod_builder_settings` immediately afterwards. **It also invalidates every
+dependent HLOD mesh**, and an open editor will start recompiling them
+immediately — which will make the remote-exec node stop answering (`ue_exec`
+exit 3) while it works. That is the editor being BUSY, not dead: check
+`MainWindowTitle` and CPU before concluding anything.
+
+## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-08f
+
+**`MeshMerge` for a distance proxy.** → SYMPTOM: 329,364 triangles per 254 m
+cell, 10.46 GB across the world, and the world stops opening. → CAUSE:
+`FMeshMergingSettings` has no reduction field; MeshMerge concatenates its
+sources. → CORRECT: `MeshApproximate` with `SimplifyMethod =
+FixedTriangleCount` and a `TargetTriCount` derived from the band the proxy
+serves. → REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08h; this amendment.
+
+**Leaving `bSupportRayTracing` at its default on HLOD proxies.** → SYMPTOM:
+peak VRAM 12,434 MiB of a 15,235 MiB budget, `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG` with a
+page fault on `StaticMesh_Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged_0`, reproduced 2 of 2.
+→ CAUSE: the field defaults to TRUE, so every proxy builds an acceleration
+structure. → CORRECT: false — a 1.5-6 px blob is never a ray-tracing target.
+→ EVIDENCE: `r.RayTracing=0` opened the same world at 812 MiB peak VRAM.
+
+**Choosing a proxy triangle count by eye, or by "what looks like a reasonable
+reduction".** → CORRECT: derive it. Quad edge = cell_size / sqrt(N/2); require
+its angular size to sit inside the band the proxy serves at the distances the
+proxy is seen. The arithmetic is three lines and it produced 4,000 from first
+principles.

+## 2026-09-08g — I wrote the lesson about extrapolating from a partial sample and then did it twice more within the hour; here is why it did not fire
+
+### The record
+
+Within one session, on one build:
+
+    DISK    from 1 merged cell        15-20 GB
+            from 202 packages         5-6 GB     reported to the operator
+            from 422 packages         ~17 GB
+            from 1010 packages        ~27 GB
+    MEMORY  7.1 -> 12.5 GB            "watch it"
+            12.5 -> 15.8 GB           "decelerating, should plateau"
+            15.8 -> 19.3 GB           "reaccelerating, will exceed 31.4 GB"
+            19.3 -> 8.9 GB            neither: it SAWTOOTHS
+
+Between the second disk figure and the first memory claim I wrote LESSONS
+2026-09-08f, whose closing paragraph is: *"An extrapolation from a running
+job's first slice is a measurement of the order of work, not of the work. Wait
+for a blended sample or say plainly that the number is provisional."*
+
+I then made the same error twice more, on a different quantity, having just
+written that sentence.
+
+### Why the lesson did not fire, which is the only useful part
+
+**It was filed under the wrong thing.** I wrote it as a fact about *disk size
+during HLOD builds* — it lives in an HLOD lesson, its example is package bytes,
+and its remedy is phrased as "wait for a blended sample". So when the next
+quantity came along it did not look like the same situation: memory is not
+disk, and I was not extrapolating a total from a slice, I was reading a *rate*
+from consecutive samples. Different surface, same fallacy, and the lesson was
+indexed by surface.
+
+**And the memory case was worse than the disk case, not merely similar.** Disk
+consumption is monotonic — it only goes up — so extrapolating it is at least
+directionally sound and only the magnitude was wrong. A process working set is
+**not monotonic**: UE flushes its package cache, so the series sawtooths. Two
+consecutive samples of a sawtooth support *any* trend you like depending on
+where in the tooth you landed. I produced three contradictory trends from four
+samples and stated each with confidence.
+
+**The tell I ignored, twice.** Each claim was built on exactly two points. Two
+points cannot distinguish a trend from a cycle — that is not a heuristic, it is
+arithmetic. I had the information needed to know the claim was unsupported at
+the moment of making it, and what was missing was not data but the question
+*"how many samples is this resting on, and can that number distinguish the
+shapes I am choosing between?"*
+
+### The rule, stated so it is indexed by the ERROR and not by the subject
+
+**A trend claim needs enough samples to rule out the shapes you are not
+claiming.** Two points fit a line, a sawtooth, a step and a plateau equally
+well, so two points support no trend claim about anything — disk, memory, frame
+time, instance counts, luma.
+
+When there are not enough samples, the honest output is the reading itself
+("19.3 GB now, up from 15.8") and not its derivative ("climbing at 1 GB/min,
+will exhaust RAM"). The reading is a measurement. The derivative is a story.
+
+**And prefer the instrument to the prediction.** The thing that actually
+protected this build was not any of my four estimates; it was a watchdog armed
+at a threshold, which does not care what the curve is doing. Where a bound
+matters, arm a trigger at the bound instead of forecasting whether the bound
+will be reached. The forecast was wrong three times; the trigger would have
+been right regardless.
+
+### Cost, and why it is not zero
+
+Nothing broke. But the 5-6 GB figure went to the operator as a correction to a
+previous estimate, which makes it worse than a first guess: it was presented as
+a refinement, carrying more authority than the number it replaced, and it was
+further from the truth. **A confident correction is more expensive than a
+confident error**, because it spends the credibility of having noticed
+something.

 **Resolve the git strategy BEFORE running the full build.** Running it first
 and deciding afterwards is the expensive order.
+
+## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08e: THE FULL BUILD, AND KEEPING ~17 GB OF IT OUT OF GIT
+
+### The command
+
+    UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe <uproject> /Game/Alpine8K \
+      -run=WorldPartitionBuilderCommandlet \
+      -Builder=WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder -BuildHLODs \
+      -noxgecontroller -AllowCommandletRendering \
+      -unattended -nosplash -nopause -abslog=<repo>/_verify/hlod/<date>/build_full.log
+
+`-noxgecontroller` is not optional here — see the 08d amendment. `-BuildHLODs`
+without `-RebuildHLODs` skips cells that are already built, so the command is
+resumable: re-running it after an interruption continues rather than restarting.
+
+### WRITE THE START MARKER FIRST, BEFORE LAUNCHING
+
+    _verify/hlod/<date>/BUILD_START_MARKER
+
+Its **mtime** is what `scripts/hlod_gitignore.py` compares against to tell this
+build's output from packages already on disk. A wall-clock string would have to
+be parsed and time-zone reasoned about; a file's mtime is compared directly
+against other files' mtimes in the same clock. Write it in the same step that
+launches the build, or the reference is wrong.
+
+Tag a restore point in the same breath — this is a risky-op checkpoint by the
+letter of the rule (bulk write across ~2,267 packages).
+
+### MEASURED COST — 8129 m world, 2,267 HLOD actors
+
+    rate      ~51-59 actors/min, blended        total ~45 min
+    disk      ~7.6 MB/actor blended             total ~17 GB
+    memory    7.1 GB at launch -> 12.5 GB by 7 min, watch it
+    exit      the process EXITS on its own with -noxgecontroller
+
+**DO NOT EXTRAPOLATE COST FROM THE FIRST FEW HUNDRED ACTORS.** The builder does
+not write cells in a representative order: early ones are cheap `Instanced`
+cells (~0.02 s, tens of KB), later ones are `Merged` cells (~11.7 s, up to
+13.9 MB). A projection from the first 202 packages gave 5–6 GB and was wrong by
+3x. Either wait for a blended sample or state the figure as provisional.
+
+### THE GIT STEP, AND ITS ORDER IS THE WHOLE POINT
+
+**The packages are ALREADY TRACKED** — `-SetupHLODs` created them as ~130-byte
+stubs and those were committed. `-BuildHLODs` inflates them in place. So:
+
+    .gitignore ALONE DOES NOTHING. Ignores do not apply to tracked paths.
+    Adding 2,267 entries succeeds, changes nothing, and the 17 GB still
+    enters the next commit.
+
+The operation is `git rm --cached` **and** the ignore entry, and it must happen
+**BEFORE the first commit after the build**:
+
+    committed then untracked   17 GB in history forever
+    untracked then committed   17 GB never in history
+
+    python scripts/hlod_gitignore.py           # dry run, writes nothing
+    python scripts/hlod_gitignore.py --apply    # manifest + rm --cached + ignore
+
+Then commit **the manifest and `.gitignore` only**. History keeps the 130-byte
+stubs, ~300 KB in total.
+
+### MEMBERSHIP IS BY CONTENT SIGNATURE (standing rule 8)
+
+World Partition hash-buckets HLOD packages into the SAME GUID directories as
+landscape proxies and foliage, so the path says nothing and `git rm --cached`
+on a real actor would be a real defect. A package is HLOD **iff its bytes
+contain `WorldPartitionHLOD`** — 3–7 hits in a built HLOD package, 0 in a
+`LandscapeStreamingProxy`. It appears within the first 16 KB even in the
+13.9 MB cell, so a 1 MB head read decides it, with a full-file fallback when
+the head is inconclusive.
+
+All three conditions required: under `__ExternalActors__`, mtime newer than the
+marker, and carrying the signature.
+
+### VERIFICATION IS BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the script exits non-zero otherwise
+
+    POSITIVE  first/middle/last manifest entries are ignored AND absent from
+              `git ls-files`
+    NEGATIVE  the four HLOD layer assets, `Alpine8K.umap`, the manifest itself
+              and a sample of surviving tracked actors are NOT ignored and
+              REMAIN in the index; no untracked files left under
+              `__ExternalActors__`
+
+A one-directional check passes just as happily with `*` in `.gitignore`.
+
+## R-HLOD REJECTED — additions 2026-09-08e
+
+**Adding `.gitignore` entries for build output without checking whether it is
+tracked.** → SYMPTOM: no error, a correct-looking 2,267-line diff,
+`git check-ignore` still reports a match, and the content lands in the next
+commit regardless. The failure is invisible until the repository is 17 GB
+heavier and only a history rewrite will help. → CAUSE: ignores do not apply to
+tracked paths, and `-BuildHLODs` rewrites tracked stubs rather than creating
+files. → CORRECT: `git rm --cached` plus the ignore entry, before any commit.
+→ REFERENCE: LESSONS 2026-09-08f.
+
+**Letting a tool silently perform an operation that has no effect.**
+→ SYMPTOM: as above — the whole class. → CORRECT: when a tool can do something
+inert, make it REFUSE and REPORT. `hlod_gitignore.py` sorts candidates into
+tracked and untracked and declines to write ignore entries for the tracked
+ones; that single decision is what surfaced the defect, in one line of output,
+before anything was committed.
+
+**Extrapolating a bulk job's cost from its first slice.** → SYMPTOM: 5–6 GB
+reported to the operator, actual ~17 GB. → CAUSE: the first 202 packages were
+cheap `Instanced` cells; the builder's write order is not representative.
+→ CORRECT: blended sample, or say "provisional" out loud.

+**Zero untracked.** `-SetupHLODs` had created all 2,267 packages as ~130-byte
+stubs on 2026-09-08 and I committed them the same day. `-BuildHLODs` does not
+create files; it **inflates the existing ones in place**, 130 bytes to
+megabytes. Every single one was already in the index.
+
+`.gitignore` does not apply to tracked paths. Adding all 2,267 entries would
+have been accepted by git without complaint, changed nothing, and the ~17 GB
+would have gone into the next commit exactly as if the file did not exist.
+
+### Why this was nearly invisible
+
+The failure mode is the dangerous shape: **an operation that succeeds and does
+nothing.** `git check-ignore` on a tracked path still reports the pattern
+matches, `git status` still shows the file as modified, and the `.gitignore`
+diff looks like 2,267 lines of correct work. Nothing errors. The discovery
+would have come after the commit, when the repository was 17 GB heavier and the
+only remedy was history rewriting — the very item (`filter-repo`, 1.2 GB) this
+project already has open and has twice declined to start.
+
+The reason it was caught is a design decision made for a different reason. The
+first version of the script sorted candidates into "untracked" and "tracked",
+and **refused to write ignore entries for the tracked ones**, on the narrow
+grounds that ignoring a tracked path is a no-op that reads as success. It then
+printed the tracked count. That count was 202 and the untracked count was 0,
+and the plan fell over in one line of output.
+
+*The general rule: when a tool can do something that has no effect, make it
+refuse and report, not silently comply.* A script that had cheerfully written
+all 2,267 entries would have been indistinguishable from a correct one.
+
+### The correct operation, and why the timing is what saves us
+
+`git rm --cached` (drop from the index, keep on disk) **and** the ignore entry.
+Neither alone is sufficient: untracking without ignoring makes 2,267 files
+reappear as untracked noise, and ignoring without untracking does nothing.
+
+**The timing is the whole point.** The inflated packages have never been
+committed. Untracking them BEFORE any commit means the bloat never enters
+history at all — what history retains is the 130-byte stubs, about 300 KB in
+total, which is nothing. Had the build been committed first and untracked
+afterwards, the 17 GB would already be permanent and only a history rewrite
+would remove it.
+
+    committed then untracked   17 GB in history forever
+    untracked then committed   17 GB never in history
+
+Same two operations. The order is the entire difference, and it is a decision
+that has to be made before the first commit rather than noticed after it.
+
+### Identifying them is a rule-8 problem, not a path problem
+
+`git rm --cached` on a real actor would be a genuine defect, and World
+Partition hash-buckets HLOD packages into the SAME GUID directories as
+landscape proxies and foliage. Path tells you nothing. Neither does mtime
+alone — the build could touch a source actor.
+
+So membership is by **content signature**: a package is HLOD iff its bytes
+contain the class name `WorldPartitionHLOD`. Measured — a built HLOD package
+hits 3–7 times, a `LandscapeStreamingProxy` package hits 0, and the signature
+lands within the first 16 KB even in the 13.9 MB merged cell, so a 1 MB head
+read decides it with a full-file fallback only when the head is inconclusive.
+Of 202 rewritten files, 202 carried the signature and 0 did not.
+
+That is standing rule 8 applied where it was actually meant to apply: identify
+by property signature when the operation is irreversible, because actor labels
+and paths collide and an index removal is not something to get approximately
+right.
+
+### And the size estimate moved twice, in both directions
+
+    from one 13.9 MB merged cell      15-20 GB   (single sample)
+    from 202 packages, 494.9 MB       5-6 GB     (unrepresentative slice --
+                                                  mostly cheap Instanced cells)
+    from 422 packages, 3.2 GB on disk ~17 GB     (blended, and holding)
+
+The middle figure was reported to the operator and was wrong. It was an
+extrapolation from whichever packages happened to have been written first, and
+the builder does not write them in a representative order. **An extrapolation
+from a running job's first slice is a measurement of the order of work, not of
+the work.** Wait for a blended sample or say plainly that the number is
+provisional.

+## 2026-09-08e — the dolly luma drift is SHADE, not auto-exposure, and the percentiles say so before the eye does
+
+### The claim being tested
+
+REGISTER, 2026-09-06: mean luma drifts 0.3486 -> 0.2749 across the 8.4 m walk,
+"**That is auto-exposure adapting**", and the fix is an exposure read-back.
+
+The read-back was done on 2026-09-08 and **passed** — one unbound
+PostProcessVolume, `AEM_MANUAL`, bias -1.923 exactly as the recipe declares,
+min = max = 1.0, every override true, and neither `bench_capture.py` nor
+`shoot.py` contains the string "exposure" at all. So the setting was applied
+the whole time, and the diagnosis needed re-testing rather than the fix needing
+re-applying.
+
+### The measurement that separates the two hypotheses
+
+18 kept frames from `_verify/bench/2026-09-06/dev_dolly/dolly/`, decoded to
+linear and reduced to percentiles:
+
+    frame   p10      mean     p90
+    0000    0.0066   0.1712   0.4497
+    0140    0.0058   0.1171   0.4001    <- minimum
+    0170    0.0059   0.1200   0.3993
+
+    change  -11%     -30%     -11%
+
+**A global exposure change is a MULTIPLY.** It scales p10, the mean and p90 by
+the same factor. Here the mean falls three times as fast as either tail, which
+a multiply cannot do — it is mass moving from the lit part of the histogram
+into the dark part while both ends stay put. That is more dark CONTENT in the
+frame, not less gain.
+
+Two more things auto-exposure would not do:
+
+* **The curve turns around.** It falls to frame ~140 and then rises again
+  (0.1171 -> 0.1200) over the last 30 frames. Eye adaptation ramps toward a
+  target and settles; it does not settle and then reverse.
+* **The sky fraction moves with it** — 0.1642 at frame 40, 0.1426 at 170 — so
+  the framing itself changed what is in shot.
+
+### Confirmed by looking, which is where it becomes obvious
+
+Frame 0000: the foreground meadow is one broad, evenly sunlit expanse.
+Frame 0170: the same meadow is striped edge to edge with long conifer shadows.
+The camera walks out of a lit gap and into the shadow the tree stand throws
+across the slope. The sun is low, so the shadows are long and the transition
+covers most of the frame.
+
+**And the parts of the frame that did NOT change are the proof.** The sky is
+the same blue in both, and the sunlit faces of the houses are the same
+brightness in both. Under auto-exposure, a scene getting darker makes the
+camera open up, and the sky and the lit faces would BRIGHTEN. They are
+unchanged. Only the ground went into shadow.
+
+### The general form, worth more than this instance
+
+**A whole-frame mean cannot distinguish "the light changed" from "the subject
+changed".** Both move it in the same direction. The percentile spread can:
+a gain change moves every quantile by one factor, a content change moves the
+mean without moving the tails. That test is three lines of numpy and it settles
+in seconds a question that had stood as a confident wrong diagnosis for two
+days and had a fix built for it.
+
+Where this bites hardest: the fix that was built — the exposure read-back —
+was a GOOD thing to build and is now standing law under rule 12. It just was
+not the cause of this. **A correct fix for a misdiagnosed problem still leaves
+the problem**, and it is more dangerous than no fix, because the problem now
+looks addressed.
+
+### Status recorded, per the operator
+
+`temporal_stability.py` scores are NOT to be re-run against these frames — the
+research desk is replacing it with tile-wise motion compensation, and Weber
+normalisation against a LOCAL luminance cannot help when the local luminance is
+what legitimately changed. The dolly baseline stays unscored.
+
+**OPEN: shade along the walk is now the SUPPORTED reading, not merely the
+possible one.** What remains genuinely open is whether the dolly should be
+re-sited to a path that does not cross a shadow boundary, or whether the
+scorer should be expected to tolerate one. That is a question for the new
+scorer, not for the exposure system.

+## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08d: IT BUILDS. `-noxgecontroller` IS MANDATORY ON THIS MACHINE
+
+**Supersedes R-HLOD PENDING and the 2026-09-08c wedge status.** The build half
+is now PROVEN, and the read-back is on record.
+
+### The one line that must be on every HLOD commandlet
+
+    -noxgecontroller
+
+Without it, on this machine, the run wedges forever. With it, the same command
+finishes in 80 seconds. Single variable, measured both ways:
+
+    without   0 ShaderCompileWorker | 0.044 cores | never completes
+    with     14 ShaderCompileWorker | 0.44 cores  | Built 6 HLOD actors, 1:20
+
+### WHY, from source — and it is deliberate engine behaviour, not a fault
+
+`r.XGEController.AvoidUsingLocalMachine` defaults to **1**, documented at
+`XGEControllerModule.cpp:74-80` as *"Avoid spawning tasks on the local
+(initiator) machine **except when running a commandlet** or -buildmachine is
+passed"*. The implementation (:97-111):
+
+    return !bForceUsingLocalMachine && !GIsBuildMachine && !IsRunningCommandlet();
+
+So:
+
+    EDITOR      IsRunningCommandlet() false -> avoid local -> falls back to
+                LOCAL ShaderCompileWorkers -> compiles fine
+    COMMANDLET  IsRunningCommandlet() true  -> DOES use local XGE -> hands the
+                jobs to IncrediBuild -> they never return -> wedge
+
+The two log lines differ by one word and that word is the whole diagnosis:
+
+    editor      "XGE tasks will not be spawned on this machine."
+    commandlet  "XGE tasks will be spawned on this machine."
+
+IncrediBuild is installed here — `docs/environment.md` records it because its
+`Manager.exe` holds port 8000 — but it does not service these jobs.
+
+Switches, `XGEControllerModule.cpp:153-161`: `-noxgecontroller`,
+`-noxgeshadercompile`, `-noshaderworker` all set `Enabled = 0`. **Use
+`-noxgecontroller`** — `-noshaderworker` reads as though it would also suppress
+the local worker being fallen back to, so it is the wrong lever even though it
+sets the same variable.
+
+### THIS APPLIES TO EVERY COMMANDLET, NOT JUST HLOD
+
+Both `-SetupHLODs` runs on 2026-09-07/08 **also hung — on the way out.** Each
+logged `Engine exit requested ... result 0`, did all its work correctly, and
+then sat at 0.005 cores holding 2.1 GB and 4.5 GB until killed an hour later.
+`FShaderCompilingManager` drains on shutdown and jobs dispatched to XGE never
+drain.
+
+    RULE: a commandlet that prints "Engine exit requested" has NOT exited.
+    Check the process list, not the log line. Every commandlet run gets a
+    post-run process check.
+
+With `-noxgecontroller` the Setup rerun exited on its own.
+

+## 2026-09-08d — the wedge was in the log all along, in a category nobody grepped: shader compilation was routed to XGE
+
+### The line
+
+Every commandlet this project has run today says, twelve seconds after start:
+
+    LogXGEController: Display: Initialized XGE controller. XGE tasks will be
+                               spawned on this machine.
+    LogShaderCompilers: Display: Using XGE Controller for shader compilation
+
+**Shader compilation is not going to local `ShaderCompileWorker` processes at
+all. It is being dispatched to XGE — IncrediBuild.** That is why the wedge
+showed zero `ShaderCompileWorker.exe` processes: none was ever going to spawn.
+The absence was not a failure to launch a worker, it was a different code path.
+
+`ShaderCompileWorker.exe` exists and is intact
+(`Engine/Binaries/Win64/ShaderCompileWorker.exe`, 251,832 bytes), so the
+"rebuild the worker target" branch was never needed.
+
+**And this project already knew IncrediBuild was on this machine.**
+`docs/environment.md` records it, for an unrelated reason — its `Manager.exe`
+holds port 8000, which is why unreal-mcp had to move to 8001. The fact sat one
+index hop away from the diagnosis for a full session.
+
+### Why I did not find it yesterday
+
+I grepped `LogWorldPartitionHLODsBuilder` and the surrounding lines, because
+that is the system that appeared to be stuck. The cause was logged under
+`LogXGEController` and `LogShaderCompilers`, thirty-nine seconds earlier, in
+the startup banner that every run prints and nobody reads.
+
+The generalisable form: **when a subsystem blocks waiting on another
+subsystem, the failure is logged in the OTHER subsystem's category, usually at
+init.** Grepping the category of the thing that stopped finds the symptom. The
+cause is upstream and under a different tag. On a wedge, grep the startup
+banner for whatever the blocked operation depends on — here, "who is doing my
+shader compiles?" — before grepping the blocked system at all.
+
+Cheap and general: `-abslog` every commandlet, then grep the WHOLE log for the
+dependency, not the tail for the symptom.
+
+### The switch, from source rather than memory
+
+`XGEControllerModule.cpp:153-161`:
+
+    if (FParse::Param(..., TEXT("xgecontroller")))          Enabled = 1;
+    if (FParse::Param(..., TEXT("noxgecontroller"))    ||
+        FParse::Param(..., TEXT("noxgeshadercompile")) ||
+        FParse::Param(..., TEXT("noshaderworker")))        Enabled = 0;
+
+and `IsSupported()` returns `Enabled == 1` (:277). `-noxgecontroller` is the
+precise one; `-noshaderworker` reads as though it would also suppress the local
+worker we are trying to fall back to, so it is the wrong lever even though it
+happens to set the same variable.
+
+### THREE processes were wedged, not one, and two of them had "finished"
+
+Found at session start, still resident:
+
+    PID 29720  -SetupHLODs (Landscape)  alive 1h,  0.006 cores, 2,116 MB
+    PID 22912  -SetupHLODs (Instanced)  alive 30m, 0.003 cores, 4,550 MB
+
+**Both had logged `Engine exit requested (reason: Commandlet ... finished
+execution (result 0))` and neither ever exited.** They did all their work
+correctly — the 2,230 packages are on disk and verified — and then hung on the
+way out.
+
+That unifies the picture: `FShaderCompilingManager` blocks waiting for
+outstanding jobs to drain, and jobs dispatched to an XGE controller that never
+returns them never drain. So **every** wait-on-shaders point hangs — at
+shutdown for a Setup run, mid-build for a Build run. One cause, two symptoms,
+and the shutdown one was invisible because the log had already said `result 0`
+and I had stopped watching.
+
+**I recorded those two runs as complete last session.** Their WORK was
+complete; the processes were not. The build commandlet then started while both
+were alive, holding 6.7 GB between them. That did not cause the wedge — the
+wedge reproduces from the same XGE routing — but it means yesterday's build ran
+under contention I had not noticed and did not report.
+
+*Rule for the log: a commandlet that prints `Engine exit requested` has not
+exited. Check the process list, not the log line.* Every commandlet run from
+now on gets a post-run process check.

+## R-HLOD — AMENDED 2026-09-08b: A LAYER IS VALID BECAUSE A RUNTIME PARTITION REGISTERS IT
+
+**This amendment supersedes the layer-choice advice in the locked half above.**
+That advice said to pick a layer by loading range. Correct, but second — the
+FIRST question is whether the world will accept the layer at all, and this
+world rejects every layer it does not register.
+
+### The rule
+
+    an HLOD layer is NOT valid because the asset exists
+    NOT valid because actors point at it
+    NOT valid because it is the world default
+    VALID only if a runtime partition lists it in
+        RuntimePartitions[].HLODSetups[].HLODLayers
+
+`IsValidHLODLayer` has three implementations that disagree, and which one runs
+depends on the world's runtime hash CLASS:
+
+    UWorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash   WorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash.h:326
+                                        returns literal TRUE -- anything passes
+    UWorldPartitionRuntimeHash (base)   WorldPartitionRuntimeHash.h:225
+                                        returns literal FALSE
+    UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet       WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.cpp:377-380
+                                        the only REAL one; delegates to
+                                        ResolveRuntimePartitionForHLODLayer
+                                        (:388-435)
+
+**`/Game/Alpine8K` is a `WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet`** — read back from
+`...WorldSettings.WorldPartition_0.WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet_0`. So this
+world enforces registration and a SpatialHash world would not. Check the class
+before reusing any of this on another map.
+
+### THE REGISTRY IS NOT REACHABLE FROM PYTHON
+
+`RuntimePartitions` is `EditAnywhere` but **`private:`**
+(`WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.h:262-263`), and `FRuntimePartitionDesc` /
+`FRuntimePartitionHLODSetup` are bare `USTRUCT()` without `BlueprintType`
+(:27-29, :55-57). `get_editor_property("runtime_partitions")` fails.
+
+    CONSEQUENCE, and it is the standing instruction:
+    DO NOT AUTHOR NEW HLODLayer ASSETS FOR THIS WORLD.
+    Reuse a registered one and tune THAT asset's own fields, which ARE
+    reachable: layer_type, cell_size, loading_range, is_spatially_loaded.
+
+Registration itself is a World Settings panel edit or a C++ change.
+
+### WHAT THIS WORLD REGISTERS, read back 2026-09-08
+
+    /Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced   runtime grid MainPartition:HLODLayer_Instanced
+    /Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Merged      runtime grid MainPartition:HLODLayer_Merged
+
+and NOTHING else. `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_FoliageApprox` and
+`Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape`, both created 2026-09-07, are registered by
+nothing and are inert.
+
+### THE MEASUREMENT, single variable
+
+    world default = Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape
+        0 HLOD actors, 2,775 "invalid HLOD layer" errors, execution 1.41 s
+    world default = Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced
+        2,230 HLOD actors, 25 errors, execution 2.84 s
+
+Nothing else changed between the two runs. External actor packages for this
+world went 3,269 -> 5,499.
+
+### THE LABEL GRID, after Setup and before Build
+
+`-BuildSingleHLOD=` matches the actor LABEL exactly
+(`WorldPartitionHLODsBuilder.cpp:1134`), and labels are only knowable after
+Setup. **Do not try to pick a cell by proximity: before Build, every HLOD actor
+desc reports zero-extent bounds at the origin** — the actors exist, the
+geometry does not, so there is nothing to be near. Read the labels instead;
+they carry `<source>_L<level>_X<i>_Y<j>`.
+
+Measured grid, cell size DERIVED from the observed index span against the
+812,800 cm world extent rather than assumed from the layer asset's `cell_size`:

+### THE ORDER
+
+    1  read the runtime hash CLASS            hlod_hash_by_name.py
+    2  set the world default to a REGISTERED layer, save
+                                              hlod_save_world_default.py
+    3  -SetupHLODs                            creates the actors, no geometry
+    4  read the label grid, pick a cell       hlod_label_grid.py

+    6  verify the built actor has NON-ZERO bounds and a mesh

+runtime partition registers it; a standalone asset is registered by nothing.

+## 2026-09-08b — an HLOD layer is valid because a RUNTIME PARTITION registers it, not because it exists and is assigned; and this world is a HashSet, not a SpatialHash
+
+### The build ran, and made nothing
+
+`-SetupHLODs` completed cleanly — `result 0`, execution 1.41 s — and reported:
+
+    #### World HLOD actors ####
+    #### World contains 0 HLOD actors ####
+
+Underneath it, once per actor, 2,775 times:
+
+    Actor /Game/Alpine8K.City_St_622 has an invalid HLOD layer
+    /Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape.Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape
+
+Counted by layer, and the count is the whole story:
+
+    2,754   Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape      (the world default I had just set)
+       21   Alpine8K_HLODLayer_FoliageApprox  (yesterday's explicit assignments)
+        0   Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced      never mentioned
+
+Both layers created yesterday are invalid. The one that predated us is not
+named at all.
+
+### The mechanism, and it is specific
+
+The message is `WorldPartitionStreamingGenerationLogErrorHandler.cpp:143`,
+raised at `WorldPartitionStreamingGeneration.cpp:2037` when
+`IsValidHLODLayer(RuntimeGrid, HLODLayer)` returns false. There are three
+implementations and they disagree completely:
+
+    UWorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash::IsValidHLODLayer
+        WorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash.h:326    returns literal TRUE
+    UWorldPartitionRuntimeHash::IsValidHLODLayer   (base)
+        WorldPartitionRuntimeHash.h:225           returns literal FALSE
+    UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet::IsValidHLODLayer
+        WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.cpp:377-380  the only REAL one
+
+The HashSet delegates to `ResolveRuntimePartitionForHLODLayer` (:388-435),
+which finds the runtime partition for the actor's grid and then searches that
+partition's `HLODSetups` for an entry whose `HLODLayers` array **contains the
+layer object**. Not found → nullptr → invalid → the actor is dropped from HLOD
+generation.
+
+**So a `UHLODLayer` asset is not made valid by existing, and not by being
+assigned to actors, and not by being the world default. It is made valid by a
+runtime partition REGISTERING it** in
+`RuntimePartitions[].HLODSetups[].HLODLayers`. `hlod_setup_layers.py` created
+two layer assets and assigned them to 2,796 actors, and never touched that
+array, because nobody knew it existed. Every one of those assignments was
+inert by construction.
+
+### This world is a HashSet, and that has a second casualty
+
+Deduced first from the error itself — the SpatialHash returns a literal `true`,
+so the message could not have been raised under it — then **read back** from
+the engine: the object at
+`...WorldSettings.WorldPartition_0.WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet_0` has class
+`WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet`.
+
+That matters beyond HLOD. The research REGISTER's "three failed force-load
+levers" records lever 2 as
+`wp.Runtime.OverrideRuntimeLoadingRange -grid=MainGrid`, with the grid name
+established as the engine default from
+`WorldPartitionRuntimeSpatialHash.cpp:1387-1388` on the evidence of zero
+`SpatialHashRuntimeGridInfo` actors. **The absence of those actors was read as
+"the spatial hash is using its default grid name" when it also means "there is
+no spatial hash".** The lever was aimed at a grid namespace this world does not
+have, which is a candidate explanation for why the command echoed a successful
+`MaxLoadingStreamingCells` on the next line and changed nothing.
+
+I am NOT declaring that solved — the REGISTER's rule is eliminations with no
+invented cause, and this is a lead, not a measurement. It is recorded so the
+elimination can be re-judged against the right class.
+
+### The reasoning error, which is the same one as this morning's
+
+Yesterday's chain was: actors read `hlod_layer: None` → nothing points at the
+layers → assign them. This morning corrected the first link: `None` is the
+normal state because the world default supplies it at generation time.
+
+Both versions share an assumption nobody checked: **that pointing an actor at
+a layer is what makes HLOD happen.** The property read was accurate at every
+step and the model of what the system does with the property was wrong at every
+step. That is standing rule 9 at the level of behaviour rather than citation —
+a property tells you what it holds, never what the engine does with it — and
+today it produced two consecutive wrong causes for one symptom.
+
+The thing that finally settled it was not another property read. It was letting
+the builder run and reading what it complained about, which is the instrument
+that had never been used: **the system's own error path knows the rule, and it
+will say so in one line if you let it fail.** Sixteen minutes of commandlet
+against two days of inference.
+
+### The registry is not reachable from Python
+
+`UWorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet::RuntimePartitions` is `EditAnywhere`
+(`WorldPartitionRuntimeHashSet.h:262-263`) and **`private:`**, and
+`FRuntimePartitionDesc` / `FRuntimePartitionHLODSetup` are bare `USTRUCT()`
+without `BlueprintType` (:27-29, :55-57). `get_editor_property("runtime_partitions")`
+fails with "Failed to find property". So the HLOD registry can be edited from
+the World Settings panel or from C++, and not from a payload.
+
+**Consequence for how this project does HLOD: reuse the layer the world already
+registers, and tune THAT asset**, rather than authoring new layer assets that
+nothing can register. An `HLODLayer` asset's own fields — `layer_type`,
+`cell_size`, `loading_range`, `is_spatially_loaded` — are all reachable and
+were read back successfully today.
+
+### The property-exposure rule, now with four data points
+
+Measured on live 5.8 objects today, and it is a cleaner rule than "check the
+reflected surface":
+
+    default_hlod_layer   UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere)              REACHABLE
+    world_partition      UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, Instanced) REACHABLE
+    persistent_level     UPROPERTY(Transient)                 NOT reachable
+    runtime_hash         UPROPERTY()                          NOT reachable
+    runtime_partitions   UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere) but PRIVATE  NOT reachable
+
+**Edit/Visible specifier AND public — both, or Python cannot see it.** A bare
+`UPROPERTY()` is serialisation state; a private one is C++-internal however it
+is decorated. And `dir()` is not the test either: `default_hlod_layer` is
+absent from `dir(world_partition)` and `get_editor_property` returns it fine.
+
+### The prediction, and the test that confirmed it
+
+The mechanism above predicts something falsifiable: if validity comes from
+registration, then reverting the world default to the layer that predated us --
+`Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced`, the one the error log never named -- should
+build, with no other change.
+
+Set default back to Instanced (save 0.484 s, umap 13,915 -> 13,755 bytes,
+exactly reversing the +160 of the earlier change, which is itself a neat
+confirmation that the delta was that one property). Re-ran `-SetupHLODs`:
+
+    #### World contains 2230 HLOD actors ####
+    Execution took 2.84 sec
+    invalid HLOD layer errors: 25   (was 2,775)
+
+2,230 HLOD actor packages on disk; the external actor count for this world went
+3,269 -> 5,499. **The first `WorldPartitionHLOD` actors this project has ever
+had.**
+
+The 25 residual errors are exactly yesterday's bounded assignment -- the 21
+`InstancedFoliageActor`s explicitly pointed at `FoliageApprox` and the 4
+`LandscapeStreamingProxy`s pointed at `Landscape`. Those 25 actors are the only
+ones now EXCLUDED from HLOD, because an explicit unregistered layer overrides a
+valid default. Yesterday's assignment did not merely fail to help; for those 25
+it is actively subtractive, and clearing their `hlod_layer` back to None is
+what returns them to the working default.
+
+Single variable, and it moved: 0 -> 2,230 on the layer identity alone.

+and after) and there were **no `ShaderCompileWorker` children** — the only
+Unreal-family processes on the box were the editor itself, the launcher and the
+EOS helpers. Working set 15.1 GB of 31.4 GB.
+
+Yesterday's spin signature was recorded as: **5–6.6 cores, no log output, no
+files written, no DDC growth.** Every one of those four is also true of this
+world sitting idle, and the core count yesterday was *lower* than the idle
+baseline I just measured. So the CPU delta did not establish that the
+assignment caused anything. It established that the editor was doing what it
+always does here, which is consume about a third of a 24-thread machine while
+apparently asleep.
+
+**What I still cannot say is that nothing was wrong yesterday.** A save that
+does not finish in ninety minutes is a real failure and it is still
+unexplained. What is withdrawn is the *evidence* — the CPU reading was never
+evidence for the attribution, and the second "reproduction" reproduced the
+baseline as much as it reproduced any defect.
+
+Root cause of the reasoning error, and it is the same shape as the two logged
+yesterday: **an absolute reading was treated as a differential one.** "Six
+cores" only means something against "how many cores when idle", and that number
+had never been taken in this project. Two failed explanations on 2026-09-07
+were both A/B-with-two-variables; this is its neighbour, A-with-no-B.
+
+The lesson is not "take a baseline" in the abstract. It is that
+`docs/non-negotiables.md` rule 0 — instruments sharing a source are ONE
+measurement — has a sibling that was missing: **an instrument with no control
+is ZERO measurements.** The four signals cited yesterday (cores, silent log, no
+files, flat DDC) read as four corroborating instruments and were one
+unbaselined reading wearing four hats.
+
+### And the work it was blocking did not need doing
+
+`UWorldPartition::DefaultHLODLayer` (`WorldPartition.h:610-612`) is applied to
+every unassigned, spatially-loaded, HLOD-relevant actor at streaming-generation
+time by `ResolveHLODLayer` (`WorldPartitionStreamingGeneration.cpp:868-875`),
+through `SetRuntimeHLODLayer` (:549-553), which writes the streaming-generation
+VIEW and not the persisted actor desc (`WorldPartitionActorDesc.cpp:153`). No
+external actor package is touched. Full chain in the research REGISTER.
+
+Setting it and saving the map:
+
+    set        0.005 s
+    save       0.520 s   Alpine8K.umap 13,755 -> 13,915 bytes, mtime moved
+    read back  correct, from a chain re-resolved out of the world
+
+**0.5 seconds, one package, against ninety minutes and 2,796 dirtied actor
+packages for the same effect.** The bounded-radius bisect I was about to spend
+six editor launches on was going to characterise the cost of a path that did
+not need taking.
+
+### The correction that matters most, because it inverts yesterday's cause
+
+Before I changed anything, `default_hlod_layer` on this world already read
+`/Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced`. **It was set the whole time.**
+
+So yesterday's headline — "the layers existed and NOTHING POINTED AT THEM",
+"every actor class read `hlod_layer: None`, `SetupHLODActors` creates actors
+only for actors that have a layer, so nothing could build" — is **wrong at the
+causal step**. Actors reading `None` inherit the world default at generation
+time; that is what `ResolveHLODLayer` is for. The world was not missing an
+assignment. "Never built" has the duller cause that the build was never
+successfully run.
+
+The per-actor `hlod_layer: None` census was accurate. The inference drawn from
+it was not, because it was drawn without opening `ResolveHLODLayer` — the
+reading was taken from the actors and the *resolution rule* was assumed. That
+is standing rule 9's shape at the level of engine behaviour rather than
+citation: **a property read tells you what the property holds, not what the
+system does with it when it is empty.**
+
+The existing default is still the wrong layer for the job, which is a separate
+and much smaller point: `Instanced` is INSTANCING with `loading_range` 76800 cm
+= 768 m, *inside* the ~1 km World Partition streaming range it is meant to
+outlive, parented to a `Merged` layer whose own range is shorter still (51200)
+and which is not spatially loaded. Changed to `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape`
+(MESH_MERGE, 200000 cm = 2 km, spatially loaded, no parent).
+

+
+Logged because each cost a round trip, and `docs/ue58-api-protocol.md` is where
+they belong:
+

+    Package.is_dirty                            AttributeError
+
+The second is the instructive one. **Being a `UPROPERTY` in C++ is not
+sufficient for the Python attribute to exist**, so C++ source is where a
+hypothesis is FORMED and the live editor is where it is CONFIRMED. I had the
+source line and still guessed wrong.
+
+The route that works: `World.get_world_settings()` — a method on `World`, not
+on `GameplayStatics` — then `world_partition`, then `default_hlod_layer`. And
+`default_hlod_layer` **does not appear in `dir(world_partition)`** while
+`get_editor_property` reaches it perfectly well, so an absence from `dir()` is
+not an absence from the contract.
+
+The `AWorldSettings` actor is also invisible to
+`EditorActorSubsystem.get_all_level_actors()` — 0 hits across 3,269 actors.
+`GameplayStatics.get_all_actors_of_class(world, WorldSettings)` finds it.

+## R-HLOD — GIVING A WORLD PARTITION WORLD ITS HLOD LAYER (2026-09-08)
+
+**Status: the ASSIGNMENT half is PROVEN and locked. The BUILD half is not yet
+in this recipe** — see R-HLOD PENDING at the end. Do not read the locked half
+as licence to assume the build works.
+
+### The one thing to know
+
+**You almost certainly do not need to assign an HLOD layer to any actor.**
+A World Partition world has a world-level default, and the engine applies it to
+every actor that has none, at streaming-generation time, without writing to a
+single external actor package.
+
+    UWorldPartition::DefaultHLODLayer      WorldPartition.h:610-612
+                                           UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere,
+                                           DisplayName "Default HLOD Layer")
+      -> WorldPartitionStreamingGeneration.cpp:1384
+             MainContainerCollectionInstance.HLODLayer =
+                 FSoftObjectPath(WorldPartitionContext->GetDefaultHLODLayer())
+      -> :1425   ResolveHLODLayer(...)
+      -> :868-875
+             if (!GetHLODLayer().IsValid()
+                 && GetIsSpatiallyLoaded()
+                 && GetActorIsHLODRelevant())
+                     SetRuntimeHLODLayer(ParentHLODLayer);
+
+`SetRuntimeHLODLayer` (:549-553) writes the streaming-generation VIEW. The
+persisted value lives at `WorldPartitionActorDesc.cpp:153` and is left alone.
+
+### The procedure
+
+    payload  scripts/payloads/hlod_save_world_default.py
+    run      python scripts/ue_exec.py scripts/payloads/hlod_save_world_default.py \
+                 --set LAYER=/Game/Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape
+    probe    scripts/payloads/hlod_route_discovery.py    (read-only, no edits)
+
+**The route, and every hop is a casualty of guessing:**
+
+    world = UnrealEditorSubsystem.get_editor_world()
+    ws    = world.get_world_settings()                  METHOD ON WORLD
+    wp    = ws.get_editor_property("world_partition")
+    wp.set_editor_property("default_hlod_layer", load_asset(LAYER))
+    LevelEditorSubsystem.save_current_level()
+
+### MEASURED COST, on Alpine8K — 3,269 actors, 1,093 IFA, 256 proxies, 1,446 SMA
+
+    set                0.005 s
+    save               0.520 s
+    Alpine8K.umap      13,755 -> 13,915 bytes, mtime moved
+    actor packages     ZERO written
+    read-back          correct, chain re-resolved from the world
+
+Against the alternative, measured 2026-09-07: 2,796 actors assigned, 843.7 s to
+assign, and a save that had not finished after 90 minutes and was killed.
+
+### Verification is the file, not the return value
+
+`save_current_level()` returning `True` proves the call ran. Capture the
+`.umap` size and mtime **before and after** and report the delta. Standing
+rule 12 — the read-back comes from the artefact, and the re-read of
+`default_hlod_layer` must come from a chain resolved afresh out of the world,
+never from the object you just wrote to.
+
+### Choosing the layer, since the world may already have a wrong one
+
+Alpine8K already had `default_hlod_layer` set — to `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Instanced`,
+INSTANCING, `loading_range` 76800 cm. **A default HLOD layer whose loading range
+is INSIDE the World Partition streaming range does nothing you want**: the mesh
+is still streamed at that distance, so the HLOD never gets to be the thing you
+see. Its parent `Merged` was worse — range 51200, shorter than its own child,
+and `is_spatially_loaded` false.
+
+    rule   the HLOD loading range must EXCEED the WP streaming range
+           (~1 km on this world), and a parent layer must outlive its child
+
+Current: `Alpine8K_HLODLayer_Landscape`, MESH_MERGE, cell 25600, range 200000,
+spatially loaded, no parent.
+
+## R-HLOD REJECTED
+
+**Assigning `hlod_layer` per actor across the world.** Symptom: the assignment
+call itself returns cleanly (843.7 s for 2,796 actors, read-back correct) and
+then the SAVE does not complete — 90 minutes, killed; reproduced once with
+`save_dirty_packages()` and once with a per-package loop, so the save API is
+NOT the variable. Correct approach: set `DefaultHLODLayer` on the
+`UWorldPartition`, above. Reference: LESSONS 2026-09-07 (two entries) and
+2026-09-08.
+
+**Concluding "nothing points at the layers" from a per-actor `hlod_layer: None`
+census.** Symptom: you will believe HLOD cannot build and go assign 2,796
+actors. `hlod_layer: None` is the NORMAL state of an actor in a world that has
+a default — `ResolveHLODLayer` supplies it at generation time. Correct check:
+read `world.get_world_settings().get_editor_property("world_partition")
+.get_editor_property("default_hlod_layer")` FIRST. On Alpine8K it had been set
+the whole time. Reference: LESSONS 2026-09-08.
+
+**Judging an editor "spinning" from an absolute CPU-core reading.** Symptom:
+5–6.6 cores with a silent log, no files and flat DDC reads as a hang, and all
+four signals agree. Alpine8K's editor IDLES at **8.19–8.28 cores** with a
+byte-identical log and no `ShaderCompileWorker` children — higher than the
+reading taken as the defect. Correct approach: take the idle baseline in the
+same session, on the same loaded world, before attributing any CPU figure to
+anything. Reference: LESSONS 2026-09-08.
+
+**`unreal.GameplayStatics.get_world_settings`** — does not exist in 5.8.
+Symptom: `AttributeError: type object 'GameplayStatics' has no attribute
+'get_world_settings'`. Correct: `World.get_world_settings()`, a method on the
+world object.
+
+**`world.get_editor_property("persistent_level")`** — symptom: `Exception:
+World: Failed to find property 'persistent_level' ... on 'World'`, *despite*
+`UWorld::PersistentLevel` being `UPROPERTY(Transient)` at `World.h:952-953`.
+Being a UPROPERTY in C++ is not sufficient for the Python attribute to exist.
+Correct: `World.get_world_settings()` reaches WorldSettings directly.
+
+**`Package.set_dirty_flag` / `Package.is_dirty`** — both `AttributeError`.
+Symptom: the set succeeds and the save line raises, leaving the value live and
+unsaved. Correct: do not touch the dirty flag; `set_editor_property` marks the
+package, and `LevelEditorSubsystem.save_current_level()` writes it. Verify by
+the `.umap` mtime, not by the flag.
+
+**Looking for the WorldSettings actor in `EditorActorSubsystem.get_all_level_actors()`**
+— symptom: zero hits across 3,269 actors, and a probe that reports `null` for
+the whole chain. Correct:
+`GameplayStatics.get_all_actors_of_class(world, WorldSettings)`, or the
+`get_world_settings()` method.
+
+**Assuming `dir(obj)` is the property contract.** `default_hlod_layer` does not
+appear in `dir(world_partition)`; `get_editor_property("default_hlod_layer")`
+returns it correctly. Absence from `dir()` is not absence from the reflected
+surface.
+
+## R-HLOD PENDING — the build half, NOT yet proven
+
+Nothing in this project has ever successfully built a `WorldPartitionHLOD`
+actor. Zero exist under `Content/__ExternalActors__/Alpine8K/`. The assignment
+above is the precondition, not the result, and the acceptance test is a
+`mid_slope` capture whose `featureless_fraction` drops toward predicted sky
+from its measured 93.8%. Until that number moves, HLOD on this world is
+UNPROVEN and no budget or perception finding may rest on it.
