+## 2026-08-27 — THE WALK TEST STILL WORKS PERFECTLY. THE WORLD MOVED UNDER IT.
+
+Unit 10 owes a PIE residency figure at mounted speed. The tool for it is
+`walk_character.py`, which walked 1000.1 m cleanly on 2026-08-15 and has been
+stamped PROVEN since. It ran twice today and STALLED both times, at 29.2 m and
+58.4 m.
+
+**Nothing about the tool regressed. The spawn moved into a town.**
+
+On 2026-08-26 the `PlayerStart` moved from a forest clearing 8,245 m out to the
+basin town, at yaw 35 *facing the landmark* — deliberately, because the landmark
+is the first thing a player should see. The landmark is an 11 × 11 × 34 m solid
+volume 29 m away, and `walk_character` drives the pawn in a straight line with
+no steering.
+
+So the first run walked into it and stood there for 291 seconds. **The stall
+report was the instrument being right**, and for about a minute I read it as the
+instrument being broken.
+
+### THE PREMISE THAT EXPIRED WITHOUT ANYONE EDITING IT
+
+R-WALKTEST's procedure says *"a straight line on a declared heading from the
+spawn point, and says so"*, and it was careful about the one limitation it knew
+of — that this is not the inter-massif corridor. It could not be careful about a
+limitation that did not exist when it was written: **the spawn was in a forest,
+where the only obstacles are foliage the walker brushes past.**
+
+A recipe stamped PROVEN records that a procedure worked *against the world it
+was proven on*. Nothing re-checks that premise when the world changes, and the
+town landed a full day before this ran. This is the same shape as R13's
+CALIBRATION CLASS — a number that is not wrong, but belongs to conditions that
+have moved — except here it is a PROCEDURE rather than a figure, and procedures
+do not usually carry their calibration class.
+
+### THE SECOND HEADING WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT AND STILL FAILED
+
+Rather than guess again, `scripts/find_clear_heading.py` marches every bearing
+against the 1,446 planned footprints, inflated by the pawn's 34 cm capsule so
+contact happens at a wall rather than at a centre:
+
+    from the PlayerStart, to 1200 m
+      including street slabs   0 of 360 bearings clear, first blocker at 57 m
+      excluding street slabs   9 of 360 (2.5%)
+      widest clear arc         3.0 deg, centred on bearing 259
+
+Bearing 259 was taken from that, and the pawn contacted a building at 58.4 m
+anyway. **A 3° arc is 2.6 m wide at 50 m**, and an unsteered walker drifts more
+than that. The tool reports the arc's CENTRE and warns in its own output that a
+clear bearing with blocked neighbours is a gap between two buildings — which is
+exactly what 3° is. The warning was right and 3° was never enough.
+
+**The finding worth carrying is the first row: with street slabs counted, ZERO
+of 360 bearings are clear.** The town does not merely obstruct a straight walk
+out of it; it forecloses one.
+
+### WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN WHAT I DID
+
+Residency WAS sampled on both runs: 3–4 landscape proxies, 10–11 foliage actors.
+That is a real number from a real PIE session and it is **residency at rest,
+inside a town** — the pawn spent 291 s and 175 s of those runs stationary.
+
+Reporting it as "streaming at mounted speed" would have closed the owed item on
+the board today. It is arithmetically true and it answers a question nobody
+asked — non-negotiable 22, the misleading denominator. The owed figure is
+residency UNDER MOTION, and it is still not obtained.
+
+**The instrument half did land and is proven.** `--speed-cm-s` is gated twice:
+the property must read back within 0.5 *and* the trace's own achieved speed must
+reach 0.9 of commanded. The second gate returned **p50 1800, max 1800, = 1.00**.
+Only the first would have been the read-back-the-field-you-wrote error — a pawn
+capped by acceleration or root motion reads 1800 on the component while
+travelling at 600, and the artefact would certify streaming at a speed nothing
+ever moved at.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**A PROVEN PROCEDURE CARRIES THE WORLD IT WAS PROVEN ON.** When a world-shaping
+change lands — a settlement, a spawn move, a terrain adoption — the tools whose
+premises that change touches have not been re-proven, and their stamps do not
+know it. The cheap version of this is not re-proving everything; it is asking,
+at the moment of the change, *which instrument's assumptions did I just
+invalidate.* Moving the PlayerStart into a town invalidated the straight-line
+walker, and the entry that recorded the move did not mention it.
+

commit 09e9ba24c967d77e1500a4158252f98b625bc1b4
Author: ryanb <ryanbme83@gmail.com>
Date:   2026-08-27 10:10:14 -0700

    Unit 11's acceptance criterion is MET, and the pair that is NOT separated says so
    
    The independent check landed on the third attempt. R-SURFACE joins RECIPES as
    the third new-element recipe of the day.
    
        samples 30,000   usable 10,881 (36.3%)   off the landscape 19,006
        Snow  0.7703      Rock  0.7064      Grass  0.6940   mean linear luma
        Snow brighter than Rock  +0.0638      than Grass  +0.0763    bar 0.02
    
    ⭐ THIS IS THE DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION THE UNIT ASKED FOR. Every earlier check
    compared the lookup to the material's INPUT -- the same weightmap -- and
    non-negotiable 0 says instruments sharing a source are one measurement. A render
    is the material's OUTPUT. Snow's base colour is 1,1,1 over Snow006, so it should
    be the brightest surface in the palette, and it is, by three times the bar.
    
    ⛔ AND ROCK AGAINST GRASS IS NOT SEPARATED BY IT. 0.0124 apart against
    standard deviations of 0.10-0.12 -- inside the noise. The tool DELIBERATELY DOES
    NOT ASSERT THAT PAIR, and the recipe, the artefact and CURRENT STATE all say so.
    Snow is corroborated by two representations; the Rock/Grass distinction rests on
    provenance alone and would need chroma rather than luma, or a flat-lit rig.
    
    Reporting a pass that quietly covered only one of three comparisons would have
    been the more comfortable option and the wrong one.
    
    THE ASSERTION IS ORDERING WITH A MARGIN, not equality, and it cannot be
    equality: the material blends three photogrammetry surfaces under a low sun with
    fog and a tonemapper, so no pixel value "is" Rock. The ordering belongs to the
    material's layer definitions; the absolute values belong to the lighting rig.
    
    ⚠ 36.3% OF SAMPLES USABLE, reported rather than hidden -- a 90 deg frame from
    9 km covers 16.9 x 10.6 km against an 8.1 km landscape, so most samples land off
    the map. The tool REFUSES below 20%, because a filter that removes most of the
    data cannot support a conclusion.
    
    TWO MAPPING TRAPS, both handled and both easy to get silently wrong: UE's FOV is
    HORIZONTAL so the vertical half-extent scales by height/width, and the
    projection plane is the MEAN TERRAIN HEIGHT (523 m) rather than z=0 -- over
    1.5 km of relief, assuming zero shifts every sample outward. Either mistake
    produces plausible-looking numbers about the wrong pixels.
    
    ⚠ AND THE EDITOR WAS NEVER HUNG. It read responding=False for minutes while

+## R-SURFACE — WHAT AM I STANDING ON, ON THE CPU (2026-08-27)
+
+**Status: PROVEN, with one pair explicitly NOT separated.** The acceptance
+clause is met for Snow against both other layers, by a render -- a different
+representation from the weightmap the lookup and the material share. **Rock
+against Grass is corroborated only by PROVENANCE**, differing by 0.0124 in mean
+luma inside a 0.10-0.12 standard deviation. `PHASE2_PLAN` unit 11.
+
+New element type: a **CPU surface-type lookup** — for footstep audio, movement
+modifiers and VFX, answered without asking the renderer.
+
+### 1. PRECONDITIONS
+
+- `textures/<biome>_weights.png` exists, baked by `make_layer_weightmap.py`.
+  **It is the material's own source and must not be re-derived here.**
+- The recipe declares exactly **three** `material.layers`, in channel order
+  R, G, B. `make_layer_weightmap` refuses at four for the same reason: RGB has
+  three channels and there is no fourth.
+- numpy, Pillow. No editor. No plugins.
+- Every layer carries a `surface` key naming its photogrammetry set, or the
+  query can report a layer and not a material.
+
+### 2. EXACT VALUES
+
+| Parameter | Locked | Range | What it affects |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `--samples` | **20000** | ≥ 1000 | size of the positive control |
+| `--seed` | **20260827** | any | which points the control draws; printed so any run is reproducible |
+| blend-boundary threshold | **dominance < 16** | 0–255 | what the query calls `on_blend_boundary` |
+| R channel | dominant layer index, recipe order | 0..N-1 | the answer |
+| G channel | dominance = winner − runner-up | 0..255 | blend depth |
+| B channel | **0, DECLARED INERT** | — | non-negotiable 21 |
+
+Measured on `alpine_8k`: Snow **21.3758%**, Rock **37.3012%**, Grass
+**41.3230%**; dominance p10 167 / p50 255 / p90 255; genuine blend boundary
+**1.04%** of the map.
+
+**DOMINANCE IS BLEND DEPTH, NOT CONFIDENCE.** The material blends; it does not
+choose. A cell at dominance 4 is genuinely half rock and half grass, and a
+consumer wanting one answer there is asking a question the world does not have.
+The query returns the weights so the caller can decide.
+
+### 3. ORDERED STEPS
+
+1. `python scripts/bake_surface_lookup.py` — report only. Read the layer shares
+   against expectation before writing anything.
+2. `python scripts/bake_surface_lookup.py --write` — writes
+   `textures/<biome>_surface.png` and its sidecar. **Both controls must pass or
+   nothing is written.**
+3. `python scripts/stamp_plan.py textures/<biome>_surface.json`.
+4. `python scripts/surface_query.py --selftest`.
+5. Query: `python scripts/surface_query.py --at X_CM Y_CM`.
+
+### 4. VERIFICATION
+
+| Check | Measured | Bar |
+|---|---|---|
+| POSITIVE control — N points re-derived straight from the weightmap by code that did not build the arrays | **20000 of 20000** | 100% |
+| NEGATIVE control — the same lookup shifted ONE ROW must stop agreeing | **9.86% disagree** | > 1% |
+| round trip — R channel survives the PNG write | equal | exact (PNG is lossless) |
+| inert B reads back zero | zero | exact |
+| selftest — a TAMPERED sha256 in the sidecar is REFUSED | refused | must refuse |
+| selftest — 50 km off the landscape returns **None** | None | not a surface |
+| sanity — the town plaza reads Grass at dominance 255 | Grass 255 | a town is sited on meadow |
+
+**THE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE, MET BY A DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION.** Every check above
+compares the lookup to the material's INPUT -- the same weightmap -- and
+non-negotiable 0 says instruments sharing a source are one measurement. A
+top-down RENDER is the material's OUTPUT.
+`python scripts/verify_surface_against_render.py --frame <top-down png>`:
+
+    samples 30,000   usable 10,881 (36.3%)   off the landscape 19,006
+    Snow  0.7703      Rock  0.7064      Grass  0.6940   (mean linear luma)
+    Snow brighter than Rock  +0.0638      than Grass  +0.0763   bar 0.02
+
+**⛔ AND ROCK AGAINST GRASS IS NOT SEPARATED BY IT** -- 0.0124 apart against
+standard deviations of 0.10-0.12, inside the noise. The tool deliberately does
+not assert that pair. So Snow is corroborated by two representations and the
+Rock/Grass distinction rests on PROVENANCE alone; separating it would need
+chroma rather than luma, or a flat-lit rig.
+
+Only 36.3% of samples are usable, because a 90 deg frame from 9 km covers
+16.9 x 10.6 km against an 8.1 km landscape. Reported, not hidden -- the tool
+refuses below 20%, because a filter that removes most of the data cannot
+support a conclusion.
+
+### 5. REJECTED
+
+- **Painting landscape layers to get this.** It forks the surface definition —
+  the painted layers and the baked weightmap become two sources for one physical
+  fact. `PHASE2_PLAN` unit 11 names it; non-negotiable 19 is the general rule.
+- **Deriving the surface from slope and height at query time.** That is a SECOND
+  implementation of the selection the weightmap already encodes, and it would
+  drift the moment a band moved.
+- **Reading `dominance` as confidence in the lookup.** It is a property of the
+  WORLD, not of the bake. Low dominance means "the material draws both here".
+- **Asking this for WALKABILITY.** `IsWalkable` reads
+  `HitComponent->GetWalkableSlopeOverride()`, a **PER-COMPONENT** override, and
+  one landscape component here is 254 m square. "Scree is unwalkable" is
+  gameplay logic on top of the query, never a landscape setting.
+- **Leaving the B channel unwritten.** A channel nobody assigns carries whatever
+  the allocator left, reads like data, and is sampled by something eventually
+  (non-negotiable 21). It is written zero AND the code says so.

+## 2026-08-27 — AN INSTRUMENT CAN OUTLIVE THE WORLD IT WAS BUILT FOR
+
+Unit 5's acceptance clause is *"walk 1 km without falling through and without a
+step-height stall"*, and `walk_character.py` implements it by driving a STRAIGHT
+LINE from the PlayerStart with no steering. It passed on 2026-08-15 at 1000.1 m.
+
+Today it stalled at **27.3 m**, and then at **57.5 m** on a second heading.
+
+**Nothing about the world got worse. A town was built on the spawn.** The
+PlayerStart now sits in a plaza ringed by 303 buildings, and measured over 72
+headings: **65 are blocked within 100 m, and the best runs 156 m.** A 1 km
+straight walk from this spawn is impossible in every direction.
+
+R-WALKTEST already carried the sentence that explains it — *"a straight-line
+walker with no steering stops there forever; that is the test's property, not
+the world's"* — written when every heading from the spawn was open ground. **The
+sentence stayed true and its consequence inverted**, because the world moved
+underneath it. That is a different failure from a stale claim: nothing in the
+record was wrong, and the instrument still silently stopped measuring what it
+was built to measure.
+
+**The narrow thing the walks DO prove is worth keeping:** `is_falling` 0.1% over
+2,312 samples across both runs. The ground holds. Traversability at scale is
+proven better elsewhere — 36.5 km² reachable by path query — so the walk test's
+remaining job is local, not global, and it should be described that way.
+
+### AND A PREFILTER WAS WRONG, THEN CALIBRATED, WHICH IS THE PART TO KEEP
+
+`find_walk_heading.py` picks a heading offline so a PIE run is not spent
+guessing. Its first version read the heightmap and the city plan, called yaw 260
+clear for 238 m, and the character stalled at 57.5.
+
+**Its own docstring had predicted that failure** — it could not see foliage, and
+~3,700 trees stand in the gaps between structures. Trees are query-collidable BY
+DESIGN (R-TREECOLLIDE made them so and a PIE trace proved it), so a trunk stops
+a straight-line walker exactly as a wall does.
+
+219,659 tree positions were already on disk in `foliage/*.json`, so seeing them
+cost a file read rather than an editor query. It now predicts both measured
+stalls, and predicts them CONSERVATIVELY:
+
+    yaw   model says             character measured
+     30   22 m (building at 24)      27.3 m
+    260   42 m (tree at 44)          57.5 m
+
+**Conservative is the right direction for a tool used to CHOOSE a test.** A
+prefilter that overshoots sends you to run an expensive test that fails; one
+that undershoots merely costs you a slightly better option.
+
+`--no-foliage` is kept so the improvement stays MEASURABLE rather than asserted:
+47 of 72 headings blocked without trees, 65 of 72 with them. A tool that quietly
+got better cannot be checked later.
+
+**And the docstring and the printed footer were both updated**, because "It
+cannot see foliage" became false the moment it could. Stale prose in a tool's
+own self-description is the defect this project keeps finding in other people's
+files, and it takes about a minute to introduce.
+
+### THE THIRD THING, AND IT IS OPERATIONAL
+
+**I orphaned a tick driver.** A 120 s tool timeout killed `walk_character`'s
+driver process while its `register_slate_post_tick_callback` kept running inside
+the editor — logging to nobody for 410 s, and after PIE ended it was ticking
+against a dead world. The tool's cleanup runs on ITS completion paths, which a
+killed driver never reaches.
+
+Stopped externally by ending PIE; the callback count went 47 → 47 over 25 s,
+which is how I know it stopped rather than assuming. **A tool that installs an
+ENGINE callback needs an external stop, not only an internal one** — because the
+thing most likely to kill it is not its own code path.
+

    thing that needed it. An encounter is a plan row, not an actor.

+## 2026-08-27 — THE AUDIT CAUGHT ME WRITING ASPIRATIONAL DOCUMENTATION
+
+Unit 10's first half — `AEncounterMarker` and `UEncounterDirectorSubsystem` —
+went to the auditor before first compilation. Seven findings, three major, and
+**the sharpest was about my own prose rather than my code.**
+
+The director's header said the subsystem *"owns the spawn and despawn of
+encounter pawns"*, that *"the pawn is spawned at bIsSpatiallyLoaded = false"*,
+and carried a bold rule that *"SPAWNING REFUSES WHEN NAVMESH PROJECTION FAILS"*.
+
+**It spawned nothing. It despawned nothing. It owned no pawns.** Two counters
+tallied refusals of spawns that could never have happened. There is no enemy
+pawn class yet — that is unit 12 — and I had written the header for the class I
+intended rather than the class I wrote.
+
+This is non-negotiable 25 in its purest form, and the mechanism is worth naming:
+**a header written before the implementation describes the design; a header left
+unedited after a smaller implementation describes a lie.** The gap was never a
+decision. Nothing re-checks a comment, so the moment the scope narrowed the
+prose became false and stayed false silently. The header now leads with what the
+class does NOT do, and says where the missing half lives.
+
+### THE TWO LOGIC DEFECTS BOTH CAME FROM THE SAME WRONG MODEL
+
+I wrote the director as if a marker were a stable object. It is not — markers are
+spatially loaded BY DESIGN, which is the entire point of the class.
+
+**Discovery was single-shot and wrong in both directions.** Rescanning only when
+`Markers.Num() == 0` meant a world with genuinely zero markers walked a full
+`TActorIterator` over 2,500+ external actors every half-second forever; and once
+ONE marker was found the list never returned to empty — stale weak pointers
+still count toward `Num()` — so **every marker that streamed in later was
+invisible to the director permanently.** The comment promising "the next
+evaluation retries once the chunk arrives" was false for the same reason.
+
+**Active state keyed on the actor pointer lost identity across exactly the event
+the design exists to survive.** A `TWeakObjectPtr` hashes on object index and
+serial number, so a marker streamed out and back is a DIFFERENT key. Stale
+entries were removed nowhere, so the set grew without bound — and the
+per-evaluation recount of active encounters, which I had written as a
+correctness measure, was *masking* the leak: the reported number stayed sane
+while the set diverged from it with no instrument watching.
+
+The durable identity was already on the marker: `(PlanId, PlanRowIndex)`, the
+plan row it came from, which I had put there for traceability and then not used
+for the one thing that needed it. **An encounter is a plan row, not an actor** —
+so a site whose marker streams out now stays active deliberately, because its
+cell coming and going is not the player leaving it.
+
+### WHAT THE AUDIT DID NOT FIND, AND WHY THAT MATTERS TOO
+
+Zero compile or link defects. Every API name — the subsystem base and its
+override signatures, `bIsSpatiallyLoaded` as a constructor write, the three-arg
+`ProjectPointToNavigation`, the stat macro, `SetHidden` in a constructor — was
+checked at engine source and confirmed. **The design was buildable and the
+reasoning was wrong**, which is the split this project keeps rediscovering:
+getting the number right from a wrong premise produces confident, wrong output.
+
+It built clean first try in 16.4 s and verified on a cold boot: both classes
+reflected, 7 of 7 and 6 of 6 properties reading back, `is_spatially_loaded`
+true, the hysteresis invariant asserted on the shipped defaults, and a negative
+control confirming a class that should not resolve does not.
+
+**Still unproven, and stated rather than implied:** no marker actor exists in any
+level, the director has never ticked against a real marker, and unit 10's
+acceptance test has not run. A reflected name is not a working feature.
+

+## 2026-08-27 — THE WORLD BECOMES WALKABLE, AND WHAT CALIBRATION IS ACTUALLY FOR
+
+Full navmesh coverage: 72 volumes from one recipe declaration, 64 chunk actors,
+**36.53 km² of ground the player can reach** against 1.5 km² yesterday.
+
+The ruling was fable's under the operator's standing delegation, and the useful
+thing it did first was **find that the decision had already been taken**.
+`PHASE2_PLAN:250` reads *"Unit 8 builds one chunk. The other 63 are a decision,
+not a plan"*, and unit 8's own note rules the navigable region to be authored,
+versioned recipe data. I had framed this as "how much navmesh does the content
+need" and was told the prior question is different and already answered: **the
+ruled boundary is the region edge, so every metre between the navmesh edge and
+the region edge is an unruled invisible wall** — and this project had just spent
+a week diagnosing one of those as a sealed basin.
+
+### THE CALIBRATION EARNED ITS COST TWICE, AND NEITHER TIME WAS "IS IT SAFE"
+
+    volumes    nav MB    wall s    peak GB    chunk actors
+       2        35.18      36.0      20.0        10
+       3        48.14      42.0      20.4        12
+       9       116.01      46.0      20.6        16
+      72       756.58     110.0      22.2        64
+
+**FIRST: the two-volume figures were unrepresentative in a way I could not have
+guessed.** They came from the only two tiles in the region that are basin-flat
+AND had 2,541 trees cleared out of them. A full-density forest tile (6,782
+trees) cost +12.96 MB and +6 s — and bought **+0.76 km² of reachable ground from
+a 1.08 km² tile**, which is the number that actually matters and which no cost
+figure would have produced.
+
+**SECOND, AND IT CHANGED THE PLAN: THE BUILDER IS NOT INCREMENTAL.** 13 packages
+created, 10 DELETED. It discards every chunk actor and regenerates. So per-tile
+cost is not additive across runs, and the batching I had planned bounds RISK —
+learning the curve as you go — rather than bounding peak memory, which is what I
+had assumed it was for. Peak commit then turned out to be nearly flat (20.0 →
+22.2 GB across a 36× increase in coverage) because the builder streams cells.
+
+**The predictions from the 9-volume point held**: ~830 MB predicted against
+756.58 actual, and every bar cleared with room. That is what a cost curve is
+for — not reassurance, but the ability to say what the next order of magnitude
+costs before paying for it.
+
+### TWO INDEPENDENT CALCULATIONS OF THE SAME THING AGREED
+
+The recipe's own tile-budget check computes 388,622 tiles for the union; the
+engine's own warning reports `maxTiles` calculated at 401,843. **3.4% apart,
+from completely different code**, and 38% of the 1,048,576 hard limit. The
+engine recreated its `dtNavMesh` at 19 bits to hold them — handling the growth
+rather than clamping, which is the failure mode the budget check exists to
+prevent.
+
+### AND THE GUARDS BUILT THIS WEEK ALL FIRED, ON REAL DRIFT
+
+**The binding check refused to merge two navmesh builds.** Installing the new
+region lattice made `reachability.py` say: *"the lattice was measured against 64
+navmesh chunk actors and the town sidecar against 10 — different builds."* That
+check was added the same morning after finding a sidecar declaring 8 chunks
+against a world with 10, where the staleness happened to cost nothing. **A
+staleness that happens not to matter is the most durable kind**, and this is
+what it was insurance against.
+
+**The stamps caught a cross-cutting change.** Adding 72 volumes to
+`recipes/alpine_8k.json` moved an input of the town plan, four foliage plans and
+the lattice; every one reported STAMP DIFFERS naming that file. All were
+regenerated and compared field by field: **content that moved, NOTHING.** 303
+buildings, 838 streets, 219,659 trees byte-identical. The stamp did exactly the
+job it was written for — it did not tell me something was wrong, it told me
+what to re-derive and then let me prove nothing had.
+
+### THE ENCOUNTER GATE REFUSED TWICE, AND THE SECOND REFUSAL WAS THE LESSON
+
+At the shipped 60 m proximity radius, 7 of 440 encounters projected but were not
+reachable. Tightening to 30 m gave 3 of 320 — and **one survivor sits 8.1 m from
+a reachable lattice cell.**
+
+An 8 m miss is not a resolution problem. Those are genuine small pockets, ground
+beside the reachable region across a gap the agent will not cross, and **no
+radius separates them from legitimate ground without discarding most of the
+region.** Proximity to a sampled lattice is a PREFILTER; the path query is the
+authority, and tightening the prefilter further would have been fitting it to
+the answer — the exact thing this project refused to do to the offline
+walkability model.
+
+**So the navmesh's verdict feeds FORWARD instead.** The plan stays
+byte-reproducible at `encounters/<region>_all.json`; the adopted set at
+`_verified.json` is the plan minus what the navmesh refused, hash-stamped
+against BOTH sources. Editing the plan in place would have destroyed the
+property `check_plan_freshness --reproduce` exists to test. **A placer reads the
+verified file; a plan stays a plan.**
+
+**One radius rule worth keeping:** a proximity radius must be well INSIDE the
+resolution of the measurement it queries, never equal to it. 60 m against a 60 m
+lattice admits a candidate a full cell from anything measured.
+
+### WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY
+
+**Nothing was placed.** 317 verified encounter sites exist and nothing spawns
+them. Writing a placer is unblocked; running it is not, because placing
+wilderness content sits behind `WORLD_VISION` item 4's POI tripwire, which
+reserves reconfirmation to the operator. Generation is delegated; placement is
+not, and the difference was stated in the ruling rather than discovered later.
+

+## 2026-08-27 — THE SAMPLE WAS THE LIMIT, NOT THE WORLD (unit 9 closes)
+
+With the search-budget error corrected, the whole chain it had blocked came
+apart in one sitting. Three separate defects, and every one of them was about
+WHERE WE LOOKED rather than what was there.
+
+### 1. A "GROUND" TRACE THAT DOES NOT EXCLUDE WHAT STANDS ON THE GROUND
+
+The rewritten reachable-region payload traced the collidable ground before
+projecting — correct in principle, and a genuinely better datum than the plan's
+own heightmap-derived z. It excluded FOLIAGE from the trace and nothing else.
+
+The result looked like a regression: 17 streets reachable in the old sidecar and
+unreachable in the new one, reproducibly, all of them projecting. Measured from
+both datums side by side:
+
+    reachable from planned z    17 of 17
+    reachable from ground z      0 of 17
+    planned - ground         -1293 cm
+
+**Twelve point nine metres.** The trace was landing on BUILDING ROOFS, and a
+navmesh projection from roof height finds no reachable polygon.
+
+`city_verify_payload.txt` already carried that exclusion, with a comment saying
+exactly why — *"otherwise a building traces onto its neighbour's roof"* — and I
+had read that comment earlier the same day. With city actors ignored: **136
+gained, 0 lost**, a strict superset of the old measurement, which is what a
+correct relay must be.
+
+**A trace answers "what is above this point", not "where is the ground".** The
+difference only shows up where something is standing there.
+
+### 2. THE REACHABLE REGION SAMPLED ONLY THE TOWN, SO NOTHING OUTSIDE IT COULD EVER QUALIFY
+
+The sidecar's rows are street midpoints and building doorsteps — every one
+INSIDE the settlement. So `near_reachable` returned True only inside the town,
+and the encounter rule *"OUTSIDE the settlement AND near reachable ground"* was
+**unsatisfiable by construction.**
+
+That is what produced "the basin cannot hold encounters", and I wrote it up as a
+fact about the world — *"in this basin those are the SAME GROUND"* — with a
+`WORLD_VISION` citation about remoteness to explain why it was correct and even
+desirable. **The reasoning was elegant and the premise was an artefact of the
+sample.** A satisfying explanation for a measurement is not evidence the
+measurement is right; if anything it makes the measurement harder to doubt.
+
+The fix is a LATTICE over the whole built navmesh — grid BFS, a cell joins when
+a path exists from an already-reachable 4-neighbour:
+
+    cells 1431 at 40 m over 2.163 km2   projecting 1423   REACHABLE 1261
+    path queries 1557 -- about one per cell
+
+**Every query is between ADJACENT cells**, so none approaches the search budget.
+That is the same transitive-closure idea as the relay, done cheaply enough to
+cover a whole region rather than a list of features.
+
+Then: available 6191 of 8646 cells (71.61%) = 1.549 km², target 6, **placed 6**,
+and all six VERIFIED reachable in the editor against the built navmesh.
+
+### 3. THE VERIFIER CARRIED THE VERY DEFECT IT WAS CHECKING FOR
+
+`city_encounter_verify_payload` reported all 6 encounters unreachable on its
+first run. It asked one query from the spawn. It now tries direct, then relays
+off the nearest measured lattice point, and only a failure of BOTH is
+unreachable.
+
+**All six come back via RELAY and none directly** — which is exactly what
+"outside the settlement" should look like, and is a small independent
+confirmation that the budget, not the ground, was the limit.
+
+**AND THAT MADE ITS LENGTH FIELD A LIE.** A relay length is only the last leg,
+from an anchor at most one lattice step away. `path_len_m` read 15.2–60.0 m for
+encounters sited outside a 940 m town. Every row now records WHICH leg answered,
+the summary counts them, and the length range is renamed
+`path_len_m_DIRECT_ONLY` with relay rows excluded. **A number whose meaning
+depends on a branch must carry the branch.**
+
+### WHAT THE WORLD ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE NOW
+
+The corrected relay sweep, 12 bearings to 1500 m:
+
+    furthest 1050 m   median 600 m   min 350 m
+
+and almost every ray stops **exactly on a NavBounds volume edge** — bearing 0 at
+x −1598 against an east edge of −1588; bearing 90 at y 3308 against a north edge
+of 3308; bearing 150 at x −2628 against a west edge of −2628. **The playable
+world is bounded by where navmesh was BUILT, not by terrain.** That is a
+completely different situation from a sealed basin, and an entirely fixable one.
+

commit e3ed8ba0103821e62d975769cd3ac2f15d8b20f4
Author: ryanb <ryanbme83@gmail.com>
Date:   2026-08-26 22:23:45 -0700

    One command for the offline suite, and FINDINGS are not FAILURES
    
    scripts/run_offline_suite.py. Eight checks, ~100 s, no editor, no world, no
    network -- the command that answers "is the repo healthy" before any editor
    work starts.
    
    ⛔ THE REASON IT EXISTS IS AN EXIT CODE THAT MEANS THE TOOL IS WORKING.
    check_plan_freshness returns 3 when a plan is stale. Left in prose, "exit 3 is
    fine here" is a fact that rots: the next person runs the suite, sees non-zero,
    and either panics or learns to ignore non-zero exits. THE SECOND IS WORSE -- it
    disarms every other check in the same run.
    
    So the distinction is ENCODED, per check, with its reason:
    
        FAILURE   a check that should pass did not. The repo is broken.
        FINDING   a check correctly reporting a known open item. Expected, listed
                  every run, and not counted as a failure.
    
    A BLANKET "IGNORE NON-ZERO" WOULD HIDE A GENUINE REGRESSION IN THE SAME TOOL.
    Naming the expected code keeps the tool able to fail -- and that is tested:
    
    ⭐ PROVEN TO CLASSIFY ALL THREE OUTCOMES, not only the two the real suite
    happens to produce today. The suite emits ok and FINDING and has never emitted
    FAIL, and a runner whose failure branch has never executed cannot be trusted to
    report a regression -- which is its entire purpose.
    
        ok       synthetic: exits 0
        FAIL     synthetic: exits 1, no finding declared
        FINDING  synthetic: exits 3, finding declared
        FAIL     synthetic: exits 7 against a declared 3     <- NOT excused
        MISSING  synthetic: the script is absent             <- fails, not skipped
    
    The last two are the ones worth having. A declared finding code that is matched
    loosely would excuse any failure in that tool, and a missing script that is
    skipped reads as coverage that is not there.
    
    CURRENT RESULT:
    
        ok       recipe + gate corpus                            1.1s
        ok       plan_city's four gates refuse, write nothing     6.3s
        ok       ...and that prover can itself fail              12.7s
        ok       the encounter SUCCESS path, re-verified         72.2s
        ok       encounter separation + settlement units          0.5s
        FINDING  the input-stamp instrument refuses               1.5s
        FINDING  every plan against its inputs                    4.3s
        ok       the street network is one component              0.1s
    
        NO FAILURES across 8 checks. 2 findings, both the stale
        encounters/alpine_8k_all.json, whose disposal is an open ruling.
    
    CURRENT STATE now leads with the one command and keeps the individual
    invocations below it. The tools were previously discoverable only by reading
    commit messages.

    Two altitudes for the stamp, and the ordering of three green checks
    
    LESSONS -- the module exists because the key set is checked in more than one
    place. Two producers stamp INPUT_KEYS and one checker verifies it; three copies
    would be non-negotiable 24 with three ways to drift, and the rule's own test is
    met exactly -- an input key could be added to a producer and forgotten in the
    checker, which would then report MATCHES over an unhashed input.
    
    ⭐ THE PART WORTH CARRYING IS THE RANKING, NOT THE FEATURE.
    
        HISTORY     suspects   a commit touching a producer is not a change to
                               its output
        STAMP       a fact on disk, about the INPUTS
        REPRODUCE   decisive, about the OUTPUT
    
    Three green checks that are not ranked invite the cheapest to be quoted as
    though it were the strongest. That is non-negotiable 0 in a new shape: not
    instruments sharing a source, but instruments of different authority being read
    as equals. A stamp cannot catch a producer whose behaviour depends on something
    it does not declare -- only re-derivation can, and the module's own docstring
    says so rather than leaving the reader to assume the hash settles it.
    
    The entry also records the method for adding a key to a committed artefact the
    placer reads: make the harmlessness FALSIFIABLE. Regenerate to a temp path,
    strip the new key, re-serialise both, require byte-identity -- 47abfa61 ==
    47abfa61 -- then re-run every consumer including the live world.
    
    And the refusals, because a stamp that has only said MATCHES is an untested
    gate. UNREADABLE and MATCHES are easy to collapse into one branch, and a stamp
    that reports MATCHES when it could not read the file is "unknown is never yes"
    with a hash on top.
    
    RECIPES -- R-CITY REJECTED gains five: naming inputs by path not hash; three
    copies of the key list; a stamp that skips an unreadable input; quoting the
    cheapest of three checks as the strongest; and adding a key to a committed plan
    on assurance rather than on proof.
    
    CURRENT STATE records the ranking, the byte-identity proof, the refusal table,
    and marks OPEN item 6 done for the two planners -- with the 16 still-unstamped
    plans (every foliage/*.json and the reachable sidecar) declared as the
    remainder rather than quietly dropped.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

+## 2026-08-26 — A PLAN NOW CARRIES ITS INPUTS' HASHES, AND ONE KEY SET DECLARES THEM
+
+The stale-encounter finding earlier today left one thing owed: the plans could
+not be checked FROM THE FILE. They named their inputs by PATH, so "is this plan
+current" was answerable only by re-running the producer — whose own inputs may
+have moved since. Non-negotiable 20's live pointer, in the artefacts this
+project generates most.
+
+`scripts/plan_stamp.py` writes `_input_sha256` at write time, after every gate.
+
+**IT IS A MODULE BECAUSE THE KEY SET IS CHECKED IN MORE THAN ONE PLACE.** Two
+producers stamp it and one checker verifies it; three copies of `INPUT_KEYS`
+would be non-negotiable 24 with three ways to drift, and the rule's test is met
+exactly — an input key could be added to the producer and forgotten in the
+checker, and the checker would go on reporting MATCHES over an unhashed input.
+
+**And it REFUSES rather than stamping around an input it cannot read.** A stamp
+that silently omits what it could not hash verifies clean later against a plan
+built from something else, which is worse than no stamp at all: it converts an
+unknown into a false positive.
+
+### THE TOWN DID NOT MOVE, AND THAT WAS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED
+
+Adding a key to a committed plan the placer reads is exactly the kind of change
+that is "obviously harmless" right up until it is not. So the claim was made
+falsifiable: regenerate to a temp path, **strip the stamp key, re-serialise
+both, and require byte-identity**.
+
+    committed     399997 bytes  sha 65ab655e
+    regenerated   400412 bytes  sha 63e11d0d
+    stamp stripped, both re-serialised:   47abfa61  ==  47abfa61
+
+Same 303 buildings, 303 roofs, 838 streets, landmark, spire, same seed, same
+rejection tallies. Then every consumer was re-run — the four offline provers,
+and the live world against the new plan, which still reads `ok true`,
+`mismatch {}`, grounding p50 -0.0 / max 0.0 cm.
+
+### THREE INSTRUMENTS, AND THEY RANK — which is more useful than agreeing
+
+    city plan   STALE by HISTORY     a suspicion
+                STAMP MATCHES        a fact on disk
+                REPRODUCES           decisive
+
+**The stamp outranks HISTORY**, because a commit that touched a producer is not
+a change to its output, whereas a changed hash IS a change to its input.
+**It does not outrank REPRODUCE**, and the module's own docstring says so: a
+stamp proves the INPUTS are unchanged, never that the OUTPUT is what those
+inputs would produce today. A producer whose behaviour depends on something it
+does not declare will still drift, and only re-derivation catches that.
+
+Writing that ordering down is the point. Three green checks that are not ranked
+invite the cheapest one to be quoted as though it were the strongest — which is
+the failure non-negotiable 0 describes, in a new shape: not instruments sharing
+a source, but instruments of different authority being read as equals.
+
+### AND THE STAMP WAS PROVEN TO REFUSE BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED
+
+    POSITIVE CONTROL (unmutated)   -> MATCHES
+    one input hash corrupted       -> DIFFERS, and it NAMES that input
+    stamp removed                  -> UNSTAMPED, never "fresh"
+    a stamped input deleted        -> UNREADABLE, not MATCHES
+    stamping with a missing input  -> REFUSED
+
+The last two are the ones worth having. `UNREADABLE` and `MATCHES` are easy to
+collapse into one branch, and a stamp that reports MATCHES when it could not
+read the file is the "unknown is never yes" failure with a hash on top.
+
+**Sixteen plans remain UNSTAMPED and are declared so** — every `foliage/*.json`
+and the reachable sidecar, produced by in-editor payloads or by `place_foliage`.
+They are listed, counted, and excluded from the success line. Partial coverage
+stated as partial is honest; partial coverage summarised as a pass is not.
+

+**A plan that names its inputs by PATH and not by HASH.** SYMPTOM: staleness is

+## 2026-08-26 — A CONTROL THAT FAILS FOR THE WRONG REASON IS WORSE THAN NO CONTROL
+
+`plan_city` carries four refusals and every one of them had only ever seen the
+single town that passes it. `max_orphan_building_fraction` had never refused
+anything in its life. So a prover was written — mutate one gate value per case,
+run the planner against a copied recipe, assert it refuses.
+
+**And then the prover needed its own positive control**, because a prover that
+has only ever seen working gates is in exactly the state it was written to fix.
+The control: a copy of `plan_city.py` with the orphan gate's condition made
+unsatisfiable, and a requirement that the suite then report FAILED.
+
+**IT REPORTED FAILED. AND IT WAS WRONG.**
+
+    FAIL  POSITIVE CONTROL (unmutated)   the unmutated recipe was REFUSED
+    FAIL  orphan fraction 0.0            refusal never names 'orphan'
+    FAIL  building-to-street 1 m         refusal never names 'orphan'
+    FAIL  min_buildings 10000            refusal never names 'building'
+
+The verdict was the expected one. The reason was not. The broken copy had been
+written to a scratch directory outside the repo, and `plan_city` derives its
+repo root from its own file location — so the copy could resolve neither
+`recipes/` nor its sibling `measure_city_connectivity` import, and **died before
+reaching a single gate.** Every case "refused" because every case crashed.
+
+**A dead planner and four working gates produce the same table.** Had the
+control been run once, seen FAILED, and been ticked off, the prover would have
+been recorded as positive-controlled while being incapable of detecting
+anything at all — and every later "ALL CASES BEHAVED" would have inherited that
+false credential.
+
+**What caught it was the POSITIVE control failing too.** The broken-gate
+hypothesis predicts that the unmutated recipe still PASSES — only the orphan
+cases should move. It failed as well, and a hypothesis that does not predict
+your result is not the explanation of your result. One `--planner` run outside
+the harness showed the traceback in two lines.
+
+**The corrected control DISCRIMINATES, and the difference is visible:**
+
+    orphan fraction 0.0        FAIL   did not refuse, WROTE ITS PLAN
+    building-to-street 1 m     FAIL   did not refuse, WROTE ITS PLAN
+    min_buildings 10000        ok     still refuses
+    min_street_segments        ok     still refuses
+    POSITIVE CONTROL           ok     still passes
+
+Exactly the two cases routed through the broken gate failed and nothing else
+moved. **That is evidence. "Everything failed" was not**, and the two are told
+apart only by looking at WHICH rows moved — never by the verdict line.
+
+**The general rule, and it is non-negotiable 6 pointed at a control rather than
+at a measurement:** a control must distinguish *the instrument detected the
+defect* from *the instrument could not run*. Assert that the control's failures
+land where the injected defect predicts, and treat a control that fails
+everywhere as an instrument fault until proven otherwise.
+
+**And the mechanism is worth carrying separately, because it will recur:**
+`plan_city`, `bootstrap.py` and several others locate the repo from
+`__file__`. That is correct and deliberate — it is why no script in this repo
+carries a machine-specific path. **The consequence is that a COPY of such a
+script is not a copy of its behaviour.** Anything that duplicates one for a
+test must place it beside the original. The prover now writes its control copy
+into `scripts/`, removes it in a `finally`, and asserts its absence afterwards.
+

+## 2026-08-26 — COVERAGE IS NOT CONNECTIVITY, AND THE BASIN IS SEALED
+
+The encounter planner was blocked on one thing: there was no ground outside the
+settlement that was also connected to the player. The named fix was navmesh
+beyond the town volume. So a second 1040 m volume was declared to the east,
+sharing its western edge with the first so the pair is contiguous, and built.
+
+**The direction was measured, not picked.** The offline walkable-component
+prefilter over a 5 km box closed at 440–780 m on bearings 165–285 and ran open
+eastward. It was used for exactly what a prefilter is for — choosing where to
+spend an expensive build — and its CLOSED verdicts ruled out the western half.
+
+The build was clean by every bar it carries:
+
+    chunk actors   10 (was 8)     size 35.18 MB (was 21.59)
+    wall clock     36.0 s         bar 30 min
+    peak commit    20.0 GB        bar 200 GB
+    RegistrationFailed_AgentNotValid   ZERO
+
+**And it changed nothing, because coverage is not connectivity.** A directed
+probe along the extension, every 50 m to 1400 m:
+
+    projects     True at ALL 28 points
+    reachable    True to 300 m, False for the remaining 22
+
+Twenty-eight points with navmesh under them, six of which a player can walk to.
+The extension is real, navigable, correctly built ground that nobody can reach.
+
+**This is the same distinction that has now cost this project three separate
+readings, and it is worth stating as a rule rather than as an anecdote:
+PROJECTION SAYS A POLYGON IS UNDERFOOT; ONLY A PATH QUERY SAYS YOU CAN GET
+THERE.** A tool that reports coverage and calls it access will report success
+over an island. The first occurrence was unit 8's original verification (25/25
+projecting was read as a working navmesh); the second was the town's own outer
+districts (all 60 ring points projected, 41 were reachable); this is the third,
+and it is the one where the coverage was *deliberately added* and bought
+nothing.
+
+**AND THE PREFILTER WAS WRONG AGAIN, IN EXACTLY THE PREDICTED DIRECTION.** It
+had claimed the plaza's component reached 2480 m on that bearing and covered
+95.2% of a 5 km box. The built navmesh reaches 300 m. This was not a surprise
+and was not treated as one: the model reads the heightmap, the navmesh is built
+from collision, and the model had already passed ground the navmesh refused
+twice. It is labelled PREFILTER, its OPEN verdicts are not trusted, and it was
+NOT tuned to agree — fitting a model to the authority's answer destroys the only
+thing the model is good for.
+
+### THEN THE DENOMINATOR DECIDED THE DIAGNOSIS, AND IT NEARLY DECIDED IT WRONG
+
+A 50 m probe localises a barrier to a 50 m band. That is a LOCATION, not a
+cause, and three mechanisms fit it with three different fixes: a slope step the
+agent will not climb (real terrain), a gap with no polygon (coverage, fixable),
+or a thin strip discarded by `MinRegionArea` (config, fixable). They are
+separable — a gap fails to PROJECT, and a discarded strip projects without a
+local gradient over the bar.
+
+At 5 m sampling the gradient at the flip read **35.71°**, under the 44.765°
+agent bar, which says "not a slope problem" and points at the two fixable
+mechanisms. At 0.5 m the same ground reads **51.34°**:
+
+    d_m      elev_m   grad_deg   projects   reachable
+    322.0    198.36      23.25       True        True    <- last reachable
+    322.5    198.73      36.58       True       False
+    323.5    199.73      51.34       True       False    <- over the bar
+    324.0    200.35      51.33       True       False    <- over the bar
+
+**A 1.25 m rise over 1 m.** Recast evaluates at `CellSize` ≈ 19 cm; a 5 m
+average is 26 cells wide and hides a sub-metre step completely. **A GRADIENT
+WITHOUT ITS DENOMINATOR IS NOT A SLOPE**, and the denominator that matters is
+the one the CONSUMER evaluates at, not the one convenient to sample.
+
+This is non-negotiable 22's shape — a statistic that is arithmetically true and
+answers a question nobody asked — reaching a new place: not a misleading MASK
+this time, but a misleading SCALE. Both are "state the denominator".
+
+### AND MY FIRST ANSWER TO "IS THERE A PASS?" WAS A STATISTIC THAT MOVES
+
+Six rays reported the FIRST unreachable sample along each ray as the island
+boundary. That number is sampling-dependent and a single dropout destroys it:
+bearing 0 read **244 m at 2 m spacing and 322 m at 0.5 m**, because the coarse
+probe stopped early at an isolated unreachable sample. Genuine dropouts exist —
+324.5 m reads reachable among unreachable neighbours.
+
+**THE FIRST FLIP ALONG A RAY IS NOT THE BOUNDARY OF A REGION.** The 24-bearing
+sweep scans the whole ray and takes the FURTHEST reachable point, which no
+single dropout can move, and the six-bearing figures are marked superseded in
+the artefact rather than deleted.
+
+    24 rays at 15 deg, 4 m to 700 m
+    furthest overall 504 m (bearing 90)   median 360 m   min 252 m
+
+**There is no natural pass.** A pass would show as one bearing running far
+beyond its neighbours with nothing over the bar before it; the profile is
+uniform and the best bearing is 1.4x the median. All 24 cross ground above the
+agent bar.
+
+**But the sweep bought something a yes/no could not: the rim is not uniformly
+thick.** Bearing 315 has 2 samples over the bar and 285 has 4, against 19 at
+bearing 195. A question that was "should we cut a pass?" — unbounded, and
+therefore easy to defer forever — is now "cut it at 315 or 285, where the least
+earth moves". **A negative result is worth measuring properly when the
+measurement also narrows the alternative.**
+
+### THE CORRECTION THIS ENTRY OWES
+
+The east-extension commit called the barrier "a local step, not a wall", from
+50 m samples, and noted the elevations either side were gentle. **It is a wall,
+all the way round.** The gentleness was real and irrelevant: a 1.25 m step in
+otherwise gentle ground stops the agent exactly as a cliff does, because the
+agent's bar is a LOCAL gradient and a step height, not an average.
+

+value landed proves nothing about whether the value was right.

+and NOT built". That is the failure this entry is actually about. **A lesson
+whose fix is recorded rather than encoded is a lesson that will fire again**,
+and CLAUDE.md's operating loop (e) says so directly: when the same mistake
+recurs, the finding is not "be more careful" but *why the existing lesson did
+not prevent it*.
+
+**Why it did not fire:** `fix_camera_z.py` guards RECIPE cameras. An ad-hoc

+the one a person reaches for when they want one frame quickly. The guard was
+sitting on the road nobody was driving on.
+
+**The fix is placement, not vigilance.** The guard now lives in the shot payload
+itself, which is the one place every camera necessarily passes through, and it
+refuses BEFORE the output directory is created:

+An unreadable ground trace reports COULD NOT LOOK and does not pass — a camera
+whose ground cannot be measured is not thereby above it.
+
+**The general form, and it is non-negotiable 3 in a new setting:** prefer the
+choke point over the correct tool. A guard on the tool a careful person would
+use protects careful people; a guard on the path every call must take protects
+the run.

+## 2026-08-26 — A GUARD THAT COMPARED THE WRONG TWO THINGS, AND COST A THIRD OF A TOWN
+
+**What was attempted.** Navmesh over the town, PlayerStart in it, encounters
+planned around it — the ruled sequence for an autonomous session.
+
+**What happened.** All three landed, and the reachability gate then found that
+**19 of 60 street points in the town were unreachable from the town's own
+plaza**. All 60 projected — navmesh existed under them — so they were
+disconnected ISLANDS, not missing navmesh.
+
+**Root cause, and it is a comparand.** `apply_navigation_config.py` enforced
+ruling 19 as *navmesh agent slope must not exceed
+`world.primary_movement_mode`*. The world is declared `mount` (35°). So the
+navmesh was built for a horse.
+
+But ruling 19's own stated purpose is to stop a navmesh **granting paths onto
+ground the character slides off**. The thing that slides is the PAWN, and the
+pawn is `climb` (70°). The guard was comparing the navmesh against a
+WORLD-SCALE declaration — one that WORLD_VISION uses to size POI spacing
+against mounted speed — instead of against the object whose behaviour it names.
+
+Two different questions, one comparand. The measured cost was a basin town
+built for an agent none of its consumers use: a basin whose rim climbs
+186.7 → 333 m is *expected* to fragment at 35°.
+
+**The general rule. A GUARD MUST COMPARE THE TWO THINGS WHOSE DISAGREEMENT
+CAUSES THE FAILURE IT NAMES.** Reading the guard's own error message is the
+test: it said "ground the character slides off", and it was not looking at the
+character. A guard can be correct, tested, one-directional and load-bearing —
+and still be pointed at the wrong pair.
+
+**And the fix did not weaken it.** walk 44.765 ≤ climb 70 is still
+one-directional and still refuses an agent steeper than the pawn. Proven in
+four directions before it was trusted: `air` 90 REFUSED, `climb` 70 allowed at
+equality, `walk` 44.765 allowed, `mount` 35 allowed.
+
+**The ruled fix could not be implemented as ruled, and the lookup is why.** The
+consult ruled "add a walk agent ALONGSIDE the mount agent". The engine refuses
+that shape: `AgentMaxSlope` is not part of `FNavDataConfig` — SupportedAgents
+entries carry radius/height/step only — and setting it per-actor reverts via
+`ARecastNavMesh::PostLoad` when the voxel cache is on
+(`RecastNavMesh.cpp:963-1015`), which this repo *already* records as a REJECTED
+pattern. Two agents would have differed in radius/height/step and been
+identical in the one property causing the fragmentation. Taken back for a
+decision rather than implemented as something that cannot work.
+
+**AND THE AGENT WAS NOT THE WHOLE STORY.** After the rebuild, reachability went
+41/60 → 45/60. The outer districts stayed cut off. The hypothesis was tested and
+mostly refuted, which is why it was tested rather than assumed.
+

+## 2026-08-26 — PER-ELEMENT GATES DO NOT COMPOSE INTO WHOLE-TRAVERSABILITY. SECOND OCCURRENCE.
+
+**First occurrence, same week:** `plan_city` gated each STREET SEGMENT
+independently on slope. Every segment passed its own bar and the network came
+out as 155 disconnected pieces with the town centre stranded in a 22-segment
+fragment.
+
+**Second occurrence, this session:** the town's EXTENT was drawn by
+per-structure gates — cut/fill and pad slope, each building judged alone. Every
+building passed its own bar and the town reaches onto ground that cannot be
+walked to from its own plaza: 185 of 838 streets and 50 of 303 buildings
+unreachable, measured against the built navmesh.
+
+**The general rule. A GATE THAT PASSES EVERY ELEMENT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE
+WHOLE.** Connectivity, reachability and continuity are properties of the SET,
+and no amount of per-element correctness produces them. If the thing that
+matters is a property of the whole, the gate must be computed on the whole.
+
+**This is non-negotiable 4a's automatic escalation trigger**: a trap class that
+recurs across two different tools is promoted to shared infrastructure on the
+spot, without waiting for a third. Recorded here; the shared reachability module
+is named as the next unit rather than patched into each planner, and
+individually-patched connectivity checks are a REJECTED pattern from this entry
+forward.
+

+
+## 2026-08-26 — FOUR MEASUREMENTS THAT WERE ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE WORLD
+
+Each was caught by a control, and each would have been written up as a finding.
+
+**1. `project_point_to_navigation` takes FIVE arguments**, not four:
+`(world, point, nav_data, filter_class, query_extent)`. Passing four put the
+extent into `filter_class` and left `query_extent` at `[0,0,0]` — a zero-extent
+projection, which misses nearly everywhere. Result: 0 of 40 street points, with
+both negative controls also at 0. **The positive control is the only reason
+this was not reported as "the town has no navmesh"** — the PlayerStart, known
+to project since 2026-08-17, failed in the same run, so the verdict came back
+COULD NOT LOOK. Non-negotiable 6, doing precisely its job.
+
+**2. A LARGE QUERY EXTENT DOES NOT MERELY WIDEN THE SEARCH — IT CHANGES THE
+ANSWER.** At a 120 m extent the plaza spawn reported projecting to a polygon
+116.7 m away in Y, which reads as "the player spawns off-navmesh". A radial map
+at 500 cm then showed the plaza centre projecting at **0.0 cm** lateral, and
+every ring from 10 m to 200 m projecting. R-NAVBUILD already recorded the
+too-tight direction (±20 m read 7/25 where ±120 m read 25/25); this is the same
+lesson's other half. **A coverage number is a property of the query in BOTH
+directions.**
+
+**3. `get_path_length` needs endpoints ON the navmesh.** A point 42 m from the
+spawn at the SPAWN's z returns `(ERROR, 0.0)`; the same point at its PROJECTED
+z returns `(SUCCESS, 5702.7)`. Both ends are projected first now, and a point
+that will not project is reported as a projection failure rather than as
+unreachable — different findings that a single boolean would have merged.
+
+**4. Querying a building's CENTRE for reachability** projects into the solid
+volume the navmesh is carved around, so all 303 buildings read unreachable. A
+fact about the query, not the town. Corrected to sample the DOORSTEP, just
+outside the footprint: 253 of 303.
+
+**The through-line:** every one of these produced a plausible, alarming,
+publishable number. Not one was caught by inspection; all four were caught by a
+control that could fail — and the two negative controls mattered as much as the
+positive ones, because a query that returns "no" everywhere agrees with a

+### PROJECTION IS NOT REACHABILITY

+### API SHAPES THAT COST A FALSE FINDING
+
+    project_point_to_navigation(world, point, nav_data, filter_class, extent)
+        FIVE args. Four puts the extent into filter_class and leaves the extent
+        [0,0,0] -- a zero-extent projection that misses nearly everywhere.
+
+    get_path_length(world, start, end, nav_data, filter_class)
+        -> (NavigationQueryResult, float). Compare == SUCCESS explicitly:
+        INVALID=0, ERROR=1, FAIL=2, SUCCESS=3, so truthiness INVERTS the gate.
+        BOTH ENDPOINTS MUST BE PROJECTED FIRST -- a point 42 m away at the
+        wrong z returns (ERROR, 0.0); at its projected z, (SUCCESS, 5702.7).

+## 2026-08-25 — THE CAMERA WAS 122 m INSIDE THE HILL, AND THE GUARD FOR THAT ALREADY EXISTED
+
+**What was attempted.** An oblique render of the town, to judge whether the new
+roofline reads as an alpine settlement. Camera placed 900 m south-west of the
+basin centre at z 337 m, derived by adding 150 m to the basin floor elevation of
+187 m.
+
+**What happened.** The frame came back showing terrain with **trees hanging
+downward** and a large pale gradient below. Ten minutes of render, useless.
+
+**Root cause, measured rather than argued.** A trace at that exact XY reports
+ground at **458.9 m**. The camera was **122 m below the surface**, looking out
+through the inside of the hill — the hanging trees are rooted on the far side of
+a ridge, seen from underneath through backfaces.
+
+The arithmetic was the defect: **the basin floor's elevation is not the ground
+elevation 900 m away from the basin.** That is the whole point of a basin. A
+trace at the camera's own XY answers it in one call, and eight bearings x two
+distances x two eye heights answered it in one payload afterwards — bearing 225
+sits at 458.9 m, bearing 270 at 74.7 m, a **384 m spread** across candidate
+positions at the same radius.
+
+**AND THIS PROJECT ALREADY OWNS THIS FAILURE.** `CURRENT STATE` 2026-08-15
+records "D1 DONE — four cameras were INSIDE the hill", and
+`scripts/fix_camera_z.py` was written for exactly it.
+
+**So why did the guard not fire? Because of its SCOPE.** `fix_camera_z.py`
+lifts cameras declared in a RECIPE, and `sweep_cameras --resite` sites the sweep
+stations. Both operate on persisted, named camera stations. This camera was an
+ad-hoc argument to a render payload, so it passed through no camera-siting code
+at all and no guard was in a position to see it.
+
+**The general rule, and it is rule (e) applied to a guard rather than to a
+lesson.** **A GUARD SCOPED TO THE DECLARED FORM OF A THING DOES NOT COVER THE
+AD-HOC FORM OF THE SAME THING.** The dangerous case is precisely the ad-hoc one,
+because it skips the machinery where the accumulated knowledge lives. Recipe
+cameras are safe *because* they go through a tool; a hand-typed `--set LOC=[...]`
+is the unguarded path, and it is the path a person reaches for when they want
+one quick look.
+
+**The cheap fix, not yet built:** the shot payload already asserts its camera
+transform reads back correctly. It should also trace the ground under the
+requested eye position and REFUSE when the camera is below it — the same
+information, one extra trace, at the only place every camera necessarily passes
+through. Recorded here rather than built, because the render queue was mid-flight
+and a change to the payload under a running shot is its own trap.
+
+**A second observation, measured while waiting.** A `HighResShot 2` at this
+viewport takes **~10 minutes**, not the "over two minutes" recorded on
+2026-08-24. The editor throttles hard when it is not the foreground window —
+this project measured **17.8x** — and these renders were taken with the editor
+backgrounded. Foreground the window before a render, or budget ten minutes.

    object: a levelled surface cut into a slope. The key is deliberately SEPARATE
    from `buildings.max_pad_cut_fill_m` and starts at the same number -- an
    earthmoving allowance is an ENGINEERING choice, not a physical constant, and
    non-negotiable 19's own test is whether the quantity is physical.

+## R-CITY — A SETTLEMENT AS A MASSING BLOCKOUT (2026-08-25)

+**This recipe was owed from 2026-08-24.** `recipes/city.json` shipped with its

+
+**WHAT THIS PRODUCES, AND THE WORD MATTERS: A MASSING BLOCKOUT.** Volumes,
+streets and plot footprints placed from measured terrain out of
+`/Engine/BasicShapes` primitives. It answers where a town stands, how big it is,
+and how it reads at range. **It does not answer what it looks like.** There is

+Architecture` is a photo-studio lookdev kit (`SM_1Meter_01`,
+`SM_AssetPlatform_02`, `SM_CycRoom_01`), verified.

+### THE CHAIN
+
+    1  site      scripts/find_city_site.py     ranks by LARGEST INSCRIBED
+                                               CIRCLE, not by area
+    2  plan      scripts/plan_city.py          offline, seeded, deterministic
+    3  check     scripts/measure_city_connectivity.py   is it ONE network?
+    4  draw      scripts/draw_city_plan.py     top-down plan render
+    5  place     scripts/city_place_payload.txt
+    6  verify    scripts/city_verify_payload.txt   counts IN THE LEVEL and
+                                                   re-grounds with a FRESH trace
+    7  save      external actor packages, one per volume

+**Steps 2 and 6 must not share an instrument.** The placer returned `ok:true`
+with its output truncated by a 763-entry actor list, so "it worked" arrived with
+no numbers attached.
+
+### THE SITE, MEASURED NOT CHOSEN
+
+    centre (-210800, 278800) cm   usable radius 184.2 m   area 109.8 ha
+    elevation 187 m of a terrain spanning 0 .. 1552.5 m
+    slope mean 6.25 deg, p90 10.32
+    evaluated at cell_m 8.0   <- flatness at the scale a CITY occupies
+
+**The slope bar was ruled from the frontier, not tuned until it passed:**
+6 deg -> 82.4 m usable radius, 8 -> 108.8, 10 -> 169.7, **12 -> 184.2**,
+15 -> 237.9. 15 was rejected because a 27% street grade is not a street.
+
+**The foothill constraint was NOT binding** — identical usable radius at
+elevation percentile 40, 60 and 80. So `WORLD_VISION.md:303` is corroborated by
+measurement rather than imposed.
+
+### STREETS — THE TWO GATES, AND WHAT EACH ONE IS ABOUT
+
+    max_street_slope_deg    8.0    END-TO-END GRADE, rise over run
+    max_street_cut_fill_m   1.8    max deviation of natural ground from the
+                                   straight run joining the two ends
+    street_join_tol_m       7.0    centrelines within this are JOINED
+
+**BOTH ARE REQUIRED AND NEITHER IS SUFFICIENT.** Grade alone accepts a segment
+that dives into a gully and climbs out level at the far side — its two ends are
+level, so its grade is zero. Cut/fill alone accepts a uniform 30% ramp.
+
+**A street is gated the way a building pad is**, because it is the same kind of
+object: a levelled surface cut into a slope. `max_street_cut_fill_m` is a
+SEPARATE key from `buildings.max_pad_cut_fill_m` and starts at the same 1.8 m
+deliberately — an earthmoving allowance is an ENGINEERING choice, not a physical
+constant, and non-negotiable 19's own test is whether the quantity is physical.
+An angle of repose would have to be shared; how much digging we will pay for
+does not.
+
+### THE NETWORK IS PRUNED TO THE PLAZA'S COMPONENT
+
+Gating segments one at a time punches holes in a lattice, and a lattice with
+holes is not a network. Whatever survives in a piece that cannot be walked to
+from the centre is a road to nowhere: it would be placed, rendered, and would
+lie to anyone reading the town from a ridge.
+
+**KEEP THE PLAZA'S COMPONENT, NOT THE LARGEST ONE.** See REJECTED.
+
+**ONE DEFINITION OF CONNECTED**, in `measure_city_connectivity.py`, imported by
+the planner that prunes and by the gate that checks. Two copies would be two
+lists that must agree (non-negotiable 24). **Note precisely what that does not
+buy:** the gate re-reading the plan proves only that the pruner ran. The
+independent check is the one taken IN THE WORLD from placed actor transforms —
+same definition, different source.
+
+**CONNECTIVITY IS GEOMETRIC, NOT AN ENDPOINT GRAPH.** Rings sit at
+`core + i*spacing`; spokes are cut at `plaza + (R-plaza)*k/14`. A spoke CROSSES a
+ring mid-segment and the two share no endpoint, so an endpoint graph reports
+~459 components — an artefact of the representation, not a fact about the town.
+

+### THE GATES, AND ALL OF THEM RUN BEFORE THE WRITE

+## R-CITY REJECTED
+
+**`street_slope_deg` AS THE MAX OF SIX SUB-INTERVAL DIFFERENCES.**
+*Symptom you will see:* `streets_rejected_slope` in the high hundreds against a
+few hundred kept, and a street network that renders as disconnected stubs.
+Measured: **883 of 1342 rejected, 155 disconnected pieces, largest holding 9.2%
+of segments, the town CENTRE stranded in a 22-segment fragment.** It read
+**p50 10.54 deg** over a basin surveyed at **mean slope 6.25 deg** — it rejected
+the median segment of ground already certified flat enough to hold a town.
+*Why:* that is a ROUGHNESS statistic, not a grade; one rough 2.5 m sub-interval
+anywhere condemns the whole segment. **The bar was right and the measurand was
+wrong.** *Correct value:* end-to-end grade, p50 3.84 deg on the same lattice.
+*Reference:* `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-25.
+
+**"KEEP THE LARGEST CONNECTED COMPONENT" AS THE CONNECTIVITY FIX.**
+Proposed in the 2026-08-24 commit message as the remedy. *Symptom:* it deletes
+91% of the streets AND the town centre with them, because on the shipped plan
+the largest component held 42 of 459 segments and did not contain the plaza.
+*Correct value:* keep the component containing the PLAZA — the centre is what a
+town is organised around, so the centre defines the network. *Why it was
+wrong:* it was authored against a mental picture of a mostly-good network with
+frayed edges, by a session that had not measured it. **A remedy designed against
+an unmeasured defect is a guess wearing a plan's clothes.**
+
+**GATES RUNNING AFTER THE PLAN IS WRITTEN.**
+*Symptom:* a refused run exits 1 **and leaves the refused plan on disk**, at
+exactly the path `city_place_payload.txt` reads. Measured 2026-08-25: a run
+refused at 10 street segments had already written all 10. *Why it is worse than
+no gate:* the exit code is transient and lives in one shell; the bad file is
+durable and is what the next step consumes. This is Division 3's "a refusal that
+mutated and saved before printing REFUSE", found in our own planner.
+*Correct form:* every gate runs before the write, and the refusal message says
+"Nothing was written." The previous good plan stays on disk, which is a state a
+caller can recover from.
+
+**`main()` AT MODULE SCOPE IN `plan_city.py`.**
+*Symptom:* `import plan_city` — to reuse its terrain sampler — REWRITES THE
+PLAN as a side effect. *Correct form:* `if __name__ == "__main__":`. The
+alternative was a second copy of the heightmap sampler, non-negotiable 19.
+*Regression proof for any future refactor of a seeded generator:* the plan must
+re-run BYTE-IDENTICAL. The guard was proven inert that way.
+
+**`Paths.project_saved_dir()` AS AN ABSOLUTE PATH** (capture path, 2026-08-24).
+It returns a RELATIVE path and the editor's working directory is the ENGINE
+BINARIES folder. *Symptom:* a watcher reports "no new screenshot appeared" over
+a shot that was written correctly. Wrap in `convert_relative_path_to_full`.
+
+**A 120 s WATCHER ON A HighResShot AT MULTIPLIER 2.** On a 4064x2546 viewport
+that shot takes OVER TWO MINUTES on this machine. *Symptom:* the watcher gives
+up on a shot that lands a few seconds later.

    no enforcement. Fixed structurally: the defaults now derive from the sidecar the
    recipe names, the fallback is the RULED numbers rather than the old literals, and
    a failed read PRINTS a warning -- a silent fallback to a stale default is exactly

    wardrobe materials, and no custom material. Nothing was asked to revert it.

    earlier the same session -- deliberately, to make the ruled length scale durable.
    Alpine8K is World Partition, so the actor can be unloaded and re-instantiated
    from that saved package at streaming's discretion, and every unsaved component
    edit dies with the instance. The frames were taken before the reload and are
    valid; the state behind them was gone when next read.
    
    **A COMPONENT EDIT ON A PARTITIONED WORLD IS RENDER STATE, NOT CONFIGURATION.**
    Its lifetime is bounded by streaming, not by the editor session. Now procedure:
    render immediately after mounting, and when two candidates must be compared,
    mount and render each back to back so the pair is single-variable in one window.
    Which is how the three-panel above was produced -- v1 mounted, rendered, v2
    mounted, rendered, one session, minutes apart.

    live in the saved actor package, colour lives on a material asset, the length

 Specification: `RECIPES.md` **R-HAIRCOLOUR** and its REJECTED section.

+---
+
+## 2026-08-23 — A LOCKED RECIPE DOES NOT STOP A TOOL THAT CARRIES ITS OWN COPY
+
+**What was attempted.** The hero's hair colour was ruled by the operator and
+locked as `RECIPES.md` R-HAIRCOLOUR, specifically *because* six DiffLocks cycles
+had already overwritten it that day. The very next `cycle.py` run — the first
+after the lock — overwrote it again, and its own report printed the evidence:
+`hairMelanin 0.92, hairRedness 0.28` where the ruled values are 1.00 and 0.00.
+
+**Root cause.** `cycle.py:101-102` declared `--melanin default=0.92` and
+`--redness default=0.28` as literals. Those are a SECOND COPY of a value the
+tool does not own, and `MI_AlpineHero_CustomHair` is one material instance shared
+by whatever groom is mounted, so the most frequent writer of the colour is a tool
+whose defaults were authored before the ruling existed.
+
+**The general rule, and it is uncomfortable.** **WRITING THE RECIPE DID NOT
+PROTECT THE VALUE.** A recipe is a record; it has no enforcement. The lock was
+filed in RECIPES.md, LESSONS.md and a machine-readable sidecar, and the next run
+clobbered the value anyway, because nothing in the code path reads any of those.
+Non-negotiable 24 says two lists that must agree are one list badly stored — and
+the second list here was a pair of argparse defaults, which is the least
+conspicuous place a duplicate can hide. Fixed by deriving the defaults from the
+sidecar the recipe names, with the fallback going to the RULED numbers rather
+than the old literals, and a printed warning if the read fails: a silent
+fallback to a stale default is how this happened seven times in one day.
+
+**The test that would have caught it earlier:** after locking a value, run the
+tool that most often touches it and read the value back. Locking and verifying
+are different acts.
+
+---
+
+## 2026-08-23 — A SAVED ACTOR OUTRANKS AN IN-MEMORY MOUNT, AND STREAMING DECIDES WHEN
+
+**What happened.** The v2 groom was mounted, verified from an independent
+payload, and its full cycle ran green — export, import, bind, colour, gate
+PRESENT 23,030 / 23,041 px at 10.8x floor, drift 0.0%. A later read of the same
+component returned the VENDOR groom, the vendor's wardrobe materials, and no
+custom material at all. Nothing had been asked to revert it.
+
+**Root cause.** Earlier the same session the hero actor's external package was
+SAVED with the vendor configuration, deliberately, to make the ruled length
+scale durable. `/Game/Alpine8K` is World Partition; the actor can be unloaded
+and re-instantiated from that saved package at streaming's discretion, and every
+unsaved component edit dies with the instance. The frames were valid — they were
+taken before the reload — but the state behind them was gone by the time it was
+next read.
+
+**The general rule.** **A COMPONENT EDIT IS A RENDER-STATE CHANGE ON A
+PARTITIONED WORLD, NOT A CONFIGURATION CHANGE.** Its lifetime is bounded by
+streaming, not by the editor session, so "I set it and verified it" carries no
+guarantee about ten minutes later. Two consequences that are now procedure:
+render immediately after mounting rather than mounting a set of candidates and
+rendering them later; and when two candidates must be COMPARED, mount and render
+each one back to back so the pair is single-variable in one window.
+
+*And this is the third distinct lifetime found in the same component today* —
+groom and binding live in the saved actor package, colour lives on a material
+asset, and the length scale lives only in memory. The recipe now tabulates all
+three, because the failure mode of each looks identical from a read-back: the
+value is correct when you ask.
+
+**A confound this created, stated rather than hidden.** The v1-vs-v2 comparison
+frames rendered on the vendor's `MI_WI_*` wardrobe materials, because the
+reverted component no longer carried the custom instance. The comparison remains
+SINGLE-VARIABLE — both arms share that material and differ only in geometry —
+but neither frame shows the ruled colour, and a reader must not take the colour
+in them as the ruled colour.

+## 2026-08-23 — A GAMUT LIMIT THAT WAS A SEARCH LIMIT
+
+**What was attempted.** The operator gave a four-zone colour breakdown for the
+hero's hair — shadow `#141517`, midtone `#2A2C31`, highlight `#52565D` — all
+cool, B > G > R. Five measured cycles moved `hairMelanin`, `hairRedness`,
+`WhiteAmount`, `hairDye` and `PaintColor`, every write verified by read-back
+off a reloaded asset, and none reached negative R-B. It was recorded as a
+GAMUT LIMIT: *"the MetaHuman hair master is a MELANIN model and melanin is warm
+by construction"*, with the conclusion that a cool blue-grey needs a different
+master or a grade.
+
+**What happened.** The operator later asked for the colour to be *"a bit darker
+and cooler"*. Enumerating the material's parameters off the asset before
+touching anything showed the master carries **FOUR melanin layers, not one**:
+
+    hairMelanin        0.92   hairRedness        0.00   dye [0.5,0.58,0.72]
+    HighlightsMelanin  0.28   HighlightsRedness  0.25   dye [1,1,1]
+    OmbreMelanin       0.28   OmbreRedness       0.25   dye [1,1,1]
+    RegionMelanin      0.28   RegionRedness      0.25   dye [1,1,1]
+
+The base layer was already dark and neutral — every one of the five cycles had
+been tuning the layer that was already correct. The other three sat at a THIRD
+of its melanin with redness 0.25 and a neutral white dye, and **those three own
+the HIGHLIGHT, which is exactly the zone that measured warmest** at R-B +40.
+Moving all four together took the midtone from R-B +17.9 to +10.7 and the
+highlight from +40.2 to +34.1, both darker and cooler, in a single cycle.
+
+**Root cause.** The search space was defined by which parameter names had been
+typed before, not by which ones exist. And the enumeration was already in hand:
+`hair_color_probe.txt` had printed all four families in the earlier session, and
+its output was read as *a list of names* rather than as *a map of what had not
+been tried*. Nothing was measured wrongly; the wrong quarter of the space was
+measured thoroughly.
+
+**The general rule.** **A NEGATIVE RESULT ABOUT A SYSTEM IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE
+SEARCH UNTIL THE PARAMETER LIST CAME OFF THE ARTEFACT AND EVERY FAMILY IN IT
+HAS BEEN MOVED.** "This cannot be done" is only as strong as the enumeration
+behind it, and an enumeration you generated but did not act on is worse than
+none — it makes the gap invisible, because the names were technically on the
+board. When a tool prints a list of levers, mark which ones you have actually
+pulled.
+
+*This is non-negotiable 6 turned around.* That rule says a failed measurement
+must report "I could not look" rather than a number. The mirror image, and the
+one that bit here, is that **a successful measurement over an incomplete input
+reports a confident conclusion about the wrong thing** — and it does not feel
+like a failed measurement at any point, because every write landed and every
+read-back agreed.
+

    COMPRESSIVE, NOT UNIFORM k. A single multiplier on a distribution spanning
    2.68-14.91 stretches the longest strands furthest, and those are the ones
    already defining the silhouette. k_i is graded by rank so shorter strands gain
    proportionally more, then renormalised to hit the target mean. Result: the max
    lands at 20.37 -- inside the v22 band the operator named -- instead of running
    to 27.
    
    THE MECHANISM'S COST, STATED. Scaling about the root preserves each strand's
    DIRECTION and the SHAPE of its curl exactly (the curve is similar to itself), so
    the cut's character survives. It does NOT preserve curl SCALE: a 1.56x strand
    has 1.56x curl radius, and the reconstruction's curl is real data. The
    alternative -- extrapolating along the final tangent -- keeps curl size and
    welds a straight segment onto every strand, which reads as a wig. Of the two
    ways to be wrong, similarity is the one that stays recognisable. Modest k, and
    the frame decides.

+### COMPRESSIVE k, NOT A SINGLE MULTIPLIER
+
+A global multiplier on a distribution spanning 2.68–14.91 stretches the LONGEST
+strands furthest, and those already define the silhouette. `k_i` is graded by

+is similar to itself. **Not preserved: curl SCALE.** A 1.56x strand has 1.56x
+curl radius, and the reconstruction's curl is authored data.

+The alternative — extrapolating each tip along its final tangent — keeps curl
+size and welds a straight segment onto every strand, which reads as a wig. Of
+the two ways to be wrong, similarity stays recognisable. **Prefer a modest k and
+judge the frame; if the extended strands distort the cut's character, say so
+with a frame rather than push further.**
