+proof rests on root positions, and a length op that shifted them silently would
+void it without any downstream check noticing.

+    no sidecar               -> exit 2. Every .abc predating the fix, produced
+                                by an unpatched process, or by another tool.
+    sidecar hash mismatch    -> exit 2. The file changed after it was gated.
+    widths all_zero or max<=0 -> exit 2.
+
+Escape: `--no-draw-gate`, documented as *"using it is a claim you own"*.
+
+**Why a sidecar and not a check.** Non-negotiable 3 prefers an input that cannot
+express the catastrophic value over a gate that rejects it. The export path now
+cannot emit zero widths. The sidecar extends that as far as it goes: a file with
+no provenance from the fixed path is refused by construction rather than
+inspected.
+
+### TO RUN
+
+    blender --background <blend> --python hero/groomloop/scripts/export_hero_groom.py -- <out.abc>
+      -> writes <out.abc> and <out.abc>.groomstats.json
+    python scripts/hero_face/likeness/ingest_groom.py --style <S> --abc <out.abc>
+      -> prints `draw gate : PASS widths max ..., root UVs N distinct, exporter <hash>`
+
+### THE UE-SIDE GUARD IS DEMOTED, DELIBERATELY
+
+`scripts/hero_face/likeness/groom_draw_guard.txt` refuses on unreadable
+`max_import_width` -- which is ALL grooms, including the two that render. That
+is correct fail-closed behaviour for a field that cannot be read, and it makes
+the guard useless as a discriminator. It is kept for `num_curves` and
+`max_curve_length` and is NOT the draw gate. **A guard that cannot see the
+defect it was written for should say so and step aside, not be tuned until its
+verdicts are agreeable.**
+
+## R-AIHAIR — AMENDED 2026-08-22: THE PANEL PATH IS A REHEARSAL, NOT A ROUTE
+
+Operator ruling: **never regenerate through the AI Hair panel to fix a groom
+that already has a validated lineage.** A regen is a different diffusion sample
+from the same image — different strands, and every registration, snap, export
+and bind proof taken on the old sample becomes void. Nothing is gained.
+
+The canonical strands are `difflocks_raw/hair_output_strands.npz`, hash-pinned.
+The hero's groom was delivered from that npz through
+`land_difflocks.py -> dl_full -> dl_k12 -> export_hero_groom.py -> UE`, one
+generation end to end.
+
+**The panel path in R-AIHAIR is retained for CHARACTER N+1 only** — the first
+generation for a character that has none. Re-running INGEST of an existing
+validated .abc through a hardened gate is not a regeneration and is always fine.
+
+## R-HEROGROOM — AMENDED: THE THREE-PANEL CROP RULE
+
+A reference portrait (1375x768) and a HighResShot (4064x2546) pasted at equal
+width compare a head against a landscape. Twice this project has produced a
+sheet that read as a hair difference and was a framing difference.
+
+    reference crops   measured, warm-subject mask restricted to the head band
+                      (find_head_crop.py)
+    game-frame crops  the warm mask FAILS -- autumn terrain is warm and it
+                      returns the full frame. Derive analytically instead:
+                      camera 75 cm out, viewport FOV 90 deg -> visible width
+                      150 cm, a ~30 cm head is 20% of frame width, centred by
+                      construction. Take 32% for margin: 0.34,0.245,0.66,0.755.
+    VERIFY IT         mean |diff| between two arms INSIDE the crop 11.49 against
+                      2.18 in a corner control -- 5.3x, so the head is in the
+                      box. A derived crop that is not verified is a guess with
+                      arithmetic attached.
+
+Every crop is burned into its panel caption with the source dimensions.

+### THE MECHANISM, FOR THE RECORD
+
+`att_groom_width` is a per-object pointer naming which Blender attribute feeds
+`groom_width`. On the clay object, built through the add-on's own operator, it
+reads `'radius'`. On every hand-built object it is the empty string.

+allocated with at `AlembicGroomExporter.py:244`. The array ships present,
+correct-length and correctly-typed.

+groom builder substitute a 1 cm default. A PRESENT width array of zeros is
+obeyed. The silent skip produced the one input shaped to slip past the safety
+net — worse than writing nothing.

+### THE EXPORT PROCEDURE, FINAL — six steps, and step 2 is a LOOP
+
+1. `att_groom_root_uv = "groom_root_uv"`
+2. **Set EVERY `att_*` pointer from one declaration**, not case by case. The
+   table lives in `export_hero_groom.py` as `(pointer, candidate source names,
+   accepted types, ue_consumed)` and reports SET / NO SOURCE per row.
+   `ue_consumed` is from `EHairAttribute` (HairAttributes.h:50-61): RootUV,
+   ClumpID, StrandID, PrecomputedGuideWeights, Color, Roughness, AO, Width.
+   Two hand-written cases is how this bug was found twice instead of once.
+3. `ob.update_tag()`; assert on the EVALUATED object.
+4. `groom_root_uv` FLOAT2 -> FLOAT_VECTOR in memory.
+5. Monkeypatch `ExporterOperators.getAttributeArray` for the FLOAT_VECTOR
+   fall-through, and STAMP the exporter's SHA-256 into the report — the add-on
+   on disk still writes zeros and the patch dies with the process, so two .abc
+   files with the same name can differ in whether the groom renders.
+6. Reopen the written ABC: refuse on all-zero widths, or fewer than two distinct
+   root UVs.
+
+### THE VALIDATOR, FINAL — eight checks
+
+Checks 1-4 presence; 5-7 degeneracy; **check 8 value variance on every resolved
+attribute.** Calibrated backwards against clay, which renders:
+`radius` min 0.012 / 12 distinct. So "distinct > 1" is NOT the bar — DiffLocks
+is legitimately uniform at 0.018 and renders. The bar is `min <= 0` or
+`all_zero`. Proven both directions: clay PASS, DiffLocks PASS, a deliberately
+zeroed radius REFUSE at exit 7.
+
+### UPSTREAM NOTE FOR THE ADD-ON AUTHOR (GroomExporter, Blender 5.2)
+
+Two defects, both silent:
+
+1. `ExporterOperators.py:65-75`, `case "FLOAT2"` — a flat `(2n,)` buffer is
+   `np.copyto`'d into an `(n,2)` memoryview with no reshape.
+   `ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (2n,) into shape
+   (n,2)`. FLOAT2 is the natural type for a UV, so `groom_root_uv` as FLOAT2 can
+   never export.
+2. `ExporterOperators.py:53` sets `out_type = type(out_array)` — a TYPE object —
+   and `:79-97` `match`es it against the STRING literals `"imath.V3fArray"` /
+   `"imath.V2fArray"`. A type never equals a string, so no case matches, the
+   `match` falls through with no default, the function returns None, and the
+   zero-initialised array ships. Same bug reaches FLOAT_COLOR and BYTE_COLOR.
+   Fix: `out_type = type(out_array).__name__`, or match on the class objects.
+
+Suggested third: when a pointer does not resolve, warn. A silent skip that
+produces a zero-filled array of the right length is indistinguishable from
+success at every downstream check.

+## R-GROOMABC, AMENDED 2026-08-22 (eyeball) — THE POINTER BUG IS A CLASS, NOT A FIELD
+
+The 2026-08-22 entry above treats the empty `att_groom_root_uv` pointer as the
+defect. It is one INSTANCE of the defect. All TWELVE exporter attributes resolve
+through their own per-object pointer and every one of them skips in silence.
+
+### THE FULL POINTER TABLE, MEASURED ON BOTH OBJECTS
+
+    pointer                    clay (operator-built)   DiffLocks (hand-built)
+    att_groom_width            'radius'      WRITE     ''   SKIP SILENTLY
+    att_groom_root_uv          'groom_root_uv' WRITE   ''   SKIP SILENTLY
+    the other ten              ''            SKIP      ''   SKIP
+
+`hero/groomloop/scripts/groom_pointer_audit.py` reproduces
+`ExporterOperators.getAttribute` against the EVALUATED attributes and prints
+WRITE / SKIP SILENTLY per pointer. Run it before any export from a hand-built
+Curves object.
+
+### THE WIDTH INSTANCE IS THE ONE THAT COSTS A RENDER
+
+`groom_width` is NOT an arb geom param. It feeds the ICurves schema's own
+`widths`, so a skipped width still produces a full-length `widths` array -- of
+zeros, from `AlembicGroomExporter.py:244`'s allocation, because
+`getAttributeArray` returns at `ExporterOperators.py:51-52`.

+    difflocks_k12_ue.abc   min 0.0    mean 0.0     max 0.0     1 distinct
+    difflocks_k12_full_ue  min 0.018  mean 0.018   max 0.018   (after the fix)
+
+**A groom with zero width draws zero pixels.** The schema diff reported `widths`
+present with the right LENGTH on both files, and that is exactly what a
+zero-filled array looks like to a presence check.
+
+### THE PROCEDURE, AMENDED — six steps now
+
+1. `ob.GroomProperty.att_groom_root_uv = "groom_root_uv"`
+2. **`ob.GroomProperty.att_groom_width = "radius"`** -- refuse if no FLOAT
+   `radius` attribute exists, because the alternative is shipping zero widths
+3. `ob.update_tag()` so both reach the evaluated copy; assert THERE
+4. convert `groom_root_uv` FLOAT2 -> FLOAT_VECTOR in memory
+5. monkeypatch `ExporterOperators.getAttributeArray` for the FLOAT_VECTOR
+   fall-through
+6. reopen the written ABC and refuse on all-zero widths OR fewer than two
+   distinct root UVs
+
+### AND THE SCHEMA CARRIES NO OTHER DIFFERENCE
+
+Re-bucketed mechanically by `abc_diff_classify.py`: of 16 differing fields, 7
+are root_uv rows, 8 are exactly (48000|576000) vs (100943|1211316), and the
+last is **`name`** -- the ICurves object name.
+`AlembicHairTranslator.cpp` reads attributes by the `groom_` prefix and has no
+object-name logic, so `name` is benign. **Beyond root_uv presence and the width
+values, the two files are structurally identical.**

+*Status: MECHANISM ESTABLISHED AT FOUR SOURCE LINES AND ONE ENGINE ASSERTION.
+The remedy is DESIGNED, NOT YET PROVEN — no render has been taken with
+interpolation data present.*
+
+### THE CHAIN
+
+    GroomAsset.cpp:3835   NeedsInterpolationData(GroupIndex) is TRUE only if
+                            IsSimulationEnable        || 
+                            IsGlobalInterpolationEnable ||
+                            GetEnableSimulationCache  ||
+                            IsDeformationEnable
+    GroomAsset.cpp:636    interpolation bulk data is built ONLY under that flag
+    GroomBuilder.cpp:1752 BuildInterplationBulkData returns early when
+                            PointCount == 0 || CurveCount == 0,
+                          leaving Header.Flags at 0
+    GroomBuilder.cpp:1758 otherwise Flags = DataFlags_HasData
+    GroomResources.cpp:1919
+                          FHairStrandsInterpolationResource's constructor
+                            check(!!(Flags & DataFlags_HasData));
+
+A groom built with simulation off AND global interpolation off has **no
+interpolation bulk data at all**. Nothing warns; the asset imports, reports the
+right curve counts, binds, and reads back correctly on every property.
+
+### THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVED IT, AND IT WAS A CRASH
+
+Setting `enable_simulation` True on a groom whose interpolation data was already
+built empty fatals the editor on that `check()`. The vendor groom, which ships
+with simulation True, does not — so the assertion is a two-sided instrument:
+
+    ours    enable_simulation True  ->  ASSERT   -> interpolation data ABSENT
+    vendor  enable_simulation True  ->  renders  -> interpolation data PRESENT
+
+### THE STATE OF EVERY GROOM ON THIS PROJECT
+
+    groom                    renders   enable_simulation   curve/vertex decim
+    DiffLocks k28              BALD         False              1.0 / 1.0
+    DiffLocks k12              BALD         False              1.0 / 1.0
+    procedural Clay_R4         BALD         False              1.0 / 1.0
+    vendor SideSweptFringe     DRAWS        True               0.8 / 0.5
+
+### THE REMEDY, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FORM OF IT DOES NOT WORK
+
+**The flag must be TRUE WHEN THE ASSET IS BUILT.** The DDC key includes
+`bNeedInterpolationData` (`GroomAsset.cpp:2494, 2607`), so the bulk data is
+produced per-key at build time. A post-hoc property write flips the flag on an
+asset whose data was already built empty, and the next resource creation walks
+into the `check()`. That is the crash above, and it is the FIRST thing anyone
+will try.
+
+So the flag goes on at IMPORT or REIMPORT, not afterwards. `GroomAsset.build()`
+is NOT the route — `RECIPES.md` R-GROOMBIND2 records it fataling this editor on
+`Assertion failed: IsUnlocked() [BulkData.cpp:596]`.
+
+**UNPROVEN.** No render exists with interpolation data present. Do not record
+this as the cause of the bald render until one does — the assertion proves the
+data is absent, not that its absence is what stops the draw.
+
+### THIS SUPERSEDES THE 2026-08-21 READING OF THE SAME CORRELATION
+
+That entry recorded six vendor hairs at `enable_global_interpolation` TRUE and
+every groom we ever made at FALSE, called it *"a correlation over five assets,
+not a mechanism"*, and guessed the mechanism was RBF-versus-rigid transfer. The
+correlation was right and the guessed mechanism was wrong:
+`IsGlobalInterpolationEnable` is one of the three disjuncts above.
+
+## R-GROOMINTERP REJECTED
+
+- **SETTING `enable_simulation` OR `enable_global_interpolation` ON A BUILT
+  GROOM.** **Symptom:** the editor dies on `Assertion failed:
+  !!(BulkData.Header.Flags & FHairStrandsInterpolationBulkData::DataFlags_HasData)`,
+  `GroomResources.cpp:1919`. **Why:** the bulk data was built empty under the
+  old DDC key and the property write does not rebuild it. **Correct:** set the
+  flag at import/reimport so the build produces the data.
+
+- **READING A ZERO FROM `get_console_variable_*` AS "OFF".** **Symptom:** four
+  hair cvars read 0 and are recorded as disabled. **Measured 2026-08-22:** a
+  deliberately impossible cvar name reads `float 0.0 / int 0 / bool false`,
+  identical to a real cvar at its default. `r.HairStrands.Cluster.Culling`,
+  `.Streaming`, `.Visibility` and `.Interpolation` are **not among the 145
+  `r.HairStrands*` names in the 5.8 source** — all four earlier reads were of
+  names that do not exist. **Correct:** grep the engine source for the name
+  first, and carry a fake-name control in the probe.
+
+- **`r.HairStrands.Visibility` AND `r.HairStrands.Interpolation` AS CVARS.**
+  They are namespace prefixes, not cvars. The real ones are
+  `r.HairStrands.Enable`, `.Strands`, `.Binding`, `.LODMode`, `.ViewMode`, and
+  the `Visibility.ComputeRaster.*` family.
+
+- **`r.HairStrands.ViewMode` AS AN ENUM INDEX.** The cvar int is mapped by a
+  switch at `GroomVisualizationData.cpp:45-90` and is NOT the `EGroomViewMode`
+  ordinal: **34 = ControlPoints, 41 = Bounds, 31 = Cluster, 21 = SimHairStrands,
+  22 = RenderHairStrands, 13 = Coverage.** The cvar sets and reads back, but
+  **it produced no visible difference through the SceneCapture path** — two
+  captures at ViewMode 34 differed by 0.02 in mean. Not established whether the
+  visualization pass runs for a SceneCapture2D at all; treat the debug view as
+  UNAVAILABLE through this rig until that is settled.
+
+- **CARRYING A CONTROL'S LABEL BETWEEN SESSIONS.** **Symptom:** `Clay_R4` sat in
+  probe after probe as `"procedural (draws)"` and had not been gated in this
+  session. It is bald. Three acquittals built on it were void. **Correct:**
+  gate the control in the session that relies on it. It is one four-minute run

+## 2026-08-22 — THE SUSPECT LIST WAS RANKED BY PLAUSIBILITY AND MEASURED IN THE OPPOSITE ORDER
+
+An external analysis arrived with a ranked causal catalog for the bald DiffLocks
+render, with probability mass attached: degenerate strands ~55%, guide
+correspondence ~15%, quantization collapse ~10%, empty render resources ~8%,
+stale-component measurement ~7%, root UVs ~2%. It was a good catalog. Four of
+the six were already measured false by the time it was written, and the one
+genuinely untested item it named — the per-group physics/simulation diff — came
+back acquitted with a positive control inside the same reading.
+
+That is not a criticism of the catalog. It is the reason to write down what a
+ranked list is FOR: it orders the CHEAP DISCRIMINATORS, and its probabilities
+are a statement about the author's information, not about the artefact. The
+useful part of the document was its list of discriminators; the percentages were
+the part that aged in one turn.
+
+### THE ACQUITTAL, AND WHY IT IS AN ACQUITTAL AND NOT A SHRUG
+
+The theory was mechanically sound: UE's documented contract says guide
+interpolation runs when simulation is enabled or a skinned binding is attached,
+which should exempt an unbound groom — but a per-GROUP `enable_simulation`
+defaulting on would push the unbound groom through interpolation with whatever
+guide weights it has. And the earlier "interpolation settings read identical"
+check had covered the ASSET-level settings, not the per-GROUP ones. A real gap.
+
+Four grooms, one call, same instrument:
+
+    groom                        enable_simulation   curve/vertex decimation
+    DiffLocks k28   BALD               False               1.0 / 1.0
+    DiffLocks k12   BALD               False               1.0 / 1.0
+    procedural      DRAWS              False               1.0 / 1.0
+    vendor          DRAWS              True                0.8 / 0.5
+
+**The field that DIFFERS between the two grooms that both render is the same
+field that is IDENTICAL between one that renders and one that does not.** That
+shape is what makes it evidence rather than a null: a reading in which every row
+agreed would have been consistent with an accessor that returns a default. Here
+one row moved, so the instrument demonstrably discriminates, and it still puts
+the bald groom on the same side as a groom that draws.
+
+### THE ARITHMETIC CORROBORATION FOR THE DEGENERACY ACQUITTAL
+
+The strand-length histogram had already cleared degeneracy (min 2.6756 cm, zero
+under 2 cm, unimodal 2.7–15 cm). A second, independent argument fell out of the
+count itself:
+
+    100,943   sqrt 317.715  (317^2 = 100489, 318^2 = 101124)
+              /1024 = 98.577
+              no small factors
+
+It is not a grid, not a power of two, not a texel budget. A generator emitting
+one strand per scalp texel produces a round number; 100,943 is what is LEFT after
+a filter. DiffLocks filtered before writing. That reasons from a completely
+different property than the histogram does, which is the whole point of asking a
+second question rather than re-asking the first more carefully.
+
+### THE GATE THAT CAME OUT OF IT — AND ITS BARS ARE SET BY A CONTROL
+
+Checks 5-7 (segment collapse, strand collapse, root collision) are now permanent
+in `validate_groom_export.py`, recipe **R-GROOMVALID**. The class is real and
+cheap to catch; the next generative style will regenerate it.
+
+But calibrating them against the groom that DRAWS inverted every intuition:
+
+    metric                     DiffLocks (BALD)   procedural (DRAWS)
+    min consecutive-point d      0.0806 cm          0.0092 cm
+    distinct root positions     76,379 of 100,943   1,211 of 48,000
+    largest root cluster            10                166
+
+**The groom that renders has 2.5% distinct root positions.** Procedural
+authoring grows clumps from guides, so its roots pile up by construction. A bar
+tightened to look strict — "refuse many roots sharing a spot" — refuses the
+known-good groom on its most characteristic property. Only the exactly-zero
+cases refuse, because a zero-length segment has no tangent and a zero-length
+strand has no direction; those are UNDEFINED rather than merely ugly.
+
+**This is the third time in two days that a gate written for a real defect class
+would have refused a working artefact if it had not been positive-controlled**
+(`verify_export_bounds.py`, retired in place; the rear rubric's `mask_frac`;
+this). The pattern is specific enough to name: **A GATE WRITTEN FROM A THEORY OF
+THE DEFECT MUST BE CALIBRATED AGAINST THE ARTEFACT THAT WORKS, NOT AGAINST THE
+THEORY.** The theory says what to measure. Only the working artefact says where
+the bar goes.
+
+### AND ONE ORDINARY BUG THAT WOULD HAVE INVERTED THE WHOLE READING
+
+Hair points are stored in one flat buffer. The last point of curve *i* and the
+first point of curve *i+1* are adjacent in it and are NOT a segment. A `diff`
+over the whole buffer invents one large bogus segment per curve — 47,999 of them
+on the procedural groom — and its magnitude dominates every statistic taken
+afterwards, so `min_segment` reads plausible and the short-segment count reads
+zero on a groom that has short segments. Masking `starts[1:] - 1` is the fix,
+and the refusal test corroborates it independently: collapsing one 12-point
+strand produces ELEVEN zero segments, not twelve.

+## R-AIHAIR — the AI Hair Toolkit operator surface, enumerated
+
+*Recorded 2026-08-22. Status: MEASURED (enumerated live, not inferred from
+the UI).*
+
+The documented fast path for CHARACTER N+1. Tonight's hero groom did NOT go
+through it — see the lineage note below — but for a fresh character this is the
+shortest route from a portrait to native Hair Curves.
+
+### THE WHOLE SURFACE. Four operators, and NONE of them takes an argument.
+
+    bpy.ops.aihair.generate_hair        Generate Hair
+    bpy.ops.aihair.apply_optimization   Apply Optimization
+    bpy.ops.aihair.first_run_setup      First-time Environment Setup
+    bpy.ops.aihair.stop_server          Stop Server
+
+    panel   AIHAIR_PT_main, N-strip category "AI Hair Toolkit"
+
+### THE THREE FACTS THAT DECIDE WHETHER YOU CAN USE IT
+
+1. THERE IS NO LOADER. No import, no open, not one filepath or directory
+   argument anywhere in the namespace. Its ONLY input is `generate_hair`, which
+   calls the live server. It cannot read an .npz off disk, so it cannot consume
+   a hash-pinned payload from a previous session.
+2. `apply_optimization` TAKES NO ARGUMENTS. It reads the panel's scene
+   properties (Hair Count %, Curve Resolution) and acts on the session's current
+   object. Scripting it headlessly means setting those properties, not passing
+   them.
+3. THE PANEL IS SERVER-GATED. It appears when the runtime server is warm on
+   8765. A missing panel is a cold server, not a missing add-on.
+
+### AND ITS DECIMATION HAS A MEASURED CAVEAT
+
+The Hair Count % slider is the obvious lever and on the hero's data it did NOT
+do what it looks like it does. Measured 2026-08-22: 33% → 100% of strands moved
+rendered silhouette mass 0.4917 → 0.5345, nine per cent and not three times,
+because `hair_area_over_face_area` measures the OUTLINE and strands added inside
+the same envelope do not grow it. Curve Resolution is what actually carries a
+reduction: 256 → 28 points is 89% fewer points at full strand count.
+**Decimate POINTS, not STRANDS**, unless you have measured otherwise on that
+character.
+
+### LINEAGE, and why tonight's groom did not use this path
+
+The canonical payload is the repo npz, hash-pinned. Since the add-on has no
+loader, its path is bound to whichever generation is live in the session — a
+second, different sample. Two generations must not blur into one lineage, and
+here they cannot: only one route reaches the pinned payload.
+
+### RELATED
+
+`GroomExporter` is the other enabled add-on and it DOES take a filepath:
+`bpy.ops.groom.buttonexport(filepath=..., groom_scale=1.0, ...)`. That is the
+export path in use, and the one that writes `groom_root_uv` — whose absence put
+every pack-derived groom on the hero's jaw.

+### A GREEN PING FROM THE WRONG PROCESS
+
+The build finished, the shim went in, the server was started, and
+`GET /ping` returned `ok`. Everything said go. **The `ok` came from a
+different server.**
+
+A pre-natten server from an earlier attempt was still bound to 8765
+(started 15:16). The freshly launched one could never take the port, sat
+there importing torch, and printed nothing but its own launcher banner —
+so its log looked like a slow start rather than a failure:
+
+    port 8765 owned by PID 31844  started 15:16:09     <- the stale one
+    my server              PID 19900  started 16:37:20 <- never bound
+
+Had `/generate` been fired then, it would have run **the old code with no
+shim and no sm_120 natten**, and whatever came back — success or failure —
+would have been attributed to a build it never touched.
+
+**THE RULE: A HEALTH CHECK PROVES SOMETHING IS LISTENING, NOT THAT YOUR
+THING IS LISTENING.** After starting a service, verify the *identity* of
+what answers — owning PID and start time against the moment you launched
+it — not merely that the port answers. The check costs one command; the
+alternative is a whole afternoon's conclusions hanging off the wrong
+process. Same family as the earlier exit-0 that only proved a redirect
+succeeded: **the cheap green signal is the one worth distrusting.**
+
+Corollary: kill stale servers before starting a new one, and confirm the
+port is actually free rather than assuming the previous session tidied up.

+## NATTEN BUILDS ON BLACKWELL; IT IS WINDOWS THAT FIGHTS BACK
+
+**Date:** 2026-08-22, continuing from the 0.17.5 wall above. Operator ruled
+for the newer-natten + shim path. Target still sm_120, RTX 5080 Laptop.
+
+### THE ARCH PROBLEM EVAPORATED AND EVERY REMAINING PROBLEM WAS PORTABILITY
+
+natten **0.21.7** deletes the `arch < 100` assert that stopped 0.17.5 — its
+validator checks only `arch >= 30`. The first build attempt printed
+
+    Building NATTEN for the following archs: [120] (max: 120)
+    --generate-code=arch=compute_120,code=[sm_120]
+
+on its way to failing for reasons that had nothing to do with Blackwell.
+**Every subsequent failure was a Windows bug, and the arch handling was
+never wrong again after the version bump.** Two of them, both in flags:
+
+**One.** `csrc/CMakeLists.txt` adds `-Xcompiler=-Wconversion` and
+`-fno-strict-aliasing` unconditionally. With nvcc's
+`-forward-unknown-to-host-compiler` these reach `cl`, which reads
+`/Wconversion` as a malformed `/W<n>`:
+
+    cl : Command line error D8021 : invalid numeric argument '/Wconversion'
+
+All 88 units failed identically. The file already had a `NATTEN_IS_WINDOWS`
+branch further down — the flags simply were not in it.
+
+**Two.** At 60/88, `natten/helpers.h` uses the C++ alternative operator
+token `not` inside a `TORCH_CHECK(not x.is_sparse(), ...)` macro that
+expands at dozens of sites:
+
+    error: identifier "not" is undefined
+
+nvcc's EDG front-end in MSVC-compatibility mode does not enable alternative
+tokens. `--pre-include iso646.h` fixes it by defining them as macros, so the
+preprocessor rewrites `not` to `!` before the front-end ever sees the token.
+
+**The trap inside the fix:** `-Xcompiler /FIiso646.h` is the obvious-looking
+equivalent and does nothing, because `-Xcompiler` forwards only to the host
+compiler pass and this error comes from nvcc's own front-end. *A CUDA
+translation unit is compiled by two different compilers and a flag aimed at
+the wrong one fails silently rather than loudly.*
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**A TWENTY-FIVE MINUTE BUILD IS A TERRIBLE PLACE TO TEST A ONE-LINE
+HYPOTHESIS.** Both flag fixes were verified against a six-line `.cu` in
+about four seconds each — reproduce the exact error without the flag, watch
+it compile with it — before touching the real build. The second probe also
+answered a question the build could not have answered cheaply: `cl` rejects
+`not` too (C2065), so the host `.cpp` path needed checking. It turned out
+`natten.cpp` is the only host source, does not include `helpers.h`, and is
+clean — **so the right change there was no change at all**, which is a
+conclusion only reachable by asking.
+
+**Why this class of bug was waiting:** natten publishes **no Windows wheels
+on PyPI** — sdist only, every version. Nobody upstream compiles this path.
+Expect flag portability bugs, not algorithmic ones, and expect them in
+whichever file the platform branch forgot.
+
+### AN OUTPUT DIRECTORY THAT DELETES ITSELF
+
+Unrelated to the build, found while reading `server.py` before trusting it
+with a ten-minute generation. `SessionOutputRegistry.clear()` removes every
+directory listed in `outputs/.aihair_session.json`, and it is reached from
+**two** places: `POST /shutdown`, and `cleanup_pending()` at **server
+startup** (`server.py:271`).
+
+**So the outputs of a run are destroyed by the next server start, not just
+by an explicit shutdown.** The manifest already listed `hero_hair_v1` from
+an earlier failed attempt. The rule this hands forward: **copy results out
+of `runtime\outputs\` before restarting or shutting down anything** —
+treat that directory as scratch with a timer on it, never as storage.

@@ -22330,3 +22330,96 @@ read as "denser guides are better" and the next session would have tuned
 density. Three points showed a cliff, and a cliff names a different mechanism
 entirely. **The second and third measurements were the cheap ones and they are
 what turned a working configuration into a diagnosis.**
+
+## NATTEN 0.17.5 CANNOT BE BUILT FOR BLACKWELL, AND THE REASON IS NOT THE TOOLCHAIN
+
+**Date:** 2026-08-22. Target: sm_120 (RTX 5080 Laptop, compute capability
+verified `(12, 0)` on hardware, not inferred from a model name).
+
+### THE TOOLCHAIN VERDICT, WHICH IS THE PART THAT WORKED
+
+Two Visual Studios were installed. **Build Tools 2022 won, and Community
+2026 lost on a version ceiling rather than a missing workload** — it had
+the C++ toolchain, it just carried MSVC 14.51:
+
+    VS 18 Community    cl 19.51.36256   REJECTED
+    Build Tools 2022   cl 19.44.35228   nvcc -arch=sm_120 COMPILES
+
+CUDA 12.8's `crt/host_config.h` refuses `_MSC_VER >= 1950`, and 19.51 is
+1951. The error names its own escape hatch (`-allow-unsupported-compiler`)
+and that hatch was not taken, because a host compiler NVIDIA has not
+qualified is a bad foundation for a twenty-minute template-heavy CUDA build.
+
+**The cheap measurement that made this a verdict instead of a guess:** a
+six-line `.cu` compiled at `-arch=sm_120` under each vcvars. Reading
+`host_config.h` predicted the answer; compiling proved it, and also proved
+the thing actually being asked — that this toolchain can emit sm_120 at all.
+
+### THE ACTUAL WALL
+
+`setup.py` never reaches the compiler. Its arch validator:
+
+    arch = float(arch) * 10          # 8.6 => 86
+    assert arch >= 30 and arch < 100, \
+        f"Only SM30 and above are supported at this time, got {arch}."
+
+`12.0 * 10 = 120`. Reproduced verbatim:
+
+    Only SM30 and above are supported at this time, got 120.0.
+
+**The upper bound is silent in the message.** It reports itself as a
+*minimum* check — "SM30 and above" — while failing on a maximum. A message
+that describes only half of its own condition sends you looking for a
+floor you clear by four generations.
+
+### TWO TRAPS UNDER THE FIRST ONE
+
+**The pinned env var was the wrong variable.** The build spec pinned
+`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0`, which is the torch convention; natten 0.17.5
+reads `NATTEN_CUDA_ARCH`. Had that been the only problem it would have
+presented as the pin being silently ignored, not as an error.
+
+**And unsetting it does not help.** With no arch specified natten derives
+one from the live device — `major + minor * 0.1` — which on this card is
+`12.0`, into the same assert. **There is no configuration of the
+environment that gets this source tree past its own front door.**
+
+### HOW DEEP IT GOES, WHICH IS THE PART THAT DECIDES THE FIX
+
+The assert is one line and patching it is one edit, so the only question
+worth asking is what is waiting behind it. The bundled CUTLASS answers:
+
+    third_party/cutlass/include/cutlass/arch/   mma_sm50 ... mma_sm90.h
+    grep -rl "sm120|Sm120|SM120"                (nothing)
+    grep -rl "Sm100|SM100"                      (nothing)
+
+Ceiling is sm90, with no Blackwell awareness anywhere in the tree. The
+autogen kernels agree: `gemm/2d/` stops at `sm80`, and the fused path
+(`fna/`) is CUTLASS-backed.
+
+**So the one-line patch buys a compile, not a kernel.** Arch-guarded
+CUTLASS kernels compile to nothing at `__CUDA_ARCH__ == 1200` and the
+result is a natten that imports, reports 0.17.5, and dies at the first
+real op with *the exact "no kernel image is available" that started this* —
+a build that looks like a success everywhere except where it is used.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**AN ASSERT IS A CHEAP LIE ABOUT HOW DEEP A GAP IS.** One line stood
+between this tree and a compile, which made "delete the line" look like
+the fix; the vendored dependency three directories down had never heard of
+the target architecture, which made it a way to convert a loud build
+failure into a quiet runtime one. **Before patching a version gate, go
+read what the gate is protecting** — the guard is a claim about the code
+behind it, and that claim is checkable in about two minutes.
+
+Corollary, earned twice today: **the shi-labs wheel index falls through to
+an sdist build in silence.** The retry produced not "index unreachable"
+but `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'` from a build-isolation
+subprocess — a message about the *build* of a package you never intended
+to build. Watch what pip actually resolved, not what it printed last.
+
+Corollary, mechanical: **CUTLASS cannot be extracted into a deep path on
+Windows.** `depthwise_fprop_activation_tile_access_iterator_direct_conv_
+fixed_stride_dilation.h` blows MAX_PATH from a normal scratchpad
+directory. Build third-party CUDA from a short root; `C:\nb` worked.

commit 04dc7bf3571ece30ad28a7d66aa6731b44e5b844
Author: ryanb <ryanbme83@gmail.com>
Date:   2026-08-22 03:27:40 -0700

    The plateau was structural, and curve index carried the answer
    
    Scores sat at 40/50 for seven iterations, which is the brief's escalation
    threshold, so a fresh-context agent was consulted with the spec, APPROACHES.md,
    the log and recon.
    
    ITS DIAGNOSIS WAS CORRECT AND I HAD NOT ARTICULATED IT. Every op in the edit
    engine has the form f(root_position) x g(t) -- the field is evaluated in ROOT
    space, never at the point's current position. Two strands rooted 1 mm apart
    therefore receive near-identical displacement at every t, forever. A map that
    is smooth in root space CANNOT open a gap between them, so clumping could only
    ever trade coverage from one place to another. That is exactly why the groom
    kept reading as a dense uniform mass no matter what the clump parameters did.
    
    THE CHEAP PROBE IT SUGGESTED PAID IMMEDIATELY. Does curve index carry authored
    structure? Consecutive-index roots sit 4.13 mm apart against 125 mm for random
    pairs -- ratio 0.033 -- decaying smoothly with stride (0.033 / 0.049 / 0.093 /
    0.166 / 0.310 / 0.578 / 0.780). The exporter emitted curves patch by patch, so
    a block of consecutive indices IS an authored, spatially coherent patch: a
    better lock partition than any quantised grid, and free.
    
    Swapping lat/long cells for index blocks improved coverage AND texture
    together, which nothing in the previous 23 iterations had managed -- every
    earlier change traded one against the other. Block size has a clear optimum:
    400 -> 36.19 mean scalp, 200 -> 33.56, 120 -> 31.48, 60 -> 29.03.
    
    New pick: iter_028, combining 026's authored lock partition with 021's fringe
    strength. Mean scalp visibility 22.93% against the untouched source's 43.88%,
    fringe +0.96 cm past the brow, forehead cover 70.3%, tip scatter 0.606. All
    three top candidates re-exported at UE scale with a corrected radius and
    re-imported into the live editor at 93,198 curves.
    
    AND THE THIRD METRIC-VERSUS-PICTURE DIVERGENCE OF THE RUN, WHICH IS THE MOST
    INSTRUCTIVE ONE. Iteration 029 scored the best numbers of everything -- mean
    18.90%, fringe +2.02 cm, cover 85.3% -- and it is REJECTED. The proxy head is
    an ellipsoid with no face, so hair hanging over where the face would be counts
    as "scalp covered": the metric was rewarding it for hiding him. 028 is the pick
    on the picture. Recorded in the report and the log as the worked example of why
    the render is the tie-breaker and the metric only the argument.
    
    Two mechanisms from the same consult remain unexplored and are written up for
    whoever picks this up: an iterated position-evaluated lock field with
    separatrices, and an arc-length-conserving directional comb that re-routes
    existing length instead of stretching it. Its criticism of grade_ratio also
    stands and is recorded: that metric compares nape-ROOTED to crown-ROOTED
    length, but a layered cut's collar-length hair is over-layer hair rooted much
    higher, so the metric can only be satisfied by the mechanism iteration 022
    proved destructive.

+## 2026-08-21 (seating, continued) — THE AUTHORED HAIR RENDERS ON THE HERO, AND THE THING THAT FIXED IT IS NOT THE THING I WAS BISECTING
+
+**The seating works.** `_verify/20260821_artdirect/TEST_v22_guides_every1_*.png` is
+the Blender-authored groom, bound, on the hero's own MetaHuman component, with
+its length and volume intact. Gated at the comparison framing: **Hair PRESENT,
+29.6x floor, crown 91%, drift 0.6%**, reproduced across two passes.
+
+### FIRST, THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE ENTRY ABOVE, ALL FROM ITS OWN TOOL
+
+**1. THE GUIDE STACK DOES NOT MOVE THE GEOMETRY.** `build_guide_stack.py`
+reports `evaluated_z` **[158.645, 181.894]** against the raw authored
+[158.633, 181.971], and `crown_delta_cm` 3.457 against the authored height gain
+3.52. The stack's evaluated output is the authored curves to within a
+millimetre.
+
+**2. SO "ONE GROOM, THREE SHAPES" IS WRONG, AND SO IS THE COMMIT NAMED AFTER
+IT.** Panels 1 and 2 of that sheet were an ORTHOGRAPHIC Blender workbench
+preview and a PERSPECTIVE UE render of the same geometry, and I read a shape
+difference into a camera difference. There are TWO shapes, not three: the
+authored one, and the collapsed one on the hero. **This is the project's own
+recurring error — judging shape across two cameras — committed by me one entry
+after writing the rule against it.**
+
+**3. THE TWO NODES I NAMED FOR THE BISECT NEVER RAN.** The tool's report says
+so, in a field called `skipped`, with a reason: `Shrinkwrap Hair Curves` and
+`Attach Hair Curves to Surface` are Blender essentials assets that are **not in
+the demo .blend** and are absent after append. The applied stack is three
+nodes, not five. I had read the comment that says this at line 153 of the file
+and written the bisect plan anyway.
+
+**And I nearly destroyed the evidence for it:** the env-override I added for
+the bisect wrote `rep["skipped"]`, which is that field's name, and overwrote it
+on the first run. Renamed to `skip_requested`. **A new key that collides with
+an existing one in the same report is a silent data loss, and it landed on the
+one field that mattered.**
+
+### WHAT ACTUALLY FIXED IT, AND IT IS A SHARP THRESHOLD NOT A GRADIENT
+
+Single variable, same blend, same builder, same session, only `guide_every`
+differing:
+
+    guide_every 20     2,400 guides    BALD
+    guide_every  4    12,000 guides    BALD
+    guide_every  1    48,000 guides    FULL HAIR, gated, reproduced
+
+**A gradient would mean density. A cliff at "every curve is a guide" means
+CORRESPONDENCE.** When every curve is its own guide, each strand's nearest
+guide is itself and its weights are trivially correct. Any subset requires
+`Merge Guide and Weight it` to compute which guides drive which strands, and
+for our groom it computes something the deformation cannot use.
+
+**So this is a WORKAROUND, not a repair.** It costs 3x the curves (144,000
+against 52,800) and it leaves the weighting defect in place. Saying that
+plainly matters more than the win: a fix that works for a reason you have not
+established will break the first time something moves.
+
+### THE OTHER THING THAT CLEARED A WHOLE SUBSYSTEM
+
+A VENDOR groom built through **our own** `build_fresh_groom_binding` renders
+correctly on the hero — indistinguishable from the vendor's own binding. That
+single control retired the binding builder as a suspect after two days of work
+had gone into binding routes.
+
+### AND A GROOM FROM A THIRD-PARTY PACK, WHICH IS THE GENERAL CASE
+
+`SC_Hairstyle_Male_11` (94,408 curves), three configurations:
+
+    its own binding GB_SC_...        BALD
+    our IDENTITY binding             DRAWS -- seated on the JAW, scalp bare
+    our SOURCE-TRANSFER binding      BALD
+      (source = the pack's own SKM_MH_Groom_Head, target = our face)
+
+**The jaw seating is the informative one.** An identity binding says "this
+groom was authored on the target's own topology", and this one was not — it was
+authored on `SKM_MH_Groom_Head`, so its raw coordinates land where they fall.
+That is what `SOURCE_MESH` exists for, and supplying it correctly still
+produced nothing, so the transfer path is unproven rather than wrong.
+
+**The rule this hands forward:** a groom carries the head it was authored on,
+and that head is discoverable — the pack's own binding declares it as BOTH its
+source and its target. Read it from the binding rather than guessing.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**A SHARP THRESHOLD AND A GRADIENT ARE DIFFERENT DIAGNOSES, AND ONE POINT
+CANNOT TELL THEM APART.** Had `guide_every 1` been tried alone it would have
+read as "denser guides are better" and the next session would have tuned
+density. Three points showed a cliff, and a cliff names a different mechanism
+entirely. **The second and third measurements were the cheap ones and they are
+what turned a working configuration into a diagnosis.**

+    guide stack        renders, collapsed to a cap
+    vendor groom       renders correctly through the SAME binding builder
+
+So the stack supplies something UE's deformation requires — the surface
+attachment and the guides — and supplies it in a form that also loses the
+shape.
+
+### THE METRIC THAT WAS TELLING ME THIS ON THE FIRST RUN
+
+`preview_hair.py` on the guide-stack blend reported `height_gain_cm` **0.05**
+against the authored blend's **3.52**, and `hair_over_face_px` 9,192 against
+2,194. **I dismissed both as metric artefacts because `hair_px` barely moved.**
+They were the finding, or at least the flag: the stack changes the geometry
+enough to move the silhouette gain by 70x.
+
+**And the metric is probably ALSO void**, which is why dismissing it was so
+easy to justify: that blend contains a guide OBJECT, so hiding the hair object
+does not produce a bare head, and the difference render's control is
+contaminated. **A number that is both alarming and untrustworthy is the worst
+kind, and the right response is to fix the control, not to explain the number
+away.**
+
+### THE DEEPER SHAPE OF IT
+
+`preview_hair.py` takes its CENSUS from raw curve data and its SILHOUETTE from
+a render, which evaluates modifiers. On a blend with a Geometry Nodes stack
+those are **two different pieces of geometry**, and the tool reports them side
+by side as though they describe one thing. Every scalp and root statistic this
+week described the pre-stack curves; every silhouette described the post-stack
+evaluation; and the alembic that shipped carried the post-stack evaluation.
+
+**This is the same disease as the entry above, one layer down.** There, two
+representations lived in different processes and never met. Here they live in
+one tool, in one report, under one heading.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**A TOOL THAT REPORTS ON MORE THAN ONE REPRESENTATION MUST LABEL EVERY NUMBER
+WITH THE ONE IT CAME FROM.** Not in a docstring — in the report, beside the
+value, where the person reading it is looking. `preview_hair.py` already
+separates GATES from DESCRIPTIVE metrics, which was the right instinct applied
+to the wrong axis: the dangerous split here is not trustworthy-versus-not, it
+is raw-versus-evaluated.
+
+### WHAT IS NOT DONE
+
+**The seating is not fixed.** It is localised to two stages with a picture of
+each, which is a much better place than the session started, and the next unit
+is a bisect of the five-node stack — Set Hair Curve Profile / Add Guide Object
+/ Shrinkwrap Hair Curves / Attach Hair Curves to Surface / Merge Guide and
+Weight it. **Shrinkwrap and Attach are the two that can move geometry**, and
+Attach is the one whose absence makes the groom draw nothing, so the bisect has
+an obvious first cut: keep Attach, drop Shrinkwrap.

+A custom groom can be wrong in at least six places, and a picture cannot tell
+them apart. This is the ordered set of controls that CAN, each moving one
+thing. Run it in order and stop at the first disagreement — that rung is where
+the shape is lost.

+### THE LADDER

+    6  standalone GroomActor, BOUND                  same, --set BIND=<path>

+       is how two days went into binding routes for a defect that is not in
+       the binding.
+    7  the real component, bound                     the shipping configuration
+    8  the real component, unbound                   expected: nothing draws

+## 2026-08-21 (art direction) — THE RUBRIC MEASURED THE FOREST, THEN MEASURED A HOLE, AND EXITED 0 BOTH TIMES
+
+The session goal was the one open item nobody had touched: three hair defects

+

+reference is a long layered shag and v22 is a short crop — a difference of
+CLASS, not of tuning. That belongs in the report
+(`_verify/20260821_artdirect/ART_DIRECTION.md`) and Ryan's ruling. What belongs
+here is what happened when I tried to put a NUMBER on the rear.
+
+### WHAT HAPPENED
+
+`rear_metrics.py` was built on 2026-08-21 and measured the rear reference
+cleanly: taper_ratio 0.5533, edge_roughness 27.9648, a width profile rising
+0.38 -> 1.00 and falling to 0.42. Those numbers are in `characters/registry.json`
+as the target. Pointing the SAME code at our own render — which is the tool's
+central design claim, one implementation for both sides — produced:
+
+    level camera   taper_ratio 0.3255   edge_roughness 283.3909   exit 0
+    sky behind     taper_ratio 0.4072   edge_roughness 142.7551   exit 0
+
+Both are garbage, and both look like measurements.
+
+### ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS TWO DIFFERENT FAILURES WEARING ONE SYMPTOM
+
+The mask is `luma <= 70 AND sat <= 0.35`, calibrated on a flat-lit studio
+portrait on plain grey where hair is the only dark thing in frame.
+
+**Failure one — the background joins the subject.** Against the level camera
+the hero stands in front of a shadowed forest, which is dark and not
+especially saturated, so it satisfies both predicates. `_largest_component`
+exists precisely to drop a dark background, and it cannot help when the
+background is CONTIGUOUS WITH the subject: the canopy touches the head
+silhouette, so hair and forest are one blob and the biggest blob is both.
+`crown_width_px` came back 1322 in a 2048 frame — the mask's bounding box was
+most of the sky.
+
+**Failure two — the subject leaves the mask.** Re-shot with the head against
+sky, the background separated and the mask became a hollow RING: the sunlit
+crown is BRIGHTER than luma_max 70, so only the silhouette rim and the shadowed
+strands survive. Area is understated and perimeter is roughly doubled by the
+inner boundary, which is what put edge_roughness at 5x the reference.
+
+**Neither is a threshold that wants nudging.** The first is a background that
+cannot be separated by luminance; the second is a subject that is not uniformly
+dark under directional light. One rig fixes both and no constant does.
+
+### WHY THE GATE DID NOT FIRE, AND THIS IS THE GENERAL PART
+
+The tool refuses a mask outside `[0.005, 0.50]` of the frame. Both failures
+sailed through, because **a wrong region can be the right SIZE.** A gate on the
+EXTENT of a measurement region cannot see whether the region is the right one.
+The forest blob was 3.2% of frame; so was a plausible head of hair.
+
+This is non-negotiable 0 in a new costume. The mask fraction and the metrics
+are computed from the SAME mask, so the check and the thing checked share a
+source and cannot corroborate each other. The instrument that actually worked
+was the one that reads a DIFFERENT representation: dumping the mask as a PNG
+and looking at it. The tool's own docstring demands exactly that — *"Look at it
+before believing any number here"* — and it is the reason this cost minutes
+instead of becoming a recorded rear taper number for the hero.
+
+**A tool that names its own weak link, and provides the instrument for
+inspecting it, is why the failure was caught by design rather than by luck.**
+That is the pattern worth repeating: when a step is known to be fragile, ship
+the means to look at it in the same tool, and say in the docstring that the
+numbers are not to be trusted until someone has.
+
+### WHAT IS OWED
+
+The rubric is not broken; its INPUT is out of range. The fix is the flat-lit
+close rig against a plain background that the eye-colour item has needed for

+## R-HAIRREAR — THE REAR RUBRIC, AND THE INPUTS IT CANNOT MEASURE (2026-08-21)
+
+**Status: PROVEN ON THE REFERENCE, REFUSED-BY-INSPECTION ON AN IN-WORLD
+RENDER.** Narrative in `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE RUBRIC MEASURED THE
+FOREST, THEN MEASURED A HOLE").
+
+`scripts/hero_face/likeness/rear_metrics.py` measures the back of a cut with
+one implementation for the reference AND the candidate, which is the whole
+point of it — a rubric with two measurement paths is two lists that must agree.
+Every metric is scale-free or normalised by head height, so the 1375x768
+portrait and a 2048 SceneCapture are comparable by construction.
+
+### WHAT IT MEASURES, AND THE TARGET VALUES
+
+Measured on `hero/reference/hero_example_pic_rear.jpg` at luma_max 70.0 /
+sat_max 0.35, mask inspected as a PNG before the numbers were used. These are
+declared in `characters/registry.json` and are the numbers to beat:
+
+    mask_frac        0.1943
+    taper_ratio      0.5533     nape width / crown width; a blunt bottom
+                                edge reads near 1.0
+    edge_roughness  27.9648     perimeter / sqrt(area), dimensionless
+    crown_width_px     476.0
+    nape_width_px      263.3
+    width_profile    rises 0.38 -> 1.00 over the upper half, falls to 0.42
+
+### THE PROCEDURE
+
+    1  render the rear                    the hero turned 180 deg:
+                                          place_hero_in_world.py --yaw-offset 90
+                                          (the frontal default is -90)
+    2  rear_metrics.py --dump-mask <png>  ALWAYS pass --dump-mask
+    3  OPEN THE MASK                      before any number is quoted
+    4  compare against the table above
+
+**STEP 3 IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT CAUGHT THE FAILURES
+BELOW.** The tool exits 0 on both of them.
+
+### THE INPUT CONTRACT — this is what the REJECTED entries are about
+
+The mask is `luma <= luma_max AND sat <= sat_max`. It is sound only where:
+
+- **the background is separable by luminance** — hair must be the darkest
+  thing touching the head silhouette; and
+- **the subject is uniformly dark** — flat or diffuse light, so the whole hair
+  mass sits under `luma_max`, not just its shadowed rim.
+
+A flat-lit portrait on plain grey satisfies both. **A sunlit in-world render
+satisfies neither, and there is no constant that fixes it.**
+
+## R-HAIRREAR REJECTED
+
+- **AN IN-WORLD RENDER WITH FOREST BEHIND THE HEAD.** **Symptom:** exit 0,

+  reference's 27.96, `taper_ratio` 0.3255. **Why:** the shadowed canopy is dark
+  and unsaturated, so it satisfies both predicates, and it TOUCHES the head
+  silhouette — so `_largest_component`, which exists to drop a dark background,
+  keeps hair and forest as one blob. **Correct:** re-render with a background
+  the mask cannot claim; do not raise the thresholds, which only trades this
+  failure for the next one. Mask kept at
+  `_verify/20260821_artdirect/rear_mask_render.png`.
+
+- **A SUNLIT HEAD AGAINST SKY.** **Symptom:** exit 0, background cleanly
+  excluded, `edge_roughness` 142.7551 — still 5x the reference — and
+  `taper_ratio` 0.4072. **Why:** the mask is a hollow RING. The sunlit crown is
+  brighter than `luma_max` 70, so only the silhouette rim and shadowed strands

+  value is that it is scale-free. Used here only to isolate the second failure

+  open items at once.

+

+## R-HAIRSHAPE — BREAKING THE BOWL (2026-08-21)
+
+**Status: GATED IN ENGINE.** Narrative in `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE BOWL
+WAS TWO THINGS" and "A BALD RENDER, AND I BLAMED THE THING I HAD JUST
+CHANGED").
+
+### THE TWO MECHANISMS
+
+**1. The ruled line across the forehead is made of ROOTS, not tips.**
+`required_z` was a hard threshold, so root density went from full to zero
+across one vertex. Fixed with a RAISE-ONLY lateral wave on the threshold:
+
+    lobe = 0.6*sin(fx*7.3 + phase) + 0.4*sin(fx*17.1 + phase*2.1)
+    required_z += hairline_wave_cm * 0.5 * (1 + lobe)     # in [0, w]
+
+**RAISE-ONLY IS LOAD-BEARING.** A symmetric wave lowers the line in half its
+columns, and at the TEMPLES — which the position-based face zone does not
+cover, because a temple is not the front of the face — that puts roots below
+the brow.
+
+**2. `lift_cm` means different things in different places.** It sends a strand
+along the scalp NORMAL, which is upward on the crown (height, the body that
+made the volume fix work) and sideways on the temple (flare past the ears, the
+dome outline). Scaled by how upward the root normal is:
+
+    lift_eff = lift_cm * (lift_side_frac + (1 - lift_side_frac) * max(0, n.z))
+
+### THE VALUES
+
+    hairline_wave_cm     3.0     raise-only
+    hairline_soft_cm     1.2     density fade below the line
+    hairline_wisp_scale  0.55    fade roots grow shorter hair
+    lift_side_frac       0.10    sideways roots get 10% of the lift
+    layer_gain           0.30    length on the BACK -- see REJECTED
+    fringe_tilt          0.18
+    len_jitter           0.72 .. 1.28
+
+### ACCEPTANCE
+
+    diagnose_face_hair.py   hairline_profile.spread_cm   0.406 -> 0.965
+    preview_hair.py         scalp_exposed_pct           13.63 -> 12.07
+                            front silhouette            72,443 -> 77,697 px
+                            over-face                    0.76 -> 1.08 %
+    groom_presence.py       Hair PRESENT 18,633 px, 9.1x floor, crown 83%,
+                            drift 2.8%, two passes at 1.7 m
+
+**MEASURE THE HAIRLINE IN GEOMETRY, NOT IN THE RENDER.** Bin front-facing
+roots by x and take the lowest root per bin. The render-side edge statistic
+read 0.69–0.73 cm across a 0 → 0.70 change in `layer_gain`, a 0 → 3.5 change
+in `hairline_soft_cm` AND a 0 → 2.2 change in `hairline_wave_cm` — it cannot
+see any of them.
+
+---
+
+## R-HAIRSHAPE REJECTED
+
+- **`layer_gain` AS THE FIX FOR THE FRINGE EDGE.** **Symptom:** 0 → 0.70 moves
+  the edge spread 0.694 → 0.689 cm while the front silhouette grows 22%.
+  **Why:** it scales length by how far BACK a root is, and forehead roots sit
+  at back_frac ≈ 0. It lengthens the back of the head — a mullet, not a layer.
+  **Correct:** it is kept at 0.30 FOR that effect, and its comment says so.
+
+- **A SYMMETRIC HAIRLINE WAVE.** **Symptom:** over-face 0.74 → 4.94% at
+  ±2.2 cm. **Why:** it lowers the line at the temples, outside the face zone's
+  reach. **Correct:** raise-only, `w * 0.5 * (1 + lobe)`.
+
+- **`hairline_soft_cm` ALONE.** **Symptom:** 0 → 3.5 moves the edge 0.691 →
+  0.711 cm and costs over-face 0.74 → 2.89%. **Why:** a fade gives every
+  column the same statistical treatment, so the boundary moves DOWN and stays
+  level. It is kept small as a wisp generator, not as the edge fix.
+
+- **THE RENDER-SIDE `fringe_edge_spread_cm` AS A GATE.** It is descriptive.
+  Three mechanisms that demonstrably work in geometry moved it by nothing.
+
+- **`flare_p95_ratio` AS EVIDENCE FOR THE LIFT CHANGE.** It moved the WRONG
+  way (0.509 → 0.540 as side lift fell) and sits near 0.5, i.e. it reports the
+  hair as narrower than the head where it was built to look. The lift change
+  rests on the render and the mechanism. The number is left in the report
+  labelled rather than quietly dropped.
+
+### AND WHEN THE RENDER COMES BACK BALD
+
+**RE-RUN THE LAST KNOWN-GOOD CONFIGURATION BEFORE DIAGNOSING THE NEW ONE.**
+On 2026-08-21 v22 rendered bald, survived a fresh binding, and was cleared by
+a new export validator — and then v21, put back on the same component, was
+bald too. The component was carrying a binding that no longer applied.
+
+On a freshly respawned actor the groom assigns and the binding reads back
+NULL; call the assignment again and it sticks. Observed four times today
+across three assets, sometimes succeeding first call. **Behaviour, not
+mechanism.**
+
+`scripts/blender/validate_groom_export.py` checks points-per-curve, root UVs,
+radius and finite positions in ~40 s. Run it BEFORE an import.

+## 2026-08-21 — A BALD RENDER, AND I BLAMED THE THING I HAD JUST CHANGED
+
+**What happened.** v22 (the bowl fix) rendered a full head of hair in Blender
+and a completely bald skull in UE. Beard and eyebrows drew normally, so it was
+the Hair component specifically. The gate confirmed it properly:
+
+    Hair    ABSENT   3,909 px (1.8x floor)     against v21's 18,786 px (9.2x)
+    control Face hidden 404,400 px (190x floor)
+
+The positive control passed, so the instrument could look. The groom genuinely
+was not drawing.
+
+### THE WRONG CONCLUSION, AND HOW FAR I TOOK IT
+
+I re-bound to a fresh binding path and re-rendered: still bald. From that I
+concluded **"it is not the binding, it is the groom content"** and started
+building a validator for the exported curves. That validator was worth having
+and it cleared v22 on every property UE consumes — curve count, points per
+curve, degenerate curves, radius range, root UVs in [0,1] — v21 and v22 are
+structurally equivalent.
+
+**Then the control I should have run first:** put v21's groom and binding back
+on the component and render. **v21 was bald too.** The identical assets that
+had rendered a full head forty minutes earlier, gated at 9.2x floor, now drew
+nothing.
+
+So v22 was innocent the whole time. **I had attributed the failure to the thing
+I had just changed** — which is the single most common error in this whole
+day's log, and I did it again while writing entries about it.
+
+### THE ACTUAL CAUSE
+
+On a freshly respawned actor the groom assigns and **the binding reads back
+null**. Calling the assignment again makes it stick, and then the render is
+correct. The component had been carrying a binding that no longer applied, and
+every render after that point was of an unbound groom — which draws nothing.
+
+**Recorded as behaviour, not mechanism.** I do not know why the first
+assignment is refused. It is now observed on four separate occasions today
+across three different assets, sometimes succeeding on the first call and
+sometimes not, so it is intermittent rather than deterministic and no theory
+here is worth the words.
+
+### WHAT THE PROCEDURE SHOULD HAVE BEEN
+
+**When a render goes wrong, re-run the last KNOWN-GOOD configuration before
+diagnosing the new one.** It is one render. It distinguishes "the change broke
+it" from "the session broke" — and those two have completely disjoint fix
+lists. I spent a validator, two bindings and three renders on the wrong branch
+because I never asked whether the baseline still worked.
+
+This is the positive-control discipline the project already applies to
+instruments, turned on the SUBJECT instead: a null result about a change is
+only evidence if the unchanged case still produces a positive.
+
+### KEPT
+
+`scripts/blender/validate_groom_export.py` came out of the wrong branch and is
+worth keeping anyway: it checks the four properties UE's groom pipeline
+consumes in about forty seconds, against a round trip that costs four minutes
+and an editor. It is now the thing to run BEFORE an import, not the thing to
+reach for after a bald render.

+

+non-negotiable 3: prefer an input that cannot express the bad value over a

+took over.
+
+### THE RESULT, ON TWO INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS
+
+    geometric (strand census)      5.62 %  ->  0.76 %  of strands
+    pixels (render difference)   17,368    ->  1,689   px      -90 %
+    front silhouette             63,026    -> 72,443   px      +15 %
+    height gain                    2.91    ->   3.41   cm
+
+The two instruments share no code path: one ray-casts strand points against the
+head mesh, the other counts rendered pixels inside the bare head's silhouette
+in the eye rows. **The silhouette went UP while the hair came off his face**,
+which is the part that says this is a fix and not a trim.
+
+### THE DIAGNOSTIC WAS WRONG THREE TIMES FIRST, AND THE DISTRIBUTION CAUGHT IT EACH TIME
+
+1. **Ray pointing at the camera instead of away.** Result: 87% of offending
+   strands rooted at the NAPE. Nape hair cannot be over the eyes — the count
+   (25.74%) was plausible and the distribution was impossible.
+2. **Sign corrected, still 100% nape.** Because a point BURIED IN THE SKULL
+   also has head geometry between it and the far side, so the ray test scored
+   it as drawn over the face. 62.3% of flagged points were at the back of the
+   head. Fixed by requiring the point to be OUTSIDE the head first.
+3. **Root statistics derived from the nearest vertex NORMAL** still said
+   "back-facing" for brow roots — the same corrupted normals that caused the
+   defect were corrupting its diagnosis. Fixed by reporting the root's own
+   POSITION.
+
+**A positive and negative control now gates the whole run**: a point 3 cm in
+front of the face must score and one 3 cm behind the skull must not, or the
+diagnostic refuses instead of reporting. That control passed while version 2
+was still wrong, which is worth stating plainly — **a control proves the test
+discriminates at the extremes; it does not prove the test is right in the
+middle.** What caught version 2 was the distribution being anatomically absurd,
+not the control.
+
+### THE GENERAL RULE
+
+**Before fixing a defect, identify the population that produces it.** Three
+fixes were aimed at strands that were never involved, and each looked
+reasonable, and each was confirmed by a number that could not have moved. The
+diagnostic cost one script and forty seconds a run; the three blind fixes cost
+a day and a UE round trip each.
+
+And the corollary for the metric: **`hair_over_face_px` was reading 17,400 and
+was correct all along.** The thing that was missing was not a better number for
+HOW MUCH, it was any number at all for WHICH.

+## R-HAIRFACE — KEEPING AN AUTHORED GROOM OFF THE FACE (2026-08-21)
+
+**Status: MEASURED ON TWO INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS.** Narrative in `LESSONS.md`
+2026-08-21 ("THE HAIR OVER THE EYES WAS HAIR GROWING ON HIS BROW").
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**No root is placed in the front of the face below the brow, and the test is on
+POSITION, not on a normal.** In `scripts/blender/author_hero_hair.py`:
+
+    brow_z  = z_lo + face_zone_z_frac * height        # 0.80 = top of eye band
+    y_frac  = (p.y - y_face_end) / (y_back_end - y_face_end)
+    if y_frac <= face_zone_y_frac and p.z < brow_z:   # 0.28
+        reject
+
+`y_face_end` / `y_back_end` are measured over the SKULL only (`z >= nape_z`) so
+the bust's shoulders do not stretch the range.
+
+### THE VALUES
+
+    face_zone_z_frac   0.80    the brow. ANATOMY, decoupled from the haircut
+    face_zone_y_frac   0.28    front-of-head depth that counts as face
+    face_reject_dot    0.95    nearly inert; see REJECTED
+    hairline_frac      0.82
+    lift_cm            3.50
+    len_top_cm         12.0
+
+### THE ACCEPTANCE NUMBERS — two instruments, no shared code path
+
+    scripts/blender/diagnose_face_hair.py     over_face_pct   5.62 -> 0.76 %
+    scripts/blender/preview_hair.py           hair_over_face  17,368 -> 1,689 px
+                                              front silhouette 63,026 -> 72,443
+                                              height gain      2.91 -> 3.41 cm
+
+**The silhouette went UP while the hair came off his face.** That is the check
+that separates a fix from a trim, and it is the one to repeat on any change
+here.
+
+**`diagnose_face_hair.py` REFUSES rather than reports** if its own control
+fails: a point 3 cm in front of the face must score and one 3 cm behind the
+skull must not.
+
+---
+
+## R-HAIRFACE REJECTED
+
+- **REJECTING FACE ROOTS BY SURFACE NORMAL ALONE** (`face_reject_dot`, and the
+  normal-driven `required_z` sweep). **Symptom:** a dark mass over both eye
+  sockets that survives every styling change aimed at it. **Why:** a MetaHuman
+  face carries eyelids, sockets and lash geometry at the brow whose normals do
+  not point forward, so a brow vertex passes the face rejection, gets a low
+  front-ness, has its required height dropped toward the nape, and becomes a
+  legal root. **Correct:** a position-based face zone, which no normal can
+  defeat.
+
+- **`face_reject_dot` 0.45.** **Symptom:** a high, receding, balding hairline
+  in every render of this groom. **Measured** with the position rule in place:
+
+        0.45 -> 0.99   over-face 0.82 -> 0.77 %   front silhouette +45%
+
+  It was removing the entire FOREHEAD, 22,600 silhouette pixels, and buying
+  nothing. **Correct:** 0.95, kept only as a cheap pre-filter.
+
+- **TYING THE FACE ZONE TO `hairline_frac`.** **Why:** lowering the hairline to
+  bring hair forward would shrink the protection over the eyes — the two are
+  not the same fact. **Correct:** `face_zone_z_frac`, the top of the measured
+  eye band, which is a property of the head.
+
+- **FIXING IT WITH `front_sweep_gain` OR `len_side_cm`.** **Symptom:** the
+  over-face figure reads 17,463 -> 17,362 across a doubling of the sweep, and
+  17,378 -> 17,378 across a 23% cut to side length. **Why:** the offending
+  strands are rooted BELOW the hairline on the brow, so neither lever reaches
+  them. **An input that moves nothing is not the input the defect is made of.**
+
+### THE DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN REJECTED VALUES — it was wrong three times
+
+- **Ray cast TOWARD the camera** to test "is this drawn over him". Symptom: 87%
+  of offenders rooted at the nape, which is impossible. The ray must go AWAY
+  from the camera.
+- **Ray test without an outside-the-head test first.** Symptom: still 100%
+  nape; 62.3% of flagged points sat at the BACK of the head. A point buried in
+  the skull also has geometry between it and the far side. Require
+  `(p - nearest).dot(normal) > 0` first.
+- **Classifying roots by the nearest vertex NORMAL.** Symptom: brow roots
+  reported as "back-facing", i.e. the corrupted normals that caused the defect
+  also corrupted its diagnosis. Report the root's own POSITION.
+
+**And note what the control did NOT catch.** The front/back control passed
+while version 2 was still wrong. A control proves the test discriminates at the
+extremes; it does not prove it is right in the middle. What caught version 2
+was the distribution being anatomically absurd.

+is no RBF bake — Build() owns the deformation"* — describing behaviour the code
+had not had for some time. **A stale claim in a comment propagated into a second
+file as though it were a specification.** Non-negotiable 25, and non-negotiable 9:
+the payload's author (me) copied a claim out of our own code without opening the
+lines below it.
+
+### THE MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIED THE BAKE DOES NOT COVER THIS INPUT
+
+The bake block cites three bindings — identity source, real source async, real
+source synchronous — producing the same picture, and concludes the binding alone
+does not move strands. That is evidence about a groom authored **somewhere
+else**. It says the bake is what moves a TRANSFERRED groom; it does not say a
+groom already in the right place needs moving. **A measurement's scope is part
+of the measurement**, and this one was carried into a case it never covered.
+
+### AND THE CALL SITE HAD DRIFTED FROM ITS UFUNCTION
+
+Before the crash, the same payload failed with
+`TypeError: build_fresh_groom_binding() required argument 'dest_groom_path'
+(pos 5) not found`. The C++ had gained `DestGroomPath` and `OutGroomPath`
+(`LandscapeLabTools.h:639-650`); the committed payload still passed four
+arguments and unpacked three outs. It also ignored the returned groom copy and
+assigned the original — which is R-GROOMBIND3's own headline defect, in the tool
+written to apply R-GROOMBIND3's successor.
+
+**A payload is a call site with no compiler.** Nothing checks it against the
+UFUNCTION it names until it runs, and it had not run since the signature moved.
+Each discovery cost a full remote-execution window.
+
+### WHAT SURVIVED
+
+`Hair_v19.uasset`, 7.3 MB, was already on disk — the import saves before the
+bind, so the crash cost the binding and not the groom. Crash log and the
+editor log at the moment of the fatal are preserved at
+`_verify/20260821_blender/rbf_crash/`. `PackageRestoreData.json` was moved to
+`_trash/autosaves_rbfcrash_20260821/` before relaunching, so the next start
+cannot raise a Restore modal — which would block the game thread, and with it
+the only channel that could report anything.
+
+
+## 2026-08-21 — TEN FRAMES WERE WRITTEN INTO THE ENGINE INSTALL, AND I PUT THEM THERE
+
+**What happened.** After relaunching the editor with `Start-Process` and no
+`-WorkingDirectory`, every capture tool reported writing a frame and no frame
+appeared. They were in
+
+    C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Binaries\Win64\_verify\...
+
+— ten files, including a complete nine-frame presence-gate set. **Outside both
+roots, in the engine install. Standing rule 1, and it was mine.**
+
+**Mechanism.** Every capture tool builds a RELATIVE output path
+(`_verify/<date>/<name>.png`) and the editor resolves it against its own
+working directory. `Start-Process` defaults that to the caller's directory,
+which for a PowerShell tool call is not guaranteed to be anything in
+particular; here it resolved to the engine's binaries folder. The write
+SUCCEEDED. Nothing was overwritten and nothing was corrupted, but the engine
+install now had a `_verify` tree in it, twice, ten minutes apart — because
+after recovering the first set I re-rendered without fixing the cause.
+
+**THE GATES CAUGHT IT AND COULD NOT NAME IT.** `world_shot.py` refused with
+*"the payload reported a frame that is not on disk"* and `groom_presence.py`
+with *"frames never landed on disk"*. Both are correct, both are fail-closed,
+and neither could say WHERE the frame went — from the editor's point of view
+there was nothing wrong to report. **A refusal that says "not here" is not the
+same as one that says "over there", and only the first was available.** What
+found the files was a filesystem search of the engine directory, i.e. asking a
+different representation.
+
+**MY FIRST FIX WAS WRONG, AND RE-TESTING IT IS WHAT SAID SO.** I wrote
+`scripts/launch_editor.ps1` to pass `-WorkingDirectory`, restarted the editor
+with it, and the very next render landed in the engine folder again. **Unreal
+sets its own working directory to the binaries dir at startup**, so the launch
+argument is inert for this purpose — the process command line confirms the flag
+was passed and the behaviour did not change.
+
+**The real fix is an ABSOLUTE `--out-dir`.** Verified: the same command with
+`C:/Users/Admin/UE5LandscapePipeline/_verify/...` wrote into the repo.
+
+The launch script is kept because its OTHER job is real — moving
+`PackageRestoreData.json` aside so the next start cannot raise a Restore modal
+— but its docstring now says plainly that the working directory it sets does
+not survive engine startup, so nobody re-derives the wrong cause from a script
+that looks like it handles it.
+
+**A fix that is not re-tested is a hypothesis with a commit message.** This one
+had a plausible mechanism, matched the symptom exactly, and was wrong. The only
+thing that caught it was rendering again and looking at where the file went.
+
+**Recovery.** All ten frames were copied back into `_verify/20260821_blender/`
+and the stray trees moved to `_trash/stray_engine_writes_20260821/`. The engine
+install has no `_verify` directory now, checked.
+
+**AND I FORCE-KILLED THE EDITOR WITHOUT READING THE DIRTY LIST FIRST.** The
+project's own procedure is to read `get_dirty_content_packages()` and treat an
+UNREADABLE count as a refusal, and I skipped it. It was harmless here — a
+force-kill writes nothing, the groom and binding had already been saved by
+`SavePackage` inside the UFUNCTION, and the only unsaved state was the hero
+placement, which is re-derivable in one run of `place_hero_in_world.py`. But
+"it turned out to be harmless" is not the same as "it was checked", and the
+step exists precisely because the harmless case and the expensive one look
+identical beforehand.

+## R-GROOMBIND4 — A FRESH BINDING FOR A GROOM AUTHORED ON ITS OWN TARGET (2026-08-21)
+
+**Status: MECHANISM CORRECTED AFTER AN EDITOR FATAL.** Narrative in
+`LESSONS.md` 2026-08-21 ("THE RBF BAKE KILLED THE EDITOR").
+
+For a groom authored in Blender directly on the character's own exported face
+mesh — not a vendor groom being retargeted — the binding is built fresh rather
+than duplicated from a vendor one:
+
+    unreal.LandscapeLabTools.build_fresh_groom_binding(
+        groom, source_mesh_or_None, target_mesh,
+        dest_package_path, dest_groom_path)
+      -> (out_binding_path, out_groom_path, b_success, out_error)
+
+**FIVE ARGUMENTS IN, FOUR OUT.** `LandscapeLabTools.h:639-650`.
+
+**PASS `source_mesh = None` WHEN THE GROOM WAS AUTHORED ON THE TARGET.** Source
+then defaults to target and the binding is an identity. This is a claim about
+the groom, so it is passed explicitly and recorded in the output rather than
+defaulted silently.
+
+**ASSIGN THE RETURNED GROOM COPY, NOT THE ORIGINAL** — `out_groom_path`, not
+the asset you passed in. R-GROOMBIND3's headline, and it applies here too.
+
+**THE RBF BAKE RUNS ONLY WHEN SOURCE != TARGET**, and the module logs which
+branch it took:
+
+    LogLandscapeLab: BuildFreshGroomBinding: RBF bake SKIPPED (source IS the target).
+

+
+## R-GROOMBIND4 REJECTED
+
+- **CALLING `FGroomRBFDeformer::GetRBFDeformedGroomAsset` ON AN IDENTITY
+  BINDING.** **Symptom:** the editor dies with
+  `Assertion failed: RootDatas[GroupIndex].MeshPositions.IsValidIndex(MeshLODIndex)`
+  at `GroomRBFDeformer.cpp:740`, on a 50,400-curve groom, after ~4 minutes of
+  apparently healthy work at ~5 CPU-s per wall-s with no log growth.
+  **Why:** the deformer computes `RootDatas` itself (`:670-683`) and `check()`s
+  that mesh LOD 0 is present; an engine `check()` is a hard crash, not a
+  refusal. **And the step is a no-op for this input** — an RBF deformation
+  transfers strands from the authoring mesh to the target mesh, and here they
+  are the same mesh. **Correct:** guard on `EffectiveSource != TargetMesh`.
+
+- **CARRYING THE THREE-BINDING MEASUREMENT INTO THIS CASE.** Wrong reasoning:
+  "three bindings produced the same picture, therefore the binding alone does
+  not move strands, therefore always bake." **Why it does not apply:** that was
+  measured on a groom authored on a DIFFERENT mesh. It shows the bake moves a
+  TRANSFERRED groom; it says nothing about a groom already in the right place.
+  A measurement's scope is part of the measurement.
+
+- **`fresh_bind_payload.txt` PASSING FOUR ARGUMENTS AND UNPACKING THREE OUTS.**
+  **Symptom:** `TypeError: build_fresh_groom_binding() required argument
+  'dest_groom_path' (pos 5) not found`, one full remote window per attempt.
+  **Why:** the UFUNCTION gained two parameters and the payload was never
+  updated; nothing checks a payload against its UFUNCTION until it runs.
+  **Correct:** five in, four out, and re-run the payload after ANY change to a
+  signature it calls.
+
+- **TRUSTING A COMMENT IN OUR OWN CODE.** The function opened with *"NO RBF
+  BAKE HERE, DELIBERATELY"* forty lines above a block that bakes and whose own
+  heading says it overturns that plan. The payload header repeated the false
+  half into a second file. **Correct:** the stale comment is struck in place
+  with the date, and the live rule sits at the code it governs.
+
+### THE PROCEDURE AROUND A GROOM FATAL
+
+1. The imported `GroomAsset` is saved before the bind, so a bind crash costs
+   the binding and not the groom — check the `.uasset` before re-importing.
+2. Copy the crash folder and `LandscapeLab.log` into `_verify/` **before**
+   relaunching; the log is overwritten on start.
+3. Move `Saved/Autosaves/PackageRestoreData.json` to `_trash/` before
+   relaunching, or the next start raises a Restore modal that blocks the game
+   thread and therefore blocks remote execution.
+4. Rebuild the plugin while the editor is down — a module rebuild is ~18 s and
+   cannot be done with it running.
