+## R-NAVBUILD REJECTED
+
+**Building without saving the world after the nav actors change.** SYMPTOM:
+the commandlet logs `NavData RegistrationFailed_AgentNotValid ... will be
+removed. This warning will disapear once the map is saved` — 166 times — and
+produces packages containing nothing usable, while the EDITOR reads the
+correct values the whole time. CAUSE: `SetConfig` corrects the navmesh actor
+in MEMORY at load and does NOT dirty its package, so `save_dirty_packages`
+writes nothing; the headless commandlet loads from disk. CORRECT: force-save
+the nav actors with `only_dirty=False`. Same defect as unit 6's foliage
+collision, six hours later, in a different subsystem. **An engine message
+saying "this will disappear once the map is saved" means the disk and the
+session disagree RIGHT NOW.**
+
+**Reading the commandlet's EXIT CODE as the success test.** SYMPTOM: exit 1
+on both the broken run and the healthy one. CAUSE: the single "error" is
+`LogHttpListener: Error: HttpListener unable to bind to 127.0.0.1:8000` —
+the IncrediBuild port conflict, unrelated to navigation — and `Failure -
+1 error(s)` is computed from it. Warnings fell 166 → 2 between the runs while
+the exit code did not move. CORRECT: judge on the log's warning summary and
+on a projection query. `build_navmesh_chunk.py` prints the exit code and
+refuses to conclude cost from it.
+
+**Setting `AgentRadius` / `AgentHeight` on ARecastNavMesh.** SYMPTOM: the CDO
+reads the declared values and the ACTOR reads 35/144, with every other
+property on the actor correct. CAUSE: `NavigationSystem.cpp:2874-2875` and
+`:4729` call `NavData->SetConfig(SupportedAgents[...])`, which overwrites the
+navmesh's agent dimensions. With `SupportedAgents` empty — verified, no entry
+anywhere in engine or project config — `FNavDataConfig`'s fallbacks stand.
+CORRECT: `+SupportedAgents=(Name="Default",AgentRadius=...,AgentHeight=...,
+AgentStepHeight=...)` under `[/Script/NavigationSystem.NavigationSystemV1]`.
+`AgentMaxSlope` is NOT part of `FNavDataConfig` and correctly stays on the
+navmesh.
+
+**Setting `TileSizeUU` or `AgentMaxSlope` on the navmesh ACTOR instead of in
+config.** SYMPTOM: the value reverts with only a log warning. CAUSE:
+`ARecastNavMesh::PostLoad` (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:963-1015`) forces both back to
+the class default when the voxel cache is on. CORRECT: config, which moves
+the CDO too, so the comparison it makes is your value against your value.
+
+**Declaring a `tile_size_uu` above `CellSize * 1024`.** SYMPTOM: the build
+uses a different tile size than the recipe says. CAUSE:
+`GetClampedTileSizeUU` (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:75-81`) clamps silently. CORRECT:
+the schema refuses anything outside [300, 19456] at the shipped `CellSize=19`.
+
+**Relying on `bWholeWorldNavigable` instead of bounds volumes.** SYMPTOM: no
+navmesh anywhere and a build that succeeds. CAUSE: its `UPROPERTY` is
+commented out at `NavigationSystem.h:370` with the engine's own "currently
+broken". CORRECT: `ANavMeshBoundsVolume` actors, declared in the recipe, which
+also makes the tile budget computable without an editor.
+
+**Leaving `TileSizeUU` and `AverageLayersPerTile` at the engine defaults for
+a world-sized navigable region.** SYMPTOM: none at build time — the engine
+logs an error and CLAMPS, leaving a navmesh quietly smaller than the region.
+CAUSE: 8128 m at 1000 uu tiles and 3 layers needs ~1.99M tiles against
+`TileNumberHardLimit` 1,048,576 (`RecastNavMesh.cpp:551`). CORRECT: 1600 uu
+and 1.5 layers gives 388,622. A `prove_gates` probe holds this.
+
+**Running the builder with an editor open.** SYMPTOM: `unable to unlink old
+... Invalid argument`, the class this project already paid for during the
+density revert. CORRECT: `build_navmesh_chunk.py` refuses to start while
+`UnrealEditor.exe` is running, and treats an unreadable process list as a
+refusal rather than as "no editor".
+
+**Extrapolating a whole-world build cost from this one.** SYMPTOM: a
+confident 21-minute figure. CAUSE: the builder iterated 81 loading cells to
+produce navmesh in ONE, so most of the 20 s was iteration with nothing to do.
+CORRECT: a whole-world volume and its own measured run. This is the
+misleading-denominator class.

+**THE BOARD SAID ONE MESH WAS BROKEN. FOURTEEN WERE.** R-COLLIDE names
+`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A`'s zero collision primitives as *the* blocker on
+unit 6. True, real, and **not the blocker**: measured before anything changed,
+**all fourteen `FT_*` foliage types read `NoCollision`**, so 219,659 trees and
+13,515 rock instances were pass-through — including the three species whose
+MESHES carry perfectly good vendor capsules. Authoring the missing capsule
+alone would have changed nothing and the session would have reported a fix.
+
+Root cause: `UFoliageType`'s constructor sets `NoCollision`
+(`InstancedFoliage.cpp:640`), `UpdateComponentSettings` copies it onto the
+component unconditionally (`:1822`), and **`place_foliage` contains no
+occurrence of the string "collision" in any form.** Nothing was set wrongly;
+nothing was set at all. **A default you never named is a decision you never
+made.**
+
+## FOUR TRAPS PAID FOR, EACH ONE LOCKED IN R-TREECOLLIDE REJECTED
+
+1. **`BlockAll` + `QUERY_ONLY` CANNOT BOTH HOLD.** `BlockAll` declares
+   `QueryAndPhysics` (`BaseEngine.ini:3104`) and `PostLoad -> FixupData ->
+   LoadProfileData` re-reads the profile **on every load**, so it reads back
+   right in the session that wrote it and flips on the next start. Fixed with a
+   project profile `FoliageBlockQueryOnly` whose own `CollisionEnabled` IS
+   `QueryOnly`. **Do not "fix" this by using `Custom`** — that inherits
+   `NoCollision`'s responses, which IGNORE Visibility and Camera, and a walk
+   test would pass over invisible trees.
+2. **`custom_navigable_geometry = "no"` does NOT keep trees out of the
+   navmesh.** `No` still runs the DEFAULT collision export; `dont_export`
+   excludes. `Yes` is the engine default and is the path that exports
+   per-instance transforms. `PHASE2_PLAN` unit 6 prescribes `No` and is
+   **backwards** — NOT applied, flagged for unit 8.
+3. **On a Nanite mesh, `RENDER_DATA` and `get_section_from_static_mesh` return
+   the FALLBACK proxy** — 6.6% too tall, 36% too wide, 1–8 vertices per low-Z
+   band. `SOURCE_MODEL` gives 76,343 vertices and a clean trunk.
+   `build_scale` is `[1,1,1]`, so they are different MESHES, not different
+   units.
+4. **THE SAVE IS PART OF THE PROCEDURE.** The load-time fixup that corrects the
+   components does **not dirty their packages** — 0 dirty against 1,093
+   corrected actors — so the editor was provably right while PIE, which
+   streams from disk, got `NoCollision`. `save_foliage_actors.py` saves with
+   `only_dirty=False`; 1,073 of 1,093 packages changed on disk, verified by
+   `git status`, not by the tool.
+
+**This is Pass 1's shape again:** the artefact on disk disagreed with the live
+editor, every asset-level check was green, and only a different representation
+— the PIE world — could see it.
+

+# 2026-08-16 (night) — UNIT 6: NOTHING IN THIS WORLD COLLIDED BUT THE LANDSCAPE
+
+**Session goal:** `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 — "trees stop him". It passes; the
+route there found four defects the board did not know about, and one of them
+is the same shape as the Pass 1 failure that started this project's whole
+verification doctrine.
+
+## THE BOARD SAID ONE MESH WAS BROKEN. FOURTEEN WERE.
+
+`R-COLLIDE` and the campaign table both record unit 3's finding:
+`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` — 63,981 instances, the largest species — has
+**zero simple collision primitives**, and R-COLLIDE names it as *the* blocker
+on unit 6. That finding is TRUE, it is a real defect, and it is **not the
+blocker.**
+
+Measured before anything was changed: **all fourteen `FT_*` foliage types read
+`NoCollision`.** 219,659 trees and 13,515 rock instances were pass-through, and
+so were the three tree species whose MESHES carry a perfectly good
+vendor-authored trunk capsule (ConiferPine 2 sphyl, SpruceSub 1, SpruceSapling
+1). **Authoring the missing capsule alone would have changed nothing
+observable, and the session would have ended reporting a fix.**
+
+Root cause at two source lines:
+
+    InstancedFoliage.cpp:640   UFoliageType's constructor:
+                               BodyInstance.SetCollisionProfileName(NoCollision)
+    InstancedFoliage.cpp:1822  UpdateComponentSettings copies the foliage
+                               type's BodyInstance onto the component
+                               UNCONDITIONALLY — no "if changed" guard —
+                               overriding the MESH's own BodySetup
+
+and `place_foliage` contains **no occurrence of the string "collision" in any
+form**. Nothing was set wrongly. Nothing was set at all.
+
+**THE GENERAL RULE: A DEFAULT YOU NEVER NAMED IS A DECISION YOU NEVER MADE.**
+Every other silent-default defect here had a value somebody typed — `t.MaxFPS`,
+`CullDistance` 0, `sections_per_component`. This one had no value anywhere, so
+no grep for a wrong number could find it and no review of the recipe would
+notice an absence. The fix is therefore structural: `collision` is now a
+REQUIRED key on every instanced species (schema v1.23), refused on grass, with
+16 `prove_gates` probes holding the refusal. **An optional field with a
+sensible default reproduces exactly the failure being fixed.**
+
+The gate was positive-controlled before it was satisfied: on the unmodified
+recipes it refused exactly 14 species — 4 in `alpine_8k`, 10 in `alpine` —
+matching the 14 `FT_*` assets one for one, with zero errors on the two grass
+species.
+
+## TWO OBJECTS, AND ONLY ONE IS ON THE PATH
+
+`Free/_measured/mesh_collision.json` reports `collision_profile` = `BlockAll`
+for all six meshes. That artefact is correct and its number is useless for this
+question: it reads the MESH's `BodySetup.default_instance`, while the runtime
+component is overwritten from the FOLIAGE TYPE at `:1822`.
+
+Non-negotiable 0 warns against two instruments that share a source. **This is
+the mirror case: two instruments that describe DIFFERENT OBJECTS, one quoted as
+an answer about the other.** `measure_foliage_collision` now prints both in one
+table so the substitution cannot be made silently again.
+
+## THE PLAN'S OWN PRESCRIPTION WAS SELF-CONTRADICTORY
+
+`PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 asks for `collision_enabled = QUERY_ONLY` together with
+`collision_profile_name = BlockAll`. Those cannot both hold:
+
+    BaseEngine.ini:3104            BlockAll declares CollisionEnabled=QueryAndPhysics
+    InstancedFoliage.cpp:806-812   UFoliageType::PostLoad -> BodyInstance.FixupData
+    BodyInstance.cpp:4567          FixupData -> LoadProfileData, on EVERY load
+    BodyInstance.cpp:4509          LoadProfileData -> UCollisionProfile::ReadConfig,
+                                   which writes the PROFILE's CollisionEnabled,
+                                   ObjectType and responses INTO the body instance
+
+A foliage type saved as `BlockAll` + `QueryOnly` reads back correct **in the one
+session where it cannot fail** and silently becomes `QueryAndPhysics` on the next
+start. Fixed by making the contradiction unrepresentable: a project profile
+`FoliageBlockQueryOnly` whose own `CollisionEnabled` **is** `QueryOnly`.
+
+**AND THE OBVIOUS SHORTCUT WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE.** Leaving the profile as
+`Custom` stops `ReadConfig` running — and inherits the response container
+`NoCollision` left at construction, which `BaseEngine.ini:3103` shows sets
+**`Visibility=Ignore` and `Camera=Ignore`**. Trees would have blocked movement
+while being invisible to visibility traces: line of sight, AI perception,
+weapon traces. **A walk test would have passed it.**
+
+## `CustomNavigableGeometry = No` DOES NOT MEAN "KEEP IT OUT OF THE NAVMESH"
+
+Per `NavRelevantInterface.h`, `No` means the custom callback is not called *but
+the default collision export still runs*; `DontExport` is the value that
+excludes. For an ISM the custom callback is `DoCustomNavigableGeometryExport`
+(`InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:5435-5438`), which exports **per-instance
+transforms** — the path that makes 63,981 instances navmesh obstacles at all.
+`Yes` is the engine default (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:868`) and is correct. The
+plan's `No` reads like a safety measure and would have removed the per-instance
+export. **NOT APPLIED**; left at `Yes`, now declared rather than inherited, and
+flagged for unit 8, which is the first thing that can test it against a built
+navmesh.
+
+## SIZING THE CAPSULE: THE OBVIOUS INSTRUMENT READ THE WRONG MESH
+
+`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` is Nanite, and both
+`ProceduralMeshLibrary.get_section_from_static_mesh` and GeometryScript's
+`RENDER_DATA` LOD return the **Nanite fallback proxy**:
+
+    SOURCE_MODEL    76,343 verts   z -0.58 .. 2731.07    x -375 .. 302
+    RENDER_DATA      7,005 verts   z -10.50 .. 2901.53   x -511 .. 459
+
+The fallback overstates the mesh by **6.6% in Z and ~36% in X**, and its low-Z
+bands hold **1 to 8 vertices each**, giving radii scattered 7–63 cm with no
+cylinder in them. That is "I could not look", not a radius, and it was one
+sentence from being written down as one. `build_scale` is `[1,1,1]`, so these
+are **different meshes, not one mesh in two unit systems** — checked, because a
+6.6% gap invites exactly that assumption.
+
+From `SOURCE_MODEL`: max **37.13 cm** in the 0–20 cm root flare, 28.6–34.6 cm
+from 0.2 m to 3.2 m, r_p50 21–24 cm throughout. Declared **38.0 cm**. Physical
+check: DBH 46–74 cm on a 29 m Norway spruce, which is right.
+
+**AND A TIGHT REFERENCE CLASS WOULD HAVE BEEN 2x WRONG.** The three sibling
+spruces' vendor capsules fit `r/h ~ 0.030` across 4.5 m, 16.7 m and 22.1 m —
+three points, `r ∝ h^0.85`, a good fit. Extrapolated to 29.12 m: **78 cm**.
+This mesh measures `r/h = 0.0120`. The vendor capsules are GAMEPLAY-FATTENED
+VOLUMES, not trunks. **A tight fit across three samples says the samples agree
+with each other, not that they measure the thing you want.**
+
+## `FHitResult` IS OPAQUE IN 5.8 PYTHON, AND THE TEST GOT BETTER FOR IT
+
+Enumerated after `component` raised: `component`, `distance`, `location`,
+`time`, `normal`, `item` are *"protected and cannot be read"*; `hit_component`,
+`hit_actor`, `impact_point`, `face_index`, `blocking_hit` are *"failed to find
+property"*. **A trace tells Python hit-or-miss and nothing else.**
+
+That forced a better instrument. A horizontal trace on alpine ground hits the
+landscape readily (a 16 degree slope rises 86 cm over the 3 m approach), so
+"something was hit" was never evidence. Every trunk trace now runs **twice —
+the second time with every `InstancedFoliageActor` in `actors_to_ignore`** —
+and counts only when the first HITS and the second MISSES. Terrain is hit by
+both and counts as nothing. The capsule radius is measured by stepping the line
+sideways until foliage stops being hit, which needs no distance field.
+
+**That geometric method then recovered capsules it was never told about:**
+implied unscaled radii of 55–63 / 45–57 / ~12–24 cm against the vendors'
+62.79 / 52.81 / 16.30 cm. A measurement that independently reproduces three
+numbers from a different source is worth more than the one it was built for.
+
+## THE LAST DEFECT WAS A SAVE NOBODY ASKED FOR — AND IT IS PASS 1'S SHAPE AGAIN
+
+With the foliage types cold-verified `QUERY_ONLY` / `FoliageBlockQueryOnly` and
+the editor world proven to stop a trace on a trunk, **PIE still found zero
+foliage hits across all four species over 4,659 loaded instances.** Measuring
+the two worlds side by side:
+
+    editor world components   QUERY_ONLY    FoliageBlockQueryOnly   BLOCK
+    PIE world components      NO_COLLISION  NoCollision             IGNORE
+
+`UpdateComponentSettings` runs at LOAD, so after the restart memory was
+correct — **and a load-time fixup does not dirty the package it corrected.**
+`get_dirty_content_packages()` returned **0** while 1,093
+`InstancedFoliageActor`s held corrected components. The external actor packages
+on disk still carried the OLD serialized `BodyInstance`, World Partition
+streams PIE from those packages, and the game got `NoCollision`.
+
+**A normal save would have written nothing and reported success.** The fix is
+`save_foliage_actors.py`, saving with `only_dirty=False` — which is the entire
+reason it exists rather than calling `save_dirty_packages`. 1,093 submitted,
+**1,073 modified on disk**, confirmed by `git status` rather than by the tool.
+
+This is Pass 1 wearing new clothes: **the artefact on disk disagreed with the
+live editor, every asset-level check was green, and only a different
+representation — the PIE world — could see it.** The difference is that this
+time the question was asked in the same session rather than three days later.
+
+## THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONE NUMBER THAT IS NOT PINNED
+
+    Conifer         5/6 trunk hits    6/6 negative controls missed
+    ConiferPine     6/6               6/6
+    SpruceSub       5/6               6/6
+    SpruceSapling   5/6               6/6
+
+The one non-hit per species is a line with terrain on it, counted as neither
+answer. Our own Conifer capsule brackets 0.1–1.4 cm **below** `38.0 x scale` on
+3 of 4 samples — consistent with `align_to_normal: 0.15` tilting the capsule
+axis (up to ~6 cm of lateral shift at the 1 m trace height on a 24 degree
+slope) plus 2–5 cm offset granularity. **Consistent, not independently pinned,
+and it should not be quoted as a verified radius.**
+
+## A LESSON THAT EXISTED AND DID NOT FIRE
+
+`ue_exec.py --timeout N` is a fixed DISCOVERY WINDOW, always spent in full.
+That was written into this file **earlier the same day**, with the words "Use
+12–15", and this session passed 120–180 anyway and paid minutes per call. The
+narrative could not stop the hand that types the flag. Fixed where it fires:
+the argument's help text now says so, and any value above 60 prints a note at
+the point of use. **A lesson whose only home is a story is a lesson that
+depends on somebody having read the story recently.**

+## R-TREECOLLIDE — MAKING SCATTERED INSTANCES COLLIDE (2026-08-16)
+
+**Status: PROVEN.** `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6. Declaration: `collision` on every
+instanced species, schema **v1.23**. Tools
+`scripts/apply_foliage_collision.py` (write),
+`scripts/measure_foliage_collision.py` (read),
+`scripts/verify_tree_collision.py` (prove),
+`scripts/save_foliage_actors.py` (persist). Artefacts
+`Free/_measured/foliage_collision.json`,
+`_verify/20260816_pie_unit1_unit6_collision_on.md`. Narrative: LESSONS
+2026-08-16 (night).
+
+**SUPERSEDES R-COLLIDE's framing.** R-COLLIDE is correct about the MESH and
+its measurement stands. Its REJECTED entry names
+`SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A`'s zero primitives as the blocker on unit 6; it is
+**one of two defects and not the decisive one.** All fourteen `FT_*` foliage
+types read `NoCollision`, so the three species with vendor-authored capsules
+did not collide either.
+
+### THE FOUR STEPS, IN THIS ORDER. THE LAST ONE IS THE ONE THAT GETS SKIPPED.
+
+    1. author a capsule ONLY where the mesh is repo-TRACKED
+    2. set the FOLIAGE TYPE's body_instance + custom_navigable_geometry
+    3. RESTART the editor  (the collision profile is read at engine init,
+       and FixupData -> LoadProfileData runs only on load)
+    4. SAVE THE FOLIAGE ACTORS WITH only_dirty=False
+
+**Step 4 is not bookkeeping.** `FFoliageStaticMesh::UpdateComponentSettings`
+copies the foliage type onto the component (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:1822`) and
+runs at LOAD, so after step 3 the editor's components are correct — and a
+load-time fixup does **not** dirty the package it corrected. Measured:
+`get_dirty_content_packages()` returns **0** with 1,093
+`InstancedFoliageActor`s holding corrected components. The external actor
+packages on disk still carry the OLD serialized `BodyInstance`, World
+Partition streams PIE from those packages, and **the game gets
+`NoCollision` while the editor is provably correct.**
+
+### THE VALUES THAT WORK
+
+    collision.enabled              "query_only"
+    collision.profile              "FoliageBlockQueryOnly"
+    collision.navigable_geometry   "yes"
+    capsule (Conifer only)         radius_cm 38.0, z 0.0 .. 2731.0
+
+`FoliageBlockQueryOnly` is declared in `LandscapeLab/Config/DefaultEngine.ini`
+under `[/Script/Engine.CollisionProfile]` with `CollisionEnabled=QueryOnly`,
+`ObjectTypeName="WorldStatic"`, `CustomResponses=` (empty = Block every
+channel), `bCanModify=False`.
+
+### THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, AND WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY
+
+    python scripts/verify_tree_collision.py --recipe recipes/alpine_8k.json \
+        --per-species 6 --settle 60 --timeout 25
+
+**Every `FHitResult` field is protected or absent in the 5.8 Python surface**
+— `component`, `distance`, `location`, `time`, `normal`, `item` all report
+"protected and cannot be read". A trace yields hit-or-miss and nothing else.
+So the test is a DIFFERENTIAL: each trunk trace runs twice, the second time
+with every `InstancedFoliageActor` in `actors_to_ignore`, and counts only when
+the first HITS and the second MISSES. Terrain is hit by both and counts as
+nothing — which matters, because a horizontal trace on alpine ground hits the
+landscape readily (a 16 degree slope rises 86 cm over the 3 m approach).
+
+Traces run on **VISIBILITY**, deliberately: the `NoCollision` profile sets
+`Visibility=Ignore` (`BaseEngine.ini:3103`), so a Visibility hit proves the
+profile's RESPONSES were loaded and not merely that a flag was set.
+
+Result: Conifer 5/6, ConiferPine 6/6, SpruceSub 5/6, SpruceSapling 5/6, with
+6/6 negative controls missing on every species.
+
+### COST, MEASURED AGAINST THE RIGHT CALIBRATION CLASS
+
+    station forest_floor_control, PIE, 300 frames, CSV categories ON
+
+                        pie002 (off)   unit6 (on)    delta
+    GameThreadTime mean     8.055        8.261       +0.206
+    GameThreadTime p50      7.986        8.128       +0.142
+    GameThreadTime p90      8.611        8.790       +0.179
+    GPUTime mean            8.338        8.335       -0.003
+
+**+0.21 ms GameThread against unit 6's +0.5 ms abort bar. PASSES.** GPU is
+unchanged to three decimals, which is what collision should do.
+
+**The comparator is `pie002`, NOT `pie001`.** This run had the diagnostic CSV
+categories enabled and `pie001` did not; the recorded cost of those categories
+is +0.52 ms GPU, and this run's GPUTime sits +0.519 above `pie001` — the
+instrument's own settings, reproduced. Comparing against `pie001` would have
+read as +1.06 ms and tripped a bar that was never crossed.
+
+**Stated as a limit:** this is a CROSS-SESSION A/B, not a single-variable run
+in one process. `SceneCulling/NumStaticInstances` reads 346,285 here against
+284,424 in `pie002` at identical residency (4 landscape proxies, 9 foliage
+actors) — that field is already recorded as NOT REPRODUCING and is not quoted
+as a confound or as a finding.
+
+## R-TREECOLLIDE REJECTED
+
+**`collision_enabled = QUERY_ONLY` together with `collision_profile_name =
+BlockAll`, which `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 prescribes.** SYMPTOM: reads back
+exactly right in the session that wrote it, and silently becomes
+`QUERY_AND_PHYSICS` on the next editor start. CAUSE: `BlockAll` declares
+`CollisionEnabled=QueryAndPhysics` (`BaseEngine.ini:3104`), and
+`UFoliageType::PostLoad` -> `FBodyInstance::FixupData`
+(`InstancedFoliage.cpp:806-812`) -> `LoadProfileData` (`BodyInstance.cpp:4567`)
+-> `UCollisionProfile::ReadConfig` (`:4509`) writes the PROFILE's own
+`CollisionEnabled` over whatever was serialized, on EVERY load. CORRECT: a
+profile whose own `CollisionEnabled` IS `QueryOnly`, so the two fields cannot
+contradict.
+
+**Dodging that by leaving the profile as `Custom`.** SYMPTOM: collision works,
+the player is blocked, and a walk test passes — while trees are INVISIBLE to
+visibility traces. CAUSE: `Custom` stops `ReadConfig` running, so the response
+container stays the one `UFoliageType`'s constructor left, which is
+`NoCollision`'s — and that sets `Visibility=Ignore` and `Camera=Ignore`
+(`BaseEngine.ini:3103`). Breaks line of sight, AI perception and weapon traces
+later, far from the change that caused it. CORRECT: a real profile with
+`CustomResponses=` empty.
+
+**`custom_navigable_geometry = "no"` to keep trees out of the navmesh**, as
+`PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 6 prescribes. SYMPTOM: reads like a safety measure and
+does the opposite of what the name suggests. CAUSE: per
+`NavRelevantInterface.h`, `No` means the custom export callback is not called
+**but the default collision export still runs**; for an ISM that callback is
+`DoCustomNavigableGeometryExport` (`InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:5435-5438`), which
+exports PER-INSTANCE transforms and is the path that makes 63,981 instances
+navmesh obstacles at all. CORRECT: `"yes"` — the engine default
+(`InstancedFoliage.cpp:868`) — declared explicitly. `"dont_export"` is the
+value that actually excludes.
+
+**Quoting the MESH's `collision_profile` as the runtime answer.** SYMPTOM:
+`Free/_measured/mesh_collision.json` reports `BlockAll` on all six meshes while
+nothing in the world collides. CAUSE: that field is the MESH's
+`BodySetup.default_instance`; the component's `BodyInstance` is overwritten
+from the FOLIAGE TYPE at `InstancedFoliage.cpp:1822`. Two different objects,
+one path. CORRECT: read the foliage type — `measure_foliage_collision` prints
+both in one table.
+
+**Sizing an authored capsule from `RENDER_DATA` or
+`get_section_from_static_mesh` on a NANITE mesh.** SYMPTOM: a confident radius
+derived from a mesh nobody renders. CAUSE: both return the Nanite FALLBACK
+proxy. Measured on `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A`: the fallback overstates the
+mesh by **6.6% in Z and ~36% in X**, and its low-Z bands hold 1–8 vertices,
+giving radii scattered 7–63 cm with no cylinder in them. CORRECT:
+`GeometryScript_AssetUtils.copy_mesh_from_static_mesh` with
+`GeometryScriptLODType.SOURCE_MODEL` — 76,343 vertices and a clean trunk. Check
+`build_scale` before assuming a conversion factor: it is `[1,1,1]` here, so the
+two are different MESHES, not one mesh in two unit systems.
+
+**Extrapolating the trunk radius from the sibling vendor capsules.** SYMPTOM: a
+tight fit across three assets (`r/h ~ 0.030`, `r ∝ h^0.85`, 4.5 m / 16.7 m /
+22.1 m) giving **78 cm** at 29.12 m — more than double the real trunk. CAUSE:
+vendor capsules are GAMEPLAY-FATTENED VOLUMES, not trunks; this mesh measures
+`r/h = 0.0120`. CORRECT: measure the mesh. A tight fit across three samples
+says the samples agree with each other, not that they measure the thing you
+want.
+
+**Declaring the capsule as the engine's `length`.** SYMPTOM: a capsule one
+diameter shorter than intended, silently. CAUSE: `KSphylElem.length` is the
+LINE SEGMENT — "add Radius to both ends to find total length"
+(`SphylElem.h`) — but it reads as a total height. CORRECT: the recipe declares
+`radius_cm` + `z_min_cm` + `z_max_cm`; the tool derives `length` once and
+refuses a span that does not exceed its own diameter. `length_cm` is a REFUSED
+key with a `prove_gates` probe holding the refusal.
+
+**Authoring collision onto a gitignored vendor mesh.** SYMPTOM: works, then
+vanishes on re-download. CAUSE: `RECIPES.md`'s Fab-boundary rule names
+"changing its LOD or collision" on a Fab static mesh as its worked example.
+CORRECT: `apply_foliage_collision` refuses by `git check-ignore` against the
+real file, and treats "could not decide" as a refusal rather than as tracked.
+Of the four tree meshes only `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` is tracked — it is the
+one this project exported itself, and the only one with no simple collision,
+which is not a coincidence.
+
+**`save_dirty_packages` after setting the foliage types.** SYMPTOM: reports
+success, writes nothing, and PIE keeps the old collision. CAUSE: the load-time
+`UpdateComponentSettings` that corrected the components does not dirty their
+packages — 0 dirty against 1,093 corrected actors. CORRECT:
+`save_foliage_actors.py`, which saves with `only_dirty=False`, and VERIFY FROM
+`git status` — 1,073 of 1,093 packages modified on disk — never from the tool's
+return value.
+
+**Making `collision` an optional field with a sensible default.** SYMPTOM: the
+exact failure being fixed, reproduced — silent, invisible, green on every
+asset-level check. CAUSE: the original defect was not a wrong value but an
+absent one; `place_foliage` contains no occurrence of the string "collision" in
+any form, so `UFoliageType`'s constructor default (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:640`)
+stood for the life of the project. CORRECT: REQUIRED on every instanced
+species, REFUSED on grass (`LandscapeGrass.cpp:3170-3172` hard-codes
+`NoCollision` there, so the field could not mean anything), 16 `prove_gates`
+probes holding it. **A default you never named is a decision you never made.**

    Hand the character back to the UI: "may be corrupted" was my lock, not his asset
    
    Ryan clicked MHC_AlpineHero and the editor told him the file may be corrupted.
    It is not, and the log says so plainly:
    
        Error: TryAddObjectToEdit called for 'MHC_AlpineHero' which is already
               added for editing
        Error: Failed to open MHC_AlpineHero failed to create editing state.
               The asset may be corrupted
    
    MY DEFECT. Every payload in scripts/hero_face/ calls try_add_object_to_edit
    and not one of them called remove_object_to_edit -- against the engine's own
    docstring, "Call RemoveObjectToEdit when done editing." The Python session
    held the editing registration, so the UI could not acquire it.
    
    THE ASSET WAS NEVER IN DOUBT, and this was checked before the fix rather than
    asserted after it: it saved at 22:47 and 22:48, passed
    "AssetCheck: Validating asset" both times, loads fine, 145,447,390 B, and
    can_build_meta_human reads true.
    
        release_character.txt   added_before true -> added_after false, released
    
    WHY IT IS WORTH A RECIPE ENTRY RATHER THAN A ONE-LINE FIX
        The editor cannot distinguish "another client holds the editing state"
        from "the bytes are bad", and it guesses the alarming one. That is the
        misleading-diagnostic class this project keeps meeting, seen from the
        other side: usually the trap is a tool reporting SUCCESS over work it
        never did; here an engine reported CATASTROPHE over an asset that was
        fine. Both are a message asserting a cause the code never established,
        and both cost trust in the record.
    
        Cost here was small only because the log was read before the file was.
        Had the message been believed, the next move would have been restoring a
        145 MB asset over a perfectly good one and losing the sculpt and grooms.

+#### R-HEROFACE, ADDENDUM — ALWAYS HAND THE CHARACTER BACK
+
+**Every payload that calls `try_add_object_to_edit` MUST call
+`remove_object_to_edit` when it is done.** The engine's own docstring says so
+and this project ignored it in nine payloads.
+
+The failure mode is not a leak. It is a **LOCKOUT WITH A LYING MESSAGE**:
+
+    Error: TryAddObjectToEdit called for 'MHC_AlpineHero' which is already
+           added for editing
+    Error: Failed to open MHC_AlpineHero failed to create editing state.
+           The asset may be corrupted
+
+Ryan double-clicked the asset and was told his hero **may be corrupted**. It
+was not: it had saved cleanly minutes earlier and passed
+`AssetCheck: Validating asset` on the way in, 145,447,390 B,
+`can_build_meta_human` true. The editor cannot distinguish "another client
+holds the editing state" from "the bytes are bad", and it reports the
+alarming one.
+
+**Fix:** `scripts/hero_face/release_character.txt` — reports
+`is_object_added_for_editing` before and after, so the release is measured.
+Restarting the editor also clears it, expensively.
+
+**This is the misleading-diagnostic class, from the other side.** This project
+has repeatedly caught tools that report success while doing nothing; here an
+engine reported CATASTROPHE over an asset that was fine. Both are the same
+defect: a message asserting a cause the code never established.
+
+| Wrong thing | Symptom | Correct thing |
+|---|---|---|
+| leaving the character registered for edit | the Content Browser refuses to open it and says **"The asset may be corrupted"** | `remove_object_to_edit` at the end of every session; `release_character.txt` |

    Groom recipe and ASSETS row: the new-element rule paid
    
    THE NEW-ELEMENT RULE requires a template-conforming recipe before a session
    that adds a new element TYPE ends. Grooms are a new type for this project, so
    they get one, plus the intake register row R-ASSET requires.
    
        RECIPES.md  +62 lines, 0 deletions -- R-HEROFACE addendum, 5 REJECTED rows
        ASSETS.md   +34 lines, 0 deletions -- the four wardrobe items, licence,
                    and an explicit verified = NO
    
    The recipe leads with the distinction that actually decides the outcome:
    try_add_item_from_wardrobe_item makes an item AVAILABLE, and only
    set_single_slot_selection on the instance makes it WORN. Every call in the
    add step returns a valid MetaHumanPaletteItemKey and the asset grows either
    way, so a session that stops after the add gets four green tool reports over
    a bald hero. That is why the two steps are separate payloads.
    
    The ASSETS row records what is NOT proven as plainly as what is: these grooms
    are verified from the character's saved bytes, and they have NO render proof,
    because they reach a frame only through the UI Assemble that has not been
    pressed. verified = NO.
    
    Licence is clean and worth stating: the grooms ship with the MetaHumanCharacter
    plugin in the UE 5.8 install, under the Unreal EULA, on the same footing as
    the template mannequin. They are NOT part of the ~3.5 GB Fab licence gap, and
    nothing was copied into the project -- MHC_AlpineHero references plugin
    content, so there is no vendor boundary to police and no hash baseline to keep.

+#### THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE HERO IS BALD
+`try_add_item_from_wardrobe_item` makes an item **AVAILABLE** in the palette.
+It does **NOT** put it on the character. The instance must SELECT it.
+Stopping after the add yields four successful-looking tool reports over a
+hero who still has no hair.
+
+    col = subsystem.get_preview_collection(character)
+    key = col.try_add_item_from_wardrobe_item(slot, wardrobe_item)  # available
+    col.get_editor_property("default_instance") \
+       .set_single_slot_selection(slot, key)                        # WORN
+    subsystem.on_edit_preview_collection(character)                 # REQUIRED
+    EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset("/Game/Hero/MHC_AlpineHero", False)
+
+`on_edit_preview_collection` is not optional — the engine docstring states
+that any code modifying the preview collection must call it to propagate the
+edits back to the Character asset.
+
+#### SLOTS (from `get_slot_names()`, measured not assumed)
+    Beard  Body  Bottom Garment  Character  Eyebrows  Eyelashes  Hair
+    Mustache  Outfits  Peachfuzz  SkeletalMesh  Top Garment
+
+#### THE VALUES, for this hero
+    Hair       WI_Hair_M_Layered        (WI_Hair_L_MessyClumps = longer)
+    Beard      WI_Beard_M_Stubble
+    Mustache   WI_Mustache_M_Stubble
+    Eyebrows   WI_Eyebrows_M_Dense
+All under `/MetaHumanCharacter/Optional/Grooms/Bindings/<Slot>/`, class
+`MetaHumanWardrobeItem`, engine content under the UE EULA.
+
+#### PROCEDURE
+1. `apply_hero_grooms.txt --set GO=False` — probe. Reports the slot names and
+   whether each item resolves; mutates nothing. **Run this first**: it turns
+   a missing asset into a refusal instead of a half-applied groom set.
+2. `apply_hero_grooms.txt --set GO=True` — add + propagate + save.
+3. `select_hero_grooms.txt --set GO=True` — recover the key per slot with
+   `get_item_keys_for_slot`, select, propagate, save.
+4. `verify_grooms_on_disk.py` — verify from the SAVED BYTES.
+
+#### VERIFICATION
+Positive-controlled byte search of `MHC_AlpineHero.uasset`: the four selected
+groom names present (3 hits each) and five deliberately unselected names

+its verdict entirely if any control appears — a substring search that matches
+everything proves nothing.
+

+|---|---|---|
+| add without selecting | every call returns a valid `MetaHumanPaletteItemKey`, the asset grows, and the hero is still bald | `set_single_slot_selection` on `default_instance` |
+| skipping `on_edit_preview_collection` | edits sit on the preview collection and never reach the Character asset | call it after every modification |

+# 2026-08-16 (evening) — THE HERO'S FACE IS SCULPTED, AND THE UNITS LIED FIRST
+
+Ryan: *"add in the hero features to the face to create the hero look based on
+the image"*, then mid-session: *"the image starting with qv94 should be the
+final product look of the hero"* — the HAIRED portrait is the product target.
+
+## A SCULPT THAT REPORTED SUCCESS AND MOVED NOTHING
+
+`MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem` exposes the sculpt directly:
+`get_face_landmarks` returns 79 control points, `translate_face_landmarks`
+moves them, `commit_face_state` persists. The first application asked for
+moves up to `3.48e-03` and the landmarks moved `6.08e-06` — 0.17% — while the
+facial rig did not move at all.
+
+**Root cause: `get_face_landmarks` REPORTS in one space and
+`translate_face_landmarks` ACCEPTS another.** A ladder of five deltas on one
+landmark settles it, and the consistency is what makes it a calibration
+rather than a coincidence:
+
+    requested   landmark moved   requested/moved   rig moved
+      0.001       1.343e-06          744.85          0.0
+      0.01        1.342e-05          745.32          0.0
+      0.1         1.342e-04          744.99          0.0
+      1.0         1.342e-03          745.11          0.0
+     10.0         5.876e-03         1701.97          0.0
+
+**745.0 delta units per landmark unit**, linear across three decades, then
+**saturating** at 10.0 — the face model constrains large single moves.
+
+Two structural consequences: a one-shot delta CANNOT land on target, so the
+applier iterates `(target - current) * 745` clamped into the linear regime and
+prints the residual per pass; and the spec carries absolute TARGETS rather
+than offsets, so re-running is a no-op instead of sculpting the face twice
+(pipeline rule 3).
+
+This is *"a value can arrive and still mean something else"* from the
+resolution protocol, landing exactly as written. The magnitude was derived
+correctly from a premise about units that was never checked.
+
+## THE GATE CAUGHT IT — AND THE GATE'S OWN INSTRUMENT WAS ALSO WRONG
+
+The applier refuses to commit when landmarks move and the mesh does not,
+because that is the signature the body `Masculine/Feminine` slider produced
+earlier the same day. It fired on the first run and produced the numbers that
+led to the calibration.
+
+**But its instrument was wrong in the dangerous direction.** It read facial
+rig joints via `get_socket_location`, which returns reference-pose positions
+and reads `0.0` even after a *successful* sculpt, even after
+`assemble_for_preview`. A gate that reports "no movement" on a working sculpt
+is a false refusal that would have blocked the correct result.
+
+What settled it was a third representation: **the asset's bytes on disk**,
+`104,960,609 B sha 95024DC2` → `104,977,162 B sha DF57585B`. Fixed in the same
+pass: the gate had treated an unreadable mesh measurement as a PASS. "I could
+not look" is not "yes" (non-negotiable 6).
+

+**The same assertion, file and line as the recorded `conform_to_target_meshes`

+## `build_meta_human` IS REFLECTED; THE UNPACK IS NOT
+
+CURRENT STATE said *"MetaHuman's Assemble is NOT REFLECTED — no unpack, no
+build anywhere in the 5.8 stub"*. **Half false, and the half that is true is
+the important half.** `build_meta_human` and `can_build_meta_human` ARE
+reflected, with `MetaHumanCharacterEditorBuildParameters`; the earlier reading
+was almost certainly taken off a stub generated BEFORE the MetaHuman plugins
+were enabled. **The Python stub is a DERIVED RECORD, regenerated per editor
+start, only as current as its last regeneration** — non-negotiable 15 in a
+file nobody treats as a config.
+
+But calling it logs **"MetaHuman Character assembly succeeded"** and writes
+nothing to disk: everything lands in `/Engine/Transient.MHC_..._Collection:`.

+`absolute_build_path`. So Python can sculpt, rig and assemble; only the editor
+UI can unpack to `/Game/Hero/Generated/SKM_HeroFace`. That is the same shape
+as the "Save Face Textures" finding: a door that exists only in the UI.

+## A CLAIM I MADE FROM A PHOTOGRAPH, AND THE MEASUREMENT REFUTED IT
+
+Seeing the bald and haired references side by side I reported them as
+different face shapes — the haired one *"leaner, hollower cheeks, tapered V
+jaw"*. Tracked with the same instrument and normalised to interpupillary
+units they agree to within ~3%:
+
+    eye_to_mouth  1.002     eye widths  1.011 / 1.003
+    mouth width   0.971     nasolabial  1.034
+
+`hero/reference/README.md`'s "the SAME face" is SUPPORTED; my reading was the
+eye being fooled by hair and beard framing the face. **Non-negotiable 16 — the
+eye is a poor photometer — extends to geometry: it is a poor proportioner
+too.** Stated narrowly, because the instrument has a scope: the tracker
+returns eyelids, lips, philtrum and nasolabial folds ONLY, so jaw and
+cheekbone contour are unmeasured on the haired image, not agreed.
+
+## ANATOMY ASSUMED IS ANATOMY GUESSED
+
+The 79 landmarks arrive unlabelled and `get_preset_body_key_points` names only
+`P1`…`P102` against BODY vertex indices. Naming them from extremes (most
+anterior = nose tip, lowest = chin) produced a nose-to-chin of **13.7 cm**
+against a scale three axis ratios agreed on. The arithmetic was right; the
+premise was invented.
+
+What worked was LOOKING. X is lateral by a bilateral-symmetry test (median
+mirror residual 0.7% of span, against 13.7% and 4.0%), and Z is up — so an
+orthographic X–Z plot IS a front view, and the mid-sagittal chain reads
+directly: 7 forehead, 59 glabella, 6 nose bridge, 64 nose tip, 65 subnasale,
+5/50/4 lips, 62 chin crease, 8 chin, 12 under-chin, 13/14/15 the POSTERIOR
+midline, 60 the crown.
+
+**And the landmarks are a CONTROL CAGE, not surface points**: nose-tip-to-chin
+implies 222 cm/unit, forehead-to-chin 315, tip-to-subnasale over 400. Three
+irreconcilable answers is the data refusing the premise, so every move is
+expressed as a fraction of head extent rather than in centimetres.
+
+## SYMMETRY BELONGS IN THE STRUCTURE, NOT IN THE TUNING
+
+Region predicates have edges, and the first plan caught nose wing 45 without
+its mirror 67, and jaw points 3 and 30 without 43 and 63 — a crooked face from
+a symmetric intent. Tuning predicates until the edges line up would need
+re-tuning on every future edit. Mirror-pairing the delta field makes symmetry
+structural: all 79 pair, worst residual asymmetry **0.000e+00**.
+
+## FOUR WHITE FRAMES, AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT REPLACED THE RENDERER
+
+Every engine capture of this character came back pure white — mean RGB
+255/255/255, nonwhite fraction 0.0000, four times, across two camera designs
+and an actor scaled 2000x. The cause: the preview mesh is ~0.12 units tall,
+its components sit at world origin and **do not follow `set_actor_location`**,
+so the subject is inside the near clip plane. `get_actor_bounds` reports a
+subject 250,000 units tall because it spans from world origin to wherever the
+actor root was moved — two readings of the same actor that cannot both be
+about the same head.
+
+The fix was to stop asking the renderer. `get_mesh_data_for_conforming` returns
+the face mesh's 33,845 vertices and 64,094 triangles; rasterised offline they
+give a clear, shaded portrait — and, unlike 79 landmarks, they ARE a
+silhouette, so the width-at-height comparison against the photograph finally
+became sound. It shows the hero still 2–18% wider than the sculpted mesh,
+largest at the jaw (1.13–1.22) and closed at the ear line (1.00–1.02), which
+drove a second, purely measured widening pass.
+
+## AN OPERATIONAL TRAP THAT COST ~8 MINUTES
+
+`ue_exec.py --timeout N` passes N into `_select_verified_node`, so **N is a
+fixed discovery window, not a deadline**: `--timeout 240` bought 240 s of
+sitting followed by 3 s of work. Same shape as the recorded `capture.py
+--timeout` lesson. Use 12–15.
+
+Also: `save_asset` immediately before `build_meta_human` wedged the editor —
+log frozen at `InternalPromptForCheckoutAndSave started...` →
+`FlushAsyncLoading`, game thread at 0.05 CPU per wall-second, an untitled
+modal up. The autorig step had already saved it; the second save bought
+nothing and cost the editor.

+## R-HEROFACE — sculpting the hero's face from reference photographs
+
+**Status: PROVEN for sculpt + rig. The UNPACK step is UI-ONLY and is NOT
+scriptable in 5.8.** Narrative: `LESSONS.md` 2026-08-16 (evening).
+Instruments: `scripts/hero_face/`.
+
+### WHAT IT DOES
+Moves a MetaHuman Character's face onto proportions measured from reference
+photographs, entirely from Python, and verifies the result against those
+photographs by a route that never uses the engine's renderer.
+
+### THE FRAME — derive it, never assume it
+`get_face_landmarks` returns 79 unlabelled points; the reflected surface says
+nothing about axes, units or anatomy.
+
+    lateral axis  X, by bilateral-symmetry test: median nearest-mirror
+                  residual 0.7% of span about the cloud mean, against
+                  13.7% (Y) and 4.0% (Z). Sagittal plane x = -0.01011.
+    up axis       Z            depth axis  Y, +Y anterior
+    anatomy       read off an orthographic X-Z plot, which IS a front view
+                  once X is lateral and Z is up:
+                    7 forehead  59 glabella  6 nose bridge  64 nose tip
+                    65 subnasale  5/50/4 lips  62 chin crease  8 chin
+                    12 under-chin   60 crown
+                    13/14/15 POSTERIOR midline (back of skull, nape)
+
+### THE UNIT IS 745 — the whole recipe in one number
+`get_face_landmarks` REPORTS in one space; `translate_face_landmarks`
+ACCEPTS another.
+
+    requested   landmark moved   ratio
+      0.001       1.343e-06      744.85
+      0.01        1.342e-05      745.32
+      0.1         1.342e-04      744.99
+      1.0         1.342e-03      745.11
+     10.0         5.876e-03     1701.97   <- SATURATED
+
+**To move a landmark by X landmark-units, request X * 745.** Above ~1.0 per
+call the face model constrains the move, so ITERATE rather than ask once.
+
+### PROCEDURE
+1. `probe_face_state.txt` -> landmarks + coefficients to disk.
+2. `plan_face_sculpt.py` -> region predicates over normalised head
+   coordinates, symmetrised by mirror-pairing, emitting ABSOLUTE TARGETS.
+3. `apply_face_sculpt.txt --set COMMIT=True --set PASSES=12 --set SPAWN=False`
+   -> iterates `(target - current) * 745` clamped to 1.0, prints residual per
+   pass, `commit_face_state`, `save_asset`.
+4. `dump_face_mesh.txt` + `render_face_mesh_offline.py` -> a picture, and the
+   width-at-height comparison against the reference silhouette.
+5. `plan_lateral_correction.py` + step 3 again -> close the measured
+   lateral shortfall. Damped 0.6, clamped 1.18.
+6. `autorig_hero.txt --set BLOCKING=False` (~25 s), then
+   `save_character.txt`. **`can_build_meta_human` must read true before the
+   character can be assembled.**
+7. **RYAN, IN THE UI:** open `MHC_AlpineHero` and press Assemble. Nothing in
+   Python unpacks.
+
+### MEASURED RESULT, 2026-08-16
+    pass 1  residual 0.00844 -> 0.00153 units (82% closed, 20 passes)
+    pass 2  residual 0.00256 -> 0.00093 units (64% closed, 10 passes)
+    asset   104,960,609 -> 104,977,162 -> 143,762,092 -> 145,442,446 B
+    mesh    33,845 verts / 64,094 tris, extent 0.11497 x 0.08275 x 0.12433
+
+**Pass 2 widened the cranium and cheeks by +7.1% to +8.1% and moved the jaw
+by +1.0% / +0.2%.** The mandible is where the face model resists: the hero
+remains 13-22% wider at the jaw than the sculpt will go. Recorded as a
+property of the model, not as a failure of the pass.
+
+### VERIFICATION — and the two instruments that must NOT be used
+- **USE** the character asset's BYTES on disk. Every "did it take?" question
+  in this work was settled by a size and hash change.
+- **USE** mesh geometry via `get_mesh_data_for_conforming` on the preview
+  `FaceMesh_N`, rasterised offline.
+- **DO NOT** use `get_face_landmarks` alone. It reads the field the setter
+  wrote and reported success on a sculpt that moved nothing
+  (non-negotiable 8) -- that is how the 745x unit error survived its first run.
+- **DO NOT** use facial rig joints via `get_socket_location`. They return
+  reference-pose positions and read 0.0 movement on a WORKING sculpt, even
+  after `assemble_for_preview`. A gate built on them is a FALSE REFUSAL.
+
+### REJECTED
+
+| Wrong thing | Symptom you will see | Correct thing |
+|---|---|---|
+| deltas in landmark units | asked 3.48e-03, moved 6.08e-06 (0.17%); every tool reports success | multiply by **745** |
+| one-shot delta | lands short of target and silently stays there | iterate; the model saturates above ~1.0 per call |
+| offset-based spec | a second run sculpts the face twice, undetectably | absolute TARGETS; re-running is a no-op |
+| region predicates without symmetrisation | nose wing 45 without mirror 67, jaw 3/30 without 43/63 -> a CROOKED face | mirror-pair the delta field; all 79 pair, residual 0.000e+00 |
+| `request_auto_rigging(blocking=True)` | **EDITOR DIES.** `Assertion failed: IsValid() [SharedPointer.h:1133]` -- the same assertion as the recorded `conform_to_target_meshes` crash | `blocking=False`; watch the log for "Auto-Rigging finished in N seconds" |
+| spawning the MetaHuman actor before `save_asset` | editor WEDGES, twice: log stops at `InternalPromptForCheckoutAndSave started...` -> `FlushAsyncLoading`, game thread 0.04 CPU/wall, untitled modal, committed sculpt LOST | `--set SPAWN=False`. The spawn brings up `/Temp/MetaHumanCharacter/LightingEnvironments/...` streamed levels and the save deadlocks on them |
+| `save_asset` again before `build_meta_human` | same wedge | the autorig step already saved it |
+| `build_meta_human(absolute_build_path=...)` | logs **"MetaHuman Character assembly succeeded"** and writes NOTHING; everything lands in `/Engine/Transient.MHC_..._Collection:` | there is **no reflected unpack in 5.8**, with any path. Assemble in the UI |
+| landmark-derived width profile vs photo silhouette | ratios up to 87 on bands of n=1-4 | 79 points are not a silhouette; use the MESH's 33,845 vertices |
+| rendering the MetaHuman preview actor | pure white, mean RGB 255/255/255, nonwhite fraction 0.0000, four times | the preview mesh is ~0.12 units tall and its components sit at world origin and do NOT follow `set_actor_location`; it is inside the near clip plane. Rasterise the mesh offline |
+| comparing two sculpt passes by their ratio tables | jaw "got worse" 1.159 -> 1.308 | each table is normalised by its OWN cranium width; when the cranium widens the denominator moves. Compare ABSOLUTE widths at matched heights (`compare_sculpt_passes.py`) |
+| `get_local_bounds` on the face component | `AttributeError` -- it is a `DebugSkelMeshComponent` | `get_actor_bounds`, or enumerate: `get_num_bones` / `get_bone_name` / `get_socket_location` exist |
+| `ue_exec.py --timeout 240` | ~240 s of nothing, then 3 s of work | it is a DISCOVERY WINDOW, not a deadline. Use 12-15 |
+
+### THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT, read out of the editor log
+    sculpt  ->  textures  ->  rig  ->  build
+Rigging LOCKS texture editing (*"Face and body texture selection are locked
+while the character is rigged. Unrig to modify them."*) and building REQUIRES
+a rig. Unrigging to do texture work is what left the character unrigged.
+**A sculpt does NOT invalidate the rig** -- measured: `can_build_meta_human`
+read true immediately after pass 2, before any re-rig.

    splits vertices. The fix caused the symptom it was meant to cure, and I only
    established the direction by reverting and comparing.

    them expecting the success.

    curve names are in the run log and I believe the measurement happened; I cannot
    demonstrate it on demand. Those are different claims and the record now makes
    the weaker one.

+same reason `ue_exec` gives every caller its own stage filename. I applied that
+rule to the payload staging tonight and not to the frames the payload wrote.

+   silhouette. Nothing to track.

+   lower kept the chin AND changed the Z extent, so a Z-based scale shrank the
+   FACE in frame: 37.5 to 32.0.

+   better: faceted planes with holes at the eyes and ears. More triangles made
+   it worse, which is the opposite of the expected direction and is why it has
+   to be looked at rather than reasoned about.

+   mid-grey with near-uniform blown-out white. The successful render's TONAL
+   RANGE, which came from a material I had thought was a defect, was part of
+   why the tracker could see anything.

+distinct cause.** Exporting the render turned one undifferentiated failure into
+four separate diagnosable ones, and that instrument was added only after the

+## 2026-08-16 (later) — THE FACE CONFORM CRASHED THE EDITOR, and the route is now known
+
+Logged BEFORE any retry, per the operating loop's step (b).
+
+### WHAT WAS ATTEMPTED
+
+`conform_to_target_meshes(character, target_mesh_key, params)` with the TRELLIS
+head as the target: `TargetPartsType.HEAD_ONLY`, `head_vertices` and
+`head_vertex_indices` taken from
+`MetaHumanCharacterEditorSubsystem.get_mesh_data_for_conforming(SM_HeroHead_TRELLIS)`,
+`auto_solve=True`, and NO `curve_tracking_points`, `camera_view_info` or
+`image_size`.
+
+### WHAT HAPPENED
+
+    CrashType     Assert
+    ErrorMessage  Assertion failed: IsValid()
+                  [Templates/SharedPointer.h] [Line: 1133]
+    CallStack     UnrealEditor_Core
+                  UnrealEditor_Core
+                  UnrealEditor_MetaHumanCharacterEditor   x4
+                  UnrealEditor_CoreUObject
+                  UnrealEditor_PythonScriptPlugin ...
+
+The editor died. `ue_exec` surfaced it as `ConnectionResetError: [WinError
+10054]`, which is what a crashed editor looks like from the client side and is
+NOT itself diagnostic — the crash log is.
+
+**NOTHING WAS DAMAGED.** `git status` clean, and `MHC_AlpineHero.uasset` still
+carries its pre-session mtime. The conform mutates in memory and nothing was
+saved. Restore point `pre-hero-face-conform-20260816` was tagged first and was
+not needed.
+
+### ROOT CAUSE, AS FAR AS IT IS ESTABLISHED
+
+A `TSharedPtr` was dereferenced unset inside `MetaHumanCharacterEditor`. The
+call reached engine code — this is not a Python type error and not a bad
+argument the binding could reject — so something the solver requires was absent
+rather than wrong.
+
+**The strong candidate is the face-tracking context.** `ConformTargetParams`
+carries `curve_tracking_points`, `camera_view_info` and `image_size` alongside
+the mesh, and all three were left at their defaults. `auto_solve=True` was
+assumed to make them optional. **That assumption is the thing that failed**, and
+it was an assumption — nothing in the reflected surface says auto_solve
+substitutes for landmarks.
+
+**STATED AS A LOCATION, NOT A CAUSE.** Without symbols I cannot say which
+pointer. What is established: the call is reachable, the argument types are
+accepted, and it dies inside the solver rather than at the boundary.
+
+### WHAT THIS BUYS THE NEXT ATTEMPT
+
+The expensive unknown is now settled, and it is the one that mattered:
+
+**`get_mesh_data_for_conforming` IS the bridge, and arbitrary topology IS
+supported.** It returns `(vertices, triangle_indices)` from a StaticMesh or
+SkeletalMesh — "the same data that the interactive conform tool uses
+internally" — and those map one-to-one onto `ConformTargetMesh.head_vertices`
+and `.head_vertex_indices`. **The indices are TRIANGLES, not archetype
+correspondence.** I had earlier read `head_vertex_indices` as implying archetype
+topology and concluded a raw TRELLIS mesh was not a drop-in. That reading was
+wrong and is corrected here.
+
+Measured on both meshes:
+
+    SM_HeroHead_TRELLIS   472,734 verts   extent (0.696, 0.921, 0.998)
+    SKM_HeroFace          33,845 verts    extent (34.99, 24.28, 37.32) cm
+                          bbox Z 134.7 .. 172.0  -- CHARACTER space, Z up
+
+Same axis convention, so no rotation is needed — only scale and translation.
+**Scale from HEIGHT, not width or depth:** the TRELLIS reconstruction includes
+the armour collar, and the bbox ratios disagree accordingly — 50.3 on width,
+26.4 on depth, 37.4 on height. Only height measures the same thing on both.
+
+### THREE THINGS THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD DO DIFFERENTLY
+
+1. **Supply the tracking inputs.** Render the target mesh from a known camera
+   into a TextureRenderTarget2D, read it as BGRA, run
+   `track_face_landmarks_from_image`, and pass the returned curves together
+   with the `MinimalViewInfo` that produced them and the image size. The
+   docstring for the tracker says exactly this: *"Use with a front-facing
+   portrait of the target mesh — typically a SceneCapture2D render."*
+2. **DECIMATE FIRST.** 472,734 vertices is not precision this solve needs, and
+   building that array crosses the Python binding once per element — the call
+   took over ten minutes before it died. `scripts/trellis/decimate_head.py`
+   produces ~40k triangles via open3d and records the bbox change so the
+   silhouette is checked, not assumed.
+3. **CROP THE COLLAR OUT OF THE MESH**, not just out of the input image. It is
+   the reason the three scale estimates disagree by 2x, and it is geometry the
+   solver has no use for.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**A crash inside engine code from a reflected call is an ARGUMENT that was
+absent, not an argument that was wrong** — the binding rejects wrong types at
+the boundary and it did not. When a struct offers several fields and only some
+are populated, the unpopulated ones are the suspects, and a flag named
+`auto_solve` is not evidence that the others are optional.
+
+And: **an editor crash is a measurement.** It cost seven minutes of restart and
+established more about this API than three careful probes had.

+## 2026-08-16 — THE HERO BECOMES PLAYABLE, and five tools lied on the way
+
+Ryan went to bed asking for one thing: *"my hero available to run around in the
+environment."* He got it. What follows is what it cost, and five of the six
+findings are instruments that reported success while doing nothing.
+
+### TRELLIS RUNS ON BLACKWELL, WHICH THE PLAN SAID THE DOCUMENTED PATH COULD NOT DO
+
+472,734 vertices, 945,456 faces, watertight, 64 s end to end from Ryan's
+portrait. TRELLIS ships PyTorch 2.4.0+cu118, which has no sm_120 support at all,
+so the install deviated to torch 2.11+cu128 and every extension had to meet a
+toolchain years newer than it expects.
+
+**The install was PIECEWISE on purpose, and that is the only reason four
+blockers were each attributable to one cause.** A `setup.sh` run would have
+produced one failure and no information.
+
+1. **`open3d` absent.** `trellis/pipelines/__init__` imports the TEXT-to-3D
+   pipeline at package import, so an image-only job pays for it anyway.
+
+2. **`ATTN_BACKEND=sdpa` WAS SILENTLY IGNORED, and this is the trap.**
+   `trellis/modules/attention/__init__.py` accepts `xformers`, `flash_attn`,
+   `sdpa`, `naive`. `trellis/modules/sparse/__init__.py` accepts ONLY
+   `xformers` or `flash_attn` and leaves its default in place otherwise. So the
+   same environment variable is honoured in one module and dropped in the other,
+   and the run printed `[SPARSE] Backend: spconv, Attention: flash_attn` while
+   the environment plainly said `sdpa` — with flash_attn not installed.
+   **A configuration value that is accepted by one reader and ignored by
+   another is worse than one that is rejected everywhere**, because the log
+   line that would tell you is the one nobody reads on a working run.
+
+3. **`kaolin` was NOT needed, and installing it would have been the wrong
+   fix.** The library path imports exactly one symbol —
+   `from kaolin.utils.testing import check_tensor`, used in six assertions with
+   `throw=False`. Every other kaolin reference in the package is under
+   `examples/` and is never imported. kaolin publishes no wheel for torch
+   2.11+cu128, so building it would have been a large risk for one shape check.
+   `scripts/trellis/kaolin_check_tensor_shim.py` IMPLEMENTS the contract
+   instead.
+   **It is implemented and not stubbed, deliberately.** `def check_tensor(*a,
+   **k): return True` would satisfy the import and silently disable all six
+   assertions — non-negotiable 2's un-failable gate, which reads as coverage
+   while being its absence. The shim's selftest asserts it REFUSES wrong rank,
+   wrong dimension, wrong dtype and non-tensors, and the installer refuses to
+   shadow a real kaolin if one ever appears.
+
+4. **xformers has no sm_120 kernel for float32.** The dispatcher named all
+   three candidates: `fa3F` and `cutlassF-pt` require capability <= (9, 0), and
+   `fa2F` supports only fp16/bf16. DINOv2's conditioning runs fp32.
+   The fix was NOT to patch TRELLIS. `dinov2/layers/attention.py:21` reads
+   `XFORMERS_ENABLED = os.environ.get("XFORMERS_DISABLED") is None`, so
+   `XFORMERS_DISABLED=1` routes DINOv2 to its own attention while leaving
+   TRELLIS's sparse attention — which imports xformers directly and never
+   consults that variable — on xformers where it must stay.
+
+xformers was installed `--no-deps` on purpose, so a resolver could not swap out
+the torch that had passed the sm_120 gate. Verified after: still 2.11.0+cu128,
+still capability (12, 0), and `memory_efficient_attention` executes a real fp16
+kernel on this card.
+
+### FOUR WAYS TO MANGLE A PAYLOAD ON THE WAY INTO WSL, ALL MEASURED
+
+Every one produced a WRONG READING rather than an error:
+
+  * PowerShell 5.1 split a single-quoted argument at the first space; bash died
+    on an unterminated `if`.
+  * Git Bash rewrote `/usr/lib/wsl/lib/nvidia-smi` into
+    `C:/Program Files/Git/usr/lib/...` — the msys path-conversion hazard this
+    repo already hooks for `/Game/...`.
+  * **`wsl.exe` RE-PARSES the command line**, so a heredoc's quoted delimiter
+    `<<"EOF"` arrived as `<<EOF` and the body expanded after all. That one wrote
+    an EXPANDED Windows PATH snapshot into `/etc/profile.d/cuda.sh`, and the
+    file then looked correct while doing the wrong thing — non-negotiable 17, in
+    a file I had written myself minutes earlier.
+  * `$(...)` inside a payload returned empty unpredictably. `command -v nvcc`
+    printed nothing in the same shell where `type -a nvcc` resolved it
+    correctly, and I was one sentence from recording "CUDA is not on PATH".
+
+`scripts/wsl_exec.sh` base64-encodes the script. The alphabet is
+`[A-Za-z0-9+/=]` — no spaces, quotes, dollars or slashes — so no layer has
+anything to mangle. It also strips CR, because a script authored on Windows
+carries CRLF and bash then fails naming the wrong thing.
+
+**And a detach that reported success and left nothing behind.** `setsid nohup`
+inside a `wsl.exe` call printed `STARTED ... log ...`, exited 0, and produced no
+log, no `/opt/trellis` and no process: **WSL tears down the whole session
+process tree when the initiating `wsl.exe` exits.** Backgrounding the CALLER is
+what holds the session open, which is why the CUDA and PyTorch installs
+completed and that one did not. Kept in the tool as a NAMED TRAP rather than
+deleted.
+
+### I REPORTED "NO HEAD" AND THE MEASUREMENT OVERTURNED IT
+
+From the first PIE frame I wrote that the face mesh was not rendering. **That
+was wrong.** The camera was ~1 m from the body and the head was simply out of
+frame. What settled it was not another look but a different question: the
+FaceMesh's `head` bone read 150 cm above its root with a correct
+root/pelvis/spine hierarchy, and lifting the pawn above the canopy then showed a
+complete head and face.
+
+Three photographs said "something is wrong" and none could say what. The eye is
+a poor instrument through a 219,659-instance forest — non-negotiable 16 again,
+and it cost three wasted frames before I asked the geometry instead of the
+pixels.
+
+### `Rotator(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)` RECURRED IN A COMMITTED TOOL
+
+`place_player_start.py:118,122` called `_unreal.Rotator(0.0, __YAW__, 0.0)`.
+The signature is `(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)`, so `--yaw 135` set **pitch** to 135,
+which the engine normalises to exactly `(roll 180, pitch 45, yaw 180)` — the
+value measured off the live actor.
+
+CLAUDE.md already records this casualty by name from 2026-08-12. **It recurred
+because the tool READ BACK LOCATION AND NEVER ROTATION.** It printed
+"drift 0.000 cm" and returned 0 over a scrambled rotation, for as long as
+nobody looked.
+
+The consequence was not cosmetic. The PlayerController inherits the
+PlayerStart's rotation and the third-person boom follows it, so a 45 degree
+pitch aimed the arm into the ground behind the player: the camera sat **88.1 cm
+BELOW** the pawn, **125.5 cm** back on a 400 cm arm, looking up at him from the
+floor. After the fix: **381.8 cm back, 138.4 cm above**. Same config, same
+probe, one correct rotation.
+
+**I first blamed the forest and shrank the collision probe.** That was not
+wasted — the probe size deserves to be config — but it was treating a symptom,
+and three more frames would not have found the cause. Reading the control
+rotation did, immediately.
+
+**The rule: a value that is never read back is a value nothing defends.** The
+tool now asserts rotation and refuses with exit 5 when it disagrees.
+
+### A SAVE REPORTED True AND WROTE NOTHING — the most dangerous shape yet
+
+`EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)` returned True. The
+PlayerStart move never reached disk. **Caught by the filesystem**, not by any
+tool: nothing under `__ExternalActors__` and no `.umap` had changed in ninety
+minutes.
+
+A Python actor edit does not reliably flag the external actor package dirty, so
+"save every DIRTY package" saved an empty set and truthfully reported success at
+having done so. And every check agreed with it:
+
+  * the location read-back said drift 0.000 cm;
+  * a second run listed the actor at its new coordinates;
+  * PIE spawned the pawn there.
+
+**All three were correct and all three read EDITOR MEMORY** — precisely where
+the unsaved change lived. Non-negotiable 0: agreement among instruments that
+share a source is one measurement, not three. Only the file on disk was a
+different representation, and only it could see the defect.
+
+The project already carries this rule from the 2026-08-09 `save_level`
+incident — *"verify a save from the ARTEFACT, never from the tool's report"* —
+written when a save SUCCEEDED and reported failure. **This is the same rule
+earning its keep against the inversion, which is far more dangerous: a false
+failure gets investigated, a false success gets built upon.**
+
+Fixed by removing the dependency rather than adding a retry: the tool reaches
+the actor's own package, saves THAT package explicitly, PRINTS ITS NAME so the
+caller knows which file's mtime to check, and refuses if the save returns false.
+
+### METAHUMAN: WHAT PYTHON CAN AND CANNOT DO IN 5.8
+
+**Can:** `try_add_object_to_edit`, `get_preview_collection`,
+`spawn_meta_human_actor`, `conform_to_target_meshes`,
+`fit_state_to_target_vertices`, `track_face_landmarks_from_image`,
+`request_auto_rigging`, `get_body_constraints` / `set_body_constraints`. All ten
+probed present and reachable.
+
+**Cannot: ASSEMBLE.** There is no unpack and no build anywhere in the 5.8 stub.
+The reachable route is duplicating `spawn_meta_human_actor`'s preview meshes
+into real packages, which works — and their materials then point at
+`/Engine/Transient` dynamic instances that are null on reload.
+
+**And the skin cannot be recovered from them.** MetaHuman sets skin as parameter
+OVERRIDES on the dynamic instance, and the getter hard-refuses that type:
+
+    GetMaterialInstanceTextureParameterValue
+    TypeError: Cannot nativize 'MaterialInstanceDynamic' as 'Object'
+               (allowed Class type: 'MaterialInstanceConstant')
+
+Measured against all 80 texture parameters of the face material. **The names
+enumerate; the values are unreachable.** So a Python-built MetaHuman is
+untextured white BY CONSTRUCTION, and `build_hero_assets` says so in its
+docstring and on every run rather than shipping a mystery.
+
+**A NULL RESULT I DID NOT TRUST, AND SHOULD NOT HAVE.** The body carries a
+`Masculine/Feminine` constraint, range -2.0 to +2.0. Setting it to -2.0 and
++2.0 produced BYTE-IDENTICAL body bounds `[53.53, 19.74, 71.22]` on all four
+trials including the baseline. A plus-or-minus-2.0 swing changing nothing to two
+decimals means the constraint almost certainly never reached the mesh — not that
+the slider does nothing. **Reported as an unusable instrument rather than as a
+finding**, and the zero dirty packages afterwards corroborate that nothing was
+written. The body is still the female medium template and that is Ryan's
+one-slider fix, not a mystery.
+
+### THE THROUGH-LINE
+
+Six findings tonight. **Five were tools reporting success while doing nothing** —
+an ignored environment variable, a detach that left no process, a rotation never
+read back, a save that wrote no bytes, and a shim that would have disabled the
+assertions it was standing in for. Not one was caught by a gate. Every one was
+caught by asking a DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION: the log line instead of the
+environment, the process table instead of the exit code, the control rotation
+instead of another frame, the filesystem instead of the editor, and — for the
+shim — writing the test before trusting the substitute.

+## R-HERO — MAKING A METAHUMAN THE PLAYABLE CHARACTER (2026-08-16)
+
+Status: **PROVEN** for everything below the line marked NOT OWNED BY THIS
+RECIPE. Verified in PIE on a fresh editor and photographed:
+`_verify/20260816_hero_press_play_FIXED.png`.
+
+### WHAT THIS BUILDS
+
+    /Game/Hero/MHC_AlpineHero          AUTHORED, tracked, Ryan's sculpt
+    /Game/Hero/Generated/SKM_HeroBody  derived, gitignored
+    /Game/Hero/Generated/SKM_HeroFace  derived, gitignored
+    /Game/Hero/Generated/SM_HeroHead_TRELLIS  derived, gitignored
+
+### THE STEPS
+
+1. **`python scripts/build_hero_assets.py --go`** — duplicates the MetaHuman
+   preview meshes into real packages and resolves their materials. Idempotent;
+   a second run reports "already present, refreshed materials only".
+2. **Point `recipes/character.json` at them.** `assets.skeletal_mesh` takes the
+   BODY, and the new `assets.face_mesh` takes the FACE. `face_mesh` is optional
+   and its absence leaves the character exactly as it was.
+3. **`python scripts/apply_character_recipe.py --ini-only`**, then RESTART the
+   editor. Config UPROPERTYs are read at class load; the tool says so itself.
+4. **`python scripts/find_hero_spawn.py --near-cm "X,Y"`** to choose ground
+   that is clear of trunks, then add it as a NAMED CAMERA in the world recipe
+   and set `spawn.from_camera` to it.
+5. **`python scripts/place_player_start.py --go`**, then CHECK THE ARTEFACT —
+   the package it names must show as modified in `git status`.
+6. **Verify in PIE**, never in the editor world (see REJECTED).
+
+### VALUES THAT WORK
+
+    movement.profile            climb          (70 deg walkable floor)
+    capsule                     34 / 88 cm
+    camera.arm_length_cm        400.0
+    camera.probe_size_cm        4.0            probe stays ENABLED
+    camera.socket_offset_z_cm   70.0
+    PlayerStart pitch           -10.0          NOT positive; see REJECTED
+    spawn clearance             15.3 m to nearest trunk, 3.4 deg slope
+
+### A CHARACTER WITH TWO MESHES
+
+`ACharacter` owns one Mesh (`Character.h:352`). A MetaHuman is a body
+(`metahuman_base_skel`, 342 bones) plus a face (`Face_Archetype_Skeleton`, 875).
+`ALandscapeLabCharacter` therefore carries a `FaceMesh` component created
+UNCONDITIONALLY in the constructor — `CreateDefaultSubobject` runs at CDO
+construction, long before config is read — and given the body as its LEADER POSE
+component in `ApplyConfiguredAssets`. One pose, one authority.
+
+**`ABP_Unarmed` DRIVES THE METAHUMAN BODY.** The AnimBP targets `SK_Mannequin`
+at 161 bones, `metahuman_base_skel` has 342, and BOTH skeletons'
+`compatible_skeletons` arrays are EMPTY. It works anyway — the frames show a
+natural standing pose, not a T-pose. **Recorded as MEASURED, NOT UNDERSTOOD.** Do
+not read this as a licence to treat the two skeletons as interchangeable
+generally.
+
+### NOT OWNED BY THIS RECIPE — and it is visible in every frame
+
+**THE HERO IS UNTEXTURED WHITE, BY CONSTRUCTION.** MetaHuman's Assemble is not
+reflected in Python — there is no unpack and no build anywhere in the 5.8 stub —
+and the skin lives in parameter OVERRIDES on a dynamic material instance whose
+getter hard-refuses that type (see REJECTED). **The fix is one click and it is
+Ryan's: Assemble, in the MetaHuman panel.** Then repoint the recipe at the
+assembled meshes and re-run step 3.
+
+The BODY is also still the female medium template, and the FACE is MetaHuman's
+default rather than the man in `hero/reference/hero_face_bald_frontal.jpg`.

+## R-HERO REJECTED
+
+**Verifying the character by spawning it in the EDITOR world.** SYMPTOM: both
+meshes read `null` and `GetResolvedSpec` returns empty strings, which looks
+exactly like a broken config. CORRECT: verify in PIE. The config is applied in
+`PostInitializeComponents` and input is bound in `BeginPlay`, and an
+editor-world spawn is not a fair test of either. REFERENCE: measured
+2026-08-16 — identical config read `null` in the editor and resolved fully in
+PIE minutes later.
+
+**`unreal.Rotator(0.0, YAW, 0.0)` to set a spawn's yaw.** SYMPTOM: the actor's
+rotation reads `(roll 180, pitch 45, yaw 180)` and the third-person camera sits
+BELOW the player looking up. CORRECT: `Rotator(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)` — pitch is
+the second argument, so this sets PITCH, and the engine normalises pitch 135 to
+that triple. The PlayerController inherits the PlayerStart's rotation and the
+boom follows it. REFERENCE: `PythonStub:66750`; the same casualty is recorded
+in CLAUDE.md from 2026-08-12 and recurred here in a committed tool.
+
+**Reading back only LOCATION after placing an actor.** SYMPTOM: "drift 0.000 cm"
+and exit 0 over a scrambled rotation, indefinitely. CORRECT: read back every
+field that was written. A value that is never read back is a value nothing
+defends.
+
+**`EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)` after a Python
+actor edit.** SYMPTOM: returns **True** and writes NOTHING; every subsequent
+read-back agrees with the change because every read-back is reading editor
+memory. CORRECT: reach the actor's own package with `get_package()` and
+`save_packages([pkg], False)`, and PRINT THE PACKAGE NAME so the caller can
+check its mtime and `git status`. A Python actor edit does not reliably flag
+the external actor package dirty. REFERENCE: measured 2026-08-16 — no file
+under `__ExternalActors__` changed in ninety minutes while the editor reported
+the actor at its new location throughout.
+
+**Disabling the spring arm's collision probe to stop it collapsing.** SYMPTOM:
+the camera ends up INSIDE the canopy, which is worse than the close-up it was
+meant to cure. CORRECT: keep the probe enabled and shrink it
+(`probe_size_cm` 4.0), and fix the SPAWN and the PITCH, which are the actual
+causes. REFERENCE: both failures photographed —
+`_verify/20260816_hero_pie_forestfloor.png` is the collapse.

+**Placing a spawn by tracing ground alone.** SYMPTOM: the player begins inside a
+stand of trees and the camera has nowhere to go. CORRECT:
+`scripts/find_hero_spawn.py` — 219,659 trunk positions in a KD-tree, and ground
+that is both clear and walkable. Rank by nearness to a chosen point, NOT by
+clearance alone: maximum clearance returns ground 1349 m from any tree, which is
+above the treeline.

+texture parameter.

+frames that all say something is wrong and none that say what. CORRECT: ask the

+was correct all along and the camera was 1 m away. REFERENCE: retracted in
