+## R-TRELLIS — IMAGE TO 3D HEAD ON A BLACKWELL GPU (2026-08-16)
+
+Status: **PROVEN** — 472,734 vertices, 945,456 faces, watertight, 64 s, from
+`hero/reference/hero_face_bald_headcrop.png`. Views:
+`hero/generated/hero_head_views.png`.
+
+### THE ENVIRONMENT, AND WHY IT DEVIATES
+
+TRELLIS installs PyTorch 2.4.0+cu118, which has **no sm_120 support at all**, so
+the documented path cannot work on an RTX 5080. Required deviation:
+
+    WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04     NOT 26.04 -- see REJECTED
+    CUDA toolkit          12.8.93   (wsl-ubuntu repo, no display driver)
+    conda env python      3.11      NOT 3.12 -- distutils
+    torch                 2.11.0+cu128, capability (12, 0), sm_120 in arch list
+    xformers              0.0.35, installed --no-deps
+    spconv                spconv-cu126
+    kaolin                NOT INSTALLED -- shim, see R-HERO's sibling note
+
+### THE GATE, WHICH IS NOT A VERSION STRING
+
+`torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` must read `(12, 0)` AND `sm_120` must
+appear in `torch.cuda.get_arch_list()` AND a real matmul and a real reduction
+must agree with a CPU reference. A build lacking sm_120 kernels can still report
+`(12, 0)` and fail at launch. `scripts/wsl_exec.sh` + the gate script.
+
+### RUNNING IT
+
+    ATTN_BACKEND=xformers      NOT sdpa -- see REJECTED
+    SPCONV_ALGO=native
+    XFORMERS_DISABLED=1        routes DINOv2 away from xformers only
+
+Formats `["mesh"]` only. Geometry is the deliverable; the gaussian rasterizers
+(`diffoctreerast`, `mip-splatting`) serve radiance-field rendering and texture
+baking and were never installed.
+
+## R-TRELLIS REJECTED
+
+**`wsl --install -d Ubuntu` and taking what you get.** SYMPTOM: Ubuntu 26.04,
+whose only Python is 3.14.3 with NO `python3.11` or `python3.12` package
+available at all. CORRECT: `-d Ubuntu-24.04` explicitly. REFERENCE: measured by
+`apt-cache policy`, which returns nothing for both. NOTE the assumption that was
+FALSE and must not be re-derived: NVIDIA **does** publish an `ubuntu2604` CUDA
+repo. The repo was never the problem; the Python floor was.
+
+**`ATTN_BACKEND=sdpa`.** SYMPTOM: the run prints `[SPARSE] Backend: spconv,
+Attention: flash_attn` while the environment says `sdpa`, and flash-attn is not
+installed. CORRECT: `xformers`. `trellis/modules/sparse/__init__.py` accepts
+ONLY `xformers` or `flash_attn` and silently keeps its default otherwise, while
+the DENSE attention module does accept `sdpa` — the same variable honoured by
+one reader and dropped by another.
+
+**Leaving xformers enabled for DINOv2 on Blackwell.** SYMPTOM:
+`NotImplementedError: No operator found for memory_efficient_attention_forward`,
+with `fa3F` and `cutlassF-pt` both requiring capability <= (9, 0) and `fa2F`
+supporting only fp16/bf16. CORRECT: `XFORMERS_DISABLED=1`, read at
+`dinov2/layers/attention.py:21`. It does not affect TRELLIS's own sparse
+attention, which imports xformers directly.
+
+**`pip install xformers` without `--no-deps`.** SYMPTOM: the resolver is free to
+replace the torch that passed the sm_120 gate, and nothing announces it.
+CORRECT: `--no-deps`, then RE-VERIFY torch's version, capability and a live
+kernel afterwards.
+
+**Installing kaolin to satisfy FlexiCubes.** SYMPTOM: a long source build with
+no wheel for torch 2.11+cu128. CORRECT: the library path imports exactly one
+symbol, `check_tensor`, used in six `throw=False` assertions; everything else is
+under `examples/`. Implement it — `scripts/trellis/kaolin_check_tensor_shim.py`
+— and NEVER as `return True`, which would satisfy the import while disabling
+every assertion it stands for.
+
+**Running `setup.sh` whole.** SYMPTOM: one failure and no information about
+which of seven extensions caused it. CORRECT: piecewise, with a marker per
+stage. Four separate blockers were each attributable this way.

+## 2026-08-15 — THE CORE DATA. MetaHuman WORKS, AND THE DESCRIPTOR WAS LYING.
+
+**Resolved by Ryan**, after four failed attempts by me. `MetaHumanCharacter`
+is ENABLED, the editor loads normally (592 CPU-s, 10.78 GB), and
+`verify_gameplay_plugin` returns exit 0 with our own classes still reflected.
+
+### THE CAUSE, AND IT IS EXACT
+
+The editor's Plugins UI told Ryan it **needed the Core Data first**. Enabling
+that alongside added **`MetaHumanCoreTech`** to `.uproject`. Verified:
+
+    MetaHumanCharacter.uplugin declares 20 plugin dependencies.
+    MetaHumanCoreTech IS NOT ONE OF THEM.
+    It does not start without it.
+
+Every route I tried enabled exactly what the descriptor **DECLARES** — the
+`.uplugin` dependency array, then the `.uproject` array. Both faithfully
+reproduced an **incomplete declaration**, and the editor blocked at module
+load with no CPU, no dialog and no log line, four times.
+
+**A plugin descriptor is a DERIVED RECORD.** It states what somebody wrote
+down about the plugin's needs, not what the plugin needs. This project has a
+non-negotiable for exactly this class (15) and three recorded instances of
+its cousin (17: a config records what was overridden, never what is in
+effect). This is a fourth, in a file nobody thought of as a config: **an
+`.uplugin`'s `Plugins` array is a claim, and Epic's own claim was wrong.**
+
+### THE ANSWER WAS IN THE DOCUMENT RYAN GAVE ME, AND I SKIPPED IT
+
+His Gemini plan, step 1, reads verbatim:
+
+> "navigate to Edit → Plugins, enable the MetaHuman Creator plugin, **and
+> ensure the Core Data is active**."
+
+I reviewed that plan critically and at length. I caught the inverted
+`ForcedLOD` advice, flagged the 8K memory risk, and correctly identified that
+the clothing pipeline was the bulk of the work. **And I read straight past
+the one clause that was load-bearing**, because it was a short phrase in a
+step I had already judged to be the easy part.
+
+**The failure is in where I aimed the scepticism.** I audited the claims the
+plan made about things I already knew about (LODs, texture budgets) and gave
+no attention at all to a bare instruction about a thing I did not know about.
+Prior familiarity decided what got checked, which is precisely backwards —
+the unfamiliar clause is the one carrying information I do not have.
+
+### WHAT THE FOUR FAILED ATTEMPTS WERE ACTUALLY WORTH
+
+Not nothing, and this matters for how the record reads. Each eliminated a
+real candidate by measurement rather than by argument: memory (2.4 GB against
+a 223 GB limit, CPU idle), missing binaries (7 DLLs present), our own C++
+(identical editor minus one line loads fine), a modal (no dialog window
+exists, twice enumerated), antivirus (engine folder excluded, no change), and
+a crash (the exit was `ConsoleCtrl`, i.e. Ryan closing the console).
+
+**The diagnosis was sound and the hypothesis space was wrong.** Every
+candidate I generated was about the ENVIRONMENT — memory, security, our code.
+None was about the plugin's own declaration being incomplete, because I had
+read that declaration and treated it as ground truth. **I verified the
+descriptor's contents and never questioned its completeness.**
+
+### AND I RETRACTED A CORRECT INSTINCT ON THE WAY
+
+The second entry claimed a modal was the cause; the third retracted it as
+unsupported. The retraction was RIGHT — there was no modal, and the log line
+I built it on was Ryan's own click. But note what the retraction cost: it
+left "root cause not established", which is honest and inert. The thing that
+actually moved this was Ryan reading a UI message I never saw.
+
+**Operationally: when a headless route fails four times, the attended route
+is not a fallback, it is the diagnostic.** The Plugins UI knew the answer the
+whole time and said so in one sentence. Nothing I could measure from outside
+the process would have produced "you need the Core Data".
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**Enable a plugin the way the editor enables it, at least once, before
+encoding it anywhere.** The descriptor route is for REPRODUCING an
+enablement that is already known to work — never for discovering one. R-GAMEPLAY's
+"attended for the first activation, reproducible after" stands, now with a
+second and better mechanism behind it than the modal I guessed at.
+
+**OWED:** `MetaHumanCharacter` and `MetaHumanCoreTech` are in `.uproject`,
+not in `LandscapeLabGameplay.uplugin` where ruling 2 wants them. Now that
+BOTH names are known, the descriptor route should work — moving them is the
+tidy end state and the test of that claim. **Not done tonight:** MetaHuman
+finally works, and another restart to prove a point about attribution is not
+worth risking it.

    Enabling a Beta plugin raises a confirmation modal. Through the Plugins UI a
    human answers it. Through a .uplugin descriptor it is raised during STARTUP
    with nobody to answer it, and it blocks the game thread -- which is the same
    thread that services Python remote execution. So the editor sat on the splash
    screen indefinitely and could not report why, because the thing that would
    have reported it was the thing being blocked.
    
    EVERY MEASUREMENT WAS CORRECT AND NONE OF THEM COULD REACH THE CAUSE. 0.02
    CPU-s per wall-s, no DDC growth, no log lines, still SplashScreenClass -- all

+## 2026-08-15 — CORRECTION: THE METAHUMAN STALL **IS** ROOT-CAUSED. IT WAS A MODAL.
+
+The entry above records the `MetaHumanCharacter` startup stall as **root
+cause NOT established**. That was honest when written and it is now **wrong**.
+Corrected here rather than edited there, so the state of knowledge at the time
+survives.
+
+**THE CAUSE, from the editor's own log**, after Ryan enabled the plugin
+through the Plugins UI:
+
+    Message dialog closed, result: Yes, title: Message, text:
+    Plugin 'MetaHuman Creator' is a beta version. Epic recommends using
+    caution when shipping projects with beta plugins... Are you sure you
+    want to enable the plugin?
+
+**Enabling a Beta plugin raises a confirmation modal.** Via the Plugins UI a
+human answers it. Via a `.uplugin` descriptor the modal is raised during
+STARTUP, with nobody to answer it — and it blocks the game thread, which is
+the same thread that services Python remote execution. So the editor sat on
+the splash screen indefinitely and could not report why, because the thing
+that would have reported it was the thing being blocked.
+
+**Every measurement in the entry above was correct and none of them could
+reach the cause.** 0.02 CPU-s per wall-s, no DDC growth, no log lines, still
+`SplashScreenClass` — all true, all consistent with a modal, and all equally
+consistent with three other explanations. The instruments correctly said
+*"stopped, and not for want of memory"*; they could not say *"waiting for a
+click"*.
+
+**What actually resolved it was a DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION** — not more
+instrumentation of the hung process, but the log of the SUCCESSFUL attended
+run, which recorded the question being asked and answered. Non-negotiable 0
+again, and worth noting the winning move was to change the experiment rather
+than sharpen the measurement.
+
+### THE PREDICTION WAS RIGHT AND WAS STILL LABELLED A GUESS, WHICH WAS CORRECT
+
+The earlier entry named "a first-run dialog that never painted" as an
+untested hypothesis, and recommended the attended route on those grounds. It
+was right. **It was still correct to label it a hypothesis**: it was one of
+two candidates, the other (`EOSShared` blocking on a network call) was
+equally consistent with the evidence, and acting on a guess dressed as a
+finding is how this project gets bad recipes. The guess earned the next
+experiment; it did not earn the entry.
+
+### CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RULE
+
+R-GAMEPLAY's "attended for the FIRST activation, reproducible for every one
+after" **stands, and now has a mechanism rather than a superstition**: the
+first activation is the one that asks. Once acknowledged, the descriptor
+route should be usable — **UNVERIFIED**, and the way to verify it is to move
+the entry back into `LandscapeLabGameplay.uplugin` and confirm a clean cold
+boot.
+
+### AND THE `.uproject` IS NO LONGER BYTE-IDENTICAL
+
+The Plugins UI wrote `MetaHumanCharacter` into `LandscapeLab.uproject`. This
+project had kept that file untouched through the C++ conversion and through
+two plugins, on ruling 2's reasoning that enablement belongs beside the code
+that needs it.
+
+**This is not a violation of standing rule 4** — that rule forbids ME editing
+`.uproject` on disk; the editor writing it through its own UI at Ryan's

+
+### THE MEASUREMENTS THAT SAID "HUNG" RATHER THAN "SLOW"
+
+This project already records that a flat CPU trace is NOT evidence of a hang
+during shader compilation, because that work happens in `ShaderCompileWorker`
+CHILD processes. So the reading was taken across four instruments at once:
+
+    working set        2.41 GB, flat over 2 minutes
+    editor CPU         0.02 CPU-s per wall-s
+    DDC growth         0.0 MB in 120 s
+    ShaderCompileWorker  0 processes
+    log                 11 minutes with no new line
+    window class        SplashScreenClass — still on the splash
+
+**No single one of those is conclusive and together they are.** DDC growth is
+the instrument that closes it: shader compilation with no CPU in the parent
+still writes to disk, and nothing was being written.
+
+**The window-class tell was used as recorded and worked.**
+`MainWindowTitle` returned *"Unreal Editor - LandscapeLab"* — identical to a
+loaded editor. Only `GetClassName` distinguishes `SplashScreenClass` from
+`UnrealWindow`.
+
+### WHAT IT WAS NOT
+
+**Not memory, and Ryan asked directly.** 2.41 GB working set against a
+223 GB commit limit, with the CPU IDLE. Memory starvation looks like heavy
+paging and pegged CPU and disk; this was a process waiting on something and
+doing nothing. **The page file needed no change** — and the temptation to
+raise it "just in case" would have spent a reboot to fix a problem that did
+not exist.
+
+**Not missing binaries.** `MetaHumanCharacter` ships **7 prebuilt DLLs** in
+this installed engine, so nothing needed compiling.
+
+**Not our C++.** The same editor, relaunched with only the `.uplugin` line
+removed, loaded normally — **993 CPU-s in 4 minutes, 10.24 GB** — and
+`verify_gameplay_plugin` returns exit 0 with every class reflected.
+
+### WHAT IS UNKNOWN, STATED PLAINLY
+
+**There are ZERO `MetaHuman` lines in the 105 KB log.** The plugin's modules
+never logged anything, so the stall is somewhere in plugin or module
+initialisation BEFORE they got that far — and nothing in the log names it.
+The last entries are a Turnkey device detection completing and DDC
+maintenance finishing, both normal.
+
+**No root cause. Standing rule 10:** this is recorded as an unexplained
+failure, not as a diagnosis. Candidates not tested — a first-run dialog that
+never painted, and `MetaHumanSDK`'s `EOSShared` dependency blocking on a
+network call — are HYPOTHESES and are labelled as such.
+
+### THE ROUTE THAT WAS NOT TRIED, AND SHOULD BE FIRST NEXT TIME
+
+**Enable it through the editor's own Plugins UI**, not through a `.uplugin`
+dependency. The descriptor route is right for a headless, reproducible,
+recipe-driven enable — and it is exactly wrong for a **Beta plugin's first
+activation**, because anything that wants a click has no one to click it, and
+a dialog blocking the game thread also blocks the only channel that could
+report it. That is the same shape as the Save Content modal earlier the same
+day.
+
+**The general rule worth carrying: prefer the attended route for the FIRST

+## R-GAMEPLAY AMENDED 2026-08-15 — DECIDING WHETHER AN EDITOR IS SLOW OR HUNG
+
+Added after enabling `MetaHumanCharacter` stalled the editor on startup for
+11 minutes. Narrative: LESSONS 2026-08-15.
+
+### THE FOUR-INSTRUMENT READING
+
+No single instrument decides this. Take all of them:
+
+    working set        flat over 2 min          -> suggestive only
+    editor CPU         < 0.1 CPU-s per wall-s   -> suggestive only
+    DDC growth         0 MB over 2 min          -> DECISIVE
+    ShaderCompileWorker count                   -> context
+    log mtime          minutes since last line  -> DECISIVE
+    window CLASS       SplashScreenClass        -> still starting
+
+**DDC growth is the one that closes it.** Shader compilation shows a flat
+parent CPU by construction — the work is in child processes — but it still
+writes to disk. No CPU AND no DDC growth AND no new log line is hung.
+
+**`MainWindowTitle` is not a tell.** It reads *"Unreal Editor - <project>"*
+on the SPLASH SCREEN, identical to a loaded editor. Use `GetClassName`:
+`SplashScreenClass` vs `UnrealWindow`.
+
+## R-GAMEPLAY REJECTED — additions
+
+**Enabling a BETA plugin for the FIRST time through a `.uplugin` dependency.**
+SYMPTOM: the editor never finishes starting; 2.41 GB working set, 0.02 CPU-s
+per wall-s, no DDC growth, and **zero lines from the plugin in a 105 KB log**.
+CORRECT: enable a first activation through the editor's **Plugins UI**, where
+a prompt has someone to answer it; use the descriptor route for every
+activation after that, once it is known not to ask anything. **A dialog
+blocking the game thread also blocks the only channel that could report it** —
+the same shape as the Save Content modal. REFERENCE: root cause NOT
+established; log preserved at
+`_verify/20260815_metahuman_enable_stall.log`.
+
+**Raising the page file because an editor hung.** SYMPTOM: a plausible fix
+that costs a reboot and changes nothing. CORRECT: memory starvation shows
+heavy paging and PEGGED CPU and disk. A hang at **2.41 GB against a 223 GB
+commit limit with the CPU idle** is a process waiting on something, and no
+amount of page file addresses a blocking wait.
+
+**Assuming a plugin that fails to load must need compiling.** SYMPTOM: time
+spent on a build that was never required. CORRECT: check for the DLLs first —
+`MetaHumanCharacter` ships **7 prebuilt binaries** in an installed 5.8 engine.

    walk003: 1000.1 m of 1000 requested, no stall, no fall. Artefact
    _verify/20260815_unit5_walk_walk003.md, recipe R-WALKTEST.
    
    The character resolves fully at spawn -- SKM_Manny_Simple, ABP_Unarmed_C,
    IMC_LandscapeLabDefault, 3 of 3 input actions -- and walks at exactly
    600 cm/s, the configured MaxWalkSpeed, which is the cheapest possible proof
    that the recipe reached the engine.
    
    RYAN RULED: GIVE IT THE ABILITY TO CLIMB
    
    movement.profile moved "walk" -> "climb". It is still a KEY into
    terrain_erosion.MOVEMENT_PROFILES (70 deg, described there as "scalable
    faces; a design choice, not an engine one"), the recipe still carries no
    angle, and apply_character_recipe derives CfgWalkableFloorAngleDeg. Ruling 19
    holds: declared once, derived twice.
    
    SetWalkableFloorAngle, never WalkableFloorAngle = . The setter also
    recomputes WalkableFloorZ, which is the value the floor test actually reads;
    assigning the angle alone lands a correct-looking number that nothing
    consults. The engine sets the pair through SetWalkableFloorZ at
    CharacterMovementComponent.cpp:682 for the same reason.
    
    THE TWO EARLIER STALLS WERE TERRAIN, AND THE TERRAIN WAS RIGHT
    
    walk001 stopped at 97.1 m, walk002 at 240.5 m. Diagnosed offline against the
    heightmap after calibrating the indexing on a measured ground truth --
    h[py,px] at the spawn XY reads 28,539.5 cm against a collision trace's
    28,540.1, agreeing to 0.6 cm, which is what makes the rest trustworthy.
    
        walk001 stop: slope 52.66 deg, next metre rises  74 cm
        walk002 stop: slope 64.39 deg, next metre rises 320 cm
    
    Both are walls, not slopes: past the 44.765 deg walkable floor and past the
    45 cm step height at once. A straight-line walker with no steering stops at
    the first such feature and stays there -- a property of the test, not of the
    world. And a straight kilometre is not available anywhere from that spawn at
    the walking limit; the best clear run is 934 m.
    
    FOUR DEFECTS IN THE INSTRUMENT, WHICH IS MOST OF WHAT THIS COMMIT LEARNED
    
    1. A COMPLETED WALK REPORTED AS "NO MARKER". The stop payload returned 1621
       samples inline and exceeded the remote-exec deserialization limit -- the
       same class as save_level's 418 KB reply. A finished trace was nearly
       thrown away. The trace now goes to a FILE before the reply, the tool
       force-tears-down and reads off disk when a reply is lost, and --from-log
       makes the analysis reachable without the code path that failed.
    
    2. "FELL THROUGH: YES" ON A CLEAN WALK. The test asked whether Z had dropped
       5,000 cm below the spawn. It had, by 10,075 cm, because the character
       walked DOWN A MOUNTAINSIDE -- 100 m of descent over 1 km. On real terrain
       descending is the job. Replaced with a geometric test: over one sample the
       ground can drop at most tan(walkable) x horizontal distance moved.
       Re-measured on the same trace, the worst excess is 0.0 cm.
    
    3. A COULD-NOT-LOOK PRINTED AS A MEASUREMENT, INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT WRITTEN
       TO ENFORCE THAT RULE. is_falling logged None on all 645 samples and the
       analysis reported "falling samples 0.0%". ACharacter has no
       get_character_movement() in Python; it raises and the exception was
       swallowed. It is on Pawn.get_movement_component() -- is_falling lives on
       NavMovementComponent, PythonStub 506206. An all-None column now prints
       COULD NOT READ.
    
    4. A POWERSHELL REGEX DOUBLE-ENCODED THE SCRIPT. Get-Content with no
       -Encoding read UTF-8 as Windows-1252, Set-Content -Encoding utf8 wrote the
       mojibake back with a BOM, and Python refused to parse its own file.
       Standing rule 3's mechanism in a different container: a shell round trip
       over text whose encoding was never declared has no failure mode that
       announces itself. Use Edit on source.
    
    STATED NARROWLY: this is a straight line on a declared heading, NOT the
    inter-massif corridor, which still has no spatial definition in this repo.
    And is_falling was unreadable for this run, so the fall verdict rests on the
    geometric test alone rather than on two representations.

+## 2026-08-15 — THE PLAYER WALKS A KILOMETRE, AND FOUR OF THE FIVE FAILURES WERE IN THE INSTRUMENT
+
+`PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 5's first acceptance clause is met. `walk003`:
+**1000.1 m of 1000 requested, no stall, no fall**, artefact
+`_verify/20260815_unit5_walk_walk003.md`.
+
+The character resolves fully at spawn — `SKM_Manny_Simple`, `ABP_Unarmed_C`,
+`IMC_LandscapeLabDefault`, 3 of 3 input actions — and walks at exactly
+**600 cm/s**, the configured `MaxWalkSpeed`, which is the cheapest possible
+proof that the recipe reached the engine.
+
+### DRIVING A PAWN NEEDS A TICK CALLBACK, NOT A LOOP
+
+`AddMovementInput` is consumed by ONE tick, and a remote-exec payload BLOCKS
+the game thread — so a Python loop gives the character input and never lets it
+move. `unreal.register_slate_post_tick_callback` (PythonStub 708181) runs in
+the engine's own loop; the script only starts, polls and stops it. State lives
+in a module-level global because the callback outlives the payload that made
+it, and is torn down explicitly for the same reason.
+
+### THE FIRST TWO WALKS STOPPED DEAD, AND THE TERRAIN WAS RIGHT BOTH TIMES
+
+    walk001  heading 135  stopped at  97.1 m
+    walk002  heading  72  stopped at 240.5 m
+
+Diagnosed offline against the heightmap, after calibrating the indexing on a
+measured ground truth — `h[py,px]` at the spawn XY reads **28,539.5 cm**
+against a collision trace's **28,540.1**, agreeing to 0.6 cm, which is what
+makes the rest of the analysis trustworthy.
+
+    walk001 stop: slope 52.66 deg, next metre rises 74 cm
+    walk002 stop: slope 64.39 deg, next metre rises 320 cm
+
+Both are **walls, not slopes**: past the 44.765 deg walkable floor and past
+the 45 cm step height simultaneously. The character was standing correctly
+on the ground and could neither walk up nor step up. **A straight-line walker
+with no steering stops at the first such feature and stays there** — which is
+a property of the test, not of the world.
+
+**And a straight kilometre is not available anywhere from that spawn.** A
+heading sweep found the best clear run at **934 m** before the 44.765 deg
+limit is exceeded. Ryan then ruled: give the character the ability to climb.
+
+### THE CLIMB RULING, AND WHY IT IS STILL "DECLARED ONCE"
+
+`recipes/character.json` → `movement.profile` moved `"walk"` → `"climb"`,
+which is a KEY into `terrain_erosion.MOVEMENT_PROFILES` (70 deg, described
+there as *"scalable faces; a design choice, not an engine one"*). The recipe
+still carries **no angle**; `apply_character_recipe` derives it and writes
+`CfgWalkableFloorAngleDeg` into the ini, which the character applies with
+`SetWalkableFloorAngle`.
+
+**`SetWalkableFloorAngle`, not `WalkableFloorAngle =`** — the setter also
+recomputes `WalkableFloorZ`, which is the value the floor test actually
+reads. Assigning the angle alone lands a correct-looking number that nothing
+consults. The engine sets the pair through `SetWalkableFloorZ` at
+`CharacterMovementComponent.cpp:682` for exactly this reason.
+
+At 70 deg the same sweep, re-run at **1 m sampling** rather than 2 m, gives
+many headings clear to the full 1200 m. The 2 m sweep had missed a 1 m-wide
+ledge — **a sweep coarser than the map's own resolution can step over the
+feature it is looking for.**
+
+### AND THEN THE INSTRUMENT FAILED FOUR TIMES, WHICH IS THE REST OF THIS ENTRY
+
+**1. A COMPLETED WALK REPORTED AS "NO MARKER".** The stop payload returned
+1621 samples inline and the reply exceeded the remote-exec deserialization
+limit — the same class as `save_level`'s 418 KB reply. A finished trace was
+nearly thrown away. Fixed by writing the trace to a FILE before replying, and
+by degrading rather than discarding when a reply is lost: the tool now
+force-tears-down and reads the trace off disk. `--from-log` exists so the
+analysis is reachable without the code path that failed.
+
+**2. "FELL THROUGH: YES" ON A CLEAN WALK.** The fall test asked whether Z had
+dropped more than 5,000 cm below the spawn. It had — by 10,075 cm — because
+the character walked **down a mountainside**, 100 m of descent over 1 km.
+**On real terrain, descending is the job.** Replaced with a geometric test:
+over one sample the ground can drop at most `tan(walkable) × horizontal
+distance moved`; sustained excess beyond that is falling rather than walking.
+Re-measured, the worst excess is **0.0 cm** — every centimetre of that
+descent is explainable by walking.
+
+**3. A COULD-NOT-LOOK PRINTED AS A MEASUREMENT, IN MY OWN TOOL.**
+`is_falling` logged `None` on all 645 samples and the analysis reported
+**"falling samples 0.0%"**. `ACharacter` has no `get_character_movement()` in
+Python; it raises, and the exception was swallowed. `is_falling` lives on
+`NavMovementComponent` (PythonStub 506206), reached via
+`Pawn.get_movement_component()`. Now the accessor is correct, the reason is
+recorded on first failure, and an all-`None` column prints **COULD NOT READ**
+rather than a percentage. This is non-negotiable 6 — inside the instrument
+written to enforce it.
+
+**4. A POWERSHELL REGEX DOUBLE-ENCODED THE SOURCE FILE.** `Get-Content` with
+no `-Encoding` read UTF-8 as Windows-1252, `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` wrote
+the mojibake back and added a BOM, and Python then refused to parse its own
+script. Repaired by inverting the transform. **This is standing rule 3's
+mechanism in a different container:** the rule sends commit messages through
+a file because a shell round trip over text it was never told the encoding of
+has no failure mode that announces itself. Editing source with a PowerShell
+regex is the same hazard, and `Edit` does not have it.
+
+### WHAT THE WALK PROVES, STATED NARROWLY
+
+The collision surface supports the character over 1 km of real varied terrain
+under genuine `CharacterMovementComponent` floor checks. It is a **straight
+line on a declared heading**, NOT the inter-massif corridor — that corridor
+still has no spatial definition anywhere in this repo. And `is_falling` was
+unreadable for this run, so the fall verdict rests on the geometric test
+alone rather than on two representations.

+## R-WALKTEST — DRIVING THE PLAYER AND JUDGING THE RESULT (2026-08-15)
+
+**Status: PROVEN.** `scripts/walk_character.py`. Artefact
+`_verify/20260815_unit5_walk_walk003.md`: **1000.1 m, no stall, no fall.**
+Narrative: LESSONS 2026-08-15.
+
+### THE PROCEDURE
+
+1. PIE, settle 30 s.
+2. `unreal.register_slate_post_tick_callback` drives the pawn with
+   `add_movement_input(dir, 1.0, force=True)` every tick and samples 4x/s.
+   **A Python loop cannot do this** — a payload blocks the game thread, so the
+   character receives input and never ticks.
+3. Poll a SUMMARY only. Never the trace.
+4. Stop: unregister, write the trace to
+   `Saved/ll_walk_log.json`, delete the global.
+5. End PIE and CONFIRM.
+
+### VALUES THAT WORK
+
+    sample rate        4 /s          settle            30 s
+    stall bar          3.0 s under 20 cm/s
+    fall bar           1.0 s of descent beyond tan(walkable) x distance
+                       + 60 cm per-sample margin
+    walkable           70 deg (profile "climb")
+
+### CHOOSING A HEADING — SWEEP AT THE MAP'S OWN RESOLUTION
+
+A straight kilometre is NOT available from the `forest_floor` spawn at the
+44.765 deg walking limit; the best clear run is **934 m**. At 70 deg many
+headings clear 1200 m. **Sweep at 1 m, not 2 m** — the map is 1 m/vertex and
+a 2 m sweep steps over the 1 m ledges that stop the character.
+

+`PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 7, pulled ahead of the rest of unit 5 because unit 5

+`scripts/verify_gameplay_plugin.py`. Recipe **R-GAMEPLAY**.
+
+### THE PROJECT FILE IS STILL BYTE-IDENTICAL, AND THAT IS THE POINT
+
+Standing rule 4 forbids touching `LandscapeLab.uproject`, and
+`PluginManager.cpp:420-433` makes it unnecessary — a project plugin with
+`EnabledByDefault` is honoured with no `.uproject` entry at all. That is the
+same reasoning that kept the project file untouched through the 2026-08-12
+C++ conversion, and it held again here for three engine plugins.
+
+**And it is measurably better than the `.uproject` route**, which is the part
+worth carrying: the dependency list lives beside the code that needs it, so
+"why is GameplayStateTree on?" is answered by reading the plugin that wants
+it rather than by reading a project-wide array with no attribution.
+
+### THE DISCRIMINATING CHECK IS `GameplayStateTree`, NOT THE PLUGIN ITSELF
+
+Ruling 1 recorded that `StateTree` is enabled here and `GameplayStateTree` is
+**not** (`EnabledByDefault: false`), and that the second is the half carrying
+`StateTreeAIComponent`, `FStateTreeMoveToTask` and `FStateTreeRunEnvQueryTask`.
+
+So the cold-boot verifier does not just ask "is my plugin enabled" — it asks
+whether `GameplayStateTree` reads ENABLED. It does. **That is the one result
+that could only be true if the dependency list did work**, because nothing
+else in this project turns it on. Checking only the plugin's own state would
+have passed identically whether or not the dependencies were honoured.
+
+### AND THE CLASS CHECK IS A DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION, DELIBERATELY
+
+`get_enabled_plugin_names()` reads the plugin DESCRIPTOR. It does not prove
+the module's DLL loaded, and it does not prove UHT generated anything — a
+plugin can read "enabled" with a module that failed to load, and the editor
+carries on. So the verifier separately asks for `unreal.LandscapeLabCharacter`
+and its CDO, and for `apply_movement_spec` on it.
+
+**The function check is the one that would catch a stale binary.** A DLL from
+a previous build reflects the class perfectly and is missing the new
+function, and it reads exactly like a working module until something calls
+it. Non-negotiable 0, at the level of a build artefact.
+
+### THE BUILD REFUSED WHILE THE EDITOR WAS OPEN, AND THE ERROR IS EXACT
+
+    Unable to build while Live Coding is active. Exit the editor and game,
+    or press Ctrl+Alt+F11 if iterating on code in the editor or game
+
+Worth recording because the obvious reading — "it just needs the DLL
+unlocked" — suggests the wrong workaround. **Live Coding cannot add a NEW
+module**, only recompile existing ones, so `Ctrl+Alt+F11` is not an
+alternative here. A new module means a full build means a closed editor.
+
+### AND CLOSING THE EDITOR HAD ITS OWN GATE
+
+`get_dirty_content_packages()` reported **one** dirty package,
+`/Game/Materials/M_AutoLandscape` — the *old* 2017 world's material, nothing
+this session touched, dirty from before the session began.
+
+A quit with a dirty package raises a **Save Content** modal, which blocks the
+game thread and therefore blocks remote execution — **the only channel that
+could see or answer it.** This project has been bitten by that modal and by
+its sibling, the next-launch `Restore Packages` modal.
+
+So the check refused to quit on a non-zero count, and refuses equally on an
+UNREADABLE count: *an unreadable count is not a zero*. Ryan closed it from
+the UI and chose Don't Save, which is the right owner for that decision —
+it is his asset, and the on-disk copy was committed and unchanged, so the
+discarded thing was an unexplained in-memory divergence from a file git
+already held.
+
+**The general shape, and it is not really about modals:** a tool that needs a
+human action should say exactly which action and why, not perform a
+destructive approximation of it because a human is inconvenient to ask.

+**Status: PROVEN.** `LandscapeLab/Plugins/LandscapeLabGameplay`, built clean

+
+### THE PROCEDURE
+
+1. **A new PLUGIN, never a game module and never a `.uproject` edit.**
+   Standing rule 4 forbids the edit; `PluginManager.cpp:420-433` honours
+   `EnabledByDefault` on a project plugin with no `.uproject` entry at all.
+   The project file stays byte-identical.
+2. **Module `Type` must match when the code runs.** `LandscapeLabEditor` is
+   `"Editor"`. Gameplay classes are `"Runtime"` or they do not exist in a
+   cooked build — the one place they must.
+3. **Engine plugin dependencies go in THIS plugin's `Plugins` array**, not in
+   the project file (ruling 2). They then live beside the code that needs
+   them, so "why is X on?" is answerable by attribution.
+4. **CLOSE THE EDITOR.** A new module cannot be added by Live Coding.
+5. Build:
+
+       "C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat"
+         LandscapeLabEditor Win64 Development
+         -Project="<UE_PROJECT_ROOT>\LandscapeLab.uproject" -WaitMutex
+
+6. **Relaunch and verify on a COLD BOOT**, never from the `.uplugin`.
+
+### THE UFUNCTION CONVENTION, CARRIED FORWARD
+
+`void` + an explicit `bOutSuccess`, **never** `bool` with out-params: a
+`UFUNCTION` returning `bool` alongside out-params LOSES the bool in the
+Python binding — Python gets `(...outs) or None`, so the failure flag
+disappears exactly when it is needed. Established 2026-08-12; applied to
+`ApplyMovementSpec`.
+
+### WHAT THE COLD-BOOT CHECK MUST ASK, AND IN WHAT ORDER
+
+    1. is the plugin in get_enabled_plugin_names()
+    2. is GameplayStateTree in it        <- THE DISCRIMINATING ONE
+    3. is unreal.<Class> reflected, with a reachable CDO
+    4. is the UFUNCTION present on it
+
+## R-GAMEPLAY REJECTED
+
+**Verifying a plugin from its `.uplugin`.** SYMPTOM: a green check over a
+plugin that is not loaded. CORRECT: read `get_enabled_plugin_names()` on the
+running editor. REFERENCE: non-negotiable 17 — a config records what was
+overridden, never what is in effect. Three recorded instances in this project

    ﻿Unit 5 begins: the character declaration, and a gate that refused its own recipe
    
    PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 5's second acceptance clause -- "verify_walkable_profile
    proves the CMC CDO, recipes/character.json and MOVEMENT_PROFILES have not

    this is its declaration and the gate over it.
    
    recipes/character.json, scripts/verify_walkable_profile.py, recipe
    R-CHARACTER, schema contract in recipes/schema.md.
    
    THE SHAPE: THE RECIPE NAMES A PROFILE AND NEVER TYPES AN ANGLE
    
    "profile": "walk" is a KEY into terrain_erosion.MOVEMENT_PROFILES, which
    holds the engine's own 44.765083 degrees. The angle is derived at read time.
    Ruling 19: declared once, derived twice. The verifier REFUSES any movement.*
    key whose name contains "angle" or "slope", because a typed angle is a second
    copy and a second copy is a second thing to drift.
    
    Every other value was read from the 5.8 constructor on 2026-08-15, not
    remembered: max_walk_speed 600 (:694), max_step_height 45 (:689),
    jump_z_velocity 420 (:679), max_acceleration 2048 (:733), gravity_scale 1
    (:677), capsule 34/88 (Character.cpp:78). Written out in full rather than
    left implicit -- non-negotiable 17 says a config records overrides and never
    the state in effect, so a recipe listing only overrides describes nothing.
    
    THE RULING-19 GATE IS CHECKED BEFORE THE PACKAGES ARE WRITTEN
    
    navigation.agent_profile must not exceed world.primary_movement_mode. Drift
    upward is SILENT -- the navmesh grants paths onto ground the character slides
    off and nothing errors -- so it is gated here rather than at navmesh build
    time. The gate is one-directional, agent <= world primary, never equality:
    the player on foot walks 44.765 while the navmesh is built for the mount at
    35, and that asymmetry is intended. The player may go where the AI will not
    path.
    
    TWO DEFECTS, BOTH MINE, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE GATES
    
    1. THE VERIFIER REFUSED ITS OWN RECIPE, AND WAS RIGHT TO. The first
       character.json carried eight prose keys explaining itself, one of them
       named _profile_is_a_key_not_an_angle -- which contains "angle", so the
       no-typed-angle scan refused the file. The tempting fix was to exempt
       underscore-prefixed keys. That would have opened a hole in the gate to
       accommodate a pattern this project had ALREADY REJECTED: R-ALPINE8K
       REJECTED rules that a schema key holding prose is the "invent a key to get
       past the validator" antipattern. So the prose moved to RECIPES.md and the
       contract to schema.md, and the recipe became data. The gate stays whole.
    
    2. A PLAUSIBLE OBJECT ANSWERED AND IT WAS THE WRONG ONE. The live check
       reported capsule DRIFT -- engine 22/44 against a recipe saying 34/88 -- on
       a correct recipe. I had read CapsuleComponent's own CDO, which is the
       GENERIC component default. ACharacter initialises its OWN capsule
       subobject to 34/88 at Character.cpp:78. Fixed to read Character CDO ->
       capsule_component. Same class as get_component_by_class reading 0 on a
       world holding 256 built meshes.
    
    VERIFIED: offline exit 0 (profile is a key, ruling 19 gate); --live exit 0
    (walkable_floor_angle 44.765083 == profile, all five movement values == CDO,
    capsule 34/88 == Character CDO).
    
    AND THE TOOL DECLARES ITS OWN EXPIRY. There is no project character class

    spawned ACharacter would carry today, and therefore the right comparator.

    class's CDO in the same commit that authors one, or it will keep proving
    something true about a class nobody spawns.

+    max_step_height_cm        45.0    :689
+    jump_z_velocity_cm_s     420.0    :679
+    max_acceleration_cm_s2  2048.0    :733
+    gravity_scale              1.0    :677
+    capsule radius / half     34 / 88 Character.cpp:78 InitCapsuleSize
+
+Written out in FULL rather than left implicit. Non-negotiable 17 says a
+config file records overrides and never the state in effect — so a recipe
+that lists only overrides describes nothing. The recipe says what the
+character IS; the verifier catches the day the engine stops agreeing.
+
+**`max_step_height_cm` stays at the engine default deliberately.** R-WALK
+established that at 1 m per vertex a step is below the heightmap's Nyquist
+limit, so `MaxStepHeight` is not a terrain constraint on this world at all —
+it governs PLACED geometry only.
+
+### THE RULING-19 GATE, CHECKED HERE AND NOT AT NAVMESH BUILD TIME
+
+`navigation.agent_profile` must not exceed `world.primary_movement_mode` in
+`recipes/alpine_8k.json`. Both are `mount` (35°) today. **Drift upward is
+SILENT** — the navmesh grants paths onto ground the character slides off and
+nothing errors — so it is gated before the packages are written.
+
+**The asymmetry is INTENDED and is not drift:** the player on foot walks
+44.765° while the navmesh is built for the mount at 35°. The gate is
+one-directional, `agent <= world primary`, never equality. The player may go
+where the AI will not path.
+
+### VERIFIED
+
+    offline (no editor)  profile is a key, not an angle; ruling 19 gate
+    --live               walkable_floor_angle 44.765083 == profile
+                         all five movement values == CDO
+                         capsule 34 / 88 == Character CDO
+                         exit 0

+## R-CHARACTER REJECTED
+
+**Prose keys inside `recipes/character.json`.** SYMPTOM: the first version
+carried `_what_this_is`, `_profile_is_a_key_not_an_angle`, `_sources` and
+five more explanatory arrays — and the verifier's own "no typed angle" scan
+**refused the recipe**, because a documentation key was named
+`_profile_is_a_key_not_an_angle` and contains the word "angle". CORRECT: the
+recipe is DATA; the reasoning lives here and the contract lives in
+`schema.md`. REFERENCE: R-ALPINE8K REJECTED already ruled this — *"adding a
+schema key to hold prose is the 'invent a key to get past the validator'
+antipattern"*. **The tempting fix was to exempt underscore-prefixed keys from
+the scan; that would have opened a hole in the gate to accommodate a pattern
+the project had already rejected.**
+
+**Reading the capsule off `CapsuleComponent`'s CDO.** SYMPTOM: `capsule
+radius 22 / half height 44` against a recipe saying 34 / 88, reported as
+DRIFT on a correct recipe. CORRECT: read `Character` CDO →
+`capsule_component`. REFERENCE: `CapsuleComponent`'s CDO is the GENERIC
+component default; `ACharacter` initialises its OWN capsule subobject at
+`Character.cpp:78`. **The generic CDO answered plausibly and was about a
+different object** — the same class as `get_component_by_class` reading 0 on
+a world holding 256 built meshes.
+
+**Pointing this tool at the engine CDO once a project character class
+exists.** SYMPTOM: it keeps passing while proving something true about a
+class nobody spawns. CORRECT: repoint it at the project class's CDO in the
+same commit that authors the class. Today there is no character class, so the
+engine CDO **is** what a spawned `ACharacter` would carry, and the tool says
+so in its own output.

+the same names off the asset.

    opened -- InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:2877-2882 -- but the guard fires on a NULL
    BodySetup, not an EMPTY one. This mesh has a BodySetup, so it sails past and
    the warning the plan expected in the log will never appear.

    a pointer check the engine already does -- but "how many elements are in its
    agg_geom". The tool asks the second, and reports an unreadable element array
    as unreadable rather than as a low count.
    
    WHY THIS MESH AND NOT THE OTHER THREE
    
    It is the only Nanite mesh in the list and the only one this project EXPORTED
    rather than received. The other three ship from vendors with author-made

    has no vendor doing the unglamorous parts. Every property a vendor would have
    authored is one our intake must check for, and the intake currently checks
    appearance.

+## 2026-08-15 — UNIT 3: 63,981 TREES THAT SAY "BlockAll" AND COLLIDE WITH NOTHING
+
+PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 3 exists to check one thing before unit 6 spends a
+session on it: do the scattered meshes actually carry simple collision. The
+answer for three of the four instanced species is yes. For the largest one it
+is no, and the way it is no is worse than absence.
+
+    species         system      simple prims   nanite   tris LOD0
+    Conifer         instanced        0          True       2335
+    ConiferPine     instanced        2 sphyl    False     27824
+    SpruceSub       instanced        1 sphyl    False     20695
+    SpruceSapling   instanced        1 sphyl    False      2604
+
+**`Conifer` is `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` at 63,981 instances — the largest
+species in the world, and the 29.31 m hero spruce the whole forest was
+re-adopted for on 2026-08-15.**
+
+### THE FAILURE IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY CHECK THAT WOULD BE RUN
+
+Read straight off the loaded asset:
+
+    body_setup            present          <- NOT null
+    agg_geom box/convex/sphere/sphyl/tapered/levelset   0 0 0 0 0 0
+    collision_profile     BlockAll         <- it already claims to block
+    collision_trace_flag  CTF_USE_DEFAULT  <- simple and complex kept separate
+    nanite                true
+
+So: the mesh **has** a BodySetup. Its profile **already says BlockAll**. Unit
+6 would set `QUERY_ONLY` + `BlockAll` on it, and every property read-back
+would confirm the setting landed — because it did. And a line trace would go
+straight through the trunk, because there is no geometry to hit.
+
+This is "a value can arrive and still mean something else", in its purest
+form. The setting is correct, present, and about nothing.
+
+### AND THE PLAN'S OWN GUARD DOES NOT CATCH IT
+
+PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 3 says that if the meshes have no simple primitive,
+`CreateAllInstanceBodies()` returns early and unit 6 silently does nothing.
+The citation is real and I opened it — `InstancedStaticMesh.cpp:2877-2882`:
+
+    UBodySetup* BodySetup = GetBodySetup();
+    if (!BodySetup) { UE_LOGF(... "unable to create InstanceBodies!"); return; }
+
+**But that guard fires on a NULL BodySetup, not on an EMPTY one.** This mesh
+has a BodySetup, so it sails past, bodies ARE created, and the engine logs
+nothing at all. The plan expected a warning in the log that will never
+appear.
+
+So the question to ask an asset is not *"does it have a BodySetup"* but
+**"how many elements are in its agg_geom"**. One is a pointer check the
+engine does for you; the other is the fact you actually need. The tool asks
+the second.
+
+### WHY THIS ONE AND NOT THE OTHER THREE
+
+It is the only Nanite mesh in the list, and the only one this project
+EXPORTED rather than received. The other three ship from vendors with
+author-made capsules. `SM_PVE_Norway_Spruce_01_A` came out of the
+skeletal-to-static PVE export on 2026-08-15 (R-BAKE), and **that path does
+not author simple collision.** Nothing in R-BAKE's verification asks whether
+it did — the bake's gates all measured fidelity-to-source, which is exactly
+the shape of the original armature defect the same export path produced.
+
+**Generalisable:** an asset this project GENERATES has no vendor doing the
+unglamorous parts. Every property a vendor would have authored is a property
+our intake must check for, and the intake currently checks appearance.
+
+### THE GOOD NEWS FOR THE FIX
+
+`git check-ignore` says the mesh is **not** vendor content: it is ours and
+tracked. So the capsule can be authored at source and committed, with none of
+the Fab-boundary problem that makes a vendor edit vanish on re-download.

+an asset, and the capsule dimensions belong in a recipe declaration rather
+than in my judgement. The plan is already explicit that the answer is one
+authored capsule per trunk and **never** `UseComplexAsSimple` — which would
+put a 2,335-triangle trimesh in the query scene for each of 63,981
+instances.

+## 2026-08-15 — UNIT 2: A METRIC THAT DOES NOT MEASURE WHAT IT SOUNDS LIKE, AND A BAR WITH NO DENOMINATOR
+
+PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 2 asked for one number: the fraction of the mount-profile
+mask whose 1 m neighbour rise exceeds `MaxStepHeight` = 45 cm. The number is
+**19.87%**. It is also close to meaningless, and the arithmetic that says so
+is one line.
+
+### THE METRIC CONFLATES RAMPS WITH LEDGES
+
+    a 45 cm rise over a 100 cm cell is atan(0.45) = 24.23 degrees
+
+The mount profile admits everything up to **35 degrees**, which is **70 cm of
+rise per cell**. So every slope between 24.23 and 35 degrees trips the metric
+**while being entirely walkable**. A character walks UP a walkable slope; it
+does not step onto it. `MaxStepHeight` governs impacts with surfaces steeper
+than the walkable floor, not the gradient of a ramp.
+
+**And at 1 m per vertex the heightmap cannot express a step at all.** A step
+is a rise over a SUB-METRE horizontal distance, and sub-metre horizontal
+detail is below this map's Nyquist limit by construction. Every transition
+this heightmap can represent is a ramp of some angle. So 19.87% is a
+restatement of the slope distribution wearing a step-height label.
+
+**Consequence worth carrying:** `MaxStepHeight` is not a TERRAIN constraint on
+this world at this resolution. It becomes one only for PLACED geometry —
+rocks, roots, stairs, a settlement's thresholds. Note also that Nanite
+displacement (+/-0.4 m peak) does NOT create steps in collision: landscape
+collision is the heightfield, not the displaced surface.
+
+This is the same shape as the `Height 2500.0` trap and the misleading
+denominator: **a number that is arithmetically correct and answers a question
+nobody asked.**
+
+### THE FINDING THAT MATTERS CAME FROM THE METRIC NOBODY ASKED FOR
+
+Running `traversability()` alongside, because slope and connectivity are what
+actually bind:
+
+    profile  crossable      largest    regions      reachable
+    walk        75.94%       72.03%      77479         94.84%
+    mount       60.67%       17.75%     219828         29.26%
+    climb       99.54%       99.51%       1523         99.97%
+
+`recipes/alpine_8k.json` declares `world.primary_movement_mode: "mount"` and
+`world.min_connected_frac: 0.8`. **Mount reads 29.26% — a FAIL by a factor of
+nearly three, on the PRIMARY movement mode, across 219,828 disconnected
+regions.** That is precisely the "a thousand isolated shelves" case
+`traversability()`'s own docstring exists to catch.
+
+### AND THEN THE CONTROL SAID IT WAS MOSTLY THE INSTRUMENT
+
+219,828 regions is a suspicious number — it has the shape of salt-and-pepper
+fragmentation, where isolated steep cells punch holes in a mask and
+connected-component labelling counts every hole as a boundary. So the same
+computation was repeated on box-reduced copies:
+
+    cell        crossable    largest      regions    reachable
+    1 m            60.67%     17.75%       219828       29.26%
+    2 m            64.17%     21.36%        64546       33.28%
+    4 m            68.57%     51.16%        14225       74.61%
+    8 m            72.83%     68.75%         2340       94.39%
+
+**Reachability goes 29% -> 94% and regions collapse 219,828 -> 2,340, on the
+SAME TERRAIN.** The fragmentation is overwhelmingly an artefact of sampling
+slope per 1 m cell, not a fact about the world.
+
+**So the FAIL is withdrawn as a claim about the terrain** — and it must not
+be re-raised by a later session reading only the first table.
+
+### THE REAL DEFECT IS THAT THE BAR HAS NO DECLARED SCALE
+
+`min_connected_frac: 0.8` is a threshold with **no stated cell size**, and it
+was written for `recipes/alpine.json`, whose world is **4 m per vertex**. The
+8K recipe inherited the number and not its denominator. At 4 m the same
+terrain reads 74.61% — near the bar; at 1 m it reads 29.26% — nowhere near.
+**Same world, same bar, opposite verdicts, and nothing in the recipe records
+which one the bar meant.**
+
+This is non-negotiable 22 (always state the denominator) meeting R13's
+calibration class: **a threshold is only meaningful conditioned on the scale
+it is evaluated at**, and a scale-free threshold silently changes meaning the
+moment the map's resolution changes. The 8K re-terrain moved four
+resolution-dependent parameters that "only ever had one value"; this is a
+fifth, and it was missed because it lives in a BAR rather than in a
+generator.
+
+### THE PRINCIPLED FIX, RECOMMENDED AND NOT TAKEN UNILATERALLY
+
+**The evaluation scale should be a physical property of the AGENT, not a
+choice.** A mount occupies roughly 2-4 m of ground; slope sampled at 1 m is
+finer than the agent can resolve, so evaluating rideability there asks
+whether a horse can stand on a dinner plate. That makes the scale a
+pass-independent physical quantity, which is exactly what non-negotiable 19
+says must be declared once and read by every consumer — beside
+`MOVEMENT_PROFILES`, not beside the bar.
+
+Not applied unilaterally because it changes a gate's verdict, and a gate
+whose bar moves to make a failing number pass needs the reasoning ratified
+before the number, not after. **The number to beat is recorded here so the
+ratification cannot be graded against a moving target.**
+
+### THE CORRIDOR HALF WAS NOT MEASURED, AND SAYS SO
+
+Unit 2's acceptance also wants the figure "restricted to the inter-massif
+corridor". **The corridor has no spatial definition anywhere in this repo.**
+`WORLD_VISION.md:304` defines it in prose as *"the primary traversal route"*
+and gives no coordinates, no mask, no endpoints; nothing in `recipes/`
+declares one. Inventing a rectangle and calling it the corridor would make
+every number computed against it unfalsifiable, so it is reported as **I
+COULD NOT LOOK** — which is not a pass. Closing it is one ruling from Ryan,
+and it is the same open item as `WORLD_VISION.md:322`.

+fragmented measurement:

+## R-WALK REJECTED
+
+**Reading "19.87% of the mount mask exceeds MaxStepHeight" as a walkability
+defect** — and `PHASE2_PLAN.md` unit 2 specifies exactly this metric.
+SYMPTOM: a large, alarming fraction that no terrain change improves.
+CORRECT: read it as a restatement of the slope distribution. REFERENCE: 45 cm
+over a 100 cm cell is **24.23 degrees**, and the mount profile admits 35
+degrees = **70 cm of rise per cell**, so every slope in between trips the
+metric while being entirely walkable. A character walks UP a walkable slope;
+it does not step onto it.
+
+**Auditing step height on a 1 m-per-vertex heightmap at all.** SYMPTOM: a
+number that looks like a step-height census. CORRECT: **a step is a rise over
+a SUB-METRE horizontal distance and is below this map's Nyquist limit by
+construction.** `MaxStepHeight` is not a terrain constraint here; it applies
+to PLACED geometry — rocks, roots, stairs, thresholds. Note Nanite
+displacement (+/-0.4 m) does NOT create collidable steps: landscape collision
+is the heightfield, not the displaced surface.
+
+**Grading `world.min_connected_frac` on a map whose resolution differs from
+the one the bar was written for.** SYMPTOM: mount reachability reads 29.26%
+against a 0.8 bar — a FAIL by nearly 3x on the PRIMARY movement mode — and
+the same terrain reads 74.61% at 4 m and 94.39% at 8 m. CORRECT: **the bar
+carries no declared cell size**, and it was authored for `recipes/alpine.json`
+at **4 m per vertex**. Do not act on the 1 m verdict. REFERENCE:
+non-negotiable 22 — a threshold is only meaningful conditioned on the scale
+it is evaluated at. This is the fifth resolution-dependent parameter the 8K
+re-terrain exposed, and the first that lives in a BAR rather than a generator.
+
+**RECOMMENDED AND NOT YET RULED:** make the evaluation scale a PHYSICAL
+property of the agent — a mount occupies ~2-4 m of ground, so slope sampled
+at 1 m asks whether a horse can stand on a dinner plate — and declare it
+beside `MOVEMENT_PROFILES`, never beside the bar. Not applied unilaterally:
+**a gate whose bar moves to make a failing number pass needs its reasoning
+ratified before the number.**
+
+**Inventing a corridor mask to satisfy unit 2's second acceptance clause.**
+SYMPTOM: a plausible per-corridor figure nobody can falsify. CORRECT: report
+**I COULD NOT LOOK**. REFERENCE: the inter-massif corridor has NO spatial
+definition in this repo — `WORLD_VISION.md:304` gives prose only, and nothing
+in `recipes/` declares coordinates, a mask or endpoints. One ruling from Ryan
+closes it; it is the same open item as `WORLD_VISION.md:322`.
+
+**Letting `np.roll` supply the neighbour differences without masking the
+border.** SYMPTOM: a one-cell ring of enormous false rises where the map's
+opposite edges are compared. CORRECT: exclude the border; the tool does.

+## 2026-08-15 — THE FIRST PIE FRAME THIS PROJECT HAS EVER MEASURED, AND THREE THINGS THAT RETURNED SUCCESS WHILE DOING NOTHING
+
+PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 1 asked for one PIE capture, on the grounds that every
+performance number this project owns is editor-viewport class and four
+variables change sign the moment a player exists. It is done, at three
+stations, with two artefacts on disk. What it found about the WORLD is one
+paragraph. What it found about INSTRUMENTS is most of this entry.
+
+### THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE INSTRUMENT WAS BUILT
+
+The whole design rests on Python remote execution continuing to answer while
+a game world is ticking, and nothing in this repo recorded whether it does.
+If it did not, an instrument built on it would not fail loudly - it would
+HANG, which is the exact shape of the 2026-08-10 capture that ran fifteen
+minutes with a live process and zero output.
+
+So `probe_pie` asked that one question in isolation first. It answers: remote
+exec responds during PIE with a 0.0 s round trip. Cheap, and it meant the
+600-line instrument was written against a measured premise rather than a
+hoped-for one.
+
+### A GREP THAT COULD NOT MATCH, READ AS AN ANSWER
+
+Searching the generated Python stub for the play API with the patterns
+`editor_play`, `request_play` and `end_play` returned exactly one function:
+`editor_play_simulate`. Read as an answer, that says **5.8 Python cannot
+start real PIE, only Simulate** - and Simulate has no PlayerController and no
+player camera, so every number would have belonged to a class nobody asked
+for.
+
+`editor_request_begin_play` (PythonStub 606201) matches none of those three
+patterns. It was found by READING THE LINES AROUND THE HITS rather than
+trusting the hit list.
+
+This is the `LandscapeNanite.cpp` near-miss again, in a different container.
+There the path did not exist; here the pattern could not match. **Both
+produce a zero that reads as "looked and absent" when it is "could not
+look"** - non-negotiable 6. The general form worth carrying: *a negative
+result from a search is only evidence if the search could have found the
+thing.*
+
+### THE STATION SEQUENCE WAS WRONG IN TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, AND THE GATES
+### CAUGHT BOTH
+
+First run, all three stations refused. Neither refusal was a bug in the
+gates; both were real.
+
+**1. TRACING FOR GROUND BEFORE MOVING THE PAWN CAN NEVER HIT.** World
+Partition streams around the PAWN. The pawn spawns at the world origin (the
+level has no PlayerStart), and the station is 4.8 km away, so the region was
+never loaded and the top-down collision trace hit nothing across a 6 km
+span. **"Not streamed" and "there is no terrain here" produce the identical
+answer**, and the tool correctly reported the raw fact - no hit - rather than
+a Z it had invented. Fix: teleport to a perch first, wait for streaming, then
+trace, then move to the real height.
+
+**2. THE VIEW POINT READ BACK AS THE ORIGIN, AND IT WAS TELLING THE TRUTH.**
+`get_player_view_point` returned [0,0,0] while the pawn's own location read
+back exactly on target. `APlayerController::GetPlayerViewPoint` returns the
+camera manager's CACHED point, gated on `GetCameraCacheTime() > 0` with the
+engine's own comment *"Whether camera was updated at least once"*. Read in
+the same payload as the teleport, it returns the cache from before the move -
+the origin, where the pawn spawned. Fix: read it on a later tick.
+
+**And this is precisely why the read-back is worth having.** The pawn's
+location is the field the setter wrote; reading it proves only that the value
+landed. The view point is a DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT - non-negotiable 8 - and it
+is the one that would have caught a frame measured somewhere other than where
+the station was declared. It fired on its first real use, on my own error.
+
+### THE PLAN'S OWN CONSOLE COMMAND IS A SILENT NO-OP
+
+PHASE2_PLAN.md unit 1 prescribes `CsvCategory VSM 1` and `CsvCategory
+GPUScene 1` to turn on the default-off diagnostic categories. Run exactly as
+written, across three stations, **every VSM column was absent from the CSV**
+- and the tool reported them ABSENT rather than as zeros, which is the only
+reason the difference was visible at all.
+
+Root cause at `CsvProfiler.cpp:1138-1148`. `HandleCSVCategoryCommand`
+compares the second argument against the literal words `enable` and
+`disable`. `"1"` matches neither, so `bIsOperationValid` goes false and the
+command falls through to a usage error **without enabling anything**. The
+console command still returns normally. The correct form is
+`CsvCategory VSM enable`.
+
+Note also `:1152-1153`: with the argument OMITTED the command **toggles**. So
+the bare form is not idempotent and a second run would switch the category
+back off. The explicit word is required for pipeline rule 3, not only for
+correctness.
+
+Re-run with `enable`: all five VSM columns record.
+
+**Three no-ops in one session - a grep that could not match, a trace that
+could not hit, a command that could not enable - and all three returned
+success.** The thing that made each one visible was refusing to print a
+number the instrument had not actually obtained.
+
+### WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT THE WORLD
+
+Tag `pie001`, categories off, which is the clean cost run:
+
+    station              GPUTime   GameThread   RenderThread   RHI
+    forest_floor           7.816       7.198          5.309    2.779
+    canopy_250m            5.082       7.084          5.198    2.765
+    airship_1500m          3.404       7.022          5.055    2.523
+
+**The control reproduces.** 7.816 ms against the editor series' 7.92 at the
+same camera - inside the plan's +/-0.2 ms acceptance - even though the two
+classes differ in streaming (4 resident landscape proxies against 256
+force-resident), in FOV (90 in PIE against the recipe camera's 75) and in
+having gameplay ticking. That agreement is worth more than it looks: it says
+the GPU cost at this station is dominated by what is in frame and not by the
+residency difference.
+
+**GPU HALVES WITH ALTITUDE AND THE GAME THREAD DOES NOT MOVE.** 7.82 -> 5.08
+-> 3.40 against 7.20 -> 7.08 -> 7.02. The game thread is a FIXED cost here,
+and it is already 7 ms with **zero gameplay**: no AI, no enemies, one dynamic
+instance. PHASE2_PLAN's headline risk was that the game thread binds before
+the GPU. On this evidence it does, and the plan's own figure of 8.0 ms for AI
+perception plus EQS at engine defaults would land the frame around 15 ms of
+game thread against a 16.67 ms budget, before one enemy exists.
+
+**Stated as a limit, because it changes what the number means:** PIE runs
+inside the editor process, so this game thread carries editor overhead a
+cooked build would not. **7 ms is an upper bound on the shipping figure, not
+the shipping figure.** The decomposition needs a cook, which this project has
+never produced and which is additionally mis-pointed - `GameDefaultMap` is
+still Epic's template world.
+
+### THE PAGE-POOL QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE PLAN NAMED THE WRONG FIELD
+
+The plan says the discriminating field is `VSM/SinglePageCount` +
+`VSM/FullCount` against the 2048-page pool, because page saturation and a
+large instance count produce the same frame time and lead to opposite work.
+The reasoning is right and the field is one step off: those two count shadow
+MAPS, not pages (`VirtualShadowMapArray.cpp:2619-2620` wrap
+`GetNumSinglePageShadowMaps` and `GetNumFullShadowMaps`). The direct measure
+is `VSM/FreePages`, `VirtualShadowMapCacheManager.cpp:685`.
+
+Measured, tag `pie002`: FreePages 1820 / 1978 / 2024 of
+`r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages` = 2048. **Peak usage is 228 pages of
+2048 - 11%.** Virtual shadow map pages are NOT the constraint at any of the
+three stations, and no work should be aimed at them.
+
+### THE DIAGNOSTIC CATEGORIES ARE NOT FREE, SO THE TWO TAGS ARE NOT ONE SERIES
+
+Same station, same camera, same session, categories the only difference:
+
+    forest_floor   GPUTime 7.816 (pie001)  ->  8.338 (pie002)   +0.52 ms
+
+**Turning on the instrumentation costs about half a millisecond of GPU.** So
+`pie001` is the cost measurement and `pie002` is the diagnostic measurement,
+and a number may not be lifted from one into the other. This is R13's
+calibration-class rule arriving one level down: the INSTRUMENT's own settings
+are part of the class.
+
+### ONE COLUMN THAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE, AND IS THEREFORE NOT YET EVIDENCE
+
+`SceneCulling/NumStaticInstances` read **284,424 at all three stations** in
+`pie001`, and **284,424 / 4,264 / 4,264** in `pie002`. Same stations, same
+order, same session. A statistic that disagrees with itself across two runs
+is not a measurement of the world yet, whatever it is measuring.
+
+**It is recorded here and deliberately NOT quoted as a finding.** The
+plausible mechanism - it is declared `ECsvCustomStatOp::Accumulate`
+(`SceneCulling.cpp:2676`), so what it means depends on how many times the
+update ran in a frame - is an inference, and the honest position is that this
+column needs its own single-variable run before anyone leans on it. Named so
+that a later session does not discover the inconsistency by trusting it.

+### WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE RECIPE FROM R-FRAMECOST

+`RECIPES.md:5889` already calls PIE *"a different calibration class that does

+### THE PROCEDURE
+
+1. **Verify the node** (standing rule 7) before anything.
+2. **Refuse if the editor is already in play.** A session you did not start
+   cannot be told from your own at teardown.
+3. `LevelEditorSubsystem.editor_request_begin_play()` — PythonStub 606201.
+   It is a REQUEST: PIE exists on a LATER TICK. Settle 30 s.
+4. **Enable the default-off CSV categories with the literal word `enable`.**
+   See REJECTED. `CsvCategory VSM enable`, `CsvCategory GPUScene enable`.
+   `SceneCulling` is default-ON (`SceneCulling.cpp:105`) and needs nothing.
+5. **Per station, in this order and no other:**
+   a. **Teleport the pawn to a perch FIRST** (250,000 cm; the terrain tops out
+      at 1552.5 m). World Partition streams around the PAWN.
+   b. Settle 25 s for streaming.
+   c. **Then** trace for ground — `SystemLibrary.line_trace_single`,
+      `TRACE_TYPE_QUERY1`, top-down, against COLLISION. Read the hit with
+      `to_dict()`; `FHitResult`'s fields are protected in 5.8.
+   d. Teleport to `ground + height_above_ground`.
+   e. **Wait 6 s, THEN read `get_player_view_point()`** and refuse the station
+      if it disagrees with the target by more than 5 m.
+   f. `CsvProfile frames=300`, then reduce the CSV.
+6. `editor_request_end_play()`, then **CONFIRM** with `is_in_play_in_editor()`.
+   A request that returns is not a session that stopped.
+
+### VALUES THAT WORK
+
+    settle after begin play        30 s
+    settle after a teleport        25 s
+    settle before reading camera    6 s
+    frames per station            300
+    perch Z                   250,000 cm
+    max view-vs-target drift      500 cm
+    min editor CPU ratio          0.30 CPU-s per wall-s

+### THE FOUR-TIER STAND, AND WHY IT IS NOT ONE RAMP
+
+The height band was a HARD window: uniform density to the top edge, then
+nothing. New shared prior `placement_priors.closure_ramp` **SCALES** where
+`centred_bias` **REDISTRIBUTES** — flow says WHERE trees stand, closure says
+HOW MANY, and a subalpine stand genuinely thins toward treeline.
+
+**The falloff differs per tier**, which is the compositional half of it. One
+shared ramp would thin all four together and give a smaller copy of the same
+uniform forest:

+    Conifer        1.00 -> 0.15   29.3 m canopy; mature crowns go first
+    ConiferPine    1.00 -> 0.20

+    SpruceSapling  1.00 -> 0.55   4.5 m regeneration — this IS the krummholz
+

+mask and four ramps. The band now ends sapling-dominated rather than empty.

+## 2026-08-15 - D4: A BAND IS NOT A GRADIENT, AND ONE RAMP IS NOT A FOREST
+
+The height band was a HARD window. Inside [120, 640] m every elevation was
+equally likely, so the forest ran at uniform density to the top edge and
+stopped dead. WORLD_VISION's complaint was UNIFORMITY as much as sparseness,
+and no amount of raising density_per_hectare addresses that - it makes the
+same flat forest thicker.
+
+### THE PRIOR THAT SCALES, AND WHY THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT
+
+placement_priors.centred_bias REDISTRIBUTES: wet ground gains exactly what
+dry ground loses, mean preserved, because flow says WHERE trees prefer to
+stand. Closure is a different KIND of fact. A subalpine stand genuinely thins
+toward treeline - fewer trees, not the same trees moved uphill - and ends in
+open krummholz. So closure_ramp SCALES, and the caller's count falls with
+it.
+
+That distinction had to be argued explicitly in the code, because the two
+functions now sit side by side in the same module and look interchangeable.
+Anything that preserved the mean here would describe a forest that does not
+exist.
+
+### ONE RAMP WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A SMALLER COPY OF THE SAME DEFECT
+
+The instinct is a single closure ramp shared by every species. That thins all
+four tiers together and yields a scale model of the uniform forest - the same
+composition everywhere, just less of it.
+
+Real stands change composition with elevation: the big crowns drop out first
+and the last thing standing is stunted regeneration. So the falloff is
+per-tier - canopy 1.00->0.15, sub-canopy ->0.30, saplings ->0.55 - and the
+top of the band ends SAPLING-DOMINATED rather than empty. The acceptance
+rates confirm it landed: 22.4% for the canopy against 30.0% for saplings,
+from one shared mask and four different ramps.
+
+### THE COUNT HAD TO BE RE-DERIVED, NOT CARRIED
+
+A multiplier that scales cannot leave the density alone. Measured: at the
+unchanged 68/ha, closure alone takes the plan from a uniform 153,796 to
+111,079. 135/ha then gives 219,659 - the ruling's ~220,000 with a 30,341
+reserve under the shared 250,000 ceiling. Deriving the density from the ramp
+rather than guessing at it took one dry run, because the planner prints
+counts before it places anything.
+
+### AND A GATE THAT REFUSED THE WORLD, NOT THE WORK
+
+save_level.py defaults to ecipes/alpine.json. Run without --recipe it
+refused with exit 7 - "recipe targets '/Game/Alpine' but the editor has
+'/Game/Alpine8K' open". That is not pedantry: the tool carries a package
+ALLOW-LIST derived from the recipe, so it would have saved 219,659 instances
+under a list scoped to a different world. The gate that looks like
+bureaucracy on every green run is the one that matters on the red one.
+
++65,863 instances for +0.18 ms GPU, against an 11 ms abort bar and a 7.92 ms
+reading. Cheap because the new tiers are light and carry imposter LODs -
+which is the D2 intake paying for the D4 budget, and the reason the two were
+ruled as one re-scatter.

+## 2026-08-15 — THE BUILDER, THE VALIDATOR AND TWO AUDITS ALL PASSED A CLAIM THAT WAS FALSE
+
+D3 put the blueberry understory on the grass system. It landed, it costs
+nothing measurable, and it produced the clearest example this project has of
+a claim surviving every gate it had.
+
+### THE CHAIN THAT AGREED, AND WAS WRONG
+
+`MA_Blueberry` carries the same wind system as the PN trees. The grass system
+gives no per-instance correction and the vendor pack must not be edited, so
+the only route is `GrassVariety.override_materials` (PythonStub :121628).
+
+That was declared in the recipe. The **validator accepted it**. The **payload
+handled it**, including a fail-closed branch for an override that will not
+load. The **builder reported success**. **Connectivity** passed 298/298 with
+0 orphans. **Samplers** passed 37/37.
+
+All eight varieties read back **`overrides: NONE`** off the saved asset.
+
+Root cause at `make_landscape_material.py:2932`: the recipe's variety dicts
+never reach the payload. They are transformed into
+`{mesh, density, smin, smax}` first, and `override_materials` was dropped in
+that transform. **The payload was correct about a field it never received.**
+
+### WHY EVERY EXISTING GATE WAS BLIND, WHICH IS THE POINT
+
+Not one of those instruments was broken, and not one was asking the question.
+A grass type with no material overrides is a **perfectly well-formed grass
+type**. Connectivity asks whether nodes are reachable. Samplers ask whether
+declared types match. The builder asks whether its own calls returned. None
+of them can distinguish "the override is absent because nobody wanted one"
+from "the override is absent because it was silently dropped in transit".
+
+**Agreement among instruments that share a source is one measurement**
+(non-negotiable 0), and here they shared more than a source: they shared an
+ASSUMPTION, that a field declared in the recipe reaches the thing that
+consumes it. The transform between them was invisible to all of them.
+
+What caught it was a new instrument that reads the SAVED asset and shares no
+code with the builder — `scripts/read_grass_type.py` — with
+`--expect-all-overridden` written as a **REFUSAL** rather than a printed
+observation. A tool that prints "overrides: NONE" and exits 0 is a tool that
+would have been skimmed past.
+
+### THE SECOND FINDING: I HAD BROKEN THE GATE THE RULING NAMED, EARLIER THE SAME DAY
+
+The ruling required `uncorrected_pivot_errors()` per mesh — the grass system
+puts the mesh's PIVOT on the surface and a box-centred pivot buries 50% by
+construction.
+
+`recipe_normalization_errors` merges two registries into one "verified" map,
+then does `if ok: continue`. Adding the engine-derived registry to that map
+this morning meant **registering a mesh as engine-derived exempted it from
+the pivot gate entirely.** The two registries never carried the same
+guarantee:
+
+    BLENDER-NORMALISED   pivot is AT THE BASE by construction
+    ENGINE-DERIVED       somebody MEASURED it; the pivot is where the
+                         vendor left it
+
+Blueberry is a grass species built from vendor `.uasset` meshes — precisely
+the combination the hole was shaped for, found one working day after the hole
+was made. Fixed by tagging provenance at merge time. Proven both directions,
+positive control first.
+
+**The general shape: a widening that looks like a convenience is a
+weakening when the two things being merged carry different guarantees.** The
+merge was written to stop a Fab rock being refused for lacking a Blender row
+it can never have — a real and correct fix — and it silently took a second
+check with it.
+
+### AND A NULL COST THAT HAD TO BE DISPROVED BEFORE IT COULD BE BELIEVED
+
+Frame cost came back GPU 7.74 against a 7.75 baseline: -0.01 ms, against a
++1.5 ms abort bar. **A zero delta is also exactly what "the grass never
+spawned" looks like**, and this project has shipped invisible grass for two
+sessions before. It was not accepted until the understory was on pixels at
+the same station. The arithmetic then agrees: ~7,634 instances at ~500
+triangles is ~3.8M against a 29.8M grass budget, which belongs under the
+noise of a 300-frame mean. Recorded as "under the measurement floor", not as
+"free".

    0.00298 quoted everywhere, across 23% of the frame, with grass off and zero
    shader compile workers. It is renderer temporal accumulation, not motion.
    0.00298 was measured on /Game/Alpine - 2017 squared, before Lumen, before
    the capable-GPU profile, before volumetric fog - and has been carried across
    a new world, resolution, lighting model and quality profile as though it
    were a constant. Every pixel A/B judged against it on this world has been
    over-crediting differences by about 4x. This is R13's CALIBRATION CLASS rule
    unapplied to the one number that gates every visual verdict.
    
    FINDING 2 - A CVAR THAT READS BACK CORRECTLY AND DOES NOTHING.
    The control was foliage.CullAll 1 + grass.Enable 0. Both read back;
    render_condition printed CONDITION SET AND READ BACK ON EVERY CVAR. The
    trees stayed on screen. Caught by measuring what the control was supposed to
    change: the upper half of the frame is canopy and sky, so culling trees must
    collapse its dark coverage. It fell 62.73% -> 53.92% while the GRASS half
    fell 56.52% -> 41.55%. The half that should have changed most changed least.

    the HISM culling path. r.Nanite.Foliage is 1 and the placed spruce is

    to a renderer the foliage no longer uses. "Set and read back" proves the
    variable holds the number, and nothing about whether the subsystem reading
    it is the one drawing the picture.

    vegetation ON 8.14 / CULLED 5.86, +2.28 ms, attributed to "154,018 conifers
    plus grass". If r.Nanite.Foliage was already 1 for that run, the 2.28 ms was
    GRASS ALONE. Not resolved here - that needs the cvar's value at that run,
    not a guess - but recorded, because the figure is on the board as a conifer
    cost. No future decomposition may use foliage.CullAll to isolate Nanite
    foliage.

    removed, so the render half of the no-animation case rests on the grass

    moved 20.9x the floor); the tree control failed it.
