+## 2026-08-15 — THE FOREST DOES NOT MOVE. THE FLOOR DOES.
+
+The question was whether the 153,796 trees standing in `/Game/Alpine8K`
+animate the way the PN spruce does. The answer is no, and the run found two
+things worth more than the answer.
+
+### THE ANSWER, FROM TWO SOURCES THAT SHARE NOTHING
+
+`MA_Foliage_Trees` (the Megaplants conifer master) declares 38 scalars, 19
+switches and 20 vectors, **every one of them shading or colour**.
+`ScotsPine_01_Leaves_Mat` declares three scalars and no switches. Not one
+wind, wobble, bending, phase or time parameter between them, against a PN
+master carrying twelve. And removing the grass left frame-to-frame variance
+unchanged, 0.011745 -> 0.012122.
+
+### FINDING 1 — THE NOISE FLOOR IS A PROPERTY OF A SCENE, NOT OF A PROJECT
+
+`/Game/Alpine8K` at `forest_floor` re-renders itself at **mae 0.0117, 3.94x
+the 0.00298 this project quotes everywhere**, across 23% of the frame, with
+the grass off and zero shader compile workers running. It is renderer
+temporal accumulation, not motion.
+
+0.00298 was measured on `/Game/Alpine` — 2017², before Lumen, before the
+capable-GPU profile, before volumetric fog. **It has been carried across a
+new world, a new resolution, a new lighting model and a new quality profile
+as though it were a constant.** Every pixel A/B judged against it on
+Alpine8K has been over-crediting differences by about 4x.
+
+This is the CALIBRATION CLASS rule that R13 already applies to GPU
+milliseconds, unapplied to the one number that gates every visual verdict.
+The fix is not a better floor; it is that a floor must be RE-DERIVED with
+its scene and its settings, and quoted with them attached.
+
+### FINDING 2 — A CVAR THAT READS BACK CORRECTLY AND DOES NOTHING
+
+The vegetation-off control was `foliage.CullAll 1` + `grass.Enable 0`. Both
+read back. `render_condition` printed CONDITION SET AND READ BACK ON EVERY
+CVAR. **The trees stayed on screen.**
+
+Caught by measuring the thing the control was supposed to change rather than
+trusting that it had: the upper half of the frame is canopy and sky, so
+culling trees must collapse its dark coverage. It fell 62.73% -> 53.92%,
+while the grass half fell 56.52% -> 41.55%. **The half that was supposed to
+change most changed least.**
+
+`foliage.CullAll` is declared in `HierarchicalInstancedStaticMesh.cpp:63-67`
+— the HISM culling path. `r.Nanite.Foliage` is 1 and the placed spruce is
+Nanite, so it never enters that path. The cvar is not broken; it is scoped
+to a renderer the foliage no longer uses.
+
+**This is exactly the protocol's own warning — a value can arrive and still
+mean something else — landing on a cvar rather than on an API argument.**
+"Set and read back" proves the variable holds the number. It proves nothing
+about whether the subsystem reading that variable is the one drawing the
+picture.
+
+**And it reaches backwards.** CURRENT STATE records the 2026-08-14
+decomposition as vegetation ON 8.14 / CULLED 5.86, delta +2.28 ms,
+attributed to "154,018 conifers plus grass". If `r.Nanite.Foliage` was
+already 1 for that run, that 2.28 ms was **grass alone**. Not resolved here,
+because resolving it needs the cvar's value at that run and not a guess —
+but recorded, because the figure is on the board as a conifer cost.
+
+### THE SHAPE
+
+Both findings are the same shape as the session's earlier ones: a number
+inherited from a context it no longer describes, and a control believed
+because it reported success. The floor was true of a different world. The
+cull was true of a different renderer. Neither announced that it had stopped
+being true, and in both cases the only thing that surfaced it was measuring
+the artefact the claim was about — the frame's own variance, and the dark
+coverage of the half that should have emptied.
+
+**A null result is only evidence when the instrument could have produced a
+non-null one.** The grass control passed that test — removing grass moved
+20.9x the floor — so "grass is not the cause" is a real finding. The tree
+control failed it, so "trees are not the cause" rests on the material
+probes, and the write-up says so rather than banking both as one result.

+## 2026-08-15 — THE WIND WAS ALREADY BLOWING, AND THE MEAN NEARLY HID IT
+
+The D2 ruling said to edit the wind out because `PN_GlobalUpdater` is a
+runtime Blueprint dependency and wiring it would breach pipeline rule 1.
+Before authoring ~73 material instances on that reasoning, the cheaper
+question was asked first: **is the wind even live without the Blueprint?**
+
+Three `highres_shot` frames, one parked camera, ~5 s apart, nothing touched
+between them, in a scratch level containing no Blueprint of any kind.
+
+    frames      mae      vs 0.00298 floor   px >2%   max local
+    1 vs 2    0.00611        2.05x           4.36%     0.7333
+    1 vs 3    0.00410        1.38x           3.66%     0.6824
+    2 vs 3    0.00561        1.88x           4.27%     0.7255
+
+**Read as a mean, 1.4-2.1x a noise floor is the kind of number this project
+has correctly dismissed before.** It is roughly what the ScreenPercentage
+A/B produced when the honest conclusion was "this lever is minor". Stopping
+at the mean would have concluded the wind was inert and moved on.
+
+Conditioned on WHERE it happens, it is not minor at all: 2.4% of the frame
+changes by more than 10%, local differences reach **0.73**, and the change
+is stratified by row band — canopy 10.32% of pixels, flat ground plane
+1.04%.
+
+**The diff image settled it in one look.** Amplified 6x it is a clean
+silhouette of the tree: canopy saturated, the bare lower branches picked out
+individually, sky and the flat untextured ground plane black. A static scene
+re-rendered twice gives TAA jitter spread along edges everywhere; this is
+confined to exactly the geometry that moves under wind and absent from the
+two large regions that physically cannot. The spatial pattern matches the
+mechanism, so it is evidence rather than a number.
+
+### THE MEAN WAS A MISLEADING DENOMINATOR, IN THE ONE PLACE THE RULE IS EASY TO FORGET
+
+Non-negotiable 22 was written about a layer-scoped selector reported against
+the whole map. This is the same defect wearing frame coordinates: a change
+occupying 2.4% of the pixels, averaged over 100% of them, reads as noise.
+**Whole-frame mae is a layer-scoped statistic whenever the subject does not
+fill the frame** — and a tree on a plain never does. The instrument that
+answered the question was the one that stated its denominator.
+
+### THE RULING'S REASON WAS WRONG AND ITS CONCLUSION WAS RIGHT
+
+`PN_GlobalUpdater` is not required: the material drives the animation from
+engine Time by itself. So the stated justification — a runtime Blueprint
+dependency — does not apply.
+
+The conclusion survives on a better ground that nobody had stated. **An
+animating canopy makes every pixel comparison non-deterministic.** This
+project's entire method is single-variable frame A/B against a floor
+measured in the third decimal place. A forest that moves between the
+"before" and the "after" does not raise the floor a little; on a
+vegetation-filled frame it removes the instrument.
+
+Worth separating clearly, because the two are easy to conflate: **frame
+COST is unaffected.** That is a timing measurement, not a pixel one, so the
+8.14 -> 7.76 ms result stands.
+
+### AND THE REMOVAL IS CHEAP, WHICH ONLY MEASURING REVEALED
+
+Wind is carried on STATIC SWITCH parameters — `Level 1/2/3 Wind` and the
+three `Bending` siblings — on `MA_Summer`, `MA_Winter` and `MA_Imposter`.
+A static switch set false in a child Material Instance COMPILES THE BRANCH
+OUT rather than zeroing an amplitude, so it costs nothing at runtime.
+
+That matters beyond convenience. The pack is gitignored with **0 tracked
+files**, so any edit to the vendor masters is unrecoverable on re-download —
+the Fab-boundary rule's own worked example. Child MIs in a tracked folder
+leave every vendor byte identical. **The safe route existed the whole time
+and was only visible after reading the parameter list**, which is the same
+shape as the LOD-group finding earlier the same session: the artefact was
+never asked.
+
+### THE PART THAT REACHES BACKWARDS, RECORDED RATHER THAN CHASED
+
+The 153,796 trees already standing in `/Game/Alpine8K` are Megaplants/PVE
+content whose materials have never been tested for this. If they animate,
+every PIXEL comparison taken on that world since the spruce adoption sits on
+an inflated floor. The check is one park and three shots and it is NOT done,
+because that world is expensive to load and it does not block D2. Stated
+here so it is a known gap rather than a silent one.
+
+Related: **the 0.00298 floor was derived on bare terrain**, before this
+project had any animated foliage. Quoting it against a vegetation-filled
+frame is a calibration-class error of the kind R13 already labels for GPU
+figures.

+## 2026-08-15 — D2 INTAKE: A GATE THAT WOULD HAVE THROWN AWAY THE REASON THE PACK WAS CHOSEN
+
+Measuring `PN_interactiveSpruceForest` before importing it produced three
+findings, and two of them contradict something that was written down as
+established.
+
+### 1. THE RULING'S PREMISE ABOUT LOD GROUPS WAS WRONG, AND MEASURING IS THE ONLY REASON IT WAS CAUGHT
+
+The D2 ruling states `LODGroup=None` on the 14 big trees, and builds a
+condition on it: explicit screen sizes and cull distances become a gate
+REFUSAL *because* the meshes supply no defaults.
+
+Measured: **15 of 21 carry `SmallProp`, 6 carry `NAME_None`**, inconsistently
+— the same tree at `high` and `low` quality differs from itself. The ruling's
+premise is false for most of the pack.
+
+`measure_rock_meshes.py`'s shared payload did not read `lod_group` at all, so
+the field had never been measured by anything. It was added this session
+before the run, specifically because the ruling made the value load-bearing.
+**A design that rests on an unmeasured property gets that property measured
+before it is built on** — the ruling was right to name it, and wrong about
+its value, and only one of those matters once you look.
+
+The conclusion survives in a stronger form: the meshes' declared screen sizes
+must be treated as authoritative, and cull distance still has to be declared
+explicitly, because nothing in the pack supplies one.
+
+### 2. AN ENGINE COMMENT THAT SAYS THE OPPOSITE OF THE CODE BENEATH IT
+
+`SmallProp` is `NumLODs=4` (`BaseEngine.ini:2685`). Every big tree has **5**
+LODs, and **LOD4 is the imposter**.
+
+`UStaticMesh::SetLODGroup` (`StaticMesh.cpp:5605-5607`):
+
+    // Set the number of LODs to at least the default. If there are already
+    // LODs they will be preserved, with default settings of the new LOD group.
+    int32 DefaultLODCount = GroupSettings.GetDefaultNumLODs();
+    SetNumSourceModels(DefaultLODCount);
+
+The comment promises preservation. `SetNumSourceModels`
+(`StaticMesh.cpp:5944-5974`) does the opposite when shrinking: for every LOD
+above the new count it calls `ClearMeshDescription()`, empties the
+`MeshDescriptionBulkData`, strips both section-info maps, then
+`SourceModels.SetNum(Num)`.
+
+**So assigning any 4-LOD group to these meshes deletes the imposter.**
+
+The dangerous part is not the engine bug — it is that **the obvious tidy-up
+is the destructive act.** Finding "15 meshes carry an inconsistent LOD group"
+invites normalising it, and normalising it destroys the imposters on all 14
+big trees. The pack was chosen *for* those imposters. A future session will
+find the same inconsistency and feel the same urge, which is why the ruling
+NOT to normalise is recorded in the artefact and here rather than left as a
+judgement someone has to re-make.
+
+This is the project's own prose-claims-rot rule (non-negotiable 25) appearing
+in engine source: a comment asserting a guarantee that nothing re-checks when
+the code below it changes.
+
+### 3. OUR OWN TOOL RETURNED A CONFIDENT WRONG VERDICT ON CORRECT CONTENT
+
+`measure_lod_materials.py` exited 4 on all 14 big trees with:
+
+    LOST MATERIAL(S): branch, leaf, trunk
+    This LOD cannot render what LOD0 renders...
+    ...the fix is to stop the chain before the loss, or to rebuild that LOD.
+
+That advice, followed, **discards the imposter LOD** — the entire reason D2
+selected this pack over four more pine variants.
+
+Root cause is a missing distinction, at `measure_lod_materials.py:181`. The
+tool computed `lost = base - used` and never computed `gained = used - base`.
+Two different facts were collapsed into one:
+
+- **LOSS** — materials disappear and nothing replaces them. The simplifier
+  dropped geometry; the mesh renders as strictly less of itself. A defect.
+- **SUBSTITUTION** — materials disappear *and* a material LOD0 never had
+  appears. The LOD is a deliberate replacement representation: a billboard or
+  octahedral imposter standing in for the whole tree.
+
+**Every imposter LOD ever authored trips the loss test by construction.** The
+tool had only ever been pointed at generated chains (R5's conifers) where a
+final LOD is always a reduction, so it had never seen a substitution — which
+is the project's own rule that a gate which has only seen one kind of input
+has not been tested.
+
+Fixed by classifying on `gained`, and the section-count check now indicts only
+a LOD that lost without gaining. Verified both directions on real meshes: the
+imposter LOD reports SUBSTITUTION and passes, while a genuine finding the same
+run surfaced — every tree drops its `_branch` material at LOD2 or LOD3, before
+the imposter — still exits 4. **The fix had to keep a real defect loud while
+silencing a false one, and that is the test it was held to**, not merely
+"does the imposter stop failing".
+
+### THE SHAPE OF ALL THREE
+
+Each came from asking the artefact a question nobody had asked it: the LOD
+group (never read by any tool), the group's effect on LOD count (read at
+source rather than assumed from a comment), and what a LOD *gained* rather
+than only what it lost. None was catchable by re-reading the plan, and the
+plan was confidently wrong about the first.

+## 2026-08-15 — FOUR DESIGN RULINGS, MADE BY THE FABLE MODEL UNDER RYAN'S DELEGATION
+
+**Provenance, stated first because it matters.** Ryan went to bed having
+said: *"you have full authority while im away ask the fable model if you
+need any guidance it will act as the decision maker for me while im away"*.
+The four rulings below were made by a Fable-model agent given the measured
+evidence, and are recorded as **model rulings under delegation — NOT as
+Ryan's own words.** Anything destructive to `LESSONS.md` or `RECIPES.md`
+still waits for him; these are all additive.
+
+### D1 — CAMERA RE-SITING: fix the four buried stations by Z-ONLY LIFT, hold the other fifteen
+
+Four ground stations measure BELOW the terrain — `sweep_0060` −4.38 m,
+`sweep_0350` −3.30 m, `trunk_base` −2.71 m, `lod_far` −1.19 m — because 19
+of 20 cameras were inherited byte-identical from a 4 m/vertex recipe.
+
+The ruling's load-bearing distinction: **a camera inside the hill has no
+baseline worth preserving**, so the "re-siting resets the A/B baseline"
+objection does not apply to those four. It applies fully to the stations
+that measure fine — above all `forest_floor` at +1.93 m, which carries the
+8.14 → 7.76 ms GPU series and both canopy A/Bs. Those stay byte-identical.
+
+Z-ONLY, not a mask re-site: keep XY and bearing, set Z from the engine line
+trace plus eye height. That preserves each station's SUBJECT — the defect is
+burial, not siting. `lod_far` especially must keep its XY because it pairs
+with `lod_near` 13 m away, and that pair geometry is the station's whole
+purpose.
+
+A full deliberate re-site becomes a named `camera_epoch` AFTER the D4
+re-scatter, so every frame can state which station set it belongs to.
+
+### D2 — TREES: import `PN_interactiveSpruceForest`; the Baltic Pine exports are DEFERRED
+
+The decisive argument is not cost, it is which gap gets closed. PN ships
+`MA_Imposter` plus 21 baked 4096² atlases, and BACKLOG's aerial-readability
+item calls imposters *"the only way real forest reaches airship altitude
+past the 730 m cull"*, against a WORLD_VISION ruling that makes aerial
+readability first-class. **Option (b) closes the project's largest recorded
+gap; four more Baltic Pine variants close none** — Scots pine already covers
+that role.
+
+Also: the forest has no sapling tier at all, and PN's 0.56–16.9 m range
+provides one. Its 10.5–16.9 m mature trees are botanically closer to a
+treeline stand than the 29.31 m spruce now placed.
+
+And the hazard asymmetry: the PVE export path was one click from writing
+skeletal meshes over gitignored vendor sources git cannot restore. Spending
+~72 minutes of 4-core compute through a fail-open path to buy marginal
+variety is the wrong side of *prefer an input that cannot express the
+catastrophic value*.
+
+FOUR CONDITIONS, and the third is the interesting one: wind is EDITED OUT
+for a static first import (`PN_GlobalUpdater` is a runtime Blueprint
+dependency; wiring it would violate single-variable measurement and pipeline
+rule 1); and **`LODGroup=None` on the 14 big trees makes explicit screen
+sizes and cull distances MANDATORY BEFORE PLACEMENT, encoded as a REFUSAL in
+the gate rather than a checklist item** — non-negotiable 3, an input that
+cannot express the bad state beating a gate that must remember to check.
+
+### D3 — UNDERSTORY: blueberry only, on the GRASS system, not instances
+
+Blueberry is the dominant spruce-forest understory to treeline in the Alps;
+blackberry and raspberry are montane-below-treeline and stay on disk. The
+484 MB demo ground texture stays behind.
+
+**Grass system rather than instances is precedent, not a new call** — the
+2026-08-08 ruling "carpet density on the grass system, instances only for
+sparse landmarks" is exactly this case. 19–178 cm carpet plants through the
+instance path would burn tens of thousands of the shared 250k ceiling that
+D4 needs for trees; through GrassOutput they cost zero instances.
+
+Two gates first: `uncorrected_pivot_errors()` on each mesh (the grass system
+corrects nothing and buries a box-centred pivot 50% by construction), and
+the landscape-material rebuild discipline, attended. Abort bar +1.5 ms GPU
+over the 7.76 ms baseline.
+
+### D4 — DENSITY: rise to ~220,000 instances as a CLOSURE GRADIENT, never uniform 70%
+
+WORLD_VISION already answers whether sparse is intended — it records foliage
+density as *"two orders of magnitude below reality"* and raising it as *"the
+next visible-quality step"*.
+
+But **70% cover was a reference-class error**: that is a managed lowland
+forestry number. Subalpine spruce near treeline is naturally patchy, 20–50%
+and gap-structured. **The defect is as much UNIFORMITY as count** — 23.28/ha
+spread evenly reads as thin everywhere instead of dense-here-open-there. The
+fix is structure: dense stands low on the arc thinning to krummholz at the
+640 m band top, which also makes WORLD_VISION's foothill→peak gradient
+visible.
+
+~220,000 is chosen to leave a **30k reserve under the shared 250k ceiling**,
+because that ceiling is ONE budget for rocks and vegetation by construction
+and the rocks are absent by ruling, not permanently. The ceiling is not
+raised: it was derived for this hardware, and 7.76 ms is an editor-viewport
+floor, not a shipped cost.
+
+ONE re-scatter combined with D2's mix, not two — every mass re-scatter
+re-rolls every position, so sequencing them separately would invalidate all
+positions twice for an intermediate state with no measurement value. Abort
+bar **11 ms GPU** at `forest_floor`.
+
+### SEQUENCING, which binds all four
+
+D1's Z-fix first (cheap, restores the instruments), then D2 import plus
+scratch-scene measurement, then D3's material rebuild, then the single D4
+re-scatter, then the D1 epoch re-site and a fresh sweep. Every step leaves
+`/Game/Alpine8K` recoverable by tag.

+**AMENDMENT, same day — `r.Nanite.Foliage` IS BROADER THAN ITS NAME.** The
+entry above called it the switch for Nanite foliage support. A second,
+wider search of the engine source found three more consumers, and two of
+them are other features entirely:
+
+    RenderUtils.cpp:1369-1376  NaniteAssembliesSupported()
+                               return bAllowNaniteFoliage || bAllowAssemblies
+    RenderUtils.cpp:1378-1385  NaniteVoxelsSupported()
+                               return bAllowNaniteFoliage || bAllowVoxels
+    TemporalSuperResolution.cpp:499-502
+                               return bNaniteFoliageEnabled
+                                      || ThinGeometryDetection != 0
+
+So setting it to 1 also enables **Nanite Assemblies**, **Nanite Voxels**
+and **TSR thin-geometry detection** — three separately-gated experimental
+features that would otherwise each need their own opt-in. On a machine that
+has already lost its GPU to a driver timeout, the blast radius of a flag is
+part of its cost.
+
+**AND IT BREAKS THE PLANNED A/B.** The recorded 8.14 ms at `forest_floor`
+with 154,018 conifers was measured with this flag OFF. Comparing a
+Nanite-foliage run against it would conflate Nanite foliage with a TSR
+path change. The fix is cheap because Nanite is PER-MESH: run the control
+with the flag ON and the trees still non-Nanite, then flip only the meshes.
+**The variable has to be the thing under test, not the thing that was
+convenient to change.**
+
+Every one of those reads is a `static const bool` initialised on first
+call, which independently corroborates the `ECVF_ReadOnly` startup-only
+behaviour rather than resting on the flag alone — two mechanisms, same
+conclusion.
+
+*Method note: the narrow grep that answered the original question was
+correct and incomplete. The broad one had been dispatched first, timed out
+into the background, and its result arrived after the conclusion was
+already committed. Reading it anyway is what caught this.*

+FIFTH LOD of 693 triangles; here it drops two sections at **LOD1, screen

+explicitly rejected. The tool prints this; the operator has to act on it.

+## THE TOOL CONFLATED "BUILD A CHAIN" WITH "DECLARE A SPECIES"
+
+Getting this far required fixing `make_mesh_lods.py`, whose only input was
+`foliage.species`. Anything needing an LOD chain had to pretend to be a

+refused all eight for two reasons that were both correct and both

+    place a mesh of unknown provenance) and says nothing about decimation.

+    placed, produced entirely by my staging file copying a template.

+    Norway_Spruce_01_A         139,851 -> 125,321   -10.4%    72,223 -> 72,223
+    Norway_Spruce_01_B         146,409 -> 128,707   -12.1%    74,952 -> 74,952
+    Norway_Spruce_01_C          71,915 ->  63,283   -12.0%    37,038 -> 37,038
+    Norway_Spruce_01_D          50,928 ->  44,952   -11.7%    26,568 -> 26,568
+    Baltic_Pine_01_A           351,106 -> 331,779    -5.5%   179,347 -> 179,154
+    Baltic_Pine_01_B           112,464 -> 105,668    -6.0%    58,513 -> 58,376
+    Baltic_Pine_01_C           225,899 -> 213,113    -5.7%   115,805 -> 115,671
+    Baltic_Pine_01_D           171,353 -> 160,755    -6.2%    87,927 -> 87,803
+
+**The triangle loss is the StaticMesh build welding and dropping degenerate
+faces, and the VERTEX column is what says so** — identical on all four
+spruces, within 0.1% on the pines, with bounds matching to under a
+centimetre everywhere. Triangles alone could not have distinguished that
+from geometry loss.
+
+### OPEN — AND IT BLOCKS ANY SCATTER
+
+**Every baked mesh has exactly ONE LOD**, because the skeletal sources do
+(PVE handles distance at runtime). The incumbent `fir_tree_01` ships
+505,494 / 126,374 / 22,293 / 3,892 and culls at 730 m. Scattering a
+single-LOD 125k-332k triangle tree into that cull disc would be
+catastrophic — the whole worst-case triangle budget assumes a chain.
+**Generate an LOD chain before placing anything**
+(`StaticMeshTools.generate_lods` + `set_lod_thresholds`, R5's
+`percent = screen_size^2`).
+
+### 5. REJECTED
+
+**`GeometryScript_NewAssets`.** The class is `GeometryScript_NewAssetUtils`.
+The wrong name read as knowledge and would have died on the first call.
+Resolve the enclosing class from the stub line number, not from memory.
+
+**`GeometryScript_MeshQueries.get_num_triangle_i_ds(mesh)`.** It is a METHOD
+on `DynamicMesh` (:265344), not a library function.
+
+**Requiring exact triangle parity as the acceptance test.** The StaticMesh
+build welds and removes degenerates, so no correct bake can match exactly.
+The first gate demanded equality and rejected all 8 correct bakes. Correct:
+bounds + materials + LOD count, with the triangle delta reported and
+bounded.
+
+**Wrapping the whole material loop in one `try`.** One failing
+`set_editor_property("imported_material_slot_name", ...)` zeroed the entire
+carry-over, and all 8 meshes came back with `WorldGridMaterial` in slot 0
+and nulls after it. **The gate caught it** — `materials 0` against 3
+expected. One optional cosmetic field must not be able to discard the
+assignment; make each step independently fault-tolerant.
+
+**Baking into the vendor folder.** Refused by the tool, by name. R-ASSET
+forbids authoring into a Fab folder and `Content/Megaplant_Library/` is
+gitignored, so the output would be lost work that looks like committed work
+the moment the pack is re-downloaded.
+
+**Deleting the failed bakes with `Remove-Item -Force`.** Standing rule 2's
+hook refused it, correctly. `.uasset` removal goes through the editor API
+(`AssetTools.delete`) under standing rule 4 anyway.

+The conifer intake ran. Both headline findings are about the SPEC being wrong
+for these assets, not about the assets being bad.
+
+**1. ALL EIGHT TREE VARIANTS ARE `SkeletalMesh`.** Discovered by a refusal, not
+by a check I had thought to write: `measure_rock_meshes`' payload came back
+with `lod_count: None` and
+`StaticMeshEditorSubsystem: Failed to convert parameter 'static_mesh'`. The
+bounds read fine (SkeletalMesh has `get_bounds` too) and `nanite_enabled` read

+`find_assets` filtered to `StaticMesh` under `/Game/Megaplant_Library` with
+name `Tree_` returns **zero rows**; only the `Instances/` parts are static.
+**The foliage system instances StaticMesh only**, so neither pack can join the
+153,796-instance forest as shipped. This is the blocking fact for any
+re-scatter and it was invisible from the store page, the file listing and the
+asset count alike.
+
+**2. NEITHER FOLIAGE MATERIAL IS ALPHA-MASKED.** `MI_Norway_Spruce_Foliage_01`
+and `MI_Baltic_Pine_01_Foliage` both carry `bOverride_BlendMode: true` with
+`blendMode: BLEND_Opaque`, parented to
+`/ProceduralVegetationEditor/.../MA_Foliage_Trees`. The needles are geometry.
+**So `conifer_asset_spec.md` section 2.3 — ">= 45% atlas opaque coverage", its
+"single most important criterion" — does not apply to these assets at all.**
+The incumbent's 24.02% is a fact about ALPHA-TESTED CARDS. Against opaque
+geometry it is not a smaller number, it is an answer to a different question.
+
+**AND MY OWN TOOL PRINTED A NUMBER THAT WAS NOT A MEASUREMENT.** The first run
+reported `T_Baltic_Pine_Foliage_CA` at **100.00% opaque** and I nearly read it
+as a spectacular result. The atlas's alpha channel is **255 everywhere — one
+distinct level**. There is no mask in it; the exporter did its job. "100%
+opaque" was the ABSENCE OF A MASK being rendered as full coverage, which is
+non-negotiable 6 wearing a number, produced by an instrument I had written
+twenty minutes earlier and had not fed a negative control.
+
+**What caught it was the magnitude, not a gate.** 100.00% and a clip spread of
+exactly 0.00 are both absurd on their face for a foliage atlas (NN11), and the
+rule that says look at the pixels before running a statistic (NN10) is what
+turned an absurd number into the alpha histogram that explained it. The tool
+now FAILS CLOSED on both conditions — constant alpha, and a consuming material
+that is not `BLEND_Masked` — and reports `coverage_applicable: false` with the
+reason instead of a percentage.
+
+**A THIRD, QUIETER DEFECT IN THE SAME TOOL.** `albedo_rgb_where_opaque` selects
+texels with alpha >= 0.5. When alpha is constant that selects EVERY texel, so
+Baltic Pine's `[137, 129, 101]` is the mean of the whole atlas including
+padding — not the needle colour. Same arithmetic, different question, and it
+would have been quoted as a needle albedo. The output now states its
+denominator explicitly (NN22).
+
+**THE CLIP-SPREAD TEST IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS, and this is worth keeping.**
+Norway Spruce reports spread 0.00 and I labelled it "effectively binary". It
+has **78 distinct alpha levels** — but every intermediate one is >= 179, so
+clip 0.1 and clip 0.5 select the identical texel set and the spread vanishes.
+The conclusion happened to be right; the test cannot distinguish "hard binary"
+from "soft fringe entirely above both thresholds". The distinct-level count is
+now reported alongside so the difference is visible.
+
+**WHAT THE MEASUREMENTS DO SAY, and it is good news on the axis that matters.**

+14.52 m: the mature variants sit inside the spec's 18-35 m band, where
+`fir_tree_01` never did. Pivots are at the trunk base to within 4-10 mm on all
+eight. Horizontal pivot offsets run 0.121-0.373 m; the worst, Norway Spruce A

+## 2026-08-14 (later) — THE FAB IMPORT ROOT CAUSE: A STAGING PATH ON A MACHINE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS
+
+The entry above stopped at "download does not progress, no error". The cause is
+now found, fixed, and PROVEN by a single-variable test. Recorded as a correction
+to that entry, not a replacement for it.
+
+**ROOT CAUSE.** `FabDownloader.cpp:314` sets
+
+    BuildInstallerConfiguration.StagingDirectory = FFabAssetsCache::GetCacheLocation() / AssetID
+
+and `FabAssetsCache.cpp:31` resolves that to
+`GetDefault<UFabSettings>()->CacheDirectoryPath.Path`. On this machine that read
+
+    CacheDirectoryPath=(Path="C:/Users/ryanb/AppData/Local/Temp/FabLibrary")
+
+**That user profile does not exist.** The project migrated to the `Admin`
+account on 2026-08-10; only `Admin` and `Public` are present under `C:/Users`.
+BuildPatchServices was being asked to stage a multi-hundred-megabyte install
+into a profile that was wiped four days ago, so nothing could ever be written.
+
+**WHY IT REPORTED SUCCESS, and this is the part worth keeping.**
+`FabDownloader.cpp:327` — `DownloadStats.DownloadedFiles = Manifest.GetBuildFileList()`.
+**The "downloaded files" list is read from the MANIFEST, never from the disk.**
+So `OnContentDownloadComplete` ran the success path, `CheckForDependencies`
+logged 138 real destination paths, and the workflow announced an import of files
+that had never been written. The 449 ms between "Add listing to project" and the
+file list was the tell — and it was a tell precisely because a file list is
+cheap and a download is not.
+
+**A GATE THAT EXISTS AND COULD NOT FIRE.** `FabSettings.cpp:33` DOES validate
+this exact field:
+
+    if (!FPaths::DirectoryExists(CacheDirectoryPath.Path) || FPaths::IsRelative(...))
+        CacheDirectoryPath = FDirectoryPath { FPlatformProcess::UserTempDir() / "FabLibrary" };
+
+and it would have repaired the path to the right one on the first try. But it
+lives in `PostEditChangeProperty` — **it only runs when a human edits the field
+in the UI.** A value loaded from an ini at startup is never checked. This is
+this project's non-negotiable 2 in someone else's code: *a gate that has only
+seen good input has not been tested*, sharpened to **a gate on the EDIT path
+does not guard the LOAD path**, which is where stale values actually come from.
+
+**THE PROOF WAS ACCIDENTALLY PERFECT.** I set the CDO's `CacheDirectoryPath` to
+this machine's temp path through the live editor (`ObjectTools.get_properties`
+read the stale value back from the RUNNING editor first, so ini and live CDO
+agreed — two representations). Then my click script **REFUSED**: the Fab window
+had been retitled, so it found no window and never clicked. Sixty seconds later
+the staging cache went 0 -> 123.8 -> 731.7 MB and the project gained 965.7 MB.
+**No click, no new request from me: only the config change, and a
+previously-issued request completed.** A cleaner single-variable test than the
+one I meant to run.
+
+**WHAT LANDED IS NOT WHAT I ASKED FOR, AND THAT MATTERS.**
+`Tree_Baltic_Pine`, 85 uassets, 965.7 MB — from listing `a2b04e81`, which Ryan
+opened as a PRODUCT PAGE (`LogFab: OpenInNewTab .../listings/a2b04e81`) and
+added from there. Norway Spruce (`f87364c9`) has been requested **four times** —
+03:44, 03:55, 04:15, 04:20 — including twice after the fix, and has never
+landed. So the stale staging path was NECESSARY but is NOT SUFFICIENT for that
+listing. The two differ in build (`Megaplan6269b53162feV1` vs
+`Megaplan043adaebd7d2V2`), in size (138 vs 85 assets), and in the route used:
+the library tile's "+" versus the product page's Add to Project. **The route is
+the one variable a human can change cheaply, and the successful one was the
+product page.**
+
+**AND THE FIX IS IN MEMORY ONLY.** `UFabSettings` is
+`config=EditorPerProjectUserSettings` in a Private header — not in the
+PythonStub, and it registers no settings section
+(`ConfigSettingsToolset.ListSections` finds no "Fab" under Editor or Project),
+so there is no scripted route to persist it. The ini still names the old
+profile, and the next editor start reinstates the bug. Persisting it needs the
+Fab settings UI, whose `PostEditChangeProperty` calls `SaveConfig()` — the same
+handler whose validation would have prevented all of this.
+
+**THE GENERAL SHAPE, because this is the third instance tonight.** The MCP
+server logged "Starting" before its socket bound. Fab logged a file list it read
+from a manifest rather than from disk. Both are **success reported from the
+INTENT rather than from the ARTEFACT**, and in both cases the artefact was one
+cheap check away. The migration sweep that deliberately left old-profile paths
+in NARRATIVE records was right to; what nobody checked was whether any live
+CONFIG still pointed there.

+from the two rectangles and asserted uniform, rather than hardcoded, so a

+position is read back before every click and a mismatch refuses.

+## 2026-08-14 — THE MCP SERVER "STARTED" THREE TIMES AND NEVER LISTENED
+
+`/mcp` reported `ConnectionRefused at http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp`. The editor
+was running, the plugins were enabled, and the editor's own log said the
+server was up. Every one of those was true and none of them was the state.
+
+**TWO INDEPENDENT FAULTS, stacked, and each alone looked like the whole
+problem.**
+
+**FAULT 1 — THE CLIENT AND THE SERVER WERE ON DIFFERENT PORTS.** `.mcp.json`
+dials 8001. `Saved/Config/WindowsEditor/EditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini:3836`
+sets `ServerPortNumber=8000` with `bAutoStartServer=True`. Whoever generated
+the client config and whoever set the port did not agree, and nothing checks
+that they do — non-negotiable 24 across a process boundary.
+
+**FAULT 2, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH THE ENTRY — THE ENGINE DEFAULT PORT WAS
+ALREADY TAKEN, AND THE PLUGIN REPORTED SUCCESS ANYWAY.** IncrediBuild's
+`Manager.exe` (PID 20712) holds `[::]:8000` dual-stack on this machine, so UE
+cannot bind it. The log, in order:
+
+    LogModelContextProtocol: Starting MCP server on port 8000 (override ...)
+    LogHttpServerModule: Error: ... the existing listener for port 8000 is
+                         not listening/bound and listeners are still enabled
+    LogHttpListener: Error: HttpListener unable to bind to 127.0.0.1:8000
+    LogHttpServerModule: Warning: failed to start listening on port 8000!
+                         (bFailOnBindFailure? false)
+    LogHttpServerModule: All listeners started
+
+**The MCP category announces the start BEFORE the bind and never retracts
+it.** The failure is logged under `LogHttpListener` and `LogHttpServerModule`,
+two categories a reader grepping for `ModelContextProtocol` never sees, and
+the last line of the sequence reads *"All listeners started"*. Root cause is
+`ModelContextProtocolServer.cpp:432` — `GetHttpRouter(ActiveServerPort)` is
+called with `bFailOnBindFailure = false`, so a bind failure is a warning and
+the server object goes on believing it is serving.
+
+`Saved/Config/ConsoleHistory.ini` records three `ModelContextProtocol.StartServer`
+attempts. All three "succeeded". None ever listened.
+
+**THE GENERAL RULE, and this project already owns it in another costume:
+A SERVER'S OWN LOG IS THE SAME CLASS OF INSTRUMENT AS A SETTER'S READ-BACK.**
+Non-negotiable 8 says verify with a different instrument than the one that made
+the claim. "Starting MCP server on port 8000" is the claim. The only instrument
+that answers the actual question is a socket opened from OUTSIDE the process.
+`scripts/start_mcp_server.py` sends a real MCP `initialize` over TCP and treats
+anything else — including the editor's own cheerful log line — as unproven.
+
+**AND A RESPONDER IS NOT AN IDENTITY.** Probing 8000 got a TCP connection and
+an HTTP response, from IncrediBuild. Had the tool tested reachability alone it
+would have declared the MCP server healthy while pointing at a build
+accelerator. Two things were tried as discriminators and only one works:
+
+  * `serverInfo` — **USELESS HERE.** UE 5.8 returns
+    `{"name": "", "title": "", "version": ""}`, measured. A tool keyed on the
+    server's name reads a live editor as anonymous.
+  * **the OWNING PID of the listening socket, compared against the PID the
+    rule-7-verified editor reports for itself.** This is the one that
+    separates, and it is what refuses 8000 by name (`Manager`, PID 20712).
+
+**A TRAP THAT COST A CORRECT TOOL A FALSE VERDICT.** The first probe parsed
+the response line by line, because MCP's streamable transport frames replies as
+`data: {...}`. UE pretty-prints its JSON across twenty lines, so no line was a
+complete object and the tool reported a server that WAS serving as dead. That
+is non-negotiable 6 in the small: "I could not parse it" printed as "it is not
+there". Fixed by trying the whole body first, SSE framing second.
+
+**AND `StartServer` MOVES THE SERVER RATHER THAN ADDING ONE.** Starting on
+8009 to run a control left 8001 still BOUND by the editor's HTTP module,
+answering 404 on `/mcp`. So a stale listener owned by our own process is
+indistinguishable from a squatter by port occupancy alone — the PID check is
+what makes the rebind safe, and the "control" run was not a control at all: it
+mutated the thing under test. A second run at the intended port was needed to
+put it back.
+
+**WHAT IS STILL WRONG AFTER THE FIX, stated plainly.** The runtime fix is
+`ModelContextProtocol.StartServer 8001` and it dies with the editor process.
+`ServerPortNumber` is still 8000 in the saved ini, so the next editor start
+will auto-start into IncrediBuild's port and silently serve nothing again.
+`UModelContextProtocolSettings` is `UCLASS(MinimalAPI, ...)` and is NOT in the
+Python stub — the same shape as `UEditorPerformanceSettings` — so there is no
+scripted route to persist it. It takes the Editor Preferences UI, or an ini
+edit with the editor closed. **This is the third instance in this project of
+"the file is not the state" and its mirror: here the state is not the file
+either, and only one of the two can be fixed from Python.**
+
+**CLAUDE.md's ENVIRONMENT line said `unreal-mcp at 127.0.0.1:8000`.** It was
+written when that was the intended port and was never true of a working
+connection. Corrected in the same commit — a derived record about project
+state, checked against the artefact at the moment it was written
+(non-negotiable 15).

+## R-MCP — GETTING THE UE 5.8 MCP SERVER SERVING (2026-08-14)
+
+**Status: PROVEN both directions on 2026-08-14** — serving on 8001 verified by
+an out-of-process `initialize`; the foreign-port refusal fired on 8000 naming
+`Manager` PID 20712.
+
+The server is Epic's shipped `ModelContextProtocol` plugin, not a third-party
+tool. It runs INSIDE the editor, so it exists only while an editor is open.
+
+### PROCEDURE
+
+    python scripts/start_mcp_server.py --port 8001
+
+Then `/mcp` in Claude Code. That is the whole procedure when the editor is
+running. The script gates on conduct rule 7, refuses a port owned by anyone
+else, sends the console command, and PROVES the result with a socket opened
+from outside the editor.
+
+### LOCKED VALUES
+
+    port                    8001        NOT the engine default 8000
+    url path                /mcp
+    client config           .mcp.json   {"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp"}
+    tools/list returns      3           list_toolsets, describe_toolset, call_tool
+    toolsets discoverable   52          via list_toolsets, because
+                                        bEnableToolSearch=True
+    plugins required        ModelContextProtocol, MCPClientToolset, AllToolsets
+                            all three already Enabled in LandscapeLab.uproject
+
+**WHY 8001 AND NOT THE ENGINE DEFAULT.** `ModelContextProtocol.h:45` sets
+`DefaultServerPort = 8000`; on THIS machine IncrediBuild's `Manager.exe` holds
+`[::]:8000` dual-stack and UE cannot bind it. 8000 is unusable here and the
+failure is silent — see REJECTED.
+
+### PERSISTENCE — NOT DONE, AND IT NEEDS THE UI
+
+`scripts/start_mcp_server.py` sets RUNTIME state. It dies with the editor.
+`Saved/Config/WindowsEditor/EditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini:3836` still reads
+`ServerPortNumber=8000` with `bAutoStartServer=True`, so every fresh editor
+auto-starts into the occupied port and serves nothing until the script is run.
+
+To fix durably, one of:
+
+  * **Editor Preferences → Plugins → Model Context Protocol → Server Port
+    Number = 8001.** The editor writes its own saved ini; safe while running.
+  * **With the editor CLOSED**, edit that ini line to 8001. Editing it while
+    the editor runs is pointless — the in-memory CDO is rewritten over the file
+    at shutdown.
+  * `-ModelContextProtocolPort=8001` on the editor command line
+    (`ModelContextProtocolSettings.cpp:17-27`), if the editor is ever launched
+    by script rather than from the Epic Launcher.
+
+**There is NO Python route.** `UModelContextProtocolSettings` is
+`UCLASS(MinimalAPI, config=EditorPerProjectUserSettings)` and appears nowhere in
+`LandscapeLab/Intermediate/PythonStub/unreal.py` — same shape as
+`UEditorPerformanceSettings`.
+
+### VERIFICATION
+
+    python scripts/start_mcp_server.py --port 8001
+    -> SERVING : MCP protocol 2025-06-18, capabilities: resources, tools
+    -> exit 0
+
+The verdict comes from an MCP `initialize` sent over TCP from a separate
+process, NOT from the editor's log. Re-running when already serving short-
+circuits at the pre-flight probe and exits 0 without touching the editor.
+
+### 5. REJECTED
+
+**`ModelContextProtocol.StartServer` on a port another process holds.**
+Symptom: the command prints nothing wrong, `LogModelContextProtocol` says
+*"Starting MCP server on port N"*, and the very next lines — under DIFFERENT
+log categories — read `HttpListener unable to bind to 127.0.0.1:N`, `failed to
+start listening on port N! (bFailOnBindFailure? false)`, and then, last,
+*"All listeners started"*. Nothing serves. Cause:
+`ModelContextProtocolServer.cpp:432` calls `GetHttpRouter` with
+`bFailOnBindFailure = false`. Correct: check the owner first and pick a free
+port. **Do not grep only `ModelContextProtocol` in the log — the failure is not
+in that category.**
+
+**Trusting the editor log that the server is up.** Same class as a setter's own
+read-back (non-negotiable 8). The only valid instrument is a socket from
+outside the process.
+
+**Identifying the server by `serverInfo`.** UE 5.8 returns
+`{"name":"","title":"","version":""}` — measured 2026-08-14. Anything keyed on
+it reads a live server as anonymous. Correct: compare the listening socket's
+OWNING PID against the PID the rule-7-verified editor reports for itself.
+
+**Treating a TCP connection as proof the MCP server is up.** Probing 8000
+CONNECTS — to IncrediBuild. Correct: require a JSON-RPC `result` carrying
+`protocolVersion`.
+
+**Parsing the initialize reply line by line.** MCP's streamable transport frames
+replies as `data: {...}`, so a line-at-a-time parser is the obvious shape — and
+UE pretty-prints its JSON across ~20 lines, so no single line is a complete
+object and a SERVING server reads as dead (exit 5). Correct: try the whole body
+first, SSE framing second.
+
+**Running `StartServer <other port>` as a "control".** It does not add a second
+server, it MOVES the one there is, and leaves the old port bound by the
+editor's HTTP module answering 404 on `/mcp`. The control mutates the thing
+under test and the intended port must then be re-bound.
+
+**`ServerPortNumber` in `LandscapeLab/Config/DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini`.**
+The saved per-user ini is layered ON TOP of the project default, so a project
+pin loses to the existing `ServerPortNumber=8000` in `Saved/Config/`. Not a
+persistence route while that line exists.

commit 60d4d8c2ebe00a78d54771cb48f1a75a6e84866e
Author: ryanb <ryanbme83@gmail.com>

    Narrative for the 8K re-terrain: six parameters that only ever had one value
    
    The LESSONS half of tonight. R-ALPINE8K already carries the specification; this
    is the story, and the story is not really about terrain.
    
    THE ROUTE was decided on evidence rather than preference. The sweep world is
    NOT a Gaea build -- it is stamp-composited by this project's own compositor,
    and AlpineLab_8129 is the Gaea one and a different mountain. Regenerating the
    base natively was ruled out because terrain/alpine_heightmap.png HAS NO
    SIDECAR: its generation parameters were never recorded, so a native 8129 run
    would mean guessing a seed and ~30 knobs and would produce a different mountain.
    Both checked before choosing.
    
    What made the re-composite work is that the nine stamp placements are expressed
    in METRES, so they ported across a 4x resolution change untouched. Non-negotiable
    19 was written to stop two passes disagreeing about a physical fact; it paid off
    here in a direction it was not written for -- being physical is what made those
    values portable at all.
    
    THE SIX DEFECTS, and they are one defect:
    
      1  derive_aux_maps output names   would overwrite Alpine's flow map
      2  droplet count (per-cell)       flow map 6.5x too sparse
      3  make_macro_variation name      producer and consumer disagree
      4  max_steps (per-cell)           talus routing would not converge
      5  talus cache path               ACTUALLY overwrote Alpine's cache
      6  landscape actor Z              terrain 1280 m too low
    
    Every one is a per-biome or per-resolution quantity written as though only one
    biome and one resolution would ever exist. This repo has had exactly one of each
    since it began; tonight is the first time a second existed, and all six surfaced
    within about four hours of that happening.
    
    THE RULE IS NOT "BE CAREFUL WITH CONSTANTS". A constant is indistinguishable
    from a correct value until a second case exists -- there is nothing to compare
    against, so no amount of review finds these. The defence is creating the second
    case deliberately, which is what this exercise turned out to be.
    
    THE INSTRUCTIVE PAIR is 2 and 4: the SAME defect, a per-cell budget tuned at
    2017. talus_deposit asserts its own convergence and refused loudly, using a
    message written on 2026-08-03 for a mistyped value and now catching a resolution
    change nobody anticipated. The droplet path asserts nothing and emitted a
    plausible wrong answer with an exit code of zero. The only difference between a
    loud refusal and a silent wrong answer was whether somebody had written the
    assertion.
    
    AND ONE MISLABELLING WORTH MORE THAN THE DEFECT IT HID: foliage.rock_scatter's
    own _comment declares it "SHARED PHYSICAL FACT ... properties of rock, not style
    knobs". True of every member except max_steps, which is a solver iteration
    budget in CELLS. An auditor scanning that block for resolution-dependence would
    read the comment and stop. A comment that is true of a block's INTENT and false
    of its CONTENTS is worse than none: it redirects the search.
    
    THE READ-BACK LESSON, which generalises furthest. The landscape imported at
    actor Z 0 against a recipe saying 128000 cm, putting the terrain at -1280..+272 m
    instead of 0..1552 m. The read-back block PRINTED the location and ASSERTED only
    the scale. Scale right, components right, proxies right, and the one wrong number
    sat in a list of correct ones.
    
    A NUMBER THAT IS DISPLAYED BUT NEVER COMPARED IS NOT VERIFIED. It is decoration
    that reads like evidence, and it is worse than an absent check, because a reader
    scanning the output sees the location printed and concludes it was checked.
    
    Of the six: two caught by reading code before running it, one by an assertion
    written three months earlier for a different reason, one by `git status`, one by
    an assertion added because the previous four had made me distrust read-backs, and
    one by comparing a statistic against the terrain it was meant to reproduce.
    NOT ONE was caught by the tool that produced it reporting failure.

+**It is not a Gaea terrain.** The sweep world is STAMP-COMPOSITED by this

+different mountain. The question "regenerate it in Gaea at 8129?" had an answer
+before it had an opinion.
+
+**It could not be regenerated natively either**, and this was forced rather than
+preferred: `terrain/alpine_heightmap.png` HAS NO SIDECAR. Its generation
+parameters were never recorded, so `make_alpine_terrain.py` at 8129 would mean
+guessing a seed and ~30 knobs and would produce a different mountain. Checked
+before choosing.
+
+**So: re-composite at 8129.** The landform comes from the existing base
+(upsampled, hence unchanged); the new detail comes from the nine 4096-pixel
+stamps, which the 2017 grid was box-reducing by between 3.9x and 9.6x, and from
+a 28 m detail-relief band that at 4 m/texel spanned SEVEN texels and at 1 m
+spans twenty-eight. The nine placements ported UNTOUCHED because they are
+expressed in METRES and the compositor converts with
+`spacing_m = scale_xy_cm/100` — being physical is what made them portable, which
+is non-negotiable 19 paying off in a direction it was not written for.
+
+Verified: correlation 0.999824, landform mae 1.41 m at 240 m scale = 0.254% of
+mean elevation. **And the detail gain reported honestly at 1.41x above the old
+Nyquist, sub-metre in absolute terms** — the whole-map mean-gradient figure of
+1.071x was discarded as a misleading denominator, since it is dominated by
+mountain-scale slopes identical in both maps by construction.
+
+### THE ACTUAL FINDING: SIX PARAMETERS THAT HAD ONLY EVER HAD ONE VALUE
+
+| # | Parameter | What it silently did at 8129 | Caught by |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `derive_aux_maps` output names | would overwrite /Game/Alpine's flow map | reading the code first |
+| 2 | droplet count (per-cell) | flow map 6.5x too sparse | **nothing** |
+| 3 | `make_macro_variation` output name | producer/consumer disagree | reading the code first |
+| 4 | `max_steps` (per-cell) | talus routing would not converge | its own assertion |
+| 5 | talus cache path | **actually overwrote** Alpine's cache | `git status` |
+| 6 | landscape actor Z | terrain 1280 m too low | a read-back I added |
+
+**Every one is a quantity that is per-biome or per-resolution, written as though
+only one biome and one resolution would ever exist.** This repo has had exactly
+one of each since it began. Tonight is the first time a second of either
+existed, and all six became visible within about four hours of that happening.
+
+That is the general rule and it is not "be careful with constants": **a constant
+is indistinguishable from a correct value until a second case exists.** No
+amount of review finds these, because until the second case there is nothing to
+compare against. The defence is not vigilance, it is creating the second case
+deliberately and early — which is what this whole exercise turned out to be.
+
+### THE TWO THAT DID NOT REFUSE ARE THE INTERESTING PAIR
+
+`max_steps` and the droplet count are the SAME defect: a per-cell budget tuned at
+2017. At 8129 one of them refused loudly and one produced a plausible wrong
+answer:
+
+- `talus_deposit` asserts its own convergence — *"it used all 600 steps with
+  108.2550 units still in transit ... Mass conservation does not detect this"* —
+  a message written on 2026-08-03 after `max_steps=60` truncated the field and
+  reported success. **It has now caught the same class in a case nobody
+  anticipated, a resolution change rather than a typo.**
+- the droplet path asserts nothing, so it emitted a flow map with 7.27% of cells
+  non-zero against alpine's 47.42%, reported success, and would have put 157,554
+  conifers on the wrong watercourses.
+
+The only difference between a loud refusal and a silent wrong answer was whether
+somebody had written the assertion. Nothing about the two defects differs in
+kind, severity, or detectability-in-principle.
+
+### AND ONE MISLABELLING THAT MADE A DEFECT UNSEARCHABLE
+
+`foliage.rock_scatter` carries a `_comment` declaring it *"SHARED PHYSICAL FACT
+... These are properties of rock, not style knobs."* Every member honours that —
+`repose_deg`, `runout_m`, `source_smooth_m` are degrees and metres — **except
+`max_steps`, which is a solver iteration budget in CELLS.** An auditor scanning
+that block for resolution-dependence would read the comment and stop. The
+comment was true of the block's intent and false of its contents, which is worse
+than no comment: it actively redirects the search.
+
+### A READ-BACK THAT PRINTED WITHOUT COMPARING
+
+The landscape imported at actor Z 0 where the recipe says 128000 cm. UE puts
+heightmap value h at `world_z = actor_z + (h-32768)*scale_z/128`, so h=0 lands
+half a span BELOW the actor, while `place_foliage.py:124` computes
+`height_m = (h/65535)*(z_scale_cm/100)` — h=0 at world zero. They agree only at
+`actor_z = z_scale_cm/2`. The terrain sat at −1280..+272 m instead of 0..1552 m,
+and every conifer would have been planted in mid-air.
+
+**The read-back block PRINTED the location from its first version and ASSERTED
+only the scale.** Scale was right, component count was right, proxy count was
+right, and the one wrong number was displayed in a list of correct ones.
+
+**A NUMBER THAT IS DISPLAYED BUT NEVER COMPARED IS NOT VERIFIED. It is
+decoration that reads like evidence** — and it is more dangerous than an absent
+check, because a reader scanning the output sees a location printed and concludes
+the location was checked. Now an explicit refusal that names the arithmetic and
+states how far every instance would have been off.
+
+### WHAT CAUGHT WHAT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING
+
+Two of six were caught by reading code before running it. One by an assertion
+written three months earlier for a different reason. One by `git status`. One by
+an assertion I added *because* the previous four had made me suspicious of
+read-backs. And one — the droplet count — by comparing a statistic against the
+terrain it was supposed to reproduce, which is the only reason it was found at
+all.
+
+**Not one was caught by the thing that produced it reporting failure.**

+### THE ROUTE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS ONES ARE WRONG
+
+**Not Gaea.** The sweep terrain is not a Gaea build — it is STAMP-COMPOSITED by
+this project's own `composite_stamps.py` from `terrain/alpine_heightmap.png`
+plus nine StampIT placements. `AlpineLab_8129` is the Gaea terrain and is a
+DIFFERENT MOUNTAIN. Regenerating in Gaea would have delivered a terrain Ryan
+did not ask for.
+
+**Not a plain upsample.** 2017 -> 8129 adds no information. That is the same
+Nyquist cap already measured as the cause of "terrain reads as smooth rolling
+mounds": 4.00 m per texel, and a cliff lip, a ledge and an arete are all sub-4 m.
+
+**Not a native regeneration of the base either, and this was forced by
+evidence:** `terrain/alpine_heightmap.png` has NO SIDECAR. Its generation
+parameters were never recorded, so regenerating it at 8129 with
+`make_alpine_terrain.py` would mean guessing a seed and ~30 parameters and would
+produce a different mountain — the one outcome the task forbids. Checked before
+choosing, not assumed.
+
+**THE ROUTE TAKEN: re-composite at 8129.** The landform comes from the existing
+base (upsampled, so unchanged); the NEW DETAIL comes from two sources that are
+native at 1 m and were being thrown away at 4 m.
+
+    1. THE STAMPS. All nine sources are 4096 x 4096. At 4 m/texel they were
+       box-reduced by between 3.9x and 9.6x before use. At 1 m/texel the
+       largest is fed at 4096 -> 4096, no reduction at all. The compositor
+       prints this per placement: "source 4096px -> box-reduced /1 -> 4096px".
+    2. THE DETAIL-RELIEF BAND. 28 m wavelength. At 4 m/texel that is SEVEN
+       texels per wavelength — aliased. At 1 m/texel it is twenty-eight.
+
+`composite_stamps` converts placements with `spacing_m = scale_xy_cm/100`
+(:1087) and `half_px = size_m*0.5/spacing_m` (:463), so placements expressed in
+METRES land on the same world positions at any resolution. **That is what makes
+the landform identical rather than merely similar**, and it is why the nine
+placements were copied across untouched.
+
+### PROCEDURE
+
+    1. python scripts/resample_heightmap.py --input terrain/alpine_heightmap.png \
+              --output terrain/alpine_8k_base.png --size 8129 --go
+    2. python scripts/composite_stamps.py --recipe recipes/alpine_8k.json --dry-run
+    3. python scripts/composite_stamps.py --recipe recipes/alpine_8k.json --allow-clamp
+    4. adopt: copy alpine_8k_stamped.png -> alpine_8k.png, asserting SHA-256
+       against the sidecar's output_sha256 BEFORE the recipe is edited
+    5. set heightmap.source = terrain/alpine_8k.png
+
+### THE ACCEPTANCE TEST — IS IT THE SAME MOUNTAIN?
+
+Downsample the 8129 composite back to 2017 and compare against
+`alpine_heightmap_v2.png`, the exact map the sweep photos were rendered from:
+
+    correlation, raw full frame          0.999824
+    landform mae at ~240 m scale         1.41 m   = 0.254% of mean elevation
+    landform mae at ~100 m scale         1.83 m   = 0.330%
+    landform mae at  ~32 m scale         2.21 m   = 0.397%
+    median residual, full frame          0.95 m
+
+**Same mountain, to a quarter of a percent of mean elevation.**
+
+### WHAT THE DETAIL GAIN ACTUALLY IS — measured, and smaller than it sounds
+
+Mean gradient magnitude over the whole map says **1.071x**, but that statistic
+is dominated by mountain-scale slopes that are identical in both maps by
+construction — the misleading-denominator class (non-negotiable 22). The
+question that matters is how much content exists ABOVE THE OLD NYQUIST:
+
+    features finer than    new 8k    old v2 upsampled    ratio
+    ~8 m (old Nyquist)     0.431 m        0.305 m        1.41x
+    ~16 m                  0.793 m        0.694 m        1.14x
+    ~32 m                  1.400 m        1.335 m        1.05x
+
+    conditioned on the stamp footprints (66.87% of the map)   1.43x at ~8 m
+    OFF the footprints (the relief band, the control)         1.35x at ~8 m
+
+**+41% more sub-8-metre relief amplitude, and it is SUB-METRE in absolute
+terms.** Both mechanisms contribute roughly equally, which is what the
+footprint/off-footprint split is for — it separates "the stamps resolved" from
+"the relief band resolved" instead of asserting both.
+
+**Read this honestly: the terrain-level gain is real but modest.** The dominant
+near-field detail on this project comes from NANITE DISPLACEMENT at the material
+level, measured 2026-08-13 at 41.1x the noise floor at ground level with visible
+stepped strata and cast shadow. The 1 m grid is what lets the silhouette carry
+that; it is not itself the whole win.
+
+### WHAT WAS CLAMPED, AND WHY IT IS NOTHING
+
+    CLAMPED: 5 px below 0 (lost 0.35 m), 0 px above 65535
+
+Five pixels of 66,080,641, at the ZERO FLOOR, from bicubic ringing in the
+upsampled base meeting a MIN-blend stamp. The original 2017 run recorded
+`clamped: false, pre_clamp_min 0.0, pre_clamp_max 39676`; ours is
+`0..39743` — 0.17% higher at the top, consistent with stamps resolving more
+detail. Clamping restores exactly the floor the original had.
+
+### KNOWN APPROXIMATIONS, stated rather than buried
+
+- The base is an UPSAMPLE. No information is added at the large scale, by
+  construction. See the "not a native regeneration" paragraph for why.
+- **World extent grows 8064 m -> 8128 m (+0.79%)**, because 8129 vertices at
+  1 m cannot span 8064 m. The landform is therefore scaled up 0.79% in XY. This
+  also means a direct pixel comparison against the old map misregisters by up to
+  ~8 px at the edges and 0 at the centre, which is why the acceptance test above
+  reports low-frequency agreement and an interior-only figure separately.
+- `z_scale_cm` is UNCHANGED at 256000.0. The heightmap values did not move, so
+  the vertical mapping must not either.

+## R-ALPINE8K REJECTED
+
+**Putting the derivation notes in the recipe as a `_derivation` key.**
+SYMPTOM: `REFUSE: recipe is not schema-valid: unknown top-level key:
+_derivation`. The validator is RIGHT — `schema.md:19` makes unknown top-level
+keys an error precisely so a typo cannot be silently ignored. CORRECT: the
+derivation lives here in RECIPES.md. **Adding a schema key to hold prose is the
+"invent a key to get past the validator" antipattern**, and it would have made
+every future typo in that position legal.
+
+**Committing the 8K intermediates inline.** SYMPTOM: three 104 MB PNGs
+permanently in git history, in a repo whose `.gitattributes` header warns that
+retrofitting LFS "means rewriting history". CORRECT: `terrain/*_8k*.png` goes to
+LFS from its FIRST commit, and only the ADOPTED map is committed at all —
+`alpine_8k_base.png` and `alpine_8k_stamped.png` are deterministic
+intermediates, gitignored with their regeneration commands recorded in
+`.gitignore` itself.
+
+**`*.png filter=lfs` as the fix for the above.** SYMPTOM: existing 2017-class
+heightmaps migrate to LFS on their next write while their history stays inline,
+producing exactly the split-storage retrofit the header warns about. CORRECT:
+scope the rule to the size class that actually changed.
+
+**Using `resample_heightmap.py`'s output AS a terrain.** SYMPTOM: 16x the
+memory for the same mountain. It is ONLY correct as the large-scale half of a
+pipeline whose detail arrives from elsewhere, and its own docstring says so.
+
+**LANCZOS on a heightmap upsample.** Not committed — the default is bicubic —
+but recorded because the temptation grows with the enlargement factor.
+`resize_gaea_build.py`'s ruling is that *"Lanczos OVERSHOOTS at ridges, and an
+overshoot in a heightmap is a spike or a terrace"*. That reasoning is STRONGER
+at 4.03x than at the 1.56% resize it was written for: a ring of false terraces
+along every arete.

Author: ryanb <ryanbme83@gmail.com>

    Exposure solved for THIS terrain: -1.786 -> -1.867 EV, verified on pixels
    
    Closes the CURRENT STATE item that refused to port alpine's constant. The
    recipe carried -1.786 under a comment reading, in its own words, "PORTED
    VERBATIM from recipes/alpine.json".
    
    WHY EXPOSURE IS THE ONE TERM IN THAT BLOCK THAT CANNOT TRAVEL. Sun, sky and
    fog describe the ATMOSPHERE and port between scenes intact -- same planet, same
    12 degree sun. Exposure describes what it takes to centre a render of a
    particular GROUND, so it depends on that ground's albedo.
    
        this terrain, top-down linear luma     0.3385
        solver target for sunlit terrain       0.3201   (albedo 0.2675)
        /Game/Alpine, IDENTICAL method         0.3169
    
    ~6.8% brighter than alpine under identical lighting; implied effective albedo
    ~0.286 against alpine's measured 0.2675.
    
        bias = -1.786 - log2(0.3385 / 0.3201) = -1.867 EV
    
    Denominator stated (non-negotiable 22): top_down from 6 km at 60 deg FOV frames
    ~6.9 km of an 8.128 km terrain, so it is ALL TERRAIN AND NO SKY -- a sky
    fraction would bias the mean.
    
    VERIFIED THREE WAYS, none of them the setter's return value: applied from the
    recipe via apply_lighting.py; read back from the LIVE PostProcessVolume as
    AEM_MANUAL / bias -1.8669999837875366 / OVERRIDDEN (so it is in effect, not an
    inert default); and RE-MEASURED ON PIXELS, 0.3385 -> 0.3246 against a 0.3201
    target. Level saved, 1 package, verified present on disk.
    
    THE NEAR-MISS IS THE POINT OF THIS COMMIT. The correct answer is -1.867.
    Alpine's Lumen-corrected -1.897 is 0.03 EV away -- close enough that applying
    it would have produced a render nobody could fault, while the record carried a
    value derived from LUMEN BOUNCE ON A DIFFERENT SCENE when the actual cause here
    is HIGHER GROUND ALBEDO ON THIS ONE. Same neighbourhood, different mechanism,

    A WRONG DERIVATION THAT LANDS ON A NEARLY-RIGHT NUMBER IS THE HARDEST KIND TO
    CATCH, BECAUSE THE OUTPUT VALIDATES IT. The defence is not "check the number",

commit 6901a3eb1eb046e489a457832318adcd29a702e0
Author: ryanb <ryanbme83@gmail.com>
Date:   2026-08-13 21:40:39 -0700

    The editor's 60 fps cap is root-caused, and it is not what anyone suspected
    
    Every frame-time figure this project has ever taken in the editor sat at
    exactly 16.67 ms and was labelled "a 60 fps cap, not a cost" without the cap
    ever being identified. It is identified now, at a source line.
    
    RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY ASSUMPTION -- each was read, not guessed:
    
        t.MaxFPS            0.0    unlimited. The board's long-standing suspect,
                                   and it is NOT the cause here.
        r.VSync             0.0
        rhi.SyncInterval    1 -> 0 moved FrameTime not at all (16.67 -> 16.71,
                                   inside run-to-run variance)
        bSmoothFrameRate    False
        battery heuristic   inert  -- PowerLineStatus Online, Win32_Battery 2 (AC)
    
    CAUSE: UEditorEngine::GetMaxTickRate, EditorEngine.cpp:2523-2566.
    
        if( !bSmoothFrameRate && GIsEditor && !GIsPlayInEditorWorld )
        {
            MaxTickRate = 1.0f / DeltaTime;                                    //   current rate
            ... FMath::Max(MaxTickRate, SmoothedFrameRateRange.GetLowerBound)  //   5
            ... FMath::Min(MaxTickRate, SmoothedFrameRateRange.GetUpperBound)  // 120
        }
    
    `MaxTickRate = 1.0f / DeltaTime` CLAMPS THE EDITOR TO THE RATE IT IS ALREADY
    RUNNING AT. It is a hysteresis loop -- the previous frame's DeltaTime sets this
    frame's ceiling -- so once anything parks the editor at 60 it stays at 60, and
    no cvar will move it. There is also a hard 120 fps editor ceiling from
    SmoothedFrameRateRange [5, 120] that applies EVEN THOUGH smoothing is disabled,
    which the engine's own comment states outright: "Clamp editor frame rate, even
    if smoothing is disabled".
    
    THE SAME FUNCTION IS WHERE TWO OTHER NUMBERS ON THE BOARD COME FROM, and
    neither was previously traced: `MaxTickRate = 3.0f` under
    ShouldThrottleCPUUsage() is the 333.33 ms / 3 fps backgrounded idle the
    throttle investigation measured on 2026-08-10, and the 60 Hz battery limit
    ("Laptops should throttle to 60 hz in editor to reduce battery drain") is
    defeatable with r.DontLimitOnBattery 1 if this machine is ever run unplugged.
    
    CONSEQUENCE, and it is a correction to method rather than to any number:
    EDITOR FRAME RATE IS NOT A VALID HEADROOM INSTRUMENT AND NEVER WAS. FrameTime
    in the editor reports the clamp, not the scene. GPU, RenderThread and
    GameThread times are unaffected -- the work is done and the engine then sleeps
    -- so every conclusion in the frame-cost artefact stands unchanged.
    
    Headroom, stated from the instrument that is valid: 4.95 ms of GPU work in a
    16.67 ms frame is ~30% GPU utilisation with ~11.7 ms unused. The ~200 fps
    GPU-bound ceiling that follows from 4.95 ms is ARITHMETIC, not a measurement,
    and is labelled as such -- nothing here demonstrates the editor reaching it.

+## 2026-08-13 — LANDSCAPE NANITE BUILT AT 256/256, AND THE PLAN'S MECHANISM WAS WRONG
+
+Ryan ruled option A: raise the page file, then build Nanite. Both happened. The
+build succeeded. **Three of the four things the handoff believed about it were
+false, and each was settled by measurement rather than by argument.**
+
+### WHAT LANDED
+
+    proxies with a built Nanite mesh   256 / 256
+    parent ALandscape                    0      (expected — owns no components)
+    external actor packages           3.03 GB, 256 carrying LandscapeNaniteMesh
+    peak system commit                189 GB of a 228.8 GB limit
+    peak editor private               176.6 GB
+    wall clock                        ~7 min building + 609 s saving
+
+Verified through two representations, per non-negotiable 0: the live editor
+reads 256/256 via `LandscapeNaniteComponent.static_mesh`, and an independent
+byte scan of the 264 external actor packages on disk finds the
+`LandscapeNaniteMesh` token in 256 of them, each over 1 MB. Neither reads the
+other's source.
+
+**OPTION A WAS THE RIGHT CALL AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO.** The build reached
+189 GB of commit. The old limit was 60.1 GB. No amount of batching would have
+fitted this build under 60 GB, and no amount of page file would have been
+needed above ~200 GB. The handoff called it "a good bet and not a guarantee";
+the bet paid, and the reason it paid is now measured rather than hoped.
+
+### THE 9.3-HOUR ESTIMATE WAS WRONG BY TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE
+
+Recorded cost was 131.0 s per proxy x 256 = 9.3 hours, extrapolated from the
+ONE proxy that completed before the OOM kill. The real figure, given commit
+headroom, is about seven minutes for all 256.
+
+The extrapolation's flaw is instructive: it measured a proxy completing inside
+a dying, memory-starved editor that was thrashing against a 60 GB ceiling, and
+it assumed proxies build SERIALLY. They do not — `BuildNanite` dispatches every
+proxy's build concurrently. **A per-unit cost measured under contention, then
+multiplied by the number of units, double-counts the contention.** The number
+was a measurement of thrashing wearing the units of build time.
+
+### THE BATCH PARAMETER DOES NOT BOUND THE WORK — ROOT CAUSE AT A SOURCE LINE
+
+The handoff's plan was "expose `InProxiesToBuild` -> bounded peak memory,
+resumable batches". The plugin was written, compiled, and called. It logged
+
+    BuildLandscapeNaniteForProxies: submitting 8 proxies (0 already up to date)
+
+and the engine then built **all 256** and drove commit to 189 GB. Measured, not
+inferred: 256 distinct `LandscapeNaniteMesh` packages appear in the log, and
+the batch's own submitted count was 8.
+
+**ROOT CAUSE.** `ALandscapeProxy::PostEditChangeProperty` calls
+`InvalidateOrUpdateNaniteRepresentation` for `bEnableNanite`,
+`bNaniteSkirtEnabled` **and** `NaniteSkirtDepth` — `LandscapeEdit.cpp:6131-6141`.
+**Setting the flag IS the build dispatch.** The setup phase flagged 257 actors,
+which queued 256 builds before `BuildNanite` was called at all; the batched
+call then added 8 and `FinishAllNaniteBuildsInFlightNow`
+(`LandscapeSubsystem.cpp:1179`) waited on **every build in flight**, not on the
+batch. The timeline confirms the direction rather than merely being consistent
+with it: submit at 03:30:10.503, first mesh build at 03:30:12.826.
+
+**THE GENERAL RULE. A PARAMETER THAT BOUNDS A CALL DOES NOT BOUND THE WORK IF
+SOMETHING ELSE ALREADY QUEUED IT.** The batch parameter is necessary and not
+sufficient; to bound memory the FLAGGING must be batched too. The existence of
+a plausible lever is not evidence that the lever is attached to anything, and
+this one was reasoned about across two sessions without once being measured.
+
+Worth naming: the engine's own throttle
+(`landscape.Nanite.MaxSimultaneousMultithreadBuilds`) IS dead code — its only
+call site is commented out at `LandscapeNaniteComponent.cpp:273` — and that
+part of the prior session's reasoning was checked at source and held. The error
+was not sloppiness about the engine; it was assuming the flag-setting phase was
+inert because nobody had asked what it did.
+
+### AN ACCESSOR THAT ANSWERED WRONGLY, AND ALMOST INVERTED THE VERDICT
+
+`get_component_by_class(LandscapeNaniteComponent)` + `get_static_mesh()` read
+**0 of 256** on a world whose saved packages demonstrably held 256 Nanite
+meshes. It did not raise. It returned a confident zero, and the tool printed
+"STOPPED EARLY ... 256 proxies remain".
+
+The correct form — plural `get_components_by_class` plus the reflected
+`static_mesh` property — reads 256/256 on the same world in the same state.
+`verify_cold_boot.py:52-61` has used it correctly all along, so the project
+already CONTAINED the right spelling while a newer tool guessed a wrong one.
+
+This is non-negotiable 23 with its worst face showing. An invented accessor
+that RAISES is a nuisance; one that EXISTS and returns a plausible falsy answer
+is a defect that propagates into a verdict. And note which instrument caught
+it: not a second live read, but the bytes on disk — a different
+representation, non-negotiable 0 doing the work again.
+
+**Swept in the same commit** (non-negotiable 4): `landscape_nanite_build.py`
+carried the identical wrong accessor, and there it was not cosmetic — its
+exit-5 gate reads *"the build returned success and NO proxy has a built Nanite
+mesh; treat the build as NOT done"*, so the wrong accessor converts a COMPLETED
+build into a reported FAILURE.
+
+### A CHECK THAT MUTATED WHAT IT MEASURED
+
+`nanite_batch_build.py`'s first verdict phase reused the SETTING payload to
+take its final reading — re-firing `PostEditChangeProperty` on all 257 actors
+at the exact moment it claimed to be observing them. Non-negotiable 5, written
+by someone who had just read the rule. Split into a `PAYLOAD_READ` that sets
+nothing, and exposed as `--verify-only`.
+
+### AND ONE INSTRUMENT LIED ABOUT THE EDITOR BEING HUNG
+
+For eleven minutes the editor showed a frozen log, private memory constant to
+the megabyte, CPU at 0.03 CPU-s per wall-s, and `MainWindowTitle` reading
+"Unreal Editor - LandscapeLab" with no map name. Every one of those said HUNG.
+It was compiling shaders.
+
+Two separate errors. First, `Get-Process().MainWindowTitle` happily returns the
+**SPLASH SCREEN's** title — enumerating top-level windows showed the only
+visible window had class `SplashScreenClass`. The handoff's advice that "the
+only tell was the WINDOW TITLE" is therefore too weak: **the tell is the window
+CLASS**, because the title is identical on the splash and the real thing.
+Second, shader compilation happens OUT OF PROCESS in `ShaderCompileWorker`
+children, so the parent's CPU and memory are flat by construction while real
+work proceeds — and I sampled at a moment when zero workers happened to be
+alive between batches. The instrument that settled it was DDC growth on disk:
+1 MiB -> 0.28 GB -> 10.73 GB.
+
+**A process that looks idle is not idle if its work is in child processes.**
+Measure the work where the work happens.
+
+### THE SECOND THROTTLE IS NOT IN EFFECT — FOUND WHILE CHECKING SOMETHING ELSE
+
+Read from the LIVE editor CDO:
+
+    bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground   False   <- the project's pin IS in effect
+    bAllowSlateThrottling           True    <- but Config/DefaultEditorSettings.ini:56 sets False
+
+So the second throttle's override has never applied, in the file the FIRST
+one's fix was moved to. Non-negotiable 17 again, and it survived the very
+session that fixed its sibling. NOT swept — it changes editor responsiveness
+during measurement and wants its own single-variable run.
+
+Also recorded, because it defeats this project's existing approach: `dir()` on
+that CDO reached by object path exposes **no reflected properties at all** —
+only generic UObject methods. `measure_frame_cost.py` ENUMERATES property names
+and filters for "hrottle", which finds NOTHING and reads as absence. Asking for
+the C++ names directly (`bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground`) works. An enumeration
+that returns an empty list is "I could not look", not "it is not there"
+(non-negotiable 6).
