+## 2026-08-12 (later still) — four pure-black 4K frames, and every tool said success
+
+**Context.** Ryan asked for the 8129 terrain taken all the way to a render
+matching what AlpineLab_v1 produced at 4033. Masks imported, material built and
+assigned, four viewpoints captured at 3840x2160.
+
+### THE CAPTURES WERE BLACK AND NOTHING SAID SO
+
+`park_viewport` read back **0.000 cm on every axis**. `highres_shot` printed
+`WROTE ... 150,569 bytes` four times and exited 0. Four different cameras,
+across a mountain range.
+
+    mean 0.0000   std 0.0000   min 0.000   max 0.000
+    and all four the SAME SHA256
+
+**The tell was not any tool's output. It was that four different cameras
+produced BYTE-IDENTICAL FILE SIZES.** A 4K terrain frame is megabytes; 150 KB
+is what a uniform image compresses to. Nothing in the pipeline compares two
+frames to each other, so nothing could notice.
+
+**Cause:** `LevelEditorSubsystem.new_level()` makes an EMPTY partitioned
+world — no directional light, no sky, no atmosphere. The level had a landscape
+and nothing else and had never been lit since it was created hours earlier.
+Every step in between — import, material build, assign, save, connectivity
+audit, sampler audit, frame-cost capture — was about geometry and graph
+topology, and not one of them had any reason to mention the absence of a sun.
+
+This is precisely the gap `verify_frames.py` was built for: it *"refuses a
+verdict unless every frame is present, correctly sized and TONALLY
+NON-TRIVIAL"*. `highres_shot.py` has no such check. **A file was written; a
+frame was not rendered**, and only the second of those is what anyone wanted.
+
+### AND IT INVALIDATED A NUMBER I HAD ALREADY REPORTED
+
+Earlier the same session I reported GPUTime **2.92 / 3.16 / 3.20 ms** for the
+8129 landscape, with a sky-vs-terrain control reading 3.20 against 2.98 and a
+conclusion that *"the landscape contributes ~0.2 ms; the geometry is cheap"*.
+
+**All of it was measured on this unlit black level.** The control that was
+supposed to discriminate terrain from sky was comparing **black terrain against
+black sky**, which is why it barely separated — and I attributed that weak
+separation to the landscape genuinely being cheap.
+
+Re-measured lit and surfaced, full residency:
+
+    GPUTime  5.07 mean, 5.05 p50, 5.30 p90     (was 3.16 unlit, default material)
+    RenderThreadTime 4.57                       (was 3.25)
+    GameThreadTime   9.57
+
+**The conclusion survives — 5 ms against a 16.67 ms cap is still cheap — but it
+survived by luck, not by method.** Had the terrain been expensive, the unlit
+measurement would have said it was cheap and I would have reported a GO on a
+scene with no lighting in it.
+
+**The lesson is not "check for lights".** It is that I ran a discriminating
+control, got a weak result, and explained the weak result with a *hypothesis
+about the subject* rather than asking whether the SCENE was in a fit state to
+be measured at all. A control that fails to separate is evidence about the
+whole setup, not just about the variable.
+
+That is the third instance today of the same family: the residency gate
+(measuring 1.6% of the landscape), the `r.ScreenPercentage` control (a lever
+not connected to the editor viewport), and now this. In all three the
+instrument was fine and the SITUATION was not, and in all three the number
+looked reportable.
+
+### TWO SPELLINGS OF ONE FACT, FIXED IN THE TOOL
+
+`apply_lighting.py` derived its actor-parking height from `location_cm` +
+`z_scale_cm` — the biome-recipe spelling. The AlpineLab evaluation recipes
+spell the same physical quantity `origin_cm` + `scale_z`.
+
+Making the recipe carry BOTH would put one quantity in one file twice under two
+names, free to drift with nothing to notice. The tool now reads either,
+prefers the biome spelling, and REFUSES when neither is present. UE landscape
+Z: scale 100 spans 512 m, so `scale_z` 180.8358 -> 92,588 cm.
+
+**Where a consumer and a producer disagree about a NAME, the fix belongs in
+the consumer. Where they disagree about a VALUE, it belongs in the producer.**
+
+### THE MASK SETTINGS WERE DECIDED BY READING THE ASSETS, BECAUSE THE RECORDS DISAGREED
+
+    ue5_import_alpinelab.py docstring   TC_VECTOR_DISPLACEMENTMAP
+    2026-08-10 handoff                  BC4
+    the live v1 assets                  TC_GRAYSCALE
+
+Three of our own records, three answers, and only the assets were ever
+authoritative — non-negotiable 15 with the derived records being ours.
+
+`max_texture_size` is the one setting deliberately changed, **in order to keep
+the result the same**: v1's 2048 over 4032 m is 1.97 m per texel; 2048 over
+8128 m would be 3.97. 4096 gives 1.98 and parity. v1's cap was imposed by a
+15.4 GB laptop and a 994 MiB DDC limit that no longer exist; copying it out of
+deference would have silently halved the surfacing resolution of the terrain
+this whole exercise exists to sharpen.
+
+**Bit depth had to be settled at engine source** because the reflected `source`
+property raises on this build: `Texture.cpp:4312-4316`, *"Grayscale is G8
+output, unless source is specifically G16"*. A 16-bit grayscale PNG imports as
+`TSF_G16`, so `TC_GRAYSCALE` yields G16. That is load-bearing: the material
+applies gains up to 128, and at G8 the smallest non-zero value (1/255) would
+land at 0.50 — past the deposits ramp's 0.18 out-edge — making that mask BINARY
+on the GPU while the CPU reference computed a mean weight of 0.083 from the
+16-bit source. Every percentile in the recipe would have described something
+the renderer never saw.
+
+### ONE MATERIAL VALUE DID NOT CARRY, AND THE DIAGNOSIS DECIDED THE FIX
+
+At v1's flow gain 12.0 the 8129 mask covers 2.3366% against 3.3306%. The cause
+is physical, not a resample artefact — **p99 halves (0.0822 -> 0.0400) while
+p99.9 RISES (0.9265 -> 0.9386)**. The higher-resolution erosion resolves
+narrower, better-defined channels. Had p99.9 fallen too, that would have been a
+resample smearing the mask and the fix would have been the resample, not the
+gain.
+
+Retuned to 21.4 by sweeping against BOTH statistics rather than solving for
+one. Recorded in the recipe as a LOOK-PARITY decision, not a correctness one:
+keeping 12.0 would be more faithful to what the simulation computed.

+## 2026-08-12 — LandscapeLab becomes a C++ project, and four names meant something other than they read
+
+**Context.** Ryan ruled for the scope change: a small editor plugin to expose
+the three landscape operations UE 5.8 declares `LANDSCAPE_API` and never marks
+`UFUNCTION`. The session built it, created the 8129² landscape, and did NOT
+get a frame-cost number. What it did get was four instances of one defect
+class, which is why they are logged together.
+
+### 1. A ban read off a directory name was a claim about a different quantity
+
+`Windows_SDK.json` bans MSVC `14.44.0-14.44.35210`. The installed toolchain
+directory is `MSVC/14.44.35207`, inside that range, and I was one sentence
+from reporting Ryan's v143 insurance component as banned. UBT reports:
+
+    Using Visual Studio 14.44.35228 toolchain (...MSVC/14.44.35207)
+
+`AddVisualCppToolChain` (`MicrosoftPlatformSDK.cs:1145-1160`) parses the
+DIRECTORY into `Family` and checks `BannedVisualCppVersions` against
+`Version`. Directory name and compiler version are different quantities that
+look like the same one. The build succeeded first try, in 79.5 s.
+
+**Rule:** when a gate compares two version-shaped things, find out which one
+it reads before predicting its answer.
+
+### 2. A `UFUNCTION` returning `bool` with out-params LOSES the `bool`
+
+I wrote the C++ and still could not predict its Python shape. Declared:
+
+    static bool GetHeightmapResolution(path, int32& W, int32& H, FString& Err)
+
+Generated:
+
+    get_heightmap_resolution(path) -> (out_width, out_height, out_error) or None
+
+The `bool` is consumed as a success flag and the ENTIRE TUPLE collapses to
+`None` when it is false — so `OutError`, the only thing worth having on a
+failure, is unreachable exactly when it is needed. All three functions are now
+`void` with an explicit `bOutSuccess`.
+
+**CLAUDE.md already says "the reflected Python surface is the contract, not
+the C++ header." This is that rule from the other side: AUTHORSHIP OF THE C++
+IS NOT AUTHORITY OVER THE BINDING.** Found by unpacking 4 values from a
+3-tuple, which is the cheap failure; the expensive one unpacks correctly and
+means something else.
+
+### 3. `unreal.Rotator(ROLL, PITCH, YAW)` — roll first
+
+C++ `FRotator` is `(Pitch, Yaw, Roll)`. The reflected constructor
+(`PythonStub unreal.py:66750`) is `(roll, pitch, yaw)`. My camera call passed
+`(pitch, yaw, roll)` and put a −25° ROLL on a level camera. **The frame was
+still full of terrain, so nothing looked wrong.** Caught only because the
+script prints the read-back rotation beside what was asked for.
+
+### 4. The setting was in the right SECTION of the wrong FILE — and this is NOT non-negotiable 17
+
+`bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground=False` has sat in
+`DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini` since 2026-08-10 under the correct
+section `[/Script/UnrealEd.EditorPerformanceSettings]`, recorded as
+"UNVERIFIED — my own fix did not take", filed under non-negotiable 17.
+
+`UEditorPerformanceSettings` is `UCLASS(minimalapi, config=EditorSettings)`
+(`EditorPerformanceSettings.h:31`). Its overrides come from
+`DefaultEditorSettings.ini`. **The override was never read at all.**
+
+17 says a file records what was OVERRIDDEN, not what is in effect — a value
+that IS read and then beaten by a later write. This is the failure one level
+below: a value never read, in a file the class does not consult, under a
+section name so plausible that every grep for the key finds it and confirms
+the wrong conclusion.

+## R-CREATE — CREATING AND IMPORTING A LANDSCAPE FROM PYTHON (2026-08-12)

+**Status: PROVEN ONCE.** Executed successfully for `/Game/GaeaLab/AlpineLab_8129`
+on 2026-08-12. Not replayed cold.
+
+**This recipe supersedes R-GAEA step 4's "the landscape is created BY HAND in
+Landscape Mode".** That instruction was correct for stock UE 5.8 and is now
+obsolete: `LandscapeLab/Plugins/LandscapeLabEditor` exposes the missing
+`UFUNCTION`s. R-GAEA's DIAGNOSIS stands — the engine ships no route — but its
+PROCEDURE does not.
+
+### WHY A PLUGIN WAS REQUIRED
+
+Verified at source, not remembered:
+
+| Operation | Declaration | Reachable from Python? |
+|---|---|---|
+| `ALandscapeProxy::Import` | `LandscapeProxy.h:1416`, `LANDSCAPE_API`, no `UFUNCTION` | no |
+| `ULandscapeSubsystem::BuildNanite` | `LandscapeSubsystem.h:148` | no |
+| `ULandscapeSubsystem::ChangeGridSize` | `LandscapeSubsystem.h:153` | no |
+
+There is no `ULandscapeEditorSubsystem`. The wrappers follow the engine's own
+New Landscape button, `LandscapeEditorDetailCustomization_NewLandscape.cpp:1150-1290`
+— the only editor call site of `Import`. The ordering (spawn → set material →
+`Import` → `UpdateLayerInfoMap` → `ChangeGridSize`) is taken from it.
+
+### THE PROCEDURE
+
+    python scripts/create_landscape_from_build.py            # DRY RUN, contacts nothing
+    python scripts/create_landscape_from_build.py --go
+
+Defaults are build 006 → `/Game/GaeaLab/AlpineLab_8129`. Everything else is
+derived from the build, not from arguments.
+
+**PRECONDITION, enforced with exit 4: a FRESH editor process.** Creating a
+level is a map transition, which is the `EditorServer.cpp:1951` fatal that
+`open_level.py`'s reference scrub exists to prevent. The scrub lives at one
+choke point and copying it is what non-negotiable 4a rejects — so this script
+requires a state in which the hazard cannot exist (a namespace that has never
+bound a UObject) and asserts it rather than assuming it. Non-negotiable 3.
+
+**To OPEN the level afterwards**, launch the editor with the map as an
+argument. There is no in-process transition on a startup load:
+
+    UnrealEditor.exe <uproject> /Game/GaeaLab/AlpineLab_8129
+
+Use the PowerShell tool, never Git Bash — the msys-game-path hook exists
+because Git Bash rewrites a bare `/Game/...` into a filesystem path.
+
+### LOCKED VALUES — the 8129 landscape
+
+    heightmap    build 006 UE5_Ready/AlpineLabHeight.png, 8129², 16-bit
+    layout       32 × 32 components, 2 sections × 127 quads
+                 32 × 254 + 1 = 8129, closes EXACTLY
+    vertices     66,080,641
+    scale_xy     100.0 cm        extent 8128 m
+    scale_z      180.8358010032807   → 925.88 m span
+    grid size    2 → 256 streaming proxies × 4 components = 1024
+    location     (-406400, -406400, 0) cm, centred on the origin

+Full provenance in `recipes/alpinelab_8129.json`.

+### VERIFICATION — and one instrument is not enough
+
+`create_landscape_from_build.py` reads back the engine's record of what it was
+told. `landscape_inventory.py` derives geometry from engine section bases and
+never sees the plan:
+
+    section base X/Y   32 distinct, 0..7874, step 254
+    implied resolution 8129
+    components         1024 across 256 proxies

+Two representations, one answer. **Neither is a check on the SURFACE** — no
+collision trace and no render has been taken, so "the terrain is the right
+terrain" is UNVERIFIED.

+## R-CREATE REJECTED
+
+**`sections_per_component` = 4 → REFUSED.**
+Only 1 and 2 are legal. The documented "1 or 4" is wrong and is on CLAUDE.md's
+casualty list. The plugin refuses before spawning.
+
+**Letting the engine resample a mismatched heightmap → REFUSED at the gate.**
+Asking for a 4033 layout against the 8129 file produces:
+
+    Heightmap '...' does not match the requested layout. Requested 4033 x 4033
+    (= 32 components x 2 sections x 63 quads + 1). File offers: 8129x8129.
+    REFUSED rather than resampled.
+
+**and the acceptance test is that the LEVEL ACTOR COUNT IS UNCHANGED** (138 →
+138), not that an error string was returned. A refusal that has already
+spawned a landscape is not a refusal; this project has shipped a "refusal"
+that mutated and saved before printing REFUSE.
+
+**Hashing `UE5_Ready/AlpineLabHeight.png` against the build sidecar → WRONG
+ARTEFACT.** The sidecar's hashes describe the PRE-RESIZE file in the build
+root; `UE5_Ready` holds a BICUBIC RESAMPLE (`resize_gaea_build.py`, "RESIZE,
+NEVER CROP" — masks must stay in register with the height). The shipped bytes
+CANNOT match, by design, and the gate refuses a correct build.
+**Correct:** hash the ROOT file against `output_sha256` (proves the sidecar
+describes THIS build), and separately check that the shipped file is on the
+SAME VALUE SCALE — root mean 20467.894 vs shipped 20467.894, drift 0.0000%.
+**The mean is the discriminating statistic and the range is not.** Resampling
+cannot invalidate the Z scale, which maps the uint16 RANGE to metres and is
+blind to what the data does inside it. A SECOND normalization pass would
+restretch the resampled data, still span 0..65535, and make every height
+wrong. Range cannot see that. The mean can.
+
+**`unreal.Rotator(pitch, yaw, roll)` → SILENTLY WRONG.**
+The reflected constructor is `(roll, pitch, yaw)` — `PythonStub unreal.py:66750`.
+The C++ `FRotator(Pitch, Yaw, Roll)` order does not apply. Symptom: a camera
+that is level with an unexplained tilt, still full of terrain, with nothing
+obviously wrong. Always print the read-back rotation beside the requested one.
+
+**A `UFUNCTION` returning `bool` alongside out-params → the `bool` VANISHES.**
+Python generates `(...out params) or None`; the tuple collapses to `None` when
+the bool is false, taking `OutError` with it exactly when it is needed.
+**Correct:** return `void` and add an explicit `bOutSuccess` out-param.
+
+**Predicting UBT's MSVC ban from the toolchain DIRECTORY NAME → WRONG
+QUANTITY.** Directory `MSVC/14.44.35207` sits inside the banned range
+`14.44.0-14.44.35210`; the compiler is 14.44.**35228** and is fine.
+`AddVisualCppToolChain` (`MicrosoftPlatformSDK.cs:1145-1160`) parses the
+directory into `Family` and checks the ban against `Version`.
+
+**Adding a primary game module to make the project C++ → UNNECESSARY, and it
+forces a `.uproject` edit standing rule 4 forbids.**
+`PluginManager.cpp:421-425` enables a plugin whose descriptor says
+`EnabledByDefault` and whose `GetLoadedFrom()` is `EPluginLoadedFrom::Project`
+**unconditionally, with no `.uproject` entry**. Two `Target.cs` files with
+EMPTY `ExtraModuleNames` are sufficient; UBT merely iterates that list
+(`UEBuildTarget.cs:5025-5030`) and `LaunchModuleName` defaults to the engine's
+own `Launch`. `LandscapeLab.uproject` is byte-identical across the conversion.
+
+---
+

+        --frames 300 --warmup 45 --tag <label>
+
+Writes a per-frame CSV to `LandscapeLab/Saved/Profiling/CSV/` via
+`CsvProfile frames=N` (`CsvProfiler.cpp:1076-1080`). **This is the first GPU
+figure in this project with an artefact on disk.** Every prior number,
+including R13's 94.45 / 75.71 ms, is an attended viewport reading the pass
+audit filed as UNVERIFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION.
+
+### THE THROTTLE — root-caused, and the fix is a DIFFERENT FILE
+
+`bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground` belongs to `UEditorPerformanceSettings`,
+`UCLASS(minimalapi, config=EditorSettings)` — `EditorPerformanceSettings.h:31`.
+Its overrides are read from **`DefaultEditorSettings.ini`**.
+
+This project had it in `DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini` under the
+CORRECT section name since 2026-08-10, which is why it looked right and never
+worked. Now pinned in `LandscapeLab/Config/DefaultEditorSettings.ini`.
+
+Proven behaviourally, single variable, editor BACKGROUNDED both times:
+
+    wrong ini file              0.08 CPU-s per wall-s   FrameTime 333.33 ms
+    DefaultEditorSettings.ini   1.70 CPU-s per wall-s   FrameTime  16.67 ms
+
+**333.33 ms is exactly 3 fps and is the editor's unfocused idle rate, not a
+cost.** The script samples editor CPU per wall-second across the capture and
+exits **5 with NO VERDICT** below 0.30.
+

+## 2026-08-11e — A MODAL DIALOG SAVED THE WORLD, AND THREE INSTRUMENTS WERE MUTE
+
+Ryan said "save the world and lock it in". It was already saved, by
+something nobody scripted, and finding that out took four instruments
+because the first three said nothing was wrong.
+
+### WHAT HAPPENED
+
+The landscape-Nanite state had been live-but-unsaved since 18:26, flagged
+in CURRENT STATE as a foot-gun in these words: *"any Save All, editor-close
+prompt, or script that saves the level will persist it."*
+
+At 05:10:35 UTC the editor's own log records:
+
+    LogSlate: Window 'Save Content' being destroyed
+    LogFileHelpers: InternalPromptForCheckoutAndSave started...
+    LogFileHelpers: Saving Package: /Game/__ExternalActors__/Alpine/...
+
+A **Save Content modal dialog** was resolved with Save, writing 257
+external actor packages and M_AutoLandscape — 284 MB. My
+`save_level.py --save` ran two minutes later and correctly reported
+"OWNED by the recipe (0), nothing to save", because by then nothing was
+dirty.
+
+I cannot attribute the click. What is certain is that it was not a
+scripted action, and that the outcome happened to be the one requested —
+which is luck, not control.
+
+**THE RULE: A LIVE-BUT-UNSAVED EDITOR STATE IS NOT OWNED BY THE SESSION
+THAT CREATED IT. It is owned by whoever next touches the window.** The
+deliberate sequencing — measure before writing 1,484 packages — was
+correct reasoning and it left a decision lying on a desk for four hours.
+If a state is worth not saving yet, it is worth saying so where the
+person at the keyboard can see it, not only in CURRENT STATE.
+
+### THE THREE MUTE INSTRUMENTS, WHICH IS THE REAL LESSON
+
+1. **`save_level --save` said "nothing to save".** Correct, and
+   completely uninformative — it cannot distinguish "your change was
+   never dirty" from "your change was already written by someone else".
+   A negative from a dirty-package probe carries no information about
+   whether the work landed.
+2. **`git status` said CLEAN.** A stat-cache artifact: the 257 files had
+   been rewritten but git had not re-stat'd them. A later `git status`
+   showed all 258. **A clean tree immediately after an external process
+   writes files is not evidence of anything.**
+3. **`git cat-file -s HEAD:<pkg>` said 130 bytes.** That is the LFS
+   POINTER, not the object — the same trap recorded on 2026-08-08, where
+   comparing `git show HEAD:<path>` against a working file reported 100%
+   of bytes differing. **I walked into a documented trap while
+   investigating.** The size comparison it produced (33 KB vs 284 MB) was
+   meaningless and briefly looked like a finding.
+
+**What actually found it:** `find -newermt` on package mtimes — 257 files
+at 22:10 — and then the ENGINE'S OWN LOG. Which is exactly what the
+standing rule for verifying a save already says: package mtimes and the
+artefact, never the tool's report.
+
+### VERIFYING THE SAVE FROM THE BYTES, WITH A CONTROL
+
+The live editor said 257 enabled / 256 built meshes. That reads memory,
+and Pass 1 sat "saved and verified" for three days on side-records exactly
+like that. So the saved `.uasset` bytes were scanned directly:
+
+    saved by this operation   scanned 257   carrying a Nanite token 257
+        bEnableNanite               257
+        LandscapeNaniteMesh         256      <- parent ALandscape has none
+        LandscapeNaniteComponent    256
+    POSITIVE CONTROL, not saved   scanned 400   carrying a token   0
+
+The control is what makes it evidence. A token found in every file it is
+looked for in proves nothing until it is shown ABSENT where it should be —
+400 untouched actor packages return zero on all three tokens. And the
+256/257 split reproduces the live reading, from bytes the live check never
+opened.
+
+**STILL NOT PROVEN, and it is a different claim: that the world LOADS
+from these bytes.** A name-table token says the data was serialised, not
+that a cold open reconstructs a working Nanite landscape. Only a restart
+closes that, and it has not run.
+
+### AND THE SAVE SWEPT VENDOR CONTENT
+
+`check_fab_boundary` reports SIX Fab source files modified in place, all
+KiteDemo rock material instances. A Save Content dialog saves EVERYTHING
+dirty, including gitignored vendor content, and those edits vanish on
+re-download. **Not re-baselined** — the tool says to re-baseline only once
+the drift is "understood and deliberately accepted", and neither is true.
+This is a second, quieter cost of leaving a modal save available: it does
+not save only the thing you were thinking about.

+## 2026-08-11c — A GATE THAT SAID 19 OF 19 OVER A RUN THAT PRODUCED 18
+
+### THE DEFECT
+
+`capture.py` wrote **18 of 19** frames for the `5080hqfix` sweep —
+`ridge_wide` was never written — and **exited 0** without reporting the
+shortfall. Then `verify_frames.py`, run bare, printed:
+
+    present and usable : 19 of 19
+    VERDICT: every expected frame is present and carries real tonal
+    structure. The instrument produced evidence.
+
+Both statements are false about that run, and the second is the exact
+sentence this tool exists to make trustworthy.
+
+### ROOT CAUSE, AND THE TOOL WAS NEVER WRONG
+
+`verify_frames --tag` defaults to `""`, and the glob is
+
+    *__<camera>__*<suffix>.png          suffix = "_" + tag, or ""
+
+With no tag that matches **every tag ever captured**, and `hits[-1]` takes
+the newest by mtime. So a camera skipped by the run in question falls back
+to some previous run's frame and reports `ok`.
+
+Run correctly it is completely right:
+
+    verify_frames --tag 5080hqfix   ->  18 of 19, MISSING ridge_wide, exit 3
+    verify_frames                   ->  19 of 19, "produced evidence", exit 0
+
+**The capability was always there. The DEFAULT was the trap, and I used
+the default twice** — including in the message where I reported 19/19 to
+Ryan.
+
+### THE RULE
+
+**A PERMISSIVE DEFAULT ON A GATE IS A GATE THAT ANSWERS A DIFFERENT
+QUESTION THAN THE ONE ASKED.** Nobody runs `verify_frames` to ask "does a
+frame for this camera exist somewhere in the archive". They run it to ask
+"did the run I just did produce its evidence". The default answered the
+first question in the voice of the second.
+
+This is a new shape for this project. The catalogue so far is about gates
+that could not SEE a defect — a self-masking reference population, an
+epsilon below the quantization floor, a residency gate that passed exactly
+when loading failed. This one saw perfectly and was **pointed at the wrong
+population**, silently, by its own default. A gate's SCOPE is part of its
+correctness, and an unscoped default makes the scope invisible at the call
+site.
+
+**FIXED BY FAILING CLOSED, not by warning.** A bare run now returns 4 and
+prints VERDICT WITHHELD; it refuses to print a green verdict at all,
+because the whole purpose of the tool is that "no defects found" must
+never be printable over evidence that does not exist (non-negotiable 1:
+unknown is never yes). Proven three directions:
+
+    bare              exit 4   VERDICT WITHHELD
+    --tag 5080hq      exit 0   19 of 19, pass
+    --tag 5080hqfix   exit 3   18 of 19, MISSING ridge_wide
+
+### AND `ridge_wide` HAS FORM
+
+It is the same station that timed out and never wrote during the
+2026-08-08 shader stall, which is recorded in that handoff. Two skips, two
+different sessions, same camera, and **both times the run reported
+success**. `capture.py` exiting 0 on a short run is the upstream half of
+this defect and is NOT fixed — logged to BACKLOG. A capture that cannot
+count its own output is the producer-side mirror of a verifier that cannot
+scope its own input.
+

    the uncentred samples, because that blend compares two heights against
    each other and shifting them by different constants would change which
    surface wins.
    
    NOT YET MEASURED: the 5080hqfix capture was running when this was
    committed. Expect a SMALL number and do not read a null as failure — this
    recovers a DC offset and a layer-boundary step, not high-frequency
    structure, so edge energy is a weak instrument for it. Reading a null here
    as "the fix did nothing" would be the same mistake as judging displacement
    by edge energy in the first place.
    
    THE RESOLUTION TARGET IS RULED, AND I ASKED A QUESTION THAT WAS ALREADY
    ANSWERED. I offered Ryan a choice between 8.1 km and a shrunk ~4 km world
    "as a WORLD_VISION question". WORLD_VISION.md:171 already reads "World
    structure: 8064 m is the PER-REGION size — CONFIRMED" (reference class
    Witcher 3 / Final Fantasy / Tales / Amalur), restated at :198 as settled

    reversed a ratified ruling and should never have been put to him — offered
    without opening the file that had already closed it, which is
    non-negotiable 9 on the author who keeps quoting it. Struck in BACKLOG
    rather than deleted.
    
    TARGET: 8129² at 1 m/vertex = 66,080,641 vertices, extent 8128 m. The
    +0.8% over 8064 is taken deliberately: 8064 does not tile at 254
    quads/component (31.75), and hitting it exactly needs 126 quads/component
    -> 4096 components instead of 1024, four times the count to save 64
    metres. The ruling is a reference CLASS, not a tolerance.
    
    The migration keeps the CURRENT layout — same 1024 components, same 256
    proxies, 4x quads per component, scale_xy_cm 400 -> 100 — and is not
    blocked, since Gaea Indie's 8K cap covers 8129. The remaining unknown is
    FRAME COST at 66 M vertices, which is a measurement and is step 0's whole
    purpose, to be taken on AlpineLab_v1 and never against /Game/Alpine first.

    The iGPU compromise that became a terrain resolution cap
    
    Measured the capable-GPU profile and pinned it. The whole intervention —
    displacement + landscape Nanite + this profile — is now a clear net win
    over the pre-displacement baseline, and the metric agrees with the frames
    instead of contradicting them.
    
        quality cvars alone   5080disp  -> 5080hq   mean +9.25%, 17/19 gained
        whole intervention    5080sp100 -> 5080hq   mean +7.49%, 18/19 above
                                                    the 2.08% noise floor
    
    THE FINDING, AND NOBODY EDITED THE THING THAT CAUSED IT.
    r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge was set to 4 by R7 as an iGPU rasterisation
    saving, with a comment that is accurate and describes MESH silhouette.
    Earlier the same day the LANDSCAPE became Nanite — and from that moment
    the cvar governed TERRAIN silhouette, the exact quantity the displacement
    unit existed to buy, at a quarter of the available edge resolution.
    
    4 -> 1, single change, 19 stations: mean +9.25%, 17 of 19 gaining. And it
    recovers the same three stations that lost most when Nanite came on —
    verify_ground +36.7% (was -15.2%), forest_floor +27.3% (was -13.3%),
    sweep_0060 +22.7% (was -23.1%). The recovery is the mirror image of the
    loss, which makes it a mechanism rather than a coincidence.
    
    So yesterday's interpretation needs amending: most of the near-field cost
    attributed to "displacement trades albedo texture for geometry" was
    actually the Nanite landscape rasterising four times too coarsely. The
    trade is real — the sweep_0060 frames show it — but it was the smaller
    term, and I had named this cvar only as a candidate.
    
    A PERFORMANCE COMPROMISE IS SCOPED TO A RENDERING PATH, AND CHANGING THE
    PATH SILENTLY RE-SCOPES IT. No gate could have caught this: every gate
    was checking that the value matched its configuration, and it did. When a
    subsystem is switched on, the standing config must be re-read asking
    WHICH LINES NOW MEAN SOMETHING DIFFERENT.
    
    THREE ERRORS IN THE EXTERNAL STANDARDS DOC, each checked at source:
      * r.Nanite.AllowTessellation DOES NOT EXIST in 5.8; the real cvar is
        r.Nanite.Tessellation (NaniteCullRaster.cpp:94). Pinned in an ini it
        is an inert line that verifies as 0.0 and reads as "off".
      * wp.Runtime.HLOD is an FAutoConsoleCommand, not a variable
        (HLODRuntimeSubsystem.cpp:150) — unreadable, unsettable from an ini,
        and its handler only acts on World->IsGameWorld() so it does nothing
        in the editor. render_condition REFUSED the whole run over it rather
        than let a capture proceed against an unverifiable change.
      * 127 quads/section x 2 sections x 64x64 components = 16257 vertices,
        not the 8129 claimed. 32x32 is correct — and is what this landscape
        already has, which makes the eventual 1 m/vertex migration a
        same-layout change: same 1024 components, same 256 proxies.
    
    THE sg.* GROUPS ARE PINNED DOWNSTREAM, not by name. This ini already
    records the measurement that [SystemSettings] sets an sg.* VALUE WITHOUT
    RUNNING THE GROUP — it is why grass.DensityScale is pinned. So the six
    values BaseScalability.ini expands at @3 are pinned explicitly beside
    sg.GlobalIlluminationQuality=3, and both are set so a later group
    expansion is idempotent rather than a silent revert. Verified in the live
    editor by reading those downstream cvars, not by reading sg.* back at
    itself (NN8).
    
    UNVERIFIED AND SAID SO: the ini is an OVERRIDE, not the state in effect

+## 2026-08-11b — THE iGPU COMPROMISE THAT BECAME A TERRAIN RESOLUTION CAP
+
+Ryan supplied an external "UE 5.8 landscape standards" document and ruled:
+adopt everything that improves landscape quality and resolution. Three of
+its rules are factually wrong and are logged here so nobody adopts them;
+the rest is mostly things this project already does. The genuinely new
+finding came from applying it, not from reading it.
+
+### 1. THE FINDING: `r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge` CHANGED MEANING UNDER US
+
+It was set to 4.0 as an iGPU saving — *"4 pixels per edge instead of the
+default 1 quarters the rasterisation work. Visible as slightly coarser
+silhouettes up close; on this GPU that is the correct trade."* That
+comment was true when written and describes MESH silhouette.
+
+**It stopped being true earlier the same day, when the landscape itself
+became Nanite.** From that moment the cvar governs TERRAIN silhouette —
+the exact quantity the whole displacement unit existed to buy — and the
+terrain was rasterising at a quarter of the available edge resolution.
+
+Measured, 4.0 -> 1.0, single change, 19 stations:
+
+    mean +9.25%  median +6.28%  gained on 17 of 19  (floor 2.08%)
+
+    verify_ground +36.70%   forest_floor +27.26%   sweep_0060 +22.73%
+    sweep_0150    +13.63%   cliff_face   +13.20%
+
+**Those are the same stations that LOST the most when Nanite was switched
+on** (verify_ground −15.23%, forest_floor −13.30%, sweep_0060 −23.11%).
+The recovery is the mirror image of the loss, which is what makes this a
+mechanism and not a coincidence: **most of the near-field cost attributed
+to "displacement trades texture for geometry" was actually the Nanite
+landscape rasterising four times too coarsely.** Part of yesterday's
+interpretation stands — the sweep_0060 frames show a real texture→geometry
+trade — but the magnitude of the loss was substantially this cvar, and I
+had named it only as a candidate.
+
+Cumulative, pre-displacement to now (`5080sp100` -> `5080hq`):
+**mean +7.49%, median +8.57%, 18 of 19 above the noise floor.**
+
+**THE RULE: A PERFORMANCE COMPROMISE IS SCOPED TO A RENDERING PATH, AND
+CHANGING THE PATH SILENTLY RE-SCOPES IT.** Nothing edited that cvar or its
+comment; the world moved underneath both. There was no gate that could
+have caught this, because every gate was checking that the value was what
+it was configured to be — and it was. **When a subsystem is switched on
+(Nanite, RVT, VSM), the standing config must be re-read ASKING WHICH LINES
+NOW MEAN SOMETHING DIFFERENT**, not merely whether it still applies.
+
+### 2. THREE ERRORS IN THE EXTERNAL DOC, EACH CHECKED AT SOURCE
+
+Logged because the doc will be consulted again, and two of the three are
+inert-line traps that verify as "off" rather than failing loudly.
+
+- **`r.Nanite.AllowTessellation` DOES NOT EXIST** in 5.8. The real cvar is
+  `r.Nanite.Tessellation` (`NaniteCullRaster.cpp:94`). Pinned in an ini it
+  is an inert line that reads like a setting, and
+  `get_console_variable_float_value` returns **0.0 for a nonexistent
+  cvar** — indistinguishable from a real one that is off. This project had
+  already been bitten by precisely this (`read_nanite_state.py` once
+  reported two nonexistent cvars as "two gates are off").
+- **`wp.Runtime.HLOD` is an `FAutoConsoleCommand`, not a variable**
+  (`HLODRuntimeSubsystem.cpp:150`). It cannot be read back at all, an ini
+  entry does not set it, and its handler acts only on
+  `World->IsGameWorld()` — so it does nothing in the editor. Deliberately
+  NOT pinned, with the reason written into the ini beside the others.
+  **`render_condition` refused the entire run over it** rather than let a
+  capture proceed against an unverifiable change. That refusal is the
+  behaviour being praised here: the tool was right and my first reading of
+  its output ("DID NOT MOVE" = the set failed) was wrong — the cause is
+  that there is nothing there to move.
+- **The component math is arithmetically wrong.** 127 quads/section × 2
+  sections × 64×64 components = **16257** vertices, not the 8129 claimed.
+  32×32 is correct. This matters because the doc says "never invent other
+  component layouts" — and because 32×32 is what this landscape ALREADY
+  has, which turns the eventual 1 m/vertex migration into a same-layout
+  change (same 1024 components, same 256 proxies, 4× quads per component).
+
+### 3. A STALE LINE IN A "DO NOT RE-DIAGNOSE" POSITION, AGAIN
+
+CLAUDE.md's ENVIRONMENT section still read *"Gaea is blocked at both ends
+by licensing ... Do not re-diagnose it."* It was resolved on 2026-08-09 by
+buying an Indie licence (8K export cap) and RECIPES records that
+resolution — but CLAUDE.md was never updated.
+
+**It was one sentence from being reported to Ryan as the blocker on the
+1 vertex/metre re-terrain.** It is not a blocker: 8129 < 8192.
+
+This is the third instance of the same shape (the talus threshold,
+2026-08-08; Pass 5's "no written scope"). The pattern is now specific
+enough to name: **when a blocker is RESOLVED, the resolution gets written
+where the WORK happened (RECIPES), and the place that TOLD PEOPLE NOT TO
+LOOK (CLAUDE.md) is the one place nobody updates.** Struck in place rather
+than deleted.
+
+### 4. A DISPLAY THAT ROUNDED AWAY THE VALUE IT WAS JUDGING
+
+`render_condition` printed every cvar with `{:.0f}`, so setting
+`r.Shadow.Virtual.ResolutionLodBiasDirectional` to −0.5 reported
+
+    asked  -0   after  -0   ok
+
+The SET was always correct (the payload writes `str(int(v))` only when the
+value is integral). Only the display rounded. But this tool exists
+*specifically because a fractional cvar was once silently truncated by
+`int()`*, and its own docstring says so — so a display that cannot show
+fractions was hiding exactly the failure the tool was built to expose. A
+verdict rendered at lower precision than the value it judges is not a
+verdict. Fixed.

    1. `r.Nanite.AllowTessellation` DOES NOT EXIST in 5.8. The real cvar is

       correctly REFUSED the run rather than let a capture proceed against an
       unverifiable change.
    3. The component math is wrong. 127 quads/section x 2 sections x 64x64
       components = 16257 vertices, not 8129. The correct layout for 8129 is
       32x32 components — which happens to be exactly what this landscape
       already has, making the eventual 1 m/vertex migration a same-layout
       change: same 1024 components, same 256 proxies, 4x quads per

    CENTRING, FIXED AT ITS SOURCE RATHER THAN DECLARED (code only, unbuilt).
    Yesterday's finding was that center 0.5 is not neutral for these maps —
    means run 0.5257 to 0.7602, so up to half the amplitude was a per-surface
    DC offset with a ~19 cm step at layer boundaries. The fix does NOT put
    the measured means in the recipe: `_centred_height` adds a second
    TextureSample of the same asset forced to the smallest mip
    (TMVM_MIP_LEVEL, const_mip_value 15) and computes
    
        centred = raw - mipped + center
    
    so the neutral is READ FROM THE TEXTURE every frame. No derived record to
    drift when a map is reimported or recompressed — and these maps have been
    recompressed before (NN15). It is also more correct than the arithmetic
    mean would be: what the centring must cancel is what the texture reads as
    when it DEGRADES, which is exactly the top mip, so a fully-mipped sample
    now displaces by zero by construction — the guarantee the original
    center-0.5 comment merely claimed.
    
    The re-centring touches ONLY the displacement path. The sub-surface
    HeightLerp keeps the uncentred samples, because that blend compares two
    heights against each other and shifting them by different constants would
    change which surface wins.

+## 2026-08-11 — MATERIAL DISPLACEMENT: four failures, and the biggest one was my own metric
+
+Landscape Nanite displacement was built, enabled and measured in one
+session. It works. Everything below is what went wrong on the way, logged
+before the successes so a fresh session reads the traps first.
+
+### 1. THE UNITS TRAP, CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED — and the handoff's instinct was right for a reason nobody had written down
+
+CURRENT STATE said `displacement_scaling` magnitude 4.0 was *"likely far
+too strong for a 4 m-per-texel landscape — start small and measure"*. It
+gave no number and no mechanism, so the next session (me) could have
+"started small" at 1.0 and still been catastrophically wrong.
+
+Read at the source instead of estimated:
+
+    NaniteRasterizationCommon.ush:568  D = (v - Center) * Magnitude
+    :578                               PointPostDeform += Normal * D
+    :588  PointWorld = mul(PointPostDeform, LocalToTranslatedWorld)
+
+**Displacement is added in LOCAL space, before the local-to-world
+transform.** The landscape's Nanite mesh is exported `RelativeToProxy`
+(LandscapeNaniteComponent.cpp:337), which LandscapeEdit.cpp:4215-4216
+defines as `ComponentTransform * ProxyTransform.Inverse()` — the proxy's
+scale is divided OUT of the mesh and re-applied by the component. That
+scale is [400, 400, 500].
+
+**So one unit of magnitude is five metres here, and the engine default
+4.0 is ±10 m — two and a half times the entire 4.00 m sampling cap the
+feature exists to add detail beneath.**
+
+The general rule, and it is non-negotiable 23's sibling: **A MAGNITUDE
+WITHOUT A SPACE IS NOT A NUMBER.** "Is 4.0 too strong" is unanswerable
+until you know what 1.0 means, and that required three files — the
+shader, the exporter, and the transform the exporter divides out. Two of
+the three were not where I would have guessed.
+
+**What was DONE about it, rather than just noted (NN3):** the recipe now
+declares `amplitude_m` in METRES and `displacement_spec` performs the one
+conversion. The catastrophic value is no longer reachable by typing a
+plausible-looking 4.0; it requires asking for 10 metres of terrain
+movement into a field that refuses above 2.0.
+
+### 2. I ASSERTED A CLAIM ABOUT PIXELS IN A GATE, AND IT WAS FALSE
+
+`displacement_scaling.center` was set to 0.5 and justified — in a code
+comment AND in a `prove_gates` assertion — as *"the value the height maps
+are neutral at, so a missing sample displaces by zero"*.
+
+That is a claim about the CONTENT OF FIVE PNGs and I never opened them.
+Measured:
+
+    Ground037 0.5257   Rock051 0.6005   Snow006 0.6490
+    Rock026   0.7602   Rock063 0.7311
+
+**Not one is centred on 0.5.** At magnitude 0.16 that is a constant
+upward lift of +2.06 to +20.82 cm — up to HALF the ±40 cm amplitude as a
+DC offset — and because it differs per surface it puts a ~19 cm step at
+layer boundaries that is not relief. A fully-mipped sample returns the
+map's MEAN, not 0.5, so the degraded-state guarantee fails too.
+
+This is non-negotiable 9 landing on me inside the same session that
+quoted it: **an unverified claim in our own code contaminating the
+knowledge base.** It is worse than the 2026-08-03 sampler case in one
+specific way — **that claim lived in a docstring, this one lived in a
+GATE.** A `prove_gates` line printing "asserted" reads as *proven*, and
+it was proving only that a float equalled 0.5 while narrating a reason
+nobody had checked.
+
+**NEW RULE: A GATE MAY ASSERT A VALUE. IT MAY NOT NARRATE AN UNVERIFIED
+REASON FOR THAT VALUE.** The reason is the part a reader trusts, and the
+gate does not test it. Either measure the reason and cite the
+measurement, or state the value and say the justification is open. Both
+the comment and the gate were fixed in the same commit that recorded this
+(NN4: the sweep is a mechanical step, not an intention).
+
+### 3. MY OWN "SECOND REPRESENTATION" REPORTED A CONFIDENT ZERO OVER WORK IN FLIGHT
+
+`enable_landscape_nanite.py` deliberately checked a DIFFERENT
+representation than the flag: not "is enable_nanite true" but "does a
+LandscapeNaniteComponent carry a static mesh". Good instinct. It reported
+
+    proxies with a BUILT Nanite mesh : 0 of 257
+
+34 seconds after the property write. A few minutes later the same query
+returned **256 of 257**, with 0 unreadable.
+
+**Nothing failed. The builds are asynchronous and throttled** to
+~6 proxies/second (`landscape.Nanite.MaxAsyncProxyBuildsPerSecond`), and
+my check measured how far the queue had got, then printed it as a state.
+A second representation that samples a process at the wrong TIME is not a
+second measurement — it is a confident wrong answer, and "0 of 257" is
+the most alarming possible way to be wrong.
+
+**This is non-negotiable 6 wearing a number.** "I looked and it is
+absent" and "it has not happened YET" are different findings and the
+check collapsed them. It also caught accessor exceptions and counted them
+as "no mesh", conflating "could not look" with "absent" in the same
+function — two instances of the same defect in code I wrote while
+thinking about that exact defect.
+
+Fixed: `unreadable` is now counted separately from `absent`, and the
+count is labelled a SNAPSHOT OF AN ASYNC QUEUE with an explicit "a low
+count is 'not yet', not 'failed'".
+
+### 4. THE HEADLINE METRIC WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, AND IT WAS THE ONE THE PLAN SPECIFIED
+
+The ratified plan said: *"Compare with EDGE ENERGY, not mae — mae cannot
+tell sharper from differently blurry, the ScreenPercentage A/B already
+paid for that lesson."* That reasoning is correct, and edge energy IS the
+right instrument for a resolution change.
+
+It is the wrong instrument for THIS change. Result: **mean −1.02% across
+19 stations.** By the plan's own acceptance criterion, displacement made
+the frame worse.
+
+**It did not.** `sweep_0060` lost the most edge energy of all nineteen
+(−23.11%) and went from a FLAT plane wearing a smeared high-contrast rock
+texture to a surface with real ledges, facets and self-shadowing. It is
+enormously better and measures 23% worse.
+
+The mechanism is structural, not a tuning problem:
+
+- mean gradient magnitude counts **high-frequency ALBEDO contrast**;
+- displacement replaces stretched texture with **GEOMETRY**, whose
+  shading varies **smoothly across facets**.
+
+At close range the change trades away exactly the quantity the metric
+counts. At distance the same relief appears as new silhouette EDGES and
+the metric rises (+5% to +12% on seven stations). One mechanism, both
+signs — which is why the result is bimodal rather than noisy, and why the
+whole-frame mean is meaningless as a summary.
+
+**THE RULE, and it generalises past this feature: AN INSTRUMENT INHERITED
+FROM A PLAN IS AN INHERITED ASSUMPTION. Step (a) — check for a locked
+procedure — applies to the METRIC as much as to the method.** The plan's
+metric was chosen to fix the LAST measurement's defect (mae's blindness
+to sign) and was never re-tested against the NEXT intervention's failure
+mode. A metric earns its place against the specific change it will judge.
+
+And the thing that actually settled it was **opening two PNGs**
+(NN10/NN16). No statistic in this session produced the finding; the
+statistic pointed the wrong way and the pixels corrected it.

+## NANITE DISPLACEMENT (schema v1.21) — LOCKED 2026-08-11, UNPROVEN
+
+**Adds silhouette BELOW the heightmap's 4.00 m sampling cap without
+re-importing the terrain or re-deriving the 171,069 placements.** It is
+the only route to that which does not invalidate Pass 1.
+
+### The one fact that decides the design
+
+`MP_Displacement` exists at value 32 (`SceneTypes.h:181`) but is
+`UMETA(Hidden)`, so UHT never emitted it into the reflected Python
+`MaterialProperty` enum — which runs `MP_FRONT_MATERIAL` 30,
+`MP_MATERIAL_ATTRIBUTES` 33, `MP_MAX` 35, with 31 and 32 absent.
+**`connect_material_property` cannot wire Displacement at all.** Positive
+control: `MaterialProperty(32)` and `.cast(32)` both refuse while
+`MP_MAX` reads 35 in the same payload.
+
+Route: `use_material_attributes` + `MakeMaterialAttributes` (whose header
+carries `FExpressionInput Displacement` at line 77) →
+`MP_MATERIAL_ATTRIBUTES`.
+
+### EXACT VALUES
+
+| Field | Value | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| `material.displacement.enabled` | `true` | keeps the three-pin path reachable |
+| `material.displacement.amplitude_m` | **0.40** | METRES, peak either side |
+| derived `displacement_scaling.magnitude` | **0.16** | `2 * amplitude_m * 100 / scale_z` |
+| derived `displacement_scaling.center` | **0.5** | see REJECTED — this is NOT a neutral |
+| `enable_tessellation` | `true` | *"Required for displacement to work"*, PythonStub :81519 |
+| `r.Nanite.Tessellation` | 1.0 | already on |
+| landscape `enable_nanite` | `true` on the PARENT only | propagates to all 256 proxies |
+
+**AMPLITUDE IS DECLARED IN METRES AND CONVERTED ONCE**, in
+`make_landscape_material.displacement_spec`. The engine's magnitude is a
+LOCAL-SPACE quantity and one unit is **five metres** on this landscape.
+Derivation: `NaniteRasterizationCommon.ush:568/578/588` (displacement is
+added before the local-to-world transform),
+`LandscapeNaniteComponent.cpp:337` + `LandscapeEdit.cpp:4215-4216` (the
+mesh is exported RelativeToProxy, so the proxy scale is divided out and
+re-applied), `landscape_spec.py:35` (`scale_z = z_scale_cm / 512` = 500).
+
+### PROCEDURE — the order is the failure modes
+
+1. **RISKY-OP tag.** Failure mode is UE's checkerboard across the whole
+   landscape, already shipped once here.
+2. **Change the BUILDER, never the graph by hand** — a hand-wired pin
+   vanishes on the next rebuild.
+3. The `_D` maps are declared by the **`d_active`** predicate, which is a
+   superset of `sub_active`. Widen the PREDICATE; never add a second
+   `SAMPLED_TEXTURES` row (NN24).
+4. **Preflight before `delete_all_material_expressions`.** The clear is
+   the point of no return in memory.
+5. `python scripts/prove_gates.py` — the DISPLACEMENT section must be
+   17/17 and the suite exit 0.
+6. **Rebuild ATTENDED.** B-BUILD-UNKNOWN is open.
+7. `audit_material_connectivity` expecting **0 orphans**, then
+   `audit_material_samplers`. Stamp both with the material SHA-256.
+8. **Confirm the grass output is still seeded** — it shares this graph.
+9. **Only then** `python scripts/enable_landscape_nanite.py --go --build`.
+   Enabling Nanite first buys no silhouette.
+10. Capture, then **read the frames** — see REJECTED on edge energy.

 ## REJECTED
+- **`displacement_scaling.magnitude 4.0` (the ENGINE DEFAULT)** → **±10
+  METRES of terrain movement**, two and a half times the entire 4.00 m
+  heightmap sampling cap the feature exists to add detail beneath.
+  Symptom: terrain heaves into landforms the heightmap cannot represent,
+  every placed instance is metres off the rendered ground, and collision
+  disagrees with the render by up to 10 m. Correct: **declare
+  `amplitude_m` in METRES and let `displacement_spec` convert** — 0.40 m
+  → magnitude **0.16**. The engine's magnitude is a LOCAL-SPACE quantity
+  and one unit is 500 cm here. Reference: `EngineTypes.h:3456` (the 4.0
+  default), `NaniteRasterizationCommon.ush:568/578/588`,
+  `LandscapeEdit.cpp:4215-4216`. **A MAGNITUDE WITHOUT A SPACE IS NOT A
+  NUMBER.**
+- **`Justifying center 0.5 as "the value the height maps are neutral
+  at"`** → a DC offset of up to HALF the amplitude, believed to be zero.
+  Symptom: nothing visible fails; the whole terrain is lifted and a step
+  appears at layer boundaries. Measured means of the five surface height
+  maps: Ground037 **0.5257**, Rock051 **0.6005**, Snow006 **0.6490**,
+  Rock026 **0.7602**, Rock063 **0.7311** — **not one is 0.5**. At
+  magnitude 0.16 that is +2.06 to +20.82 cm of constant lift, differing
+  per surface by up to ~19 cm. A fully-mipped sample returns the map's
+  MEAN, not 0.5, so the degraded-state guarantee also fails. Correct:
+  **keep 0.5** (it is one material-level scalar and the maps disagree, so
+  no value is neutral for all) **but state it as a known measured offset,
+  and normalise each map in the GRAPH** — subtract its own mean before
+  compositing. **AND: a gate may assert a VALUE; it may not narrate an
+  unverified REASON for that value.** This claim was in a `prove_gates`
+  line printing "asserted", which reads as proven.
+- **`Judging displacement by whole-frame EDGE ENERGY`** → the feature
+  reads as a REGRESSION when it is working. Symptom: mean **−1.02%**
+  across 19 stations, and the single most improved frame — `sweep_0060`,
+  a flat smeared texture that became real ledges, facets and
+  self-shadowing — measures **−23.11%**, the worst of all nineteen.
+  Cause: mean gradient magnitude counts high-frequency ALBEDO contrast,
+  and displacement TRADES that for GEOMETRY whose shading varies smoothly
+  across facets. Correct: **the result is bimodal and the mean is not a
+  summary of it.** Distant/aerial stations GAIN (+5% to +12% on seven);
+  ground-level stations LOSE. **Open the frames** — no statistic in that
+  session produced the finding and the statistic pointed the wrong way.
+  Reference: `_verify/20260811_displacement_interpretation.md`.
+  **An instrument inherited from a plan is an inherited assumption:**
+  edge energy was chosen to fix mae's blindness to SIGN and was never
+  re-tested against displacement's failure mode.
+- **`Reading the Nanite mesh count immediately after setting
+  enable_nanite`** → a confident **"0 of 257"** over work that succeeded.
+  Symptom: `enable_landscape_nanite.py` reported 0 built meshes 34 s
+  after the write; the same query minutes later returned **256 of 257**,
+  0 unreadable. Cause: the builds are ASYNC and throttled to ~6/s
+  (`landscape.Nanite.MaxAsyncProxyBuildsPerSecond`). Correct: **label the
+  count a SNAPSHOT OF AN ASYNC QUEUE** — a low number is "not yet", not
+  "failed" — **and count `unreadable` separately from `absent`.** The
+  parent `ALandscape` legitimately has no mesh in a World Partition
+  world; the geometry lives in the 256 proxies.
+- **`Setting enable_nanite and expecting a build`** → the flag is true
+  and nothing is built. `ALandscape::PostEditChangeProperty` calls
+  `InvalidateOrUpdateNaniteRepresentation`, which BUILDS only when
+  `IsLiveNaniteRebuildEnabled()` — exactly
+  `landscape.Nanite.LiveRebuildOnModification > 0`, **default 0**
+  (`Landscape.cpp:598-605`, `LandscapeSubsystem.cpp:1561-1564`). Correct:
+  set that cvar BEFORE the property write (`--build` does this and
+  refuses if the cvar does not read back). `ULandscapeSubsystem::BuildNanite`
+  is `LANDSCAPE_API` but has **no `UFUNCTION`**, so it is absent from the
+  Python surface and cannot be called instead.

commit 187a9321ab63493f194f9adc6be3eff97504fc42
Author: ryanb <ryanbme83@gmail.com>
Date:   2026-08-11 16:46:51 -0700

    The terrain's smoothness is a sampling cap at 4.00 m per texel, not a material defect
    
    Ryan pointed out the map is 2017x2017, not 4K. The arithmetic turns that
    from a note into a reclassification of the AAA gap list.
    
      2017 vertices, scale_xy_cm 400.0
      -> (2017-1) x 400 cm = 8.064 km per side, 6,503 ha
      -> 4.00 METRES PER HEIGHTMAP TEXEL
    
    A cliff lip, a ledge and a crisp arete are all sub-4 m features, so they
    cannot be represented at all. The smooth rolling profile in every ground
    frame is the heightmap's Nyquist limit. That is why triplanar, macro
    variation, detail relief and GI did not fix it and never could -- they buy
    SURFACE detail against a smooth SILHOUETTE, which is precisely what the
    frames show.
    
    THREE ROUTES, NOT EQUIVALENT
      (a) more texels at the same extent (4033 -> 2 m, 8129 -> 1 m): means
          re-importing terrain and re-deriving weightmaps and all 171,069
          placements, invalidating Pass 1 and every grounding proof.
      (b) shrink the world at current resolution: trades the open-world premise.
      (c) landscape Nanite + displacement: adds real silhouette ABOVE the
          heightmap frequency without touching the heightmap or any placement.
          Ruled out historically on the iGPU; the obvious candidate on a 5080.
    
    Route (c) is the only one that does not invalidate existing work, so it
    gets costed first. The Gaea AlpineLab_v1 build is already 4033^2, which
    makes it the place to test the resolution question without touching
    /Game/Alpine.
    
    ALSO RECORDED: two remote-exec clients against one editor. I ran
    render_condition.py twice as a regression check while capture.py held a
    command connection to the same node. The capture produced zero frames and
    logged nothing for ~15 minutes while its process stayed alive -- no error,
    no timeout. The editor served my calls normally throughout, so only the
    capture was dead. One command connection per node; the second client wins
    and the victim hangs silently. What settled it was the EDITOR's log rather
    than the capture's stdout: the newest line was my own payload with no
    capture activity after it. Operational rule until a guard exists: nothing
    touches the editor while a capture runs.

+## 2026-08-10 — the migration to the 5080 machine, and the check that was briefed wrong

+COST TWO FILES.** `git fsck` validates the git OBJECT DATABASE — 391 MB

+different failures and only the first was being checked. **2 of 18,241

+the same mechanism this file already records for 2026-08-08 — "unable to
+unlink old ... Invalid argument", where two bulk checkouts reported exit
+0 while writing nothing. **The migration script verified COUNTS and
+BYTES and still missed it, because 2 files in 23,050 is inside the noise
+of any count-based check.** Only per-object identity found it.
+General rule: *a bulk file operation verifies that no process holds the
+tree open BEFORE it runs, and verifies the DESTINATION afterwards rather
+than trusting its own exit code.*
+
+**NON-NEGOTIABLE 17 FIRED ON MY OWN EDIT, WHICH IS THE HONEST PART.** I

+**The brief said "LandscapeLab/ProjectTitan" as though it were one path.
+It is two projects**, and the second one lives in OneDrive, which is a
+different migration problem from a folder on a local disk.
+
+**A STALE DUPLICATE OF THE GAEA PROJECT IS ON THE DESKTOP.**
+`OneDrive\Desktop\AlpineLabe_v1.terrain`, 18:42, against the canonical
+`C:\Dev\...\AlpineLabe_v1.terrain` at 19:40 -- an hour older. Two files
+with the same name and different contents, and the older one is the one
+sitting where a human would grab it. Not deleted; named here so it is
+not the copy that survives the move. This is non-negotiable 20's problem
+in miniature: the same artefact at two names with no hash between them.

+**Also present and not asked about:** `MedievalVillageMegascansS` under
+Unreal Projects, and Epic's VaultCache copy of `Titan_5.8`.
+
+### THE CLEAN
+
+Editor closed first -- it holds `Saved` and `Intermediate` open, and
+deleting underneath a live editor fails on locked files.
+
+    LandscapeLab UE5 project   11.09 GB -> 10.36 GB   (0.73 GB)
+
+Moved to `_trash/migration_clean_20260810` rather than deleted, per
+standing rule 2. `_trash` is excluded from the migration set, so the
+space is freed for the copy either way, and the move stays reversible --
+which matters because `Saved/Autosaves` held an autosave of the level.
+`Saved/Config` and `Saved/Screenshots` kept, per Ryan.
+

+anyone plans around it.** `DerivedDataCache` inside the project is 9
+files and effectively empty; the real DDC lives in `AppData\Local`. The
+weight in this repo is `_trash` (17.8 GB), `.git` (9.2 GB), `Content`
+(10.3 GB) and `Free` (4.2 GB).
+
+### THE INSTRUCTION THAT WOULD HAVE DESTROYED THE MIGRATION
+
+The brief said to robocopy each source to `<Drive>\Migration\` with
+`/MIR`. **`/MIR` mirrors: it deletes anything at the destination that is
+not in the current source.** Three sources into one destination root
+means the second copy deletes the first and the third deletes the
+second, and **robocopy reports success every time** -- the deletions are
+what mirroring is FOR. `scripts/migrate_to_drive.ps1` gives each source
+its own subfolder, where `/MIR` does the useful thing instead: a re-run
+converges rather than accumulating.
+
+### ONEDRIVE IS NOT RUNNING, SO "THE CLOUD WILL CARRY IT" IS UNPROVEN
+
+Ryan's plan was to skip ProjectTitan's 61 GB and re-hydrate it from
+OneDrive on the new machine, conditional on sync being demonstrably
+clean. It is not demonstrable: **there is no OneDrive process running**,
+642 files under `ProjectTitan\Binaries\Win64` carry reparse points, and
+Windows exposes no "fully uploaded" flag a script can read. All 208,726
+files are local (0 marked Offline), which proves they are DOWNLOADED and
+says nothing about whether they are UPLOADED -- the direction that
+matters here.
+
+By his own rule -- "if sync status is at all murky, add it to the drive
+anyway" -- ProjectTitan is IN the copy set. **Reading an absence as a
+negative is non-negotiable 17's mechanism**, and "no offline files" is
+exactly that kind of absence.
+
+### NOT DONE
+
+The copy, the hash verification and the manifest. `C:` is the only
+volume on this machine, 19.4 GB free against a 92.9 GB set.
+`scripts/migrate_to_drive.ps1` is written and its preflight is proven to
+refuse three ways: unmounted drive, malformed drive spec, and `C:` as a
+destination (a copy onto the source is not a backup). It needs the drive
+connected and its letter.

+## 2026-08-10 — THE OVERNIGHT ALPINELAB SESSION: FOUR DEFECTS, AND THE ONE THAT MADE THE GROUND A CHECKERBOARD
+
+Ryan went to bed asking for a fully rendered 4K environment. The terrain
+ended the night with 30,589 instances on it, a compiling material and
+3840x2160 frames. Everything below is what went wrong on the way, because
+that is the part worth keeping.
+
+### 1. I BROKE THE MATERIAL BY FIXING THE TEXTURES
+
+The five 4033-square masks were imported UNCOMPRESSED
+(`TC_VECTOR_DISPLACEMENTMAP`), inherited from `import_layer_textures.py`
+whose reasoning is sound: a block compressor destroys thin drainage
+lines. On this machine it was fatal for a different reason -- the editor
+logged, for tens of minutes at four cores:
+
+    BEWARE: AssetCompile memory estimate is greater than available, but
+    we're running it [TextureDerivedData] anyway!
+    RequiredMemory = 4609 MiB, MemoryLimit = 994 MiB
+
+with free RAM pinned near 0.9 GB. So I recompressed them to
+`TC_GRAYSCALE` (BC4).
+
+**That changed what sampler type the engine requires**, from
+`LINEAR_COLOR` to `LINEAR_GRAYSCALE`. The material's five mask samplers
+still declared the old type. `VerifySamplerType` errors on EVERY
+mismatch, so the WHOLE MATERIAL failed to compile, and the landscape fell
+back to UE's default material -- which is why every ground frame came
+back as a grey CHECKERBOARD.
+
+**The trap is already in CLAUDE.md, and I reached it from the direction
+nobody was watching.** Non-negotiable 9's motivating case is exactly
+"VerifySamplerType errors on EVERY mismatch". Every prior instance was a
+sampler typed wrongly by hand. This was a sampler typed CORRECTLY and
+then invalidated by changing the texture underneath it. A sampler audit
+had passed on these same nodes hours earlier, when the compression still
+matched -- so the audit was right, and then quietly stopped being right.
+
+**The instrument that found it in one call:**
+`MaterialEditingLibrary.recompile_material` RETURNS the error list. The
+editor log only says *"Failed to compile Material for platform
+PCD3D_SM6, Default Material will be used in game"*, which names the
+symptom and not one of the five offending nodes.
+
+**General rule: changing a texture's COMPRESSION is a change to every
+material that samples it.** The sampler type is a contract between the
+two, and only one side was edited.
+
+### 2. MODE_EXEC_FILE MEANS THE COMMAND IS A FILENAME
+
+Payloads had been sent as inline source with
+`exec_mode=MODE_EXEC_FILE` and it worked, so it looked like the
+established pattern. It fails for longer commands, and the failure is
+almost unreadable:
+
+    Could not load Python file
+    'C:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8/Engine/Binaries/Win64/<the
+     entire payload, with newlines rendered as /n>'
+
+-- the engine resolving the source text as a path relative to its own
+binaries directory. **The scatter placed nothing three times before this
+was understood**, and the first two theories were both wrong (transport
+size limit; busy editor).
+
+What settled it was a bisect: 6,000 bytes of filler went through, so it
+was not length; prefixes of the real payload failed at a REPRODUCIBLE
+boundary, which ruled out load. Both builders now write the payload to a
+file under `Saved/` and send the PATH.
+
+### 3. AN API I REMEMBERED, AGAIN
+
+`Actor.add_component_by_class` does not exist in 5.8's reflected
+surface. I used it to attach a HierarchicalInstancedStaticMeshComponent;
+the editor raised AttributeError and the stub confirmed the absence.
+Non-negotiable 23, and `place_foliage.py` had the correct path
+(`FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh` + `InstancedFoliageActor.add_
+instances`) the whole time. **Step (a) is a search, not a recall** --
+and I searched the stub only after the failure, not before the call.
+
+### 4. THE FOG WAS TUNED FOR A TERRAIN THAT STARTS AT ZERO
+
+`ExponentialHeightFog` attenuates by height above its OWN actor, which
+the Basic template puts at -68 m. This terrain spans -462 m to +462 m,
+so a valley camera sat 240 m BELOW the datum, at the thickest part of
+the curve. The first ground frame was a blue wash with ghost trees, and
+it read as a render failure rather than a fog setting.
+
+Datum moved to -460 m, density 0.0436 -> 0.008, falloff 0.2 -> 0.08.
+**A fog default is a statement about where the ground is.** A terrain
+whose datum is its MIDDLE breaks that assumption by half its height.
+
+### 5. A READ-BACK THAT COULD NOT MATCH REPORTED A CATASTROPHE
+
+The scatter's own verification compared `static_mesh.get_path_name()`
+against the recipe's package path. `get_path_name()` returns
+`/Game/X/SM_Foo.SM_Foo` -- the OBJECT path -- so the comparison was
+false for every mesh and the tool reported **0 placed for all six
+species** while the engine actually held 30,589. A separate probe found
+them immediately.
+
+Non-negotiable 6 says a failed measurement must report that it could not
+measure. This one reported a NUMBER, and the number was zero, which is
+indistinguishable from the disaster it was describing.
+
+### WHAT IS NOT WORKING, AND IS THE FIRST THING TO LOOK AT
+
+**Grass does not spawn.** `GT_AlpineLab_Ground` exists with three
+varieties at 14/18/22 instances per 10 m2, read back from the asset; a
+`LandscapeGrassOutput` is in the graph; the material compiles with zero

+suspect is the wire from the weight expression to the output's named
+input pin -- the pin is named by the GrassInput's `name`, and a failed
+lookup there would leave a graph that compiles and produces nothing.

+## 2026-08-09 — I READ FIVE CAPTURE OUTCOMES OFF 196 BYTES OF TAIL, AND REPORTED ONE OF THEM BACKWARDS
+
+The AlpineLab_v1 mountain frames landed and are good. The story I told
+about how they landed was wrong, and the mechanism is the plainest
+non-negotiable in the file.
+
+### WHAT I CLAIMED
+
+Commit `7db2d79f` records a controlled comparison: five capture attempts,
+one variable, conclusion that WINDOW FOCUS is what makes a HighResShot
+complete on this machine. The discriminating row was
+
+    21:09  multiplier 2  SUCCEEDED  1.6 GB free, editor forced foreground
+
+### WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED
+
+That run reported **NO NEW OR REWRITTEN FILE**. So did the three before
+it. `HighresScreenshot00003.png` appeared at 21:09:40 anyway, and it is
+**856x561** -- the viewport's own size, which is what `HighResShot 1`
+produces, not the 1712x1122 a `HighResShot 2` would. The likeliest
+origin is the 21:02 `HighResShot 1` completing late once focus let a
+backlog drain. **Which request produced it is genuinely unknown.**
+
+### ROOT CAUSE
+
+Every one of those runs was invoked as
+
+    python scripts/highres_shot.py ... | tail -4
+
+`highres_shot.py` prints its verdict as a BANNER FOLLOWED BY A LONG
+DIAGNOSTIC. `tail -4` therefore kept the diagnostic and threw away the
+verdict. The saved task outputs are 196, 196, 257 and 319 bytes. I read
+five outcomes off the last four lines of a message whose FIRST line said
+the opposite, and then built a five-row causal table on top of them.
+
+**Non-negotiable 14: never truncate the output of an operation you
+cannot repeat.** A HighResShot on a throttled editor at 1.6 GB free is
+that operation exactly -- each attempt cost minutes of wall clock and
+could not simply be re-run. I truncated all five.
+
+The one run I could read in full (581 bytes, the 20:50 success) is the
+only capture outcome of the night that rests on the tool's own verdict
+rather than on my inference from a directory listing.
+
+### THE SECOND, COMPOUNDING ERROR
+
+Having discarded the verdicts, I fell back on the file system -- and
+attributed a new file to the request I had just made. That is the SAME
+defect I had caught and written up ninety minutes earlier in the same
+session, when `HighresScreenshot00001.png` turned out to be a four-hour
+old frame of a different world. I identified the trap ("a file is there
+is not my shot landed"), wrote it into a commit message, and then walked
+into it from the other direction: not a stale file read as fresh, but a
+fresh file read as MINE.
+
+`highres_shot.py` already solves both: it snapshots `{path: mtime}`
+before the command and reports only genuinely new or rewritten files.
+The tool was right and available in both cases. I overrode it with a
+directory listing twice.
+
+### WHAT CHANGES
+
+- Capture runs go to a FILE, or are read whole. `tail` on a tool that
+  prints a verdict then an essay is a truncation of the answer.
+- Focus before a capture stays worth doing. It is a PLAUSIBLE
+  contributor to the stall class, alongside memory. **It is not
+  demonstrated**, and the record now says so.
+- The frames themselves are unaffected: the camera was parked at 20:55
+  with position and aim read back to 0.00 cm and 0.000 deg, and every
+  request after that time renders that same view.
+
+### THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART
+
+The wrong claim was not a guess I flagged as a guess. It was presented
+as a measurement, with a table, in a commit message, as the kind of
+controlled comparison this project treats as evidence. A fabricated
+control is worse than no control, because it ends the investigation.

+## 2026-08-09 — THE LANDSCAPE IMPORT FAILED SILENTLY, AND THE FILENAME WAS THE CAUSE
+
+Ryan ran the manual landscape import from `IMPORT` step 4 of R-GAEA. The
+dialog asked *"Use 'AlpineLab_v<v>_Height_normalized.png' Tiled Image?"*,
+and after it, **no Landscape actor existed**. No modal error, nothing in
+the log worth reading. The mask textures imported fine, so the session
+looked mostly successful.
+
+### ROOT CAUSE, AT SOURCE LINES
+
+`Engine/Source/Editor/LandscapeEditor/Private/LandscapeTiledImage.cpp`:
+
+    :14-19   Tokens = { u, v, x, y }
+    :22-24   GetTokenRegex(prefix) -> prefix + "(-?[0-9]+)"
+    :190     CheckTiledNamePath -- replaces every token match in the
+             BASE FILENAME with a glob, then looks for matching files
+    :86-104  only <u>/<x> assign the tile X coordinate;
+             only <v>/<y> assign Y
+    :105     if (X >= 0 && Y >= 0)  -- the guard that decides whether a
+             tile is recorded at all
+    :149-155 TileFilenames.Num() == 0  ->  Error "No files found"
+
+`LandscapeEditorUtils.cpp:80` is the prompt, and YES sets
+`Filename = TiledFileNamePattern`.
+
+So: `AlpineLab_v1_Height_normalized` contains `v1`, which matches
+`v(-?[0-9]+)`. The pattern becomes `AlpineLab_v<v>_Height_normalized
+.png`, the glob finds one file, and the prompt fires. Answering YES then
+sets **Y = 1-1 = 0 and leaves X = -1**, because the name has no `u` or
+`x` token. The `X >= 0 && Y >= 0` guard adds no tiles, the tile list is
+empty, and Load returns "No files found" -- which the dialog does almost
+nothing with. **The import cannot succeed and does not say so.**
+
+### WHAT I GOT WRONG ON THE WAY, AND IT MATTERS
+
+Ryan described the trigger as *"the `_v1_` pattern"* and *"digit-adjacent
+underscores"*, and I wrote a `_\d+_` regex to detect it. **That regex is
+wrong and would have called the canonical filename SAFE** -- `_v1_` is
+underscore-letter-digit-underscore, not underscore-digit-underscore. My
+own detector printed "clean" for the exact file that had just failed.
+
+That mismatch is the only reason I opened the engine source instead of
+shipping the fix. **An instrument that disagrees with a known-bad case is
+information, not noise** -- the same shape as the 2026-08-08 near-miss
+where `git show` reported 100% of bytes differing. The real rule is
+broader and stranger than the reported one: **any `u`, `v`, `x` or `y`
+followed by digits, anywhere in the base filename, with no underscore
+required.** `Terrain_x0_y0` trips it (correctly, it is tiled).
+`Alpine_v2` trips it. `Everest_y2024` trips it.
+
+### THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS A COPY AND NOT A RENAME
+
+`AlpineLabHeight.png` -- byte-identical (sha256 verified), no digits at
+all, so no token can match. `rebuild_terrain.py` now writes BOTH names on
+every build, and `verify_build.py` declares the alias, asserts it is
+byte-identical to its canonical, and REFUSES on mismatch.
+
+Renaming would have been simpler and wrong. The canonical name is the
+provenance record that R-GAEA, the recipes and the sidecar all refer to;
+the alias is a convenience for one dialog. **Non-negotiable 3 applies
+here in its literal form: prefer an input that cannot express the
+catastrophic value over a gate that rejects it.** The prompt cannot be
+answered wrongly if it is never asked.
+
+`verify_build.py` also now prints, for every file in the package, which
+tiled tokens it matches -- so the next person hits a warning in a build
+report instead of a dialog at 11pm.
+
+### THE OTHER HALF: A VERIFIER THAT COULD NOT TELL FAILURE FROM SUCCESS
+
+`ue5_import_alpinelab.py` had checked the landscape and then imported the
+masks REGARDLESS. On this failure it would have reported "landscape
+verified: NO, masks imported: 5 of 5" -- a partial success over a level
+with no terrain. Masks are terrain-registered data; without a landscape
+they register to nothing.
+
+It now REFUSES at the landscape check and imports nothing, printing the
+tiled-prompt cause directly in the failure banner. It also gained two
+checks it should have had from the start:
+
+- **component count** vs the expected 4096 (64 x 64). A dialog set to
+  127 quads imports a perfectly valid landscape of the wrong terrain.
+- **height span** vs the 925.7 m that Z 180.81 predicts for a full-range
+  heightmap. This is a DIFFERENT REPRESENTATION of the Z scale than
+  reading `scale.z` back: `scale.z` is what the dialog wrote, the span is
+  what the geometry came out as. Non-negotiable 8 -- a read-back that
+  reads the field the setter wrote proves only that the value landed.
+
+And it now SKIPS masks that already exist rather than re-importing over
+live assets, reporting what is there instead of asserting it is right.

+## 2026-08-09 — THE GAEA REBUILD IS AUTOMATED, AND THE Z SCALE WAS ONE ARITHMETIC STEP FROM BEING 2.7x WRONG
+
+Ryan ruled on the two items R-GAEA left open and asked for the headless
+rebuild path. Three things worth keeping came out of it.
+
+### 1. A NORMALIZATION THAT DESTROYS THE THING YOU LATER NEED
+
+`ue5_import_alpinelab.py` shipped with `TODO_Z_SCALE_PLACEHOLDER = 100.0`
+and a note that solving it was not trivial. It was solvable, and the
+solution is instructive about WHY it looked hard.
+
+The Gaea project declares its elevation range:
+
+    C:\Users\ryanb\AppData\Roaming\QuadSpinner\Gaea\2.0\Autosaves\
+      AlpineLabe_v1_2026-08-09_19-12-59.terrain      (JSON)
+        /Assets/$values[0]/Terrain/Height = 2500.0     metres
+
+Reading that and typing `2500 / 512 * 100 = 488.3` into the import dialog
+gives a landscape **2.7x too tall**. It would look like a dramatic alpine
+range and nothing would flag it, because there is no instrument in this
+project that measures a mountain against reality.
+
+The 2500 is the PROJECT's full range. This BUILD occupied only 496-24763
+of 65535 before the export was stretched to full range, so the real span
+is `2500 * (24763-496)/65535 = 925.73 m` and Z is **180.81**.
+
+**The general shape: a normalization step destroys the very quantity a
+later step needs, and it does so silently, leaving a file that looks
+complete.** The number was still recoverable here only because the
+un-normalized `Snow_Out.png` happened to be kept in `_archive/`. Had it
+been deleted as "superseded", the vertical scale of this terrain would
+have been unrecoverable from the package.
+
+So `rebuild_terrain.py` records the source range into
+`height_normalization.json` BEFORE it stretches, alongside the derived Z
+and both sha256s. And `derive_z_scale()` returns `None` when the project
+range cannot be read — an unknown vertical scale is reported as unknown,
+never defaulted to UE's 100, which would read as a decision.
+
+### 2. AN ACCEPTANCE TEST THAT FAILED ON A CORRECT RESULT
+
+The proof that automated normalization reproduces tonight's manual
+process compared **sha256**, because that is what this project does
+everywhere — non-negotiable 20 hashes adopted artefacts against their
+source, and it is right to.
+
+It FAILED. `9d21f165...` against `11bb09f7...`, and the file sizes were
+26 MB against 14 MB — an 88% difference, which is an absurd magnitude for
+"the same image".
+
+**An absurd magnitude is a question about the instrument** (the
+2026-08-08 audit's own near-miss, where `git show` returned an LFS
+pointer and reported 100% of bytes differing). Decoding both PNGs and
+differencing the arrays gives **16,777,216 of 16,777,216 samples
+identical, max |diff| 0**. `write_png16_grey` emits filter-0 rows; the
+reference uses adaptive PNG filters. Same samples, different encoding.
+
+**The rule this yields: hashing is correct for a file COPIED and wrong
+for a file RE-ENCODED.** A hash test on a re-encoded artefact tests the
+encoder. The sha INEQUALITY is now kept in the proof as the positive
+control for the pixel test — if both ever passed, the test would be
+comparing a file with itself.
+
+Nearly-shipped consequence: I would have concluded the automation did not
+match the manual process, and gone looking for a difference in the
+arithmetic that was not there.
+
+### 3. A REJECTED ENTRY THAT BANNED THE OPERATION INSTEAD OF THE DEFECT
+
+R1 REJECTED said **CROP, NEVER RESAMPLE**. The intake resampled, on
+instruction, and R-GAEA section 7 recorded the conflict rather than
+resolving it.
+
+Ryan ruled: narrow the entry, do not grandfather the intake. The recorded
+failure is height resampled while the masks are NOT — a defect of
+INDEPENDENCE, which an entry phrased as a ban on resampling cannot
+express. Whole-package resampling in one verified operation is permitted;
+independent or differently-filtered resampling is not.
+
+**And the permission is enforced rather than intended.** `verify_build.py`
+now collects the dimensions of the heightmap and every mask and exits 4
+if more than one distinct size is present — non-negotiable 24, because a
+rule that lives only in a REJECTED entry is a rule the next session has
+to remember. Proven on `002/UE5_Ready`: all 6 files at 4033x4033.
+
+The register claim behind the permission is tested too, and offline:
+`check_registration()` takes the brightest 1% of the flow mask and asks
+where those pixels sit in the heightmap's percentile ranks. Water runs
+downhill, so a registered mask must sit below the median. Measured
+**37.7** against a random control at **50.1** — the control is what makes
+the low median evidence rather than an artefact of the statistic.
+
+### WHAT IS NOT DONE
+
+`rebuild_terrain.py` has **never built anything**. Its preflight, its
+normalization and its refusals are proven (12/12, offline); the Gaea
+subprocess call is not. It also cannot run yet: every `AlpineLabe_v1
+.terrain` on this machine is an AUTOSAVE, and the script refuses to build
+the canonical terrain from a file Gaea rotates and overwrites. Saving the
+project once from Gaea is the unblock, and it is Ryan's to do.
