+## 8. REGISTRATION IS CHECKED OFFLINE, BEFORE THE EDITOR EVER SEES IT
+
+The §7 ruling permits whole-package resampling **because register is
+preserved**. That claim is now tested rather than argued.
+`verify_build.py --build <pkg>/UE5_Ready` runs `check_registration()`:
+
+- Take the brightest **1%** of `Erosion2_Flow` (drainage lines).
+- Convert the HEIGHTMAP to percentile ranks, 0-100.
+- Report the median height-rank under those flow pixels.
+
+Water runs downhill, so a registered flow mask must sit **below** the
+median terrain. A random control of the same pixel count is drawn in the
+same run and must land at ~50, which is what makes a low flow median
+evidence rather than an artefact of the statistic
+(non-negotiable 8 — the control uses a different population, not the
+same one measured twice).
+
+Measured on `002/UE5_Ready` after the resize:

+    flow median rank   37.7
+    random control     50.1      (control valid: |50.1 - 50| < 5)
+    separation        -12.4      PASS
+
+**This is a REGISTER test, not a terrain-quality test.** It proves the
+masks still point at the same ground the heightmap describes. It says
+nothing about whether the erosion looks good.

+# R-GAEA — AlpineLab_v1 terrain package intake (LOCKED, PARTIALLY PROVEN)
+
+Intake path for a Gaea 2 export package into a UE5 landscape. Proven
+through resize + verification on build `002`; the editor import half is
+written and **NOT YET RUN**.
+
+## 1. THE GAEA GRAPH
+
+    Mountain + Ridge
+      -> Combine [Max]
+      -> Erosion2 [ Duration 21.65, Downcutting 0.45,
+                    ErosionScale 1413.25 ]
+      -> Snow     [ Melt 0.45, Snow Line ~0.65,
+                    Depth channel via Autolevel ]
+
+## 2. TWO GOTCHAS, both Gaea 2.3 behaviour
+
+- **Snow Line is INVERTED.** A LOWER value produces MORE snow. Setting
+  it "higher for more snow" gives the opposite of the intent and reads
+  as a broken sim rather than a reversed control.
+- **The Snow channel exports as a degenerate near-1-bit PNG when the sim
+  output is uniform.** The file is present, correctly named and correctly
+  sized, and carries no information. **Presence is not content.**
+  `verify_build.py` checks distinct-value count for exactly this, and
+  file SIZE is NOT a usable proxy — on build 002 `Snow_Snow.png` is 515
+  KB against ~11 MB siblings and is perfectly healthy at 42,677 unique
+  values; it is small because it is 12% coverage compressing well.
+
+## 3. PACKAGE CONTRACT — build 002, measured at intake
+
+All 16-bit greyscale PNG, 4096², verified by `scripts/verify_build.py`:
+
+    AlpineLab_v1_Height_normalized.png  0-65535  mean 20477.9  THE heightmap
+    Erosion2_Flow.png                   0-65535  20.0% nonzero, sparse
+    Erosion2_Wear.png                   0-6019   NEEDS REMAP
+    Erosion2_Deposits.png               0-512    NEEDS STRONG REMAP
+    Snow_Snow.png                       0-65535  hard coverage
+    SnowMask_Out.png                    0-65535  graded depth, autoleveled
+
+**PROVENANCE — the heightmap was normalized before export.** The
+pre-normalization Gaea output spanned **496-24763** of 65535 and was
+stretched to full range. This matters and is not bookkeeping: the
+normalization ALREADY changed the height mapping, so any "Gaea metres"
+figure applied naively to the imported landscape is wrong by that ratio.
+
+`Snow_Out.png` is the un-normalized original height and is **EXCLUDED**;
+it lives in `_archive/` and must not be imported.
+
+## 4. ORDERED STEPS
+
+```
+1. python scripts/verify_build.py --build <pkg>/002
+2. python scripts/resize_gaea_build.py --build <pkg>/002 --archive-excluded
+3. python scripts/verify_build.py --build <pkg>/002/UE5_Ready \
+       --expect-size 4033x4033
+4. IN THE EDITOR, BY HAND: Landscape Mode > New > Import from File
+5. IN THE EDITOR: run scripts/ue5_import_alpinelab.py
+```
+
+Step 4 is manual **because UE 5.8 cannot create a landscape from
+Python** — verified against the generated stub for this install: there
+is no create/import-landscape function in the reflected surface, and the
+only two import entry points are methods on an EXISTING `LandscapeProxy`
+taking a `TextureRenderTarget2D`, not a file
+(`unreal.py:531939` and `:531954`). The Landscape tool's own Import
+dialog does heightmap, section layout and scale in one place; scripting
+around it would reimplement a solved problem badly.
+
+## 5. THE MASKS IMPORT AS TEXTURES, NOT WEIGHTMAPS
+
+Decided for this build, with reasons, because the brief left it open:
+a weightmap import needs a render target, a `LandscapeLayerInfoObject`
+per layer AND a landscape material declaring matching layers — none of
+which exist for a new evaluation landscape, so "import as weightmaps"
+silently becomes "author a layered landscape material first". Texture
+import via `AssetImportTask` is the ordinary path and loses nothing: the
+16-bit data is preserved and a texture can be promoted later.
+
+Settings inherited from `import_layer_textures.py`, and READ BACK after
+setting: `srgb=False`, `TC_VECTOR_DISPLACEMENTMAP` (uncompressed —
+a block compressor destroys thin drainage lines), `TA_CLAMP` both axes
+(these map 1:1 onto the terrain and must never tile).
+
+## 6. OPEN — Z SCALE IS A PLACEHOLDER
+
+`TODO_Z_SCALE_PLACEHOLDER = 100.0` is UE's default, **not a
+measurement**. The Gaea metres-per-unit mapping is unconfirmed for this
+build and is complicated by the normalization above. Solve it against a
+known real-world elevation span; until then every elevation-derived
+number off this landscape is provisional.
+
+## 7. CONFLICT WITH R1's REJECTED ENTRY — UNRESOLVED, RYAN TO RULE
+
+R1 REJECTED says: *"Resampling a power-of-two Gaea export to N+1 →
+geometry stretches and the terrain no longer matches the weightmap →
+**CROP, NEVER RESAMPLE**"*.
+
+This intake **RESAMPLED** 4096 → 4033, on Ryan's explicit instruction
+("Resize, do NOT crop") given 2026-08-09.
+
+The two are not obviously reconcilable and the locked entry is NOT
+amended here. What can be said:
+
+- The recorded failure mode is *height resampled while the weightmap is
+  not*, so the two fall out of register. **That does not apply here:**
+  the heightmap and all five masks were resampled by the identical
+  factor to the identical target in one operation, so they remain in
+  register with each other. Mean values were preserved almost exactly
+  (height 20477.9 -> 20477.9, wear 985.8 -> 985.9).
+- What DOES change is **metres-per-pixel, by 1.56%**, which is the
+  "geometry stretches" half of the entry. That lands inside the
+  unresolved Z-scale question rather than beside it.
+- A measured side effect worth knowing: resampling SPREAD the sparse
+  masks. `Erosion2_Flow` went from **20.0% to 43.1% nonzero** while its
+  mean moved only +4.6% — Lanczos tails widening thin drainage lines at
+  low amplitude. Harmless for a mask that gets remapped; not harmless if
+  anyone ever treats flow coverage as a measured quantity.
+
+**Ruling needed:** either the R1 entry is narrowed to "resample height
+without resampling the masks", or this intake is redone with a crop.

    Found by re-reading the build output when Ryan asked me to check it. The

    about to claim", and the answer was a number that was not there.
    
    WHAT THE OUTPUT DID NOT SAY
    
      GroundClutter  ->  /Game/Foliage/GT_alpine_GroundClutter
          SM_Boulder05a                       0.900 /10m2
          SM_River_Rock_01                    0.600 /10m2
          2 variety(ies), densities sum to 1.5 against a species total of 1.5
    
    Densities get a real read-back -- the builder sums what the ENGINE kept
    on the asset and compares it to the species total, which is a different
    instrument from the list it wrote. The CULL DISTANCE appears nowhere. It
    is set and never mentioned, so nothing in the report distinguishes "cull
    70 m applied" from "cull silently defaulted".
    
    THE DEFECT BEHIND IT
    
    make_landscape_material.py:2441 read
    
        "cull_cm": float(sp.get("cull_distance_m", 12000.0)) * 100.0,
    
    and import_heightmap validated the key only `if "cull_distance_m" in sp`.
    So a grass species could omit it, validate clean, and receive a TWELVE
    KILOMETRE cull. At this recipe's locked 12 tufts/m2 that is pi*12000^2*12
    = about 5.4 BILLION instances.
    
    AND THE LESSON WAS ALREADY IN THAT FILE, FORTY LINES ABOVE
    
    The comment on the instanced cull records that every instanced species
    was left on the engine default of 0, "which FoliageType.h:292 documents
    as '0 disables', so 28,302 505k-triangle trees were submitted every frame
    across an 8 km map until the GPU missed the Windows TDR deadline and
    returned DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG".
    
    Same file, same validator function, same field name, same failure mode --
    and the grass branch beside it never got the rule.
    
      A LESSON APPLIED TO ONE BRANCH OF A FUNCTION IS NOT APPLIED.
    
    Non-negotiable 4 says sweep the class the moment you find it. This is
    that sweep failing at the smallest possible radius: not "grep the repo"
    but "read the other half of the if". The instanced path got the fix and
    its post-mortem comment; the grass path got neither, and the comment's
    presence made the area LOOK audited.
    
    The shape is also already on CLAUDE.md's casualty list -- "CullDistance 0
    means 'disabled', not 'unlimited', and cost a GPU hang". A magnitude that
    reads as a harmless default meaning something catastrophic.
    
    THE FIX IS NON-NEGOTIABLE 3, NOT A BIGGER GATE
    
    cull_distance_m is now REQUIRED for system:"grass" and bounded (0, 250],
    so 12 km is no longer EXPRESSIBLE rather than merely refused. There is no
    default left in the builder.
    
    Enforced in BOTH places -- validator and
    make_landscape_material._grass_cull_cm() -- because the builder is
    runnable without preflight. That is the second time in one session that
    "the validator will have run" turned out to be an assumption rather than
    a fact, after the rock `role` fail-open this morning.
    
    The bound comes from this recipe's own locked 50 m, which R11 measured as
    already the best trade; 250 m is about 24x that cost and is a ceiling,
    not a recommendation.

      validator: key removed / 12000 / 0 / "far"        4 rejected
      builder:   shipped recipe resolves  [+ve control]
                 key removed / 12000.0 / 0.0 / True     4 refused

+## 2026-08-08 — THE BUILD OUTPUT REPORTED WHAT IT SET AND NOT WHAT IT MEANT, AND A 12 KM GRASS CULL WAS ONE MISSING KEY AWAY
+
+**What prompted it.** Ryan said *"check the build output"* after I had
+already read it once and called it clean. Reading it again with the
+question *"what does this NOT tell me?"* rather than *"is anything
+wrong?"* produced the finding.
+
+**What the output says about the new grass type:**
+
+    GroundClutter  ->  /Game/Foliage/GT_alpine_GroundClutter
+        SM_Boulder05a                       0.900 /10m2
+        SM_River_Rock_01                    0.600 /10m2
+        2 variety(ies), densities sum to 1.5 against a species total of 1.5
+
+**Densities get a genuine read-back** — the builder sums what the ENGINE
+kept on the asset and compares it against the species total, which is a
+different instrument from the list it wrote. **The CULL DISTANCE appears
+nowhere.** It is set and never mentioned, so nothing in the report
+distinguishes "cull 70 m applied" from "cull silently defaulted".
+
+**What was behind it.**
+`make_landscape_material.py:2441` read
+
+    "cull_cm": float(sp.get("cull_distance_m", 12000.0)) * 100.0,
+
+and `import_heightmap` validated the key only `if "cull_distance_m" in
+sp`. So a grass species could omit it, validate clean, and receive a
+**twelve kilometre** cull. At this recipe's locked 12 tufts/m² that is
+`π·12000²·12` ≈ **5.4 billion instances**.
+
+**AND THE LESSON WAS ALREADY IN THAT FILE, FORTY LINES ABOVE.** The
+comment on the instanced cull reads:
+
+> *"…every instanced species was left on the engine default of 0, which
+> `FoliageType.h:292` documents as '0 disables', so 28,302
+> 505k-triangle trees were submitted every frame across an 8 km map
+> until the GPU missed the Windows TDR deadline and returned
+> `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`."*
+
+The same file, the same validator function, the same field name, the same
+failure mode — and the grass branch beside it was never given the rule.
+
+> **A LESSON APPLIED TO ONE BRANCH OF A FUNCTION IS NOT APPLIED.** Non-
+> negotiable 4 says sweep the defect class the moment you find it; this
+> is the sweep failing at the smallest possible radius — not "grep the
+> repo", but "read the other half of the `if`". The instanced path got
+> the fix and its post-mortem comment; the grass path got neither, and
+> the comment's presence made the area *look* audited.
+
+**And the shape of the defect is the one CLAUDE.md's casualty list already
+names:** *"`CullDistance` 0 means 'disabled', not 'unlimited', and cost a
+GPU hang."* A magnitude that reads as a harmless default — `12000.0`, or
+`0` — meaning something catastrophic.
+
+**The fix is non-negotiable 3, not a bigger gate.** `cull_distance_m` is
+now REQUIRED for `system: "grass"` and bounded `(0, 250]`, so the
+12 km value is no longer expressible rather than merely refused. Enforced
+in BOTH places, because the builder is runnable without preflight — the
+same assumption that let an unknown rock `role` be dropped silently
+earlier the same day, and the second time in one session that "the
+validator will have run" turned out to be an assumption rather than a
+fact.
+
+**Proven 9 ways**, positive control first: 4 validator probes (key
+removed, 12000, 0, a string), 5 builder probes (including a bool, since a
+bool IS an int in Python and this suite has been bitten by that before).
+The shipped recipe still resolves to Meadow 5000 cm and GroundClutter
+7000 cm — **which is also the answer to the original question: the 70 m I
+wrote did reach the payload.**
+
+**What this says about reading output.** My first pass asked "is anything
+wrong here?" and everything present was correct, so it passed. The second
+pass asked "what would I need to see to believe the thing I am about to
+claim?" — and the answer was a number that was not there. **An output
+review that only examines what was printed cannot find an omission.**

+## 2026-08-08 — I CALLED A RUNNING BUILD DEAD, AND THE EVIDENCE I USED WAS REAL
+
+**What happened.** The landscape material rebuild was submitted at 05:06.
+Ten minutes later I checked the editor log and found **two** non-heartbeat
+lines since submission, one of them my own identity probe. No
+`LogMaterial`, no `LogShaderCompilers`, no `ShaderCompileWorker` process.
+I reported to Ryan that *"the payload never began executing"*.
+
+It had. Shader compilation appears in the log at **05:24**, the build
+completed cleanly, and `GT_alpine_GroundClutter` is on disk.
+
+**Root cause.** `make_landscape_material` runs as ONE remote-exec payload
+and prints its marker at the END. From outside, a long successful build
+and a dead one look **identical** for as long as the build takes. I
+treated silence as a measurement when silence was the expected state.
+
+> **AN ABSENCE OF OUTPUT FROM A BATCH OPERATION IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT ITS
+> LIVENESS UNTIL YOU KNOW WHEN THAT OPERATION WOULD FIRST SPEAK.** The
+> question to ask before concluding anything is *"what would I expect to
+> see by now if this were working?"* — and if the honest answer is
+> "nothing", the observation carries no information.
+> This is non-negotiable 6 turned on myself: I could not look, and I
+> reported the number the broken measurement produced.
+
+**What I did right, and it is why this cost nothing:** I did not retry,
+did not kill the client, and checked the ARTEFACT — the material SHA on
+disk was byte-identical to the pre-build value, so I could say truthfully
+that nothing was damaged. Standing rule 6 says diagnose rather than
+brute-force, and diagnosing is what left the build alive to finish.
+
+**A better instrument existed and I used it late.** Editor CPU delta
+(2669 → 2689 s over 45 s) was the live-vs-stalled discriminator, and it
+said *working*. I read it, saw ~44% of one core, and talked myself out of
+it because it was not the multi-core burst I expected from shader
+compilation. **The measurement was right and my model of what it should
+look like was wrong.**

+capture and every background build silently inherits it.

+> This one survived seven days. The project has no instrument that reads
+> it, so its reversion is invisible until it costs a session — the same
+> shape as non-negotiable 17: *the file is not the state, and nothing was
+> checking either.*
+
+Candidate remedy, NOT built: a read-only line in `resource_guard` or
+`bootstrap` that reports the effective value alongside RAM, so a

+## 2026-08-08 — A GATE ROUTED BY THE WRONG KEY, AND THE FIX HAD TO BE STRICTER THAN THE THING IT REPLACED
+
+**What was attempted.** Ryan ruled: move carpet clutter density to the
+grass system. `ClutterRock` and `DrainageStone` became one grass species
+with two varieties, both using the same measured Fab rock meshes they had
+used as instances.
+
+**What happened.** The recipe validator refused:
+
+    foliage: .../SM_Boulder05a has no VERIFIED row in the normalisation
+    report ... after running scripts/blender/normalize_asset.py.
+
+These are native Fab `.uasset`s that **never went through Blender and
+never can** — R-ASSET forbids authoring into a Fab folder, the same
+boundary that closed the Nanite item earlier the same day.
+
+**Root cause, and the gate's own docstring stated the intent correctly.**
+`landscape_spec._recipe_mesh_paths_split:202` routes meshes with
+
+    out = rock if "role" in sp else veg
+
+— by **SPECIES KIND**. And the docstring says the two sets *"carry the
+SAME guarantee (this project knows where the mesh's base is) through two
+different instruments."*
+
+**But that guarantee is a property of the MESH, not of the species that
+names it.** `boulder_small` has a measured row and passes ruling (c);
+nothing about calling it "grass" instead of "rock" changes where its base
+is. The gate asked *"what kind of species is this?"* when the question is
+*"which instrument knows this mesh's base?"* — and those two keys agreed
+for as long as rocks were only ever used by rock species.
+
+> **WHEN A GATE ROUTES A CHECK, THE ROUTING KEY IS PART OF THE GATE AND
+> MUST BE DERIVED FROM THE SAME QUESTION THE CHECK ASKS.** A key that
+> merely CORRELATES with the right answer works until the first case
+> where the correlation breaks — and the failure is a refusal of valid
+> input, which reads as the gate working.
+
+**THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A ROUTING FIX.** Asking both
+registries would have been a relaxation if the two placers were
+equivalent. **They are not**, and I nearly missed it:
+
+- `rock_scatter.plan_species` **READS** `base_offset_z_m` and subtracts
+  it. The dry run prints `base offset -0.618 m -> corrected`. A rock
+  lands on its base whatever the vendor pivot.
+- The engine's landscape grass system **corrects nothing.** It places the
+  mesh's PIVOT on the surface and the geometry falls where it falls.
+
+So the same measured row means two different things depending on who
+places the mesh. A mesh that is perfectly safe as a rock can be
+**half-buried** as grass — and a BOX-CENTRED pivot buries exactly 50% by
+construction, because `base_offset == -extent_z`.
+
+Measured across the registry:
+
+    boulder_small        buried  17.0%    OK
+    river_rock           buried  16.8%    OK
+    tree_stump           buried   5.5%    OK
+    boulder_medium_01    buried  47.6%    REFUSED for grass
+    hero_boulder_large   buried  50.0%    REFUSED for grass   <- exactly half
+
+**So the fix adds a condition that neither gate had:**
+`uncorrected_pivot_errors()`, bounded at 25% by matching the rock path's
+`embed_frac` validator message ("0.9 buries more than half the rock") —
+half is the stated disaster line, so a quarter is the conservative side.
+The net change is **stricter**, not looser: a mesh in neither registry is
+still refused, and grass meshes now face a test that did not exist.
+
+**The two carpet meshes passing at ~17% was LUCK, not design.** They
+happen to have near-base pivots. I checked the number before relying on
+it, and the 50.0% cases are in the probe suite precisely so the next
+person cannot rely on that luck silently.
+
+**Five probes, positive control first**, folded into `prove_gates` rather
+than left in a scratch file — the shipped recipe must PASS, two
+box-centred rocks must refuse, a mesh in neither registry must refuse,
+and the rock path must be provably unchanged. 41 checkers, exit 0.

    asserts each mesh's measured lod_count equals the lod_depth it declares,
    so there is no longer a place to type either.
    
    DEADFALL IS REFUSED BY RULING (c), AND THE GATE WAS RIGHT
    
    The first dry run refused the whole plan:
    
      Deadfall  horizontal 0.419 m (limit 0.258 = 0.25 x min extent) REFUSE
    
    vegetation_debris is 3.64 x 1.03 x 0.75 m with its pivot 0.419 m
    off-centre. Under the rock path's random yaw it sweeps a 0.84 m circle
    while being 1.03 m wide, so it would visibly wander off the spot the
    scatter aimed at. I had flagged that 0.419 m as notable when it was
    measured earlier today; the gate refused it independently, which is two
    representations agreeing rather than one.
    
    Dropped rather than the gate weakened. The pivot cannot be fixed at
    source -- Fab content, and R-ASSET forbids authoring into a Fab folder,
    the same boundary that closed the Nanite item this morning. The enabling
    work is in BACKLOG: rock_pivots.json stores the pivot MAGNITUDE and
    discards the VECTOR, so the offset cannot currently be cancelled at
    placement by offsetting each instance by the yaw-rotated pivot.
    
    FINDING 1 -- THE PRIOR WORKS, AND ITS POSITIVE DIRECTION IS WEAK
    
    TreeStump planned four ways, same seed, only canopy_bias varying,
    measuring each stump's distance to its nearest conifer:
    
      canopy_bias   placed   d_p50 m   frac within one canopy radius
             0.00     1206      5.67          0.172
             0.45     1193      5.54          0.186
             0.90     1158      5.39          0.194
            -0.90      947      6.51          0.022    <- negative control
    
    The negative control is what makes this evidence. A knob that only moves
    one way tells you it does something; one that pushes stumps AWAY when
    inverted tells you it does the thing it claims.
    
    But +0.90 buys 13% relative where -0.90 removes 7.8x, and the asymmetry
    is STRUCTURAL. Canopy occupancy is a peaked field -- canopy radius
    3.07 m against a median nearest-trunk distance of 5.67 m gives
    exp(-(5.67/3.07)^2) about 0.03 -- so most candidates sit near zero, the
    population mean sits near the bottom of the range, and
    clip(1 + bias*(c-mean)*2, 0, 2) has the whole interval going down while
    SATURATING against the clip going up. Flow is a smooth field with a
    mid-range mean and does not have this.
    
    Deliberately NOT fixed. The formula is shared with place_foliage, is
    correct there, and its output is proven bit-identical across 157,554
    conifers. Changing the reference changes a shared definition, which is a
    ruling. The lever is named in RECIPES and BACKLOG: a low percentile
    instead of the mean, or a non-linear occupancy.

+## 2026-08-08 — A GATE THAT COULD NOT SEE THE DEFECT IT WAS WRITTEN FOR, AND THE SELFTEST THAT SAID SO
+
+**What was attempted.** Ryan ruled that the rock path should gain the
+shared flow prior and use conifer positions for under-tree clustering.
+`placement_priors.load_trunks()` converts a plan's ABSOLUTE centimetres
+into the LOCAL metres that candidate positions use. Coordinate frames are
+the dangerous part, so I guarded it — and cited, in the docstring, the
+defect it was guarding against: `place_foliage.py:247-251`, where metres
+were stored under a header saying "cm" and the offline verifier
+*"sampled the map CENTRE for every instance and duly reported that
+flow_bias did nothing"*.
+
+**What happened.** The guard was an extent check: refuse if the converted
+points fall outside `[0, span]`. The selftest fed it exactly the cited
+defect — a plan with metres where centimetres belong — and **the check
+passed it.**
+
+**Root cause, and it is arithmetic.** Dividing metres by 100 does not
+scatter points outside the map. It **collapses them toward the origin**,
+which after the origin offset lands them near the map **CENTRE**. On this
+world that is 4032 m into an 8064 m span — as comfortably inside the
+bounds as a point can be. The extent check is not weak here; it is
+**structurally blind**, because the failure mode moves points *inward*
+and the check only looks *outward*.
+
+And the original defect report said so. *"Sampled the map CENTRE for
+every instance"* is the symptom written down years of sessions ago, and I
+read it, quoted it in the docstring, and then wrote a guard that cannot
+detect a point at the centre.
+
+> **WHEN A DEFECT REPORT NAMES THE SYMPTOM, THE GATE MUST BE ABLE TO
+> DETECT THAT SYMPTOM. Quoting the report is not the same as satisfying
+> it.** Writing the citation into the docstring made the guard *feel*
+> derived from evidence while its actual logic was derived from a generic
+> intuition ("bad coordinates go out of range"). The citation and the
+> code were never checked against each other.
+
+**The fix, and why it is TWO checks.** The honest discriminator is not
+geometry at all — it is the **declared contract**. `place_foliage` writes
+`"units": "cm, degrees, uniform scale"` into every plan. That declaration
+is now READ and required; absent or non-cm REFUSES. The extent check is
+kept as a second, independent check because it catches a *different*
+error the units check cannot see: correct units against the **wrong
+origin**.
+
+Neither check subsumes the other, and the selftest asserts each against
+the case the other misses — including an explicit assertion that the
+extent check alone *would* have passed the metres-as-cm plan, so the
+blindness is recorded as a passing test rather than as a memory.
+**21/21.**
+
+**Why non-negotiable 2 caught it and review would not have.** *"A gate
+that has only seen good input has not been tested. Prove it refuses."*
+The guard was written, looked correct, cited its source, and would have
+survived any amount of reading. It took **feeding it the actual failing
+input** — which cost about four lines — to find that it was decorative.
+

+## 2026-08-08 — A VALIDATOR THAT RAISES HAS CONVERTED "INVALID RECIPE" INTO "TOOL CRASHED"
+
+**What happened.** I added a cross-field rule: a rock species declaring
+`canopy_bias` requires a `foliage.canopy` block. Written as
+
+    if float(sp.get("canopy_bias", 0.0) or 0.0) != 0.0:
+
+Then a new `prove_gates` probe fed it `canopy_bias: "lots"` — a string,
+the ordinary shape of a typo — and `_validate_recipe` died with
+`ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'lots'`, taking the whole
+suite with it.
+
+**Root cause.** The bounds check immediately above already refuses a
+non-numeric `canopy_bias`. But error *accumulation* is not error
+*handling*: this validator appends to a list and keeps going, so the
+recorded error does not stop the next line from touching the same bad
+value. **I wrote the cross-field check as though the bounds check above
+it were a guard clause.** It is not; it is a note-taker.
+
+> **IN AN ERROR-ACCUMULATING VALIDATOR, EVERY CHECK MUST ASSUME EVERY
+> OTHER CHECK HAS ALREADY FAILED.** Recording that a value is invalid
+> does not make the value safe to use, and the checks after it still run
+> on it. Validate the TYPE before consuming the value, in each check that
+> consumes it.
+
+**Why this matters more than an ordinary crash.** A validator's entire
+job is to convert bad input into a *list of what to fix*. When it raises,
+the caller gets a traceback naming a line inside the validator instead —
+which reads as "the tool is broken", not "your recipe is wrong", and
+sends the next session debugging the wrong file. This project already has
+that lesson from the other direction: R12 REJECTED records *"a one-line
+exception summary from the planner"* as the wrong output for a failure
+that cost eight minutes to reproduce.
+
+**Fixed in both places, and the second is the important one.**
+`_is_num()` now precedes the float in the validator. AND
+`rock_scatter._bias()` refuses a non-numeric rather than letting
+`float()` raise — because that planner is runnable **without preflight**,
+which is the exact assumption that let an unknown `role` be dropped
+silently earlier the same day. A tool that can run standalone cannot
+treat validation as having happened.
+
+**The probe that found it took one line.** `("canopy_bias 'lots' (a
+string)", True, lambda s: s.update(canopy_bias="lots"), ...)`. Non-
+negotiable 2 again, and the second time in one session that writing the
+probe was worth more than writing the gate.
+

+## 2026-08-08 — THE PRIOR WORKS AND THE DENSITY DOES NOT, AND ONLY MEASURING SEPARATED THOSE TWO
+
+**What was attempted.** Ryan ruled: add the shared flow prior to the rock
+path and use conifer positions for under-tree clustering. Built, wired,
+gated, probed. Then two questions that a clean dry run does NOT answer:
+*does the prior actually cluster*, and *is the resulting density the
+thing Pass 5 asked for*.
+
+### FINDING 1 — the prior clusters, and its positive direction is weak
+
+`TreeStump` planned four ways, same seed, only `canopy_bias` varying,
+measuring each stump's distance to its nearest conifer:
+
+    canopy_bias   placed   d_p50 m   frac within one canopy radius
+           0.00     1206      5.67          0.172
+           0.45     1193      5.54          0.186
+           0.90     1158      5.39          0.194
+          -0.90      947      6.51          0.022    <- negative control
+
+**The negative control is what makes this evidence.** A knob that only
+moves one way tells you it does *something*; a knob that pushes stumps
+away from trunks when inverted tells you it does *the thing it claims*.
+
+**But +0.90 buys 13% relative where −0.90 removes 7.8×, and that
+asymmetry is STRUCTURAL.** Canopy occupancy is a **peaked** field: with a
+canopy radius of 3.07 m and a median nearest-trunk distance of 5.67 m,
+`exp(-(5.67/3.07)²)` ≈ 0.03, so most candidates sit near zero and the
+population mean sits near the bottom of the range. The shared multiplier
+`clip(1 + bias*(c − mean)*2, 0, 2)` therefore has the entire interval
+available going DOWN and **saturates against the clip at 2.0 going UP**.
+
+> **A CENTRED MULTIPLIER IS ONLY SYMMETRIC IF ITS REFERENCE SITS IN THE
+> MIDDLE OF THE PRIOR'S RANGE.** For a smooth field (flow) the mean does.
+> For a peaked field (canopy occupancy, proximity to anything sparse) it
+> does not, and the same formula silently becomes an EXCLUDER that can
+> barely attract. The formula is not wrong; the assumption that one
+> centring suits every prior is.
+
+**Deliberately NOT "fixed".** The formula is shared with `place_foliage`,
+is correct there, and its output is proven bit-identical across 157,554
+conifers. Changing the reference would change a shared definition, which
+is a ruling, not a tweak. Recorded with the lever named (a low percentile
+instead of the mean, or a non-linear occupancy).
+
+### FINDING 2 — the density is a CEILING ARTEFACT, not a tuning choice
+
+I picked the densities from measured geometry and the shipped Boulder
+species as precedent, then computed what they MEAN at 1.7 m eye height
+rather than trusting that they looked reasonable in a table:
+
+    ClutterRock   14,785 placed   5.81/ha   one per 1,721 m²   41.5 m apart
+    DrainageStone  9,024          3.66/ha   one per 2,736 m²   52.3 m apart
+
+**About fifteen small rocks across the entire 90 m cull disc.** A viewer
+walks 40 m between rocks. That is occasional debris; Pass 5 asked for
+ground you can read at foot level.
+
+And it cannot be tuned into existence. On the same ~2500 ha mask:
+
+    spacing 10 m ->   100/ha ->   250,000 instances = 1.0x the WHOLE ceiling
+    spacing  5 m ->   400/ha -> 1,000,000           = 4.0x
+    spacing  3 m -> 1,111/ha -> 2,777,778           = 11.1x
+
+against a 250,000 ceiling that conifers already occupy 157,554 of.
+
+> **WHEN A REQUIREMENT IS OFF BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE FROM ITS
+> MECHANISM'S CEILING, THE ANSWER IS THE WRONG MECHANISM, NOT THE WRONG
+> NUMBER.** The tell is that no value inside the allowed range delivers
+> the stated intent. I nearly recorded 5.8/ha as a first-pass value to
+> tune later; "tune it later" would have been years of tuning inside a
+> box that cannot contain the answer.
+
+**And the right mechanism was already in the recipe.** `Meadow` runs
+`system: "grass"` at `density_per_10m2: 120` — **120,000 per hectare** —
+generated by the landscape material's GrassOutput
+(`make_landscape_material.py:2150`, `LandscapeGrassType`), culled at
+50 m, at **zero** cost against the instance ceiling. Foot-level ground
+detail is exactly what that path is for.
+
+**Why the mistake was available at all.** RECIPES' Pass 5 ruling says
+clutter is *"added as new species entries through R12's existing
+machinery"*, and R12 is the INSTANCE machinery. I read a sentence about
+*which recipe governs* as a sentence about *which mechanism to use*, and
+never asked whether the mechanism could reach the density. **A scoping
+ruling names the owner, not the implementation** — and the two were
+written in one clause, so it took a measurement to notice they were
+separable.
+
+Recommendation recorded and NOT acted on, because moving carpet density
+to the grass system means a landscape material rebuild and
+B-BUILD-UNKNOWN is still open on that builder. Ryan's call.

+## 6. THE `clutter` ROLE — Pass 5 ground clutter (PLANNED, NOT PLACED)
+
+Added 2026-08-08. Pass 5's ruling says clutter is *"added as new species
+entries through R12's existing machinery"*, so it is a fourth `role`
+here rather than a recipe of its own. **`clutter` carries no special
+handling — the MASK does the placing.** It is a distinct role only so the
+per-role coverage and triangle reports group by it: folding ~25k
+foot-level pieces into `hero`'s row beside 759 landmark boulders produces
+a number that is arithmetically true and answers a question nobody asked
+(non-negotiable 22).
+
+### 6a. TWO NEW PRIORS, BOTH SHARED — `scripts/placement_priors.py`
+
+    flow_bias     [-1, 1]   drainage. Reads terrain/alpine_flow.png,
+                            the SAME map place_foliage's Conifer reads.
+    canopy_bias   [-1, 1]   under trees. Reads the conifer PLAN.
+
+Defined once for every consumer because a wetness field and a canopy
+field are physical facts, not per-tool knobs (non-negotiable 19).
+Bounded at |1.0| because the shared multiplier is
+`clip(1 + bias*(v - ref)*2, 0, 2)` — past 1.0 the clip does the work and
+the knob stops changing the result.
+
+**THE FLOW MAP IS NOT RAW ACCUMULATION.** `derive_aux_maps.py:213` writes
+`np.log1p(flow)`, min-max normalised. Do not read 0.5 as "half the water".
+
+**THE CANOPY PRIOR ASKS THE TRUNKS, NOT A RASTER, AND A MEASUREMENT
+FORCES THAT.** The grid is 4.0 m; the measured canopy radius is
+**3.068 m** (`fir_tree_01_c_LOD0`, dims 6.306 × 5.966 × 14.521 m,
+`Free/_measured/fir_tree_01.json` — the mesh actually PLACED, not the
+higher-poly `_a`/`_b`). A canopy is ~1.6 cells across, sigma 0.8, so **a
+rasterised field at map resolution cannot express "under this tree"** —
+only "in the woods vs in a clearing". Candidates are continuous, so a
+cKDTree gives each its nearest trunk AND that trunk's scale, and
+`c = exp(-(d/r)²)` with `r = radius_m × scale`.
+
+Shared block, sibling to `rock_scatter`:
+
+    foliage.canopy.plan       "alpine_Conifer.json"
+    foliage.canopy.radius_m   3.068     MEASURED — cite the source
+
+A declared bias with no field **REFUSES**; it is never skipped. A no-op
+bias that reads in the log as if it applied is the class at
+`place_foliage.py:247-251`.
+
+### 6a-i. THE PRIOR IS PROVEN TO WORK, AND ITS POSITIVE DIRECTION IS WEAK
+
+`TreeStump` planned four ways, same seed, only the knob varying;
+distance from each stump to its nearest conifer:
+
+    canopy_bias   placed   d_p50 m   frac within one canopy radius
+           0.00     1206      5.67          0.172
+           0.45     1193      5.54          0.186
+           0.90     1158      5.39          0.194
+          -0.90      947      6.51          0.022    <- negative control
+
+Direction is correct in both directions, which is what makes it evidence
+rather than motion. **But +0.90 buys only a 13% relative increase, while
+−0.90 removes 7.8× — and the asymmetry is STRUCTURAL, not a tuning
+miss.** Canopy occupancy is a PEAKED field: most candidates sit near 0,
+so the mean sits near the bottom of the range. `1 + bias*(c − mean)*2`
+then has the whole interval to push down and **saturates against the
+clip at 2.0** pushing up. Flow, a smooth field whose mean sits mid-range,
+does not have this.
+
+**Not silently "fixed", because the formula is shared and correct for
+flow.** If stronger clustering is wanted the lever is the REFERENCE
+(a lower percentile instead of the mean) or a non-linear occupancy, and
+either changes a shared definition — a decision, not a tweak. BACKLOG.
+
+### 6b. THE THREE SPECIES, AND WHY THERE ARE NOT FOUR
+
+    ClutterRock     boulder_small     0.89 x 0.90 x 0.43 m   5.8/ha on mask
+    DrainageStone   river_rock        0.49 x 0.56 x 0.39 m   3.7/ha
+    TreeStump       tree_stump        0.79 x 0.67 x 2.33 m   0.6/ha
+
+`lod_depth` 4 for all three, equal to the MEASURED `lod_count`.
+`TreeStump` is deliberately sparse because it measures **2.33 m tall** —
+a landmark, not foot-level clutter — and stands upright
+(`align_to_normal` 0.20) as the tree did.
+
+**Deadfall (`vegetation_debris`) is REFUSED by ruling (c) and is not
+here.** Measured 3.64 × 1.03 × 0.75 m with its pivot **0.419 m**
+off-centre horizontally against a limit of 0.258 m (0.25 × smallest
+horizontal dimension); under random yaw it sweeps a 0.84 m circle while
+being 1.03 m wide. The pivot cannot be fixed at source — Fab content, and
+R-ASSET forbids authoring into a Fab folder. `rock_pivots.json` stores
+the pivot MAGNITUDE and discards the VECTOR, so the offset cannot
+currently be cancelled at placement. BACKLOG carries the enabling work.
+
+### 6c. THE DENSITY FINDING — READ THIS BEFORE TUNING THE NUMBERS
+
+**The instance system structurally cannot deliver foot-level ground
+clutter at map scale. The planned densities are a ceiling artefact, not a
+tuning choice.** Measured from the dry run:
+
+    species          placed   per ha   1 per        spacing   in its cull disc
+    ClutterRock      14,785     5.81   1,721 m²      41.5 m         15
+    DrainageStone     9,024     3.66   2,736 m²      52.3 m          6
+    TreeStump         1,208     0.59  16,906 m²     130.0 m          3
+
+A viewer standing anywhere sees about **fifteen small rocks spread across
+a 90 m radius**. That is occasional debris, not ground texture. What
+foot-level texture would cost on the same ~2500 ha mask:
+
+    spacing 10 m ->    100/ha ->   250,000 instances = 1.0x the WHOLE ceiling
+    spacing  5 m ->    400/ha -> 1,000,000           = 4.0x
+    spacing  3 m ->  1,111/ha -> 2,777,778           = 11.1x
+
+The ceiling is 250,000 for the whole recipe and conifers already hold
+157,554.
+

    Flow and canopy become SHARED priors, and the canopy one asks the real trunks
    
    Ryan ruled: add the shared flow prior to the rock path and use conifer
    positions for the under-tree clustering. This builds both. Nothing is
    placed, no species is authored yet, the world is untouched.
    
    WHY A MODULE AND NOT TWO COPIES
    
    Pass 5's ruled density philosophy says clutter "gathers under trees,
    along drainage, and at cliff bases". Cliff bases were already covered by
    rock_scatter's talus deposit field. The other two were not:
    
      drainage      lived inline in place_foliage, VEGETATION path only
      under trees   existed nowhere
    
    A wetness field and a canopy field are physical facts about the world,
    not per-consumer style knobs, so non-negotiable 19 applies exactly as it
    applied to foliage.rock_scatter. Had the rock path grown its own flow
    lookup, rock clutter and conifers would have followed drainage lines that
    disagreed -- and neither tool's verification could have caught it,
    because each would be internally consistent.
    
    scripts/placement_priors.py is the one definition: load_flow(),
    centred_bias(), load_trunks(), canopy_occupancy().
    
    THE REFACTOR MOVED NOTHING, AND THAT IS PROVEN NOT ASSUMED
    
    place_foliage's inline flow load and bias formula now come from the
    module. Replaying plan() in memory against the shipped
    foliage/alpine_Conifer.json, with the writer's own rounding applied
    (place_foliage.py:517-519):
    
      BIT-IDENTICAL across all 157,554 instances x 7 columns.
    
    Re-proven after the recipe change too. The 5-tuple from load_inputs
    became a 6-tuple carrying the flow STATUS, and its three callers were
    updated.
    
    THE CANOPY PRIOR ASKS THE TRUNKS, AND THE REASON IS A MEASUREMENT
    
    The map grid is 4.0 m. The measured canopy radius is 3.068 m at scale
    1.0 -- fir_tree_01_c_LOD0, dims 6.306 x 5.966 x 14.521 m, from
    Free/_measured/fir_tree_01.json, which is the mesh actually PLACED as
    Conifer rather than the higher-poly _a or _b variants.
    
    So a canopy is about 1.6 cells across: sigma 0.8 cells. A rasterised
    field at map resolution CANNOT express "under this tree". It can only
    express "in the woods versus in a clearing", which is a different and
    much coarser claim, and writing it as a raster would have quietly
    delivered that instead.
    
    rock_scatter's candidates are continuous jittered positions, so the
    honest implementation asks the actual trunks: a cKDTree query gives the
    nearest trunk and its INDEX, so each candidate is scored against that
    specific tree's own radius (radius_m * its scale; the shipped plan's
    scales run 0.700-1.400). c = exp(-(d/r)^2).
    
    ONE CENTRING RULE, WITH THE REFERENCE MADE EXPLICIT
    
    centred_bias() is the single definition of prior -> multiplier, centred
    so a bias REDISTRIBUTES rather than scales. The reference is an argument
    rather than an implicit mean, because the two callers legitimately
    differ and the difference belongs at the call site:
    
      flow    the WHOLE FIELD's mean -- "the average wetness of the map",
              exactly as place_foliage always did it
      canopy  the candidate mean, an unbiased estimate of the map-wide mean
              because candidates are a uniform jittered grid over the span
    
    WHAT THE FLOW MAP ACTUALLY IS
    
    terrain/alpine_flow.png is NOT raw accumulation. derive_aux_maps.py:213
    writes np.log1p(flow) and min-max normalises it. The module says so and
    the log line now says so, because a caller reading 0.5 as "half the
    water" would be wrong.
    
    FAIL CLOSED, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
    
    A declared bias with no field REFUSES rather than silently doing nothing
    -- that no-op is the defect class place_foliage.py:247-251 records, where
    a frame error made the verifier "sample the map CENTRE for every instance
    and duly report that flow_bias did nothing". load_flow returns one of
    three explicit statuses (LOADED / ABSENT / SHAPE_MISMATCH) instead of the
    old bare None, so a stale aux map and a missing one no longer read alike.
    
    THE FRAME GUARD I GOT WRONG FIRST, AND THE SELFTEST CAUGHT IT
    
    load_trunks converts absolute centimetres to local metres. My first
    version guarded it with an extent check alone. The selftest proved that
    check cannot see the defect it was written for: metres under a cm header
    divide by 100 into a cluster near the map CENTRE, which is comfortably
    inside the span and passes. That is precisely why the original defect
    reported the centre.
    
    Now TWO independent checks -- the plan's DECLARED units (place_foliage
    writes "units": "cm, degrees, uniform scale"; absent or non-cm refuses)
    and the converted extent, which catches the different error of right
    units against the wrong origin. The selftest asserts each against the
    case the other misses, and explicitly demonstrates the extent check
    passing the metres-as-cm plan at 4032 m into an 8064 m span.
    
    placement_priors selftest: 21/21.
    
    PROBED, AND A PROBE FOUND A REAL DEFECT IMMEDIATELY
    
    Eight new prove_gates probes for the two knobs, bounded at |1.0| because
    past that the shared multiplier saturates its own clip and the number
    stops changing the result -- a knob that lies.
    
    The "canopy_bias 'lots' (a string)" probe crashed the validator:
    float("lots") raised out of the new cross-field check. A validator that
    raises has converted "your recipe is invalid" into "the tool crashed",
    which is strictly worse -- the caller gets a traceback instead of the

       2 names my exact proposal as its worked example: "AN IN-PLACE
       MODIFICATION IS NOT A COMMITTABLE DERIVATIVE. Enabling Nanite on a Fab
       static mesh, or changing its LOD or collision, edits an ignored file:

       decision.

       we DO import -- "NANITE COMES FROM THE RECIPE AND IS SET AT IMPORT
       TIME, never toggled on the asset afterwards" -- including the

       earlier and presented as new.
    
    ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS NOT "I FORGOT TO GREP"
    
    I framed 1.5 as a MEASUREMENT problem when it was a CONSTRAINTS problem.
    Having correctly withdrawn the silhouette argument on measured triangle
    counts, I concluded what remained was empirical -- does popping cost
    enough to justify the GPU -- and empirical questions feel like they are
    answered by instruments. So I went looking for one.
    
    The actual obstacle was on disk the whole time and no amount of rendering
    would have surfaced it. A perfectly-executed on/off comparison would have
    produced a real number, recommended enablement, and the change would have
    evaporated on the next fresh clone with no error anywhere.
    
      BEFORE BUILDING AN INSTRUMENT TO ANSWER A QUESTION, ESTABLISH THAT THE
      ANSWER IS ACTIONABLE. An instrument prices an option; it cannot tell
      you the option is unavailable, and it will happily return a confident
      number for a change that cannot be kept.
    
    The near-miss is the point. The measurement I had specified was
    well-designed -- same-settings noise floor, on/off pair, a temporal
    metric because the surviving benefit is temporal. It would have been
    built carefully, run correctly, and been entirely wasted, and it would
    have carried a recommendation into 1.1 on the strength of a number that
    was never the binding consideration. A rigorous measurement of the wrong
    question is more dangerous than no measurement, because rigour is what
    makes it persuasive.
    
    WHAT THE RULING LEAVES BEHIND, AND IT IS REAL
    
    LOD popping across a move is still the one defect class no still frame in
    this project can test. Nanite was never the lever for it on this content.
    lod_depth, the LOD chain and cull_distance_m are, and all three are
    recipe data we own outright. R12 already measured what makes popping
    likely: boulder_medium_01's vendor LOD screen sizes are 1.504 / 0.752 /
    0.319 / 0.238 against the cost model's assumed 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.21 / 0.088 --

+## 2026-08-08 — I PROPOSED REVERSING A LOCKED RULING WITHOUT CITING IT, AND THE OBSTACLE WAS NOT THE ONE I ARGUED ABOUT
+
+**What was attempted.** Ryan ratified the clip sequence and asked for
+item **1.5 — the Nanite decision** — first. My own rewritten §1.5 (see
+the previous entry) had already withdrawn half the argument on measured
+triangle counts and recommended *"MEASURE before enabling: a Nanite
+on/off pair judged on popping across a move."*
+
+**What happened.** Before building that instrument I ran operating loop
+step (a) — the rule the previous entry in this file had just been written
+about. `grep -rn -i "nanite" RECIPES.md scripts/*.py` returned the answer
+in one command, and it was not the answer I was preparing to measure
+toward.
+
+**Three things came back, and the measurement would not have found any
+of them.**
+
+1. **A LOCKED RULING ALREADY EXISTED.** `RECIPES.md` R12 §2c:
+   *"Nanite is FALSE on all 13 — measured from the reflected
+   `nanite_settings`, definitively, not absent. **Pass 3 does not enable
+   it.**"* My §1.5 proposed reversing a locked ruling **without citing
+   that it existed.** Operating loop (d) permits refining a locked
+   recipe; it requires testing the improvement in isolation and logging
+   the old version as superseded. It does not permit not knowing.
+
+2. **THE FAB BOUNDARY, AND IT IS DECISIVE ON ITS OWN.** `RECIPES.md`'s
+   Fab-boundary rule 2 names my exact proposal as its worked example:
+
+   > *"**AN IN-PLACE MODIFICATION IS NOT A COMMITTABLE DERIVATIVE.**
+   > Enabling Nanite on a Fab static mesh, or changing its LOD or
+   > collision, edits an ignored file: the asset re-downloads in its
+   > original state and the change is gone. **Express it as a REPLAYABLE
+   > STEP in the recipe instead.**"*
+
+   Verified rather than believed — `git check-ignore` over every rock
+   mesh in the palette: **17 of 17 gitignored**, caught by
+   `.gitignore:92` on `LandscapeLab/Content/KiteDemo/`, **0 authorable.**
+
+3. **`import_static_mesh.py:8-18` had already reasoned the whole thing
+   through**, for assets we DO import: *"NANITE COMES FROM THE RECIPE AND
+   IS SET AT IMPORT TIME, never toggled on the asset afterwards"*, plus
+   an argument for Nanite-off on alpha-masked foliage that is the same
+   argument I re-derived from a triangle table an hour earlier and
+   presented as a new finding.
+
+**Root cause, and it is NOT "I forgot to grep".** It is that I framed
+1.5 as a **measurement problem** when it was a **constraints problem**.
+Having correctly withdrawn the silhouette argument, I concluded the
+remaining question was empirical — *does popping cost enough to justify
+the GPU?* — and empirical questions feel like they are answered by
+instruments. So I went looking for an instrument. **The actual obstacle
+was on disk the whole time and no amount of rendering would have
+surfaced it:** a perfectly-executed on/off comparison would have produced
+a real number, recommended enablement, and the change would have
+evaporated on the next fresh clone with no error anywhere.
+
+> **BEFORE BUILDING AN INSTRUMENT TO ANSWER A QUESTION, ESTABLISH THAT
+> THE ANSWER IS ACTIONABLE.** An instrument prices an option. It cannot
+> tell you the option is unavailable, and it will happily return a
+> confident number for a change that cannot be kept. Check what CONSTRAINS
+> the decision before measuring what OPTIMISES it — the constraint is
+> usually cheaper to check and it can close the question outright.
+
+**The near-miss is the point.** The measurement I had specified was
+well-designed: a same-settings noise floor, an on/off pair, a temporal
+metric because the surviving benefit is temporal. It would have been
+built carefully, run correctly, and been **entirely wasted** — and worse,
+it would have carried a recommendation into 1.1, where cliff and talus
+meshes are placed, on the strength of a number that was never the
+binding consideration. **A rigorous measurement of the wrong question is
+more dangerous than no measurement, because rigour is what makes it
+persuasive.**

+## 2026-08-08 — THE NANITE ARGUMENT WAS HALF WRONG, AND OUR OWN MEASUREMENT FILE SAID SO
+
+**What was claimed.** `plans/clip_30s_proposal.md` §1.5 recommended
+enabling Nanite on rock meshes for the render path, on the grounds that
+it gives *"full-density rock silhouettes with no LOD popping"*, and
+called it *"close to free quality"* for an offline render.
+
+**What the artefact says.** `Free/_measured/palette_live.json` — the
+2026-08-07 loaded-mesh measurement — records `triangles` for all 38
+palette entries. The whole palette is **already low-poly**:
+
+    ScotsPine_01          60,120   (tallest entry, and it is FOLIAGE)
+    Scree_001             33,855
+    SM_Cliff01            29,154
+    Medium_Boulder_001     4,136   <- the ONLY rock actually placed
+                                      LODs [4136, 1186, 892, 596]
+
+**Nanite cannot add detail an asset never had.** "Full density" on the
+placed boulder is 4,136 triangles. The silhouette benefit — the reason
+Nanite is worth its cost on million-triangle photogrammetry — **does not
+exist on this palette**, and the project has never intaken an asset where
+it would.
+
+**What survives, and it is still worth having.** Nanite removes discrete
+LOD transitions. **LOD popping across a moving camera is the single
+defect class no still frame in this project has ever been able to test**
+— 19 static captures cannot see it by construction. That is a real
+argument and it should be made on its own terms.
+
+**Root cause.** The claim bundled two benefits that come from the same
+feature but depend on completely different properties of the asset:
+*detail* (needs high source density — absent here) and *temporal
+stability* (needs only that LODs exist — present here). Bundling them let
+the strong half carry the weak half through unexamined.
+
+**The general rule.**
+
+> **WHEN A FEATURE IS RECOMMENDED FOR TWO BENEFITS AT ONCE, PRICE EACH
+> ONE AGAINST THE ARTEFACT SEPARATELY.** A compound justification fails
+> silently: the half that is true makes the whole sentence read true, and
+> the half that is false never gets tested. Split it, or the weaker claim
+> is smuggled in.
+
+**Second finding, from the same table.** Any enablement must be **ROCK
+ONLY**. The tall palette entries are foliage using masked materials — a
+materially different and more expensive Nanite path, not a free win. The
+original recommendation did say "rock/cliff meshes", but the triangle
+table is what makes the boundary defensible rather than stylistic.
+
+**Status.** Not enabled. §1.5 rewritten to recommend **measuring a
+Nanite on/off pair across a MOVE** before touching 38 assets — because
+the surviving benefit is temporal, and a still frame cannot photograph
+it. Logged at the specification altitude in BACKLOG; there is no locked
+recipe for Nanite yet, and there will not be one until the measurement
+exists.
+
+### ADDENDUM, same session, same entry — THE SPECIFICATION WAS CORRECT THE WHOLE TIME
+
+Written as an append because `.claude/hooks/guard.py lessons-append-only`
+refused an in-place edit of text added minutes earlier in this same
+commit. **That refusal is correct and is recorded here as a gate working
+rather than as friction:** the hook cannot tell a legitimate supersession
+from a quiet deletion, so it refuses both. This is B-APPEND-GUARD, built
+after the 2026-08-08 truncation took this file from 11,434 lines to 35 —
+and this is the first time it has been exercised against a live edit.
+
+**The sharpest part of the finding, which the entry above missed.**
+`RECIPES.md` R12 documents the talus fix **in full**, and always did:
+
+- **:2684-2696** — `source_smooth_m 16.0` in the parameter table with its
+  valid range `8-32`, followed by three sentences stating it is *"not
+  cosmetic"* and carrying the identical measurement (detail_relief's
+  ±4.7 m at 28 m wavelength; cell-scale ≥50° = **9.152%**; 16 m landform
+  ≈ **5.3%**; *"roughly 40% of the cell-scale cliff area is texture, not
+  landform, and a source test run on cell-scale slope manufactures
+  phantom cliffs"*).
+- **:2919** — a second mention tying it to the tilt mechanism.
+
+`grep -n "landform" RECIPES.md` returns it in one command.
+
+**So the two-altitude rule DID its job — the spec was right.** What
+failed is that I read the **constitution** and never grepped the
+**spec**. CLAUDE.md's operating loop step (a) is the rule that says to,
+in words written for exactly this case:
+
+> *"STEP (a) IS A SEARCH, NOT A RECALL. `RECIPES.md` gets grepped before
+> any procedure is invented."*
+
+**Why step (a) did not fire.** Because I was **writing a plan, not
+executing a step.** The rule reads as being about *doing* — "before
+attempting anything", "no freelancing on solved problems" — and authoring
+a document does not feel like attempting. That reading is wrong, and
+expensively so: **a plan that schedules solved work is freelancing on a
+solved problem at one remove, and it is worse than doing it directly,
+because it commits FUTURE sessions to the wasted work and carries the
+authority of a plan while doing it.**
+
+> **STEP (a) APPLIES TO AUTHORING A PLAN EXACTLY AS IT APPLIES TO RUNNING
+> A SCRIPT.** Before any document asserts that work is OWED, grep
+> `RECIPES.md` and `scripts/` for whether it is already DONE. The
+> motivating case for step (a) was `scripts/open_level.py` sitting
+> unlisted while I hand-rolled a payload and crashed the editor; this is
+> the same rule failing in the documentation direction instead of the
+> execution direction.
+
+**And the ordering nobody had applied to CLAUDE.md itself.** CLAUDE.md
+already rules that `RECIPES.md` outranks docs and source once proven. It
+had not occurred to me that CLAUDE.md's *own standing notes* fall under
+that same ordering. They do.
+
+> **CLAUDE.md GOVERNS METHOD. IT IS NOT A SOURCE OF TRUTH ABOUT STATE.**
+> Its `CURRENT STATE`, its "four things a fresh session must not
+> re-derive", its open-defect lists — these are DERIVED RECORDS like any
+> other and fall under non-negotiable 15. When the constitution and a
+> recipe disagree about what is BUILT, **the recipe wins.** The
+> constitution wins about how to WORK.
+
+This is why the fix in this commit is a strike-in-place with source lines
+rather than a rewrite: the stale paragraph is now evidence of its own
+failure mode, sitting in the section it discredits.

+## 2026-08-08 — THE GPU READING: TWO R13 CLAIMS FALL, AND THE FIRST FRAME IS ALWAYS A LIE
+
+Attended run with Ryan at the overlay. Eight readings across two stations.
+Artefact: `_verify/20260808_gpu_readings.md`. The measurement that was
+asked for — triplanar's cost — is still not taken; everything below is
+what the attempt uncovered on the way.
+
+### THE SCENE IS NOT STABLE AT A FIXED CAMERA, AND THE FIRST READING IS THE WORST
+
+Prims after parking `sweep_0060`: 121.7K → 81.3K → 73.3K → 73.3K. Roughly
+three readings of drain before steady state. The first A/B I took spanned
+that drain and reported **clouds as CHEAPER than no clouds** — physically
+impossible, and the tell was not the milliseconds but the **40,400
+primitives that vanished at a camera that had not moved.**
+
+**A second field of the same overlay caught what the headline number could
+not.** GPU time alone was plausible in both directions; Prims was not.
+This is the conditioned-statistic lesson from the morning's cloud-state
+work arriving in a different instrument on the same day.
+
+**And I designed the experiment without a noise floor** — the exact
+omission LESSONS 2026-08-06 already logged ("two identical-settings runs
+differ by up to 26%... always capture a same-settings repeat"), which I
+had applied rigorously to the image comparison hours earlier. A lesson
+learned in one instrument did not transfer to another. Measured floor,
+once I bothered: **1.06 ms** between two OFF readings at identical Prims.
+
+**Rule that follows: an A/B at a parked camera is invalid until Prims
+stops moving, and a pair whose Prims disagree is not a pair.**
+
+### R13's CLOUDS PREMISE IS FALSE
+
+Measured cost of clouds: **+1.78 ms GPU (4.4%)** at `sweep_0060`, **+6.48
+ms (8.6%)** at `sweep_2000`, both at matched Prims, corroborated by Draws
+separating with no overlap (~6 extra draw calls, every reading, both
+stations).
+
+R13 ADDENDUM rules clouds OFF interactive because *"a per-pixel volumetric
+on a saturated iGPU takes the viewport from slow to unusable."* The frame
+goes 79.12 → 86.14 ms: **12.6 fps versus 11.6 fps.** It was never the
+difference between usable and unusable, because the viewport is unusable
+either way. **The ruling optimised a term worth 8% and left the other 92%
+unexamined** — which is what an unmeasured fear does to a budget.
+
+To R13's credit its ADDENDUM demanded exactly this measurement before any
+re-rule. The measurement now exists.
+
+### THE BIGGER ONE: BOTH STATIONS ARE DRAW-THREAD BOUND
+
+Six settled readings, two stations, unanimous — Frame tracks **Draw**,
+GPU 3.5-4 ms behind:
+
+    sweep_0060  Frame 45.04  Draw 45.00  GPU 40.94
+    sweep_2000  Frame 79.12  Draw 79.08  GPU 75.50
+
+R13 records the opposite and builds advice on it: *"GPU-bound at both
+stations … the cost is PER-PIXEL SHADING — not scene bloat … the lever is
+shader/material cost and resolution, not instance counts or draw
+batching."* At steady state **the lever is precisely what that sentence
+rules out.** A free shader would not shorten these frames.
+
+**HOW BOTH OF US GOT IT WRONG, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT TWICE.** My first
+`sweep_2000` reading showed **Draw 0.02 ms** — not a plausible draw-thread
+time, and I committed it as a baseline without blinking. Settled, it reads
+**79.08**, nearly four thousand times larger. An unsettled first frame
+makes a scene look purely GPU-bound. **An absurd magnitude is a question
+about the instrument** (the `git show` / LFS near-miss, logged this same
+day, in different clothes) — and 0.02 ms for a draw thread issuing 1,976
+draw calls is absurd on its face. I read it, wrote it into an artefact,
+committed it, and only caught it because a later reading disagreed by four
+orders of magnitude.
+
+**SCOPE, STATED BEFORE ANYONE ACTS ON IT.** This is an EDITOR viewport
+measurement and the editor draw thread carries editor-only work. It
+firmly changes the EDITOR conclusion. It does NOT establish that a
+shipping build is draw-bound, and it does not license a foliage-reduction
+campaign — that needs a PIE or packaged reading, a different calibration
+class that does not exist yet. What it retires is the claim that this
+project has MEASURED its cost to be per-pixel shading.
+
+### THE CROSS-SESSION COMPARISON WAS RETIRED THE HARD WAY
+
+I tried to use 94.45 / 75.71 twice: once as raw ms, once via a per-pixel
+normalisation that felt rigorous. The second station killed it —
+`sweep_2000` came out **+2.5%** and `sweep_0060` **−31.0%** per pixel. A
+material cost cannot have two signs. One station alone would have handed
+me a tidy +2.5% with no way to doubt it; **the positive control was simply
+taking the second station, and it was free.**
+
+### WHAT THIS DOES TO THE TRIPLANAR MEASUREMENT STILL OWED
+
+Finding 2 changes what that measurement can show. If the draw thread is
+the critical path, triplanar's two extra rock albedo samples may be
+invisible in FRAME time while costing real GPU milliseconds. **Read GPU
+Time, not Frame** — otherwise a genuine cost gets recorded as "free", and
+this project would have written that down.

+## 2026-08-08 — THE VS/COPILOT TRANSCRIPT: SIX FINDINGS THE ARTEFACTS ALONE DID NOT CARRY
+
+`VS stuido Work.txt`, 4,505 lines, was the primary record of the session I
+had previously audited only from its outputs. Reading it changed four
+conclusions and produced one whole deliverable. Moved to `_trash/` after
+extraction; every finding below is reproduced from the repo, not from the
+transcript, because the transcript is now a derived record like any other.
+
+### 1. THE LESSONS.md TRUNCATION IS ROOT-CAUSED, AND IT IS RULE 3's MECHANISM
+
+Two failures in series, both PowerShell quoting.
+
+**The corruption.** `Add-Content LESSONS.md "... (backtick)r.VolumetricCloud=0 ...
+(backtick)triplanar_no_clouds ..."` — a DOUBLE-QUOTED string. PowerShell expands
+backtick escapes inside double quotes, so backtick-r became a CARRIAGE
+RETURN and backtick-t became a TAB. The one-line entry landed as three
+broken lines reading `.VolumetricCloud=0` and `[TAB]riplanar_no_clouds`.
+The `r` and the `t` were not mangled — they were CONSUMED as escape
+characters.
+
+**The destruction.** Six repair attempts failed (POSIX heredocs into
+PowerShell, `python -c` with a literal escaped-n, a here-string
+`.Contains()` that returned "not found"). The seventh was:
+
+    $lines = Get-Content LESSONS.md; $prefix = $lines[0..33]; $prefix + '...' | Set-Content LESSONS.md
+
+`$lines[0..33]` takes the FIRST 34 LINES. The intent was "everything
+except the malformed tail". 34 + 1 appended = **35 lines**, from 11,434.
+That is the whole of the loss, in one subscript.
+
+**The rule this breaks is one we already had.** Standing rule 3 sends
+COMMIT MESSAGES through a file *because backticks expand and silently
+delete words*. The identical mechanism ate a LESSONS.md append, and rule 3
+did not cover it because rule 3 names commit messages. **The rule was
+scoped to an instance of the hazard rather than to the hazard.** Any
+shell-authored prose destined for a file needs the file path, not just
+`git commit -F`. BACKLOG B-APPEND-GUARD now has a root cause, not just a
+symptom.
+
+**Nothing noticed for the rest of the session.** `Get-Content -Tail 5`
+after the truncation printed the file's own first-34-lines header table,
+which looks like ordinary content. A tail is not an integrity check.
+
+### 2. THE ONE ORPHAN WAS THE DEFECT, AND IT WAS DISMISSED AS "LOW-RISK"
+
+After the triplanar fix, connectivity read **261 of 262 reachable**, one
+orphan: `MaterialExpressionComponentMask@-1950,200`. It was reported as
+*"not the issue we were fixing and is a low-risk residual"*.
+
+`make_landscape_material.py:1282` reads:
+
+    _wz = _n(_unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, -1950, 200)
+
+**The coordinates are an exact match.** That orphan was the
+world-position-Z mask, orphaned because the triplanar block at :1352
+rebound `_wz` at the same function scope to `|N.z|^sharpness`. Nothing
+consumed the real world-Z node any more — so the altitude bands and the
+forest-floor tint were comparing a cosine against centimetres, and the
+node that should have fed them dangled.
+
+**The reachability audit had found the shadowing bug and printed its
+node.** One orphan of 262 read as rounding error; it was a live shading
+defect wearing a small number. **A single orphan in a graph that asserts
+EXACT is not a residual — it is one thing the builder did not intend.**
+The correct reading of "0 expected, 1 found" is never "1 is small".
+
+### 3. A BUILD REPORTED CATASTROPHE ON A GRAPH THAT WAS COMPLETE
+
+`make_landscape_material.py` died with `RuntimeError: Remote party failed
+to send a valid response!` after the remote-exec channel truncated a
+payload mid-string, and printed its destructive-failure banner:
+
+    WARNING: the payload clears the existing graph with
+    delete_all_material_expressions() before rebuilding.
+    If it died mid-build, /Game/Materials/M_AutoLandscape
+    is now EMPTY in memory and dirty ... Do NOT 'Save All'
+
+The connectivity audit run seconds later read **262 expressions, 262
+reachable, CONNECTED**. The build had SUCCEEDED; only the response failed
+to return. The banner is conditioned on "if it died mid-build" and cannot
+tell a mid-build death from a transport failure **after** a clean build —
+so it prints the same alarm for both, tells the operator not to save a
+good graph, and invites a destructive re-run of a rebuild that already
+worked.
+
+This is the `save_level` deserialization class (CURRENT STATE, 2026-08-04:
+*"can exceed the remote-exec deserialization limit and exit non-zero on a
+save that SUCCEEDED"*) arriving at a SECOND tool. **Non-negotiable 4a's
+trigger is met: a trap class across two different tools is promoted to
+shared infrastructure on the spot.** The fix is not a better warning
+string — non-negotiable 25 forbids the prose — it is for the builder to
+ASK THE GRAPH before it reports, exactly as the audit did. A build whose
+outcome is unknown must print UNKNOWN and say how to settle it.
+
+### 4. THE NARRATIVE WAS WRONG ABOUT THE CLOUDS, AND MEASURING STOPPED ME
+
+I was one edit away from recording that the 18-frame `044840Z` set was
+MISLABELLED `triplanar_no_clouds` while rendered with clouds ACTIVE —
+the transcript says so in its own words, twice, and then verifies
+"cloud-free" against those very frames.
+
+The pixels disagree. Sky-band luma std, per camera, against two
+`read_cloud_state` controls (`044118Z` ACTIVE, `051749Z` INERT; the
+controls separate on 12 of 18 cameras, so the statistic discriminates):
+`044840Z` tracks the OFF control to four decimal places on **every**
+camera — `player_eye` ON 0.0634 vs 0.0210 = 0.0210; `cliff_face` 0.0905
+vs 0.0453 = 0.0453.
+
+**Resolution:** the cvars were typed during the `ridge_wide` shader
+stall. `ridge_wide` is the ONLY frame that would have been clouds-on, and
+it is the one that timed out at 900 s and never wrote. The 18 that wrote
+are clean, and the label is correct.
+
+**Two lessons, and the second is the one that matters.** First, the
+whole-frame diff I reached for FIRST could not settle it (mae 0.0156 vs
+0.0080, pointing the wrong way) because terrain is most of the frame and
+dilutes a sky-only change — *the right statistic is the one conditioned on
+where the effect lives*, which is non-negotiable 22 again. Second: **a
+transcript is a DERIVED RECORD.** Non-negotiable 15 says narrative is not
+a source for state claims, and this was a state claim about frames on
+disk, sourced from prose, about to be written into the record as fact.
+The rule fired because the measurement was taken first.
+
+### 5. THE ATTENDED "BEFORE/AFTER RENDER" WAS ALREADY ON DISK
+
+The board said the triplanar LOOK was unmeasured and attended. It was not:
+three complete 19-frame sets spanning both fixes were sitting in
+`captures/alpine/`, and both comparisons are **single-variable**, verified
+by `git log <range> -- scripts/make_landscape_material.py recipes/alpine.json`
+returning exactly one commit each.
+
+Measured against a same-settings noise floor (`044840Z` vs `054655Z`, same
+commit, same cloud state, two runs — mean mae **0.00298**):
+
+| | mean mae | vs noise |
+|---|---|---|
+| **Triplanar** `fb9a1bc2` to `75802995` | 0.02480 | **8.3x** |
+| **`_wz_axis`** `75802995` to `236358db` | 0.01274 | **4.3x** |
+
+Both clear it, and — the part that makes this evidence rather than a
+number — **each spatial pattern matches its own mechanism**:
+
+- Triplanar moves `rock_grounding` 32x and `cliff_face` 8.3x, and moves
+  `diag_topdown` only 1.9x. That weakest camera is the DISCRIMINATING
+  CONTROL: from directly overhead every surface has `|N.z|` near 1 and the
+  triplanar blend collapses to the top-down projection **by construction**.
+  The one view where the feature predicts near-identity is the one view
+  that barely moved.
+- `_wz_axis` moves `verify_ground` 5.0x (84.95% of pixels) and
+  `rock_grounding` 18x, and leaves `cliff_face` at 1.2x and `sweep_0060`
+  BELOW noise. The forest-floor tint reads world-Z, so views spanning
+  altitude move and views at a single elevation do not.
+
+**What it does not establish:** that the cliffs look BETTER — that is a
+judgement and it is Ryan's; and the GPU cost, which still needs a viewport
+reading. Artefact: `_verify/20260808_before_after_material_fixes.txt`.
+
+**The general lesson:** "attended" was doing double duty for two different
+things — the RENDER, which only needed frames, and the GPU READING, which
+needs a human at an overlay. Bundling them parked a measurable result
+behind an unmeasurable one for two days. **Split an attended item into its
+attended and unattended halves before deferring it.**
+
+### 6. THE REPOSITORY WAS PUSHED TO A PUBLIC REMOTE MID-SESSION
+
+`git remote add origin https://github.com/ryan772177/LandscapeLab.git`
+followed by `git push -u origin main`, at commit **`cb41d7f7`** — which is
+the commit immediately AFTER the truncation. `.git/refs/remotes/origin/main`
+confirms it locally. The remote therefore holds `LESSONS.md` **at 35
+lines**, and none of the repair. Not acted on: pushing is outward-facing
+and Ryan's call. Recorded because a project whose most valuable artefact is
+published in its destroyed state should not learn that by accident.

+## 2026-08-08 — THE COLLISION GATE'S DEFAULT SAMPLE SIZE CAN FAIL A GOOD WORLD
+
+**What happened.** Running `check_collision_truth.py` at its documented
+default `--n 100` on the freshly-reopened, correct world:
+
+    seed 20260808   p90 0.182   PASS
+    seed 7          p90 0.317   FAIL: THE LANDSCAPE DOES NOT COLLIDE WHAT IT RENDERS
+    seed 99991      p90 0.258   PASS
+
+One seed in three **failed**, with a banner asserting a defect that does
+not exist. Raising the sample to `--n 500` settled it — p90 **0.182** and
+**0.189** on the same two seeds, and the same measurement seed 7 had just
+called a failure.
+
+**Root cause, and it is statistical rather than a coding error.** p90 from
+n=100 is the ~10th largest of 100 draws, an order statistic with wide
+variance, and the population's true p90 (~0.185 m) sits close enough to
+the 0.30 m threshold that the estimator's spread straddles the bar. The
+gate is not measuring the world wrongly; it is measuring it too coarsely
+to decide the question it asks.
+
+**Why this is the dangerous direction.** The tempting reading of a mixed
+result is *"two of three passed, so it passes"*, which is cherry-picking,
+or *"one failed, so the terrain regressed"*, which would have sent the
+next session re-diagnosing a world that is correct — and the recorded
+history here is that a wrong terrain diagnosis costs days. Neither
+reading is available if the estimator is stable to begin with.
+
+**The general rule.**
+
+> **A GATE'S SAMPLE SIZE IS PART OF ITS THRESHOLD, NOT A PERFORMANCE
+> KNOB.** A threshold is only meaningful against an estimator whose
+> spread is small compared to the margin. Where the measured value sits
+> at ~60% of the bar, an order statistic from 100 samples is not
+> precise enough to adjudicate, and the gate becomes a coin-flip that
+> speaks in absolute sentences. **Derive n from the margin**, or report
+> a confidence interval and refuse to render a verdict when it crosses
+> the threshold — non-negotiable 6's "I could not measure this" applies
+> to precision, not only to access.
+
+This is also non-negotiable 2 from the other side. That rule says a gate
+that has only seen good input has not been tested. **This gate saw good
+input and refused it** — the failure mode a green-only test suite cannot
+find either.
+
+**Fix NOT applied, and named.** The default is still 100. Raising it
+changes the cost of every call and the threshold's derivation is not in
+the repo, so this wants deriving rather than nudging. `BACKLOG.md`. Until
+then: **`--n 500` is the honest setting for a verdict, and a bare `--n
+100` result near the bar is not evidence in either direction.**

+# Lessons — what worked, what didn't
+
+Written 2026-07-31 from the alpine milestone: repo scaffold through verified
+heightmap import, one destructive editor mutation, and a failed capture.
+
+This is not a summary of what was built. It is a record of **which practices
+caught real defects** and **which mistakes recurred**, so the next project can
+skip the tuition. Every item below is traceable to a specific incident in
+`docs/audit-log.md` or `docs/decisions.md`.
+
+The headline: the pipeline shipped roughly a dozen scripts. **Every serious
+defect in them was caught by an independent review before execution, and
+almost every one came from assuming an API's semantics instead of reading the
+engine source.** Those two facts are the whole guide.
+
+---
+
+## 1. What worked — repeat these
+
+### 1.1 A mandatory audit gate with an independent reviewer
+Non-negotiable, and it paid for itself many times over. Real defects it caught
+*before first execution*:
+
+| Defect | Would have caused |
+|---|---|
+| `set_base_material_usage(MATUSAGE_Landscape)` | `AttributeError` on **every** run — the enum was removed in UE 5.8 — one line after the material graph had been wiped |
+| Residency gate compared against a number measured on a *partially loaded* level | The gate would have passed **exactly when loading failed** — an inverted safety check |
+| `set_actor_location` on a World Partition landscape | Parent moved, 64 components left behind, torn state **saved to disk** |
+| Verifier read only the parent actor's location | Would have **PASSed** that torn state |
+| Band masks feathered inward | Diagnostic tool would have painted a fake coverage gap at every layer boundary |
+| `biome_id` interpolated into a filename unvalidated | Recipe could steer a file write outside its sandbox |
+| Scale-mismatch "refusal" that moved and saved *first*, then printed REFUSE | A persisted mutation reported as a no-op |
+| Derived-resolution check fed the expected value into its own verification | Verified nothing, in the tripwire |
+| Un-doubled braces in a `.format()` template | `KeyError` at import — the module could never have run |
+
+**The pattern:** the reviewer must be independent of the author, must have
+source access, and its verdict must gate execution — not merely inform it.
+A review that only advises gets rationalised away under time pressure.
+
+**Corollary that mattered:** when the reviewer gained the ability to *fix* its
+own findings, the author must still verify those fixes. It caught things I
+missed; I caught nothing wrong in its fixes — but checking cost minutes and the
+alternative was a reviewer marking its own homework.
+
+### 1.2 Verify semantics at an engine source line, not just arithmetic
+The single highest-value habit, learned the hard way (see 2.1).
+
+The rule that emerged: **every value handed to an editor UI field or API
+parameter needs its *meaning* confirmed at a source line — not just its
+magnitude derived correctly.** Getting the number right from a wrong premise
+produces confident, wrong output.
+
+### 1.3 Fail-closed gates, layered and independent
+Every gate refused rather than guessed, and each was independent of the others:
+
+- **Identity** — refuse unless exactly one editor matches the expected project.
+- **Residency** — refuse unless loaded counts equal on-disk counts (World
+  Partition only exposes *loaded* actors, so a census taken blind is a lie).
+- **Exactly-one** — refuse unless precisely one target exists.
+- **Positive attribution** — act only on things provably attributed to the
+  target; "unknown" is never treated as "yes".
+- **Hard assertion** — a final check that *raises* rather than filters. A
+  filter silently shrinks a kill list; an assertion stops the run.
+
+**Test each gate can't be satisfied by the failure it guards against.** The
+residency gate originally passed when loading failed — the inverse of its job.
+
+### 1.4 Dry-run mode on anything destructive
+`--dry-run` printed the full kill list with per-item evidence before deleting
+anything. It also surfaced the wrong invariant (68 vs 80) harmlessly. Any
+irreversible operation should be runnable in a mode that proves what it *would*
+do.
+
