+# R16 — Photoreal coherence is ruled by PROVENANCE (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)
+
+**RULED 2026-08-05 (Ryan), after the appearance-statistics instrument
+failed its own acceptance test twice.**
+
+## 1. THE RULING
+
+**A surface belongs to the photoreal lane if its PROVENANCE says so —
+vendor and capture method — not if its pixels resemble ones that do.**
+
+Admissible provenance: a photogrammetry/scan vendor (Quixel Megascans,
+ambientCG, Poliigon scans) with the capture method recorded in the
+`ASSETS.md` row. Inadmissible: procedural or hand-authored packs
+(Substance Designer, stylised marketplaces), whatever their pixels look
+like.
+
+## 2. WHY THE MEASURED INSTRUMENT WAS RETIRED
+
+`surface_coherence.py` was built, calibrated and honestly reported, and
+it **could not do the job**:
+
+- **Unconditioned:** gap 0.0000 on all three features. The photoreal
+  class spans snow to gravel and the stylized class sits inside it —
+  **material identity dominates authoring method.**
+- **Conditioned on family, grass at n=1:** two features appeared to
+  separate.
+- **Conditioned, grass at n=4:** **all three OVERLAP.** The n=1 result
+  was an artefact — a single point cannot overlap a range, so every
+  apparent gap was absence of evidence about spread, read as evidence of
+  separation.
+
+**ADDING SPECIMENS CANNOT MAKE A REAL SEPARATION WORSE — IT CAN ONLY
+REVEAL THERE WAS NONE.**
+
+Rock separates (spec_slope 1.08 SD, norm_hf 1.31 SD) but its only
+stylized specimens ARE its calibration set, so it cannot rule on
+anything either.
+
+## 3. WHAT PROVENANCE BUYS
+
+**Checkable.** A vendor and a capture method are facts with a source,
+verifiable at intake and stable afterwards — where an appearance
+threshold drifts with every specimen added.
+
+**Honest about its own limits.** It says "this came from a scanner",
+which is exactly the claim WORLD_VISION's photoreal bar makes. It does
+NOT claim the surface looks right, and it should not — that is an art
+judgement and was never what the check was for.
+
+**It cannot be gamed by resemblance.** A stylised pack that happens to
+have broadband statistics still fails, correctly.
+
+## 4. WHAT IS KEPT
+
+`surface_coherence.py` and `per_family_calibration.py` are **retained as
+DESCRIPTIVE instruments, not gates.** They still answer "how does this
+surface compare to our set", which is useful for spotting an outlier
+before it ships. They issue no verdicts.
+
+The `norm_hf` finding is kept as an observation with its bound:
+photoreal carries LESS high-frequency normal energy than procedural, as
+a **mean-level tendency in both paired families** (grass 0.6645 vs
+0.7961, rock 0.3095 vs 0.5468) — and **a direction in the means is not a
+separation in the ranges.** Only the latter could have supported a gate.
+
+## 5. REJECTED
+
+- **Ruling coherence by appearance statistics** -> the check cannot
+  separate its own calibration classes, and a discriminator that cannot
+  tell knowns apart cannot tell unknowns apart -> rule by provenance.
+- **Trusting an n=1 "separation"** -> a single point cannot overlap a
+  range, so the gap measures the sample size, not the classes -> require
+  n>=3 per side before reading any separation at all.
+- **Judging a calibration set with itself** -> circular; the stylized
+  rock specimens ARE the rock calibration -> a verdict needs a specimen
+  that played no part in calibration.
+
+## 6. PACK_BONUS — the verdict, now issuable
+
+**EXCLUDED — provenance.** Lord Enot Store, Substance Designer,
+procedurally authored. It is not a scan, and no measurement is needed to
+establish that. Catalogued excluded-with-reason.

+Ground037 is natural gravel; Pack_Bonus `Tile_1` is a man-made tile.
+They are not the same material family, and pairing them measures
+material rather than authoring, which is the exact confound that broke
+the unconditioned calibration.
+
+**A "family" is only a control if the two sides actually match.**
+Conditioning is not a checkbox — naming two things a family does not
+make them one. Pack_Bonus ships grass, stone, tile, wall and wooden
+floor; our natural set is grass, rock, snow, ground. **Only two families
+pair at all**, and that bounds what this instrument can ever rule on
+against this stylized set.
+
+### The holdout still fails the bar, and this is the finding
+
+Wild Grass `norm_hf` = **0.6509**, against photoreal 0.5677 and stylized
+min 0.7521. It lands on the photoreal side of the midpoint by **0.009**.
+
+**That is a classification, not a margin.** With grass at n=1 there is no
+spread to measure the gap against, so "which side" is answerable and
+"with margin" is not — and the ruling requires margin before any verdict
+on anything is trusted.
+
+**So no Pack_Bonus verdict is issued.** Exclusion remains the expected
+outcome and remains unrecorded, because recording it would rest on my
+judgement rather than the instrument — the exact substitution the
+instrument was built to prevent. Three more grass specimens is what
+changes that, not three more features.
+
+### The rule
+
+**A CLASSIFICATION IS NOT A MARGIN.** An instrument that puts a specimen
+on the correct side by 0.009 has told you almost nothing: it cannot
+distinguish a real separation from noise, and the next specimen will
+land wherever it lands. Reporting the side without the spread is how a
+weak instrument gets trusted.

+## 15. SKILL AUTHORING DOCTRINE
+
+**A SKILL THAT STATES A RULE WITHOUT ITS COST GETS ARGUED WITH; ONE THAT
+NAMES THE EIGHT MINUTES DOES NOT.**
+
+This is the two-altitude principle surfacing in a third place. LESSONS
+carries the narrative and RECIPES the specification; a SKILL must carry
+enough of the narrative to make the specification stick, because it is
+read at the moment of action by someone deciding whether the rule
+applies to them.
+
+So every rule in a skill names its cost: the eight minutes lost to an
+`IndexError` after talus routing, the 157,554 instances an orphan sweep
+would delete, the 4608 MB texture encode that hung the editor for twenty
+minutes, the 5x underlit scene. **Future skills are authored to that
+bar.**
+
+## 16. TRIGGERING IS PROVEN BY THE SURFACE, NOT BY FRONTMATTER
+
+The five rituals carry `disable-model-invocation: true`, and the proof
+that it works is that **the model-visible skill listing shows the 7
+knowledge skills and not the 12** — the effective state, read off the
+surface, rather than the configuration read back to itself.
+
+This is non-negotiable 17's spirit: **a config file records what was
+overridden, never what is in effect.** Reading the frontmatter back
+would have proven only that the file says what I wrote in it.
+
+**The third direction for a skill is triggering:** proven to load on the
+right task AND stay unloaded on the wrong one. A skill that fires
+everywhere is context cost wearing a helpful face.
+
+## 17. PER-FIELD TRUST, MEASURED
+
+**AN ANALYST THAT KNOWS WHICH OF ITS INSTRUMENT'S DIALS LIE IS WORTH TEN
+THAT TRUST THE PANEL.**
+
+The Fab asset registry is not trustworthy as a whole or untrustworthy as
+a whole — it is trustworthy **per field**, and the split is measured:
+
+| Field | Verdict | Evidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| `Triangles` | **TRUSTED** | matched live exactly on every mesh spot-checked |
+| `ApproxSize` | **TRUSTED** | used for screen-size constants throughout |
+| `Materials` | **NOT TRUSTED** | 8 of 13 disagree; all 13 report 1 slot live against claims of 2 and 12 |
+| `NaniteEnabled` | **ABSENT IS NOT OFF** | a row without the tag was cached by an engine predating it — "I could not look" |
+
+`registry-analyst` carries this table in its brief, and the generalised
+form is the point: **state per-field trust with the measurement behind
+it**, rather than a global verdict on the source.
+
+## 18. THE FAIL-DIRECTION THEORY IS COMPLETE — four landings
+
+**MAKE THE FAILURE LAND WHERE IT COSTS LEAST.**
+
+| Hook | Failure mode | Direction |
+|---|---|---|
+| `guard.py` deny rules | unguarded action | **CLOSED** — exit 2 on any internal failure |
+| `stop_dirty_tree.py` | trapped operator | **OPEN** — allow what it cannot establish |
+| `session_context.py` | missing context (cannot block) | **DEGRADE** — valid JSON naming the gap |
+| `subagent_output.py` | a misleading report | **DEGRADE** — blocking would discard work already paid for |
+| `advisory.py` | a missing hint | **SILENT** — say nothing rather than emit noise |
+
+Five hooks, four directions, one principle. **Fail-closed was never the
+principle.**
+
+## 19. H11 AND H12 ARE ADVISORY — the decisions, written as decisions
+
+Per the migration doc's standard, **a rule that is not enforced states
+why, or it reads as a gap.**
+
+**H11 (standing rule 6, consecutive failures) is advisory because
+BLOCKING WOULD PREVENT THE SANCTIONED RESPONSE.** The rule says stop and
+diagnose — and diagnosing usually means editing the script and running
+it again. The same command failing twice with a fix in between is
+compliance, not violation. So it counts (by command signature, so
+unrelated failures do not accumulate) and **points at the LESSONS search
+the streak implies**: if this error is already a logged lesson, the

+
+**H12 (standing rule 5, dependencies) is advisory because there is

+prevents. A guard that stays silent about what it could not read is the
+"I could not look" defect at the session boundary. Neither is fixed by
+applying fail-closed harder.
+
+**The mid-merge allowances are the bounded-exception pattern applied
+correctly:** `MERGE_HEAD` / `REBASE_HEAD` / `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` mean the
+tree is *expected* to be dirty, so blocking there would trap someone
+mid-conflict — precisely when stopping is the right move. The exception
+is named, reasoned, and narrow.
+
+## 13. A BLOCKED-AND-REBUILT OPERATION IS A RESUMPTION HAZARD
+
+**When a guard blocks a compound action, the rebuild must re-verify that
+EVERY part of the original intent landed — not just the part that
+tripped the guard.**
+
+Twice on 2026-08-05 a commit message described work that was not in the
+tree. The second had a clean mechanism: the `msys-game-path` hook
+blocked a command that both wrote R15 *and* committed; the commit was
+rebuilt; the R15 insertion bundled into the same command was never
+re-run. The message shipped describing a recipe that did not exist.
+
+Closure is **verified by grep, not asserted** — and now enforced.
+`commit-claims` reads the message file behind `git commit -F` and denies
+when it names an `R<number>` with no matching `# R<number>` heading in
+`RECIPES.md`.
+
+**The discriminator is deliberately narrow.** Recipe IDs are
+unambiguous, cheap to check, and were the thing wrong both times. File
+paths are NOT checked: a commit legitimately names files it deletes,
+renames or merely discusses, and firing on those would be the
+commentary-about-itself false positive that §7 already paid for.
+
+## 14. A TEST CONFOUNDED BY LIVE STATE ASSERTS AN OUTCOME, NOT A CONTRACT
+
+**The suite must pass identically whatever the repo looks like when it
+runs.**
+
+The first H10 direction-3 test asserted *"malformed input ⇒ allow"* and
+failed twice. The hook was right and the test was wrong: those inputs
+fall through to the real check, the working tree genuinely was dirty,
+and blocking was correct. The test could not distinguish *blocked by
+malformed input* from *blocked because the tree really is dirty*.
+
+Rewritten to assert the CONTRACT — exit 0, parseable output, and any
+block carrying the dirty-tree reason.
+
+This is non-negotiable 22's newest instance, and it joins **"a false
+alarm on a gate is expensive"** as the pair of gate-distrust lessons:
+*the test was wrong, not its subject* is the other half of *the gate was
+wrong, not the input*.
+

+## 2026-08-05 - THE WALLS STOPPED THE MASON: HOOKS CAUGHT THEIR OWN AUTHOR
+
+### The acceptance evidence
+
+The enforcement layer was built today, and during its own construction
+it blocked its own author five times:
+
+1. `msys-game-path` blocked the commit INTRODUCING it, because the
+   message described the defect it guards.
+2. Repairing that rule through a shell heredoc mangled the reason string
+   — escapes became literal newlines.
+3. `outside-repo` blocked writing a commit-message file to the sanctioned
+   session scratchpad.
+4. The heredoc trap struck again while writing the TEST CASES for the
+   hook that prevents it.
+5. Backticks in an inline `python -c` expanded as command substitution
+   while recording this very lesson — the *other* half of the defect
+   that promoted standing rule 3.
+
+Three were TRUE POSITIVES on real mistakes (2, 4, 5 — all shell mangling,
+which is now hook-enforced). Two were FALSE POSITIVES that located
+boundaries the rules had assumed rather than stated (1, 3).
+
+### Why this is acceptance evidence, not embarrassment
+
+A governance layer built by the same agent it governs has an obvious
+failure mode: **it encodes what the author already remembers to do, and
+therefore never fires.** A layer like that reads as rigour and delivers
+nothing.
+
+These hooks fired immediately, on their author, during construction.
+That is the strongest available evidence that they constrain ACTUAL
+behaviour rather than describing INTENDED behaviour.
+
+The false positives matter as much as the true ones. Each located a
+boundary that had been assumed:
+
+* a guard must not fire on commentary about itself, or it costs the
+  layer its credibility;
+* a guard whose refusal pushes mess INTO the repo has its bounds wrong.
+
+Neither would have surfaced from testing alone, because both required
+the author to do something legitimate that the author had not
+anticipated — which is exactly what a test written by that same author
+does not contain.
+
+### The rule
+
+**A GOVERNANCE LAYER THAT NEVER INCONVENIENCES ITS AUTHOR HAS NOT BEEN
+TESTED, IT HAS BEEN DESCRIBED.**
+
+Walls that stop the mason are working walls. The measure is not that the
+layer was written correctly, but that it caught something its author was
+about to do wrong — five times, before it was finished.
+
+### The shell-mangling tally, for the record
+
+Five costs in one session, in three different shapes: heredoc escapes
+(three times), backtick command substitution (once), MSYS path rewriting
+(once). All five are now structurally prevented rather than remembered:
+`heredoc-escapes` and `msys-game-path` block the shell paths, and the
+file tools are the sanctioned route for content. **The same mistake
+twice is a process failure; five times in one session is a design
+failure, and the design has now changed.**

+# R15 — The enforcement layer (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)
+
+Constitution rules migrated onto Claude Code's native surfaces. Full
+classification in `GOVERNANCE_MIGRATION.md`. Proof:
+`python .claude/hooks/prove_hooks.py`.
+
+## 1. FIRST PRINCIPLE — the contract makes fail-closed mandatory
+
+    EXIT CODES OTHER THAN 0 AND 2 ARE NON-BLOCKING.
+    A HOOK THAT CRASHES DOES NOT BLOCK.
+
+Verified against `code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks`: exit 0 proceeds, exit
+2 blocks with stderr as the reason, **anything else is a non-blocking
+error and the action proceeds.** So an exception, a missing dependency
+or an unparseable payload lets through the very thing the hook exists to
+stop.
+
+**Therefore every deny hook wraps its logic so ANY internal failure
+exits 2.** `guard.py`'s `main()` catches `BaseException` and denies.
+Non-negotiable 1 applied to the enforcement layer itself.
+
+## 2. THREE-DIRECTIONS TESTING — the standard for this layer
+
+1. **BLOCK the violation**
+2. **PASS the legitimate case**
+3. **BLOCK WHEN BROKEN** — garbage input, malformed state, missing
+   fields must DENY, not crash through
+
+## 3. LOAD-BEARING FOR THE CONSTITUTION — do not weaken in a refactor
+
+Standing rules 7 and 8 are **deliberately NOT hooks**: re-implementing
+them would be two implementations of one fact (NN24). They are enforced
+in code, and those points are now **governance, not local validation**:
+
+| Enforcement point | Enforces |
+|---|---|
+| `verify_landscape._select_verified_node` | **Standing 7** — connected editor matches `UE_PROJECT_ROOT` |
+| each editor script's dry-run / `--place` gate | **Standing 8** — dry-run anything destructive |
+| `place_foliage.adopt_rock_plans` | orphan-sweep protection for 157k instances |
+| `save_level` allow-list | only recipe-owned packages are written |
+
+**A refactor that weakens any of these is touching the governance
+layer.** Listed here so that is visible at the point of change.
+
+## 4. H5 — LESSONS append-only: DUMB HOOK, LOUD EXCEPTION
+
+**Ruled: deny ALL non-appends.** Permitting the documented supersession
+pattern would require the hook to distinguish a correction-with-marker
+from a quiet deletion — semantic judgement it cannot do reliably, and
+getting it wrong silently destroys the guarantee.
+
+A genuine loop-(d) supersession goes through a **deliberate hook-disable
+plus a checkpoint**: loud and auditable instead of routine. NN3 — prefer
+an input that cannot express the catastrophic value over a gate that
+must judge it.
+
+## 5. THE HOOKS
+
+| Rule | Enforces |
+|---|---|
+| `commit-file` | standing 3 — `git commit -F`, never `-m` |
+| `no-force-delete` | standing 2 |
+| `engine-files` | standing 4 — `.uproject`/`.uasset`/`.umap` |
+| `outside-repo` | standing 1, with the scratchpad exception in §8 |
+| `lessons-append-only` | append-only, §4 |
+| `fab-protection` | R-ASSET — no authoring into vendor folders |
+| `load-level` | R14 — `open_level.py` only |
+| `msys-game-path` | MSYS argument rewriting, §7 |
+| `heredoc-escapes` | shell escape mangling, §9 |
+| `session_context.py` | SessionStart — injects CURRENT STATE (cannot block) |
+| `stop_dirty_tree.py` | Stop — session protocol, fails OPEN by design, §10 |
+
+## 6. THE FOUNDING THEOREM OF THIS LAYER
+
+**A RULE THAT ALLOWS-BY-DEFAULT WHEN IT MATCHES NOTHING FAILS OPEN ON
+EVERY INPUT IT NEVER IMAGINED.**
+
+*Proof, first run of the three-directions prover:* eight rules, each
+perfect on well-formed input, **32 of 109 malformed payloads sailed
+through**. A payload with no `tool_input`, a null `command`, or an
+integer where a path belongs matched nothing — and matching nothing was
+written as ALLOW.
+
+**FIX PATTERN: VALIDATE THE PAYLOAD'S SHAPE BEFORE INTERROGATING ITS
+CONTENT.** `require_input(data, need)` denies a malformed payload before
+any rule body executes. Shape first, content second.
+
+**Directions 1 and 2 structurally could not have found this.** Both feed
+well-formed input by construction — one violating, one legitimate. Only
+direction 3 supplies the malformed case, and it found the defect on its
+first outing. That is direction 3's charter, now demonstrated rather
+than argued.
+
+## 7. H8 — THE DISCRIMINATOR, AND THE WRONG FIX THAT PRECEDED IT
+
+**A GUARD THAT FIRES ON COMMENTARY ABOUT ITSELF IS THE FALSE POSITIVE
+THAT GETS GUARDS DISABLED** — worse than the defect it prevents, because
+it costs the layer its credibility rather than merely failing once.
+
+`msys-game-path` blocked the very commit introducing it: the message
+described the defect, so a content path appeared as prose inside a
+heredoc and matched as though it were argv.
+
+**The intermediate WRONG fix is recorded because it is as instructive as
+the right one.** Stripping every quoted string removed the false
+positive and simultaneously let a genuine `--material "/Game/..."`
+through — a fix that traded a false positive for a false negative, which
+in a guard is the worse trade.
+
+**The discriminator that holds:**
+
+- **Heredoc bodies are DOCUMENTS, never argv** → stripped outright.
+- **A quoted string is an ARGUMENT if it *is* a path, and PROSE if it
+  merely *contains* one** → match only when the quoted content starts
+  with the content root.
+
+## 8. H4 — A BOUNDED EXCEPTION, AND HOW EXCEPTIONS STAY BOUNDED
+
+`outside-repo` blocked writing a commit-message file into the harness's
+own session scratchpad.
+
+**Standing rule 1 protects OTHER PROJECTS AND SYSTEM CONFIG** —
+*"autonomy over this project is not authority over somebody else's"*.
+The per-session scratchpad is neither. It is the environment's
+designated location for exactly this, it is disposable, and **refusing
+it pushes temporary files INTO the repo — a guard whose refusal creates
+the mess it guards against has its bounds wrong.**
+
+The exception stays bounded by a **direction-1 test proving a DIFFERENT
+temp directory still blocks**. An exception without a test proving its
+edge is not bounded, it is just a hole.
+
+## 9. HEREDOCS — PROMOTED AFTER FOUR COSTS IN ONE SESSION
+
+**ANY MULTI-LINE CONTENT DESTINED FOR A FILE GOES THROUGH THE FILE
+TOOLS, NEVER THROUGH A SHELL HEREDOC.**
+
+The shell layer rewrites backslash escapes inside heredoc bodies. Four
+instances on 2026-08-05, each wearing a different face:
+
+1. `\n` in a Python string became a real newline → unterminated literal.
+2. A doubled backslash collapsed → a regex matched something else.
+3. The same fault broke **this hook's own reason string** during repair.
+4. And then broke **the test cases for the hook that prevents it**.
+
+Enforced by `heredoc-escapes`, whose discriminator is **backslashes in a
+heredoc body**: an escape-free heredoc survives the shell intact and is
+not blocked, so ordinary `cat <<EOF` usage is untouched.
+
+## 10. THE STOP HOOK FAILS **OPEN**, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE
+
+Every deny hook fails closed. `stop_dirty_tree.py` does the opposite,
+for a stated reason:
+
+**THE FAILURE MODE OF A STOP HOOK IS TRAPPING THE OPERATOR, AND AN
+OPERATOR WHO CANNOT STOP CANNOT FIX ANYTHING** — including the condition
+being complained about. A guard that can lock the door from the inside
+is worse than the mess it prevents.
+
+So it allows anything it cannot establish, and says why: `stop_hook_active`
+already set (loop guard), git unreadable, or `MERGE_HEAD`/`REBASE_HEAD`
+present — a mid-merge tree is *expected* to be dirty, and blocking there
+traps someone mid-conflict, precisely when stopping is the right move.
+
+**SessionStart cannot block at all** (verified in the docs), so its
+failure mode is *missing context*. It emits valid JSON naming the gap
+rather than crashing — non-negotiable 6 at the session boundary.
+
+## 11. A TEST WHOSE EXPECTATION WAS WRONG, NOT ITS SUBJECT
+
+The first H10 direction-3 test asserted *"malformed input ⇒ allow"* and
+failed on two cases. **The hook was right and the test was wrong:** those
+inputs fall through to the real check, the working tree genuinely was
+dirty, and blocking was correct. The test could not distinguish *blocked
+by malformed input* from *blocked because the tree really is dirty* — it
+was confounded by live state, which is non-negotiable 22's shape.
+
+Rewritten to assert the CONTRACT — exit 0, parseable output, and any
+block carrying the dirty-tree reason — rather than an outcome that
+depends on what the repo happens to look like when the suite runs.
+

+## 2026-08-05 - THE COHERENCE INSTRUMENT REFUSES, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE FINDING
+
+### What was built and what it returned
+
+`scripts/surface_coherence.py` — the instrument R-ASSET step 2 has never
+had. Three appearance features, one code path for every class, calibrated
+on the five ambientCG photoscans against six `Pack_Bonus` surfaces, with
+Wild Grass held out.
+
+**It refuses. No feature separates the calibration classes with any
+margin at all** — the gap is 0.0000 on all three:
+
+    feature      photoreal range        stylized range        gap
+    spec_slope   [0.7334, 2.2054]       [1.1422, 1.7948]      0.0000
+    norm_hf      [0.1905, 0.8921]       [0.5385, 0.8574]      0.0000
+    palette      [2.1124, 9.5119]       [5.5790, 7.4109]      0.0000
+
+The stylized range sits **entirely inside** the photoreal range on every
+feature. No threshold exists.
+
+### The diagnosis, tested rather than assumed
+
+The photoreal class spans **snow (palette 2.11) to ground (9.51)**,
+because "photoreal" contains materials as different as uniform white
+snow and busy gravel. Within-class spread against a between-class gap of
+zero:
+
+    spec_slope   within-class range 1.4719   between-class gap 0.0000
+    norm_hf      within-class range 0.7016   between-class gap 0.0000
+    palette      within-class range 7.3995   between-class gap 0.0000
+
+So I ran the controlled version — **grass against grass**, material held
+roughly constant, Wild Grass against the three Pack_Bonus grasses:
+
+    spec_slope   photoreal 1.1224   stylized [1.1422, 1.4857]  SEPARATED
+    norm_hf      photoreal 0.6509   stylized [0.7521, 0.8574]  SEPARATED
+    palette      photoreal 6.5938   stylized [5.9546, 7.4109]  overlaps
+
+**Two of three features separate once material is controlled, and both
+in a consistent direction.** The signal is real; it was being drowned.
+
+### The rule
+
+**MATERIAL IDENTITY DOMINATES AUTHORING METHOD IN APPEARANCE
+STATISTICS.** The classes are defined by PROVENANCE — how the texture
+was made. The features measure APPEARANCE. And appearance is driven far
+more by *what the material is* than by *how it was authored*. Snow and
+gravel differ more from each other than a photoscanned grass differs
+from a procedural one.
+
+This is **non-negotiable 22 in a new costume**: a statistic is only
+meaningful conditioned on where it applies. The forest-floor selector
+read 72% against the whole map and 99% against the layer it actually
+modulates; same array, and only the conditioned number was about the
+decision. Here the coherence statistic is only meaningful **conditioned
+on material class**.
+
+### What I did NOT do
+
+I did not tune the features until the classes separated. The expected
+answer was known in advance — Ryan predicted excluded-with-reason, and I
+agreed — and that is precisely the condition under which tuning a metric
+stops being calibration and becomes fitting to a desired conclusion.
+**A discriminator that cannot tell its calibration classes apart cannot
+tell anything apart, and the honest output is a refusal.**
+
+**NO VERDICT IS ISSUED ON Pack_Bonus.** Its ASSETS.md row stays
+verdict-pending. The expected outcome is still exclusion; it is not
+recorded as one, because it would be recorded on my judgement rather than
+on the instrument, which is the exact problem the instrument was built
+to remove.
+
+### What would make it work
+
+Condition on material. A verdict on a candidate GRASS is calibrated
+against photoreal GRASS, not against snow. That needs a photoreal
+calibration specimen per material family, which today exists for exactly
+one family — and Wild Grass is it, so using it as calibration would
+destroy the only holdout available.
+
+So the instrument is honest but not yet usable, and the shortest path to
+usable is more photoreal specimens per family, not more features.
+
+### Also fixed
+
+The diagnostics JSON was written only on success, so the refusal path —
+the case where the numbers matter most — produced nothing to inspect.
+It is now written before any early return.

+# R14 — Teardown-class editor operations (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)
+
+Level switch, project switch, engine restart: operations that destroy
+the context the calling payload is running inside.
+
+## 1. PURPOSE AND THE RULE
+
+**Teardown-class operations ARE callable from remote-exec Python.** The
+tool is `scripts/open_level.py`, which had already root-caused this
+crash TWICE before tonight.
+
+**THE GENERAL REMEDY: EXPLICITLY RELEASE THE CALLER'S REFERENCES TO THE
+DOOMED CONTEXT — `gc.collect()` — IMMEDIATELY BEFORE AND ATOMICALLY WITH
+THE CALL, after any guard that had to read that context.**
+
+The ordering is load-bearing in both directions. The guard must read the
+world (to refuse discarding unsaved work), so the reference cannot be
+avoided; and the release must sit between the guard and the call, so it
+cannot be hoisted out or left to Python's garbage collector to get
+around to.
+
+## 2. THE MECHANISM, at a source line
+
+    Fatal error: [Engine/Source/Editor/UnrealEd/Private/EditorServer.cpp]
+                 [Line: 1951]
+    World Memory Leaks: 1 leaks objects and packages.
+
+That is `UEditorEngine::VerifyLoadMapWorldCleanup`. On a map transition
+the engine verifies that **nothing** still references the world being
+torn down, and a survivor is a **fatal error, not a warning** — it takes
+the whole editor down.
+
+**A `unreal.World` handed to Python is a wrapper holding a real UObject
+reference, so MERELY HAVING READ THE CURRENT LEVEL in the payload is
+enough to kill the editor when `load_level` runs in the same frame.**
+
+`gc.collect()` is Python-side only and is deliberately the whole fix:
+the leak is a Python wrapper refcount, not an engine-side root.
+
+## 3. ORDERED STEPS
+
+```
+1. python scripts/open_level.py        # do NOT hand-roll a load payload
+```
+
+Launching with the map on the command line —
+`UnrealEditor.exe "<project>.uproject" /Game/Alpine` — remains a fine way
+to START in a level. It is **not** the only way to CHANGE level.
+
+## 4. VERIFICATION
+
+`open_level.py` re-evaluates its guard immediately before the call
+(TOCTOU) and verifies by READ-BACK: `load_level` returning without
+raising says the call happened, not that the level changed.
+
+## 5. REJECTED
+
+    WRONG VALUE/APPROACH  ->  SYMPTOM YOU WILL SEE  ->  CORRECT VALUE  ->  ref
+
+- **A hand-rolled `load_level` payload that reads the world first** ->
+  `ConnectionResetError [WinError 10054]` mid-command, editor process
+  gone, `EditorServer.cpp:1951 World Memory Leaks` in the log ->
+  `scripts/open_level.py`. Calling `get_editor_world()` to inventory
+  actors is exactly the fatal reference. -> LESSONS 2026-08-05.
+- **"Level switching is a LAUNCH-TIME argument only, never a runtime
+  call"** -> WITHDRAWN 2026-08-05, same day it was written and ratified.
+  It is not true, and recording it would have deprecated a working tool
+  that had already solved the problem twice. Superseded per operating
+  loop (d); the original stays logged. The correct statement is the
+  remedy in section 1.
+- **Searching for the crash instead of searching for the tool** -> an
+  accurate root cause, an engine citation, a two-altitude log, an
+  operator ratification, and a wrong rule -> operating loop step (a).
+  See the constitution: **step (a) is a SEARCH, not a recall.**

+## 2026-08-05 - CORRECTION: THE TOOL ALREADY EXISTED, AND I CRASHED THE EDITOR REINVENTING IT
+
+### What I got wrong
+
+One entry ago I recorded, and Ryan ratified, that `load_level` must
+never be called from a remote-exec payload and that level switching is a
+**launch-time argument only**.
+
+**That is wrong, and the evidence was already in `scripts/`.**
+
+`scripts/open_level.py` exists. It has existed. Its docstring opens:
+
+> WHY THIS EXISTS - a crash, reproduced twice, root-caused from the log:
+>     Fatal error: [EditorServer.cpp] [Line: 1951]
+>     World Memory Leaks: 1 leaks objects and packages.
+
+The same fatal, the same line, already root-caused **twice**, with a
+working fix:
+
+    def _release_world_refs():
+        _gc.collect()
+
+and the reasoning beside it: *"A `unreal.World` handed to Python is a
+wrapper holding a real UObject reference, so simply having read the
+current level in this payload was enough to kill the editor when
+load_level ran in the same frame... they have to be released, and
+released before load_level, not left to Python's GC to get around to."*
+
+My ad-hoc payload called `get_editor_world()` to inventory the actors.
+**That is exactly the reference the docstring names.** I reproduced a
+known crash, from a known cause, by writing my own version of a tool
+that already handles it.
+
+### The actual root cause
+
+Not `load_level`. **Operating loop step (a): check for an existing
+procedure before attempting anything. No freelancing on solved
+problems.**
+
+I searched for the crash AFTER it happened and found the engine source
+line. I did not search for a tool BEFORE acting. A `ls scripts/ | grep
+level` would have cost two seconds and returned `open_level.py`.
+
+### The corrected rule
+
+The general class rule Ryan stated still holds and is still worth
+having: **an operation that tears down the context its caller runs
+inside is dangerous from that caller.** What changes is the remedy.
+
+The remedy is NOT "launch-time only". It is **explicitly release the
+caller's references to the doomed context, immediately before the
+operation, atomically with any guard that had to read it.** That is a
+solved problem here with a worked implementation.
+
+Launching with the map on the command line remains a legitimate way to
+START in the right level. It is not the only way to CHANGE level, and
+recording it as the only way would have deprecated a working tool.
+
+### The sharper lesson
+
+**A LESSON WRITTEN FROM A CRASH IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE SEARCH THAT
+PRECEDED IT.** I root-caused accurately, cited engine source, wrote it
+at two altitudes, and got it ratified -- and the conclusion was still
+wrong, because I diagnosed the mechanism without asking whether the
+project had already solved it. **Rigour downstream of an unchecked
+premise produces confident, well-cited, wrong guidance** -- and this one
+would have sent future sessions away from the working tool.
+
+This is the same shape as the pale-flare gate: I disproved a mechanism
+and stopped, instead of asking the next question. Twice in one session,
+the error was stopping at a correct-but-partial answer.
+
+### Note on how it surfaced
+
+It surfaced because Ryan asked for a SWEEP -- "this class generalizes:
+sweep for any other payload-driven operation that tears down what the
+payload runs in". The sweep's first hit was `open_level.py`. **The
+instruction to generalise is what caught the error in the specific
+case**, which is an argument for the sweep habit beyond its stated
+purpose.

    Correct form is the command line: UnrealEditor.exe project.uproject
    /Game/Alpine. No teardown, no leak check, no frame holding the outgoing
    world. Relaunched that way.
    
    Generalised: an operation that destroys the context its own caller runs
    inside cannot be driven from that caller. Level switch, project switch
    and engine restart are LAUNCH-TIME arguments, not runtime calls.
    
    Nothing was lost. Alpine was verified clean before the restart (0 dirty
    packages) and the level that died unsaved was UE 5.8 Open World
    template, created by the editor itself minutes earlier.
    
    The pre-switch guard is worth keeping in the record because it half
    worked. It refused the discard on unrecognised actor classes, which
    correctly told me the level was not empty and identified it as the
    template by composition -- 1 landscape + 64 proxies + 64 HLOD against
    Alpine 256. I widened it on a sound argument about the discard being
    safe, and that argument was simply irrelevant to what killed the editor.
    A guard that clears the risk you thought about does not clear the
    operation, and widening one is exactly the moment to ask what else the

+## 2026-08-05 - `load_level` FROM REMOTE-EXEC PYTHON FATALS THE EDITOR
+
+### What happened
+
+A freshly launched editor opens `/Temp/Untitled_1`, not the recipe's
+level, so the level gate correctly refused every operation. I called
+`LevelEditorSubsystem.load_level("/Game/Alpine")` from a remote-exec
+payload to switch. The connection died mid-command with
+`ConnectionResetError [WinError 10054]`, and the editor process was gone.
+
+### Root cause, at an engine source line
+
+    Fatal error: [File: .../Editor/UnrealEd/Private/EditorServer.cpp]
+                 [Line: 1951]
+    World Memory Leaks: 1 leaks objects and packages.
+
+with `UnrealEditor-PythonScriptPlugin.dll` in the callstack.
+
+`load_level` tears down the outgoing world and then asserts that nothing
+still references it. **The executing Python frame IS a reference.** The
+remote-exec payload is running inside the very world being destroyed, so
+the check cannot pass, and it is a `Fatal error`, not a recoverable one.
+
+This is not a memory-pressure crash. RAM was 7.58 GB free immediately
+afterwards. The engine chose to abort.
+
+### The rule
+
+**NEVER SWITCH LEVELS FROM A REMOTE-EXEC PAYLOAD. Pass the map on the
+COMMAND LINE instead:**
+
+    UnrealEditor.exe "<project>.uproject" /Game/Alpine
+
+The map argument makes the editor open the right world at startup, so
+there is no teardown, no leak check, and no Python frame holding the
+outgoing world.
+
+Generalised: **an operation that destroys the context its own caller is
+running inside cannot be driven from that caller.** The same shape
+applies to anything that tears down the world or the Python
+interpreter -- level switching, project switching, engine restart. Those
+are LAUNCH-TIME arguments, not runtime calls.
+
+### What this cost, and what it did not
+
+Nothing was lost. `/Game/Alpine` had been verified clean before the
+restart -- `save_level` dry-run reported 0 dirty packages owned by the
+recipe -- and the level that died unsaved was UE 5.8's Open World
+template, created by the editor itself minutes earlier.
+
+### A guard that worked, and then did not
+
+Before switching I probed the untitled level and refused to discard it
+because it held `Landscape`, `LandscapeStreamingProxy`,
+`WorldPartitionHLOD`, `WorldDataLayers`, `WorldPartitionMiniMap` -- not
+in my default-template allow-list. **That refusal was correct and
+useful:** it told me the "empty" level was not empty, and the actor
+composition (1 landscape + 64 proxies + 64 HLOD, against Alpine's 256
+proxies) identified it as the Open World template rather than anything
+of ours.
+
+I then widened the allow-list and proceeded, on the sound argument that
+the editor process had been launched by the automation minutes earlier
+and no human had touched it, so an unsaved `/Temp/` level could not hold
+work. **That argument was right about the DISCARD and irrelevant to the
+CRASH.** The guard was answering "is it safe to lose this level", and
+the thing that actually killed the editor was the mechanism of
+switching, which no content check could see.
+
+**A guard that clears the risk you thought about does not clear the
+operation.** Widening a guard to proceed is exactly the moment to ask
+what ELSE the operation does, because having satisfied one objection
+feels like having satisfied them all.

+## 2026-08-05 - "IMPOSSIBLE" WAS AN ARBITRARY THRESHOLD, AND THE POP IS 1.4%
+
+### Correcting the previous entry
+
+One entry ago I wrote that the two-camera LOD framing is **not
+achievable**, removed the cameras, and committed it (77f4d94b). That
+conclusion was wrong.
+
+It rested on `VERDICT: WORKABLE if score > 12`, where `score` was the
+minimum distance from any conifer to the sight line and to the two
+camera positions -- and **12 was a number I typed, derived from
+nothing.** The constitution has a rule for exactly this: a tolerance
+chosen to make a test come out is not a tolerance. I have applied that
+rule carefully to gates all session, and then let an underived number
+inside a one-off script decide that a whole approach was impossible.
+
+The question that matters is not "how far is the nearest tree" but
+"does any canopy CROSS the sight line", which is a projection test:
+
+    perpendicular distance from each tree axis to the camera->subject
+    segment  <  that tree's canopy radius,  for trees between the two
+
+Run properly over the 85,569 lit instances, subjects with a completely
+clear line at BOTH 40 m and 53 m were found immediately -- the search
+stopped at five. **A distance heuristic said impossible; the geometry
+said "here are five".**
+
+### The measurement
+
+Instance 325: isolated, sunlit, verified-clear line, cameras on-map.
+Segmented by HUE rather than luminance -- sky is blue-dominant, the tree
+is warm -- so the segmentation does not depend on the brightness being
+measured, which is the quantity under test.
+
+    LOD0 side, 40 m    RGB 203.6 / 187.1 / 158.9   luma 188.6
+    LOD1 side, 53 m    RGB 205.5 / 190.0 / 162.3   luma 191.3

+beyond ~50 m go uniformly pale" as a LOD artefact.

+Ryan ruled on (R13 2d) -- a consequence of exposing for horizontal

+

+## 2026-08-04 - I DIAGNOSED FROM THE ABSENCE OF A PROCESS INSTEAD OF THE LOG IT WROTE
+
+### What happened
+
+A capture run produced no frames. I ran `tasklist`, saw no `python.exe`,
+saw 1.10 GB free RAM, and reported that the capture **"died on a shader
+recompile at 1.10 GB free RAM"**. I committed that as the root cause in
+`fe61559f` and handed it to the next session.
+
+It was wrong. `capture.py` had run to completion and written a log the
+whole time:
+
+    --- ridge_wide ---
+      waiting for alpine__ridge_wide__...png ...
+        still waiting after 90s
+      FAIL: screenshot did not appear within 900s (engine task_done=False)
+
+    --- diag_oblique ---
+      FAIL: screenshot did not appear within 900s (engine task_done=False)
+
+    Stopping: two in-editor failures - not continuing against the live
+    editor (conduct rule 6).
+
+and it exited **5**, not 0. The tool did everything right: it waited the
+full timeout, distinguished "the engine says the task is not done" from
+"the file is missing", refused to keep hammering a live editor after two
+failures, and returned a distinct non-zero code.
+
+### Root cause of MY error
+
+**No `python.exe` means the script FINISHED. It does not mean the script
+died.** I read process absence as abnormal termination, and process
+absence is the normal end state of every script that ever completes.
+
+The log was on disk, its path was in my own command, and I had tailed it
+six minutes earlier. I stopped reading it at the point it was still
+running and never went back.
+
+### The rule
+
+**A PROCESS TABLE IS NOT AN ERROR REPORT.** When something a tool did is
+in question, read the tool's own output before inferring from the
+environment around it. Environment evidence -- free memory, missing
+processes, file timestamps -- is circumstantial and reads as
+explanatory; the log is testimony.
+
+This is the same failure as the save that succeeded while its receipt
+was lost, three hours earlier: **I confused the absence of a signal with
+a signal about the operation.** There, a deserialization failure looked
+like a failed save. Here, a finished process looked like a killed one.
+Both times the answer was available by asking a direct question instead
+of reading tea leaves.
+
+**And the damage is different in kind from a normal mistake, because I
+COMMITTED it.** A wrong root cause in BACKLOG is an instruction to the
+next session: it would have rebooted the machine chasing memory, when
+the actual condition is a shader cache invalidated by the lighting
+change and an engine that has not finished compiling. Non-negotiable 15
+says derived records verify against ground truth at the moment they are
+written -- and a log I had already opened was the ground truth.
+
+### Corrected
+
+`capture.py` needs no change; it behaved correctly on every axis. The
+BACKLOG entry and CURRENT STATE now record the real mechanism: 900 s
+timeouts with `task_done=False`, a self-imposed stop under conduct rule
+6, exit 5, zero frames.

+### The correction
+
+Earlier tonight I wrote that Pass 4 exit gate 1 -- "root flare renders

+    for, because I had stopped looking.
+
+**Disproving the stated cause is not the same as closing the defect.**
+The brief named a mechanism; I refuted the mechanism and wrote down
+"resolved". A defect report is a claim about a SYMPTOM, and only a
+measurement of the symptom can close it.
+
+### What the symptom actually is
+
+Measured on the corrected frame:
+
+    near trunk (vertical, sunlit)   RGB 205.7 / 186.0 / 155.1   0.0% clipped
+    ground, lit                     RGB 188.3 / 170.6 / 130.1   0.0% clipped
+
+The trunk is pale but NOT blown out. And its hue identifies the texture:
+
+    bark atlas       1.000 / 0.914 / 0.781      G < R, warm brown
+    rendered trunk   1.000 / 0.904 / 0.754      G < R, matches bark
+    twig background  1.000 / 1.085 / 0.600      G > R, yellow-green
+
+**The trunk is rendering bark.** The twig hypothesis is dead twice over.
+
+The cause is geometry against a low sun. At 12 degrees elevation:
+
+    vertical surface facing the sun   58,550 lux    5.19 x white point
+    horizontal ground                 12,445 lux    1.10 x white point
+
+**A sunlit vertical surface receives 4.7x the illuminance of the ground
+it stands on.** R13's exposure is solved so that HORIZONTAL terrain of
+the measured albedo sits at linear 0.32. That choice necessarily renders
+every sunlit vertical -- trunks, cliff faces, boulder flanks -- near the
+top of the range. Pale trunks are the arithmetic working correctly.
+
+### The rule
+
+**AN EXPOSURE SOLVED AGAINST ONE SURFACE ORIENTATION IS WRONG FOR THE
+OTHERS, AND THE ERROR SCALES WITH 1/tan(sun elevation).** At 45 degrees
+the vertical/horizontal ratio is 1.0 and the choice does not matter. At
+12 degrees it is 4.7. The lower and more dramatic the sun, the more the
+exposure target has to state WHICH surface it is targeting -- and R13
+currently states "sunlit terrain", meaning horizontal, without saying
+what that implies for everything standing up out of it.
+
+This is the same shape as the misleading-denominator rule (non-negotiable
+22): the number is arithmetically right and answers a question nobody
+asked. "Sunlit terrain sits at 0.32" is true and says nothing about the
+trunks, which are what a player looks at.
+
+### Not fixed here
+
+Three options, none chosen: expose for an orientation-weighted mix
+rather than horizontal; raise `sun.elevation_deg` so the ratio falls;
+or accept pale verticals as the look of a low alpine sun. That is a
+LOOK decision with a measured cost attached, and it wants Ryan.
+Recorded in BACKLOG with the numbers.

+## 2026-08-04 - THE SUN WAS FIVE TIMES TOO DIM AND THE FIELD MEANS SOMETHING ELSE THAN IT READS
+
+### What happened
+
+I spent most of a session blaming dark frames on everything except the
+light. Camera on the shadowed side (twice). Camera framing a crest
+against sky. 45.7% of conifers in terrain shadow. A tree that looked
+like it floated. Every one of those was REAL, and none was the cause.
+
+Then I ran `atmosphere_solve.py` -- which has been in the repo for days,
+is correct, and had never been pointed at the shipping recipe:
+
+    intensity_lux 18000 (recipe as written)
+      -> ground illuminance normal to sun  12656 / 8288 / 3952 lux
+    clear-sky direct-normal at 12 deg elevation: 49,000-60,000 lux
+
+**The scene was about five times underlit.**
+
+### Root cause
+
+`apply_lighting.py:260` sets `atmosphere_sun_light = True`
+unconditionally. `DirectionalLightComponent.cpp:601-615` then returns
+`GetOuterSpaceIlluminance() * GetAtmosphereTransmittanceTowardSun()`,
+and `:581-584` defines outer-space illuminance as the light's colour
+times its intensity.
+
+So `intensity` is **top-of-atmosphere** illuminance, and the engine
+attenuates it by the atmosphere before it touches a surface. A
+ground-level number in that field is attenuated TWICE. 18000 was somebody
+reasonably writing down "a bright day" -- and the field does not mean
+that.
+
+Corrected to the luminous solar constant, 130,000 lux. Ground
+illuminance becomes 91404 / 59858 / 28543, green at 59,858, inside the
+physical band. Exposure re-solved from EV100, the white point and the
+measured albedo: -1.18 -> -1.786 EV, putting sunlit terrain at linear
+0.3201 against a 0.32 target.
+
+Measured, same cameras and world, only those two values changed:
+
+    forest_floor   luma 109.1 -> 178.4   blown 0.0108
+    player_eye      72.8 -> 133.3        blown 0.0000
+    verify_ground   96.7 -> 175.8        blown 0.0000
+    ridge_wide     107.4 -> 179.0        blown 0.0000
+
+### The rules
+
+**A UNIT IS NOT A DATUM.** `intensity_lux` is honestly named -- the
+number really is in lux -- and it is still the wrong number, because it
+is lux measured somewhere else. The UE resolution protocol already says
+to ask "in what units, in what space, against what datum". Lux was
+right, datum was wrong, and the field name carried no warning. **This is
+the same class as reading `written_utc` as a local date earlier tonight.
+Twice in one session, on values whose names looked self-explanatory.**
+
+**AN INSTRUMENT NOBODY POINTS AT THE ARTEFACT IS THE SAME AS NO
+INSTRUMENT.** This is the session's third instance of that shape: two
+invariant suites that never ran, a third that never ran, and now a
+solver that ran only on hypotheticals. The tool was written to serve
+non-negotiable 11 -- sanity-check magnitudes against physical reality --
+and until today that rule had no evidence behind it in this project
+despite having a working implementation sitting in `scripts/`.
+
+**Corollary, and it is the expensive part: a wrong global makes every
+local investigation plausible.** Each dark-frame theory I formed was
+locally true and cost real time. When many independent things all look
+slightly wrong in the same direction, suspect a shared upstream value
+before investigating them one at a time.
+
+### Fixed the gate too
+
+The validator only checked `_is_num` on this field, which is how
+`intensity_lux: 5.0` once produced a fully black frame INCLUDING THE
+SKY. It is now bounded [100000, 160000] with the source lines in the
+message and an explicit instruction that dimming is
+`exposure.compensation_ev`'s job. Proven to refuse 18000, 5.0 and 1e6.

+
+## 1. PURPOSE
+
+Set sun, sky, fog and exposure from PHYSICAL quantities rather than by
+eye, and give every number an instrument that can refute it. Constitution
+non-negotiable 11 says sanity-check magnitudes against physical reality;
+until this pass nothing in the repo could compute the physical reality,
+so the rule was a slogan.
+
+## 2. EXACT VALUES — `recipes/alpine.json` -> `lighting`
+
+    sun.elevation_deg          12.0     valid 5-60     low raking alpine sun
+    sun.azimuth_deg           285.0     valid 0-360    SEE THE TRAP BELOW
+    sun.intensity_lux      130000.0     valid 100000-160000   TOP-OF-ATMOSPHERE
+    sun.temperature_kelvin   7800.0     valid 1500-15000

+### 2a. `intensity_lux` IS TOP-OF-ATMOSPHERE, NOT GROUND LEVEL
+
+`apply_lighting.py:260` sets `atmosphere_sun_light = True`
+**unconditionally**. Then:
+
+    DirectionalLightComponent.cpp:601-615
+      GetSunIlluminanceAccountingForSkyAtmospherePerPixelTransmittance()
+        if (IsUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight())
+          return GetOuterSpaceIlluminance()
+               * GetAtmosphereTransmittanceTowardSun()
+
+    DirectionalLightComponent.cpp:581-584
+      GetOuterSpaceIlluminance() { return GetColor(); }   // intensity x colour
+
+So the engine attenuates this value by the atmosphere before it reaches
+any surface. **A ground-level number here is attenuated twice.**
+
+The locked value is the luminous solar constant: solar constant
+1361 W/m2 x AM0 luminous efficacy ~93-98 lm/W = **126,000-134,000 lux**.
+130,000 is locked.
+
+Measured consequence at 12 degrees elevation, transmittance toward sun
+`[0.7031, 0.4604, 0.2196]`:

+    18000            12656 / 8288 / 3952                       8,288   WRONG
+    130000           91404 / 59858 / 28543                    59,858   correct
+
+Clear-sky direct-normal illuminance at 12 degrees solar elevation is
+**49,000-60,000 lux**. The shipped 18000 was roughly **five times too
+dim**, and every verification frame in the campaign came back dark.
+
+**To make a scene dimmer, change `exposure.compensation_ev`.** That is
+what it is for. Do not dim the sun by lying to the atmosphere.
+
+### 2b. The exposure compensation is SOLVED
+
+Manual exposure, f/4, 1/60 s, ISO 100 -> EV100 9.9069, white-point
+960.0 cd/m2 (`Scene.cpp:490-607`, `PostProcessEyeAdaptation.cpp:376-389`
+with `ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange=True`).
+
+At 130,000 lux and the MEASURED area-weighted ground albedo **0.2675**,
+sunlit terrain is **1059.67 cd/m2**, and the bias that puts it at linear
+0.32 is **-1.786 EV**. Verified: the solver reports linear 0.3201 at that
+bias.
+
+Snow reads far brighter than 0.32 and that is correct — its albedo is
+~0.8 against the 0.2675 reference, so it lands near the top of the range.
+Sunlit snow is dazzling in reality.
+
+### 2c. THE AZIMUTH TRAP
+
+**`sun.azimuth_deg` is the light ACTOR'S YAW — the direction light
+TRAVELS. It is NOT the sun's bearing.**
+
+    recipe azimuth_deg              285
+    measured actor rotation         pitch -12.0, yaw -75.0, roll 0.0
+    measured forward vector         (0.2532, -0.9448, -0.2079)
+    SUN IS AT BEARING               105
+
+Reading the field as the sun's position puts a verification camera on the
+SHADOWED side. That cost three unusable captures before it was measured.
+`sun_exposure.py` carries the measured vector as its default and derives
+the bearing from it.
+
+## 3. ORDERED STEPS
+
+1. `python scripts/atmosphere_solve.py` — offline. Prints ground
+   illuminance, the exposure bias, aerial perspective and fog opacity at
+   distance, and the cloud ray-march ceiling. **No editor.**
+2. Set `lighting.sun.intensity_lux` and `lighting.exposure.
+   compensation_ev` from step 1.
+3. `python scripts/import_heightmap.py --validate`.
+4. `python scripts/apply_lighting.py`.
+5. `python scripts/capture.py` — pipeline rule 4; this is a scene change.
+6. `python scripts/save_level.py --save`.
+
+## 4. VERIFICATION
+
+### 4a. Objective pass tests
+
+    ground illuminance normal to sun, green   59,858 lux    band 49,000-60,000
+    sunlit terrain luminance                 1059.67 cd/m2
+    linear value at the locked bias            0.3201       target 0.32 +/- 0.02
+    transmittance toward sun            [0.7031, 0.4604, 0.2196]
+
+Measured frame means before -> after the correction, same cameras, same
+world, only `intensity_lux` and `compensation_ev` changed:
+
+    camera           luma before -> after     blown (>250)
+    forest_floor        109.1 -> 178.4          0.0108
+    player_eye           72.8 -> 133.3          0.0000
+    verify_ground        96.7 -> 175.8          0.0000
+    ridge_wide          107.4 -> 179.0          0.0000
+    trunk_base           98.3 -> 159.1          0.0000
+
+**The blown-white fraction is the acceptance criterion, not the mean.** A
+brighter frame is only correct if it is not clipping; 1.1% on one camera
+that looks into the sun over snow is acceptable, and anything above ~5%
+means the bias is wrong rather than the sun.
+
+### 4b. Independent instrument (non-negotiable 8)
+
+`atmosphere_solve.py` shares no code with `apply_lighting.py`. It is a
+line-by-line port of `FAtmosphereSetup::GetTransmittanceAtGroundLevel`
+(`SkyAtmosphereCommonData.cpp:182-267`) including its 15-sample loop and
+`BottomRadius + 0.5 km` origin. The engine renders; the solver predicts;
+they are compared at the frame.
+
+### 4c. The gate, proven in BOTH directions
+
+`prove_gates.py` proves `lighting.sun.intensity_lux` REFUSES:
+
+    18000     a GROUND reading in a TOP-OF-ATMOSPHERE field
+    5.0       the historical value that produced a fully black frame
+    1000000   an order of magnitude above the solar constant
+
+## 5. REJECTED
+
+    WRONG VALUE/APPROACH  ->  SYMPTOM YOU WILL SEE  ->  CORRECT VALUE  ->  ref
+
+- **`intensity_lux: 18000`** (a ground-level illuminance) -> every frame
+  renders dark; verification captures are unusable and the darkness is
+  blamed on camera placement, terrain shadow and sun bearing in turn ->
+  **130000**, top-of-atmosphere, because `atmosphere_sun_light` is always
+  True. -> LESSONS 2026-08-04.
+- **`intensity_lux: 5.0`** -> a fully black frame INCLUDING THE SKY ->
+  same. Now refused by the validator rather than surviving to a render.
+- **Dimming the scene by lowering `intensity_lux`** -> the atmosphere is
+  fed a false top-of-atmosphere value, so transmittance, aerial
+  perspective and sky colour are all computed from a sun that does not
+  exist -> lower `exposure.compensation_ev` instead.
+- **Reading `azimuth_deg` as the sun's bearing** -> a verification camera
+  placed on the SHADOWED side; three unusable captures -> it is the light
+  actor's YAW, the direction light TRAVELS. Sun bearing = azimuth - 180.
+  Measure the forward vector; do not trust the field name.
+- **Judging "is it bright enough" from the frame mean** -> a clipped
+  frame has a high mean and no detail -> the blown-white fraction is the
+  criterion.
+- **Tuning `compensation_ev` by eye** -> a value that looks right on one
+  camera and wrong on the next -> solve it from EV100, the white point
+  and the measured albedo.
+
+## WHAT IS NOT HERE — stated, not implied
+
+- **No volumetric clouds.** The solver reports a ray-march CEILING of
+  195M samples/frame at `r.ScreenPercentage 70`, and explicitly says it
+  **could not measure** frame cost offline — that needs `stat gpu` in the
+  editor. On a machine that has already lost its GPU to a driver timeout,
+  clouds are not enabled on an unmeasured budget.
+- **Aerial perspective and fog are computed but NOT tuned.** Section 3
+  and 4 of the solver print the numbers; no acceptance test has been run
+  against a render at 2 km.
+- **UNPROVEN.** Never replayed cold.

+## 2026-08-04 - THE PALE ROOT FLARE WAS ALREADY FIXED, AND THE BACKLOG ENTRY OUTLIVED ITS DEFECT
+
+### The claim under test
+
+BACKLOG, Pass 4 exit gate 1:
+
+> ROOT FLARE MATERIAL: flare geometry renders pale flat tan. It is the
+> BACKGROUND-OF-ATLAS colour, not bark. This is the SAME
+> MATERIAL-ROLE-BINDING DEFECT CLASS as the twig/bark incident --
+> **different slot, same mechanism**. Expect the root cause to be a role
+> binding, not a texture.
+
+### What the measurements say
+
+**1. The vendor ships TWO texture sets, not four.** On disk:
+`fir_tree_01_bark_{diff,nor_gl,rough,disp}` and
+`fir_tree_01_twig_{diff,nor_gl,rough,alpha}`. There is no `trunk_c`
+texture and no `dead_branches` texture.
+
+**2. The mesh has four slots and they resolve to those two sets.**
+Measured live:
+
+    [0] fir_tree_01_bark           -> M_fir_bark
+    [1] fir_tree_01_twig           -> M_fir_twig
+    [2] fir_tree_01_dead_branches  -> M_fir_bark
+    [3] fir_tree_01_trunk_c        -> M_fir_bark
+
+**So there is no "different slot" to have a different binding defect.**
+The flare is slot 3, it shares ONE material with the trunk, and that
+material is either right for both or wrong for both. The brief's premise
+- that a separate slot is separately mis-bound - has no referent.
+
+**3. That shared material audits clean.**
+`audit_material_samplers` reads the built graph and asks the ENGINE what
+each texture needs: `T_fir_tree_01_bark_diff_4k` COLOR,
+`..._nor_gl_4k` NORMAL, `..._rough_4k` MASKS. **3 samplers, 0
+mismatches.**
+
+**4. The bark atlas has no pale region to sample.** Measured over all
+4096x4096: quadrant luma 63.8-67.0, p99 99.2, **max 146.6, and 0.000 of
+texels above luma 150**. There is no "background of atlas" in it.
+
+**5. The TWIG atlas is exactly the reported colour.** 74.4% of its
+texels are background (alpha < 8), and that background is
+**RGB 89.5 / 97.1 / 53.7, luma 92.4** - a flat pale yellow-tan, against
+bark at luma 65.
+
+### Conclusion
+
+Geometry sampling the twig atlas with unrelated UVs renders a **flat
+pale tan over three quarters of its area**. That is the reported
+symptom, precisely. And that is the defect fixed on 2026-08-03: R3
+REJECTED records `texture_map` silently last-winning on a contested
+role, so `M_fir_bark` sampled TWIG textures - which the flare uses.
+
+**The visual review that produced this entry predates the fix. The gate
+was closed by the bark fix and the entry outlived it.**
+
+### The rule
+
+**A BACKLOG ENTRY IS A DERIVED RECORD AND DECAYS LIKE ONE.** Non-
+negotiable 15 already says a state claim must be checked against the
+artefact at the moment it is written. This extends it: an entry written
+against a state that has since been repaired keeps asserting a defect
+that no longer exists, and the next session spends its budget hunting it.
+
+The tell was available without any of the above work, and I missed it
+for four captures: **the brief asserted a mechanism ("a different slot,
+same mechanism") that could be checked in one query.** There is no
+different slot. Checking the PREMISE of a defect report costs one
+measurement; reproducing the SYMPTOM cost four renders, three of which
+were unusable for unrelated reasons.
+
+**Check whether a reported defect still exists before investigating why
+it exists.** Especially when the report and the fix share a date.

+## 2026-08-04 - THE LOD SWITCH DISTANCE MATCHES THE REPORT, AND I COULD NOT MEASURE THE POP
+
+### What is solid
+
+Pass 4 exit gate 3: "trunks beyond ~50 m go uniformly pale."
+

+    0      505,494   1.0000   0->M_fir_bark, 1->M_fir_twig, 2->M_fir_bark, 3->M_fir_bark
+    1      126,374   0.5000   (identical)
+    2       22,293   0.2100   (identical)
+    3        3,892   0.0880   (identical)
+
+All four LODs carry all four sections and both materials. This rules out
+the failure mode R3 REJECTED records for a 5th LOD, where the simplifier
+ate the twig canopy and distant trees became bare sticks.
+
+**The switch distance matches the report exactly.** From the mesh bounds
+measured at placement (6.3059 x 5.9662 x 14.5206 m), mean scale 1.05 and
+FOV 75:
+
+    C = 2r*scale / tan(FOV/2) = 23.15 m,  switch at screen 0.5 -> 46.3 m
+
+    LOD0 -> LOD1   46.3 m    505,494 -> 126,374 triangles  (-75.0%)
+    LOD1 -> LOD2  110.2 m
+    LOD2 -> LOD3  263.1 m
+
+**46.3 m against a report of "beyond ~50 m", and a 75% decimation in one
+step.** That is the transition to investigate, and the cause candidate
+is geometric: an alpha-tested canopy losing three quarters of its cards
+changes coverage, and coverage change reads as a colour change.
+
+### What I could NOT measure, and why I am not reporting a number
+
+I tried to quantify the pop with two cameras straddling 46.3 m. Twice.
+
+**First attempt** picked the subject with `sun_exposure --pick`, which
+prefers an instance with many lit NEIGHBOURS so the frame looks natural.
+In a stand with 46 neighbours within 40 m, the 40 m camera was looking
+straight into an intervening trunk: the frame was 90% black. The
+comparison produced "+1786%", which is not a LOD finding, it is a black
+frame divided by a normal one.
+
+**Second attempt** selected an ISOLATED lit instance with a clear
+6 m corridor along the sight line. Both frames then came back as
+SILHOUETTES against bright sky - tree luma 0.9 at 40 m and 6.5 at 53 m -
+and my "tree pixel" rule is a luminance percentile that also selects
+shadowed terrain. The ratio it produced is a statistic about my
+threshold, not about the tree.
+
+**So the pop magnitude is UNMEASURED.** Non-negotiable 6: a failed
+measurement reports that it failed, never the number the broken
+measurement produced.
+
+### The rules
+
+**TWO VERIFICATION TESTS OF THE SAME ASSET CAN WANT OPPOSITE SUBJECTS,
+AND A "PICK ME A GOOD ONE" HELPER WILL SILENTLY SERVE THE WRONG ONE.**
+The flare test wants a tree WITH neighbours, so the frame is a forest
+floor and not a specimen on a plinth. The LOD test wants an ISOLATED
+tree with a clear corridor, because a neighbour between camera and
+subject destroys the measurement. One `--pick` served both and was right
+once. A selector needs to know which question it is being asked.
+
+**A SEGMENTATION RULE IS AN INSTRUMENT AND NEEDS ITS OWN VALIDATION.**
+"Dark pixels are the tree" is an assumption, and against a bright sky
+with shadowed ground in frame it is false. Every number I derived from
+it tonight was a number about the threshold. The fix is a segmentation
+that can be checked - a frame WITHOUT the tree, differenced against one
+with it - not a better percentile.
+
+### What would settle it
+
+Render the same isolated tree at 40 m and 53 m with the sun BEHIND the
+camera (bearing 285 from the tree, not 105 - the camera must be between
+sun and subject), and difference each frame against a matching frame
+with the instance removed. The difference isolates the tree exactly, and
+the acceptance test the backlog asks for - a continuous zoom with no
+visible pop - then has a defensible per-frame statistic behind it.

    tree. Full population deliberately: a floater is rare by construction, so
    sampling 200 of 157,554 would return a clean bill of health for a map
    with hundreds of them.
    
    The script states what it is NOT, prominently: it shares the heightmap
    and world transform with the planner, so a shared-transform error is
    invisible to both, and it says so in its success message rather than
    only in a docstring.

    First version assumed expected offset = 0 and reported 582 of 759
    boulders "outside tolerance" on a correct placement -- it ignored that a
    rock's pivot lift and embed depth BOTH scale with per-instance scale.
    Second version still failed all 157,554 conifers, because a deliberate
    0.12 m sink is indistinguishable from a 0.12 m error to a check that
    assumes zero.
    
    Both fixed by making the PLAN declare its intent -- `sink_depth_m` and
    `embed_depth_per_scale_m` -- rather than having the verifier infer it
    from the recipe, which would reintroduce exactly the drift the declared
    pivot offset was added to catch. A check that manufactures failures is
    worse than no check, because someone acts on it.

+## 2026-08-04 - THE SAVE SUCCEEDED AND THE REPORT OF IT DID NOT ARRIVE
+
+### What happened
+
+`save_level.py --save` exited 2 with:
+
+    Failed to deserialize JSON "{"version":1,"magic":"ue_py",
+    "type":"command_result", ... "data":{"success":true,"command":"...
+
+The response carries the ENTIRE dispatched command back as a `command`
+field, plus the result payload. With 1,330 package paths in the result
+and the whole script echoed alongside it, the message exceeded what the
+remote-execution transport would deserialize, and the client discarded
+it.
+
+Note what is visible in the fragment that did arrive: `"success":true`.
+
+### Root cause
+
+Not in the save. The save ran. A fresh `save_level` dry-run immediately
+afterwards reported:
+
+    OWNED by the recipe (0):
+    Nothing to save: no dirty package matched the recipe's allow-list.
+
+1,330 dirty packages before, zero after. The editor did the work and the
+report of it was too big to come home.
+
+### The rule
+
+**A transport failure and an operation failure are different events, and
+a non-zero exit conflates them.** The script was right to exit non-zero -
+it genuinely could not read the result, and non-negotiable 6 says report
+"I could not measure this", never a number. But the operator reading that
+exit code will conclude the SAVE failed, and the correct next move for a
+failed save (re-run it) is different from the correct next move for a
+lost receipt (verify independently, then carry on).
+
+**The size of a success report should not scale with the size of the
+success.** A result that enumerates every one of 1,330 packages is a
+result that gets less reliable the more work it did - the failure mode
+appears exactly when the operation was most substantial, and never in
+testing, where the set is small.
+
+### What settles it, and what should
+
+Settled here by asking a DIFFERENT question - "are any packages still
+dirty?" - rather than by re-reading the answer that was lost. That is
+non-negotiable 8 doing real work: the instrument that made the claim was
+unavailable, so a second instrument decided it.
+
+Backlog: `save_level` should return a SUMMARY (counts, plus the first N
+paths and a truncation notice) and expose the full list on request, so a
+1,330-package save reports in a message that fits. And the payload does
+not need its own command echoed back to it.

+## 2026-08-04 - THE GATE THAT COULD NOT BE SATISFIED BY THE THING IT WAS GUARDING
+
+### What happened
+
+Step 5 of R12 - the one irreversible step, run behind a named restore
+tag - refused:
+
+    FAIL at stage done: ruling (c):
+    .../Medium_Boulder_001 has its base -0.6183 m from its pivot
+    (limit 0.25 m). Every instance would sit that far into or above the
+    ground. Re-import from a normalised source.
+
+The conifers placed. 157,554 of them, verified afterwards by
+`recover_state.py` reading the live world. Only the rock was refused, and
+nothing was left half-done - the payload breaks BEFORE `add_instances`.
+
+### Root cause
+
+`place_foliage.py`'s ruling-(c) gate enforces `|base_offset_z_m| <= 0.25`
+against every mesh it places. That limit exists because every mesh this
+project had ever instanced went through `blender/normalize_asset.py` to a
+base-centre pivot, and a large offset therefore meant a broken import. It
+is the check that caught the fir sitting 12.406 m from its own geometry.
+
+The KiteDemo rocks are box-centred by the vendor. `Medium_Boulder_001`
+measures -0.6183 m and **always will**. R-ASSET forbids authoring into a
+Fab folder, so it can never be normalised.
+
+`rock_scatter.py` already knew this. Its `measured_pivot()` docstring says
+so in as many words, and the plan's Z values are ALREADY corrected by the
+measured offset. The correction was applied, was right, and was invisible
+- because the plan file never said it had happened.
+
+### The rule
+
+**A gate states a PREMISE, and a new input class can be correct while
+being unable to satisfy it.** The premise here was "every mesh is
+Blender-normalised". That was true of every mesh in the project on the
+day it was written, which is exactly why it was expressed as a limit on
+the measurement rather than as a question about the pipeline.
+
+The wrong repairs, both tempting:
+
+  * **Raise the limit.** It would admit the genuinely broken import the
+    gate was built to catch. Constitution: a tolerance widened to make a
+    run pass is not a tolerance.
+  * **Exempt rocks.** That removes the check for the one asset class
+    whose pivots this project does NOT control, which is precisely
+    backwards.
+
+The repair is to make the plan **declare** its correction and have the
+gate verify the declaration against the live asset:
+
+    if the plan declares pivot_base_offset_m:
+        require |declared - measured| <= 0.01 m
+    else:
+        require |measured| <= 0.25 m      (unchanged)
+
+This is **strictly stronger than what it replaces**. The old gate could
+not see a plan computed against a stale measurement - a rock re-exported
+by the vendor with a different origin would have passed, and every
+instance would have floated. The new one refuses that. And it cannot be
+satisfied by omission: a plan that declares nothing gets the strict limit.
+
+**When a correct input cannot satisfy a gate, the fix is usually to make
+the input CARRY ITS PROOF, not to loosen the gate or exempt the input.**
+A declaration that must match a measurement is a check. An exemption is
+an absence of one.
+
+### Note on the shape of the failure
+
+This is the second time tonight that a thing was right and unverifiable
+rather than wrong. The invariant suites were correct and never ran; the
+pivot correction was correct and never declared. Both presented as
+success until something forced the question. **Correct-but-unproven and
+wrong look identical from outside, and only one of them is safe to build
+on.**

+## 2026-08-03 — "DEPTH" MEANT COUNT IN ONE FILE AND INDEX IN ANOTHER, AND THE COST MODEL WAS SOLVED FOR A DIFFERENT MESH
+
+Two defects in the Pass 3 triangle budget, found by the same run. The
+first killed it; the second would have shipped.
+
+### 1. `lod_depth`: a count and an index wearing one name
+
+Eight minutes into a talus routing pass, the plan died:
+
+    --- triangle budget (project convention: full 360-degree disc) ---
+      species           LOD0  mats   C (m)    cull m ...
+    ERROR: IndexError: tuple index out of range
+
+`lod_chain(lod0_tris, depth)` read `range(depth + 1)` — treating `depth`
+as the deepest LOD **index**. Its only caller defaulted to
+`sp.get("lod_depth", 3)`, i.e. "LOD0..LOD3", also an index. But
+`measure_rock_meshes.py` writes `lod_count`, and the validator I had
+written hours earlier documented the field as *"the MEASURED LOD count of
+the mesh, not a wish"*. The measured count for every KiteDemo rock is
+**4**. `LOD_PERCENT` is a 4-tuple. `LOD_PERCENT[4]` raised.
+
+Root cause: `scripts/rock_scatter.py:454`, `range(depth + 1)`, against
+`scripts/rock_scatter.py:78`, `LOD_PERCENT` of length 4.
+
+**The two spellings differ by exactly the off-by-one, so the code was
+correct for as long as nobody supplied the measured number.** The default
+`3` and the measurement `4` describe the same chain. Nothing could
+surface the disagreement until a real measurement arrived — which is to
+say, the first time it mattered.
+
+This is the project's own casualty list repeating: *`ReductionSettings[0]`
+IS LOD 0*. That lesson is in `CLAUDE.md`, and the tool that reproduced it
+was written after it. **A lesson stated as a fact about one API does not
+generalise itself to the next place the same ambiguity appears.** What
+would have caught it is the rule, not the instance: *when a number can be
+read as a count or an index, the name must say which, and the bound must
+come from the table it indexes.*
+
+Fixes: `lod_chain` takes a COUNT, refuses `< 1`, and refuses
+`> MAX_LOD_DEPTH = len(LOD_PERCENT)` with an explanation of why a longer
+chain cannot merely be truncated. The validator imports that bound rather
+than repeating `8` (NN24), and now also asserts the recipe's declared
+`lod_depth` **equals the measured `lod_count`** — so the recipe documents
+the chain while the artefact decides it.
+
+### 2. The cost model was solved for conifers and applied to vendor rocks
+
+With the crash fixed, the budget ran — and was wrong.
+
+`LOD_PERCENT = (1.0, 0.25, 0.0441, 0.0077)` is `percent = screen_size²`,
+which is how R5 **generated** the conifer chain. These rocks are Fab
+assets with **vendor-authored** chains. Asking the editor for the real
+numbers (`StaticMesh.get_num_triangles(lod_index)` and
+`StaticMeshEditorSubsystem.get_lod_screen_sizes(mesh)`, both confirmed by
+enumerating the reflected surface rather than recalled):
+
+    boulder_medium_01   modelled  4136 / 1034 /  182 /  32
+                        MEASURED  4136 / 1186 /  892 / 596
+    screen sizes        modelled  1.0  / 0.5   / 0.21 / 0.088
+                        MEASURED  1.504/ 0.752 / 0.319/ 0.238
+
+Vendor chains do not decimate that hard, and they switch to the deepest
+LOD much **nearer** the camera. Cost per instance, measured against
+modelled, at 1/ha and a 140 m cull, over all thirteen rocks:
+
+    boulder_small        20.3x     model UNDERSTATES
+    boulder_medium_02    14.1x
+    boulder_medium_01     9.5x
+    mountain_rock         1.4x
+    mountain_rock_closed  1.0x     model happens to agree
+    scree_slab_001        0.7x
+    cliff_face_01         0.4x     model OVERSTATES
+
+### The rule
+
+**A calibrated model is calibrated against a SPECIMEN, and its validity
+does not travel to a different specimen.** The comment above
+`LOD_PERCENT` says it was "reverse-engineered from R5's locked budget
+table and reproduced to within 0.10% on all four of its rows" — which is
+true, and was the reason to trust it, and is exactly why it was applied
+to meshes it had never seen. **The tighter the fit to the calibration
+set, the more confident the wrong extrapolation.**
+
+Note that the error runs **both ways**, per mesh. That matters, because
+the tempting repair — a correction factor — would have been wrong for ten
+of the thirteen. The chain is a property of the asset, so it is now read
+from the asset. `LOD_PERCENT` survives only to compute a comparison the
+run PRINTS when the two disagree by more than 25%.
+
+### Also confirmed
+
+All 13 rocks report **1 material slot** live, against registry claims of
+2 (`Medium_Boulder_001`) and 12 (`Scree_001_A`). The Fab registry's
+`Materials` tag is stale on the whole set, not on the 8 spot-checked
+earlier. `live_lods_and_materials()` now sources slots from the live
+measurement and refuses a null rather than defaulting.
+
+### And one process note
+
+The failure printed a single line — `ERROR: IndexError: tuple index out
+of range` — naming neither file nor line, from a run that costs eight
+minutes of MFD routing to reproduce. The handler now prints the full
+traceback. **An exception summary is a reasonable default only for
+operations you can cheaply repeat** (non-negotiable 14).

+# R12 — Rock, cliff and talus scatter (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)
+
+Places rock meshes as instanced foliage against the **same deposition
+field** the Pass 2 landscape material uses for its scree sub-surface.
+Four roles are specified; the alpine recipe currently ships **one**
+species, `Boulder` (role `hero`). The rest are specified and unplaced —
+see WHAT IS NOT HERE.
+
+Informed by LESSONS: "THE TALUS MODEL IS RIGHT AND THE TERRAIN HAS NO
+CLIFFS", "MASS WAS CONSERVED AND THE FIELD WAS STILL WRONG", "EVERY
+METRIC PICKED THE MOSS", and "DEPTH MEANT COUNT IN ONE FILE AND INDEX IN
+ANOTHER".
+
+## 1. PURPOSE
+
+A rock is not placed by a material layer's weight. Cliff rocks live on a
+slope band, talus lives on a **computed deposition field**, and hero
+boulders live on meadow. So a rock species declares a `mask`, not a
+`layer` + `weight_share`, and it does **not** draw from
+`foliage.density_per_hectare` — that number is the tree budget, and
+coupling the two would move every rock whenever anyone retunes the
+forest.
+
+## 2. EXACT VALUES
+
+### 2a. Shared physical facts — `recipes/alpine.json` -> `foliage.rock_scatter`
+
+**Read by BOTH this scatter and the Pass 2 material's scree mask**
+(CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 19). Neither consumer keeps a copy. These are
+properties of rock, not style knobs.
+
+    repose_deg               35.0    valid 25-40    angle of repose; raise it and fans run further
+    cliff_source_slope_deg   45.0    valid 35-70    what counts as a rockfall SOURCE
+    source_smooth_m          16.0    valid 8-32     landform smoothing before the source test
+    runout_m                120.0    valid 40-300   how far debris travels from its source
+    mfd_exponent              1.3    valid 1.0-2.0  multiple-flow-direction concentration
+    max_steps               600      valid >= 400   routing cap; HITTING IT IS A REFUSAL
+    saturation                0.03   valid 0.01-0.2 deposit -> probability, p = 1 - exp(-d/s)
+
+`source_smooth_m` is **not** cosmetic. `stamps.detail_relief` adds plus
+or minus 4.7 m of ridged noise at 28 m wavelength to every face steeper
+than 30 degrees, which tilts individual 4 m cells past any slope
+threshold. Measured on the adopted terrain: cell-scale slope >= 50 deg
+covers **9.152%** of the map, 16 m landform slope about **5.3%**. So
+roughly **40% of the cell-scale cliff area is texture, not landform**,
+and a source test run on cell-scale slope manufactures phantom cliffs.
+
+### 2b. Per-species — a `foliage.species[]` entry that declares `role`

+`role` is the discriminator. The rock and vegetation key sets are
+**disjoint**, enforced by `_validate_rock_species` in
+`scripts/import_heightmap.py`. The shipped species:

+**DISCRIMINATION IS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, not apron area.** A talus field
+that ignores what is above it reads as noise. The naive "scatter on 25-38

+discrimination collapses toward 0% has silently become a slope band.
