+## 2026-08-03 — I DISCARDED TWO WORKING INSTRUMENTS BECAUSE THE CONTROL'S ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG
+
+Cataloguing the GameDevGary heightmap pack, I wanted to know whether the
+512/1K/2K/4K/8K folders hold the SAME ten terrains at five resolutions.
+
+I built a correlation test and gave it a control: same filename across two
+tiers must correlate near +1.0. The control "failed" -- Hills +0.08,
+Wetlands +0.01, Alien -0.01, but Island +0.92.
+
+**I concluded the instrument was broken, three times.**
+
+  Attempt 1: PIL resize on I;16 mode. Suspected bad resampling. Rewrote.
+  Attempt 2: numpy block-mean. Same result. Hypothesised aliasing of
+             high-frequency terrain, since Island is the smoothest map
+             and it was the one that passed.
+  Attempt 3: float32 + PIL BOX, a TRUE area average, which kills the
+             aliasing hypothesis outright. IDENTICAL result.
+
+Then I generated a contact sheet and LOOKED at nine images.
+
+**The tiers are independently generated terrains.** Hills at 512, 1K and
+2K are three unrelated landscapes. Alien is cellular at 512, eroded
+ridges at 1K, different cells at 2K. Island "passed" only because all
+three share a circular island envelope -- the low-frequency shape
+matched, the terrain did not.
+
+The pack is **50 DISTINCT heightmaps**, not 10 at 5 resolutions.
+
+### The actual lesson
+
+**Every instrument was working. The CONTROL's assumption was wrong.**
+"Same filename means same terrain" was a premise I invented, and when
+the data contradicted it I rewrote the measuring device rather than the
+premise -- twice more, each time constructing a new theory (bad
+resampler, then aliasing) to explain away a correct reading.
+
+The tell was there from the first run and I looked straight past it:
+**Island passed.** If the instrument were broken, it would have been
+broken for Island too. One passing case inside a "failed" control means
+the instrument works and the expectation is wrong.
+
+**Rules:**
+1. **When a control fails, suspect the control's ASSUMPTION before the
+   instrument.** A control encodes a belief; a failing control is
+   evidence against that belief just as much as against the tool.
+2. **A partially passing control exonerates the instrument.** Mixed
+   results are a signal about the DATA, not noise to be engineered away.
+3. Non-negotiable 16 says measure the artefact when a fix lands but the
+   frame disagrees. This is the same failure one level up: I was
+   measuring, but I would not believe the measurement. **Looking at nine
+   thumbnails settled in one command what three rewrites could not.**
+
+This is the third time this session that LOOKING resolved something that
+metrics had confused (after the 0.00% vegetation metric and the "pale
+cream" trunks). The pattern is consistent enough to name: *when a
+numeric result is surprising, render it before you refine it.*

+## 2026-08-03 — THE TRUNKS WERE WEARING THE CANOPY'S TEXTURES
+
+Task as given: "reimport the fir through the 8-bit conversion". The
+first measurement refuted the premise, and my own backlog entry with it.
+
+**The reimport was already done.** T_fir_tree_01_bark_rough_4k and
+T_fir_tree_01_twig_rough_4k both trace to *_8bit.png sources in
+Free/_normalized/. And fir_tree_01_twig_alpha_4k.png is **RGB 8-bit** --
+the canopy mask was NEVER in the 16-bit trap. I had written "the fir was
+never reimported after the fix shipped" into BACKLOG the previous
+session, from the LESSONS narrative, without checking the engine.
+
+**A backlog claim about project state is a measurement.** It has to be
+made against the project. Mine was made against the log, and it was
+wrong in a way that would have sent this session to redo completed work.
+
+### The actual root cause, found by asking what M_fir_bark samples
+
+    M_fir_bark samples:  twig_diff x3, twig_nor_gl x2, twig_rough
+    ...and never a bark texture at all.
+
+`texture_map` built `{role: asset}` with a plain `out[role] = ...`.
+`fir_tree_01` ships bark_* and twig_* sets and BOTH provide `color`,
+`normal` and `roughness`. Called without `--slot`, the later file wins
+every contested role -- and "bark" sorts before "twig". So the material
+bound to THREE of the fir's four slots, across 160,448 instances,
+textured every trunk with the pale twig atlas.
+
+**Why nothing caught it.** Every downstream check was satisfied: the
+textures existed, each sampler's type matched its compression setting,
+the material compiled clean against the editor log, and the read-back
+confirmed all three slots were bound. The map was internally consistent.
+It simply described the wrong texture set, and no gate in the pipeline
+knows what a trunk is supposed to look like.
+
+Fixed at the input rather than with a gate (non-negotiable 3): a role
+claimed by more than one file is now a REFUSAL that names the competing
+files. Tested both directions -- refuses with no `--slot`, resolves
+cleanly with `--slot bark` and `--slot twig`.
+
+### THE SECOND DEFECT, WHICH HID THE FIRST FIX
+
+Rebuilding with `--slot bark` reported success and changed NOTHING on
+screen. `M_fir_bark` then had SIX samplers: the three new bark ones and
+the three old twig ones, still wired to BaseColor.
+
+`make_foliage_material` cleared with `delete_all_material_expressions`
+alone. **R2 REJECTED has recorded since 2026-08-02 that this call does
+not delete all material expressions** -- the landscape material was
+fixed then, with an explicit sweep of survivors and a residual count.
+That fix was never swept to the foliage builder.
+
+Instrumented, the numbers are unambiguous: **7 expressions survived on
+M_fir_bark, 8 on M_fir_twig.** Now every survivor is deleted explicitly,
+a nonzero remainder REFUSES rather than building on debris, and both
+counts print on every run.
+
+**This is non-negotiable 4 -- "when you find a defect class, grep for it
+everywhere immediately" -- failing for the THIRD time in this project**
+(after the Rotator transposition and the scalability-multiplier pins).
+The pattern is identical each time: fix the instance, log the instance,
+skip the sweep. The lesson exists and does not fire.
+
+**What would actually fire:** the sweep has to happen in the SAME commit
+as the fix, as a mechanical step, not as an intention recorded for
+later. Every one of these three was logged conscientiously and swept
+never.
+
+### What the render finally showed
+
+Trunks now sample bark_diff (mean brightness 64, dark brown). The change
+is modest in the strongly side-lit verify_ground frame -- near-trunk RGB
+115/98/64 -> 109/90/62 -- and obvious in the backlit forest_floor frame,
+where trunks read dark brown-grey and the needle branches are clearly
+conifer.
+
+**I twice called the trunks "pale cream" from a frame where the measured
+value was a tan-brown under direct sun.** The eye is a poor photometer
+against a dark background; the patch mean settled in one command what
+two rounds of looking did not.
+
+Remaining sparseness is the ASSET -- fir_tree_01_c is a slender,
+high-branching fir -- plus aggressive mid-LODs. That is a judgement
+call, now in BACKLOG, not a defect.

+## 2026-08-03 — RETROACTIVE CAPTURE PASS: applying new rules to old work
+
+Ryan's governance rules landed AFTER the work they govern. This pass
+went back through the session (13 commits after dad6ffa7) and captured
+everything to the new standard, as if the rules had existed then.
+
+The interesting part was not the mechanical retrofit. It was what the
+sweep FOUND.
+
+### A stale claim had hardened into a fact
+
+`WORLD_VISION.md` carried "AERIAL READABILITY IS ZERO ... 0.00%
+vegetation-coloured pixels -- measured, not estimated." I wrote that.
+The words "measured, not estimated" were doing real damage: they told
+every future session not to re-check it. The measurement was broken, and
+the emphasis on its rigour is exactly what would have stopped anyone
+noticing.
+
+Corrected in place, with the correction stated rather than silently
+swapped, so the next reader learns the metric was wrong instead of
+merely seeing different words.
+
+**Rule: an assertion of rigour ("measured, not estimated", "verified by
+read-back", "confirmed at source") is a claim that itself needs to be
+true.** Attaching it to a bad number makes the number harder to
+dislodge, not more reliable. This is the same failure mode as the
+material compile gate that printed "verified by read-back" over a
+broken material.
+
+### The constitution contradicted itself about its own file set
+
+`CLAUDE.md` had BOTH "Plus four load-bearing non-documents" and "Plus
+three load-bearing non-documents" -- I edited the table to six files and
+added the new paragraph without deleting the one it replaced. The
+governing document was internally inconsistent for a full commit.
+
+**Rule: an edit that ADDS a replacement must delete the thing it
+replaces in the same edit.** Append-only is right for LESSONS, which is
+a narrative log. It is wrong for CLAUDE and RECIPES, which are
+statements of what is currently true.
+
+### A live defect was recovered from an old class sweep
+
+The 2026-08-02 sweep recorded that the fir's bark and twig ROUGHNESS
+maps are also I;16, under TC_Masks, "presumed silently wrong (a shine
+defect, not invisibility)". The 8-bit conversion shipped -- but the fir

+it is a candidate cause of the currently-open "conifers render as bare
+spindly poles" defect.
+
+That connection was sitting in LESSONS the whole time and had not been
+made, because the sweep's finding was logged as narrative and never
+became an actionable item anywhere.
+
+**Rule: a class sweep that finds additional affected sites must create a
+work item per site, not a sentence.** "Presumed silently wrong" is a
+defect report, and it belongs in BACKLOG the moment it is written.
+

-# CURRENT STATE — 2026-08-02
+# SESSION PROTOCOL
+
+**No session ends with uncommitted work or a stale CURRENT STATE.**
+
+**At session start, in this order:**
+1. Read `CURRENT STATE` at the bottom of this file.
+2. Read `BACKLOG.md`. **This is the only moment work may be pulled from
+   the backlog** — pulling mid-session is the scope creep the backlog
+   exists to prevent.
+3. **State the session goal in one line, out loud, before touching
+   anything.** A goal you did not write down is a goal you will drift
+   from.
+
+**At session end:**
+1. Descriptive commit — what changed and *why*, not just what.
+2. Update `CURRENT STATE`: open defects, active frontier, next step.
+3. Confirm two-altitude logging happened for every failure this session.
+
+# THE TWO-ALTITUDE LOGGING RULE
+
+**Every failure gets logged twice, in the same commit:**
+
+| Altitude | Where | What |
+|---|---|---|
+| Narrative | `LESSONS.md` | What was attempted, what happened, root cause at a source line or schema, the general rule it implies |
+| Specification | `RECIPES.md`, the relevant recipe's REJECTED section | The exact wrong value/approach → the symptom you will see → the correct value → the reference |
+
+**A recipe with an empty REJECTED section, after a session that hit
+failures, is an incomplete commit.** The narrative alone does not stop
+recurrence — a fresh session follows the recipe, not the story. The
+completeness test: *could a fresh session repeat this mistake without
+opening LESSONS.md?* If yes, it is not yet captured.
+
+# THE NEW-ELEMENT RULE
+
+**No new element without its recipe.** Any session that adds a new
+element TYPE to the world — a new asset kind, material, scatter type, or
+import path — must produce a template-conforming recipe before the
+session ends: exact import settings, compression, LODs, collision,
+placement parameters.
+
+**Tuning an existing element updates its recipe's values in the same
+commit.** A recipe that describes last week's values is worse than no
+recipe, because it will be trusted.
+
+# THE RISKY-OP CHECKPOINT
+
+**Before any operation touching many assets, or not cleanly undoable:**
+create a git branch or tagged commit first, **named for the operation**.
+
+Applies to, at minimum: bulk reimport, landscape resize, mass foliage
+regeneration, engine or plugin version change, batch retarget.
+
+This is not the same as rule 3's ordinary commit discipline. Rule 3 says
+commit before anything where a restore point matters; this says the
+restore point must be *findable by name* six weeks later, when nobody
+remembers which of forty commits preceded the bad reimport.
+

+# Session 4 — 2026-08-03

+## 2026-08-03 — THE 0.00% MEASUREMENT WAS THE DEFECT, NOT THE SCENE
+
+I reported "0.00% vegetation pixels at 2 km" as a FINDING at the end of
+the previous session, and it became the headline entry in the aerial
+backlog. It measured nothing.
+
+The rule was green dominance: (G > R+8) AND (G > B+8). This scene is
+warm-lit. Mean terrain RGB on the ground frame is R 92.5 > G 79.2 >
+B 54.0, so vegetation renders RED-dominant and the test can never fire.
+Proof it was broken rather than merely strict: re-run on the GROUND
+frame -- which visibly contains grass and 160,448 trees -- and it also
+returns 0.00%.
+
+Two further metrics were wrong before I stopped:
+
+1. G - (R+B)/2 above an ABSOLUTE threshold. Brightness-dependent. The
+   forest tint MULTIPLIES albedo, so it darkens; a darker-but-greener
+   surface scores LOWER. It reported the aerial frame had got slightly
+   worse.
+2. Only after normalising by (R+G+B) did the numbers behave -- ground
+   +0.0216 -> +0.0249 with brightness 80.7 -> 65.7 (tint landing),
+   aerial -0.0255 -> -0.0266 (unchanged).
+
+Then I looked at the frames, which settled in seconds what three metrics
+had failed to settle in twenty minutes. The aerial camera is pointed at
+a rock-and-snow peak with half the frame in deep shadow; the forest band
+is a minority of pixels. That camera would report ~0% vegetation no
+matter how good the vegetation was.
+
+### The rule
+
+A measurement is an INSTRUMENT, and an instrument needs calibrating
+against a case with a KNOWN answer before its output is a finding. The
+ground frame was available the whole time and is exactly that case: any
+vegetation metric that scores it near zero is broken, full stop.
+
+This is the same shape as non-negotiable 9 and the fov_deg defect: a
+number arrived, it was in range, and it meant something else. It is also
+the THIRD time this project has been misled by trusting a computed
+verdict over the raw data underneath it -- see the 0.6000000238418579
+float-equality entry from 2026-08-02. Print the measurement AND look at
+the artefact; the verdict is the least trustworthy layer.
+
+## 2026-08-03 — THE REDUCER EATS THE CANOPY FIRST
+
+Re-solving the conifer LOD chain for a longer cull, I added a fifth
+level at 0.137% (693 triangles). It hit its triangle target exactly and
+came back with 2 material sections where LOD 0 has 4. make_mesh_lods
+refused to save, correctly.
+
+I formed a hypothesis that the guard was too strict: three of the fir's
+four slots (bark, dead_branches, trunk_c) are bound to the SAME material
+M_fir_bark, so two surviving sections could in principle still cover
+both DISTINCT materials, leaving nothing unbound.
+
+I probed instead of relaxing the guard, and the hypothesis was WRONG.
+Surviving slots were [0, 3] -- both M_fir_bark. The dropped section was
+slot 1, fir_tree_01_twig: the canopy, and the sole user of M_fir_twig.
+Every distant conifer would have rendered as a bare stick.
+
+Root cause is mesh-simplifier behaviour: a trunk is a connected cylinder
+and survives decimation; a canopy is thousands of disconnected leaf
+cards and is collapsed first. THE VISUALLY DOMINANT FEATURE IS THE FIRST
+THING AN AGGRESSIVE LOD DELETES.
+
+### The rules
+
+1. A guard you are about to weaken deserves one probe first. The probe
+   cost one read and refuted a plausible, well-argued theory that would
+   have shipped bare sticks across the whole forest.
+2. Section count is not a proxy for material coverage, and material
+   count is not a proxy for visual completeness. The right invariant is
+   that every DISTINCT material still has geometry -- and even that
+   would have passed here only by accident.
+
+Locked in R5 REJECTED with the exact percentage and symptom.
+
+## 2026-08-03 — THE CHAIN WAS THE WASTE, NOT THE CULL
+
+The aerial backlog assumed the fix for "no trees at distance" was
+imposters, because extending the 300 m cull was assumed unaffordable.
+Both halves were wrong, and the arithmetic said so before anything was
+built.
+
+Decomposing the 35.9M triangle frame at the 300 m cull:
+
+    LOD0    0- 44 m     15 trees x 505,494 =  7.6M   (909 tris/px)
+    LOD1   44-110 m     79 trees x 126,374 = 10.0M   (563 tris/px)
+    LOD2  110-300 m    603 trees x  30,329 = 18.3M   (367 tris/px)
+
+A tree 110 m away is 45 pixels tall and was being drawn with 30,329
+triangles. Half the frame budget went to the band where the trees are
+smallest. Extending the cull on that chain is unaffordable at any depth
+-- even a 505-triangle deepest level only buys 350 m.
+
+Re-solving on percent_triangles = screen_size^2 -- which holds
+triangles-per-pixel roughly constant and reproduces the existing,
+visually verified LOD1 (0.5 -> 25%) exactly -- gives every band an equal
+8.9M cost and yields cull 730 m at 39.6M. The same chain costs 26.3M at
+the original 300 m, i.e. 27% cheaper than before at equal distance.
+
+### The rule
+
+Before buying a new mechanism, decompose the cost of the existing one.
+The backlog had already decided imposters were needed; ten lines of
+arithmetic showed 2.4x the draw distance was available for +10% cost,
+from fixing a chain nobody had questioned since it was written.
+
+## 2026-08-03 — "I COULDN'T LOOK" REPORTED AS "IT'S ABSENT", TWICE
+
+Verifying the forest tint reached the material graph, my probe printed:
+
+    FOREST FLOOR IN GRAPH: False
+
+The truth was that enumeration had failed outright --
+expression_collection does not exist on Material in 5.8 -- so the probe
+had inspected an EMPTY LIST and correctly reported that an empty list
+contains no tint. The verdict was a false negative dressed as a
+measurement. Had I believed it, I would have "fixed" working code.
+
+The same probe had already guessed get_number_triangles and
+get_number_materials(lod); neither exists. The working accessors were in
+this repo the whole time -- MaterialEditingLibrary.get_material_
+expressions and mesh.get_num_triangles(lod) / get_num_sections(lod),
+both used by scripts I had already run THAT DAY.
+
+### The rules
+
+1. Non-negotiable 10 is not automatic -- it has to be BUILT IN. The
+   probe now returns a distinct exit code and prints "COULD NOT LOOK ...
+   This is NOT evidence of absence" rather than a verdict.
+2. Before guessing an API name, grep the repo for a script that already
+   does the same read. The resolution protocol says query the running
+   editor first; the cheaper prior step is querying our own working code.
+
+scripts/recover_state.py was written with this built in: every read is
+individually guarded, failures come back as an error marker, and the
+report ENDS by listing every value it could not read, so unreadable
+values become VALUE UNVERIFIED in RECIPES rather than silent defaults.
+
+## 2026-08-03 — A KILLED CLIENT IS NOT A CANCELLED OPERATION
+
+place_foliage.py --place was invoked with a 40-minute timeout. The tool
+running it caps at 10 minutes, so the CLIENT was killed at 10.
+
+The payload runs IN THE EDITOR. Killing the client stops the reporting,
+not the work. A read-back probe showed the placement had COMPLETED:
+160,448 instances at cull 54750..73000 cm, exactly as specified.
+
+Had I re-run it on the assumption that an interrupted command did
+nothing, I would have placed a second time on top of a completed one.
+
+### The rule
+
+For any remote-executed operation, an interrupted client leaves the
+outcome UNKNOWN, never "did not happen". Settle it with a read-only
+probe before acting. This is the same shape as R1's rule that
+push_heightmap exit 5 means UNKNOWN and must not be retried.
+
+## 2026-08-03 — t.MaxFPS=45 IS IN THE CONFIG AND NOT IN THE EDITOR

+scripts/recover_state.py read the live session and found t.MaxFPS = 0.0

+# RECIPES.md — the executable spec, and its anti-spec

+**A recipe is a deterministic, replayable specification.** The test it
+must pass: *a session with zero context reproduces the identical result
+by following it, making no judgment calls.* If any step requires the

+is an incomplete commit (CLAUDE.md, two-altitude logging rule).

+what happened, why, the story, the root cause at a source line.

+work, exact values that failed. The same failure is logged in BOTH, at

+---

+## THE RECIPE TEMPLATE (mandatory for every recipe)
+
+Every recipe below MUST carry these five sections, in this order. A
+recipe missing one is not conforming and may not be marked LOCKED.
+
+### 1. PRECONDITIONS
+What must already be true. State each as a checkable fact, not a vibe:
+- Exact engine version (e.g. `5.8.0-55116800+++UE5+Release-5.8`).
+- Required plugins, by name.
+- Config files depended on, **with the specific values assumed** — not
+  "the perf config", but `DefaultEngine.ini [SystemSettings]
+  foliage.DensityScale=1.0`.
+- Assets that must exist first, by full `/Game/...` path.
+- Recipes that must have run before this one, by ID.
+
+### 2. EXACT VALUES
+Every setting the recipe touches, with its full path and literal value.
+- **Nothing may be described as "appropriate", "default", "sensible", or
+  "as needed".** If the value is the engine default, write the default's
+  literal value and say it is the default.
+- Tunable parameters state three things: **locked default**, **valid
+  range**, and **what changing it affects**.
+- A value that could not be read from the project is marked
+  **`VALUE UNVERIFIED`** with a recovery backlog item. **Never invent a
+  value.** Recover values with `python scripts/recover_state.py --out
+  PROJECT_STATE.json`, which reads them out of the running editor and
+  reports every read it could not make.
+
+### 3. ORDERED STEPS
+Numbered, one operation each. Exact menu path, console command, Python
+call, or UDP op — copy-pasteable. If the order is load-bearing, say why
+in one line directly under the step.
+
+### 4. VERIFICATION
+An objective pass test: the render, count, or log output that proves
+success, plus a reference screenshot path in `_verify/`.
+**"Looks right" is not a criterion.** State the number and its tolerance.
+
+### 5. REJECTED
+Everything that failed, at the same precision as the working steps:
+
+```
+WRONG VALUE/APPROACH  →  SYMPTOM YOU WILL SEE  →  CORRECT VALUE  →  ref
+```
+
+Worked examples of the required standard:
+- `16-bit PNG WITH alpha → weightmap clips to zero, grass never renders
+  → 16-bit greyscale, no alpha → R11`
+- `Slope-normal tree alignment → trees tilt up to 40° on foothills →
+  world-up + max 4° jitter → R4`
+
 ## Status key

+## Replay verification tags
+
+A recipe is not truly locked until **replayed cold**: executed on a
+fresh or scratch map purely from the written steps, with the result
+diffed against the reference verification. This suite doubles as the
+engine-migration test — when we move off 5.8, replaying it is how we
+find what broke.
+
+- **UNPROVEN** — never replayed cold. The recipe reflects what was done,
+  but nobody has demonstrated the writing alone is sufficient.
+- **REPLAYED `<date>` PASS/FAIL** — replayed cold on that date.
+
+**Every recipe below is currently UNPROVEN.** The first replay batch is
+scheduled in `BACKLOG.md`. This is expected, not a defect: the tags exist
+so nobody mistakes "written down carefully" for "proven reproducible".

+**THE PINS ARE LOAD-BEARING AND MUST APPEAR AFTER THE `sg.*` LINES.**
+`sg.FoliageQuality=1` expands to `grass.DensityScale=0.4` and
+`foliage.DensityScale=0.4` (`BaseScalability.ini:972`), and
+`sg.ViewDistanceQuality=1` expands to `r.ViewDistanceScale=0.6`
+(`BaseScalability.ini:116`). Without the pins, vegetation density and
+every draw distance silently drop the moment anything expands a group.
+This is the **FoliageQuality split** — low scalability everywhere, but
+vegetation density and draw distance stay truthful.
+

+```
+PercentageUnusedShaderCompilingThreads=70
+NumUnusedShaderCompilingThreads=10
+MaxShaderJobBatchSize=5
+WorkerTimeToLive=10
+```
+Shader worker count is **derived, not set**:
+`NumShaderCompilingThreads = cores − ceil(cores × Pct/100)`. Verified
+headless: `LogShaderCompilers: Using 4 local workers`.
+

+bShowFrameRateAndMemory=True
+```

+# R1 — Terrain generation and push (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)
 
 Informed by: LESSONS §2.1, §6.2, §7.2, §13, §14, and the D4 ruling on
 `--expect-change`.
 
+## PRECONDITIONS
+- R0 satisfied.
+- `recipes/alpine.json` present and schema-valid.
+- No Gaea dependency — see BROKEN.
+
+## EXACT VALUES
+Read live 2026-08-03:
+- Landscape actor label: `Landscape_Alpine`
+- `location_cm = [-403200.0, -403200.0, 128000.0]`
+- `relative_scale3d = [400.0, 400.0, 500.0]`
+- Resolution: **2017 × 2017** (UE resolutions are always N+1)
+- Components: 1024 (32 × 32); quads per component 63; sections per
+  component 1; section size 63 quads — all four DERIVED from measured
+  component spacing, because UE 5.8 refuses `get_editor_property` on
+  these bare `UPROPERTY()` fields
+- Streaming proxies: 256
+- Heightmap: 16-bit greyscale PNG, **no alpha channel**
+- Heightmap datum: value **32768**, not 0, maps to the actor's Z
+- `terrain/alpine_heightmap.png` is the export contract
+
+Tunable: `--resolution` (locked 2017; valid 1009 / 2017 / 4033; raising
+it multiplies generation time ~4× per step and is capped by what the
+Community Gaea licence could ever match — see BROKEN).
+
+## ORDERED STEPS
 ```
-python scripts/make_alpine_terrain.py --resolution 2017   # ~3m20, local only
-python scripts/make_layer_weightmap.py
-python scripts/push_heightmap.py --push [--expect-change]
-python scripts/verify_landscape.py
+1. python scripts/make_alpine_terrain.py --resolution 2017   # ~3m20, local only
+2. python scripts/make_layer_weightmap.py
+3. python scripts/push_heightmap.py --push [--expect-change]
+4. python scripts/verify_landscape.py
 ```
+Step 2 must precede step 3: foliage density reads the BAKED weightmap,
+and a stale bake silently misplaces every plant.
+
+## VERIFICATION
+- `verify_landscape.py` exits 0, reports 1 landscape + 256 proxies,
+  "fully resident", and the scale/location above.
+- The generated heightmap has been opened AS AN IMAGE before pushing.
+- Reference: `_verify/` alpine frames.
+
+## REJECTED
+- `Resampling a power-of-two Gaea export to N+1` → geometry stretches
+  and the terrain no longer matches the weightmap → **CROP, NEVER
+  RESAMPLE** → R1.
+- `--push without --expect-change when the heightmap differs` → the run
+  refuses, by design. That refusal is correct; supply the flag → R1.
+- `Retrying push_heightmap after exit 5` → exit 5 is a TRANSPORT error
+  and the terrain **may already be written**; retrying can double-apply
+  → exit 5 means UNKNOWN: settle it with a read-only
+  `python scripts/push_heightmap.py` dry run → R1.
+- `Exporting immediately after a push to confirm it` → you read the
+  PRE-push terrain, because the import applies **deferred** → re-export
+  after the deferred apply → R1.
+- `Trusting a component census taken while World Partition regions were
+  unloaded` → landscape read as "resolution 505" when it was 1009 →
+  establish residency first; WP exposes only LOADED actors → R1.
+- `Heightmap 0 as the actor Z datum` → terrain sits half a Z-range low,
+  and with `SkyAtmosphere`'s ground plane at world Z 0 the buried half
+  reads convincingly as a fog bank rather than as geometry → 32768 is
+  the datum → R1.
 
-- `--expect-change` is **required** when the heightmap differs from the
-  live terrain. Without it the run refuses, by design.
-- **UE landscape resolutions are always N+1** (1009, 2017, 4033). Gaea
-  builds at powers of two. They never agree — **crop, never resample**.
-- **Heightmap value 32768, not 0, maps to the actor's Z.**
-- Inspect the generated heightmap as an image before pushing it. Two bad
-  terrains were caught in seconds each this way; each would otherwise
-  have cost a full manual import to discover.
-- `push_heightmap --push` can exit 5 with a transport error and **still
-  have written the terrain**. Exit 5 means UNKNOWN. Do not retry — settle
-  it read-only with a plain `python scripts/push_heightmap.py` dry run.
-- The heightmap import applies **deferred**. An export taken immediately
-  after reads the PRE-push terrain.

+# R2 — Landscape material (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)
 
 Informed by: LESSONS §1.9, §14.5, §23.16.
 
+## PRECONDITIONS
+- R1 complete; `textures/alpine_weights.png` baked.
+- Surface sets imported (R3) for any layer declaring `surface`.
+
+## EXACT VALUES
+Live 2026-08-03: material `/Game/Materials/M_AutoLandscape`, assigned to
+`Landscape_Alpine`, **97 expressions**, 10 `LinearInterpolate` nodes.
+
+Three layers, in `recipes/alpine.json`. The weightmap is **RGB — one
+channel per layer, indexed by layer position**, so **three layers is a
+hard ceiling** (`place_foliage.py:176`).
+
+| Layer | slope° | height m | roughness | detail m | macro m | surface |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| Snow | 0–48 | 730–2560 | 0.30 | 4.0 | 188 | Snow006 |
+| Rock | 29–90 | 0–2560 | 0.85 | 4.0 | 188 | Rock051 |
+| Grass | 0–29 | 0–730 | 0.60 | 2.1 | 98.7 | Ground037 |
+
+- `height_jitter_m = 45.0`, `height_jitter_scale_m = 700.0`
+- `blend_sharpness`: Snow 0.25, Rock 0.70, Grass 0.50. Feather is
+  derived: `(1 − sharpness) × MAX`, giving Snow ±9.0°/±115 m,
+  Rock ±3.6°/±46 m, Grass ±6.0°/±77 m.
+- Albedo gain is an **encoding constant**, not a scene parameter: 4.0
+  with a macro sample, 2.0 without, so a mipped-out layer renders
+  exactly `base_color`.
+
+**`material.forest_floor` (schema v1.11)** — added 2026-08-03:
+```
+layer      "Grass"          height_m  [120.0, 640.0]
+feather_m  55.0             strength  0.72
+tint       [0.36, 0.44, 0.28]
+```
+Applies `albedo *= lerp(white, tint, band × strength)` over the tree
+elevation band. Tunable: `strength` (locked 0.72; valid 0.0–1.0; raising
+it darkens the forest floor at ground level as well as at distance).
+
+## ORDERED STEPS
 ```
-python scripts/import_layer_textures.py
-python scripts/make_landscape_material.py --assign
+1. python scripts/import_layer_textures.py
+2. python scripts/make_landscape_material.py --assign
 ```
 
-- The material's layer bands and the baked weightmap are **two
-  instruments for one decision**. Foliage density reads the BAKE, never a
-  re-evaluation of the recipe bands — they disagree by ~115 m of height
-  feathering on this world.
-- `delete_all_material_expressions` does **not** delete all material
-  expressions. Custom outputs survive it. The script now deletes every
-  survivor explicitly and records the residual count; without that, each
-  rebuild layered on the last (158 expressions → 80 once fixed).
+## VERIFICATION
+- The script prints all three layers plus a `forest floor (v1.11)` line.
+- Expression count is **97**, not growing between runs.
+- `compiled clean` AND the tint constants are present in the graph.
+  Confirm structurally — "compiled clean" is true of an empty change too.
+- Reference: `_verify/20260803-0039_alpine_ground-player-eye.png`.
+
+## REJECTED
+- `Applying a per-layer albedo change inside _albedo()` → **silent
+  no-op that still reports a successful build**, because a layer
+  declaring `surface` takes the `_surface_albedo` branch instead →
+  apply where the two paths converge, at the `_lc, _lc_pin` call site →
+  2026-08-03.
+- `Masking the forest tint by slope` → the tint fails at exactly the
+  distance it exists to serve, because the slope term reads the VERTEX
+  normal, which is the DECIMATED mesh's normal and flattens with
+  distance → mask by height only and ride on the layer's baked-weightmap
+  mask, which carries the slope limit at full resolution → 2026-08-03.
+- `Adding a fourth "Forest" layer` → not representable; the weightmap is
+  RGB with one channel per layer → express it as a modulation inside an
+  existing layer → 2026-08-03.
+- `Deriving layer masks from the vertex normal` → rendered coverage
+  drifts from predicted coverage at every LOD, toward the flat-favouring
+  layer → use the BAKED weightmap → R2.
+- `Re-running the builder without clearing custom outputs` →
+  expressions accumulate every rebuild, 80 → 158 → delete every
+  survivor explicitly and record the residual count;
+  `delete_all_material_expressions` does NOT delete all of them → R2.
+- `A band that reaches 0° or 90° with an outward feather` → the outer
+  bound collapses onto the inner one, handing the ramp a zero span:
+  Snow's AND Grass's slope masks were identically ZERO over the whole
+  terrain, so only Rock rendered and the "green" in every capture was a
+  flat background constant → push the outer bound just past the closed
+  cosine range → R2.
+- `Re-evaluating recipe bands for foliage instead of reading the bake` →
+  the two disagree by ~115 m of height feathering → foliage reads the
+  BAKE → R2.
+

+# R4 — Foliage placement (LOCKED, UNPROVEN)
 
 Informed by: LESSONS §23.1, §23.4, §23.12, and RULING (c).
 
+## PRECONDITIONS
+- R1 (weightmap baked), R2 (material assigned), R3 (mesh normalized),
+  R5 (LOD chain built) all complete.
+- `foliage.DensityScale=1.0` pinned (R0) — otherwise you are verifying
+  suppressed vegetation.
+
+## EXACT VALUES
+Live 2026-08-03, `/Game/Foliage/FT_Conifer`:
+```
+mesh                     /Game/Meshes/fir_tree_01_c_LOD0
+cull_distance            {min: 54750, max: 73000}   cm
+enable_density_scaling   False
+align_to_normal          True        align_max_angle      0.0
+random_yaw               True        random_pitch_angle   0.0
+scaling                  UNIFORM     scale_x   {min: 1.0, max: 1.0}
+ground_slope_angle       {min: 0.0, max: 45.0}
+collision_with_world     False       cast_shadow          True
+mobility                 STATIC      density              100.0
+```
+**The FoliageType's own `density`, `ground_slope_angle` and scale fields
+are NOT the operative ones** — placement is computed CPU-side from the
+recipe and baked into instance transforms. The recipe is authoritative:
+```
+density_per_hectare  68     -> 24.7/ha placed (36.4% acceptance)
+slope_deg            [0.0, 24.0]      height_m   [120.0, 640.0]
+scale_range          [0.7, 1.4]       align_to_normal  0.15
+flow_bias            0.45             cull_distance_m  730.0
+```
+Measured result: **160,448 instances**, 1111 components, 1230
+`InstancedFoliageActor`s, cull `54750..73000 cm` (start = 75% of end).
+
+Tunable: `density_per_hectare` (locked 68; valid up to ~68 on this
+hardware; 50/ha breaches both the 250,000 `MAX_INSTANCES` ceiling and
+the triangle budget). `cull_distance_m` (locked 730; valid 300–730 with
+the R5 chain; see R5's budget table before raising).
+

 ```

 ```
+Step 1 is fully offline and verifiable at full resolution before

+  pre-mask target, yielding 24.7/ha placed → R4.
+- `Skipping the orphan sweep` → a deleted species keeps its instances
+  forever: 28,302 planned against **70,923 in the world** → the sweep
+  clears `FT_*` types with no matching species first → R4.
+- `--timeout 6 (the default)` → reads as "no editor is running" on a
+  busy editor → `--timeout 25` minimum; 600 for a full place → R4.
+- `Running a full --place under a 10-minute client cap` → the client is
+  killed mid-run while the **editor keeps executing**, so the work
+  completes with no report → verify with a read-back probe before
+  assuming anything; on 2026-08-03 the placement had in fact finished →
+  2026-08-03.
+- `CullDistance 0` → culling DISABLED, not "cull at zero": every
+  instance draws at every distance, which is how the GPU hit
+  `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG` → set an explicit end cull → R4.

+## 2026-08-02 — TREES: random yaw fed into PITCH; the forest was lying down
+
+`place_foliage` built each instance rotator POSITIONALLY as
+`Rotator(_r[4], _r[3], _r[5])`, against a constructor whose contract is
+`Rotator(roll, pitch, yaw)`, while the row is
+`[x, y, z, YAW, PITCH, ROLL, scale]`. The 0-360 degree random yaw
+therefore landed in PITCH. Measured over the 28,302 placed instances:
+
+    97.6% tilted past 4 degrees
+    MEDIAN TILT 90 degrees
+    55.6% past 80 degrees
+
+One transposition produced every symptom reported: the ~40 degree tilt,
+the floating/clipping bases (a base-centre pivot on a tree pitched past
+horizontal), and much of the "too sparse" read — trees lying flat do not
+present as trees.
+
+The alignment model was never wrong: `align_to_normal: 0.15` against a
+24 degree slope cap yields max 3.6 degrees, already inside the "max ~4
+degrees, never steep slope normals" requirement. Nothing about slope
+handling needed changing.
+
+### THIS IS A PROCESS FAILURE, not just a bug (constitution rule e)
+
+**I logged this exact defect as §23.15 EARLIER THE SAME DAY** — the
+`unreal.Rotator(roll, pitch, yaw)` transposition, found when a viewport
+camera ended up pitched at the sky. The lesson existed and did not
+prevent this.
+
+**Why it did not fire:** I logged the INSTANCE and never swept the
+CLASS. Non-negotiable 4 says "when you find a defect class, grep for it
+everywhere immediately" and I did not. The sweep, done now, takes one
+command and is decisive:
+
+    apply_lighting  Rotator(roll=, pitch=, yaw=)   KEYWORDS — correct
+    capture         Rotator(roll=, pitch=, yaw=)   KEYWORDS — correct
+    frame_cameras   (a comment documenting the order)
+    place_foliage   Rotator(_r[4], _r[3], _r[5])   POSITIONAL — THE BUG
+
+Every site that used keywords was correct. The single positional call
+was the single bug. **The gap fix is therefore not "remember the
+order" — it is that positional construction of Rotator is banned.**
+Keywords make the transposition unrepresentable.
+
+**Rule: after logging a lesson about an API misuse, grep the repo for
+every other call site of that API in the same commit.** A lesson that
+names one instance protects one instance.
+
+## 2026-08-02 — THE MATERIAL COMPILE GATE WAS INERT; the log is the instrument
+
+`M_fir_bark` failed to compile seven times —
+`(Node AppendVector) Missing AppendVector input A`, "Default Material
+will be used in game" — and that material is bound to THREE of the fir's
+four slots. Trunk, dead branches and trunk_c therefore rendered on the
+engine Default Material across every conifer, which is exactly the

+separate defect. **Tasks 3 and 4 were one defect.**

+Persistent debug draw was REFUTED three independent ways — no live trace
+call exists in any script.

+**The real defect was the gate.** `make_foliage_material` captured
+`compile_errors` and returned non-zero on them, but
+`recompile_material()` had returned an EMPTY LIST six seconds before the
+engine logged the seven failures. **Its return is a request-accepted,
+not a verdict** — the compile is asynchronous. So the broken material
+was written to disk and the script printed "verified by read-back".
+
+Worse: my first fix attempt re-verified the rebuild with the SAME inert
+instrument and I nearly closed it on that. An adversarial reviewer caught
+it, citing non-negotiable 2.
+
+**Fixed three ways:** every `connect_material_expressions` return is now
+checked (unchecked returns are how an AppendVector shipped with no A
+input); the build payload no longer saves at all; and the verdict comes
+from the EDITOR LOG — a different instrument than the one that lied —
+with the save issued only afterwards.
+
+**The gate was then tested in both directions** against the real
+historical failure text: it catches the genuine failure, does not
+false-positive when a different material is being built, passes a clean
+log, and errs toward refusing on a stale warning inside its window —
+failing safe.
+
+**Rule: an asynchronous operation's return value is never its verdict.**
+Find an instrument that observes the OUTCOME.

+    after    cull  50 m, 120/10m2  = 12 tufts/m2,  94,248 inst,  29.8M tris

+count rise without the cost following it. `tall_a` at 25% keeps the
+silhouette that reads at eye height.

+
+**Rule: when a density looks wrong, check what it is being spent ON
+before raising it.** Density and draw distance trade against each other,
+and the cheap direction is usually to shorten the reach.

+## 2026-08-02 — [SystemSettings] sets sg.* VALUES but does NOT APPLY THE GROUPS
+
+Task 1a asked whether our own low-spec config suppresses grass. The
+answer for grass is NO, twice over — but finding that out exposed a
+larger defect in the low-spec profile itself.
+
+### The grass answer (NULL RESULT — locked so nobody re-tests it)
+
+`sg.FoliageQuality` **cannot thin our grass or our trees.** Two
+independent reasons, both established rather than assumed:
+
+1. **At source.** `LandscapeGrass.cpp:2040`:
+       const float DensityScale = bEnableDensityScaling ? GGrassDensityScale : 1.0f;
+       GrassDensity = GrassVariety.GetDensity() * DensityScale;
+   with `GrassType->bEnableDensityScaling` passed at :2161. Our
+   `GT_alpine_Meadow` has it FALSE (set deliberately by
+   make_landscape_material), so `grass.DensityScale` is ignored outright.
+   The TREES are immune too, and by accident rather than design:
+   `UFoliageType`'s constructor defaults `bEnableDensityScaling = false`
+   (`InstancedFoliage.cpp:669`), and place_foliage never sets it.
+2. **By measurement.** Grass component count at `sg.FoliageQuality=1`:
+   **16** (4 per variety). After setting 3, flushing and dwelling:
+   **16**, identical mesh distribution. No change.
+
+### The larger defect this exposed
+
+`Engine/Config/BaseScalability.ini:972` — `[FoliageQuality@1]` sets
+`grass.DensityScale=0.4` AND `foliage.DensityScale=0.4`.
+
+Yet a freshly launched editor carrying `sg.FoliageQuality=1` from
+`DefaultEngine.ini [SystemSettings]` reported `grass.DensityScale=1.0`.
+Both cannot be true unless the group never ran.
+
+Discriminating test: issue `sg.FoliageQuality 0` from the console —
+both scales went to **0.0**, and `pcg.Quality` to 0. Restore to 1 —
+both went to **0.4**. So the cvar sink DOES apply groups on a console
+set; it simply had not applied at startup.
+
+**Conclusion: `[SystemSettings]` writes the sg.* cvar's VALUE at load
+without running the scalability group.** The group applies later if
+anything touches the Scalability UI or issues a console set.
+
+**This makes RECIPES.md R7 partly wrong as written.** R7 claimed the
+`[SystemSettings]` block is "authoritative, applied every launch,
+cannot be shadowed". The ten `sg.*` entries are RECORDED at launch but
+their groups are NOT applied. The plain cvars in that block
+(`r.ScreenPercentage`, `t.MaxFPS`, `r.Nanite.MaxPixelsPerEdge`, the
+Lumen switches, `r.ShaderPipelineCache.Enabled`) DO apply — those were
+each confirmed by `LogConfig: Set CVar` at the headless boot. It is
+specifically the scalability GROUPS that do not expand.
+
+**Why this is dangerous rather than merely untidy:** vegetation would
+silently drop to 40% partway through a session the moment anything
+triggered the sink, and a verification pass taken after that point
+would be measuring suppressed vegetation with no indication. That is
+the exact failure mode Ryan named — "never again verify a veg pass
+under settings that hide the vegetation".
+
+**Fix (the split config Ryan asked for):** `grass.DensityScale=1.0` and
+`foliage.DensityScale=1.0` are now pinned explicitly in
+`[SystemSettings]`, AFTER the sg.* lines. Low scalability everywhere
+else; vegetation density stays truthful regardless of whether the group
+ever expands. The live session was restored to 1.0/1.0 as well, since
+the ini only takes effect next launch and the verification screenshots
+are being taken in this one.
+
+**Rule: a config value being PRESENT is not the same as it being IN
+EFFECT.** Verify the derived state, not the setting you wrote. This is
+the same shape as the grass root cause — settings read-backs passed for
+two sessions while the mask clipped every pixel.

+## 2026-08-02 — GRASS ROOT CAUSE: a 16-bit grayscale alpha source clips every pixel
+
+**The grass was never broken. Its opacity mask was.** Root cause found
+by finishing the recorded frontier, in order, exactly as written.
+
+**Step 1 — weights proven non-zero, from source.** The capture path
+calls `InitializeFrom(..., bStripEmptyWeights = true)`
+(`LandscapeGrassWeightExporter.cpp:1190`), and with strip on, a grass
+type whose rendered weights are ALL ZERO is dropped from `WeightOffsets`
+(`LandscapeGrass.cpp:1825-1837`). The engine's own dump reported
+`GT_alpine_Meadow: Num components = 902` of 1024 — and the arithmetic
+corroborates to the byte: 8192 KB height / 1024 = exactly 4096 uint16
+samples; 3608 KB / 902 = exactly 4096 weight bytes. 122 components WERE
+stripped as all-zero, which proves the strip ran on this very data.
+Conclusion: 902 components hold non-zero Meadow weights.
+
+**Step 2 — the bisect, two verdicts in one dwell.**
+- Engine Plane (2 tris, stock WorldGridMaterial) as the grass variety:
+  RENDERED — a carpet of checkered quads following the weight
+  distribution. Grass data, instance building, and rendering all work.
+- Cross test: Plane + `M_grass_medium_01` override — INVISIBLE (the
+  same mesh that just carpeted the hill). Our tuft mesh +
+  WorldGridMaterial override — RENDERED as specks. **The material
+  kills; the mesh is exonerated.**
+
+**Root cause.** `M_grass_medium_01`'s opacity mask samples
+`T_grass_medium_01_alpha_4k` (R pin → MP_OPACITY_MASK, clip 0.333).
+The fir twig — identical construction, renders correctly — has an
+**RGB 8-bit** alpha source. The grass alpha source is
+**`I;16`: single-channel 16-BIT grayscale**. Through the TC_Alpha
+import path, the 16-bit gray's data does not land where the R pin
+reads it — the mask evaluates ≤ clip everywhere, every pixel clips,
+and the material compiles clean, binds clean, and renders nothing.
+
+**Why every earlier check passed:** the import read-back verified
+compression SETTINGS, not content; the material read-back verified the
+mask INPUT was connected, not what it evaluated to; and
+`M_grass_medium_01` had never rendered anywhere — Meadow is
+grass-system only, so no placed instance ever proved it. **A material
+that has never rendered is unproven even when an identically
+constructed sibling renders — the construction was never the variable;
+the source file was.**
+
+**Class sweep (non-negotiable 4), all Free/ import sources by PIL
+mode:** `grass_medium_02` alpha is the same I;16 trap. The fir's bark
+and twig ROUGHNESS maps are ALSO I;16 — imported under TC_Masks and
+"verified" by settings read-back, so the fir's roughness is presumed
+silently wrong (a shine defect, not invisibility). AmbientCG surface
+maps are all 8-bit — unaffected, which is why the landscape renders.
+Displacements are 16-bit but never imported.
+
+**Fix (verification pending at time of logging, appended below when
+done):** normalize 16-bit single-channel sources for mask-type roles
+(alpha, roughness) to 8-bit at import time, into `Free/_normalized/
+textures/`, vendor file untouched — the same derivative pattern as
+pivot normalisation. Then reimport and re-verify by RENDER, the
+instrument that catches what settings read-backs cannot.

+# THE OPERATING LOOP
+
+This is the whole method. Everything below it is detail.
+
+### a. Check `RECIPES.md` first
+Before attempting anything, look for a locked procedure. **If one exists,
+follow it exactly.** No freelancing on solved problems. The recipes exist
+because someone already paid for the mistakes.
+
+### b. No recipe? Experiment freely — but log the moment it fails
+You may try anything. **The moment something fails, log it in
+`LESSONS.md` with root cause before retrying.** Not after the session,
+not once it's fixed — before the retry. A failure you retry without
+understanding is a failure you will have again.
+
+Root cause means a source line, a schema, or a measured number. "It
+didn't work" is not a root cause.
+
+### c. Succeeded and verified? Lock it into `RECIPES.md`
+Verified means: the editor launches clean, the output validates, and
+nothing regressed. Note which `LESSONS.md` entries informed the recipe.
+
+A recipe locked on the strength of one lucky run is worse than no recipe.
+
+### d. Refine deliberately
+A locked recipe can be improved. **Test the improvement in isolation
+first.** Only replace the recipe once the new version is verified. Log the
+old version in `LESSONS.md` as superseded, with the reasoning — never
+delete it.
+
+### e. Rework trends toward zero
+That is the success metric across sessions. **The same mistake twice is a
+process failure, not an accident.** When it happens, the lesson is not
+"be more careful" — log *why the existing lesson did not prevent it* and
+fix that gap. A lesson that exists and doesn't fire is a defect in the
+lesson.
+
+### f. Full autonomy, two escalations
+Decide anything within the RPG vision without asking. Escalate only:
+
+1. **Scope changes** — adding or cutting a major system.
+2. **Anything destructive to `LESSONS.md` or `RECIPES.md`.**
+

+3. **context7**, scoped to the subsystem.
+4. The 5.8 documentation.
+
+Then, in order of authority:
+
+- **The reflected Python surface is the contract, not the C++ header.**
+  C++ declares `SetLightColor(FLinearColor, bool bSRGB)`; Python exposes
+  one argument.
+- **Prove the call reaches the code, not just that the code exists.**
+- **A value can arrive and still mean something else.** Ask not only "did
+  it arrive" but "in what units, in what space, against what datum".
+- **If a lookup contradicts an assumption, the lookup wins — say so.**
+- State the maturity tier of any 5.8 feature you recommend.
+
+## The one rule that would have prevented most defects
+
+**Read the engine source before trusting a name.** Every value handed to
+an API needs its *meaning* confirmed at a source line, not just its
+magnitude derived correctly. Getting the number right from a wrong
+premise produces confident, wrong output.
+
+Casualties: `ReductionSettings[0]` IS LOD 0, so the obvious LOD chain
+would have decimated the source mesh; `delete_all_material_expressions`
+does not delete all material expressions; `CullDistance` 0 means
+"disabled", not "unlimited", and cost a GPU hang; `FGrassVariety` has two
+density fields and the engine reads whichever a runtime switch selects;
+`sections_per_component` allows only {1,2} where the docs said 1-or-4;
+`MATUSAGE_Landscape` was removed in 5.8.
+
+---
+
+# NON-NEGOTIABLES
+
+Distilled from `LESSONS.md`. Each cost a real defect.
+
+1. **Fail closed, and test that each gate cannot be satisfied by the
+   failure it guards against.** "Unknown" is never "yes".
+2. **A gate that has only seen good input has not been tested.** Prove it
+   refuses.
+3. **Prefer an input that cannot express the catastrophic value over a
+   gate that rejects it.** A gate can be wrong; an unreachable state
+   cannot.
+4. **When you find a defect class, grep for it everywhere immediately.**
+   NaN-passing-range-checks was fixed five times because it was fixed
+   locally each time.
+5. **A check that consumes the value it is verifying verifies nothing.**
+6. **Diagnostics must distinguish "I looked and it's absent" from "I
+   couldn't look".** A failed measurement reports *"I could not measure
+   this"*, never the number the broken measurement produced.
+7. **Verify an invariant on complete state.** A count taken while World
+   Partition regions were unloaded became a gate that inverted itself.
+8. **Verify with a different instrument than the one that made the
+   claim.** A read-back that reads the field the setter wrote proves only
+   that the value landed, not that the engine reads it.
+9. **Before writing "as recorded in X", open X.**
+10. **Inspect the artefact before shipping it downstream.** Look at the
+    pixels before running a statistic.
+11. **Sanity-check magnitudes against physical reality.**
+12. **Any step a human does by hand needs a machine check after it.**
+13. **When you must act on an inference, build the disproof into the same
+    operation.**
+14. **Never truncate the output of an operation you cannot repeat.**
+
+---

+# THE AUDIT
+
+**Not a gate. Still the highest-value habit.** No verdict blocks
+execution; nothing waits on it.
+
+`LESSONS.md` Division 3 is a table of defects an independent review caught
+*before first execution* — an enum removed in 5.8 that would have crashed
+every run; a residency gate that would have passed **exactly when loading
+failed**; a "refusal" that mutated and saved before printing REFUSE; two
+findings that meant a script could not run at all. Not one was found by
+the author.
+
 - **Reach for review when the cost of being wrong is not recoverable by
-  git** — anything that deletes, saves, or mutates editor state that a
-  reload will not restore.
+  git** — anything that deletes, saves, or mutates editor state a reload
+  will not restore.
 - **Skip it freely** for generators, analysis, materials, docs, and
   anything whose failure mode is a bad number in a printout.
-- A review that runs is still logged to `docs/audit-log.md` with its
-  verdict and findings, and every edit it makes appears in its findings
-  list — no silent changes.
-- Every audit prompt states REPO_ROOT and UE_PROJECT_ROOT as absolute
-  paths, verbatim, at the top of the request.
-
-**The substitute for the gate is the lessons loop.** With no independent
-reviewer in the path, `docs/lessons.md` is the only mechanism left that
-stops a defect class recurring — which makes the MANDATORY section below
-more load-bearing than it has ever been, not less.
-
-## Hard rules (pipeline)
-1. Logic in Python/C++ — Blueprints only as thin wrappers.
-2. Every scene parameter comes from recipe JSON, never hardcoded.
-3. Scripts idempotent — re-running a recipe rebuilds deterministically.
-4. After any scene change: run scripts/capture.py, one-line note in
-   docs/changelog.md.
-   Editor-touching executions that are not scene changes (connectivity
-   checks, read-only probes) get a one-line entry in docs/audit-log.md's
-   commit annotations or docs/decisions.md instead.

-## HARD-WON LESSONS (full text: docs/lessons.md)
-Distilled from the alpine milestone. Every line below cost a real defect.
-
-### The one rule that would have prevented most of them
-**Read the engine source before trusting a name.** Every value handed to an
-editor UI field or API parameter needs its *meaning* confirmed at a source
-line — not just its magnitude derived correctly. Getting the number right from
-a wrong premise produces confident, wrong output.
-
-Casualties of not doing this: `sections_per_component` documented as 1-or-4
-when the engine allows only {1,2} (hidden because `63*4*8+1` and `63*2*16+1`
-both equal 2017 — an arithmetic coincidence masking a semantic error); the New
-Landscape dialog's Location being the terrain *centre*, not the actor origin;
-`fov_deg` never reaching the engine at all, so captures were framed wrong for
-days; `MATUSAGE_Landscape` removed in 5.8; `get_outermost()` returning the map
-package where `get_package()` was needed.
-
-### The three ways that rule keeps getting evaded
-1. **A header signature is not the binding signature.** C++ declares
-   `SetLightColor(FLinearColor, bool bSRGB = true)`; Python exposes one
-   argument. The reflected surface is the contract.
-2. **Prove the call reaches the code, not just that the code exists.**
-   `RelativeScale3D` really is in the `FixupProxiesTransform` trigger list —
-   but in the ACTOR's handler. Setting it on the root component fired the
-   component's handler instead and tore a landscape into 1024 pieces
-   disagreeing by 7.8 km.
-3. **A value can arrive and still mean something else.** `set_light_color`
-   decodes as sRGB; recipe colours are linear. `fov_deg` reached the engine
-   but not the screenshot. These fail silently — nothing errors, the image is
-   just wrong.
-
-Ask not only "did it arrive" but "in what units, in what space, against what
-datum."
-
-### Non-negotiables
-1. **Audit before first execution.** The gate caught, among others: an enum
-   removed in 5.8 that would have crashed every run; a residency check that
-   would have passed *exactly when loading failed*; a landscape move that would
-   have torn parent from components and saved it; a verifier that would have
-   PASSed that torn state; and a "refusal" that mutated and saved before
-   printing REFUSE.
-2. **Fail closed, and test that each gate cannot be satisfied by the failure it
-   guards against.** Refuse rather than guess. "Unknown" is never "yes".
-3. **Dry-run every destructive operation** before running it for real.
-4. **Identify by property signature, never by name**, wherever an operation is
-   irreversible. Actor labels collide.
-5. **Commit before anything irreversible.** Git is the only undo.
-6. **Never truncate the output of an operation you cannot repeat.**
-7. **Verify an invariant is measured on complete state.** A count taken while
-   World Partition regions were unloaded became a gate that inverted its own
-   meaning.
-8. **When you find a defect class, grep for it everywhere immediately.**
-   NaN-passes-range-checks was fixed three times in three files because it was
-   fixed locally each time.
-9. **A check that consumes the value it is verifying verifies nothing.**
-10. **Diagnostics must distinguish "I looked and it's absent" from "I couldn't
-    look."**
-11. **Before writing "as recorded in X", open X.**
-12. **State honestly when an obligation wasn't met.** The changelog says "no
-    capture accompanies this change" rather than skipping it. A process that
-    quietly tolerates gaps stops being a process.
-13. **When you must act on an inference, build the disproof into the same
-    operation.** The scale script re-read every component's implied origin and
-    refused to claim success unless they agreed — which is the only reason a
-    torn landscape never reached a save.
-14. **Inspect the artefact before shipping it downstream.** Viewing the
-    generated heightmap caught two bad terrains in seconds each; each would
-    otherwise have cost a full manual import to discover.
-15. **When attempts are scarce, spend one read verifying everything.** After
-    one wrong property name, a single source read checked four at once —
-    three were wrong. Guessing one per attempt would have burnt the rule 6
-    budget without ever applying lighting.
-16. **Any step a human does by hand needs a machine check after it.** The
-    import dialog silently produced the wrong sections-per-component and scale
-    on both imports; only the verifier caught it.
-17. **Sanity-check magnitudes against physical reality.** `intensity_lux: 5.0`
-    rendered a fully black frame — sky included. It had been flagged in the
-    first recipe audit and carried unchallenged for the whole project. A
-    flagged risk nobody actions is just a defect with paperwork.
-
-### UE/World Partition gotchas that cost the most time
-- WP exposes only **loaded** actors — every census is silently partial until
-  residency is established. A landscape read as "resolution 505" when it was
-  1009; that was residency, not geometry.
-- OFPA gives each actor its **own hash-named package**; dirty-package lists
-  carry no actor identity.
-- `ALandscape` derives from `ALandscapeProxy`, so panel "proxy counts" may
-  include the parent.
-- Heightmap value **32768**, not 0, maps to the actor's Z.
-- Saving a level saves **every** dirty external package, not just yours.
-- Restoring a file on disk under a live editor desyncs memory; the next save
-  silently overwrites the restore. Close the level first.
-- Bare `UPROPERTY()` fields are unreadable from Python — plan a derivation.
-- In `.gitattributes` **later rules win**; in `.gitignore` `*` **does not cross
-  `/`**. Verify with `git check-attr` / `git check-ignore`.
-- **`SkyAtmosphere` has a ground plane at world Z 0.** With the 32768 datum, a
-  landscape at Z 0 has half its height range buried inside the planet — and it
-  reads convincingly as a fog bank, not as geometry.
-- **The sun drives the sky** when `atmosphere_sun_light` is set, so one
-  implausible intensity blacks out everything, not just the terrain.
-- **Property names strip the `b` and keep the rest**: `bEnableVolumetricFog` →
-  `enable_volumetric_fog`, not `volumetric_fog`.
-- **`ALight` declares `LightComponent`**, so it is `light_component` on every
-  light actor — no `directional_light_component` / `sky_light_component`.
-- **UE landscape resolutions are always N+1** (1009, 2017, 4033); Gaea builds
-  at powers of two. They never agree — crop, never resample.
-- **numpy 2.0 removed `ndarray.ptp()`** — use `np.ptp(a)`. Libraries drop APIs
-  across major versions; pinning a version in docs is not checking its API.
-

+# Lessons — what worked, what didn't
+
+Written 2026-07-31 from the alpine milestone: repo scaffold through verified
+heightmap import, one destructive editor mutation, and a failed capture.
+
+This is not a summary of what was built. It is a record of **which practices
+caught real defects** and **which mistakes recurred**, so the next project can
+skip the tuition. Every item below is traceable to a specific incident in
+`docs/audit-log.md` or `docs/decisions.md`.
+
+The headline: the pipeline shipped roughly a dozen scripts. **Every serious
+defect in them was caught by an independent review before execution, and
+almost every one came from assuming an API's semantics instead of reading the
+engine source.** Those two facts are the whole guide.
+
+---
+
+## 1. What worked — repeat these
+
+### 1.1 A mandatory audit gate with an independent reviewer
+Non-negotiable, and it paid for itself many times over. Real defects it caught
+*before first execution*:
+
+| Defect | Would have caused |
+|---|---|
+| `set_base_material_usage(MATUSAGE_Landscape)` | `AttributeError` on **every** run — the enum was removed in UE 5.8 — one line after the material graph had been wiped |
+| Residency gate compared against a number measured on a *partially loaded* level | The gate would have passed **exactly when loading failed** — an inverted safety check |
+| `set_actor_location` on a World Partition landscape | Parent moved, 64 components left behind, torn state **saved to disk** |
+| Verifier read only the parent actor's location | Would have **PASSed** that torn state |
+| Band masks feathered inward | Diagnostic tool would have painted a fake coverage gap at every layer boundary |
+| `biome_id` interpolated into a filename unvalidated | Recipe could steer a file write outside its sandbox |
+| Scale-mismatch "refusal" that moved and saved *first*, then printed REFUSE | A persisted mutation reported as a no-op |
+| Derived-resolution check fed the expected value into its own verification | Verified nothing, in the tripwire |
+| Un-doubled braces in a `.format()` template | `KeyError` at import — the module could never have run |
+
+**The pattern:** the reviewer must be independent of the author, must have
+source access, and its verdict must gate execution — not merely inform it.
+A review that only advises gets rationalised away under time pressure.
+
+**Corollary that mattered:** when the reviewer gained the ability to *fix* its
+own findings, the author must still verify those fixes. It caught things I
+missed; I caught nothing wrong in its fixes — but checking cost minutes and the
+alternative was a reviewer marking its own homework.
+
+### 1.2 Verify semantics at an engine source line, not just arithmetic
+The single highest-value habit, learned the hard way (see 2.1).
+
+The rule that emerged: **every value handed to an editor UI field or API
+parameter needs its *meaning* confirmed at a source line — not just its
+magnitude derived correctly.** Getting the number right from a wrong premise
+produces confident, wrong output.
+
+### 1.3 Fail-closed gates, layered and independent
+Every gate refused rather than guessed, and each was independent of the others:
+
+- **Identity** — refuse unless exactly one editor matches the expected project.
+- **Residency** — refuse unless loaded counts equal on-disk counts (World
+  Partition only exposes *loaded* actors, so a census taken blind is a lie).
+- **Exactly-one** — refuse unless precisely one target exists.
+- **Positive attribution** — act only on things provably attributed to the
+  target; "unknown" is never treated as "yes".
+- **Hard assertion** — a final check that *raises* rather than filters. A
+  filter silently shrinks a kill list; an assertion stops the run.
+
+**Test each gate can't be satisfied by the failure it guards against.** The
+residency gate originally passed when loading failed — the inverse of its job.
+
+### 1.4 Dry-run mode on anything destructive
+`--dry-run` printed the full kill list with per-item evidence before deleting
+anything. It also surfaced the wrong invariant (68 vs 80) harmlessly. Any
+irreversible operation should be runnable in a mode that proves what it *would*
+do.
+
+### 1.5 Identify by property signature, never by name
+Two landscapes had proxies with **identical labels** — names were generated
+from grid coordinates and collided. Deletion by name-matching would have
+destroyed the wrong terrain.
+
+The deletion script required **three independent signature conditions** and
+aborted on zero or multiple matches. **When an operation is irreversible,
+identify by intrinsic properties and require the match to be unique.**
+
+### 1.6 Commit before every irreversible operation
+Git was the only undo. A pre-mutation commit made the deletion recoverable and
+let an accepted-but-unwanted change be restored later. Cheap, and the one time
+it mattered it mattered completely.
+
+### 1.7 Write rulings to disk, not just into the conversation
+Decisions recorded in `docs/decisions.md` survived context loss; decisions that
+lived only in messages did not. Several times a ruling had to be re-derived
+because it existed only in prose.
+
+**If a decision will constrain future work, it belongs in a file** — with the
+reasoning, not just the outcome, so it isn't re-litigated.
+
+### 1.8 Deterministic synthetic fixtures unblock real work
+A generated heightmap (fixed seed, reproducible) unblocked the whole milestone
+while the real source was unavailable — same path, same format, same contract,
+so the real export drops in with no downstream change.
+
+**Bonus:** because it was synthetic and regenerable, an accidental edit to it
+was a shrug instead of a crisis.
+
+### 1.9 One derivation, shared by producer and checker
+The spec printer and the verifier imported the *same* `derive_spec` function,
+so what was printed and what was verified could not drift. **If two components
+must agree, make them share the code that decides — not a convention.**
+
+### 1.10 Report derived values as derived
+When the engine refused to expose three geometry properties, they were computed
+from measured spacing and printed under a loud `DERIVED` banner. The value was
+trustworthy (a uniqueness proof backed it), but it was never presented as
+something the engine had confirmed.
+
+---
+
+## 2. What didn't work — avoid these
+
+### 2.1 Assuming API semantics instead of reading source
+**This caused more defects than everything else combined.** The incidents:
+
+- `sections_per_component` documented as "1 or 4"; the engine's legal values are
+  `{1, 2}`. The error survived because `63×4×8+1` and `63×2×16+1` both equal
+  2017 — **an arithmetic coincidence hid a semantic error.**
+- The New Landscape dialog's `Location` is the terrain's **centre**, not the
+  actor origin. The actor landed 403200 cm from where intended.
+- `fov_deg` never reached the engine — the viewport-camera call copies only
+  location and rotation. **Captures were framed at the wrong FOV for days**, and
+  analysis of those images rested on a false premise.
+- `MATUSAGE_Landscape` was removed from the enum in 5.8.
+- `get_outermost()` returns the *map* package; `get_package()` returns the
+  actor's own package. Under one-file-per-actor these differ, and the wrong one
+  guarantees a false "no match" — on a lookup that gated a deletion.
+- `EditorLevelLibrary.get_editor_world` deprecated since 5.0, used in a gate
+  intended to front every subsequent script.
+
+**Rule: if a name is being trusted to mean something, find the line that
+defines it.** Reading source costs minutes; a wrong assumption costs a
+debugging session and sometimes data.
+
+### 2.2 Writing code against a spec that was never traced to source
+The schema's own worked example was unbuildable. Everything downstream
+inherited the error — two scripts hard-coded the illegal value, and a spec
+printer would have told a human to type a number the dialog cannot accept.
+
+**Validate the specification itself before building on it**, especially where
+it describes an external system.
+
+### 2.3 Implementing against semantics the spec doesn't have
+Material layers were authored as overlapping ranges assuming weighted blending.
+The schema plainly specified first-match-wins. Result: the intended 60% snow
+line was really 54.7%, and one bound was dead range.
+
+Worse, the fix was initially proposed as *changing the schema* — forking a
+specification to justify one artefact's encoding error. **When output disagrees
+with spec, first assume the output is wrong.**
+
+### 2.4 Resolving design-level findings unilaterally
+A review returned a BLOCK requiring a design decision. It was rewritten,
+re-reviewed, and committed before the owner ever saw the finding. The code was
+fine; the process was inverted — the implementer chose the design and review
+followed.
+
+This produced a standing rule: **design-level findings must be surfaced and
+signed off *before* implementation, commit, or re-review. A rewrite does not
+retire a design finding — sign-off does.**
+
+### 2.5 Claiming something was recorded when it wasn't
+Four rulings were reported as "recorded in decisions.md" when they existed only
+in a schema file and commit messages. Caught by the reviewer, which correctly
+refused to write the decision record on the author's behalf.
+
+**Before writing "as recorded in X", open X.**
+
+### 2.6 Measuring an invariant on partial state
+A proxy count of 68 was measured while most actors were unloaded; the true
+total was 80. That number was then baked into a safety gate — which, combined
+with a survivable load error, would have passed *only* when loading failed.
+
+**An invariant measured on incomplete state is not an invariant.** Derive it
+from an authoritative source (on-disk descriptors), or verify completeness
+before trusting the measurement.
+
+### 2.7 Diagnostics that can lie
+A debug visualiser is only useful if its failure modes are distinguishable from
+the failures it reports. Inward-feathered masks would have shown fake gaps at
+layer boundaries — read as a recipe bug that didn't exist.
+
+Likewise, "NO MATCH" originally conflated *"the accessor doesn't work"* with
+*"genuinely absent"*. **A diagnostic must distinguish "I looked and it's not
+there" from "I couldn't look".**
+
+### 2.8 Truncating your own output on an irreversible run
+A destructive script's output was piped through a line limit, discarding the
+result. State had to be reconstructed from git and the filesystem.
+
+**Never truncate the output of an operation you cannot repeat.**
+
+### 2.9 Recurring input-validation blind spots
+The same class of bug appeared **three separate times** in different files:
+
+- `NaN` / `Infinity` pass numeric range checks (`nan <= 0` is `False`), and
+  JSON parsers accept those literals by default.
+- A value interpolated into a filename or path without charset validation is a
+  traversal vector.
+
+**When a defect class is found once, grep for it everywhere immediately.** It
+was fixed three times because it was fixed locally each time.
+
+### 2.10 Config file ordering and glob subtleties
+- In `.gitattributes`, **later rules override earlier ones**. Placing a general
+  rule after specific ones silently re-enabled text conversion on 162 binaries.
+- In `.gitignore`, `*` **does not cross `/`** — `captures/*.png` doesn't match
+  `captures/alpine/x.png`. Consequence: the first output file went untracked,
+  making the tree permanently "dirty" and destroying a reproducibility marker.
+
+**Verify config files behave as intended (`git check-attr`, `git check-ignore`)
+rather than assuming they read top-down like code.**
+
+### 2.11 Circular verification
+A check computed its "actual" value using the expected value it was verifying.
+It could not fail. **A check that consumes the answer verifies nothing** — trace
+each assertion back to an independent measurement.
+
+### 2.12 Referring to context the reader may not have
+Reports repeatedly cited option labels, finding IDs, and verdicts the reader
+had never received, because messages arrived truncated. This wasted several
+exchanges.
+
+**Carry the content, not the label** — or a path where the full text lives.
+`(i)`, `F2`, `D1` are indexes, not information.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Domain gotchas (Unreal Engine, World Partition, OFPA)
+
+Cheap to know, expensive to discover:
+
+- **World Partition exposes only *loaded* actors.** Any census, count, or
+  geometry derivation is silently partial unless residency is established
+  first. A landscape reported "resolution 505" when it was 1009 — that was
+  residency, not geometry.
+- **One File Per Actor: each actor is its own package**, named by hash. Dirty
+  package lists give you hashes with no actor identity; map package → actor via
+  the actor's own package accessor.
+- **Actor labels are not unique.** Grid-generated names collide across
+  different parents.
+- **`ALandscape` derives from `ALandscapeProxy`**, so a "proxy count" in the
+  details panel may include the parent itself. Off-by-one confusion followed.
+- **Deprecation fixups fire on load**, dirtying packages that were never
+  touched. A batch of warnings after loading previously-unloaded actors is
+  usually pre-existing data, not damage just caused.
+- **Bare `UPROPERTY()` fields are not readable from Python.** Only
+  editor/Blueprint-exposed properties are. Plan a derivation path.
+- **Landscape height datum:** heightmap value 32768 (mid-grey), not 0, maps to
+  the actor's Z. Terrain at actor Z 0 spans ±half the height range, not 0..range.
+- **Saving a level saves *every* dirty external package**, not just the
+  intended one. An unrelated in-progress edit gets committed as a side effect.
+- **Editors hold packages in memory.** Restoring a file on disk under a live
+  editor desyncs them, and the next save silently overwrites the restore. Close
+  the level first.
+
+---
+
+## 4. Process rules worth carrying forward
+
+1. **Audit before first execution**, with an independent reviewer that has
+   source access and whose verdict gates execution.
+2. **Surface design-level findings for sign-off before implementing.** A
+   rewrite doesn't retire them.
+3. **Commit before and after anything irreversible.**
+4. **Dry-run mode on every destructive operation.**
+5. **Fail closed everywhere.** Test that each gate can't be satisfied by the
+   failure it guards.
+6. **Stop after two consecutive failures** against a live external system.
+   Diagnose; don't iterate variations blind.
+7. **Reports must carry content, not references** to things the reader may not
+   have received.
+8. **Record rulings in files**, with reasoning.
+9. **State honestly when an obligation wasn't met** — the changelog says "no
+   capture accompanies this change" rather than skipping it silently. A process
+   that quietly tolerates gaps stops being a process.
+
+---
+
+---
+
+# Session 2 — terrain, material, lighting (2026-08-01)
+
+The first milestone completed end to end. Everything below is new; nothing
+above is retracted. The pattern from §2.1 — assuming an API's meaning instead
+of reading it — recurred in three fresh disguises, so it is worth studying how
+it hid each time.
+
+## 6. New failure modes
+
+### 6.1 A header signature is not the binding signature
+`ULightComponent::SetLightColor(FLinearColor, bool bSRGB = true)` is what the
+C++ header declares. The Python binding exposes **one** argument:
+`set_light_color() takes at most 1 argument (2 given)`.
+
+Reading the header told me the function existed and what it accepted. It did
+not tell me what the *binding* accepted. **When calling into a foreign runtime,
+the reflected surface is the contract — not the native declaration behind it.**
+
+### 6.2 A value that arrives but means something else
+Because `bSRGB` is unreachable and defaults true, the engine decodes whatever
+you pass as sRGB. Recipe colours are linear. Passing linear values directly
+would have produced a deeper, more saturated tint than specified — **with no
+error, and no way to notice from the image alone.**
+
+Same class as the `fov_deg` bug that framed every capture wrong for days: the
+call succeeds, the value lands, and the meaning is wrong. These are the
+expensive ones, because nothing fails.
+
+**Ask not only "did it arrive" but "in what units, in what space, against what
+datum."**
+
+### 6.3 Verify the dispatch path, not just the line
+`LandscapeEdit.cpp:6644-6652` puts `RelativeScale3D` in the list that triggers
+`FixupProxiesTransform`. I read that, concluded a property-system write would
+reach it, and set the property **on the root component**. That fires the
+*component's* handler. The trigger list lives in
+`ALandscapeProxy::PostEditChangeProperty` — the **actor's**.
+
+Result: 1024 components disagreeing on the landscape origin by 7,812 m.
+
+**Finding the line that does what you want is half the work. The other half is
+proving your call actually reaches it.**
+
+### 6.4 Implausible magnitudes render as "broken", not "wrong"
+`intensity_lux: 5.0` produced a **fully black frame**. Not dark — black,
+including the sky, because `SkyAtmosphere` is driven by the sun and 5 lux makes
+the atmosphere itself unlit. Real golden-hour sun is 10,000–20,000 lux.
+
+That value had been flagged as an exposure risk in the *first* recipe audit and
+was carried unchallenged through the entire project. **A flagged risk that
+nobody actions is just a defect with paperwork.** Sanity-check magnitudes
+against physical reality before assuming the renderer is at fault.
+
+### 6.5 Libraries remove things across major versions
+`ndarray.ptp()` was removed in numpy 2.0; this project runs 2.5.1. Use
+`np.ptp(a)`. Cost one failed run. Pinning a version in docs is not the same as
+checking the version's API.
+
+### 6.6 Manual steps need verification every single time
+The import dialog silently produced `sections_per_component` 1 instead of 2 and
+kept scale 800 instead of 400 — twice across two imports. Both were caught only
+because a verifier compared the live scene against the recipe.
+
+**Any step a human performs by hand needs a machine check afterwards.** Not
+because people are careless, but because a dialog with a dozen fields will
+eventually disagree with the instructions in ways nobody notices.
+
+## 7. New things that worked
+
+### 7.1 Instrument a risky inference so failure is immediate
+Before setting the scale by script — an action I believed safe but had inferred
+rather than proven — the same script was written to re-read every component's
+implied origin afterwards and refuse to report success unless they agreed.
+
